More particularly, the invention relates to a device and a method for skin mole detection algorithm for Digital images of Skin Cancer. More particularly, there is provided a device for skin mole detection, and a method to implement skin mole detection method. The method comprises following steps: Obtaining an image of Skin Mole by camera on an electronic device, such as a computer, or a handheld device such as tablet, mobile, and the kind; Running GUI mode of algorithm installed in said electronic device; Detection of Melanoma Type Cancer affected Skin Mole (Indicated with Red Color Border) using the Sobel Edge Detector using GUI mode of algorithm. If there is no Red Color Border, then Melanoma Type Skin Cancer is not affected.

AU YIN W
   ZHANG M
   TAO Y
   LI Y
AE UNIV SHANGHAI JIAOTONG (USJT-C)
GA 202067856X
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves placing a skin by using a laser with wavelength in the range of 400 nanometer to 700 nanometer to excite auto-fluorescence of the skin. Auto-fluorescence distribution and intensity of the skin with the wavelength in range of 420 nanometer to 800 nanometer are detected. The distribution and intensity of the auto-fluorescence is compared with a healthy skin tissue. Determination is made to check whether skin cancer and a degree of the skin cancer are affected to complete detection process of the skin cancer based on skin auto-fluorescence, where the auto-fluorescence intensity of skin cancer lesion area tissue is greater than that of adjacent tissues and normal skin tissues.
   USE - Method for manufacturing a biomarker for skin auto-fluorescence detection of skin cancer during product production.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables determining a type and a stage of the skin cancer according to characteristics of the auto-fluorescence intensity, shape and left-right symmetry.

TI Process for detecting developed or incipient breast cancer - comprises testing for free aminoacid(s) in skin secretions, and is suitable for mass screening.
AU ETTARE R C
AE ONCOLAB INC (ONCO-Non-standard)
   PRIMARY DIAGNOSTIC (PRIM-Non-standard)
GA 1984076974
AB       Detection of a developed or incipient malignant tumour beneath human skin, the tumour being present in tissue continuous with the tissue underlying the portion of skin, comprises collecting a sample of secretion from the outer surface of the skin and testing an aliquot portion for the presence of decreased free aminoacids. Presence of free aminoacids in the sample shows probable absence of tumour, and their absence indicates a high probability of incipient or developed malignancy.
   The test reagent is pref. ninhydrin or it may be isatine or cadmium acetate. The process is esp. suitable for diagnosing incipient or developed breast cancer.
   The process is simple, inexpensive, has a high degree of reliability and is readily adaptable for mass screening. It is also able to detect malignant growth at a "high risk" stage. The process avoids risks associated with cancer detection by X-ray provides a non-invasive diagnostic test.
EA    (US4542750-A)      To detect a developed or incipient malignant tumour in tissue contigaious with the tissue beneath a predetermined portion of skin, secretion from an outer surface of the skin portion is collected. The presence of a tumour is then determined according to the quantity of amino acids that are detected in the secretion. A standard ninhydrin test can be used.
   USE -   Esp. for mass screening for detection of breast cancer.
   (5pp)

AU KAZEEV V I

GA 201832292C
AB    NOVELTY - Invention relates to medicine, namely to                oncology, and can be used to guide patients after                the primary detection of skin cancer in them. For                this purpose, clinical examination is carried out                with carrying out of examinations in the volume                necessary for the timely diagnosis of new malignant                tumors, including other localization. When a                patient is diagnosed with skin cancer, clinical                examination is performed within the first 10 years.                At the same time, during the first five years,                patients undergo an oncological examination twice a                year, chest x-ray 2 times a year,                fibrogatroduodenoscopy once a year,                fibrocolonoscopy once a year, ultrasound                examination of the abdominal cavity organs, small                pelvis and kidneys, peripheral lymph nodes, thyroid                gland once a year, and also, respectively, the                patient's floor, ultrasound examination of the                breast 2 times a year, mammogram from the age of                forty 1 every 2 years, transrectal ultrasound                examination of the prostate 2 times a year, a study                of the general and free prostate-specific antigen 2                times a year. If there is no cancer detection                within 10 years of the dispensary observation, the                patient is considered healthy and taken off the                register. When cancer is detected, the patient is                clinicized for another 10 years with the                above-mentioned examinations for 5 years and in the                absence of a recurrence of cancer, the patient is                recognized as healthy and taken off the                register.
   USE - Medicine.
   ADVANTAGE - Method provides timely diagnosis of malignant                neoplasms of other localization in patients after                primary detection of skin cancer due to adequate                timing parameters of the clinical examination with                the necessary volume of examinations with clear                deadlines.

TI Cancer detection method in patients e.g. cancers such as testicular, prostate, ovarian, breast, respiratory tract, digestive tract, urinary tract, skin, tumors of internal organs including reproductive organs, or metastatic tumors.
AU JORDAN B L
   FANG T
   JORDAN B
AE UNIV FLORIDA (UYFL-C)
   JORDAN B (JORD-Individual)
   FANG T (FANG-Individual)
GA 2000052885
AB    NOVELTY - The method for the detection of cancer in a patient involves evaluating the patient to determine whether the patient has at least one retinal deficit which does not cause a significant loss of visual acuity, and where the patient does not have melanoma associated retinopathy (MAR) or cancer associated retinopathy (CAR), and where the presence of the retinal deficit is correlated with the presence of cancer in the patient.
   USE - The methods can be used for detecting cancers such as testicular, prostate, ovarian, breast, respiratory tract, digestive tract, urinary tract, skin, tumors of internal organs including reproductive organs, or metastatic tumors (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The detection of retinal dysfunctions indicating the presence or status of cancers provides for non-invasive early diagnosis of cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for: (1) a method for the detection of cancer in a patient where the method comprises detection in the patient of a toxic factor which interacts with neural cells; (2) a method for the treatment of cancer comprising blocking the activity of, or reducing the concentration of, a toxic factor where the toxic factor interacts with neural cells; (3) a method for monitoring the progression of a cancerous condition and/or the efficacy of treatment, where the method comprises monitoring changes in retinal deficits associated with CAR deficit (CARD); (4) a kit for the detection of cancer which comprises at least 2 of the following: (a) dark adaptation test materials; (b) color vision test materials; (c) electroretinogram (ERG) test materials; (d) electroencephalogram (EEG) test materials; and (e) a vision questionnaire; (5) a method for the detection of cancer in a patient which comprises determining whether the serum of the patient has antibodies to a protein of at least 30kD when the antibodies bind to neural cells.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - The retinal deficit tested for may be e.g. a loss of dark adaptation, a defect in color vision, an abnormality in the ERG or an abnormality in the EEG. The toxic factor which interacts with neural cells may be e.g. antibodies, cytokines, hormones, or other proteins.
   EXAMPLE - Patients (n=25) with various cancers were tested. Initial testing involved Ishihara plates, near visual acuity, and questions about visual symptoms. Further testing consisted of an ophthalmologic exam, Humphries or Glodmann visual fields, Farnsworth-Munsell 100-hue color test, Glodmann/Weekers (central and peripheral) dark adaptation test, fundus photos, Heidelberg laser scanning tomography, and measurements of electrical function of neural tissue. Serum samples were drawn for autoantibody testing on Western blots with purified proteins. The results showed that (1) 100% of patients in the sample had at least 1 identifiable visual deficit, over 95% had 2 or more identifiable deficits, (2) no patients with melanoma associated retinopathy (MAR) or cancer associated retinopathy (CAR) were found; instead, based upon the widespread indications of visual deficits in these cancer patients, a third clinical visual syndrome associated with cancer (CAR deficit (CARD)) is pro posed, (3) patients with CARD exhibit no apparent loss of best corrected visual acuity, (4) rare color vision deficits are associated with patients who have CARD, (5) in contrast to CAR and MAR the electroretinogram (ERG) may be only moderately effected in CARD, (6) rather than random errors in color vision, specific axes are apparent in CARD patients; the aberrant axis may be the same or different in each eye. 4 patients had detectable antinuclear antibodies (ARA) detectable at a titer of 1/400 on Western blot of human retinal proteins, 50% of the patients had IgG antibodies to the human retinal form of glyceraldehyde 6 phosphate dehydrogenase, only 4 patients had IgM antibodies to enolase, while 4 had weak IgG and 10 had strong IgG responses against enolase.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for:
   (1) detecting (M1) a deletion spanning 547-4443 nucleotides in the minor arc of the mtDNA genome, where the deletion is associated with skin cancer and/or sun exposure, in a subject having mtDNA, comprises providing a biological sample from sun exposed skin of the subject, extracting mtDNA from the biological sample, and detecting the presence of the deletion in the mtDNA;
   (2) monitoring (M2) a subject for the progression toward skin cancer, involves providing a biological sample from the subject, extracting mtDNA from the biological sample, and detecting the presence or absence of 3895 base pair deletion;
   (3) determining (M3) the cumulative UV exposure in a subject having mtDNA, involves carrying out the steps of (M2);
   (4) early detection (M4) for NMSC development, involves carrying out the steps of (M2);

   (6) a nucleic acid primer L404 or H4676; and
   (7) a method for the collection of a patient sample for use in diagnosing skin cancer by using a deletion spanning 547-4443 nucleotides in the minor arc of the mtDNA genome, involves providing a biological sample from the subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In (M1)-(M5), the deletion is an approximately 3895 base pair deletion, where the deletion comprises a span of mtDNA from mtTF1 binding site in the D-loop to transfer RNA (tRNA) methionine. The deletion includes substantially a 12s ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene, 16s rRNA gene, ND1 gene and promoters for transcription of H and L strands. The step of detecting the presence of the deletion in the mtDNA comprises PCR analysis, where the PCR analysis includes radioactive PCR analysis. The biological sample is from a dermis layer of the subject. The biological sample is from rarely sun exposed, occasionally sun exposed or usually sun exposed skin. (M1) or (M2) further involves a step of comparing the absence or presence of 3895 base pair deletion in rarely sun exposed, occasionally sun exposed or usually sun exposed skin.Preferred Primer: The L404 primer comprises sequence such as cttttggcggtatgcacttt, or H4676 primer comprises sequence such as gattatggatgcggttgctt.

   USE - Biomedical image analysis system for detecting                skin cancer through classification of dermoscopic                images in clinical settings. Can also be used in                radiology and pathology.

AE TRANSLATIONAL GENOMICS RES INST (CITY-C)

GA 2010B25957
AB    NOVELTY - Screening for a skin cancer in a subject                comprises detecting an expression level of dual                specificity phosphatase 1 protein (DUSP1) in the                subject and comparing the expression level of DUSP1                to a level of DUSP1 expression predetermined to                correlate with the presence or absence of the skin                cancer.
   USE - The methods are useful for screening for skin                cancer in subject; prognosing survivability of                subject having skin cancer; and for treating skin                cancer, where the skin cancer is basal cell                carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma,                dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, Merkel cell                carcinoma, neuroectodermal tumor, lympathic                epithelial tumor or sarcoma Kaposi, where melanoma                is selected from malignant melanoma, cutaneous                melanoma and intraocular melanoma, preferably an                early stage melanoma (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The invention provides method for diagnosing                an early stage melanoma as well as a better defined                and less variable method for determining the                prognosis for a subject with melanoma.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   (1) a method for prognosis of survivability of                a subject having a skin cancer comprising detecting                an expression level of DUSP1 in the subject and                comparing the expression level of DUSP1 to an                expression level index of DUSP1 predetermined to                correlate with survivability;
   (2) a method of treating a skin cancer                comprising administering to a patient in need of                such treatment an effective amount of DUSP1 or an                active fragment, a nucleic acid that encodes a                protein comprising DUSP1 or an active fragment, an                analog or a prodrug;
   (3) a pharmaceutical composition for treating                a skin cancer comprising a DUSP1 or an active                fragment, a nucleic acid that encodes a protein                comprising DUSPI or an active fragment, an analog                or a prodrug, and a pharmaceutically acceptable                carrier, excipient or diluent; and
   (4) a kit comprising a reagent for detection                of DUSP1 expression level, a compilation comprising                DUSP1 expression level indices that have, been                predetermined to correlate with the presence or                absence of skin cancer, assay components and                components for collection of a sample; or a kit                comprising a reagent for detection of DUSP1                expression level, a compilation comprising DUSP1                expression level indices that have been                predetermined to correlate with cancer                survivability, assay components and components for                collection of a sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method above, the                  expression level of DUSP1 is detected by protein                  detection technique, where the protein detection                  technique is selected from western blot, protein                  array, immunohistochemical assay, enzyme-linked                  immunosorbent assay (ELISA),                  fluorescent-activated cell sorting, flow:                  cytometry, and mass spectrometry. The protein                  detection technique is immunohistochemical                  staining. In prognosis of survivability of                  subject having skin cancer, the predetermined                  DUSP1 expression level index is obtained by                  assaying skin cancer samples from subjects with                  the same type of skin cancer for the expression                  of DUSP1 and correlating the DUSP1 expression                  levels with the observed survivability of the                  subjects. The patients' survivability corresponds                  to a percentage of DUSP1 expressing cells on the                  predetermined DUSP1 expression level index. The                  DUSP1 expression level index is determined by                  assaying the percentage of cells in a skin cancer                  sample that are positive for DUSP1 expression,                  where the DUSP1 expression level index values                  that correlate with increased survivability range                  from about 5% to about 100%; or the DUSP1                  expression level index is determined by assaying                  the percentage of cells in a skin cancer sample                  that are positive for DUSP1 expression, and                  categorizing the positive cells into                  semi-quantitative levels of expression based on                  the intensity of the staining, where the range of                  staining is from 0 to 3. The DUSP1 expression                  level index is determined by assaying the                  percentage of cells in a skin cancer sample that                  are negative for DUSP1 expression, where the                  DUSP1 expression level index values that                  correlate with reduced survivability range from                  about 5% to about 100%. Treating skin cancer                  further comprises administering to a patient an                  agent that increases the expression of DUSP1,                  where the agent is angiotensin, aldosterone,                  AG1478 or U0126.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Composition: The pharmaceutical                  composition further comprises an agent that                  increases the expression of DUSP1, where the                  agent is angiotensin, aldosterone, AG 1478 or                  U0126.

GA 2002507831
AB    NOVELTY - Sulfonamide derivative (I)used as                photosensitizer in photodynamic therapy is                new.
   USE - (I) is used as a photosensitizer in PDT, in                photochemical internalization, in the production of                cancer vaccines or in the diagnosis or detection of                medical condition (all claimed); to treat                pre-cancerous conditions (e.g. Barrett's does and                cervical intraepithelial neoplasia), cancer (e.g.                bladder cancer and colon cancer), ophthalmological                disease including macular degeneration, vascular                problems such as cardiovascular disease,                arteriosclerosis and restenosis and autoimmune                diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, skin                diseases such as psoriasis, acne and eczema and                other benign conditions such as endometriosis and                mennorrhagia. The compounds may also be used as                anti-microbial treatments for skin and wound                infections, other local infections as well as in                the treatment of dental bacterial disease, in                treatment, diagnosis and/or detection of conditions                in various parts of the body including the skin,                lungs, brain, eye, colon, bladder, cervix and                does.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) is not only highly effective as                photosensitizing agent when used in vivo but also                is rapidly cleared from the body, has little or no                skin photosensitivity and unlike some other                sensitizers, does not cause unacceptable skin                discoloration. (I) has good water solubility                allowing easy formulation of appropriate                composition.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Sulfonamide derivative of formula (I),                excluding tetrasulfonylaminoglycine zinc (II)                phthalocyanine, used as photosensitizer in                photodynamic therapy (PDT) is new.
   Q = photosensitizing chromophoric                system;
   X = bond or 1-5C alkyl (optionally substituted                by at least one hydrophilic group);
   Y1 = 1-5C alkyl (optionally substituted by at                least one hydroxy group); and
   n = 1-4.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   (1) use of (I) in the manufacture of                medicament for the treatment of a condition by PDT                or for photochemical internalization in the                production of cancer vaccine or in the manufacture                of an agent for use as a photosensitizer in the                diagnosis or detection of a medical condition;                and
   (2) diagnosis or detection of a medical                condition in an animal (including human being)                involving applying (I) to the animal and                irradiating the animal to elicit a fluorescent                response from (I).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Compound: The salt of (I) is of                  formula (II).R = -NH-X-CO2H.
   Preferred Definitions:
   X = CH2, CH2CH2, CH(CH3)(CH2)3 or (CH2)4;                and
   Q = residue of a metal phthalocyanine,                benzoporphyrin, purpurin, chlorin or                bacteriochlorin.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Ophthalmological; Cardiant;                Antiarteriosclerotic; Vasotropic;                Immunosuppressive; Antirheumatic; Antiarthritic;                Antipsoriatic; Antiseborrheic; Dermatological;                Gynecological; Antibacterial; Vulnerary.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - Zinc phthalocyanine tetrasulfonyl chloride (5                g) and alpha-alanine (12 g) were combined at                ambient temperature and heated to 55 degrees C for                2 hours. The resultant solution was dialyzed for 1                week and evaporated to dryness and the residue was                dried in an oven to give TsZnPc-alpha-alanine (A)                (1.27 g). Skin of Wistar rats were depilated and                injected with (A) intravenously at different                concentrations. At 24th the skin patch was exposed                to broad band white light from a xenon arc lamp.                The patch showed definite edema or erythema heating                after 24 hours and 2 weeks.

The altered potentials detected by non-invasive measurement on the skin reflect the presence of underlying malignancy in the tissue(breast). When an array of specially designed sensors is placed on the skin surface of the breast, the effect of electrical alternations impedance values can be used as an indicator for the breast cancer detection as the sensors receives a small bio potential field from the surface of the breast and breast tissue density does not adversely affect it.

AB    NOVELTY - The system leverages deep learning to classify                lung cancer, skin melanoma, and breast tumours. The                system employs InceptionResNetV2 with transfer                learning, data augmentation, and fine-tuning to                improve classification accuracy. The image                preprocessing techniques such as normalization,                resizing, and augmentation ensure robust                predictions across varying imaging conditions. The                system is deployed as a Flask-based web                application, enabling doctors to upload medical                images and receive real-time classification                results. The automated report generation and                email-based result sharing ensure seamless                communication between doctors and specialists for                timely referrals.
   USE - Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered cancer                prediction system for early detection of breast                tumors, skin melanoma, and lung cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The system improves early cancer detection by                reducing chances of missed diagnoses during primary                consultations. The system enables general                practitioners (GPs) to identify potential cancer                cases sooner and refer patients to specialists at                an earlier stage, and supports doctors in making                quicker and more accurate referrals to                specialists.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of the                AI-powered cancer prediction system.

   detection, diagnosis and/or treatment of                patient suffering from skin cancer by administering                the photoimmuno-theranostics reagent defined above                to a patient;

   a vector comprising a polynucleotide encoding                a single-chain variable fragment antibody of SEQ ID                No. 1; and
   a host cell comprising the vector of (3)                and/or producing a polynucleotide encoding a                single-chain variable fragment antibody of SEQ ID                No. 1.

AB    NOVELTY - Nanoparticles with metal containing compound                (Q) are new.
   USE - (Q) is useful in a drug composition and a                cosmetic composition for the detection, treatment,                monitor, prevention, delay, onset and/or recurrence                of a condition such as cancers, cell proliferative                diseases, skin diseases (claimed), inflammatory                diseases and tissue damage.
   ADVANTAGE - (Q) is economical to prepare, has low                toxicity, and improved biocompatibility.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Nanoparticles with metal containing compound                (Q) of formula (I) or (II) are new.
   A=porous silicon nanoparticle;
   M=transition metal;
   X=halo or carboxylic acid anion;
   R=(-NH-CO-NH-) or (-NH-CS-NH-);
   W1=1-12C alkanediyl;
   x=0-1;
   R1a=monovalent compound of formulae (Ia) and                (Ib);
   Z =organic or inorganic cation;
   Y =-COO - or -SO 3 - ;
   A =halo or carboxylic acid anion;
   R1=1-10C alkyl; and
   Cbg=specific targeting molecule of neoplastic                tissues.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   Preparing (Q); and
   a kit for the detection, treatment, monitor,                prevention, delay, onset and/or recurrence of a                condition such as cancers, tumors, cell                proliferative diseases and diseases of the skin                comprising the porous silicon nanoparticles grafted                by intermediate covalent bond by a photosensitive                molecule or a drug composition, and a biphotonic                infra-red radiation.
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preparation (Claimed): Preparation of (Q)                  comprises functionalizing porous silicon                  nanoparticles by groups containing at least an                  amine group or at least isocyanate or                  isothiocyanate group, providing and grafting a                  photosensitive molecule, carrying a complementary                  group carried by the nanoparticle, so as to form                  an urea or thiourea connection, and optionally                  grafting by at least a targeting molecule.                  Preferred Components: (Q) has a particle size of                  20-200 nm, preferably 140-160 nm and a pore size                  of 5-50 nm, preferably 10-30 nm. Preferred                  Method: The method further comprises (a)                  electrochemically etching a single crystal                  silicon wafer in a ethanolic solution of                  hydrofluoric acid and eliminating a porous film                  and ultrasonic treating the film, (b) performing                  oxidation and silanization so as to produce                  silicon-hydroxide group and titanium dioxide on a                  surface of the porous silicon and performing                  hydrosilylation step, (c) grafting the                  nanoparticles by a porphyrin type photosensitive                  molecule of formula (III), and (d) grafting the                  nanoparticles by sugar or its derivative using a                  phenylsquarate group.T=-NH 2 , -N=C=O or -N=C=S.                                                                                                                              
   Preferred Definitions:
   X=Cl - , Br - , I - , acetate, propionate,                butyrate, ascorbate, benzoate, cinnamate, citrate,                fumarate, glycolate, malonate, tartrate, malate,                maleate, mandelate or tosylate;
   W1=-(CH 2 ) 3 -;
   R1=1-3C alkyl;
   Z =K + , Li + , Na + or NH 4 + ;
   A=Cl - , Br - , I - , acetate, propionate,                butyrate, ascorbate, benzoate, cinnamate, citrate,                fumarate, glycolate, malonate, tartrate, malate,                maleate, mandelate or tosylate;
   R1a=(1-methylpyridin-1-ium-4-yl) iodide or                (4-sulfonatophenyl) ammonium hydride; and
   Cbg=sugars and sugar derivatives when it is                present.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Dermatological; Antiinflammatory;                Vulnerary.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   SPECIFIC COMPOUNDS - 2 Compounds (Q) are specifically claimed                  i.e. metal containing compounds of formulae (Qa)                  and (Qb).
                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                 
   EXAMPLE - Positive type monocrystalline silicon was                electrochemically etched in hydrofluoric/ethanol                acid solution at 3:1 in Teflon(RTM: PTEF) cell                using a circular electrode against platinum. A                constant current (200 mA/cm 2) was applied for                150&#176; C. Sample was rinsed for three times                with ethanol. The porous layer was                electro-dissolved in hydrofluoric solution in 3.3%                ethanol by applying constant current (4 mA/c) for                250 seconds and was deposited in ethanol in a glass                bottle. The sample, after degreased under nitrogen                flux for 20 minutes, was sonicated in an ultrasonic                bath for 16 hours. The particle dispersion in                ethanol was filtered and centrifuged at 14000                revolutions per minutes for 30 minutes. The                dispersion of nanoparticles with particle size of                115 nm was obtained.

   R1 = ethyl, butyl, hexyl, octyl or dodecyl                (all optionally substituted); and
   R2-R5 = H.

No dosage details                given.
   EXAMPLE - Polylactic acid (100 mg) and lauric acid (40                mg) were each dissolved in acetone (1 ml).                Hexylaminolevulinate octyl benzene sulfonate (100                mu mole) was dissolved in ethanol (1 ml). The                polylactic acid-, lauric acid - and hexyl                aminolevulinate octyl benzene sulfonate                salt-solution were mixed and completed to 10 ml                with acetone. The obtained nanosuspension was then                filtered through a paper filter to discard large                aggregates. The resulting nanoparticles were                centrifuged for 10 minutes, the supernatant was                discarded and the particles were resuspended in                water (5 ml). The procedure was repeated once and                the nanoparticles were then lyophilized for 48                hrs.

GA 2019324677
AB    NOVELTY - An isolated polynucleotide, is new. The                isolated polynucleotide has a (a) 472 base pair                sequence (SEQ ID NO: 1) fully defined in the                specification, (b) fragment of polynucleotide of                (a), where at least one modified cytosine                triphosphate deoxynucleotide-phosphodiester-guanine                triphosphate deoxynucleotide (CpG) site is present                and/or (c) a nucleic acid complementary to                polynucleotide or fragment of (a) or (b).
   USE - The isolated polynucleotide is useful in                preparation of detection reagent or kit for                detecting tumor. The tumor is chosen from digestive                system tumors such as esophageal cancer, gastric                cancer, colorectal cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic                adenocarcinoma, bile duct and gallbladder cancer,                gynecological and reproductive system tumors such                as breast cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical cancer,                vulvar cancer, testicular cancer, prostate cancer                and penile cancer, hematological tumors such as                leukemia, lymphoma and multiple myeloma,                respiratory tumor such as lung cancer and pleural                tumors, nervous system tumors such as glioma,                neuroblastoma and meningioma, head and neck tumors                such as oral cancer, tongue cancer, laryngeal                cancer and nasopharyngeal cancer and urinary system                tumors such as kidney cancer, bladder cancer, skin                and other systems such as skin cancer, melanoma,                osteosarcoma, liposarcoma and thyroid cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The isolated polynucleotide detects tumor with                high sensitivity and specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) a method for preparing a tumor detecting                reagent involves providing the polynucleotide,                using the full length or fragment of polynucleotide                as a target sequence, designing a detection reagent                that specifically detects modification of the CpG                site of the target sequence, the detection reagent                comprises a primer and a probe;
   (2) reagent or reagent combination;
   (3) a test kit comprising a container, or a                reagent or reagent combination located in the                container; and
   (4) a method for detecting a methylation                profile of a sample in vitro involves (i) providing                a sample to extract nucleic acids, and (ii)                detecting CpG site.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecule: The modification is                  5-methylated modification, 5-hydroxymethylation                  modification, 5-aldehyde methylation modification                  or 5-carboxymethylation modification. The                  isolated polynucleotide further comprises (d)                  polynucleotide having 472 base pair sequence (SEQ                  ID NO: 2 or 4) fully defined in the specification                  and (e) a fragment of polynucleotide of                  (d).

TI Method for segmenting skin cancer lesion, involves            outputting distribution probability map of target area            after test image passing through network, and obtaining            segmentation result of lesion skin target to be            divided.
AU QU A
   CHENG Z
   LIANG H
   CHUNG H
   HUANG J
AE UNIV SOUTH CHINA (USOA-C)
GA 2020B7246R
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves obtaining a training skin                mirror image sample and performing data                normalization. One end to end of two branch neural                network architecture is constructed. The                distribution probability map of the target area is                obtained. The loss is transmitted backwards in the                network, so as to obtain the gradient of network                parameters, and adjust the parameters according to                the adaptive moment estimation optimizer to                minimize the loss and achieve the best network. A                to-be-divided skin mirror image is directly                inputted to the network after finishing the                training; using the learned network to predict the                skin mirror image to be tested; the distribution                probability map of the target area is outputted                after the test image passing through the network.                The segmentation result of the lesion skin target                to be divided is finally obtained.
   USE - Method for segmenting skin cancer                lesion.
   ADVANTAGE - The method for segmenting skin cancer lesion                realizes the detection of the edge details of the                image, uses MultiBlock module to expand the                receptive field of the model so as to enhance the                sensitive ability of different scale target,                combines the space attention mechanism to restrain                the interference of the background                information.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flowchart illustrating                the method for segmenting skin cancer lesion.                (Drawing includes non-English language text)

AU NARAYANA L G
   MANJU D
   BABU P S
   CHANDRA V K
   PRASAD R R
   SAGAR V K
AE VALLURUPALLI NAGESWARA RAO VIGNANA JYOTH (VALL-Non-standard)
GA 202604989J
AB    NOVELTY - The apparatus has a microstrip substrate                supporting a radiating structure, and a central                circular radiating patch generating millimeterwave                electromagnetic fields. A circular ring resonant                element concentrically surrounds the central                circular patch. A set of star-shaped perturbation                structures is arranged symmetrically around a                circular ring to enhance field localization. A                coaxial feed mechanism is coupled to the radiating                structure to excite the antenna at 37.65 GigaHertz.                A set of conductive vias is arranged along a                periphery of the substrate to reduce surface-wave                losses and stabilize impedance. TI Deep learning-based system for detecting and            classifying skin cancer using convolutional neural            networks, has transfer learning module that integrates            ResNet50, Xception, DensityNet201, and InceptionV3            models, and model optimization module that adjusts            hyper parameters to improve performance.

GA 202535597M
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a convolutional neural network                (CNN) trained on a preprocessed dermoscopic image                dataset. An image preprocessing module utilizes                autoencoder based segmentation and dull razor                filtering. A transfer learning module integrates                ResNet50, DenseNet169, Xception, DensityNet201, and                InceptionV3 models. A model optimization module                adjusts hyper parameters to improve classification                performance. The dataset is pre-processed using                oversampling and undersampling techniques for                balanced training.
   USE - Deep learning-based system for detecting and                classifying skin cancer using CNNs and transfer                learning techniques in medical image processing and                artificial intelligence (AI).
   ADVANTAGE - The system achieves early and accurate                detection of skin cancer using CNNs and transfer                learning techniques. The system realizes                application of deep networks even with limited                datasets, thus improving diagnostic accuracy. The                system provides a confidence score for each                prediction, thus enhancing reliability and                classification accuracy and F1-score.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for detecting skin cancer using deep                learning.

TI Diagnosing skin cancer and/or melanoma, involves            determining expression profile of predetermined set of            micro RNAs in biological sample and comparing            expression profile with reference expression            profile.
AU KELLER A
   MEESE E
   BORRIES A
   STAEHLER P F
   BEIER M
   STAEHLER P
AE FEBIT HOLDING GMBH (FEBI-Non-standard)
   FEBIT HOLDING GMBH (FEBI-Non-standard)
   FEBIT HOLDING GMBH (FEBI-Non-standard)
   COMPREHENSIVE BIOMARKER CENT GMBH (COMP-Non-standard)

   COMPREHENSIVE BIOMARKER CENT GMBH (COMP-Non-standard)
GA 2010Q08811
AB    NOVELTY - Method for diagnosing skin cancer and/or                melanoma, involves determining expression profile                of predetermined set of micro RNAs (miRNAs) in                biological sample and comparing the expression                profile with reference expression profile. The                predetermined set of miRNAs comprise at least 1, 7,                10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50, 75 or 100 miRNAs                chosen from miRNA given in figure 3OA, 3OB 32A,                32B, 33A and 33B provided in the patent                specification. The biological sample is chosen from                blood, plasma and/or serum.
   USE - The method is useful for diagnosing skin                cancer and/or melanoma, lung cancer, cardiovascular                disease, infectious disease, inflammatory disease                and autoimmune disease e.g. multiple                sclerosis.
   ADVANTAGE - The skin cancer can be diagnosed accurately                with high specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   kit for diagnosing and/or predicting state of                health in a subject, comprising (a) unit for                determining miRNA expression profile of RNA sample                and (b) at least one reference set of miRNA                profile;
   apparatus for diagnosing state of health in a                subject, comprising (a) database for storing                several non-coding RNAs profile corresponding to                individuals and several diseases, (b) capture probe                matrix for determining non-coding RNA profile from                several capture probes designed for parallel                detection of several non-coding RNAs comprising                miRNAs, (c) fluidic system, (d) detection system,                (e) unit for injection of RNA sample, (f) unit for                holding capture probe matrix, (g) unit for                connecting the sample injection and capture probe                matrix holding to the fluidic system, (h) unit for                hybridization, enzymatic reactions and washing                steps, (i) unit for heating and cooling the                reactions carried out on capture probe matrix and                (j) computer and algorithm for comparing non-coding                RNAs profiles and calculating probabilities;                and
   et of oligo or polynucleotides for diagnosis                of melanoma and/or skin cancer, comprising the                sequences of set of the above-mentioned miRNAs or                their complements.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Nucleic acid: The predetermined                  set of miRNAs comprises miRNA or set of miRNAs                  given in figure 33A or predetermined set of                  miRNAs comprises miRNA or set of miRNAs given in                  figure 33B provided in the patent specification.                  Preferred Method: The method for diagnosing                  and/or predicting skin cancer, involves (a)                  providing RNA sample, (b) providing unit for                  determining expression profile for several miRNA                  and/or other non-coding RNA molecules chosen from                  at least 4, 6, 8, 10, 20, 100, 1000 or 15000 and                  up to 1000000 molecules, (c) contacting the                  above-cited RNA sample with above-cited unit, (d)                  determining the expression profile of several                  miRNAs and/or other non-coding RNAs in the                  above-cited RNA sample, (e) providing several                  reference miRNA and/or non-coding RNA expression                  profiles obtained from several different                  reference profiles, (f) calculating common                  signature profile from combination of at least 2                  conditions, (g) comparing miRNA and/or non-coding                  RNA profile obtained from step (d) with common                  signature profile of step (f) and (h),                  calculating the probability for at least 2                  conditions and (i) repeating steps (f), (g) and                  (h) for at least another common signature profile                  and (j) collecting the probability values for the                  particular common signature profiles. The common                  signature profile is subset of miRNAs or                  non-coding RNAs differentiating between at least                  2 conditions providing several reference miRNA                  and/or non-coding RNA expression profiles. The                  method for providing several reference miRNA                  and/or non-coding RNA expression profiles                  involves (a) providing at least 10, 50, 100 and                  up to 1000, 2000 or 5000 reference miRNAs and/or                  other non-coding RNA expression profiles obtained                  from several different reference subjects                  representing different conditions and selecting                  subset of miRNAs and/or non-coding RNAs in the                  expression profile comprising several miRNAs                  and/or non-coding RNAs characteristic for the                  particular condition and analyzing the subset of                  miRNAs and/or other non-coding RNAs and at least                  two groups of reference subjects. The unit for                  determining expression profile for several miRNA                  and/or other non-coding RNA molecules is matrix                  comprising several capture probes. The miRNA                  expression profile is determined by nucleic acid                  hybridization, nucleic acid amplification,                  polymerase extension, sequencing, mass                  spectroscopy or their combinations. The nucleic                  acid hybridization is performed using solid-phase                  nucleic acid biochip array, microarray, beads or                  in situ hybridization. The nucleic acid                  amplification is performed by real-time PCR                  (RT-PCR) or quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR).                  The miRNA expression profile of the reference                  expression profiles and predetermined set of                  miRNAs are stored in database. The biological                  sample is not labeled before determination of the                  expression profile. The method for diagnosing                  skin cancer, further involves determining                  survival rate, responsiveness to drugs,                  monitoring the course of the disease or the                  therapy, e.g. chemotherapy, staging of disease,                  measuring the response of patient to therapeutic                  intervention, segmentation of patients suffering                  from the disease, identifying patient and                  predicting the occurrence, preferably severity of                  the occurrence of the disease and/or predicting                  the response of patient with the disease to                  therapeutic intervention. Preferred Kit: The kit                  for diagnosing skin cancer and/or melanoma                  comprises unit for determining one or more                  above-mentioned miRNAs.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Female torso training aid for breast cancer            simulation has skin covering over jointed arms ribs and            breasts with implants representing normal malignant and            benign conditions that may be illuminated.
AU HAQUE P
AE HAQUE P (HAQU-Individual)
   HAQUE P (HAQU-Individual)
GA 2002751246
AB    NOVELTY - The torso is supported on a stand adjustable                for height and angle and has a hollow back. The                breasts contain sacs of lower viscosity fluid and                implants (24) to represent benign, malignant and/or                normal breast conditions. The torso is constructed                with ribs and articulated arm joints all covered by                artificial skin. The breasts may be varied in size                and heated to body temperature. The implants may be                illuminated.
   USE - To assist in training for the detection                especially self-detection of breast cancer and                lumps.
   ADVANTAGE - The hollow back allows a woman to stand                relative to the training aid with the breasts in a                similar position to her own. Ribs, arm movement,                size variation and temperature control aid                realism.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - Front view of the torso
   24Implanted lumps.

TI Detecting cancer e.g. liver cancer, bone cancer,            pancreatic cancer, and skin cancer, comprises obtaining            biological sample comprising cells, enriching target            cell from cells, and analyzing target cell and            quantifying features of target cell.
AU DUDLEY J C
   VOGELSTEIN B
   KINZLER K W
   PAPADOPOULOS N
AE UNIV JOHNS HOPKINS (UYJO-C)
GA 202536687N
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting a cancer in a subject, comprises (a)                obtaining a biological sample from the subject,                where the biological sample comprises many cells,                (b) enriching a target cell from the cells, and (c)                analyzing the target cell and quantifying at least                one features of the target cell.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting a cancer in                a subject (claimed), and detecting a cancer cell                from a biological sample (e.g. body fluids) from a                subject, where the cancer comprises hematopoietic                cancers including leukemia, lymphomas (Hodgkin's                and non-Hodgkin's), myelomas and myeloproliferative                disorders, sarcomas, melanomas, adenomas,                carcinomas of solid tissue, squamous cell                carcinomas of the mouth, throat, larynx, and lung,                liver cancer, genitourinary cancers e.g. prostate,                cervical, bladder, uterine, and endometrial cancer,                renal cell carcinomas, bone cancer, pancreatic                cancer, skin cancer, cutaneous or intraocular                melanoma, cancer of the endocrine system, cancer of                the thyroid gland, cancer of the parathyroid gland,                head and neck cancers, breast cancer,                gastrointestinal cancers and nervous system                cancers, or benign lesions e.g. papillomas.
   ADVANTAGE - The method utilizes biomarkers in clinical                applications for early cancer diagnosis, improved                cancer prognosis, early detection of cancer                relapse, real-time monitoring of therapeutic                efficacy and therapeutic resistance, and in cancer                diagnostics by relatively easily obtaining                biological samples using minimally invasive                procedures before, during, and after cancer                treatment.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method further                  comprises dissociating the cells into single                  cells before the enrichment step (b), where the                  enrichment step (b) comprises separating the                  target cell based on the target cell size, and                  the enriching the target cell based on the target                  cell susceptibility to lysis. The dissociating                  and enrichment step comprises using an                  alcohol-based cytology preservative. The                  analyzing step (c) comprises using flow                  cytometry, and staining the target cell with a                  fluorescent dye and/or an antibody. Preferred                  Components: The features comprise a presence of                  aneuploidy, global hypomethylation, tumor                  suppressor protein loss, presence of cancer                  specific biomarkers, phosphorylation of                  oncoproteins, elevated proliferation rate,                  tetraploidy, and/or elevated nuclear to                  cytoplasmic ratio, preferably presence of                  aneuploidy in the target cell, and global                  hypomethylation of DNA in the target cell. The                  fluorescent dye comprises GelRed(RTM: Fluorescent                  nucleic acid dye), SYBR green(RTM: Asymmetrical                  cyanine dye), (4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole),                  propidium iodide, or fluorescein. The fluorescent                  dye is conjugated to the antibody, where the                  antibody specifically binds to methylated DNA, a                  tumor suppressor protein, or a phosphoryl-group                  on an oncoprotein. The antibody is an                  anti-cytokeratin (CAM) 5.2 antibody, an                  anti-cytokeratin antibody, an anti-cluster of                  differentiation (CD) 45 antibody, an anti-CD66b                  antibody, an estrogen receptor antibody, or a                  progesterone receptor antibody. The biological                  sample comprises: saliva, pap test fluid, urine,                  cerebrospinal fluid, ascites fluid, or pleural                  fluid from the subject; urine from the subject;                  and pap test fluid from the subject. The target                  cell comprises a urothelial cell, or an                  endometrial cell.

AB       Method for detecting a target antigen (Ag) closely associated with a body component comprises: (1) treating the component in situ with an antibody (Ab) that binds Ag to form a complex; (2) labelling the complex and (3) detecting the label. Also new are kits for this process used to detect Ag in the skin.
   USE -   The method is used for diagnosis, prognosis and monitoring of fungal infection (esp. Candida albicans or Aspergillus), neoplasms (esp. melanoma, leukaemia and polyoma), bacterial infections (esp. Clostridium perfringens, C. tetani, Mycobacterium leprae or Treponema pallidum), or viral infections (esp. measles, rubella, herpes, papilloma, or HIV). The method can also be applied to plants.
   ADVANTAGE -   Detection of Ag can now be done without requiring laboratory equipment or biopsy samples, facilitating field screening for pathogens. The method may also detect Ag below the skin surface, e.g. in wounds or body cavities.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves activating a                dermatological examination device with a housing.                The main portion is coupled to the housing and                provided with a LED. The end caps are collectively                provided to control operable to selectively                activate the dermatological examination device by                electrically coupling the LED to an electrical                energy source. The optical filtering component is                arranged in optical alignment with light emitted by                the LED. GA 2006814711
AB    NOVELTY - A predisposition to cancer, early detection of                cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                progression of cancer, absence of cancer, or sun                exposure in a biological sample having                mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is detected by providing                a biological sample comprising mtDNA; and detecting                a deletion in the mtDNA.
   USE - The method is used in diagnosis such as                predisposition to cancer (e.g. non-melanoma skin                cancer or prostate cancer), early detection of                cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                progression of cancer, absence of cancer, sun                exposure or aging. It is used in detecting sun                exposure or non-melanoma skin cancer. It is useful                for detecting a deletion spanning approximately                nucleotides 10744 to 14124 of the mtDNA genome,                where the deletion is associated with prostate                cancer. (All claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The inventive method allows the detection of                the presence of preneoplasia, neoplasia, and                progression towards potential malignancy before                common clinical symptoms are evident. It is simple                and straightforward. It allows differentiation                between mutations in mtDNA that cause disease and                simply variations within and between                populations.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   an array comprising nucleic acid members, and                solid substrate, where each nucleic acid member is                mitochondrial DNA, RNA transcribed from                mitochondrial DNA, or cDNA, and has unique position                on the array and is stably associated with the                solid substrate;
   a kit for diagnosing a predisposition to                cancer (e.g. skin cancer), early detection of                cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                progression of cancer, absence of cancer or sun                exposure, comprising solid support, nucleic acid                member array, device for holding the solid support,                device for extraction of mitochondrial DNA, device                for access to a database of mitochondrial DNA                sequences, primers, reagents and                instructions;
   a database containing mitochondrial DNA                sequences such as normal control sequences                associated with non-disease states, sequences                associated with interpopulation variations,                sequences associated with intrapopulation                variations, or sequences associated with a                predisposition to cancer, early detection of                cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                progression of cancer, absence of cancer, sun                exposure or aging;
   a method of detecting a deletion spanning                approximately nucleotides 10744 to 14124 of the                mtDNA genome, where the deletion is associated with                prostate cancer, in a subject having mtDNA;
   A nucleic acid primer 3.4 forward comprising                TAG ACT ACG TAC ATA CTA ACC CTA CTC CTA (SEQ ID No.                139);
   a nucleic acid primer 3.4 reverse comprising                GAG GTA GGA TTG GTG CTG T (SEQ ID No. 140);
   a method of monitoring a person for the                progression toward prostate cancer or progression                of prostate cancer, comprising providing a                biological sample from the subject; extracting DNA                from the biological sample; detecting the absence                or presence of deletions of the mtDNA; and                determining whether the deletions are associated                with normal interpopulation or intrapopulation                variations;
   a method for confirming or refuting a prostate                cancer biopsy test from a biopsy sample, comprising                obtaining normal tissue from a biopsy sample; and                detecting the absence or presence of a mtDNA                deletion of approximately 3379 base pairs in the                normal tissue;
   a method for three-dimensional prostate tumor                mapping, comprising obtaining sextant needle biopsy                samples; and detecting the absence or presence of a                mtDNA deletion of approximately 3379 base pairs in                each of the sextant samples;
   a mitochondrial deletion spanning                approximately nucleotides 10744-14124 of the mtDNA                genome for use in diagnosing prostate cancer;
   a method for monitoring the long term safety                of clinical UV phototherapy regimes, comprising                providing a biological sample from the subject; and                detecting the presence of a deletion spanning                approximately nucleotides 547-4443 in the minor arc                of the mtDNA genome; and
   a method for a sensitive detection of a                rearrangement in a DNA sample, comprising providing                a DNA sample comprising or suspected of comprising                a rearrangement; providing a primer or a probe                which spans the newly formed junction created by                the rearrangement; and detecting the rearrangement                by amplifying or probing the junction.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a histogram showing the                number of mutations at nucleotide position in                mitochondrial DNA from patients with prostate                cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The detecting method                  further comprises determining whether the                  deletion is associated with normal                  interpopulation or intrapopulation variations, or                  whether the deletion is associated with a                  predisposition to cancer, early detection of                  cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                  progression of cancer, absence of cancer, sun                  exposure or aging by: comparing the mtDNA of the                  biological sample to a database containing data                  of interpopulation and intrapopulation                  variations, and deletions associated with a                  predisposition to cancer, early detection of                  cancer, genesis of cancer, presence of cancer,                  progression of cancer, absence of cancer, sun                  exposure or aging; determining total mutation                  load of the biological sample; and comparing the                  cycle threshold of normal interpopulation or                  intrapopulation mtDNA and mtDNA which may                  comprise the deletion. It further includes                  determining the mutation load in the mtDNA of the                  biological sample and determining the identity of                  the deletion in the mtDNA of the biological                  sample. The step of detecting the presence of                  deletions is sequencing the mtDNA; amplifying                  mtDNA; denaturing HPLC; hybridization to                  microarrays, gene chips or biochips; molecular                  marker analysis; and/or detecting a fluorescence                  trace upon amplification. The malignancy or sun                  exposure is determined if the deletion is                  detected at a cycle threshold of 20-60                  (preferably 25-35) cycles. The deletion can be in                  the range of 3000 to 4000 (preferably 3379) base                  pairs. It deletes all or part of base pairs                  between 10744 and 14124. The step of amplifying                  is carried out by PCR using fluorescent labeled                  probe or fluorescent dye. The method for                  monitoring the progression toward prostate cancer                  or progression of prostate cancer further                  comprises monitoring the subject at successive                  time periods for an increase in deletions                  associated with prostate cancer, or an increase                  in the number of mitochondrial genomes having                  deletions associated with prostate cancer.Preferred Sample: The biological sample is                  non-involved tissue, distant benign tissue,                  adjacent benign tissue, atypical tissue,                  precursor lesions, histologically abnormal                  tissue, and malignant tissue, prostate massage                  fluid, urine, or post- digital rectal exam                  urine.Preferred Components: The mitochondrial DNA                  comprises the entire mitochondrial genome. The                  solid support is disposable chip. The deletion                  comprises genes encoding NADH dehydrogenase                  subunit 4L, NADH dehydrogenase subunit 4, NADH                  dehydrogenase subunit 5, tRNA histidine,                  tRNAserine2, and tRNA leucine2.

AU MITRA P
AE LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP (LOCK-C)
GA 2007716531
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves recording two series of infrared (IR) images of an area of tissue and skin (100) in respective bands of IR wavelengths. The two series of images are converted into two sets of thermal images having subareas. Two sets of average temperature values are determined for each subarea from the respective set of thermal images. Two radiance measurements are taken and correlated with respective bands of IR wavelengths of a healthy tissue. The average temperature values are correlated and analyzed for each subarea.
   USE - Used for detecting a diseased/cancerous tissue e.g. cancerous lesion (claimed), of a patient, in the field of breast cancer detection.
   ADVANTAGE - The method allows reliable detection of diseased or cancerous tissue even in the presence of skin tone variations such as birthmarks, tattoos and freckles. The method requires lower IR imager sensitivity, thus increasing manufacturability and cost of an IR imager, and hence providing greater accessibility to cancer screening and detection.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for an apparatus for detecting a diseased tissue, comprising an imager for recording two series of infrared images.
