TI Assessing malignancy of skin lesions used for            diagnosing skin cancer by extracting features from test            histopathology images of lesions, inputting scores into            machine learning architecture and generating malignancy            determination of lesion.
AU RATNER N
   SHEA C
   SHACHAF C
   SHACHAF A
   MANBECK K
   FLORELL S
AE ORLUCENT INC (ORLU-Non-standard)
GA 2025B0836K
AB    NOVELTY - Method for assessing malignancy of one or more                skin lesions involves (a) extracting one or more                predetermined features from one or more test                histopathology images of the one or more skin                lesions, (b) using a first machine learning                architecture, determining one or more scores for                each of the one or more predetermined features from                the one or more test histopathology images, (c)                inputting the one or more scores for each of the                one or more predetermined features into a second                machine learning architecture and (d) based on the                one or more scores for each of the one or more                predetermined features, generating a malignancy                determination of the one or more skin lesions using                the second machine learning architecture.
   USE - The method or system is useful for assessing                malignancy of one or more skin lesions which is                used for diagnosing skin cancer, preferably                melanoma, high grade atypia, or melanoma in situ                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The early detection and accurate diagnosis of                skin cancer are crucial for successful treatment                and improved patient outcomes.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   ystem configured to implement the                above-mentioned method or to train an untrained or                partially untrained machine learning algorithm or                predictive model; and
   ystem for assessing malignancy of one or more                skin lesions.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: The one or more skin                  lesions comprise one or more melanocytic                  neoplasms. The first machine learning                  architecture comprises an encoder. The first                  machine learning architecture comprises a first                  neural network. The first machine learning                  architecture comprises a transformer. The second                  machine learning architecture comprises a second                  neural network. The first machine learning                  architecture comprises a first neural network and                  the second machine learning architecture                  comprises a second neural network. The second                  neural network comprises several convolutional                  layers that gradually increase a receptive field                  and outlets leading to several feed-forward                  networks for each convolutional layer of several                  convolutional layers. Each feed-forward network                  of several feed-forward networks is responsible                  for estimating a specific feature. Each                  convolutional layer used as an input to each                  feed- forward network matches an approximate                  receptive field corresponding to an approximate                  scale of a specific feature. An input to the                  first machine learning architecture comprises a                  concatenated tensor, where the concatenated                  tensor comprises a concatenation of a                  segmentation map of cells that appear in the one                  or more test histopathology images with the one                  or more test histopathology images. Preferred                  Method: The segmentation map of cells is                  generated using a vision transformer. A                  predetermined feature of the one or more                  predetermined features comprises a cytology                  feature, an architecture feature and a host                  response feature. The architecture feature                  comprises symmetry of a lesion of the one or more                  skin lesions. The symmetry of the lesion is                  determined by extent and/or location of a                  junctional component with respect an intradermal                  component, size of one or more nests, and/or                  extent and/or location of inflammatory                  infiltrate. The symmetry of the lesion is not                  assessed together with any cytopathologic                  features. A grade for the symmetry of the lesion                  is determined to be 0+ (comprising high                  symmetry), 1+ (comprising moderate symmetry), 2+                  (comprising low symmetry), or 3+ (comprising                  minimal symmetry). The architecture feature                  comprises circumscription of a lesion of the one                  or more skin lesions. The circumscription of the                  lesion involves identifying one or more lateral                  borders of the lesion. The method involves                  identifying of the one or more lateral borders of                  the lesion by identifying one or more lateral                  borders of the lesion that end with a discrete                  nest of at least two cells together. The method                  involves identifying of the one or more lateral                  borders of the lesion by identifying one or more                  lateral borders of the lesion comprising clearly                  demarcated melanin. A grade for the                  circumscription of the lesion is determined to be                  0+ (where at least 4 borders appear                  well-circumscribed), 1+ (where 2 to 3 borders                  appear well-circumscribed), 2+ (where 1 border                  appears well-circumscribed), or 3+ (where 0                  borders appear well- circumscribed). The                  architecture feature comprises cohesion of a                  lesion of the one or more skin lesions. The                  cohesion of the lesion is determined by assessing                  a tendency of nests in the lesion to be composed                  of tightly aggregated melanocytes, where each                  nest is comprised of one or more melanocytes. The                  cohesion of the lesion is determined by assessing                  a percentage of the nests in the lesion in which                  at least half of the one or more melanocytes in                  each nest are tightly aggregated. A grade for the                  cohesion of the lesion is determined to be 0+                  (where at least 75% of the nests in the lesion                  have at least half of the one or more melanocytes                  in each nest tightly aggregated), 1+ (where at                  least 50-75% of the nests in the lesion have at                  least half of the melanocytes in each nest                  tightly aggregated), 2+ (where at least 25-50% of                  the nests in the lesion have at least half of the                  melanocytes in each nest tightly aggregated), or                  3+ (where 0-25% of the nests in the lesion have                  at least half of the melanocytes in each nest                  tightly aggregated). The architecture feature                  comprises confluence of a lesion of the one or                  more skin lesions. The confluence of the lesion                  is determined by identifying a dermal-epidermal                  junction of the lesion. The confluence of the                  lesion is determined by assessing a percentage of                  the dermal-epidermal junction of the lesion in                  which one or more melanocytes in the lesion                  appear to run together or touch one another. A                  grade for the confluence of the lesion is                  determined to be 0+ (where 0-25% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction of the lesion comprises                  melanocytes that appear to run together or touch                  one another), 1+ (where at least 25-50% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction of the lesion comprises                  melanocytes that appear to run together or touch                  one another), 2+ (where at least 50-75% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction of the lesion comprises                  melanocytes that appear to run together or touch                  one another), or 3+ (where at least 75% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction of the lesion comprises                  melanocytes that appear to run together or touch                  one another). A predetermined feature of the one                  or more predetermined features is graded globally                  for an entire lesion. The architecture feature                  comprises suprabasal/pagetoid spread of a lesion                  of the one or more skin lesions. The                  suprabasal/pagetoid spread of the lesion is                  determined by assessing a presence in the lesion                  of one or more melanocytes above an epidermal                  basal layer in at least two high-power fields.                  The suprabasal/pagetoid spread of the lesion is                  assessed in a central third of the lesion and in                  remaining peripheral regions. A grade for the                  suprabasal/pagetoid spread of the lesion is                  determined to be 0+ (suprabasal/pagetoid spread                  absent), 1+ (suprabasal/pagetoid spread present                  at a center of the lesion only), 2+                  (suprabasal/pagetoid spread present at 1-2                  peripheries of the lesion), or 3+                  (suprabasal/pagetoid spread present at at-least 3                  peripheries of the lesion). The architecture                  feature comprises single- cell/lentiginous spread                  of a lesion of the one or more skin lesions. The                  single-cell/lentiginous spread of the lesion is                  determined to be a tendency of melanocytes at an                  epidermal basal layer to be arranged as                  individual cells rather than in nests. The                  single-cell/lentiginous spread of the lesion is                  determined to be a percentage of a                  dermal-epidermal junction in which the lesion is                  comprised mainly of single cells rather than                  nests. A grade for the single- cell/lentiginous                  spread of the lesion is determined to be 0+                  (where 0 to 25% of the dermal-epidermal junction                  is comprised mainly of single cells), 1+ (where                  at least 25% to 50% of the dermal-epidermal                  junction is comprised mainly of single cells), 2+                  (where at least 50% to 75% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction is comprised mainly of                  single cells), or 3+ (where at least 75% of the                  dermal-epidermal junction is comprised mainly of                  single cells). The cytology feature comprises a                  nuclear size feature. The nuclear size feature                  comprises a comparison of an average melanocyte                  nucleus size for a lesion of the one or more skin                  lesions with an average basal keratinocyte                  nucleus size for the lesion. A grade for the                  nuclear size feature for the lesion is determined                  to be 0+ (where the average melanocyte nucleus                  size is 1x or less the average basal keratinocyte                  nucleus size), 1+ (where the average melanocyte                  nucleus size is 1.0-1.5x the average basal                  keratinocyte nucleus size), 2+ (where the average                  melanocyte nucleus size is 1.5-2.0x the average                  basal keratinocyte nucleus size), or 3+ (where                  the average melanocyte nucleus size is at least                  2.0x the average basal keratinocyte nucleus                  size). The cytology feature comprises a cell size                  feature. The cell size feature comprises a                  comparison of an average melanocyte cell size for                  a lesion of the one or more skin lesions with an                  average basal keratinocyte cell size for the                  lesion. A grade for the cell size feature for the                  lesion is determined to be 0+ (where the average                  melanocyte cell size is 1x or less the average                  basal keratinocyte cell size), 1+ (where the                  average melanocyte cell size is 1.0-1.5x the                  average basal keratinocyte cell size), 2+ (where                  the average melanocyte cell size is 1.5-2.0x the                  average basal keratinocyte cell size), or 3+                  (where the average melanocyte cell size is at                  least 2.0x the average basal keratinocyte cell                  size). The determination of the grade for the                  cell size feature for the lesion is determined to                  be a highest grade seen in at least 50% of                  melanocytes in two 40x fields. The cytology                  feature comprises a nuclear pleomorphism feature.                  A determination of the nuclear pleomorphism                  feature comprises determining a percentage of                  neoplastic melanocytes in a lesion of the one or                  more skin lesions with variation in nuclear size,                  nuclear shape, or both. A grade for the nuclear                  pleomorphism feature for the lesion is determined                  to be 0+ (fewer than 5% of the neoplastic                  melanocytes in the lesion having variation in                  nuclear size, nuclear shape, or both), 1+ (5-20%                  of the neoplastic melanocytes in the lesion                  having variation in nuclear size, nuclear shape,                  or both), 2+ (at least 20% to 50% of the                  neoplastic melanocytes in the lesion having                  variation in nuclear size, nuclear shape, or                  both), or 3+ (at least 50% of the neoplastic                  melanocytes in the lesion having variation in                  nuclear size, nuclear shape, or both). The                  cytology feature comprises a nuclear chromatism                  feature. The nuclear chromatism feature comprises                  an assessment of an average neoplastic melanocyte                  nuclear chromatism for a lesion of the one or                  more skin lesions with an average normal                  melanocyte nuclear chromatism for the lesion. A                  grade for the nuclear chromatism feature for the                  lesion is determined to be 0+ (normal), 1+                  (dispersed), 2+ (coarsely granular or with                  peripheral condensation), or 3+ (hyper- or                  irregularly-chromatic). The host response feature                  comprises a lymphocytic infiltrate feature. A                  grade for the lymphocytic infiltrate feature is                  determined for a lesion of the one or more skin                  lesions to be 0+ (lymphocytic infiltrate absent                  to minimal), 1+ (mild lymphocytic infiltrate                  present), 2+ (moderate lymphocytic infiltrate                  present), or 3+ (dense lymphocytic infiltrate                  present). A lymphocytic infiltrate feature of 0+                  for a lesion comprises few, if any, perivascular                  lymphocytes in a superficial dermis of the                  lesion, where the perivascular lymphocytes are                  not necessarily in proximity to a melanocytic                  neoplasm of the lesion. A lymphocytic infiltrate                  feature of 0+ for a lesion comprises compound or                  intradermal melanocytic nevus that is not                  dysplastic. A lymphocytic infiltrate feature of                  0+ for a lesion is not readily identifiable at                  scanning magnification. A lymphocytic infiltrate                  feature of 1+ for a lesion comprises mild numbers                  of perivascular lymphocytes in a superficial                  dermis of the lesion, where the perivascular                  lymphocytes are in proximity to a melanocytic                  neoplasm of the lesion. A lymphocytic infiltrate                  feature of 1+ for a lesion comprises dysplastic                  melanocytic nevus. A lymphocytic infiltrated                  feature of 1+ for a lesion is identifiable but                  not obvious at scanning magnification. A                  lymphocytic infiltrate feature of 2+ for a lesion                  comprises moderate numbers of perivascular                  lymphocytes in superficial and/or deeper dermis                  in a patchy distribution, in proximity to a                  melanocytic neoplasm of the lesion. A lymphocytic                  infiltrate feature of 2+ for a lesion comprises                  malignant melanoma with intermediate-stage                  regression. A lymphocytic infiltrate feature of                  2+ for a lesion is obvious at scanning                  magnification. A lymphocytic infiltrate feature                  of 3+ for a lesion comprises a nodular/band-like                  infiltrate of perivascular lymphocytes in                  superficial and/or deep dermis, filling a                  papillary dermis, percolating among one or more                  neoplastic melanocytes, and/or obscuring one or                  more borders of a melanocytic neoplasm. A                  lymphocytic infiltrate feature of 3+ for a lesion                  comprises a halo melanocytic nevus. A lymphocytic                  infiltrate feature of 3+ for a lesion is                  prominently observed at scanning magnification.                  The host response feature comprises a fibrosis                  feature. A grade for the fibrosis feature is                  determined for a lesion of the one or more skin                  lesions to be 0+ (fibrosis absent), 1+ (mild                  fibrosis), 2+ (moderate fibrosis), or 3+ (dense                  fibrosis). The host response feature comprises a                  neovascularization feature. A grade for the                  neovascularization feature is determined for a                  lesion of the one or more skin lesions to be 0+                  (neovascularization absent), 1+ (focal                  neovascularization), 2+ (moderate                  neovascularization), or 3+ (extensive                  neovascularization). The predetermined features                  of the one or more lesions in the one or more                  histopathology images are chosen from symmetry,                  circumscription, cohesion, confluence,                  suprabasal/pagetoid spread,                  single-cell/lentiginous spread, nuclear size,                  cell size, nuclear pleomorphism, nucleolar                  prominence, nuclear chromatism, lymphocytic                  infiltrate, fibrosis, and neovascularization. The                  predetermined features of the one or more lesions                  in the one or more histopathology images are                  chosen from suprabasal/pagetoid spread, symmetry,                  nuclear size, nuclear pleomorphism, nuclear                  chromatism, fibrosis, and confluence. The one or                  more histopathology images are acquired from                  imaging one or more biopsies of the one or more                  skin lesions. The first machine learning                  architecture or the second machine learning                  architecture is trained using training annotated                  histopathology images from one or more training                  skin lesions, where the training annotated                  histopathology images comprise annotated scores                  for the pre- determined features, and the                  annotated scores were provided by one or more                  clinicians or technicians. The one or more                  clinicians or technicians comprise pathologists,                  dermatologists, oncologists, or laboratory                  technicians. The one or more training skin                  lesions have been identified as malignant or                  benign by the one or more clinicians or                  technicians. The one or more training skin                  lesions have been identified as concerning or not                  concerning. The malignancy determination is a                  numerical output indicating a likelihood of the                  one or more skin lesions being malignant or                  benign. The malignancy determination is a                  numerical output indicating a likelihood of a                  lesion of the one or more skin lesions being                  concerning or not concerning. The concerning                  lesion conditions comprise high grade atypia,                  melanoma in situ, or melanoma. The lesion                  conditions that are not concerning comprise no                  atypia or low atypia. The one or more                  histopathology images or one or more training                  annotated histopathology images are produced by                  processing a tissue specimen of the one or more                  skin lesions through fixation, embedding,                  sectioning, and staining, for enabling                  microscopic examination of the tissue specimen.                  The tissue specimen is placed on a glass slide                  and stained using hematoxylin and eosin staining,                  for producing stained slides that highlight                  different structures within the tissue specimen.                  The immunohistochemistry staining methods are                  used to identify specific cellular components in                  the tissue specimen. The immunohistochemistry                  staining methods comprise staining for sex                  determining region Y (SRY)box 10 (SOX10), melan 1                  (MART1), cluster of differentiation (CD)3 and/or                  CD45. The immunohistochemistry staining methods                  are used in combination with the hematoxylin and                  eosin staining to produce multiple image inputs                  to the first machine learning architecture for a                  single skin lesion of the one or more skin                  lesions. The stained slides are scanned, for                  producing scanned slides. The scanned slides are                  digitally provided to one or more clinicians or                  technicians to identify one or more predetermined                  features, for producing one or more training                  annotated histopathology images. The scanned                  slides are processed automatically using the                  first machine learning architecture, for                  producing one or more test histopathology images                  with one or more predetermined features. The                  malignancy determination identifies a lesion as                  having a high likelihood to progress to skin                  cancer or not having a high likelihood to                  progress to skin cancer. The lesion identified as                  having the high likelihood to progress to skin                  cancer comprises high grade atypia, melanoma in                  situ, or melanoma. The lesion identified as not                  having a high likelihood to progress to skin                  cancer comprises no atypia or low atypia. The                  malignancy determination further comprises a                  measure of agreement between clinicians or                  technicians. The predetermined features comprise                  architecture features, cytology features, host                  response features, or their combination. The                  architecture features comprise: symmetry,                  circumscription, cohesion, confluence, suprabasal                  spread, and/or single- cell/lentiginous spread.                  The cytology features comprise: nuclear size,                  cell size, nuclear pleomorphism, nucleolar                  prominence, and/or nuclear chromatism. The host                  response features comprise: lymphocytic                  infiltrate, fibrosis, and/or neovascularization.                  The measure of agreement is used to adjust or                  tune the predetermined features before input into                  the second machine learning algorithm. The                  predetermined features are measured on a scale of                  0-3. The localization of image regions                  contributing to grades of the one or more                  predetermined features is used to provide                  additional interpretability. The localization of                  the image regions is obtained using a visual                  explanation method. The method further involves                  storing the one or more test histopathology                  images locally at a participating data source,                  where the participating data source comprises a                  healthcare provider. The method further involves                  training the first machine learning architecture                  and the second machine learning architecture on                  the locally-stored test histopathology images                  only. Only model updates, and not an entirety of                  the locally-stored test histopathology images,                  are sent back to a central server. The model                  updates are aggregated at the central server to                  create a global model that learns from all                  participating data sources. The method further                  involves augmenting the one or more test                  histopathology images with subject metadata. The                  subject metadata includes age, gender, hair                  color, density of moles, number of sunburns,                  density of sunburns, density of freckles on arms,                  and level of inflammation.

TI Method for classifying lesions e.g. macular benign            skin lesions, as malignant or benign, involves            determining malignancy probability that lesion is            malignant, and classifying lesion based on malignancy            probability.

   KRISHNA S
   GODOY S E
   RAMIREZ D A

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves receiving temporal                sequence of thermal images of an area of skin                representing thermal recovery of the area of skin.                A temporal profile of thermal recovery is generated                based on temporal sequence of thermal images.                Temporal statistical properties of the temporal                profile are analyzed. Malignancy probability that a                lesion is malignant is determined based on analysis                of the temporal profile by extracting statistical                features based on continuous-time stochastic                signals in the sequence of thermal images. The                lesion is classified based on the malignancy                probability.
   USE - Method for classifying lesions e.g. dysplastic                nevus, papular benign skin lesions and macular                benign skin lesions, as malignant or benign for                detecting skin cancer of a patient by applying                statistical decision theory and image-processing                techniques to dynamic infrared image                sequences.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables utilizing a physical model                for warming-up process referred to as                thermal-recovery process represented by the thermal                image sequence in conjunction with automated                mathematical decision-making algorithm to identify                lesions as malignant or benign. AB    NOVELTY - The method involves scanning a human skin                surface according to an ultrasonic wave of a preset                frequency, and obtaining an M-type ultrasonic image                (S101), where the M-type ultrasonic image is                provided with skin tissue fluid position                information. The obtained M-type ultrasonic image                is converted (S102) based on a preset gray scale                image pixel value to output. A region of interest                in the gray map is extracted (S103) based on a                rectangular area frame of preset size. A judgment                is made to check whether a pixel value in the                region of interest is less than a third preset                pixel value. The pixel value is taken (S105) as                foreground if the pixel value in the region of                interest is less than the third preset pixel value.                A white pixel in the binary image is detected                according to a spot detection algorithm.    USE - Method for positioning skin tissue fluid in a                human body based on ultrasonic detection for early                screening and diagnosis of cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables quickly detecting the                position of high skin tissue fluid content by                ultrasonic detecting the distribution of tissue                fluid in the skin, and identifying and locating the                tissue fluid based on the extracted region of                interest, thus improving the tissue fluid                extraction efficiency.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) a                skin tissue fluid positioning system based on                ultrasonic detection; (2) an electronic device for                positioning skin tissue fluid in a human body based                on ultrasonic detection; (3) a computer readable                storage medium for storing a computer program for                positioning skin tissue fluid in a human body based                on ultrasonic detection.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow diagram illustrating                a skin tissue fluid positioning method based on                ultrasonic detection. (Drawing includes non-English                language text).

   Step for converting the obtained M-type                ultrasonic image based on a preset gray scale image                pixel value to output (S102)
   Step for extracting a region of interest in                the gray map based on the rectangular area frame of                the preset size (S103)
   Step for judging whether one pixel value in                the region of interest is less than a third preset                pixel value (S104)
   Step for taking the pixel value as foreground                if the pixel value in the region of interest is                less than the third preset pixel value                (S105)
   Step for detecting the white pixel in the                binary image according to the spot detection                algorithm and calculating the area of the white                pixel area to output the image of the skin tissue                fluid (S106)

   KONINK PHILIPS ELECTRONICS NV (PHIG-C)

GA 2009J55114
AB    NOVELTY - An encoded signal containing photoacoustic                imaging data of target blood vessel is obtained                using photoacoustic imaging system, and encoded                signal is decoded. The decoded signal is                demodulated and filtered using demodulator and low                pass filter, respectively, to generate base-band                signal. The base-band signal is passed to a wall                filter to generate an uncluttered signal.    USE - Blood flow detection method for treating                disease such as rheumatoid arthritis, age-related                macular degeneration and endometriosis.    ADVANTAGE - Reduced blood flow rates can be detected with                enhanced signal-to-noise (SNR) ratio performance,                reduced aliasing effect and reduced potential for                flash artifacts from tissue motion while enabling                skin line elimination.

TI Method of detection of breast cancer involves            comparison of skin temp. in two areas using fusible            sensors.
AU SAGI Z L
AE BCSI LAB INC (BCSI-Non-standard)
GA 1986331493
AB    NOVELTY - The method of early detection of abnormalities                in the body involves comparison of the skin                temperature of an area on one side of the body with                that of a corresponding area on the other side. It                comprises applying to the areas two temperature                sensors, each having temperature indicators which                melt at predetermined temperatures to display a                change in appearance. The indicators in each sensor                are arranged in a pattern to form an array covering                the area of skin of temperature to be sensed.
The patterns of the indicators of the arrays                are comparable and the several indicators in one                array have melting temperatures different from each                other but identical with comparable indicators in                the other array to facilitate temperature                comparison of the two areas. The indicators are                brought into conforming contiguous contact with the                area by pressing the indicators against by applying                pressure through a backing comprising a thickness                of a flexible compressible material.

TI System for detecting and classifying an irregular            form of skin lesion due to skin cancer by            characterizing symmetry or asymmetry using image            processing techniques and machine learning algorithms,            comprises image capturing device to capture skin lesion            images of subject.
AU REEJA S R
   SHAIK R
AE UNIV VIT AP (VELR-C)
GA 2024033515
AB    NOVELTY - The system (100) comprises an image capturing                device (104) to capture skin lesion images (106) of                the subject (102), and a control unit has multiple                modules to process the captured images. The                database stores multiple datasets, where processor                is communicatively coupled with memory storing                instructions that receive an image of the skin                lesion from the subject for analysis. The captured                image is preprocessed to resize and remove                artifacts, and apply segmentation of the image to                extract features to compare with the database                images. The symmetry and asymmetry of the image are                determined by drawing multiple lines to find                centroid of the skin lesion and calculate                midpoints. The mean deviation error is computed                between straight line and untouched midpoints, and                apply multiple machine learning classifier to                classify symmetric skin lesion (116) and asymmetric                skin lesion (118) from the skin of the subject. The                image capturing device is a high resolution                camera.
   USE - System for detecting and classifying an                irregular form of skin lesion due to skin cancer by                characterizing symmetry or asymmetry using image                processing techniques and machine learning                algorithms.
   ADVANTAGE - The system provides a simple, most accurate,                cost-effective, system to obtain a better framework                that can significantly improve the detection and                classification of irregular form of skin lesion                characterizing symmetry or asymmetry shapes of a                subject for an early and better treatment, and                ensures to improve accuracy in detection and                classification of skin lesions, and provides a                framework for identification of the centroid of the                lesion shape through the utilization of the                bounding box technique.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for classification of skin lesion of a                subject.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of a system                for classification of skin lesion of a                subject.

AE DERMASENSOR INC (DERM-Non-standard)

GA 2022E6244K
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves receiving a signal                comprising an elastic scattering spectrum resulting                from illuminating a skin lesion sample at a high                output setting, and determining whether the                received signal has an intensity greater than a                saturation threshold associated with optical                detection sensor. The elastic scattering spectrum                resulting from illuminating the skin lesion sample                at the high output setting is stored in response to                determining that the received signal has intensity                greater than saturation threshold. The skin lesion                sample is illuminated with second pulse from light                source adjusted to low output setting in response                to determining that the received signal does not                have intensity greater than the saturation                threshold. A signal comprising an elastic                scattering spectrum resulting from illuminating the                skin lesion sample at the low output setting is                received, and the elastic scattering spectrum                resulting from illuminating the skin lesion sample                at the low output setting is stored.
   USE - Method for dynamically calibrating intensity                of light source in system for evaluating skin                lesion using elastic-scattering spectroscopy (ESS)                system (claimed) for non-invasive detection of skin                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables dynamically calibrating                intensity of a light source in a system for                evaluating a skin lesion using elastic-scattering                spectroscopy (ESS) in an effective manner.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for an                elastic-scattering spectroscopy system for                non-invasive detection of skin cancer.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows the schematic diagram of                the lighting system for performing ESS.

TI Automated detection of cancer cells and            precursors, by simultaneous detection of two markers            and evaluation of combined signal intensities.
AU HENNIG G
   WIRTZ R
   BOHMANN K
   SCHOEPPER B
   SCHOPPER B
   HENNING G
AE BAYER AG (FARB-C)
   BAYER AG (FARB-C)
   BAYER AG (FARB-C)
   HENNING G (HENN-Individual)
   WIRTZ R (WIRT-Individual)
   BOHMANN K (BOHM-Individual)
   SCHOPPER B (SCHO-Individual)
   BAYER AG (FARB-C)
   SIEMENS HEALTHCARE DIAGNOSTICS INC (SIEI-C)
GA 2002521730
AB    NOVELTY - Automatable method for identifying cancer                cells and their precursors in which at least two                markers in a cell or tissue sample are detected                simultaneously, and the signal intensities are                combined and evaluated.
   USE - The method is specifically used to detect                tumors of breast, lung, cervix, colon, skin and                prostate, particularly by 'reflex testing'.
   ADVANTAGE - Simultaneous detection of two or more markers                improves the specificity of diagnosis, compared                with detecting a single marker. The method allows                early detection and may identify the origin of                metastases; also it is rapid, making it suitable                for screening.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                kit for the process.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Process: The automated information                  processing is linked to an expert system that                  consolidates the image information to produce a                  suggested diagnosis. Quantitative detection of                  the markers is by analysis of chromogenic                  reactions or fluorescent signals in particular                  regions of the tissue section, so that mixed                  colors (or the spatial proximity of individual                  colors) provide more information than use of a                  single color.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Markers: These are generally                  oncogenes, or tumor repressor, apoptosis,                  proliferation, repair or viral genes. More than                  20 pairs of markers are specified, e.g. Her2/neu                  with any of Ki67, p53, bcl-2 or MN; or p16 with                  p53 or epidermal growth factor receptor.
   EXAMPLE - A conventionally treated biopsy section, on a                silanized glass slide in a commercial staining                instrument, was treated to inactivate endogenous                peroxidase, treated to block non-specific binding                (goat serum), reacted with commercial monoclonal                antibody (Ab1) specific for Her2/neu, reacted with                rabbit anti-mouse antibody (Ab2), reactive with                Ab1, reacted with mouse anti-rabbit antibody (Ab3),                reactive with Ab2, reacted with biotinylated                'multilink' antibody, reactive with all of Ab1-3,                reacted with streptavidin conjugated to horseradish                peroxidase and reacted with                diaminobenzidine-hydrogen peroxide to form a brown                precipitate. Essentially the same procedure was                repeated using a first antibody directed against                p53, but here a conjugate of streptavidin and                alkaline phosphatase was used and color was                developed from Fast Red and naphthol. Nuclei were                stained with hematoxylin and the slides were                stained with 'Bluing Reagent'. The slides were                examined in a computer-controlled fluorescence                microscope. The individual color values (red and                brown) were determined and compared with specific                thresholds. Samples are scored as 'diseased' if                more than one threshold value is exceeded.

TI Multifunctional nanomaterial for detecting and            treating cancer comprises a nanorod comprising a noble            metal and exhibiting surface plasmon resonance            absorption in the near-infrared spectrum, and an            up-conversion phosphor.
AU PARK W
   FLAIG T
   YANG X
   SU L S
   EMOTO K
   SU L
AE UNIV COLORADO (COLS-C)
   UNIV COLORADO (COLS-C)
   UNIV COLORADO (COLS-C)
   UNIV COLORADO (COLS-C)
GA 2013M11030
AB    NOVELTY - A multifunctional nanomaterial comprises (i) a                nanorod comprising a noble metal, where the nanorod                exhibits surface plasmon resonance absorption in                the near-infrared spectrum; (ii) an up-conversion                phosphor that absorbs infrared light and emits                visible luminescence; and optionally (iii) a                biomolecule targeting moiety.
   USE - The multifunctional nanomaterial is used for                treating cancer, and for the in vivo detection of                cancer cells. The cancer is selected from bladder                cancer, a skin cancer, and oral cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - Improved detection and treatment methods of                cancers, including bladder cancer, are                provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method of treating cancer in a subject;                and
   a method for the in vivo detection of cancer                cells in a subject by (a) administering to the                subject multifunctional nanomaterials above, where                the biomolecule targeting moiety selectively binds                to cancer cells; (b) subjecting the cancer cells to                infrared light, where the up-conversion phosphor of                the multifunctional nanomaterial absorbs the                infrared light and emits visible luminescence; and                (c) detecting the visible luminescence of the                up-conversion phosphor, thus detecting the cancer                cells in the subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Multifunctional Nanomaterial: The                  surface plasmon resonance of the noble metal                  nanorod enhances the efficiency of frequency                  up-conversion of the up-conversion phosphor. The                  enhancement of up-conversion efficiency is by up                  to about one order of magnitude. The noble metal                  is selected from gold and silver and their                  combination. The nanorod is a gold nanorod. The                  nanorod has an aspect ratio of 3.5-6.5,                  preferably 5.0. The surface plasmon resonance                  absorption maximum is 800-1300 nm, preferably 980                  nm. The up-conversion phosphor comprises                  optically active donor and acceptor ions embedded                  in a host material. The donor and acceptor ions                  are rare earth ions. The host material is                  selected from oxides, fluorides, chlorides,                  oxyfluorides and oxychlorides. The up-conversion                  phosphor is selected from NaYF 4:Yb 3+,Er 3+, SrF                  2:Er 3+, YF 3:Yb 3+,Tb 3+, YbPO 4:Yb 3+, CaF 2:Eu                  2+, YF 3:Yb 3+,Tm 3+, NaYF 4:Yb 3+,Tm 3+, Na 2Y                  3Fn:Yb 3+,Er 3+, YF 3:Yb 3+,Er 3+, SrCl 2:Yb                  3+and SrCl 2:Yb 3+,Tb 3+. The up-conversion                  phosphor absorbs infrared light with a wavelength                  of 800-1100 nm, preferably 980 nm. The                  biomolecule targeting moiety comprises an                  antibody, peptide, polypeptide, lipid, nucleic                  acid, carbohydrate, aptamer and a small organic                  molecule. The biomolecule targeting moiety                  comprises an antibody. The biomolecule targeting                  moiety comprises a monoclonal antibody. The                  antibody is a whole antibody that includes an F                  cregion. The antibody is an antibody fragment                  that does not include an F cregion, where the                  antibody fragment is a (Fab')2 fragment or Fab                  fragment. The biomolecule targeting moiety is an                  antibody that specifically binds a biomolecule                  expressed on the surface of a cancer cell                  selected from a bladder cancer cell, a skin                  cancer cell, and an oral cancer cell. The                  biomolecule expressed on the surface of a cancer                  cell is a growth factor receptor, where the                  growth factor receptor is the epidermal growth                  factor receptor. The antibody is a chimeric,                  humanized antibody. The antibody is cetuximab.                  The biomolecule targeting moiety is conjugated                  directly to the nanorod. The biomolecule                  targeting moiety is conjugated indirectly to the                  nanorod via a linker, where the linker comprises                  polyethylene glycol (PEG). Preferred Method:                  Treating cancer in a subject comprises (a)                  administering to the subject multifunctional                  nanomaterials above, where the biomolecule                  targeting moiety selectively binds to cancer                  cells; and (b) subjecting the cancer cells to a                  first intensity of near infrared light, where the                  up-conversion phosphor absorbs the near infrared                  light and emits visible luminescence that is                  detected, thus detecting the cancer cells; and                  (c) subjecting the detected cancer cells to a                  second intensity of near infrared light, where                  the nanorod of the multifunctional nanomaterial                  exhibits surface plasmon resonance absorbance of                  the near infrared light, causing an increase in                  the temperature of the nanorod, where the                  increase in temperature results in thermal                  ablation of the cancer cells bound to the                  multifunctional nanomaterials. The first                  intensity of near infrared light is less than the                  second intensity of near infrared light. The                  nanorod absorbs the first intensity of near                  infrared light and the surface plasmon resonance                  of the nanorod enhances the efficiency of                  frequency up-conversion of the up-conversion                  phosphor. Treating cancer in a subject comprises                  (a) administering to the subject multifunctional                  nanomaterials above, where the biomolecule                  targeting moiety selectively binds to cancer                  cells; (b) subjecting the cancer cells to near                  infrared light, where the up-conversion phosphor                  absorbs the near infrared light and emits visible                  luminescence that is detected, thus detecting the                  cancer cells where the nanorod of the                  multifunctional nanomaterial exhibits surface                  plasmon resonance absorbance of the near infrared                  light, causing an increase in the temperature of                  the nanorod, where the increase in temperature                  results in thermal ablation of the cancer cells                  bound to the multifunctional nanomaterials.                  Treating cancer in a subject comprises (a)                  administering to the subject multifunctional                  nanomaterials above, where the biomolecule                  targeting moiety selectively binds to cancer                  cells; and (b) subjecting the cancer cells to                  near infrared light, where the nanorod of the                  multifunctional nanomaterial exhibits surface                  plasmon resonance absorbance of the near infrared                  light, causing an increase in the temperature of                  the nanorod, where the increase in temperature                  results in thermal ablation of the cancer cells                  bound to the multifunctional nanomaterials.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None Given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - The assembly has an OCT unit that is provided                with an illumination beam and a collection beam. A                beam splitter (400) is configured to direct a                portion of light from sample to microscope imaging                optics and to direct another portion of light from                sample to OCT unit collection beam. The beam                splitter is further configured to direct                illumination beam from OCT unit to sample. A beam                forming unit is provided between OCT unit and beam                splitter. The beam forming unit is provided to form                illumination beam of the OCT unit.
   USE - Surgical microscope assembly for use during                cancer detection of staging skin, gastrointestinal,                and genitourinary tracts.

TI Heterogeneous breast phantom used in breast            imaging modalities for detection of early cancer and            lesions, comprises skin mimicking segment that having            polyvinyl alcohol and sugar, adipose tissue mimicking            segment having beeswax and agar and fibro-glandular            tissue mimicking segment having glycerol.
AU ALMOZAIN M
   ZAINALABEDIN M
   ALJABR A
   ALFARES B
   SALEH G
AE UNIV IMAM ABDULRAHMAN BIN FAISAL (UYIM-Non-standard)
GA 202492530H
AB    NOVELTY - Heterogeneous breast phantom comprises skin                mimicking segment comprising polyvinyl alcohol and                sugar, where polyvinyl alcohol and sugar are                present in skin mimicking segment in amounts of 4-6                and 27-35 wt.% and each relative to total weight of                skin mimicking segment, and adipose tissue                mimicking segment comprises beeswax and agar, where                beeswax is present in adipose tissue mimicking                segment in amount of 38-45 wt.% relative to total                weight of adipose tissue mimicking segment, and                fibro-glandular tissue mimicking segment comprises                glycerol, where glycerol is present in                fibro-glandular tissue mimicking segment in amount                of 10-15 wt.% relative to total weight of                fibro-glandular tissue mimicking segment and                pectoral muscle mimicking segment comprises sugar                and egg whites, where the sugar is present in                pectoral muscle mimicking segment in amount of                22-28 wt.%, and egg whites are present in an amount                of 2-8 wt.% relative to a total weight of pectoral                muscle mimicking segment.
   USE - Heterogeneous breast phantom used in various                breast imaging modalities for detection of early                cancer and lesions.
   ADVANTAGE - The heterogeneous breast phantom mimics the                anatomy and properties of real breast tissues when                screened with ionizing and nonionizing imaging                modalities.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Conditions: The skin mimicking,                  adipose tissue mimicking, fibro-glandular tissue                  mimicking, and the carcinoma mimicking segment                  each further comprise at least one type of                  scattering particles selected from the group of                  sodium chloride (NaCl), potassium chloride (KCl),                  aluminium oxide (Al2O3), and silicon carbide                  (SiC) particles. The adipose tissue mimicking                  segment comprises sodium chloride, deionized                  water, Triton (RTM: Nonionic surfactant)-X-100,                  safflower oil, beeswax, agar, silicon carbide,                  and potassium chloride.The adipose tissue                  mimicking segment comprises 0.21 wt.% sodium                  chloride, 11.64 wt.% deionized water, 10.58 wt.%                  Triton (RTM: Nonionic surfactant)-X-100, 33.32                  wt.% safflower oil, 42.31 wt.% beeswax, 0.74 wt.%                  agar, 0.52 wt.% silicon carbide, and 0.68 wt.%                  potassium chloride based on a total weight of the                  adipose tissue mimicking segment.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The heterogeneous                  breast phantom further comprises carcinoma                  mimicking segment which contains sugar. The                  segment further comprises water, vegetable oil,                  surfactant, and agar. The vegetable oil is                  safflower oil. The surfactant is a non-ionic                  surfactant. Preferred Conditions: The sugar is                  present in the carcinoma mimicking segment in an                  amount of 20-25 wt.% relative to a total weight                  of the carcinoma mimicking segment. The skin                  mimicking segment has an electron density (ne) of                  3.59E+23-3.61E+23 e/g and an effective atomic                  number (Zeff) of 7.2-7.3 where the adipose tissue                  mimicking segment has an electron density (ne) of                  3.17E+23-3.20E+23 e/g and an effective atomic                  number (Zeff) of 6.3-6.4, where the                  fibro-glandular tissue mimicking segment has an                  electron density (ne) of 3.15E+23-3.45E+23 e/g                  and an effective atomic number (Zeff) of 6.9-7.4,                  and the pectoral muscle mimicking segment has an                  electron density (ne) of 3.40E+23-3.5E+23 e/g and                  an effective atomic number (Zeff) of 8.1-8.3. The                  heterogeneous breast phantom stimulates the                  breast tissue under a medical imaging technique.                  The medical imaging technique is magnetic                  resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography scan                  (CT scan), or both. The adipose tissue mimicking                  segment has a mass attenuation coefficient                  approximately the same as or within 5% of mass                  attenuation coefficient of a real adipose breast                  tissue in an energy range of 10-150 KeV.

TI Patch for detection of breast abnormalities            comprises array of spaced-apart temp. indicators on            flexible heat-conductive web.
AU SAGI J L
AE BCSI LAB INC (BCSI-Non-standard)
GA 1987100805
AB    NOVELTY - Detection patch for use in early detection of                breast abnormalities comprises: (a) a flexible                heat-conductive web (W) having opposite surfaces,                (b) an array of spaced-apart temp. indicators                (T.I.) adjacent to each other on one surface of W,                each TI comprising a dye or pigment and a                temp.-sensitive substance (I) having a m.pt.                precisely different from the m.pt. of (I) in the                adjacent indicator, where each of the indicators                displays a permanent change in colour upon melting                of (I) and co-action with the dye or pigment, (c) a                transparent flexible layer (FL) overlying W and                sealed to one surface and (d) a backing web (BW) on                the other surface of W, BW being composed of a                flexible compressible material adapted to effect                conformal contiguous contact between the indicator                bearing surface of W and the breast skin when the                patch is applied in the breast-receiving cup of a                brassiere.
More specifically, W is made of aluminium foil                and (I) is a crystalline organic chemical.
   USE - The patch is used for visual detection of                breast cancer. The flexible conformable BW provides                additional padding which insures a more intimate                contact between the breast skin and the indicator                surface. The patch is readily adaptable for mass                screening and affords a rapid means whereby a                person can determine if she (or he) is afflicted                with breast cancer before undergoing a more                comprehensive examination.
   ADVANTAGE - The patch is used for visual detection of                breast cancer. The flexible conformable BW provides                additional padding which insures a more intimate                contact between the breast skin and the indicator                surface. The patch is readily adaptable for mass                screening and affords a rapid means whereby a                person can determine if she (or he) is afflicted                with breast cancer before undergoing a more                comprehensive examination.

TI Skin protection device against the sun useful in detecting and/or treating skin disorders e.g. cancer and its preliminary stages.
AU GUDMUNDSON F
   GUDMUNDSSON F
AE MEDEIKONOS AB (MEDE-Non-standard)
   MEDEIKONOS AB (MEDE-Non-standard)
   MEDEIKONOS AB (MEDE-Non-standard)
   MEDEIKONOS AB (MEDE-Non-standard)
GA 2000126710
AB    NOVELTY - A skin area is protected against light when detecting and/or treating skin disorders such as cancer and its preliminary stages by an opaque foil (1) forming a cavity (4) relative to the skin and having edges (3) engaging the skin.
   USE - The device is used as an application and protection device for applying compositions and/or compounds, with photoreactive substance, to the skin, and protecting the skin area against sunlight (claimed) before and after the detection procedure.
   ADVANTAGE - The skin protection device with a foil made of heat insulating material gives higher temperature in skin area treated resulting a better blood supply and contributes to the efficiency of the treatment. The foil ensures that no substance goes outside of the treated area.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The skin protection device comprises an opaque foil forming a cavity relative to the skin and having edges engaging the skin. The width of the edges of the skin is determined by the formula (I):
   (I) m greater than delta.ln(t.I0/Ddiffused);
   m = width of the edge;
   delta = penetration depth of the light in the skin;
   ln = natural logarithm;
   t = the time of the effect of the light;
   I0 = luminous intensity at the skin surface; and
   Ddiffused = the diffused energy dose which is allowed to reach the skin concerned.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - A figure showing the cross-sectional view of the skin protection device.
   Casing or foil (1)
   Edges (3)
   Cavity (4).
EA    (EP1089786-A1)   NOVELTY - A skin area is protected against light when detecting and/or treating skin disorders such as cancer and its preliminary stages by an opaque foil (1) forming a cavity (4) relative to the skin and having edges (3) engaging the skin.
   USE - The device is used as an application and protection device for applying compositions and/or compounds, with photoreactive substance, to the skin, and protecting the skin area against sunlight (claimed) before and after the detection procedure.
   ADVANTAGE - The skin protection device with a foil made of heat insulating material gives higher temperature in skin area treated resulting a better blood supply and contributes to the efficiency of the treatment. The foil ensures that no substance goes outside of the treated area.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Foil: The foil is formable and consists of metal on plastic, opaque plastic or preferably a heat-insulating material.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Foil: The foil is made of metal.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Composition: The skin applied compound and/or composition contains delta-aminolevulinic acid and the photoreactive substance is photoporphyrin IX.

An insulator (130)                is coupled to the housing, and interposed between                the first and second electrodes. A                processor (140) controls the skin treatment device                to deliver direct current (DC) electroporation                energy from the first electrode in response to                identifying an image captured by the camera as skin                irregularity. TI Method for creating machine learning based skin            cancer detector that can generalize without racial            biases, involves inputting images into exported trained            second to first skin tone generator for outputting            adapted images, classifying adapted images.
AU ABHARI J S
AE ABHARI J S (ABHA-Individual)
   ABHARI J S (ABHA-Individual)
GA 2024D32218
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves collecting real first skin                tone images from real dermatologic image data. Real                second skin tone images (100) is collected from                real dermatologic image data, a CycleGAN with a                second is created to first skin tone generator, a                first to second skin tone generator, and a                discriminator. Real first skin tone images and real                second skin tone images are inputted into CycleGAN,                is trained to augment real second skin tone images                to look like real first skin tone images. Trained                second is exported to first skin tone generator of                CycleGAN, images is inputted into exported trained                second to first skin tone generator for outputting                adapted images, adapted images is classified.
   USE - Method for creating machine learning based                skin cancer detector that can generalize without                racial biases by creating general model that can                leam from traditional biased majority datasets and                from smaller diverse datasets, implementing                unbiased computer vision model.
   ADVANTAGE - The technique isolates regions of data that                contain only a mole, along with utilization of sty                le matching models to match minority data to                majority data, thus allowing for much smaller                datasets to gather with effective generalizations.                The method to create this general model, it is                desirable to use the innovative domain adaptation                technique of attention maps, which isolate regions                of data that contain only a mole, along with style                matching models to match minority data to majority                data, which allows for much smaller datasets to                gather with effective generalizations. The                application operates by stylizing images of                minority skin types to resemble majority datasets,                thus enhancing the performance of the                classification model. The goal was to create a                machine learning based skin cancer detector that                would be able to have as good of an Fl score and                accuracy for darker skin tone images as lighter                skin tone images, thus mitigating the racial biases                learned in machine learning based skin cancer                detection.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of image                generated during Cycle GAN training.

TI Cancerous tissue detection device for use in            colon, esophagus, breast, skin and cervix.
AU BANERJEE B
   YOUNG J D
AE BANERJEE B (BANE-Individual)
   BANERJEE B (BANE-Individual)
   YOUNG J D (YOUN-Individual)
GA 2000126514
AB    NOVELTY - An optical filter (14) transmits light from a                white light source (12) at a wavelength of 280-315                nm. An optical fiber bundle (22) with a sampling                end (28) transmits the light to the tissue (T)                under investigation and samples reflected light                sample. A lens unit (30) between the optical fiber                bundle and the tissue focuses the reflected light                to a filter (34), which transmits light of                wavelength 320-340 nm to a photodetector                (36).
   USE - The apparatus is used to detect cancerous                tissue in colon, esophagus, breast, skin and                cervix.
   ADVANTAGE - The precancerous and cancerous cells are                detected easily by measuring the intensity of                sample light at an emission wavelength of about 330                nm. The extra cellular changes which are                nonspecific to cancer are excluded and only                cellular changes are detected at 330 nm.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A charge coupled unit is provided in which                autofluorescence emission is displayed. The optical                fiber bundle is inserted into biopsy channel of                endoscope.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                cancerous tissue detection method.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows schematic diagram of cancer                detection device.

AB    NOVELTY - A medicinal composition comprises an ionic                mineral complex and carrier.
   USE - The medicinal composition is used for treating                plant and animal diseases. The composition is                formed for incorporation into transdermal patch,                and/or incorporation into a gel cap, tablet,                powder, food additive, drops, liquid, beverage,                rinse, mouthwash, gargle, pill, capsule, lozenge,                ointment, salve, cream, lotion and gel (all                claimed). The composition is particularly used for                treating pain and cancer (including skin, stomach,                thyroid, lymph node or prostate cancer) in human                and animal; for treating conditions affecting                adrenal system, musculoskeletal system,                cardiovascular system, digestive system, excretory                system, immune system, nervous system, respiratory                system, different systemic and organ based cancers                and conditions relating to protein production; for                aiding human nutrition related problems; and for                use in fertilizers and in hydroponics.
   ADVANTAGE - The composition has little or no effect to                host or on normal cells while destroying mutant                cells, and is able to interrupt the metabolic                pathway of diseases affecting plants and animals.                The ionic mineral ligand complex composition will                detect skin cancers and other types of cancer and                eliminate at rate of 95% or better for skin cancers                and have the potential for a high level of efficacy                in other cancers. The cancer detection is fast,                easy to administer and near 100% effective.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for                production of medicinal composition comprising                adding ammonium hydrogen sulfate, mineral                composition(s) and distilled water to a mixture,                agitating mixture, and diluting to a desired                concentration.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Component: The ionic mineral                  complex comprises an ionic mineral ligand bonded                  to ammonia molecules enabling transport of ionic                  mineral complex through a biological system to a                  target cell affected by a disease. The ionic                  mineral complex is a cation; and is silver,                  manganese, magnesium, cobalt, chromium,                  molybdenum, selenium, vanadium, or preferably                  zinc and copper present at 7:2 ratio. The greater                  than or equal to 2 ionic mineral complexes are                  present in a ratio of 1:1.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Component: The composition further                  comprises surfactants, dimethyl sulfoxide,                  urea-based compounds, detergents, hydroscopic                  compounds and/or any other carrier; plant                  extract(s) including graviola (Annona muricata),                  bitter melon (Momordica charantia), espinheira                  santa (Maytenus ilicifolia), mullaca (Physalis                  angulata), vassourinha (Scoparia dulcis), mutamba                  (Guazuma ulmifolia), suma (Pfaffia paniculata),                  cat's claw (Uncaria tomentosa) or bloodroot                  (Sanguinaria canadensis); and mineral supplement                  or vitamin supplement. The composition has pH of                  less than 1.0. The diluted mixture includes ionic                  mineral complexes encapsulated by ligand bound                  ammonia molecules. Preferred Process: The                  agitating step is a slow agitation at a speed                  able to reduce exothermic interaction between                  ingredients. The method further comprises                  combining diluted mixture with carrier.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Condition: The composition, upon                  introduction into biological system, bonds with                  superoxide dismutase composition and transported                  throughout the biological system for delivery to                  target cells. The ionic mineral complex includes                  a cation and, upon introduction into target cell,                  the cation is dissociated from ionic mineral                  complex and is taken up by a disease causing                  organism in an amount toxic to disease causing                  organism causing its death without harming a host                  biological system. The composition, upon                  introduction to target cell, stimulates a host                  immune response by degrading a sheath around                  target cell.
   ACTIVITY - Analgesic; Cytostatic; Endocrine-Gen;                Muscular-Gen; Osteopathic; Cardiovascular-Gen;                Gastrointestinal-Gen; Immunomodulator; CNS-Gen;                Respiratory-Gen; Fertilizer. Test details are                described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition is introduced into a                biological system by topical application, orally                ingestion, parenterally, intravenously and/or                subcutaneously (claimed). No dosage details                given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

   USE - Device for monitoring and analyzing early oral cancer detection from Photo Plethysmography (PPG) and temperature signal, for use in health care centers for peripheral blood flow mapping and temperature profile of any organs (all claimed).

The blood flow and temperature values are analyzed by using fuzzy system to classify the severity of oral cancer. The device is made user friendly and made available in all health care centers. The results are made within short period without any delay for further processing.

The porphyrin derivative is chosen from compounds                of formulae (1)-(6).

GA 202234367U
AB    NOVELTY - The integrated system has a deep learning based skin disease image classification system for accurate skin disease detection. A machine learning based system identifies the disease causes and detects the types of skin diseases. An effective fusion of multi classifiers uses the dynamic weighted voting method. The deep learning techniques are used to identify the causes of the skin disease and its causes. The machine learning is used to detect the type of skin disease that is caused by the user. The system is also used to determine the type of the disease that the user is suffering from, and to determine if the user has the same type of disease.
   USE - Integrated system for identification of skin disease and its causes using deep learning technique. Uses include but are not limited to eczema, psoriasis, darier disease, pigment darkening, sunburn, skin cancer, and infectious diseases.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables utilizing deep learning and machine learning techniques to classify the skin disease images by convolutional neural network (CNN) neural networks in an effective manner, thus improving accuracy of diagnosis of skin disease in an efficient manner. The method allows a medical officer/doctor to provide treatment based on his suspicion, thus providing treatment to cure the disease at an early stage, and hence reducing the number of people who die from cancer-related causes in a time-saving and convenient manner.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of an integrated system for identification of skin disease and its causes using deep learning technique.

   ADVANTAGE - The crystal form A of (I) has a high purity,                less residual solvent, solubility and excellent                stability, fluidity and compressibility, and is                convenient for production, detection, preparation                of formulations, transportation and storage. The                method is easy to operate and is suitable for                industrial production.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Crystal form A of                5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                of formula (I) exhibiting an X-ray powder                diffraction pattern at 2&#952; angle using                copper-K&#945; radiation with characteristic                peaks as given in the specification, is new.    preparation of (I); and

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preparation (Claimed): The preparation of                  (I), comprises: either dissolving                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  in an organic solvent, stirring, and collecting                  precipitated solid; dissolving                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  in an organic solvent, heating to                  70-100&#176; C until to dissolve, reducing                  temperature to 50-75&#176; C, adding a seed                  crystal, keeping constant temperature,                  precipitating solid, slowly cooling to                  0-25&#176; C, collecting the precipitated                  solid at constant temperature and drying, where                  the seed crystal is crystal form A of (I) or a                  solid which precipitates during the preparation                  of the crystal form A of (I), and the amount of                  the seed crystal added is 0.1-3 wt.%, preferably                  0.1-0.2%, 0.2-0.5%, 0.5-1%, 1-1.5%, 1.5-2%,                  2-2.5% or 2.5-3% of mass of (I);
