C until to dissolve, reducing                  the temperature to 50-65&#176; C, adding the                  seed crystal, and keeping constant temperature to                  obtain a solid, slowly reducing the temperature                  to 0-25&#176; C, keeping constant                  temperature, filtering and drying, where the seed                  crystal form A or a solid prior to drying in the                  preparation of crystal form A and the mass ratio                  of the seed crystal to                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  is 0.1-3%, preferably 0.1-0.2%, 0.2-0.5%, 0.5-1%,                  1-1.5%, 1.5-2%, 2-2.5% or 2.5-3%. Preferred                  Method: The method comprises: either dissolving                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  in an organic solvent, heating to                  60-100&#176; C, stirring to dissolve the                  above compound, cooling to 0-25&#176; C,                  stirring at a constant temperature for 1-24 hours                  and collecting precipitated solid; dissolving                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  in an organic solvent, heating to                  60-100&#176; C, stirring to dissolve the                  above compound, cooling to 30-55&#176; C to                  precipitate a solid, cooling to 0-25&#176; C,                  stirring for 1-24 hours at constant temperature,                  collecting the precipitated solid, and drying; or                  dissolving                  5-((4-ethylpiperazin-1-yl)methyl)-N-(5-fluoro-4-(4-fluoro-1-isopropyl-2-methyl-1Hbenzo[d]imidazol-6-yl)pyridin-2-yl)pyrimidin-2-amine                  in an organic solvent, heating to                  60-100&#176; C, and stirring to dissolve the                  above compound, continuously stirring, cooling to                  0-25&#176; C, separating solid, stirring at a                  constant temperature for 1-24 hours, suction                  filtering, and drying to obtain crystal form A of                  (I). Preferred Components: (I) has an endothermic                  peak at 195-215&#176; C, preferably                  205&#177; 3&#176; C in a differential                  scanning calorimetry pattern. The alicyclic                  alcohol solvent is cyclopentanol, cyclopentanol,                  cyclohexanol, cyclohexylethanol or                  cyclohexylethanol. AE GUANGZHOU BURNING ROCK MED LAB CO LTD (GUAN-Non-standard)
   GUANGZHOU BURNING ROCK DX CO LTD (GUAN-Non-standard)

GA 2023421260
AB    NOVELTY - Bio-composition comprises at least one                positive cell line, as a positive standard, at                least one negative cell line, as a negative                standard, at least one positive genomic vector, as                a positive reference and at least one negative                genomic vector, as a negative reference.
   USE - The bio-composition is used as a standard for                evaluating accuracy of cancer gene detection and                tissue traceability. The cancer comprises brain                cancer, lung cancer, skin cancer, nasopharyngeal                cancer, throat cancer, liver cancer, bone cancer,                lymphoma, pancreatic cancer, skin cancer,                intestinal cancer, rectal cancer, thyroid cancer,                bladder cancer, kidney cancer, oral cancer, stomach                cancer, solid tumor, ovarian cancer, esophageal                cancer, gallbladder cancer, biliary tract cancer,                breast cancer, cervical cancer, uterine cancer,                prostate cancer, head and neck cancer, sarcoma,                malignancies of the thoracic cavity (except lung),                melanoma, testicular cancer and leukemia (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The bio-composition can realize different                gradient positive signals, and evaluate accuracy of                the methylation detection method.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method (M1) for preparing the bio-composition,                involves (a) obtaining positive cell line and                negative cell line, (b) performing nucleus                separation on the positive cell line and the                negative cell line and then converting the positive                cell line and the negative cell line into positive                fragmented DNA and negative fragmented DNA by                enzyme digestion, (c) mixing the positive                fragmented DNA and the negative fragmented DNA, (d)                obtaining positive genome vector and negative                genome vector, mixing the positive genome vector                and the negative genome vector, and fragmenting and                (e) uniformly mixing the products obtained step (c)                and step (d);
   kit comprising the bio-composition; and
   method (M2) for verifying accuracy of a gene                sequencing method, involves (a) sequencing the                bio-composition in accordance with the gene                sequencing method and comparing error of the                positive level of sequencing in a certain interval                and the mass ratio of positive cell line/negative                cell line, and if the error is less than 30%, the                gene sequencing method is considered accurate or                (b) sequencing the bio-composition in accordance                with the gene sequencing method, and comparing the                error between the methylation level of positive                genome carrier sequencing and the theoretical                methylation level (97%) of positive genome carrier,                if the error If it is less than 5%, the gene                sequencing method is considered accurate or (c)                sequencing the bio-composition in accordance with                the gene sequencing method and comparing the                methylation level of negative genome carrier                sequencing, if the methylation level is less than                1%, the gene sequencing method is considered                accurate.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The base number of the                  positive genome vector is less than the base                  number of the positive cell line. The base number                  of the negative genome vector is smaller than                  that of the negative cell line. The base number                  of the positive genome vector is less than 1/100,                  preferably 1/10000 of the base number of the                  positive cell line. The base number of the                  negative genome vector is less than 1/100,                  preferably 1/10000 of the base number of the                  negative cell line. The negative cell line and                  negative genome vector are in a mass ratio of                  1:2&#215;10-3-1:1&#215;10-6, preferably                  1:2&#215;10-4-1:1&#215;10-5. The positive                  cell line and positive genome vector are in a                  mass ratio of                  1:2&#215;10-3-1:1&#215;10-6, preferably                  1:2&#215;10-4-1:1&#215;10-5. The positive                  cell line and negative cell line are in a mass                  ratio of 0.1:99.9-25:75, preferably 1:99-5:95.                  The positive genome vector and negative genome                  vector are in a mass ratio of 1:99-25:75 or                  99:1-75:25, preferably 1:19 or 19:1. Preferred                  Cells: Both the positive cell line and the                  negative cell line are fragmented with an average                  fragment size of about 140-160 base pair (bp).                  The positive cell line is chosen from the                  combination of the following cell lines: human                  colorectal cancer cell line (e.g.: SW48), human                  lung adenocarcinoma cell line (e.g.: H1975),                  human liver cancer cell line (e.g.: HepG2), human                  esophageal cancer cell line (e.g.: T.T), human                  ovarian cancer cell lines (e.g.: CaoV3) and human                  pancreatic cancer cell lines (e.g.: PANC-1 or                  PSN-1). The negative cell line is chosen from a                  combination of the following cell lines: human B                  lymphocytes (e.g.: GM24385, GM12878, GM24631,                  NCI.BL1184) or human normal cell lines (e.g.:                  Beads-2B and other normal cell lines). Preferred                  Biomolecule: The positive genome vector is pUC19                  DNA treated with methyltransferase and/or                  &#955; DNA treated with methyltransferase,                  preferably M.Sssl. The negative genome vector is                  unmethylated &#955; DNA and/or unmethylated                  pUC19 DNA. Preferred Method: The fragmentation                  treatment involves enzymatic fragmentation and/or                  physical fragmentation. The digestion involves                  fragmenting the genomic DNA by restriction                  endonuclease or micrococcal nuclease. The method                  (M2) (a) involves calculating error by                  calculating difference in the positive cell                  line/negative cell line mass ratio was subtracted                  from the sequenced positive level score and                  divided by the positive cell line/negative cell                  line mass ratio, if the error is less than 25%,                  the gene sequencing method is considered                  accurate. The method (M2) (b) involves                  calculating error by calculating the difference                  between the methylation level of the positive                  genome carrier sequenced minus the theoretical                  methylation level of the positive genome carrier,                  and then dividing by the theoretical methylation                  level of the positive genome carrier, where if                  the error is less than 3%, the gene sequencing                  method is considered accurate. In method (M2)                  (c), if the methylation level is less than 0.5%,                  preferably 0.02%, the gene sequencing method is                  considered to be accurate.

TI Method for detecting fluoroacetaldehyde in            fluorouracil injection used in treatment of e.g. skin            cancer, involves adding fluorouracil injection to be            tested and derivative solution to bottle, adjusting pH,            performing derivatization reaction to obtain test            sample solution and detecting by HPLC.
AU BAI P
   JIA L
   JI X
AE SHANGHAI RONGDI BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD (SHAN-Non-standard)
GA 202353457D
AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting fluoroacetaldehyde in                fluorouracil injection solution involves preparing                an acetic acid-sodium acetate buffer solution with                pH value of 4.5-5.5, mixing with a                dinitrophenylhydrazine solution to obtain                derivative solution, precisely measuring                fluorouracil injection to be tested and the                derivative solution in same measuring bottle,                adding acetic acid to adjust the pH value to                3.0-3.5, sealing, performing derivatization                reaction at 30-50&#8451; for 20-60 minutes,                cooling to room temperature, and diluting to                constant volume with acetic acid-sodium acetate                buffer solution to obtain test sample solution,                detecting the fluoroacetaldehyde in the test sample                solution by reversed-phase HPLC using phosphate                buffer with pH of 2.5 as mobile phase (A), and                acetonitrile as mobile phase (B) at wavelength of                350-360 nm, injection volume of 18-22 &#956;L,                and flow rate of 0.9-1.1 mL/minute.
   USE - Method for detecting fluoroacetaldehyde in                fluorouracil injection solution used in treatment                of gastrointestinal cancer, chorion epithelial                cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, lung cancer,                cervical cancer, bladder cancer and skin                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is simple and effectively detects                fluoroacetaldehyde concentration in fluorouracil                injection solution with excellent specificity, high                sensitivity, detecting limit concentration of up to                1.21 ng/ml, quantitative limit of 12.1 ng/ ml with                fluoroacetaldehyde solution with known                concentration in test sample, standard recovery                rate of 81.4% and high accuracy; and is suitable                for quantitative detection of trace                fluoroacetaldehyde impurity in fluorouracil                injection.

   EXAMPLE - A solution of 10 g                2-methylnaphtho[1,2-d]thiazole in a mixture of                ethylene glycol and aqueous 50% sodium hydroxide                was refluxed under argon for 16 hours before being                poured into an ice-water bath and acidified to a pH                of 3 with 1M hydrochloric acid solution. The                organic phase was then extracted with                dichloromethane, dried over magnesium sulfate, and                concentrated under reduced pressure. The resulting                crude 1-aminonaphthalene-2-thiol was directly                engaged in the next step without further                purification. The crude mixture was blended with 11                g 4-bromo-1,8-naphthalic anhydride and 5.49 g                potassium carbonate. 270 mL Dimethylformamide was                then added under air atmosphere and the reaction                mixture was stirred for 16 hours at room                temperature. 15.7 mL Isopentyl nitrite was then                added. An orange precipitate appeared upon stirring                at 60&#176; C. After 24 hours, the latter was                filtrated, successively washed with water and                methanol, and finally dried with a rotary                evaporator under reduced pressure. TI Test kit and adhesive tape e.g. for zytological            examination of surface of skin, has adhesive tape            having transparent carrier film and adhesive layer            which, when placed on skin, has strong contact with            cells of skin.
AU STRASSER W
AE STRASSER W (STRA-Individual)
GA 2006090349
AB    NOVELTY - The kit has an adhesive tape having a                transparent carrier film and an adhesive layer                which, when the tape is placed on the skin, has a                strong contact with the cells on the surface of the                skin that epithelial cells and keratin cells are                torn from the skin and adhere to the adhesive tape                when the transparent adhesive tape is removed. The                cells can be zytomorphologically evaluated,                according to color, for the presence of melanomas,                basaliomas, precanceroses, prekeratoses, aktinic                keratoses and spinocellular canceroses.
   USE - For zytological examination of surface of                skin. For diagnosing skin cancer such as                melanomas
   ADVANTAGE - Easy for pain free skin tissue sampling. Early                detection of malignant melanomas possible. Provides                tool for early non invasive detection of relevant                skin changes
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows a photograph of the                invention.

AB    NOVELTY - Heterogeneous breast phantom comprises a skin                mimicking segment comprising 4-6 wt.% polyvinyl                alcohol and 27-35 wt.% sugar, 38-45 wt.% adipose                tissue mimicking segment, a fibro-glandular tissue                mimicking segment comprising 10-15 wt.% glycerol,                22-28 wt.% pectoral muscle mimicking segment                comprising sugar and 2-8 wt.% egg whites, and a                carcinoma mimicking segment comprising a sugar                selected from lactose, sucrose, mannitol, and                sorbitol in an amount of 20-25 wt % relative to a                total weight of the carcinoma mimicking segment.                Each segment is shaped and arranged such that the                breast phantom represents a breast tissue.
   USE - Heterogeneous breast phantom for use in                various breast imaging modalities for detection of                early cancer and lesions.
   ADVANTAGE - The heterogeneous breast phantom mimics the                real breast tissues in terms of anatomy and tissue                properties concerning the conventional breast                imaging techniques, and provides accurate                simulation of tumors, masses or other lesions in a                single imaging modality by simulating the tissue                material response only for single modality                considering quality assurance (QA) only, and                simulates the breast tissue under a medical imaging                technique.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The segment further                  comprises water, a vegetable oil, a surfactant,                  and agar. The vegetable oil is safflower oil. The                  surfactant is a nonionic surfactant. The skin                  mimicking segment, the adipose tissue mimicking                  segment, the fibro-glandular tissue mimicking                  segment, and the carcinoma mimicking segment each                  further comprise at least one type of scattering                  particles selected from sodium chloride,                  Potassium chloride (KCl), Aluminium oxide, and                  Silicon carbide (SiC) particle. The medical                  imaging technique is magnetic resonance imaging                  (MRI), computed tomography scan (CT scan), or                  both.

GA 2008D54946
AB    NOVELTY - Detection of cancer cells in a biological                sample of a patient (or other mammal) comprises                extraction of biological material of a biological                sample taken from the patient or mammal followed by                contacting with at least 7 specific reagents                comprising specific reagents of Liv21 complex                target genes or their interactive partners having a                nucleotide sequence of SEQ ID NO: 119-146 (Not                defined) and determining the expression of the                target genes. Sequences not defined here may be                found at ftp://ftp.wipo.int/pub/published pct                sequences/publication.
   USE - The method is useful for the detection of                metastatic cancer, to monitor therapy and/or to                repeat treatment (claimed). Examples of the cancers                that can be detected using the method are breast                cancer, bladder cancer, ovarian cancer, lung                cancer, skin cancer, prostate cancer, colon cancer,                liver cancer, sarcoma and leukemia.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a support                containing at least 7 hybridization probes of                specific target genes with a nucleotide/urea                peptide sequence with any one of SEQ ID NO: 119-146                and at least one control.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The process is done with                  12 reagents. The product of gene expression is                  detected at messenger RNA and/or protein. The                  protein is detected using a specific antibody or                  products of gene expression made using a DNA chip                  or proteins. The protein is detected by Western                  blot analysis, by immunohistochemistry,                  immunocytochemistry, immunoradiography or by                  marking a peroxidase or Surface Plasmon Resonance                  (SPR). The indication of the presence of cancer                  cells in the process is a significant increase in                  protein kinase C epsilon (PKC-&#949; ) in the                  cytoplasm of cells extracted. The method further                  comprises the detection of the expression                  products of a gene comprising the gene of the                  PKC-&#949; , E2F1 gene and E2F4 gene.                  Preferred Components: The biological sample is a                  blood sample. The biological material extracted                  from the sample taken from the patient or other                  mammal consists of nucleic acids. The specific                  reagents are hybridization probes immobilized on                  a substrate, where the medium is a biochip. The                  expression products of LIV21 complex gene are                  polypeptides comprising a peptide sequence of SEQ                  ID NO: 1-121. The antibody binds specifically to                  a polypeptide comprising a peptide sequence of                  SEQ ID NO: 1-121.

TI Method for capturing ultrasound images of e.g.            breast of woman by using ultrasound patch for detection            of cancer, involves calculating image of tissue in body            part based on measurements of reflections and three            dimensional positions of phased arrays.
AU ZHANG L
   DAGDEVIREN C
AE MASSACHUSETTS INST TECHNOLOGY (MASI-C)
GA 2025154419
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves transmitting ultrasound                signals and taking measurements of reflections of                the signals by a set of phased arrays(110, 111)                embedded in a substrate, while the substrate                touches skin of a body part e.g. breast of a woman.                A set of three-dimensional (3D) positions of the                phased arrays is detected based on measurements of                other ultrasound signals, where each 3D position in                the set of positions is a 3D position of a phased                array in the set of arrays. An image of tissue in                the body part is calculated based on the                measurements of the reflections and the 3D                positions of the phased arrays, where the image of                tissue is a 3D image of a volume of the                tissue.
   USE - Method for capturing ultrasound images of                underlying tissue or human body part e.g. breast of                a woman, shoulder or portion of a finger, toe,                wrist or ankle (all claimed), by using an                ultrasound patch for detection of pathological                conditions such as cancer and other soft tissue                diseases.
   ADVANTAGE - The ultrasound patch touches and fits snugly                against the skin throughout a large region even                though the surface of the skin is curved in that                region without any gel or adhesive, and without                requiring any external support structure to support                weight of the patches or to press the patches                against the skin. The patches can be comfortably                worn for long durations and easily removed from the                skin without damaging the skin. The patch reduces                stress and strain to prevent the patch from being                damaged.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of                ultrasound patches that conform to curvilinear                surfaces of a human body.
   101, 102Ultrasound patches
   110, 111Phased arrays
   130Link

GA 201662751Y
AB    NOVELTY - An isolated antibody which selectively binds                to glycosylated Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)                relative to unglycosylated PD-L1 and inhibits                binding of glycosylated PD-L1 to Programmed cell                death protein 1 (PD-1), is new.
   USE - The antibody and composition are useful for                treating a PD-L1 positive cancer; and assaying for                the presence of glycosylated PD-L1 in a biological                sample. The cancer is a breast cancer, lung cancer,                head and neck cancer, prostate cancer, esophageal                cancer, tracheal cancer, skin cancer brain cancer,                liver cancer, bladder cancer, stomach cancer,                pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer,                cervical cancer, testicular cancer, colon cancer,                rectal cancer or skin cancer. The cancer is a                hematological cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - New and more effective therapeutics and                methodologies that successfully target the                PD-1/PD-L1 pathway and activate effector cells of                the immune system to attack the tumor cells and                treat cancers are provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   an isolated nucleic acid molecule comprising a                nucleotide sequence encoding a heavy chain variable                (VH) domain of the antibody defined above, where                the nucleotide sequence is &#8805; 90-98%                identical to the nucleotide sequence of SEQ ID NOs:                2 or 18 and/or a nucleotide sequence encoding a                light chain variable (VL) domain of the antibody                defined above, where the nucleotide sequence is                &#8805; 90-98% identical to the nucleotide                sequence of SEQ ID NOs: 19 or 26;
   a method of treating a PD-L1 positive cancer                in a subject by administering the antibody defined                above;
   a method of assaying for the presence of                glycosylated PD-L1 in a biological sample by                contacting a biological sample with an antibody                defined above, where detection of binding of the                antibody indicates that the sample comprises                glycosylated PD-L1;
   an isolated polypeptide comprising a fragment                of &#8805; 7 contiguous amino acids of human                PD-L1 comprising an amino acid corresponding to                position Asn35, Asn192, Asn200, or Asn219 of SEQ ID                NO: 1, where one of the amino acids corresponding                to position Asn35, Asn192, Asn200, or Asn219 of                PD-L1 is glycosylated; and
   a method of identifying a candidate cancer                patient for treatment with an agent that blocks                binding of PD-L1 with PD-1 by testing for the                presence of glycosylated PD-L1 on cells derived                from a sample of the patient's cancer cells using                an antibody defined above, where if the cells are                positive for glycosylated PD-L1, the patient is a                candidate for the treatment.
EA    (US2022155307-A1)   NOVELTY - Isolated chimeric, humanized or fully human                monoclonal antibody that selectively binds to                glycosylated programmed cell death protein (PD)-1                relative to unglycosylated PD-1, is new.
   USE - Isolated chimeric, humanized or fully human                monoclonal antibody for treating PD-L1 positive                cancer such as breast cancer, lung cancer, head and                neck cancer, prostate cancer, esophageal cancer,                tracheal cancer, skin cancer, brain cancer, liver                cancer, bladder cancer, stomach cancer, pancreatic                cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, cervical                cancer, testicular cancer, colon cancer, rectal                cancer and skin cancer, and for assessing PD-1                glycosylation in a cell sample from cancer or tumor                of subject (all claimed).
Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The isolated chimeric, humanized or fully                human monoclonal antibody provides effective                therapeutics and methodologies that successfully                target the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway and activate effector                cells of the immune system to attack the tumor                cells and treat cancers.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Antibody: The isolated antibody is                  recombinantly engineered, chimeric, humanized or                  fully human. The antibody selectively binds to                  amino acid residues within regions of the PD-L1                  protein comprising amino acid positions 35, 192,                  200 and/or 219 in SEQ ID NO: 1 relative to                  unglycosylated PD-L1. The antibody binds to                  glycosylated PD-L1 with a Kdthat is less than                  half of the Kdexhibited by the antibody binding                  to unglycosylated PD-L1. The antibody binds                  glycosylated PD-L1 with an affinity of 5-20 nM.                  The isolated antibody is directly or indirectly                  detectable by a fluorescent label, preferentially                  binds to cells expressing glycosylated PD-L1 with                  a measured fluorescence intensity (MFI) that is                  2-fold to 10-fold higher than the MFI exhibited                  by the antibody binding to cells expressing                  unglycosylated PD-L1 in a cell flow cytometry                  assay. The isolated antibody specifically binds                  to an epitope of glycosylated PD-L1 comprising                  one of amino acids 56, 62, 69 and 75 of SEQ ID                  NO: 1. The isolated antibody specifically binds                  to the epitope of PD-L1 recognized by the                  monoclonal antibody (MAb) STM004 or MAb STM115.                  The isolated antibody competes or cross competes                  for specific binding to glycosylated PD-L1 with                  MAb STM004 or MAb STM115. The isolated antibody                  comprises the VH domain or the VL domain of MAb                  STM004 or MAb STM115. The isolated antibody                  comprises heavy chain complementarity determining                  regions (CDRs)1-3 and/or light chain CDRs1l-3                  from MAb STM004 or MAb STM115. The VH domain has                  an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3 or 19. The                  VL domain has an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID                  NO: 11 or 27. The VH domain has an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3 and the VL has an amino                  acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 11. The VH domain has                  an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 19 and the                  VL domain has an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID                  NO: 27. The VH domain has an amino acid sequence                  that is &#8805; 90% identical to the amino                  acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3 or 19. The VL                  domain has an amino acid sequence that is                  &#8805; 90% identical to the amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 11 or 27. The isolated                  antibody has a VH domain comprising a CDR H1 with                  an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 4, a CDR H2                  with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 6, and                  a CDR H3 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID                  NO: 8, or a VH domain comprising a CDR H1 with an                  amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 5, a CDR H2                  with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 7, and                  a CDR H3 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID                  NO: 9. The isolated antibody has a VL domain                  comprising a CDR L1 with an amino acid sequence                  of SEQ ID NO: 12, a CDR L2 with an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 14, and a CDR L3 with an                  amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 16. The                  isolated antibody has a VH domain comprising a                  CDR H1 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                  20, a CDR H2 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ                  ID NO: 22, and a CDR H3 with an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 24, or a VH comprising a                  CDR H1 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                  21 a CDR H2 with an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID                  NO: 23, and a CDR H3 with an amino acid sequence                  of SEQ ID NO: 25. The isolated antibody has a VL                  domain comprising a CDR L1 with an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 28, a CDR L2 with an amino                  acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 30, and a CDR L3 with                  an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 32. The                  isolated antibody has a VH domain comprising CDRs                  H1, H2 and H3 with amino acid sequences that have                  1-5 amino acid substitutions in 1-3 CDRs having                  the amino acid sequences of SEQ ID NO: 4, SEQ ID                  NO: 6, and SEQ ID NO: 8, respectively, or having                  the amino acid sequences of SEQ ID NO: 5, SEQ ID                  NO: 7, and SEQ ID NO: 9, respectively. The                  isolated antibody has a VL domain comprising CDRs                  L1, L2 and L3 with amino acid sequences that have                  1-5 amino acid substitutions in 1-3 CDRs having                  the amino acid sequences of SEQ ID NO: 12, SEQ ID                  NO: 14, and SEQ ID NO: 16, respectively. The                  isolated antibody has a VH domain comprising CDRs                  H1, H2 and H3 with amino acid sequences that have                  1-5 amino acid substitutions in 1-3 CDRs having                  the amino acid sequences of SEQ ID NO: 20, SEQ ID                  NO: 22, and SEQ ID NO: 24, respectively, or SEQ                  ID NO: 21, SEQ ID NO: 23, and SEQ ID NO: 25,                  respectively. The isolated antibody has a VL                  domain comprising CDRs L1, L2 and L3 with amino                  acid sequences that have 1-5 amino acid                  substitutions in 1-3 CDRs having the amino acid                  sequences of SEQ ID NO: 28, SEQ ID NO: 30, and                  SEQ ID NO: 32, respectively. The antibody is an                  immunoglobulin (Ig)G, IgM, IgA antibody, or its                  antigen binding fragment. The antibody is a Fab',                  a F(ab')2, a F(ab')3, a monovalent single chain                  variable fragment (scFv), a bivalent scFv, or a                  single domain antibody. The antibody is                  conjugated to an imaging agent, a                  chemotherapeutic agent, a toxin or a                  radionuclide. Preferred Method: In the method of                  treating a PD-L1 positive cancer in a subject,                  the subject is a human. The antibody is                  administered in a composition. The method further                  comprises administering a second anticancer drug                  and/or anticancer therapy to the subject, where                  the second anticancer therapy is a surgical                  therapy, chemotherapy, radiation therapy,                  cryotherapy, hormonal therapy, immunotherapy or                  cytokine therapy. In the method of assaying for                  the presence of glycosylated PD-L1 in a                  biological sample, the sample is cell sample. The                  cell sample is from a cancer or tumor of a                  subject. The method of identifying a candidate                  cancer patient for treatment with an agent that                  blocks binding of PD-L1 with PD-1 further                  comprises administering to a patient identified                  as a candidate cancer patient an effective amount                  of an agent that prevents binding of glycosylated                  PD-L1 to PD-1. The agent that prevents binding of                  glycosylated PD-L1 to PD-1 is an isolated                  antibody defined above. The isolated antibody is                  administered in combination with another                  anti-cancer drug or therapeutic. Preferred                  Polypeptide: The polypeptide comprises 8-20                  contiguous amino acids of human PD-L1. The                  polypeptide comprises a glycosylated amino acid                  corresponding to position Asn35, Asn192, Asn200,                  and/or Asn219 of SEQ ID NO: 1. The polypeptide is                  fused or conjugated at its amino or carboxy                  terminus to an immunogenic polypeptide. Preferred                  Nucleic Acid Molecule: The nucleotide sequence                  encoding the VH domain is 95-99% identical to SEQ                  ID NOs: 2 or 18 and/or the nucleotide sequence                  encoding the VL domain is 95 to 99% identical to                  SEQ ID NOs: 10 or 26. All sequences are shown in                  Table 3 in the specification. Preparation: No                  preparation method given.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - PD-L1 Modulator.
   ADMINISTRATION - The antibody is administered systemically,                intravenously, intradermally, intratumorally,                intramuscularly, intraperitoneally, subcutaneously                or locally (all claimed). Dosage is 0.1-100                mg/kg.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Detection of genetic susceptibility to cancer by            calculation of frequency of chromatid breaks and gaps            in X-irradiated of fluorescence exposed meta-phase skin            fibroblasts.
AU SANFORD K K
   PARSHAD R
   JONES G M
AE US DEPT HEALTH & HUMAN SERVICE (USSH-C)
GA 1990075805
AB       Process for determining genetic susceptibility                to cancer is disclosed in which the frequency of                chromatid breaks and gaps is calculated in                metaphase skin fibroblasts or stimulated peripheral                blood lymphocytes after X-irradiation or                fluorescent light exposure. Susceptibility to                cancer is found when the frequency of breaks and                gaps in the cell sample is 2-3-fold higher than                that in comparable cells from control                individuals.
   USE/ADVANTAGE -   Assay can detect clinically normal carriers of                mutant disease genes (eg those causing ataxia                telangiectasia (A-T) or hereditary cutaneous                malginanat melanoma (HCMM) and those individuals                who have the mutant gene in either homozygous or                heterozygous form, even before appearance of                clinical symptons. The process is suitable for                population screening.
EA    (US4933274-A)      Genetic susceptibility to cancer is detected by                (a) irradiating a cell culture where G2 cells are                present with X-ray or fluorescent light, the                culture being sub-confluent on the growth surface                during irradiation; (b) incubating the culture to                allow for DNA repair; (c) removing culture medium                in the culture about 0.5 hours after irradiation;                (d) arresting cell division in the culture 0.5-2                hrs. after irradiation; (e) determining the number                of chromatid breaks and gaps in G2 cells from the                culture; (f) analysing the numerical results from                (e) to determine the frequency of chromatid breaks                and gaps in the G2 cells; and (g) using the results                to determine cancer susceptibility.
   ADVANTAGE -   Process can screen the population for                individual genetically pre-disposed to cancer and                so at high cancer risk.
   (24pp)

Treating,                  preventing or alleviating or diagnosing cancer                  selected from the group consisting of: (a) a                  method of treatment, prophylaxis or alleviation                  of a cancer selected from the group consisting                  of: colon cancer, lung cancer, squamous cell                  carcinoma including lip, larynx, vulva, cervix                  and penis cancer, pancreatic cancer, brain                  cancer, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer,                  bladder cancer, kidney cancer, skin cancer, ovary                  cancer, prostate cancer and testicular cancer in                  an individual, the method comprising modulating                  the expression, amount or activity of a VHZ in a                  cell of an individual, preferably in which the                  expression, amount or activity of VHZ is                  decreased in a cancer cell of the individual; and                  (b) a method of diagnosis of a cancer selected                  from the group consisting of: colon cancer, lung                  cancer, squamous cell carcinoma including lip,                  larynx, vulva, cervix and penis cancer,                  pancreatic cancer, brain cancer, esophageal                  cancer, stomach cancer, bladder cancer, kidney                  cancer, skin cancer, ovary cancer, prostate                  cancer and testicular cancer or susceptibility to                  such a cancer in an individual or prognosis of an                  individual with such a cancer, the method                  comprising detecting modulation of expression,                  amount or activity of VHZ in a cell of the                  individual. Alternatively, treatment, prophylaxis                  or alleviation of a cancer selected from the                  group consisting of: colon cancer, lung cancer,                  squamous cell carcinoma including lip, larynx,                  vulva, cervix and penis cancer, pancreatic                  cancer, brain cancer, esophageal cancer, stomach                  cancer, bladder cancer, kidney cancer, skin                  cancer, ovary cancer, prostate cancer and                  testicular cancer in an individual comprises                  detecting modulation of expression, amount or                  activity of VHZ in a cell of the individual and                  administering an appropriate therapy, such as an                  anti-VHZ agent, to the individual based on the                  aggressiveness of the tumor. The diagnosis,                  prognosis or choice of therapy is further                  determined by assessing the size of the tumor, or                  the lymph node stage, or both, optionally                  together or in combination with other risk                  factors, preferably in which the diagnosis,                  prognosis or choice of therapy is further                  determined by assessing the estrogen receptor                  (ER) status of the tumor. Preferred Antibody: The                  antibody capable of binding to an VHZ                  polypeptide, in which the antibody is capable of                  binding to an epitope bound by antibody 209, or a                  variant, homolog, derivative or fragment, in                  which the antibody preferably: (a) is capable of                  binding to an epitope on a VHZ polypeptide bound                  by antibody 209; (b) comprises an anti-VHZ                  antibody capable of binding to an epitope being a                  sequence comprising residue C95 of VHZ, or a                  variant, homolog, derivative or fragment; (c)                  comprises the variable region of monoclonal                  antibody 209, or a variant, homolog, derivative                  or fragment which is capable of binding VHZ; (d)                  is capable of binding to an intracellular VHZ                  polypeptide; (e) is capable of crossing the                  plasma membrane of a cell; (f) is capable of                  binding to and inhibiting a biological activity                  of VHZ; (g) is capable of preventing metastasis                  of a cancer, such as colon cancer, lung cancer,                  squamous cell carcinoma including lip, larynx,                  vulva, cervix and penis cancer, pancreatic                  cancer, brain cancer, esophageal cancer, stomach                  cancer, bladder cancer, kidney cancer, skin                  cancer, ovary cancer, prostate cancer and                  testicular cancer; or (h) comprises a monoclonal                  antibody or a humanized monoclonal antibody.                  Preferred Polypeptide: The polypeptide comprises                  a sequence selected from the group consisting of                  fully defined 125-145 amino acids (SEQ ID NO. 4                  and 5) given in the specification, or a variant,                  homolog, derivative or fragment which is capable                  of binding VHZ. The nucleic acid comprises a                  sequence capable of encoding a molecule, or a                  variant, homolog, derivative or fragment which is                  capable of encoding a polypeptide having VHZ                  binding activity. The cell comprises or                  transformed with a nucleic acid sequence or a                  descendent of such a cell.

AB       A brassiere includes panels through which water                may be circulated from an external appts. to cool                the skin tissue of female breasts. The water passes                through refrigeration or heating units and then                enters a holding reservoir. A temp. sensor within                the reservoir directs the liq. through the                refrigeration or heating units as appropriate to                maintain a preselected temp. within the reservoir.                Pref. the dervice cools the skin tissue to 15                degrees C. The female breasts is cooled by the bra                and after its removal an infrared thermographic                scan of the breast is carried out to reveal                discontinuities in the skin temp. Such                discontinuities may indicate the presence of                malignant tumours. The water-cooled bra maintains                an even and controlled temp. of the breast prior to                scanning.

PN US2007167831-A1; US7510532-B2
TI Diseased tissue e.g. cancerous tissue, detecting            method for use in human body, involves determining            contributing frequency of homogeneity of skin            temperature values for each subarea using series of            thermal images.
AU MITRA P
AE LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP (LOCK-C)
GA 2007571200
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves determining a contributing                frequency of homogeneity of skin temperature values                for each of a set of subareas using a series of                thermal images. The tissue corresponding to a                cluster is preliminarily determined to be diseased,                when a spatial distribution of contributing                frequencies of the cluster is less than a lower                threshold frequency or more than an upper threshold                frequency. The tissue corresponding to the cluster                is confirmed to be diseased, when tissue                corresponding to the cluster is preliminarily                determined to be diseased.
   USE - Used for detecting a diseased tissue (claimed)                e.g. cancerous tissue, in a human body. Can also be                used for detecting breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides greater accessibility to                cancer screening and detection.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for an                apparatus for detecting diseased tissue, comprising                an imager.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a blood perfusion                process.
DC P31 (Diagnosis, surgery (A61B).); S03 (Scientific Instrumentation)

PN WO2006110585-A2; EP1871911-A2; JP2008535494-W; US2009220495-A1; WO2006110585-A3
TI Detecting cancerous cells in a biological sample            comprises determining the sequence or expression level            of the prolactin receptor gene in breast, prostate,            lung or skin tissue.
AU FANIDI A
   BOOHER R
   TSE C
AE CHIRON CORP (CHIR-C)
   SAGRES DISCOVERY INC (SAGR-Non-standard)
   CHIRON CORP (CHIR-C)
   SAGRES DISCOVERY INC (SAGR-Non-standard)
   FANIDI A (FANI-Individual)
   BOOHER R (BOOH-Individual)
   TSE C (TSEC-Individual)
GA 2006814682
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting cancerous cells in a biological                sample comprises determining the sequence or                expression level of prolactin receptor (PRLR) gene,                where the biological sample comprises breast,                prostate, lung or skin tissue.
   USE - The antibody, nucleic acid, or polypeptide                that modulates the level of an expression product                of a PRLR gene is useful in manufacturing a                medicament for the treatment or diagnosis of                cancer, e.g. breast, lung, prostate, or skin cancer                (claimed). The methods and kits are useful for                detecting cancerous cells in a biological sample,                for assessing the progression of cancer, and for                identifying a patient as susceptible to treatment                with an antibody that binds to a PRLR                antigen.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a method for assessing the progression of                cancer in a patient;
   a kit, useful for diagnosing cancer,                comprising an antibody that binds to a polypeptide                expression product of a PRLR gene, and a reagent                useful for the detection of a binding reaction                between the antibody and the polypeptide, or a kit,                useful for diagnosing cancer, comprising a nucleic                acid probe that hybridizes under stringent                conditions to a PRLR gene, primers useful for                amplifying the PRLR gene, and optionally                instructions for using the probe and primers for                facilitating the diagnosis of disease;
   an antibody, a nucleic acid, a protein or a                pharmaceutical composition for modulating the                expression of an expression product of a PRLR gene                and for treating cancer;
   a method for treating cancer in a                patient;
   use of an antibody, a nucleic acid, or a                polypeptide that modulates the level of an                expression product of a PRLR gene, in the                manufacture of a medicament for the treatment or                diagnosis of cancer;
   a method for identifying a patient as                susceptible to treatment with an antibody that                binds to a PRLR antigen;
   an assay for identifying a candidate agent                that modulates the growth of a cancerous                cell;
   a method for identifying an agent that                modifies the expression level of a PRLR gene;
   an isolated antibody that specifically binds                to the extracellular domain of PRLR having the                amino acid sequence of residues 25-234 of a                sequence comprising 622 amino acids (SEQ ID NO:                2);
   a pharmaceutical composition comprising an                antibody and a pharmaceutical carrier, excipient or                diluent;
   use of the antibody in preparation of a                medicament for treatment of a cancer selected from                breast, lung, prostate, or skin cancer; and
   a method of screening for an antibody to the                extracellular domain of a PRLR protein useful for                the treatment of cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method comprises                  measuring the level of expression of an                  expression product of PRLR gene, where a level of                  expression that is different compared to a                  control level is indicative of disease. The                  expression product is a protein. The level of                  expression of protein is measured using an                  antibody, which binds specifically to the                  protein. The expression product is mRNA. The                  method comprises contacting the biological sample                  with a probe under stringent conditions that                  allow the formation of a hybrid complex between                  the mRNA and the probe, and detecting the                  formation of a complex. The method comprises                  contacting the biological sample with a nucleic                  acid probe under stringent conditions that allow                  the formation of a hybrid complex between a                  nucleic acid expression product encoding a PRLR                  gene and the probe and detecting the formation of                  a complex between the probe and the nucleic acid                  from the biological sample, where the absence of                  the formation of a complex is indicative of a                  mutation in the sequence of a PRLR gene. The                  method further comprises comparing the amount of                  complex formed with that formed when a control                  tissue is used, where a difference in the amount                  of complex formed between the control and the                  sample indicates the presence of cancer. The                  difference in the amount of complex formed is                  either an increase or decrease, where a two-fold                  or more increase or decrease in the amount of                  complex formed by the sample compared to the                  normal tissue is indicative of disease. The                  biological sample is a tissue sample, e.g. breast                  tissue, lung tissue, prostate tissue, or skin                  tissue. Detecting breast, lung, prostate, or skin                  cancer in a biological sample comprises                  determining the sequence or expression level of                  PRLR, which is correlated to breast, lung,                  prostate, or skin cancer. Assessing the                  progression of cancer in a patient comprises                  comparing the expression of an expression product                  of a PRLR gene in a biological sample at a first                  time point to the expression of the same                  expression product at a second time point, where                  an increase or decrease in expression at the                  second time point relative to the first time                  point is indicative of the progression of the                  cancer. Treating cancer in a patient comprises                  modulating the level of an expression product of                  a PRLR gene. The method comprises administering                  to the patient an antibody, a nucleic acid, or a                  polypeptide that modulates the level of the                  expression product. The expression is modulated                  by action on the gene, mRNA or the encoded                  protein. The expression level of the expression                  product is either upregulated or downregulated,                  where the expression level of the expression                  product is upregulated or downregulated by at                  least a 2-fold change. The nucleic acid is an                  antisense construct, a ribozyme or RNAi. The                  cancer is treated by the inhibition of tumor                  growth or the reduction of tumor volume. The                  cancer is treated by reducing the invasiveness of                  a cancer cell. A medicament is used in                  conjunction with radiotherapy, surgery, hormone                  ablation therapy or chemotherapy, where in a                  patient who is receiving radiotherapy, surgery,                  hormone ablation therapy or chemotherapy,                  administering a compound that modulates the level                  of an expression product of a PRLR gene. Treating                  a subject suffering from breast, lung, prostate,                  or skin cancer comprises administering an                  antibody above in a therapeutic amount, where the                  antibody inhibits prolactin binding to PRLR. The                  subject is suffering from breast lung, prostate,                  or skin cancer. The binding of the antibody to                  PRLR inhibits the induction of MAPK                  phosphorylation. The binding of the antibody to                  PRLR inhibits the induction of Stat5                  phosphorylation. Identifying a patient as                  susceptible to treatment with an antibody that                  binds to a PRLR antigen comprises measuring the                  expression level of an expression product of a                  PRLR gene in a biological sample from that                  patient. The expression level of a PRLR gene                  expression product at a first time point is                  compared to the expression of the same expression                  product at a second time point, where an increase                  or decrease in expression at the second time                  point relative to the first time point is                  indicative of the progression of a cancer in                  which a PRLR gene is implicated. Identifying a                  candidate agent that modulates the growth of a                  cancerous cell comprises detecting the level of                  expression of an expression product of a PRLR                  gene in the presence of the candidate agent, and                  comparing that level of expression with the level                  of expression in the absence of the candidate                  agent, where a difference in expression indicates                  that the candidate agent modulates the level of                  expression of the expression product of a PRLR                  gene. Identifying an agent that modifies the                  expression level of a PRLR gene comprises                  contacting a cell expressing a PRLR gene with a                  candidate agent, and determining the effect of                  the candidate agent on the cell, where a change                  in expression level indicates that the candidate                  agent is able to modulate expression. The                  candidate agent is a polynucleotide, a                  polypeptide, an antibody or a small organic                  molecule. Screening for an antibody to the                  extracellular domain of a PRLR protein useful for                  the treatment of cancer comprises contacting a                  breast, lung, prostate, or skin cell with a                  candidate antibody, detecting proliferation or                  survival of the cell, and identifying the                  candidate antibody as an antibody useful for the                  treatment of cancer if a decrease in cell                  proliferation or survival is detected.Preferred Antibody: The antibody                  specifically binds to an S1 or an S2 domain of a                  PRLR isoforms. The antibody inhibits                  proliferation or survival of breast, lung,                  prostate, or skin cancer cells. The antibody is a                  monoclonal antibody, a humanized antibody, or a                  human antibody. The antibody retains binding                  affinity to the extracellular domain of PRLR of                  10 -8or 10 -9M or less.Preferred Composition: The pharmaceutical                  composition further comprises a second                  therapeutic agent, e.g. a cancer chemotherapeutic                  agent.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Prolactin receptor modulator; Gene                Therapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - Dosage is 1 &#956;g/kg - 100 mg/kg by                parenteral, subcutaneous, intraperitoneal,                intrapulmonary, or intranasal means.

TI Detecting methylation profile of nucleic acid in            sample, by partitioning nucleic acids based on presence            or absence of 5-hydroxymethylcytosine nucleic acid            bases, subjecting nucleic acid to conversion procedure,            amplifying nucleic acids, and analyzing sequencing            data.
AU KENNEDY A
AE GUARDANT HEALTH INC (GUAT-C)
   GUARDANT HEALTH INC (GUAT-C)
   GUARDANT HEALTH INC (GUAT-C)
GA 202482245D
AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting methylation profile of a                nucleic acid in a sample involves (a) partitioning                the nucleic acids based on the presence or absence                of 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) nucleic acid                bases in the nucleic acids, (b) subjecting the                nucleic acids to a conversion procedure that                selectively converts the base pairing specificity                of 5-methylcytosines (5mC) or unmethylated                cytosines (C) in the nucleic acids, (c) amplifying                the nucleic acids which have been subjected to both                steps (a) and (b) to generate amplification                products, (d) sequencing the amplification products                to obtain sequencing data, and (e) analyzing the                sequencing data to determine whether the cytosine                nucleic acid bases of the nucleic acids in the                sample are 5hmC, 5mC or C, where the step (a) is                performed before step (b), or the step (b) is                performed before step (a).
   USE - The method is useful for detecting methylation                profile of nucleic acid in a sample, analyzing                methylation status of cell free DNA, and monitoring                residual disease or recurrence of disease. The                disease includes blood cancers, brain cancers, lung                cancers, skin cancers, nose cancers, throat                cancers, liver cancers, bone cancers, lymphomas,                pancreatic cancers, skin cancers, bowel cancers,                rectal cancers, thyroid cancers, bladder cancers,                kidney cancers, mouth cancers, stomach cancers,                solid state tumors, heterogeneous tumors, or                homogeneous tumors.
   ADVANTAGE - The method allows simultaneous detection of                unmethylated cytosine, 5-methylcytosine and                5-hydroxymethyl cytosine at single nucleotide                resolution, and obtains accurate modified                nucleoside profile of DNA in any DNA sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The step (a) is performed                  before step (b), and the partitioning provides at                  least two subsamples of nucleic acids, where a                  first subsample is enriched for nucleic acids                  comprising 5hmC nucleic acid bases and a second                  subsample is depleted of nucleic acids comprising                  5hmC nucleic acid bases, preferably the steps                  (b)-(e) are performed on (i) at least the first                  subsample, (ii) at least the second subsample, or                  (iii) at least the first subsample and the second                  subsample. The step (b) is performed before step                  (a), and the partitioning provides at least two                  subsamples of nucleic acids, where a first                  subsample is enriched for nucleic acids                  comprising 5hmC nucleic acid bases and a second                  subsample is depleted of nucleic acids comprising                  5hmC nucleic acid bases, preferably the steps                  (c)-(e) are performed on (i) at least the first                  subsample, (ii) at least the second subsample, or                  (iii) at least the first subsample and the second                  subsample. The partitioning is performed by                  modifying the 5hmC nucleic acid base by attaching                  an isolation tag and partitioning using an agent                  which binds to the isolation tag. The method                  further involves incubating the nucleic acids                  with glucosyltransferase and uridine                  diphosphoglucose (UDP-Glu) molecule to                  glycosylate 5hmC nucleic acid bases in the                  nucleic acid molecule with a glucose molecule                  prior to steps (a) and (b), where the UDP-Glu is                  a modified UDP-Glu and the glycosylation of 5hmC                  is with a modified glucose molecule. The                  partitioning is performed by (i) reacting the                  modified glucose with an isolation tag, or (ii)                  binding the glycosylated 5hmC with J binding                  protein 1 (JBP1), where the isolation tag is an                  isolation tag comprising biotin. The partitioning                  is performed by exposing the nucleic acids to a                  binding agent which selectively binds 5hmC, where                  the binding agent is an anti-5hmC antibody, or                  its antigen-binding fragment. The conversion                  procedure selectively converts the base pairing                  specificity of 5-methylcytosines (5mC) in the                  nucleic acids. The conversion procedure comprises                  Tet-assisted conversion of nucleic acids with a                  substituted borane reducing agent, where 5hmC                  nucleic acid bases are protected from conversion,                  through glucosylation, and the substituted borane                  reducing agent is 2-picoline borane, borane                  pyridine, tert-butylamine borane, ammonia borane                  or pyridine borane. The conversion procedure is                  performed by (i) reacting the nucleic acids with                  a variant methyltransferase having                  carboxymethyltransferase activity in the presence                  of carboxy-5-adenosyl-Z-methionine (CxSAM)                  substrate, for labeling any unmethylated C and                  rendering it resistant to deaminase action, where                  5hmC nucleic acid bases are protected from                  conversion through glucosylation, and (ii)                  contacting the nucleic acids with a deaminase                  enzyme which is AP0BEC3A, where the variant                  methyltransferase having carboxymethylase                  activity is a recombinant methyltransferase from                  Mycoplasma penetrans(M.Mpel) Asn374Lys. The                  conversion procedure selectively converts the                  base pairing specificity of unmethylated                  cytosines (C) in the nucleic acids, where the                  conversion procedure is bisulfite conversion. The                  sequencing data is further analyzed by                  identifying the presence or absence of genetic                  variants, where the genetic variants are chosen                  from a single nucleotide variant (SNV), an                  insertion or deletion (indel), and a copy number                  variation. The 5hmC methylation status of the                  nucleic acids in the sample is determined by                  analyzing the base coverage of cytosines in a                  reference sequence. The method further involves                  enriching the nucleic acids by capturing a target                  region set from the sample, where the capture                  step is before, after or in between the                  partitioning of step (a) and the conversion                  procedure of step (b), or between steps (c) and                  (d). The nucleic acid comprises DNA, preferably                  cell-free DNA (cfDNA) obtained from a subject,                  where the subject is a patient having or                  suspected of having cancer. The method further                  involves using the detection of the methylation                  status in the nucleic acids to determine or                  predict the presence or absence of nucleic acids                  produced by a cancer cell or tumor, to determine                  the probability that a subject has a tumor or                  cancer, or to characterize a cancer or tumor of                  the subject. The target region set further                  comprises one or more epigenetic target region                  sets, and the target region set further comprises                  one or more sequence-variable target region sets.                  The method further involves amplifying the                  enriched nucleic acids of the first subsample                  prior to combining the enriched nucleic acids of                  the first subsample and the nucleic acids of the                  second subsample. The amplification comprises one                  or more of PCR, linear amplification, rolling                  circle amplification, ligase chain reaction,                  strand displacement amplification, nucleic acid                  sequence-based amplification, and self-sustained                  sequence-based replication. The amplification                  comprises thermocycled amplification or                  isothermal amplification. The nucleic acids of                  the first subsample and the nucleic acids of the                  second subsample are differentially tagged, and                  the nucleic acids comprise barcodes. The method                  further involves ligating adapters to the nucleic                  acids, where at least one cytosine in the                  adapters is a modification resistant cytosine,                  the ligating occurs before step (c) and/or after                  step (a), each cytosine in the adapters is a                  modification resistant cytosine. The method                  involves ligating adapters comprising barcodes to                  the amplification products prior to the                  sequencing, where the ligating occurs before step                  (c) and/or after step (a). The method involves                  ligating adapters comprising barcodes to the                  nucleic acids prior to the amplifying. The                  sequencing comprises next generation sequencing,                  long-read sequencing or nanopore sequencing. The                  sequencing of nucleic acids of the amplification                  products is performed by generating several                  sequencing reads, and the method further involves                  mapping the several sequence reads to one or more                  reference sequences to generate mapped sequence                  reads, and processing the mapped sequence reads                  corresponding to a sequence-variable target                  region set and to an epigenetic target region                  set, where the nucleic acids comprise cell-free                  DNA, and the cell-free DNA is in an amount of                  1-500 ng. Preferred Component: The modified                  UDP-Glu comprises an azide linker and/or a thiol                  linker. The modified UDP-Glu comprises an                  isolation tag which is used in the partitioning                  step. The isolation tag is biotin or a histidine                  tag. TI Leak detection sensor for stoma pouch assembly for            detecting passage of fluid between adhesive layer of            flange and patient's skin during treatment of e.g.            cancer of colon, has electrodes coated with coating,            where current is made to flow.
AU DAVIS J
   PHAIR J
   MCDONALD D
AE UNIV ULSTER (UULS-C)
GA 2015106409
AB    NOVELTY - The sensor (10) has a pair of electrodes                coated with electrically insulating coating with                fractures. The fractures are formed with breadth of                about less than 500nm. Current is made to flow                between the electrodes when the electrodes are                exposed to electrically conductive fluid. Fractures                are formed by process of laser ablation. The                electrically insulating coating comprises polymeric                coating, where the polymeric coating comprises                thermopolymer, polyvinylacetate, polyimide,                polyester or polyurethane.
   USE - Leak detection sensor for a stoma pouch                assembly (claimed), for detecting passage of fluid                between an adhesive layer of a flange and patient's                skin during treatment of certain medical conditions                such as cancer of colon.
   ADVANTAGE - The sensor can be connected to an                early-warning system or alarm device or detector,                which comprises a conductivity circuit connected to                a vibration alarm or other user perceptible alert                such as audible and/or visually perceptible alarm,                to alert the patient to impending leak and provide                sufficient time to take preventative action so as                to avoid debilitating scenario with pouch failure                in public. The sensor includes a porous wick                intertwined with wires so as to increase                sensitivity of the device for transporting the                fluid along a wire network by capillary action upon                leak emerging at a discrete point, thus contacting                greater proportion of nanoscale fractures and                increasing the sensitivity of the sensor. The                sensor ensures reliable and cost effective effect,                and is shaped and dimensioned to encircle an                opening in the flange of a stoma pouch to sit                between the skin and the adhesive layer of the                flange when the flange is located over a stoma                protruding through the skin from a small intestine                so as to detect fluid leaking behind the adhesive                layer by the sensor and triggering a discrete alarm                device. The insulating coating covering intertwined                copper wires of the sensor during laser ablation,                creates nanoscale fractures in the coating through                which fluid permeates to enable detection of leaks                between the adhesive layer and the skin of the                patient without risk of short circuits between the                wires. The sensor is mounted between the skin and                the flange, so that the insulating coating eases                issues of biocompatibility, where surface area of                copper exposed via the nanoscale fractures is                minimal and transport through the factures of the                mobilized copper ion can be restricted when the                stoma fluid can corrode the copper, thus avoiding                irritation issues.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a stoma pouch assembly
   a method for manufacturing a leak detection                sensor.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows an exploded perspective                view of a stoma pouch leak detection                assembly.

AB       Telomerase activity is detected in cells by (1)                elongating a telomerase substrate (TS primer) using                the cell telomerase; amplifying the elongated                substrate by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using                a second primer (CX primer); (2) hybridising the                amplification product with a probe labelled with a                non-radioactive (preferably chemoluminescent)                label; (3) assaying the label.
   Alternatively the TS primer is attached to a                promoter sequence (e.g. T7 RNA polymerase, T3 RNA                polymerase or SP6 RNA polymerase promoter) and the                elongated substrate is amplified using an RNA                polymerase to synthesise multiple RNA copies of the                sequence and a reverse transcriptase to form DNA                copies. Kits for carrying out the telomerase                activity detection are also claimed.
   USE -   Detection of cancer cells and diagnosis of                cancer by detection of telomerase activity in the                cells. This may be by invasive methods (e.g. biopsy                of tissue from bladder, uterus, cervix, spleen,                liver, mammary, colon, stomach, lung, kidney, skin,                oesophagus, brain, mouth etc) or non-invasive                methods (e.g. examination of biological samples                such as urine, uterine smear, bladder washings,                mouth washings, colonic washings, duodenal                secretion, saliva, sputum, etc).
   ADVANTAGE -   The method is rapid and of high sensitivity,                and does not require the use of a radioactive                label.
