AB    NOVELTY - Hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) and                machine learning system has a deep learning-based                image analysis module configured to process                high-resolution dermoscopic images of skin lesions                using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for                feature extraction. A machine learning-based                classification module employs algorithms such as                support vector machines (SVM) and random forest                classifiers to refine lesion classification. A                clinical data integration module incorporates                non-visual metadata including patient demographics                and medical history into the diagnostic process. A                probabilistic ensemble model combines the outputs                of the image analysis and classification modules                with clinical data to produce a final diagnostic                decision with confidence scores. A cloud-based                infrastructure enables real-time data processing                and storage. A user interface accessible via mobile                and web platforms allow users to upload dermoscopic                images and receive diagnostic results.
   USE - Hybrid AI and machine learning system for                accurate skin cancer detection and                classification.
   ADVANTAGE - The system features continuous learning                through reinforcement mechanisms, and provides a                user-friendly interface for real-time diagnosis,                offers a scalable and reliable diagnostic tool, and                reduces diagnostic disparities particularly in                regions with limited specialized care.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Hybrid Artificial Intelligence (AI) and                machine learning system has a deep learning-based                image analysis module configured to process                high-resolution dermoscopic images of skin lesions                using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for                feature extraction. A machine learning-based                classification module employs algorithms such as                support vector machines (SVM) and random forest                classifiers to refine lesion classification. A                clinical data integration module incorporates                non-visual metadata including patient demographics                and medical history into the diagnostic process. A                probabilistic ensemble model combines the outputs                of the image analysis and classification modules                with clinical data to produce a final diagnostic                decision with confidence scores. A cloud-based                infrastructure enables real-time data processing                and storage. A user interface accessible via mobile                and web platforms allow users to upload dermoscopic                images and receive diagnostic results, where the                system continuously improves its accuracy through                reinforcement learning and feedback mechanisms and                is designed to detect and classify skin cancer into                subtypes such as melanoma, basal cell carcinoma,                and squamous cell carcinoma.

TI Method for removing masking structures in images            for detection of anomaly i.e. cancer by using screening            technique, involves analyzing image for masked            anomalies, where masked anomalies comprising anomalies            that is undetected in analysis.
AU KARIMABADI H
AE CUREMETRIX INC (CURE-Non-standard)
   CUREMETRIX INC (CURE-Non-standard)
GA 201825634K
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves obtaining a first image.                The first image is analyzed to detect unmasked                anomalies. The first image is shifted to provide a                second shifted image. The first image and second                shifted image are compared. A residual image                comprising a combination of the first image and the                second shifted image is obtained. The residual                image is analyzed for masked anomalies, where the                masked anomalies comprising anomalies that went                undetected in the analysis of the first image for                the unmasked anomalies due to presence of masking                features in the first image.
   USE - Method for removing masking structures in                images for detection of anomaly i.e. cancer by                using cancer screening technique in a women with                dense breasts. Can also be used for brain cancer,                lung cancer, liver cancer, prostate cancer, bone                cancer, cervical cancer, colon cancer, leukemia                cancer, Hodgkin disease, kidney cancer, lymphoma                cancer, oral cancer, skin cancer, stomach cancer,                testicular cancer and thyroid.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables reducing need to find an                optimal pivot point for a shift. The method enables                utilizing a memory to improve performance by                providing higher speed memory physically adjacent                to a processor for registers and caching in order                to remove a masking feature while retaining an                anomaly of interest. The method enables shifting                the image for taking residual of the shifted image                and the original unshifted image. The method                enables utilizing masking feature removal process                to lead to a significant reduction in false                positive cancer indications.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a method for detecting breast cancer
   a computer program product comprising a set of                instructions for removing masking structures in                images for detection of anomaly by using cancer                screening technique in a women with dense                breasts
   a system for removing masking structures in                images for detection of anomaly by using cancer                screening technique in a women with dense                breasts.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a photograph of a mammogram                image of a breast.

TI Cancerous cell detecting method for skin cancer, involves determining difference between expected level and determined level of marker element, where difference between level is indicative of cancerous cells.
AU MYERS M J
   MYERS J D
   MYERS J A
   MYERS A G
AE MYERS M J (MYER-Individual)
   MYERS J D (MYER-Individual)
   MYERS J A (MYER-Individual)
   MYERS A G (MYER-Individual)
GA 2008M63250
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves directing a pulsed laser beam to produce a plasma spark at a surface of multiple cells. A line spectra emission of a marker element is detected resulting from the plasma spark. A level of the marker element is based on an intensity of the emission. The determined level is compared to an expected level of the marker element, where the expected level is the level found in a non-cancerous cell. A difference between the expected level and a determined level of the marker element is determined, where a difference is an indicative of cancerous cells.
   USE - Method for detecting a cancerous cell to detect a skin cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method allows emission data to detect changes in the levels of a series of elements that are associated with cancerous cells versus normal skin cells. The method finds use during excisional biopsy procedures to ensure that cancerous cells have been removed.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a detection system.
   Laser output pulse (12)
   Conditioning optics (14)

   Spectrophotometer (20)

   ZHOU N

GA 202352515Q
AB    NOVELTY - Gene expression state classification model                comprising grading the expression state of the                imprinted gene by calculating the changes in the                total expression level, monoallelic gene expression                level, biallelic gene expression level and                multi-allelic gene expression level in the tumor,                is new. The imprinted gene includes Z16, Z19 and                Z21, imprinted gene Z16 is small nuclear                ribonucleoprotein polypeptide N (SNRPN)/small                nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide n opposite                strand (SNURF), imprinted gene Z19 is HM13, and                imprinted gene Z21 is SNU13.
   USE - The gene expression state classification model                is useful for detection and/or treatment tumor                i.e., thyroid cancer, lung cancer, bladder cancer,                prostate cancer, skin cancer, breast cancer,                cervical cancer, intestinal cancer, gastric cancer,                esophageal cancer, pancreatic cancer, liver cancer                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The gene expression state classification model                prevents recurrence of tumor and prolongs life, and                molecular markers is of great significance for                early diagnosis of cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also includes                for:
   tumor detection method, comprising using the                classification model, and sample to be detected for                tumor type and/or tumor benign and malignant                judgment; and
   tumor monitoring method, comprising using                classification model, judging benign and malignant                degree of the tumor before and after the patient,                so as to monitor the tumor development condition of                the patient.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Components: The imprinted gene further                  comprises more than one Z1, Z3, Z5, Z6, Z8, Z9,                  Z10, Z11, Z12, Z13, Z14, Z18, Z20, Z22, Z28,                  where imprinted gene Z1 is GNAS, imprinted gene                  Z3 is PEG10, imprinted gene Z5 is MEST, imprinted                  gene Z6 is PLAGL1, imprinted gene Z8 is DCN,                  imprinted gene Z9 is DLK1, imprinted gene Z10 is                  GATM, imprinted gene Z11 is GRB10, imprinted gene                  Z12 is PEG3, imprinted gene Z13 is SGCE,                  imprinted gene Z14 is SLC38A4, imprinted gene Z18                  is GATA3, imprinted gene Z20 is KCNQ1, imprinted                  gene Z22 is PON2, and imprinted gene Z28 is ZIC1.                  The equation for calculating the total expression                  level, monoallelic gene expression level,                  biallelic gene expression level and multi-allelic                  gene expression level of imprinted genes are                  total expression level = (b+c+d)/(a+b+c+d),                  monoallelic expression = b/(b+c+d), biallelic                  gene expression = c/(b+c+d), multi-allelic gene                  expression=d/(b+c+d), where a is the number of                  cells in which there is no marker in the nucleus                  and the imprinted gene is not expressed, b is the                  number of cells with an imprinted gene marker in                  the nucleus, c is the number of cells with two                  imprinted gene markers in the nucleus, d is the                  number of cells with more than two imprinted gene                  markers in the nucleus. The five different grades                  for biallelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z16 are: Grade 0: biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z16 is less than 15%, Grade I: the                  biallelic expression of the imprinted gene Z16 is                  15-20%, grade II: the biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z16 is 20-26%, grade III: the                  biallelic expression of the imprinted gene Z16 is                  26-30%, grade IV: the biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z16 is greater than 30%, five                  different levels for the multi-allelic expression                  of the imprinted gene Z16 are: grade 0:                  multi-allelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z16 is less than 1.4%, grade I: the multi-allelic                  expression of the imprinted gene Z16 is 1.4-3.4%,                  grade II: the multi-allelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z16 is 3.4-5.5%, grade III: the                  multi-allelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z16 is 5.5-9%, grade IV: the multi-allelic                  expression of the imprinted gene Z16 is greater                  than 9%, two different grades for the total                  expression of the imprinted gene Z16 are: Grade                  0, total expression level of the imprinted gene                  Z16 is less than 17%, grade I: the total                  expression level of the imprinted gene Z16 is                  &#8805; 17%. The five different grades for                  the biallelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z19 are: Grade 0: the biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z19 is less than 12%, Grade I:                  biallelic expression of the imprinted gene Z19 is                  12-20%, grade II: biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z19 is 20-26%, grade III:                  biallelic expression of the imprinted gene Z19 is                  26-30%, grade IV: biallelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z19 is greater than 30%. The five                  different grades for the multi-allelic expression                  of the imprinted gene Z19 are: grade 0:                  multi-allelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z19 is less than 1.4%, grade I: multi-allelic                  expression of the imprinted gene Z19 is 1.4-3.4%,                  grade II: multi-allelic expression of the                  imprinted gene Z19 is 3.4-6.3%, grade III:                  multi-allelic expression of the imprinted gene                  Z19 is 6.3-9%, grade IV: multi-allelic expression                  of the imprinted gene Z19 is greater than 9%, two                  different grades for the total expression of the                  imprinted gene Z19 are: Grade 0: the total                  expression of the imprinted gene Z19 is less than                  11%, grade I: the total expression level of the                  imprinted gene Z19 is &#8805; 11%. The                  positive degree of imprinted genes Z16, Z19 and                  Z21 was divided into negative, positive                  potential, low positive, moderate positive and                  high positive. The result of judging the positive                  degree of the imprinted gene is that the total                  expression level of the imprinted gene is level                  0, or the total expression level of the imprinted                  gene is level I and the biallelic expression                  level and multi-allelic expression level are both                  level 0, negative for imprinted genes. The result                  of judging the positive degree of imprinted genes                  is that the total expression of imprinted genes                  is grade I and at least one of the biallelic                  expression and multi-allelic expression is grade                  I and neither of them reaches grade II, is the                  positive potential of imprinted gene. The result                  of judging the positive degree of imprinted genes                  is that the total expression level of imprinted                  genes is level I and at least one of the                  biallelic expression level and multi-allelic                  expression level is level II and neither of them                  reaches level III, is low positive for imprinted                  gene. The result of judging the positive degree                  of imprinted genes is that the total expression                  of imprinted genes is grade I and at least one of                  the biallelic expression and multi-allelic                  expression is grade III and neither of them                  reaches grade IV, is moderately positive for                  imprinted genes. If the result of judging the                  positive degree of imprinted genes is that the                  total expression level of imprinted genes is                  grade I and at least one of the biallelic                  expression level and multi-allelic expression                  level is level IV, then the imprinted gene is                  highly positive, where positive degrees of                  imprinted genes Z16, Z19 and Z21 are independent.                  The degree of benign and malignant tumors are                  divided into benign tumors, cancer potential,                  early cancer, mid-stage cancer and advanced                  cancer, if the result of judging the benign and                  malignant degree of the tumor is that the                  positive degree of imprinted genes Z16, Z19 and                  Z21 are all negative, or the positive degree of                  no more than one imprinted gene among imprinted                  genes Z16, Z19 and Z21 is positive potential,                  then it is a benign tumor. The result of judging                  the benign and malignant degree of the tumor is                  that the positive degree of at least two                  imprinted genes among imprinted genes Z16, Z19                  and Z21 is positive potential, or the positive                  degree of no more than one imprinted gene is low                  positive, which is cancer potential. If the                  result of judging the benign and malignant degree                  of the tumor is that at least two of the                  imprinted genes Z16, Z19 and Z21 are low                  positive, or no more than one imprinted gene is                  moderately positive, it is an early cancer. AB    NOVELTY - Use of GLS2K151 acetylation enzyme, a modified                form of glutamine synthetase 2 (GLS2) as a                biomarker in assessing or predicting the                sensitivity of tumor patients to                immunotherapy.
   USE - The GLS2K151 acetylation enzyme, a modified                form of glutamine synthetase 2 (GLS2)/GLS2K151                acetylated antibodies is used as a biomarker in                assessing or predicting the sensitivity of tumor                patients to immunotherapy. Can also be used in                preparation of tumor (e.g. oral cancer,                oropharyngeal cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer,                respiratory cancer, genitourinary cancer,                gastrointestinal cancer, central or peripheral                nervous system tissue cancer, endocrine or                neuroendocrine system cancer, hematopoietic system                cancer, glioma, sarcoma, epithelial cancer,                lymphoma, melanoma, fibroma, meningioma, brain                cancer, kidney cancer, biliary system cancer,                pheochromocytoma, islet cell carcinoma,                Leigh-Fraumeni tumor, thyroid cancer, parathyroid                cancer, pituitary tumor, adrenal tumor, osteogenic                sarcoma tumor, neuroendocrine system tumor, breast                cancer, lung cancer, head and neck cancer, prostate                cancer, esophageal cancer, tracheal cancer, liver                cancer, bladder cancer, gastric cancer, pancreatic                cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, cervical                cancer, testicular cancer, colon cancer, rectal                cancer or skin cancer) diagnostic kits (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The GLS2K151 acetylated antibodies can                diagnose the sensitivity of tumor immunotherapy by                detecting the expression level of GLS2K151                acetylation enzyme.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   a method for evaluating or predicting the                sensitivity of tumor patients to immunotherapy,                including detecting the expression level of                GLS2K151 acetylation in a sample from the tumor                patient, and evaluating or predicting the                sensitivity of the tumor patient to immunotherapy                based on the detection result; and
   a kit for quantitative or semi-quantitative                detection of proteins, containing an antibody that                can specifically bind to acetylated GLS2K151.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: In the method,                  achieving the detection of the expression level                  of GLS2K151 acetylation in the sample from the                  tumor patient by Elisa or Western Blot method.                  The kit capable of quantitatively or                  semi-quantitatively detecting proteins is a kit                  capable of detecting proteins by enzyme-linked                  immunosorbent assay (ELISA) or Western Blot, the                  kit contains a first antibody and a second                  antibody, the first antibody is an antibody                  capable of specifically binding to acetylated                  GLS2K151, and the second antibody is an                  enzyme-labeled antibody homologous to the first                  antibody. Preferred Method: In the method, the                  detection of the expression level of GLS2K151                  acetylation in the sample from the tumor patient                  is to detect the expression level of GLS2K151                  acetylation in the venous peripheral blood,                  paracancerous tissue and/or tumor tissue from the                  tumor patient. The evaluation or prediction of                  the sensitivity of tumor patients to                  immunotherapy based on the test results comprises                  when the test results show that GLS2K151                  acetylation is expressed in the sample, it is                  judged that the tumor patient is resistant to                  immunotherapy, conversely the tumor patient is                  not resistant to immunotherapy.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.

PN US6811995-B1
TI Non-invasive method to facilitate diagnosis of            cancer of epithelial origin e.g. cancers of lung, liver            or breast comprises detection of presence or absence of            a matrix metalloproteinase in an urine sample.
AU MOSES M A
   FREEMAN M R
   WIEDERSCHAIN D
AE CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
GA 2004774374
AB    NOVELTY - Non-invasive method for facilitating diagnosis                for a cancer of epithelial origin comprises                obtaining a urine sample from the subject and                detecting a presence or absence of a matrix                metalloproteinase (I) in the urine sample (where                (I) has a molecular weight from 50 kilo Daltons                (kDa) to equal to or greater than approximately 150                kDa) and the presence of (I) is indicative of the                presence of cancer of epithelial origin).
   USE - The method is useful for facilitating                diagnosis of a subject for a cancer of epithelial                origin (prostate cancer, cancer of the nervous                system, breast cancer, retina cancer, lung cancer,                skin cancer, kidney cancer, liver cancer,                pancreatic cancer, cancer of the genital urinary or                gastrointestinal tract and bladder cancer)(all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides biological markers to                non-invasively monitor the diagnosis and prognosis                of prostate disorders and other tissue                remodeling-associated conditions.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: (I) is a proenzyme                  (preferably a gelatinase).Preferred Method: The method further                  comprises removal of low molecular weight                  contaminants from the urine prior to the                  detection step. The urine is dialyzed in this                  method. The subject has previously been treated                  surgically or hormonally (preferably to block                  testosterone). (I) has a molecular weight of                  approximately 72 kDa (preferably approximately                  150 kDa). (I) is detected or monitored                  electrophoretically, immunochemically (preferably                  by a radioimmunoassay) or by an enzyme-linked                  immunosorbant assay. The electrophoretic pattern                  is a zymogram. The method detects the presence or                  absence of at least two matrix metalloproteinase                  (approximately 72-92 kDa (preferably 72 kDa                  matrix metalloproteinase)) in the urine                  sample.
   EXAMPLE - Urine samples were obtained from subjects with                clinically determined prostate cancer (13 subjects)                and with no history of cancer (13 subjects). Urine                samples were kept frozen until assay, thawed                overnight at 4 C, and a 10 ml aliquot was dialyzed                against double-distilled water in 45 mm dialysis                tubing (Spectra/Por membrane MWCO: 3,500, Spectrum,                Houston, Tex.). Urine samples were centrifuged at                4,000 rpm for 5 minutes at 4 C, the supernatant was                taken and stored at 4 C prior to analysis. Analysis                of urine for enzyme activity was by zymography,                comprising gel electrophoresis performed in the                presence of enzyme substrate followed by in situ                digestion. Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis in                the presence of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and                0.1% (w/v) gelatin was used. A sample comprising 30                micro liters of dialyzed urine was mixed with 15                micro liters of sample buffer consisting of 4% SDS,                0.15 Tris pH 6.8, 20% (v/v) glycerol, and 0.5%                (w/v) bromophenol blue. Samples were applied to                slots in a 4% stacking gel above a 10%                polyacrylamide separating gel on a mini-gel slab                gel apparatus (Mini-Protein II, Bio-Rad). Following                electrophoresis, gels were incubated for 30 minutes                in 2.5% Triton X-100 (v/v) to remove SDS, rinsed,                and incubated overnight at 37 C in substrate buffer                (0.05 M Tris, pH 8.5, 5 mM CaCl2, 0.02% sodium                azide). To visualize bands of active enzyme, were                stained for protein in 0.5% (w/v) Coomassie Blue                R-250 in acetic acid:isopropanol:water (1:3:6),                then destained in acetic acid ethanol water                (1:3:6). The electrophoretic mobility of each clear                band was determined by correlation with molecular                weight protein standards and positive controls                (purified mmp2 and mmp-9 proteins). The molecular                weight of each band of active enzyme was recorded.                The identity of these MMPs was confirmed by western                blot analysis using anti-MMP antibodies (Oncogene                Sciences, Cambridge, Mass.). To verify that enzyme                activity observed by zymography detected were                metal-dependent proteases, samples were subjected                also to incubation in substrate buffer in the                presence of 1,10-phenanthroline, an MMP inhibitor.                Samples of urine from 13 young healthy male                subjects revealed 8 positives of 52 possible                metalloproteinase bands (15%, Table 1). Thus, 4 of                13 (31%) healthy subjects had detectable gelatinase                activity in urine. Analysis of the distribution of                the enzyme activity shows that none of the urine                samples contained enzyme activity of 72 kDa size.                Analysis of urine of prostate cancer patients (CaP)                showed gelatinase in 12 of the 13 samples. 92% of                urine from CaP patients contained a band of 92 kDa                or higher molecular weight, and 48% of the 52                possible zymogram activity categories are positive                for the CaP group. These frequencies are over                3-fold higher than comparable findings for the                urine from the normal controls.

The                  heterogeneous breast phantom simulates the breast                  tissue under a medical imaging technique. The                  medical imaging technique is magnetic resonance                  imaging (MRI), computed tomography scan (CT                  scan), or both. At least one of the molds is                  produced via three dimensional printing.

TI New monoclonal enabling detection of TP53INP1            protein, useful in manufacturing a drug for the            prognosis or diagnosis of cancers and/or of            precancerous lesions, or for the screening of drugs            active on cancers.
AU CARRIER A
   PEBUSQUE M
AE INSERM INST NAT SANTE & RECH MEDICALE (INRM-C)
GA 2005747406
AB    NOVELTY - New monoclonal antibody secreted by the                hybridoma deposited under the Budapest Treaty at                the CNCM (Collection Nationale de Culture de                Microorganismes, Institut Pasteur, Paris, France)                on March 26, 2004, under accession number CNCM                1-3194.
   USE - The compound which enables detection of the                substantial lack of expression of the TP53INP1                protein in a biological sample is useful in                manufacturing a drug for the prognosis or the                diagnosis of cancers and/or of precancerous                lesions, or for the screening of drugs active on                cancers. The kit and method are useful for                diagnosing cancers and/or of precancerous lesions,                where the cancers or precancerous lesions are                selected from epithelial cancers comprising                pancreas cancer, colon cancer, lung cancer,                prostate cancer, bladder cancer, breast cancer,                uterine cervix cancer, ovary cancer, head and neck                cancer, oral cancer, skin cancer, kidney cancer,                thyroid cancer, stomach cancer, conjunctiva-cornea                cancer, glioma, thymoma, or neuroblastoma, or from                precancerous lesions arising from inflammatory                bowel disease (IBD), such as ulcerative colitis                (UC) or Crohn's disease, or endo-brachy-oesophagus                (EBO) (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   a cancer prognosis or diagnosis kit comprising                at least one anti-TP53INPl (Tumor Protein p53                Induced Nuclear Protein) protein antibody, in                particular a labeled anti-TP53INPl protein                antibody, and a sample of the TP53INP1 protein as a                control or a reference;
   a method for the in vitro diagnosis of cancers                at an early stage, of cancers, or of precancerous                lesions; and
   an anti-cancer drug screening method.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Compound: The compound enables the                  detection of the substantial lack of expression                  of the TP53INP1 protein in a biological sample,                  for the manufacture of a drug intended for the                  diagnosis of cancers at an early stage or for the                  manufacture of a drug intended to differentiate                  malignant tumors, in particular early stage                  malignant tumors, or precancerous lesions, from                  healthy tissues and benign tumors. The compound                  enables the detection of the substantial absence                  of the TP53INP1 mRNA and/or of the TP53INP1                  protein. The compound is liable to bind to the                  TP53INP1 mRNA and/or to the TP53INP1 protein. The                  TP53INP1 mRNA or protein corresponds to the mRNA                  or to the protein of TP53INP1 isoforms, such as                  the TPSSINP1&#945; mRNA or protein, or the                  TP53INP1&#946; mRNA or protein. The compound                  is a monoclonal or a polyclonal antibody which                  binds to the TP53INP1&#945; protein and/or to                  the TP53TNP1&#946; protein. The compound                  comprises at least one nucleotide sequence, the                  nucleotide sequence containing at least 10                  contiguous nucleotides selected from a sequence                  comprising 5625 or 5587 bp (SEQ ID NOS: 1 or 3),                  or from the sequence complementary to SEQ ID NOS:                  1 or 3, or at least one sequence derived from one                  of the nucleotide sequence, by insertion,                  deletion or substitution of at least one                  nucleotide and presenting at least 90% similarity                  with the nucleotide sequence of SEQ ID NOS: 1 or                  3. Detection is carried out with a method                  selected from PCR, real-time PCR, RT-PCR, NASBA,                  Northern Blot, in situhybridization, chromatin                  precipitation, ELISA, Western Blot, far Western                  protein interaction assay, immunoprecipitation,                  FACS, flow cytometry, cytochemistry,                  cytofluorescence, immunofluorescence, or                  immunohistochemistry. Preferred Method: In vitro                  diagnosis of cancers at an early stage, of                  cancers, or of precancerous lesions comprises                  contacting a tissue sample taken from an                  individual with a anti-TP53INPl protein antibody,                  in particular a monoclonal antibody of (1),                  washing the tissue sample, and revealing the                  presence, or the absence, of the antibody, in the                  washed sample, the substantial absence of the                  antibody in the washed sample as compared to a                  sample of a corresponding healthy tissue being an                  indication that the tissue is afflicted with a                  cancer at an early stage, with a cancer, or with                  a precancerous lesion. Anti-cancer drug screening                  method which comprises contacting a sample of                  precancerous or cancerous cells, in which the                  TP53INP1 protein is substantially absent, with a                  molecule liable to be an anti-cancer drug,                  detecting the substantial presence or the                  substantial absence of the TP53INP1 protein, in                  the cell sample which has been contacted with the                  molecule to screen, with an antibody of (1), and                  selecting the molecule responsible for the                  presence of the TP53INP1 protein in the cells, as                  an anti-cancer drug.

The amino acid in the X amino acid                sequence is C, G or N.
   USE - The polypeptide nano-magnetic nano-particles                are useful in medicine and/or medical product for                diagnosing and treating cancer including esophageal                cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer, gastric cancer,                breast cancer, colorectal cancer, cervical cancer,                thyroid cancer, prostate cancer, pancreatic cancer,                renal cancer, bladder cancer, skin cancer,                melanoma; preferably breast cancer, esophageal                cancer, gastric cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer,                colorectal cancer, cervical cancer and/or prostate                cancer, and medicine for circulating tumor cell                detection and/or molecular type of biomarker                including programmed death-ligand 1, protein called                human epidermal growth factor receptor 2, estrogen                receptor, progesterone receptor, androgen receptor,                epidermal growth factor receptor, vascular                endothelial growth factor receptors and CXC                chemokine receptor 4.
   ADVANTAGE - The polypeptide magnetic nanoparticle is                helpful for CTC detection and the qualitative and                semiquantitative analysis of expression levels of                biomarkers at CTC level, thus performing precise                therapy i.e. targeted individualized targeted                therapy or immunotherapy on patients.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                preparation method of polypeptide magnetic                nano-particle comprising (i) preparing polypeptide                and magnetic nanoparticle solution, and (ii) mixing                the polypeptide with the magnetic nanoparticle                solution to obtain the polypeptide magnetic                nano-particle.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The polypeptide is a                  specific recognition polypeptide targeting                  epithelial cell adhesion molecule. The magnetic nano-particle is magnetic                  nano-particle with streptavidin. The magnetic                  nanoparticle has grain diameter of 100-900 nm and                  particle diameter of 300-800 nm. In the step (i),                  the solvent for preparing the polypeptide                  solution is water, physiological saline, PBS,                  HEPES; and/or water, PBS or HEPES. In the step                  (ii), the final concentration of the polypeptide                  solution is 1-1000 &#956; g/ml, preferably                  100-500 &#956; g/ml, and/or final                  concentration of the magnetic nano-particle                  solution is 1-10000 &#956; g/ml, preferably                  1000-5000 &#956; g/ml. In the step (2), the                  mass ratio of the polypeptide and the magnetic                  nano-particle is 1:10-5:1, preferably is                  2:5.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

The method enables greatly reducing                diagnostic error rates, when cutting-edge deep                learning algorithms are combined with                Internet-of-Things technology. The method enables                combining the imaging data with additional patient                information, including medical history and genetic                information, and improving diagnosis' precision and                efficacy.

TI System for classifying skin cancer from            dermoscopic images using convolution neural network            algorithm for petrained architectures, such as ResNet,            has output module configured to classify skin lesions            into malignant melanoma or benign categories.
AU PANT I
   TRIPATHI V
   YADAV A
   NIGAM S
   SHARMA N
AE GL BAJAJ TECHNOLOGY & MANAGEMENT INST (GLBA-Non-standard)
GA 2025B96988
AB    NOVELTY - The system comprises a reprocessing module                configured to normalize and resize dermoscopic                images. A machine learning classification model                includes a convolutional neural network trained on                dermoscopic image datasets. An output module is                configured to classify skin lesions into malignant                melanoma or benign categories. The machine learning                classification model is a convolutional neural                network (CNN) trained using dermoscopic datasets                including ISIC. The transfer learning is employed                using pre-trained models selected from ResNet,                efficient net, or MobileNet. The performance is                evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and                F1-score. The CNN model is configured for offline                operation to ensure data privacy.
   USE - System for classifying skin cancer from                dermoscopic images using convolution neural network                (CNN) algorithm for petrained architectures, such                as ResNet. Uses include but are not limited to                EfficientNet and MobileNet.
   ADVANTAGE - The early detection of melanoma is                facilitated, which results in increased survival                rates for patients. The diagnostic tool is                efficient and non-invasive, as well as low-cost for                dermatologists. The system's performance is                measured using recognized statistical analysis of                accurate classification, precision, recall, and the                F1-score to provide the confidence, that the system                is not defective. The system is extremely versatile                and can be deployed on numerous systems such as the                cloud, mobile, and embedded systems. The system                streamlines the entire process of screening for                dermatologists, thus reduces the overall burden on                the healthcare system, while improving patient                outcomes through timely action. The device makes                the entire process simple by providing features on                a mobile application, web, or hospital                system.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for classifying skin cancer.

AB    NOVELTY - Identifying preneoplastic or neoplastic tissue                of a mammal, comprises detecting autoantibodies                complexed to antigen at the tissue, where an                increase in the amount of autoantibodies complexed                to antigen at the tissue, as compared to that at a                control tissue, is indicative that the tissue is                preneoplastic or neoplastic.
   USE - The method is useful for identifying                preneoplastic or neoplastic tissue of a mammal                including a human, where the preneoplastic or                neoplastic tissue is liver, skin, breast or                prostate tissue (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method: allows the detection of both                preneoplastic and neoplastic tissue, thus providing                an earlier detection of neoplasia; provides                sensitive detection of altered cells at the                margins; and is a non-invasive way to diagnose                cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: In the method: the                  detecting is done intra-operatively, or prior to                  surgery; and the autoantibodies are detected                  using an antibody detection reagent. Preferred                  Components: The tissue: is in the body of the                  mammal; or that has been explanted from the                  mammal, where the explant is a fresh explant, a                  frozen explant or a fixed explant. The                  autoantibodies are labeled with a label. The                  label on the antibody is an optical reporter, a                  positron-emission tomography reporter, MRI                  reporter, or a biochemical marker. The antibody                  detection reagent is anti-immunoglobulin (Ig)-G,                  protein A, protein G, fragment antigen-binding                  (Fab)(2) fragment of anti-IgG, Fab(1) of                  anti-IgG, a humanized mouse anti-human IgG,                  peptides that bind to the fragment crystallizable                  (Fc) region of antibodies, small molecules that                  recognize IgG for the species of interest, or                  small molecules that bind the Fc region. The                  autoantibodies and tissue are: autologous; or                  heterologous but are from at least one individual                  of the same species. The preneoplastic or                  neoplastic tissue is in the liver. The neoplastic                  tissue is a fibrolamellar hepatocellular                  carcinoma. The neoplastic tissue is a liver,                  skin, breast or prostate cancer.

PN WO2025128926-A1; WO2025128926-A9
TI Treating individual at risk for incidence or            recurrence of cancer e.g. teratoid and throat cancer,            by identifying individual, analyzing biological sample            using multi-cancer detection test and administering            neoantigen immunogenic composition to individual at            risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer.
AU TANG H
   SCHMITZ F W
   HECKERMAN D
   WALKER M
   SOOD N
   HEIT A
   PRICE L C
   IMATA SAFO A
   DANZIGER S A
   HARLEY A
   SARKIS B
   STOCKWELL S M
   HOANE B Y
AE AMAZON TECHNOLOGIES INC (AMAZ-C)
GA 2025630183
AB    NOVELTY - Method of treating an individual at risk for                incidence or recurrence of cancer, involves (a)                identifying the individual at risk for incidence or                recurrence of cancer based on a risk stratification                parameter, (b) analyzing a biological sample from                the individual at risk for incidence or recurrence                of cancer using a multi-cancer detection (MCD) test                to yield an multi-cancer detection (MCD) test                result, and (c) administering a neoantigen                immunogenic composition to the individual at risk                for incidence or recurrence of cancer based on the                MCD test result and optionally the risk                stratification parameter.
   USE - The method is used for treating an individual                at risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer,                where the individual at risk for incidence or                recurrence of cancer is diagnosed with a cancer                that is chronic lymphocytic leukemia, ductal                carcinoma in situ (DCIS), hormone receptor-positive                breast cancer, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, prostate                cancer, or rectal cancer, the individual at risk                for incidence or recurrence of cancer is diagnosed                with stage 0 cancer, stage I cancer, or carcinoma                in-situ, and the individual at risk for incidence                or recurrence of cancer is diagnosed with a                pre-cancer or a benign cancer (all claimed), and                cancers include, for example, adrenocortical                carcinoma, anal cancer, appendiceal cancer,                astrocytoma, basal cell carcinoma, brain tumor,                bile duct cancer, bladder cancer, embryonal tumor,                endometrial cancer, ependymoma, esophageal cancer,                esthesioneuroblastoma, fibrous histiocytoma, Ewing                sarcoma, eye cancer, germ cell tumor, clonal                eosinophilias, lip and oral cavity cancer, skin                cancer, small cell lung cancer, small intestine                cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, spinal cord tumor,                stomach cancer, T-cell lymphoma, teratoid tumor,                testicular cancer, throat cancer, thymoma and                thymic carcinoma, thyroid cancer, urethral cancer,                uterine cancer, vaginal cancer, vulvar cancer, and                Wilms tumor. Test details are described but no                results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method treats individuals at high or                elevated risk for developing cancer or at high risk                of cancer recurrence with treatments that can                delay, prevent, or cure cancer. The method has few                or no side effects to allow for the early                intervention in individuals at risk for incidence                or recurrence of cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The biological sample                  from the individual at risk for incidence or                  recurrence of cancer is an amniotic fluid sample,                  an ascitic fluid sample, a blood sample, a buccal                  sample, a cerebrospinal fluid sample, a fecal                  sample, a hair sample, a peritoneal fluid sample,                  a pleural effusion sample, a saliva sample, a                  semen sample, a synovial fluid sample, a tissue                  sample and/or a urine sample, preferably blood                  sample. The biological sample is a tissue sample                  from a tissue biopsy of a tumor or surgical                  tissue resection of a tumor.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The risk stratification                  parameter is age, sex, family medical history,                  medications, germ-line mutations, somatic                  mutations, exposure to carcinogens, exposure to                  radiation, medical history and/or previous cancer                  diagnosis. The MCD test analyzes nucleic acid                  methylation, nucleic acid mutation, nucleic acid                  fragmentation patterns, extracellular vesicle                  proteins, nucleic acid of circulating tumor                  cells, gene expression and/or circulating cancer                  antigens. The MCD test comprises nucleic acid                  sequencing of the biological sample from the                  individual at risk for incidence or recurrence of                  cancer. The MCD test analyzes a nucleic acid that                  is cell free DNA (cfDNA), circulating tumor DNA                  (ctDNA), cell free RNA (cfRNA) and/or circulating                  tumor RNA (ctRNA). The method further comprises                  sequencing and analyzing of the biological sample                  from the individual at risk for incidence or                  recurrence of cancer or a new biological sample                  from the individual at risk for incidence or                  recurrence of cancer to identify neoantigens to                  be included in the neoantigen immunogenic                  composition. The method further comprises                  determining the human leukocyte antigen (HLA)                  type for the individual at risk for incidence or                  recurrence of cancer, scoring neoantigens of the                  biological sample from the individual at risk for                  incidence or recurrence of cancer, selecting                  neoantigens of the biological sample for                  inclusion in the neoantigen immunogenic                  composition, and/or generating the neoantigen                  immunogenic composition. The individual at risk                  for incidence or recurrence of cancer is a cancer                  survivor. The conventional standard of care for                  the individual at risk for incidence or                  recurrence of cancer at the time of practicing                  the method is no treatment. The individual at                  risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer has                  not been diagnosed with a cancer prior to the                  step of analyzing the biological sample. No tumor                  has been located in the individual at risk for                  incidence or recurrence of cancer. The individual                  at risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer is                  diagnosed with cancer of unknown origin. The                  conventional standard of care for the individual                  at risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer                  does not include surgery, radiation,                  chemotherapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy,                  hormone therapy, photodynamic therapy and/or cell                  therapy. The method further comprises analyzing a                  second biological sample from the individual at                  risk for incidence or recurrence of cancer using                  a second multi-cancer detection test during a                  course of treatment to determine efficacy of the                  neoantigen immunogenic composition. A negative                  test result for the second MCD test indicates the                  neoantigen immunogenic composition is                  efficacious. The step (b) and optionally step (c)                  are repeated at least once over a course of                  treatment for the individual at risk for                  incidence or recurrence of cancer. The method                  further comprises sequencing nucleic acids of the                  biological sample to yield non-cancer sequencing                  results and cancer sequencing results, wherein                  the non-cancer sequencing results are subtracted                  from the cancer sequencing results to improve the                  signal to noise ratio for variant calling of                  neoantigens. The method further comprises                  administering a co-therapy or procedure that (i)                  is not the neoantigen immunogenic composition and                  (ii) is a radiation treatment, a surgical                  procedure, a chemotherapeutic, an immunotherapy,                  a targeted therapy, a hormone therapy, a                  photodynamic therapy and/or a cell therapy.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

TI Microwave thermoacoustic imaging device for            detecting breast cancer, has flexible detector which            includes flexible substrate which is bent and deformed            to fit shape of surface of breast but can not be            stretched.
AU XING D
   ZHAO Y
   JI Z
   YANG S
   DING W
AE UNIV SOUTH CHINA NORMAL (USCN-C)
   UNIV SOUTH CHINA NORMAL (USCN-C)
GA 2016710370
AB    NOVELTY - The device has a flexible detector (1-2) which                includes a flexible substrate which is bent and                deformed to fit the shape of the surface of the                breast but can not be stretched. Several array                elements are distributed on a flexible substrate to                receive ultrasonic signal reflected from breast. A                pulse microwave generator that transmits microwave                signals to the mammary gland, a data acquisition                and image reconstruction components are connected                with the array element of the flexible detector. A                rotating scan detection assembly causes a flexible                probe to surround a breast to be scanned.
   USE - Microwave thermal acoustic imaging device for                detecting breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The device is provided with simple structure,                small volume, light weight, low cost, small energy                consumption, and has safety, high efficiency, high                resolution, high contrast. The detection process is                comfortable, can make a preliminary detection of                breast cancer. The clinical application of thermo                acoustic technology is promoted widely. The high                flexibility of the flexible detector also provides                a good foundation for the control of the relative                motion of the skin and the damage to the skin. The                internal scanning device can make the flexible                detector move up and down relative to the breast,                and the three-dimensional image of the entire                breast can be scanned according to the motion. The                confined space is formed by the microwave absorbing                layer between housing and the base of microwave to                avoid damage to the human body and the surrounding                equipment, thus thermoacoustic process is carried                out under microwave leak enclosed equipment.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for Microwave                thermal acoustic imaging method for detecting                breast cancer.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic diagram of the                rotating scanning detection component.
   Housing (1-1)
   Flexible detector (1-2)
   End head (1-3)
   Base (1-4)
   Rotary drive motor (1-5)

PT P
PN WO200248395-A1; AU200215689-A; EP1352085-A1; US2004067542-A1; ZA200304853-A; JP2004520025-W; CN1533440-A; AU2002215689-B2; US2008227122-A1; EP1352085-B1; DE60138415-E; JP2009143933-A; JP4334223-B2; CN100448486-C; EP1352085-A4
TI Diagnosing or staging pre-neoplastic and/or            neoplastic state in mammal, by detecting P2Y purinergic            receptor expression profile of cell and/or tissue and            comparing profile with predetermined expression            profile.
AU BARDEN J
   SLATER M
AE BIOSCEPTRE PTY LTD (BIOS-Non-standard)
   BARDEN J (BARD-Individual)
   SLATER M (SLAT-Individual)
   BIOSCEPTRE PTY LTD (BIOS-Non-standard)
   BIOSCEPTRE PTY LTD (BIOS-Non-standard)
GA 2002583534
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing or staging (M1) pre-neoplastic                and/or neoplastic state in a mammal, comprising                detection of the P2Y purinergic receptor expression                profile of a cell and/or tissue from the mammal and                comparison of the profile with a predetermined                expression profile of a normal cell and/or tissue,                is new.
   USE - M1 is useful for diagnosing or staging of a                pre-neoplastic and/or neoplastic state in a mammal.                M2 is useful for determining the aetiology of                carcinogenesis in a mammal. In M1 and M2, the                mammal is a human, horse, bovine animal, sheep,                dog, cat, rat, or a mouse, preferably a human. The                cell and/or tissue is from a prostate, breast, skin                or other epithelial source. The pre-neoplastic or                neoplastic state is prostate, breast or skin                pre-cancer or prostate, breast or skin cancer and                an increase, or decrease in the intensity of the                P2Y 2 purinergic receptor expression profile in a                prostate cell or prostate tissue, or breast or skin                cell and/or breast or skin tissue obtained from the                mammal, compared to the expression profile of a                normal prostate cell or tissue, or breast or skin                cell and/or breast or skin tissue from a normal                breast or skin, is diagnostic of the presence of                prostate, breast or skin pre-cancer or prostate,                breast or skin cancer. The skin cancer is malignant                melanoma, squamous cell carcinoma or basal cell                carcinoma. (I) or (II) is useful for diagnosing or                staging of a pre-neoplastic and/or neoplastic state                in a mammal and for determining the aetiology of                carcinogenesis in a mammal, and to differentiate                between pre-neoplastic or neoplastic cells and/or                tissue and normal cells and/or tissue, where the                cell and/or tissue is obtained by biopsy. The                biopsy is taken by fine needle aspirate, from a                body fluid, or in the case of a prostate cell                and/or tissue, from digital rectal examination                (DRE) exudate or from semen. (All claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   determining (M2) the aetiology of                carcinogenesis in a mammal as in M1;
   a P2Y purinergic receptor-specific antibody                (I) is capable of differentiating between a                pre-neoplastic or neoplastic cell and/or tissue and                a normal cell and/or tissue;
   a suite (II) comprising (I);
   an isolated mammalian cell or tissue sample                (III) complexed with (I) or (II); and
   a kit (IV) for diagnosing or staging a                pre-neoplastic and/or neoplastic state, or for                determining the aetiology of carcinogenesis in a                mammal comprises unit for detecting P2Y purinergic                receptor expression profile.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In M1 and M2, the P2Y                  receptor expression profile is the P2Y 2, P2Y                  4and/or P2Y 6receptor expression profile,                  preferably P2Y2 receptor expression profile. The                  pre-neoplastic state is an early or advanced                  pre-neoplastic state in which the P2Y receptor                  expression profile is altered in the nucleus of                  the cell, or is a profile in which the P2Y                  receptors are in the cytoplasm and/or lateral                  membranes and/or basal membranes. The neoplastic                  state is a state in which the P2Y receptor                  expression profile is a profile where the P2Y                  receptors are on the apical membrane of an                  epithelial cell. The P2Y receptor expression                  profile is combined with the expression profile                  of other markers, P2X receptor expression profile                  or with an expression profile of P2X 1and/or P2X                  2. The P2Y receptor expression profile is                  detected by immunohistochemical unit, Western or                  Northern blotting techniques, enzyme linked                  immunosorbent assay (ELISA) or radio immunoassay                  (RIA), or colorimetric assay. M1 and M2 are                  combined with a complementary test which is a                  test for malignancy. The test for malignancy is                  an anti-telomerase antibody test using a specific                  antibody against human telomerase protein 1 (hTP                  1) or an anti-tenascin test.Preferred Antibody: (I) is specific for P2Y                  2, P2Y 4and/or P2Y 6receptors, preferably P2Y                  2receptors. (I) is a monoclonal or polyclonal                  antibody. (I) is combined with at least one other                  antibody. At least one other antibody is P2Y                  receptor-specific antibody or P2X                  receptor-specific antibody. The P2X receptor                  antibody is a P2X 1or P2X 2receptor-specific                  antibody. At least one other antibody is a                  monoclonal or polyclonal antibody.Preferred Kit: In (IV), the unit for                  detecting a P2Y purinergic receptor expression                  profile is (I) or (II). The cell and/or tissue                  from the mammal is proximal to a pre-neoplastic                  or neoplastic cell and is not itself                  pre-neoplastic or neoplastic.
   EXAMPLE - The consensus sequences of the human P2Y                2[12], human P2Y 4[13], and human P2Y 6[14] cloned                receptors were examined for suitable epitopes. The                non-homologous epitope corresponding to the segment                Leu226-Lys242 in P2Y 2was used, with the comparable                sequences in P2Y 4(Arg226-Arg242) and P2Y                6(Cys220-Lys236). Each was attached to diphtheria                toxoid by maleimidocaproyl-N-hydroxysuccinimide                crosslinker through adding an N-terminal Cys to P2Y                2, and P2Y 4epitopes. All synthesis were carried                out. The peptide-antigen conjugates were suspended                in water at 5 mg/mL and aliquots emulsified.                Emulsion volumes of 1 mL containing 2 mg of peptide                were injected intramuscularly with second, third,                fourth and fifth immunizations followed at 2 week                intervals using incomplete Freund's adjuvant. Final                bleeds by venepuncture were obtained at 10-12                weeks, after it was established that adequate                antibody titers had been obtained in the rabbits or                sheep used for each epitope. The blood was                incubated and stored after which the serum was                collected following centrifugation and stored at                -20 &#176;C in small aliquots. Sera were tested                with enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for                antibodies specific for each peptide. The antibody                titer, defined as the reciprocal of the serum                dilution resulting in an absorbance of 1.0 above                background in the ELISA assay, was in the range                75000&#177;4000 compared with 225&#177;25                for the preimmune samples. Each antibody was found                to be specific against the particular subtype.                Affinity purification of each of the antibodies                against the specific epitopes for that antibody                resulted in reduced background but identical                labeling trends. A monoclonal antibody raised                against the same P2Y 2epitope in mice yielded the                same results.

TI Deep learning-based system for skin cancer            classification using dermoscopic image, is trained on            annotated dermoscopic datasets for multi-class            prediction including melanoma, basal cell carcinoma,            squamous cell carcinoma, and benign nevi.
AU KHAN Z A N
   MAYIGOWDA P
AE UNIV BENGALURU PRESIDENCY (UYBE-Non-standard)
   KHAN Z A N (KHAN-Individual)
   MAYIGOWDA P (MAYI-Individual)
GA 202579163N
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a residual neural block, a                depthwise separable convolutional block, a                layer-wise integration mechanism, an attention                module, and a classification head. The system is                trained on annotated dermoscopic datasets for                multi-class prediction including melanoma, basal                cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and benign                nevi. Residual and Xception blocks are stacked                alternately to balance depth and computational                efficiency. Model provides interpretability through                class activation mapping. The system is deployed on                cloud or edge infrastructure with support for open                neural network exchange (ONNX) or TensorFlow(RTM:                Free and open-source software library) Lite.
   USE - Deep learning-based system for skin cancer                classification using dermoscopic image for                dermatological application.
   ADVANTAGE - Dermoscopic images are fed into the model,                which outputs the cancer class along with visual                explanations. The invention improves diagnostic                reliability and provides a deployable artificial                intelligence (AI) framework for dermatological                applications. The residual blocks enable better                gradient flow, whereas the Xception modules reduce                computation using depthwise separable convolutions,                ensuring fast training and inference. The                layer-wise integration ensures that intermediate                features from multiple depths are aggregated,                allowing the model to learn both local and global                features relevant to cancer detection. The model                combines the strengths of residual learning and                depthwise separable convolutions and introduces a                layer-wise integration mechanism to enhance                gradient flow, reduce overfitting, and improve                classification accuracy. The robust system is                deployable in clinical decision support                tools.

AB    NOVELTY - The fluorescence imaging system comprises a                light source module (110) for irradiating a sample                (10) with a light source corresponding to an                absorption wavelength of a fluorescent agent, and a                wavelength detection unit (120) for detecting                wavelength of fluorescence generated in the sample                and which is composed of an optical fiber-based                spectroscope (122). A wavelength tunable filter                unit (130) selectively adjusts a transmission                wavelength to pass only the light having a                wavelength corresponding to the emission                fluorescence of the sample. A fluorescence signal                detection unit (140) detects the emission                fluorescence transmitted through the tunable                filter. A control unit (150) adjusts the                transmission wavelength of variable filter unit in                accordance with a detection signal of the                wavelength detection unit.
   USE - Fluorescence imaging system with wavelength                tunable filter combined with optical fiber based                spectroscopy system, for observing various cancers                such as breast cancer and skin cancer and finding                position of correct lesion during surgery in                real-time in a non-invasive manner, and for                carrying out auto-fluorescence method in dental                clinic, etc.
   ADVANTAGE - The fluorescence signal is filtered                efficiently, and the fluorescence acquisition                efficiency is improved. The fluorescence image                saturation due to the intensity of light source                generating the absorbed light is removed actively,                to obtain a high-quality fluorescence image in                real-time.

TI Analyzing a genetically modified T cell to detect            a contaminant, where the genetically modified T cell            comprises a nucleic acid encoding a chimeric antigen            receptor.

GA 2014B55868
AB    NOVELTY - Analyzing a genetically modified T cell to                detect a contaminant, where the genetically                modified T cell comprises a nucleic acid encoding a                chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), where the CAR                comprises an antigen binding domain, a                transmembrane domain, a costimulatory signaling                region, and a signaling domain.
   USE - The method is used for analyzing a genetically                modified T cell to detect a contaminant (claimed).                The T cell is used for autoimmune diseases                including, but not limited to, alopecia areata,                ulcerative colitis, diabetes (Type I),                glomerulonephritis, Graves' disease, hemolytic                anemia, multiple sclerosis, myasthenia gravis,                psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, and rheumatic                fever; and cancer including, but not limited to,                breast cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian cancer,                cervical cancer, skin cancer, pancreatic cancer,                colorectal cancer, renal cancer, liver cancer, and                brain cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - A method for analyzing transduced T cells for                their suitability for administration to a human                subject, through the detection of contaminants that                may negatively impact the persistence and function                of genetically modified cells, is provided.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method above, the                  genetically modified T cell was genetically                  modified by transduction with a lentiviral                  vector. The contaminant is at least one selected                  from endotoxin, Mycoplasma, replication competent                  lentivirus (RCL), p24, G glycoprotein of the                  vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV-G) nucleic acid,                  HIV gag, residual anti-CD3/anti-CD28 coated                  beads, mouse antibodies, pooled human serum,                  bovine serum albumin, bovine serum, culture media                  components, vector packaging cell or plasmid                  components, a bacterium and a fungus. The                  bacterium is at least one selected from                  Alcaligenes faecalis, Candida albicans,                  Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenza,                  Neisseria meningitides, Pseudomonas aeruginosa,                  Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumonia,                  and Streptococcus pyogenesgroup A. The signaling                  domain is a CD3 zeta signaling domain. The                  antigen binding domain is an antibody or its                  antigen-binding fragment, antigen-binding                  fragment is a Fab or a single chain variable                  fragment (scFv). The antigen binding domain binds                  to a tumor antigen. The tumor antigen is                  associated with a hematologic malignancy or a                  solid tumor. The tumor antigen is selected from                  CD19, CD20, CD22, receptor tyrosine kinase-like                  orphan receptor 1 (ROR1), mesothelin,                  CD33/interleukin 3 receptor &#945; (IL3Ra),                  c-Met, prostate specific membrane antigen (PSMA),                  Glycolipid F77, epidermal growth factor receptor                  (EGFR)vIII, GD-2, NY-ESO-1 TCR, melanoma antigen                  gene (MAGE) A3 TCR, and their combination. The                  costimulatory signaling region comprises the                  intracellular domain of a costimulatory molecule                  selected from CD27, CD28, 4-1BB, OX40, CD30,                  CD40, Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1),                  inducible T-cell co-stimulator (ICOS), lymphocyte                  function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1), CD2, CD7,                  LIGHT, killer cell lectin-like receptor subfamily                  C, member 2 (NKG2C), B7-H3, a ligand that                  specifically binds with CD83, and their                  combination. The genetically modified T cell is                  not administered to a human subject because of                  the identification and quantification of the                  contaminant or because the quantity of the                  contaminant is excessive as compared with a                  corresponding control level.
   ACTIVITY - Immunosuppressive; Antipyretic; Antirheumatic;                Antiinflammatory; Antiulcer; Gastrointestinal-Gen;                Antidiabetic; Nephrotropic; Antithyroid;                Antianemic; Neuroprotective; Muscular-Gen;                Antipsoriatic; Antiarthritic; Cytostatic. Test                details are described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Cell Therapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - Dosage is 10 4to 10 9cells/kg, by aerosol                inhalation, injection, ingestion, transfusion,                implantation or transplantation. The composition                may be administered to a patient subcutaneously,                intradermally, intratumorally, intranodally,                intramedullary, intramuscularly, by intravenous                injection, or intraperitoneally.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.
DC B04 (Natural products and polymers. Including testing of body fluids (other than blood typing or cell counting), pharmaceuticals or veterinary compounds of unknown structure, testing of microorganisms for pathogenicity, testing of chemicals for mutagenicity or human toxicity and fermentative production of DNA or RNA. General compositions.); D16 (Fermentation industry - including fermentation equipment, brewing, yeast production, production of pharmaceuticals and other chemicals by fermentation, microbiology, production of vaccines and antibodies, cell and tissue culture and genetic engineering.)
