TI Determining cancer-related parameters in tissue or            cell sample obtained from subject is carried out with            help of kit used in detection of cancer, cancer is            blastoma, leukemia, involves determining engulfment of            particles by cells in sample.
AU BENNY O
   BRILL KARNIELY Y
   BRILL K Y
AE YISSUM RES DEV CO HEBREW UNIV JERUSALEM (YISS-C)
   YISSUM RES DEV CO HEBREW UNIV JERUSALEM (YISS-C)
   YISSUM RES DEV CO HEBREW UNIV JERUSALEM (YISS-C)
GA 202139258T
AB    NOVELTY - Determining cancer-related parameter in a                tissue or cells sample obtained from a subject                involves determining engulfment or uptake of                particles by cells in the sample having been                treated or contacted with a particle population                comprising two different particle sub-populations,                each of particle sub-population being                distinguishable from the other by a different                physical parameter and a different identifiable                barcode. The engulfment or uptake of a portion of                particle population, or a preferential engulfment                or uptake of a portion of a sub-population, or a                preferential engulfment or uptake of a combination                of sub-populations determines the cancer-related                parameter.
   USE - Method for determining cancer-related                parameters in a tissue or cell sample obtained from                a subject is carried out with the help of a kit                used in the detection of cancer. The cancer is                selected from blastoma, carcinoma, lymphoma,                leukemia, sarcoma, mesothelioma, glioma, germinoma,                choriocarcinoma, melanoma, glioblastoma, lymphoid                malignancies, and neoplastic diseases or disorders.                The cancer is squamous cell cancer, lung cancer                including small-cell lung cancer, non-small cell                lung cancer, adenocarcinoma of the lung and                squamous carcinoma of the lung, cancer of the                peritoneum, hepatocellular cancer, gastric or                stomach cancer including gastrointestinal cancer,                pancreatic cancer, glioblastoma, cervical cancer,                ovarian cancer, liver cancer, bladder cancer,                hepatoma, breast cancer, colon cancer, rectal                cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial or uterine                carcinoma, salivary gland carcinoma, kidney or                renal cancer, prostate cancer, vulval cancer,                thyroid cancer, hepatic carcinoma, anal carcinoma,                penile carcinoma, skin cancer as well as head and                neck cancer, or a solid tumor cancer or a cancer of                a hematopoietic line.
   ADVANTAGE - The method uses cell uptake assessments that                can provide a simple, robust, and accurate                diagnostic method and add mechanical knowledge to                the existing clinical tools.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a tool for carrying out a method; and
   a kit for use in the detection of cancer, or                in carrying out a method, which comprises a                composition of different particles population,                optionally carried in a liquid medium and                instructions of use.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Process: The method for                  determining the presence of a cancer cell in the                  tissue or cells sample comprises: The uptake or                  engulfment of the particles by cells in the                  sample having been treated or contacted with the                  particle population is determined, where cells                  engulfing or uptaking a portion of particle                  population, or cells demonstrating preferential                  uptake of a particle sub-population, or cells                  demonstrating a preferential engulfment or uptake                  of a combination of sub-populations are cancer                  cells, provided that the cells are not                  macrophages, astrocytes, dendritic cells or                  osteoclasts. The tissue sample or a cell sample                  in vivo, ex vivo or in vitro are treated and                  contacted with a particle population are provided                  under conditions enabling particles uptake by                  cells in a sample, the particle population                  comprising different particle sub-populations,                  each of at least two particle sub-population                  comprises or consists particles of a different                  physical parameter and a different identifiable                  barcode. Preferred Parameters: The cancer-related                  parameter are: presence of cancer cells in the                  sample, (2) grade and severity of cancer in a                  sample identified as cancerous or in a subject                  diagnosed with cancer, (3) metastasis or                  invasiveness potential of cancer in a sample                  identified as cancerous or in a subject diagnosed                  with cancer, (4) whether a particular treatment                  is effective as an anticancer treatment, (5)                  whether a potential anticancer treatment is                  effective against particular cancer in a subject,                  and ()6 whether a particular mode of delivery of                  a therapeutic agent for specific cancer or                  patient is effective. The physical parameter is                  particle shape, size, or stiffness (elastic                  deformability). Each sub-population differs from                  another in particle size or shape or particle                  deformability. The subpopulations comprising                  particles having a size or a diameter in the                  nanometric range and sub-populations comprising                  particles having a size or a diameter in the                  micrometric range. All particles in the particle                  population are nanometric in size, or micrometric                  in size. The population of particles comprising a                  sub-population having a particle size between                  300-800 nanometers (nm), another subpopulation                  comprising particles having a size between 800                  nm-1.5 microns, and a further subpopulation                  comprising particles having a size between 1.5-4                  microns. The particles in each sub-population                  having a size distribution with a coefficient of                  variation being at most 5 %, or lower than 0.5 %.                  The particles are selected to have Young's                  modulus ranging between 0.1-10,000 kilopascals                  (kPa). Each of the sub-populations is                  distinguishable by an identifiable barcode in a                  form of a tracer moiety enabling selective                  tracing and identification of the                  sub-populations. The sample is analyzed to                  determine uptake of particles or to determine                  signal intensity indicative of degree or extent                  of uptake and identify an uptake profile                  characteristic of the sample. The uptake profile                  is compared to a fingerprint profile obtained for                  a control sample to determine the presence or                  absence of malignancy, severity, and metastatic                  potential. The uptake profile relating to the                  particle population or multiple sub-populations                  or the amount or number of particles taken up by                  the cells is determined. The uptake profile is                  compared to a fingerprint profile obtained for                  heathy cells utilizing a particle population                  identical to the particle population with which                  the sample was contacted, where a deviation from                  the fingerprint profile is indicative of presence                  or absence of a cancer cell in the sample, and                  metastatic potential or malignancy or                  aggressiveness of cells in the sample. Preferred                  Condition: The sub-populations have the same                  chemical or biological affinity to the cells. The                  particles are not liposomes, vesicles, lysosomes,                  micelles or reverse micelles. Preferred                  Components: The particle population is a mixed                  particle population comprising between 2 and 10                  sub-populations, or between 2 and 9, 2 and 8, 2                  and 7, 2 and 6, 2 and 5, 2 and 4, or 2 or 3                  sub-populations. The particles are selected from                  circular or spherical-shaped particles,                  disc-shaped, round particles, elongated                  particles, and polygonal-shaped particles. The                  particles are polymeric particles. The polymeric                  particles are of a material selected from                  polyesters, polyamides, polycarbonates,                  polycarbamates, polyacrylates, polystyrene,                  polyureas, polyethers, polyamines,                  poly-anhydrides, poly(hydroxy acids), poly(lactic                  acid), poly(glycolic acid), poly (orthoesters),                  polyphosphazene, ethylene-vinyl acetate                  copolymer, polyurethanes, poly acrylates,                  polymethacrylates, polyacrylonitriles,                  poly(amidoamine) dendrimers,                  poly(L-lactide-co-L-lysine), poly(serine ester),                  poly(4-hydroxy-L-proline ester),                  maleimide-poly(ethylene                  glycol)-block-poly(D,L-lactic acid),                  COOH-poly(ethylene glycol)-block-poly(D,L-lactic                  acid), methoxy poly(ethylene                  glycol)-block-poly(D,L-lactic acid), proteins,                  polysaccharides, PEGylated poly(hydroxy acids),                  PEGylated poly(orthoesters), poly(caprolactone),                  PEGylated poly(caprolactone), polylysine,                  PEGylated polylysine, poly(ethylene imine),                  PEGylated poly (ethylene imine). The particles                  are selected from polystyrene,                  poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) and                  PEGylated particles. The barcode is provided in a                  form of a chemical moiety on a surface region of                  the particles, or in a form of a material                  comprised within the particles. The chemical                  moiety having a characteristic distinguishable                  signal. The chemical moiety is in a form of a                  luminescent tag, a photoluminescent tag, a                  chemiluminescent tag, a fluorescent tag, a                  magnetic tag, an MRI tag, a colorimetric tag, a                  chemical tag, a hybridization tag, a                  polynucleotide tag, a peptide tag, a                  semiconductor tag, an X-ray fluorescence (XRF)                  tag, an X-ray tag, or a quantum dot. The                  fluorescent tag is selected from xanthenes,                  cyanines, squaraines, naphthalenes, coumarins,                  oxadiazoles, anthracenes, pyrenes, oxazines,                  acridines, Arylmethines, tetrapyrroles,                  dipyrromethenes, hydroxycoumarin, aminocoumarin,                  methoxycoumarin, cascade blue, pacific blue,                  pacific orange, lucifer yellow,                  Nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD), R-Phycoerythrin,                  fluorescein, G-DyelOO, G-Dye200, G-Dye300,                  G-Dye400, Cyanine Dyes-2 (Cy2), Cy3, Cy3B, Cy3.5,                  Cy5, Cy5.5, Cy7, Rhodamine, Lissamine Rhodamine,                  Texas Red, and allophycocyanin. The deviation                  from the fingerprint comprises a change in the                  particles sub-population that is taken up by the                  cells, a change in the relative uptake of one                  sub-population over the other, a change in the                  amount/number of particles being taken up by the                  cells, a change in the relative amounts of                  particles of different subpopulations that are                  taken up by the cells, a change in the type of                  cells that uptake one or more of the                  subpopulations, a change in the uptake profile by                  certain types of cells, or a change in the                  diversity of particles taken up by the cells. The                  tool is being in a form of a diagnostic device                  comprising a chamber or a region for holding a                  tissue or cell sample and bringing a dispersion                  or suspension of particles into contact with the                  sample or in a form of a microfluidic device or a                  flow chip.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - The Cell invasion assay assesses the migratory                and invasiveness potential of cells, we measured                spatial cell invasion from multicellular spheroids                (3-dimensional culture) in an extracellular matrix.                Briefly, cells were seeded in a multiwall 2 wt.%                Agarose micro-wells array templated with a Master                3D Petri Dish(RTM: 3D cell culture system) 96 well                arrays at 3,000 cells/well as previously described,                3,000 cells/well. Following cell seeding, the                micro-wells were incubated with a fresh medium to                allow spheroid formation for 48 h. Forty-eight                hours post spheroids incubation, the spheroids were                harvested and embedded in a solution of 0.25 wt.%                methylcellulose in suitable media. Spheroids were                then mixed with collagen in neutral pH, seeded in a                24 well plate, and incubated for 30 minutes at                37&#176; C. After gel stabilization, 300 pi of                fresh media was added in order to provide                sufficient media supply. The gel containing the                spheroids was gently detached from the well walla                and Images of the spheroids were taken by an                inverted fluorescent microscope every hours.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - Treating gremlin (GREM)1-expressing cancer                (M1) in a subject, comprises administering GREM1                antagonist, where the cancer is characterized in                reduced androgen receptor (AR) signaling.
   USE - The methods are useful for: treating                GREM1-expressing cancer in a subject, where the                cancer is characterized in reduced AR signaling, or                the cancer is AR-expressing cancer or is AR                negative cancer, prostate cancer, breast cancer                (triple negative breast cancer), lung cancer, head                and neck cancer, testis cancer, endometrial cancer,                ovarian cancer, skin cancer, glioma, liposarcoma,                hepatocellular carcinoma, lung cancer, cervical                cancer, endometrial carcinoma, uterine                leiomyosarcoma, squamous cell carcinoma of the head                and neck, thyroid cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic                cancer, bladder cancer, colon cancer, esophageal                cancer, bile duct cancer, osteosarcoma,                glioblastoma, ovarian cancer, gastric cancer, small                cell lung cancer or melanoma; increasing                sensitivity of AR-expressing cancer to an androgen                deprivation therapy in a subject; and treating a                GREM1-related disease or condition characterized in                deficiency in PTEN and/or p53 in a subject, or                inhibiting fibroblast growth factor receptor                (FGFR)1 activation in a subject, or inhibiting MAPK                signaling; determining likelihood of responsiveness                to a GREM1 antagonist in a subject having or                suspected of having cancer; detecting presence or                amount of GREM1 in a sample determined to be absent                in AR expression or determined to have reduced AR                signaling; determining likelihood of responsiveness                to a GREM1 antagonist in a subject having or                suspected of having a disease or condition; and                detecting presence or amount of GREM1 in a sample                determined to be deficient in PTEN and/or p53. The                cancer: is metastatic, optionally, metastatic                prostate cancer, or lung metastasis of prostate                cancer; is characterized in GREM1 overexpression.                The GREM1-related disease or condition comprises                cancer (preferred), fibrotic disease, angiogenesis,                glaucoma or retinal disease, kidney disease,                pulmonary arterial hypertension, or osteoarthritis.                The prostate cancer is (1a) negative in androgen                receptor (AR) expression, (1b) negative in both                androgen receptor (AR) expression and                neuroendocrine (NE) differentiation; (1c) resistant                to an androgen deprivation therapy, optionally                castration-resistant, and/or (1d) showing a level                of prostate specific antigen (PSA) lower than a                reference level. The fibrotic disease is lung                fibrosis, skin fibrosis, diabetic nephropathy, or                ischemic renal injury (all claimed). Test details                are described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method utilizes the GREM1 antagonist                which: reduces GREM1 level or GREM1 activity;                reduces the GREM1 activity selectively in cancer                cell over in non-cancer cell; and has high affinity                and specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   increasing (M2) sensitivity of AR-expressing                cancer to an androgen deprivation therapy in a                subject, comprising administering GREM1                antagonist;
   treating (M3) a GREM1-related disease or                condition characterized in deficiency in                phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) and/or p53 in                a subject, or inhibiting fibroblast growth factor                receptor (FGFR)1 activation in a subject, or                inhibiting MAPK signaling, comprising administering                GREM1 antagonist;
   determining (M4) likelihood of responsiveness                to a GREM1 antagonist in a subject having or                suspected of having cancer, comprising (a)                detecting androgen receptor (AR) expression or                signaling in a biological sample from the subject,                and (b) determining the likelihood of                responsiveness based on the AR expression or                signaling detected in step (a);
   detecting (M5) presence or amount of GREM1 in                a sample determined to be absent in AR expression                or determined to have reduced AR signaling,                comprising contacting the sample with a detection                reagent for detection of GREM1, and determining the                presence or the amount of GREM1 in the                sample;
   determining (M6) likelihood of responsiveness                to a GREM1 antagonist in a subject having or                suspected of having a disease or condition,                comprising (aa) detecting deficiency of PTEN and/or                p53 in a biological sample from the subject, and                (bb) determining the likelihood of responsiveness                based on the deficiency of PTEN and/or p53 detected                in step (aa); and
   detecting (M7) presence or amount of GREM1 in                a sample determined to be deficient in PTEN and/or                p53, comprising contacting the sample with a                detection reagent for detection of GREM1, and                determining the presence or the amount of GREM1 in                the sample.

The inhibitory nucleic acid                  targeting GREM1 RNA or DNA including a short                  hairpin RNA (shRNA), micro interfering RNA                  (miRNA), double strand RNA (dsRNA), small                  interfering RNA (siRNA), guide RNA, or antisense                  oligonucleotide. The GREM1 antagonist includes a                  GREM1-fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR)1                  axis inhibitor. The GREM1-FGFR1 axis inhibitor:                  inhibits GREM1 dependent FGFR1 signalling; blocks                  binding between GREM1 and FGFR1; and comprises                  FGFR1-binding inhibitor. The antibody against                  hGREM1 or antigen-binding fragment is a diabody,                  antigen binding fragment (Fab), a Fab', a F (ab')                  2 , Fd, variable fragment (Fv), a disulfide                  stabilized Fv fragment (dsFv) , a (dsFv) 2, a                  bispecific dsFv (dsFv-dsFv') , a disulfide                  stabilized diabody (ds diabody) , a single-chain                  antibody molecule (scFv), scFv dimer (bivalent                  diabody) , a multispecific antibody, a camelized                  single domain antibody, a nanobody, a domain                  antibody, or a bivalent domain antibody. The                  antibody against hGREM1 or antigen-binding                  fragment is bispecific. The antibody against                  hGREM1 or antigen-binding fragment is capable of                  specifically binding to a first and a second                  epitope of gremlin, or capable of specifically                  binding to hGREM1 and a second antigen. The                  second antigen comprises an immune related                  target. The second antigen includes e.g.                  programmed cell death protein (PD)-1, programmed                  cell death ligand (PD)-L1, PD-L2, CD160, 2B4,                  OX40, CD2, CD27, CD28, CD30, CD40, CD47, CD122,                  4-1BB, CD7, interleukin (IL)-2, IL-7, IL-15,                  IL-21, CD3, CD16 and CD83, or tumor antigen. The tumor antigen                  includes e.g. prostate specific antigen (PSA),                  carcinoembryonic antigen (CA)-125, gangliosides G                  (D2), G (M2) and G (D3), CD20, CD52, CD33, CEA,                  bombesin-like peptides, human epidermal growth                  factor receptor 2/neu, epidermal growth factor                  receptor, cancer-associated mucin, vascular                  endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR),                  estrogen receptors, Lewis-Y antigen, transferrin                  receptor, claudin 18.2, Nectin-4, methothelin,                  and IL-2 receptor. The antibody against hGREM1 or                  antigen-binding fragment is not cross-reactive or                  cross-reactive to mouse GREM1.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The subject is receiving                  or has received an androgen deprivation therapy,                  or is resistant to an androgen deprivation                  therapy. The method further comprises                  administering a second therapeutic agent. The                  deficiency in PTEN and/or p53 is characterized:                  in absence of functional PTEN and/or p53; in the                  presence of inactivating mutation in PTEN and/or                  p53; in absence of PTEN and/or p53 expression.    Y1=straight or branched 1-10C alkyl                substituted with at least two hydroxy;

   L=bond or linker; and
   n=0-1.

   diagnostic composition comprising (I) and at                least one carrier or excipient; and

   EXAMPLE - In a 50 ml centrifuge tube 15 mg                4-(5-carboxy-2-((1E,3E,5E,7E)-7-(3,3-dimethyl-5-((2S,3R,4R,5R)-2,3,4,5,6-pentahydroxyhexylcarbamoyl)-1-(4-sulfobutyl)indolin-2-ylidene)hepta-1,3,5-trienyl)-3,3-dimethyl-3H-indolium-1-yl)butane-1-sulfonate                was dissolved in 1.5 ml dry N,N-dimethylformamide                (DMF) and 4 &#956; l N-methylmorpholine and 7.5                mg O-(N-succinimidyl)-1,1,3,3-tetramethyluronium                tetrafluoroborate were added. The dark blue/green                solution was stirred for 1 hour at room temperature                in the dark, reaching 88.1% of conversion at 756                nm. 25 ml Cold ethyl acetate was added and the                suspension was centrifuged for 10 minutes at 4010                rpm and 5&#176; C. Then, the organic layer was                decanted, the solid was suspended twice in 10 ml                ethyl acetate and centrifuged again. The crude                solid was finally dried under nitrogen atmosphere                and then dissolved in a solution of 6.7 mg                8-amino-N-(5-sulfamoyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-yl)octanamide                and 12 &#956; l N,N-diisopropylethylamine in 2                ml anhydrous DMF. The solution was stirred in the                dark at room temperature for 1 hour. Since the                N-hydroxysuccinimide ester was not completely                converted into the desired product, an excess of                2.5 mg                8-amino-N-(5-sulfamoyl-1,3,4-thiadiazol-2-yl)octanamide                was added. The obtained solution was stirred for                other 30 minutes, then it was dropped into 25 ml                cold diethyl ether. AU TSO J Y
   MCPHATE GREEN J
   GREEN J M
AE PROTEIN DESIGN LABS INC (PROT-Non-standard)
   TSO J Y (TSOJ-Individual)
   GREEN J M (GREE-Individual)
   PROTEIN DESIGN LABS INC (PROT-Non-standard)
GA 2003381675
AB    NOVELTY - A pharmaceutical composition comprises an inhibitor of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthase.
   USE - For treating prostate cancer, leukemia and for inhibiting growth of prostate cancer cell (claimed). Also useful for treating Hodgkin's disease, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, multiple myeloma, neuroblastoma, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, lung cancer, rhabdomyosarcoma, primary thrombocytosis, primary macroglobulinemia, small-cell lung tumors, primary brain tumors, stomach cancer, colon cancer, malignant pancreatic insulanoma, malignant carcinoid, urinary bladder cancer, premalignant skin lesions, testicular cancer, lymphomas, thyroid cancer, esophageal cancer, genitourinary tract cancer, malignant hypercalcemia, cervical cancer, endometrial cancer or adrenal cortical cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - Inhibitor down-regulates biological activities of ATP synthase. The antibody inhibits prostate cancer cell proliferation by at least 10 (preferably 20)% and prostate cancer cell colony formation by at least 50 (preferably 95)%.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for following:
   (1) method (M1) of treating or preventing prostate cancer involving administering an inhibitor of ATP synthase activity;
   (2) inducing apoptosis of leukemia cells derived from THP-1 cell line involving contacting an antibody which binds to or neutralizes ATP synthase with leukemia cells;
   (3) detection of prostate cancer, breast cancer, colon cancer or leukemia e.g. acute myelogenous leukemia involving detecting presence of ATP synthase in the cells.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Inhibitor: Inhibitor is an anti-sense nucleic acid of a nucleic acid sequence encoding part of full ATP synthase; a protein (P1) that directly interacts with ATP synthase; an antibody conjugate comprising an anti-ATP synthase antibody conjugated to a cytotoxin agent; or an antibody that binds to or neutralizes ATP synthase. (P1) is an anti-ATP synthase antibody (preferably a monoclonal antibody which is a humanized antibody, a fully human antibody or a chimeric antibody, an antibody tetramer, Fab, (Fab')2 or Fv). Cytotoxin agent is a protein cytotoxin or a Fc domain of a monoclonal antibody.Preferred Method: (M1) further involves administration of a chemotherapeutic agent.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. The anticancer activity of anti-ATP synthase was demonstrated in the AML cell line THP-1, which expresses ATP synthase on the cell surface. Incubation of THP-1 cells with anti-ATP synthase at 5 microg/ml for 24 hours led to substantial cell death as assayed by flow cytometry. The results showed that the percentage cell death by use of control and ATP synthase inhibitor was 25% and 38% respectively.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Inhibitor of protein expression of ATP synthase; Cancer cell growth inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - Inhibitor is administered serially or in combination with another agent (claimed). The dosage is 0.01 - 100 (preferably 0.05 - 100, most preferably 0.5 - 50) mg for parenteral (e.g. intravenous, intramuscular or subcutaneous) administration.
   EXAMPLE - No relevant example given.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The second assay is                  conducted on the same biological sample as the                  first assay. The first assay involves contacting                  the sample material with at least first and                  second oligo-linked probes; ligating together                  first and second oligos of the probes to form a                  covalently contiguous ligation product; and                  detecting the ligation product by amplification                  or sequencing. The amplification is digital                  polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The steo prior                  to the first assay, a predetermined marker                  comprising a surface protein of an extracellular                  vesicle is captured by antibody-functionalized                  beads, and the sample material comprises                  extracellular vesicles. AU ARNISON P
   BALSEVICH J
   BISHOP G

AE NAT RES COUNCIL CANADA (CANA-C)

   NAT RES COUNCIL CANADA (CANA-C)

AB    NOVELTY - Saponin extract (I) from Saponaria vaccaria,                is claimed.
   USE - (I) is useful for: treating a subject with                cancer; and stimulating apoptosis in cancer cells,                which are human prostate cancer cells, human breast                cancer cells or human colon cancer cells (all                claimed), skin cell, uterine cell, ovarian cell,                pancreatic cell, lung cell, bladder cell and/or                renal cell. The ability of (I) (PC1448) to induce                apoptosis in prostate cancer (PC-3) cells was                tested using a Dual Sensor-MitoCasp (RTM: Assay for                mitochondrial membrane potential detection and                caspase activity) assay. The result showed the                number of cells with caspase 3/7 activity and cells                with decreased mitochondrial membrane potential was                57.2% and 94.1% (for treatment with PC1448 (14                &#956; M)) and 24.6% and 4.5% (for untreated),                respectively at 20 hours.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) can be isolated on a large scale at                reasonable cost using conventional farming                practices and machinery. The utility of (I) does                not necessarily require the isolation or                purification of the saponin compounds. The                precipitation of (I) by cooling has reduced cost                compared to extraction and purification methods                using chromatographic procedures that require                expensive resins. (I) does not stimulate apoptosis                in non-cancer (CRL-2522) cells. (I) has little or                no cytotoxicity to normal human cells. (I) is less                hemolytic.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for a method                of preparing an isolated bisdesmosidic saponin                composition from Saponaria vaccariacomprising (a)                milling seed of Saponaria vaccaria, (b) treating                the milled seed with a solvent to produce a saponin                mixture, (c) cooling the saponin mixture to                precipitate bisdesmosidic saponins, and (d)                recovering the precipitate comprising the isolated                bisdesmosidic saponin composition containing                bisdesmosidic saponins (at least 60 wt.%); or step                (a), step (b), drying the saponin extract to                produce a crude saponin composition, titurating the                crude saponin composition with 100% methanol, and                recovering a solid residue comprising bisdesmosidic                saponins (at least 50 wt.%).
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure show a schematic representation of                preparation of various saponin containing extracts                from Saponin vaccaria seed and roots by extraction                and processing.
   20Hydroalcoholic extract
   30Precipitate containing more than 70 wt.% of                saponin
   40Crude seed extract powder
   50Saponin enriched seed extract powder
   90Crude root extract powder.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: (I) is isolated from                  Saponaria vaccariaseed. (I) comprises one or more                  triterpene saponin, which comprises a                  bisdesmosidic saponin having a molecular weight                  of 1448, 1464, 1422, 1526, 1596, 1688-1 or                  1688-2. The solvent is aqueous methanol.                  Preferred Method: The saponin mixture is cooled                  at -10&#176; C to -30&#176; C for 36-48                  hours. The method further comprises: addition of                  a second solvent to the saponin mixture following                  step (b), where the second solvent is ethanol;                  applying the isolated bisdesmosidic saponin                  composition to a column to effect separation of                  individual saponins; and recovering bisdesmosidic                  saponin of molecular weight 1448 or 1464.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Apoptotic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of (I) is oral, parenteral (by                subcutaneous, intradermal, intravenous,                intramuscular or intraperitoneal injection or                infusion), or via skin patch. No dosage details                given.
   EXAMPLE - Saponaria vaccariacleaned seed (500 g) was                ground to a fine powder in a mill. A de-fatted                ground seed was produced by washing the ground seed                with ethyl acetate to remove lipids and allowed to                air dry. The de-fatted ground seed was mixed with                60% methanol (1200 ml) containing citric acid (100                mg) and allowed to stand for 1 day at room                temperature. The resultant mixture was filtered                through a sintered glass filter with minimal or no                vacuum. The filter cake was re-extracted with 60%                methanol (1000 ml) resulting in a hydroalcoholic                extract (2 l). A crude saponin mixture was obtained                by placing the hydroalcoholic extract in a tray in                a fume hood and allowing the filtrate to evaporate                to produce a dry seed extract. The aqueous extract                concentrate was adjusted to pH 5 if required by                addition of citric acid. The seed extract                concentrate was diluted with ethanol (500 ml) and                butanol (100 ml) and evaporated on a rotary                evaporator until the foam point was reached. The                process was repeated until water was removed and a                solid residue remained. The last traces of water                were removed under high vacuum. The resultant solid                was powdered and stored in glass bottles to give a                powder containing saponins (28%).

TI Hybrid deep-learning system for classifying skin            cancer of patient in e.g. clinical healthcare            environments, has transformer layer operatively coupled            to Convolutional Neural Network feature extractor and            applying self-attention to model global contextual            relationships among extracted feature.
AU KIRAN K
   SHAIK A R
AE VISHNU TECHNOLOGY INST (VISH-Non-standard)
GA 202604935F
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a preprocessing module for                resizing, normalizing, augmenting and rebalancing                dermoscopic images. A convolutional neural network                (CNN) feature extractor comprises convolutional and                pooling layers arranged to learn local textural and                structural lesion features. A transformer layer is                operatively coupled to the CNN feature extractor,                and applies self-attention to model global                contextual relationships among the extracted                features. The integration of CNN-based local                feature extraction with transformer-based global                dependency modeling enhances diagnostic accuracy                and improves generalization across diverse                dermoscopic datasets.
   USE - Hybrid deep-learning system for classifying                skin cancer of patient in remote, telemedicine and                clinical healthcare environments and large-scale                dermatological screening environments.
   ADVANTAGE - The system develops optimized preprocessing,                data balancing, normalization, and                hyperparameter-tuning strategies that enhance                diagnostic accuracy, generalization capability, and                clinical applicability in telemedicine and                large-scale dermatological screening environments.                The system integrates CNNs with Transformer-based                self-attention mechanisms for accurate and reliable                classification of skin cancer lesions from                dermoscopic images. The system simultaneously                captures fine-grained local texture features and                long-range global contextual relationships, thus                overcoming the inherent limitations of standalone                CNN architectures and enabling the detection of                subtle malignancy patterns distributed across the                lesion surface. The system employs robust                preprocessing, normalization, data augmentation,                and class-rebalancing techniques to address                challenges associated with dataset imbalance,                imaging variability, and limited availability of                minority lesion classes, thus improving model                stability and generalization. The system                incorporates batch normalization, dropout, and                hyperparameter-tuning strategies to mitigate                overfitting, enhance convergence behavior, and                optimize model performance on large-scale                dermoscopic datasets or HAM10000. The system                achieves high diagnostic accuracy suitable for                deployment in clinical, telemedicine, and remote                healthcare environments, thus reducing dependency                on specialized dermatological expertise and                enabling timely screening of skin cancer.

GA 2023A7287T
AB    NOVELTY - Composition comprises                developmentally-regulated GTP-binding protein 2                (DRG2) gene, its mRNA, or a protein detection                agent, as an active ingredient.
   USE - The composition or DRG2 inducer is useful for                producing a drug for predicting ovarian metastasis                of cancer including melanoma, liver cancer, glioma,                sarcoma, colon cancer, breast cancer, prostate                cancer, lung cancer, head and neck cancer, bladder                cancer, stomach cancer, esophageal cancer, bile                duct cancer, pancreatic cancer, cervical cancer,                skin cancer, lymphoma, thyroid cancer, bone marrow                cancer, endometrial cancer, kidney cancer, rectal                cancer and brain tumor (all claimed). Test details                are described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The composition efficiently prevents ovarian                metastasis of cancer, increases treatment                efficiency for ovarian cancer, predicts high risk                of cancer specifically metastasizing to the                ovaries, effectively prevents cancer from                metastasizing to ovaries, and prevents and                increases efficiency of ovarian cancer                treatment.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) (1) a kit comprising the                composition;
   (2) (2) a method for providing information for                predicting ovarian metastasis of cancer, involving                detecting the expression or expression level of the                DRG2 gene, its mRNA, or protein from a biological                sample;
   (3) (3) a pharmaceutical composition                comprising DRG2 inducer, as an active                ingredient;
   (4) (4) a method for screening candidate                substances for inhibiting cancer metastasis to the                ovary, involving (a) processing a candidate                material in a biological sample in which DRG2,                which has been knocked out and (b) detecting the                presence or expression level of the DRG2 gene, its                mRNA, or protein from the biological sample;                and
   (5) (5) a method of inhibiting ovarian                metastasis of cancer, involving administering the                composition comprising DRG2 inducer to an                individual.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: The detection agent                  comprises a primer or probe which specifically                  binds to the DRG2 gene or its mRNA; or an aptamer                  or antibody which specifically binds to the DRG2                  protein. The biological sample is chosen from                  blood, plasma, serum, bone marrow, tissue, cells,                  saliva, sputum, peritoneal fluid, hair, nasal                  fluid, urine, stool, and samples obtained by                  biopsy. The DRG2 inducer is an expression                  promoter of the DRG2 gene or an activator of the                  DRG2 protein. The DRG2 inducer is DRG2 protein,                  or an mRNA or expression vector containing a                  polynucleotide encoding the DRG2 protein. The                  DRG2 protein comprises an amino acid sequence                  represented by SEQ ID NO: 1. The polynucleotide                  comprises a base sequence represented by SEQ ID                  NO: 2. Preferred Method: The method further                  involves predicting a high risk of ovarian                  metastasis of cancer, where expression of the                  DRG2 gene, its mRNA, or protein is not detected;                  or when the expression level of the DRG2 gene,                  its mRNA, or protein is reduced compared to the                  control group. The method further involves (c)                  selecting the candidate as a candidate for                  inhibiting cancer metastasis to the ovary when                  the expression level of the DRG2 gene, its mRNA,                  or protein is increased compared to before                  treatment with the candidate.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - Examples describes about confirmation of                effect of reducing lung metastasis of melanoma in                DRG2 KO mice, and confirmation of increased ovarian                metastasis of melanoma in DRG2 KO mice, so does not                support the claims.

TI New monoclonal antibody specific for cytokeratin            19 and produced by specific hybridomas, useful in kit            for detecting cancer e.g. breast cancer, lung cancer,            stomach cancer, colon cancer, esophagus cancer and            thyroid cancer.
AU NAGAYASU T
   OTSUBO RYOTA
   OTSUBO R

GA 201730157N
AB    NOVELTY - A monoclonal antibody specific for cytokeratin                19 and produced by the hybridoma of accession                number NITE ABP-02135 or NITE ABP-02136, is                new.
   USE - The monoclonal antibody is useful in kit for                detecting cancer (all claimed) including breast                cancer, lung cancer, stomach cancer, colon cancer,                esophagus cancer, thyroid cancer, gynecologic                cancer, skin cancer and head and neck cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The monoclonal antibody detects cancer in a                simple, cost-effective, less time-consuming, rapid                and accurate manner without using expensive                equipment and specimen.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   kit for detecting cancer, which comprises a                labeled antibody in which a label and a first                antibody that undergoes an antigen-antibody                reaction with cytokeratin 19 are bonded, and a                chromatography medium provided with an                antibody-capturing section in which a second                antibody that undergoes an antigen-antibody                reaction with cytokeratin 19 is immobilized, where                the first antibody is a monoclonal antibody                produced by a hybridoma of accession number NITE                ABP-02136 and the second antibody is a monoclonal                antibody produced by a hybridoma of accession                number NITE ABP-02135;
   method for detecting cancer by                immunochromatography using the kit, which involves                (a) developing a mixed solution containing a sample                derived from a lymph node of a subject and the                labeled antibody to the antibody capturing section,                and (b) detecting a complex of cytokeratin 19 and                the labeled antibody in the sample by the antibody                capturing section and determining that a cancer                cell is contained in the sample; and
   method for determining the metastasis of a                cancer by immunochromatography using the kit, which                involves (a) developing a mixed solution containing                a sample derived from a lymph node of a subject and                the labeled antibody to the antibody capturing                section, and (b) determining the metastasis of a                cancer (i) when a complex of cytokeratin 19 and the                labeled antibody in the sample is detected by the                antibody capturing section in the low-sensitivity                detection kit and the high-sensitivity detection                kit, it is judged that there is a macro-transition                exceeding the reference size to perform lymph node                dissection, (ii) when the complex is not detected                by the antibody capturing section in                low-sensitivity detection kit and the complex is                detected by the antibody capturing section in the                high-sensitivity detection kit, it is judged that                at least one of micro-translation below the size of                lymph node dissection, isolated tumor cells (ITCs)                of 0.2 mm or less, and contamination of epithelial                component is present, and (iii) when the complex is                not detected in the antibody capturing section in                the low-sensitivity detection kit and the                high-sensitivity detection kit, it is judged that                there is no cancer metastasis.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Method: The magnitude of metastasis as                  a reference for conducting lymph node dissection                  is 2 mm. The labeled antibody of the                  low-sensitivity detection kit is labeled with a                  metal colloid having an average particle size of                  20-60 nm, and the labeled antibody of the                  high-sensitivity detection kit is labeled with a                  metal colloid which is larger than the particle                  size of the metal colloid of the labeled antibody                  of the low-sensitivity detection kit and has an                  average particle diameter of 40-80 nm.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - Method (I) for identifying molecular markers                useful for detecting tumor cells metastasized from                an origin tissue to a destination tissue or fluid,                is new.

   ADVANTAGE - The early diagnosis of cancer allows more                effective treatment to be implemented. The method                involves identifying candidate marker molecules                associated with terminal differentiation in the                tissue in which a tumor arises, and identifying                marker molecules that are continued to be expressed                in the tumors from that tissue but not in the                biopsy tissue.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A method (I) for identifying a molecular                marker useful for detecting tumor cells                metastasized from an origin tissue to a destination                tissue or fluid, comprising:
   (a) down-regulating, in a population of origin                tissue cells, the activity of a transcription                factor associated with terminally differentiated                origin tissue;
   (b) comparing an expression profile of the                population of down-regulated origin cells with the                expression profile a population of control origin                cells;
   (c) identifying candidate markers which are                expressed in the population of control origin cells                but not in the population of down-regulated origin                cells; and
   (d) comparing expression of candidate markers                in control population of origin cells cancerous                population of origin cells and population of                destination cells wherein a candidate marker that                is express in the population of control origin                cells and the population of cancerous origin cells                and not in the population of destination cells is                useful as a molecular marker for the detection of                cancer metastasized from the origin tissue to the                destination tissue or fluid.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Methods: In the method (I) the                  activity of the transcription factor is                  down-regulated by a method selected from                  down-regulating the transcription factor gene,                  down-regulating the activity of the transcription                  factor and activating a signaling event that                  inactivates the transcription factor. The                  population of down-regulated origin cells is                  derived from a cdx2-null intestinal polyp. The                  molecular marker is a polynucleic acid and the                  expression profiles are compared by a technique                  selected from differential display, subtractive                  hybridization, expression array, Serial Analysis                  of Gene Expression (SAGE), Rapid Analysis of Gene                  Expression (RAGE), Massively Parallel Signature                  Sequencing (MPSS) and Tandem Arrayed Ligation of                  Expressed Sequence Tags (TALEST).Alternatively, the molecular marker is a                  protein and the expression profiles are compared                  by a technique selected from 2-D gel                  electrophoresis and Isotope-Coded Affinity Tags                  (ICM). The origin tissue and destination tissue                  are mammalian, especially human. The control                  origin cells are from an origin tissue which is                  selected from colorectal, intestine, stomach,                  liver, mouth, oesophagus, throat, thyroid, skin,                  brain, kidney, pancreas, breast, cervix, ovary,                  uterus, testicle, prostate, bone, muscle, bladder                  and lung. The population of control origin cells                  is a cell line selected from the group consisting                  of T84, Caco2, HT29, 5W480, 5W620, NCI H508,                  SW1116, SW1463, Hep G2, and HeLa.The cancerous origin cells are cancer cells                  from tissue selected from colon, stomach, liver,                  throat, thyroid, skin, brain and lung. The                  population of cancerous origin cells are a cell                  line selected from T84, Caco2, HT29, SW480,                  5W620, NCI H508, SW1116, SW1463, Hep G2, and                  HeLa. The destination tissue or body fluid is                  selected from lymph node, blood, cerebral spinal                  fluid, and bone marrow. The transcriptional                  factor is selected from Cdx2, STATS, NKX3.1,                  FREAC-1, FREAC-2, Pit1, HNF4, LFB1, IPF1, Is11                  and MyoD.The method further comprises the additional                  step of isolating the molecular marker of step                  (d). The transcription factor gene is isolated                  by:(i) isolating a transcription factor that                  binds to the regulatory regions of a gene                  associated with terminal differentiation of the                  origin tissue; and(ii) isolating the gene that expresses the                  transcription factor.

   SUBRAMANIAN V
AE SRM INST SCI & TECHNOLOGY (USRM-C)
GA 2025684671
AB    NOVELTY - System comprises: (a) a remote device                configured to capture a high-resolution image of a                skin lesion, where remote device is selected from a                wireless dermatoscope, a smartphone with an                artificial intelligence (AI)-based medical imaging                application, or a remote medical imaging scanner                capable of transmitting images via a secure                communication protocol; (b) an acquisition module                communicatively connected to remote device,                configured to receive and store said captured                high-resolution image in a structured format for                further processing; (c) a preprocessing module                configured to connect with acquisition module to                enhance the quality of captured image by performing                noise reduction through Gaussian filtering,                contrast enhancement through adaptive histogram                equalization, and red, green, blue (RGB) color                normalization to generate a processed image; (d) a                matrix decomposition module.
   USE - System for automating skin cancer detection in                image recognition (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The system automates the detection of                abnormalities in skin regions; improves accuracy                and efficiency in detecting skin cancer; enhances                image analysis; reduces the need for human                intervention; provides precise detection of                cancerous areas; provides cost-effective solutions                for medical diagnostics; handles large volumes of                images efficiently; enhances the chances of early                detection; reduces computational resource                requirements.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - System comprisises: (a) a remote device                configured to capture a high-resolution image of a                skin lesion, where remote device is selected from a                wireless dermatoscope, a smartphone with an                artificial intelligence (AI)-based medical imaging                application, or a remote medical imaging scanner                capable of transmitting images via a secure                communication protocol; (b) an acquisition module                communicatively connected to remote device,                configured to receive and store said captured                high-resolution image in a structured format for                further processing; (c) a preprocessing module                configured to connect with acquisition module to                enhance the quality of captured image by performing                noise reduction through Gaussian filtering,                contrast enhancement through adaptive histogram                equalization, and red, green, blue (RGB) color                normalization to generate a processed image; (d) a                matrix decomposition module configured to receive                the processed image from the preprocessing module                and divide the processed image into sub-matrices of                predetermined sizes to construct pseudo-graphs by                assigning nodes to each sub-matrix and defining                edges based on color similarity, texture gradients,                and spatial relationships; (e) a feature extraction                module configured to analyze said pseudo-graphs                generated by the matrix decomposition module and                extract relevant features including color                histograms, texture patterns, graph connectivity                metrics, and spatial irregularities through modular                irregular labeling and RGB color persistence; (f) a                region-based convolutional neural network (R-CNN)                module configured to: apply region proposal                networks (RPNs) on the extracted features to                generate bounding boxes around potential cancerous                regions; classify the extracted features through                fully connected layers and a softmax classifier to                assign a probability score to each detected region;                and refine detected regions through intersection                over union (IoU) thresholding and non-maximum                suppression (NMS) to eliminate overlapping bounding                boxes, ensuring accurate localization of the                cancerous area; (g) a feedback module configured to                refine the R-CNN module based on corrections and                annotations provided by medical professionals,                enabling continuous learning and improvement                through periodic retraining of said R-CNN module;                and (h) a user interface configured to present                analyzed results to healthcare professionals in                real time, where the user interface displays                original images, segmented graph representations,                bounding box predictions, detected cancerous                regions, and risk assessment scores, while                providing zoom-in functionalities, heatmaps, and                probability score for enhanced decision                making.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for automating skin cancer detection in image                recognition, comprising: (a1) capturing a                high-resolution image of a skin lesion by a remote                device; (b1) receiving and storing the captured                high-resolution image by an acquisition module;                (c1) enhancing the quality of the captured image                through noise reduction, contrast enhancement, and                RGB color normalization to generate a processed                image by a preprocessing module; (d1) dividing the                processed image into sub-matrices to construct a                pseudo-graph by a matrix decomposition module,                where nodes and edges are defined based on spatial                relationships, color similarity, and texture                variations; (e1) analyzing the pseudo-graphs and                extracting features using modular irregular                labeling and RGB color persistence by a feature                extraction module; (f1) detecting cancerous regions                by processing the extracted features and analyzing                spatial, textural, and color-based patterns through                a region-based convolutional neural network (R-CNN)                module; (g1) refining the R-CNN module by                incorporating feedback from medical professionals                via a feedback module to enable continuous learning                and enhance model accuracy; and (h1) presenting the                analyzed results through a user interface, where                the results include original images, segmented                graph representations, bounding box predictions,                and risk assessment scores for review by healthcare                professionals.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Process: The acquisition module is                  configured to store, organize, and retrieve                  patient images in an electronic medical record                  (EMR) system. The reprocessing module applies the                  operations selected from: (a2) Gaussian filtering                  to reduce the captured noise, (b2) adaptive                  histogram equalization to enhance the contrast of                  said captured image, and (c2) color normalization                  techniques to adjust RGB values for consistent                  image representation. The matrix decomposition                  module divides the processed image into                  submatrices of a predetermined size and                  constructs a graph-based representation by                  assigning: nodes to each sub-matrix based on                  pixel intensity and spatial positioning, and                  edges between said nodes based on texture                  gradients, color similarity, and spatial                  relationships. The feature extraction module                  implements modular irregular labeling and RGB                  color persistence analysis to enhance the                  identification of abnormal patterns and anomalies                  associated with cancerous regions. The R-CNN                  module is trained on large-scale dermatological                  datasets, fine-tuned to detect and classify                  cancerous regions into categories including                  benign, malignant, and precancerous lesions. The                  feedback module is configured to: collect                  annotations and corrections from medical                  professionals; update and retrain the R-CNN                  module periodically to improve prediction                  accuracy based on real-world outcomes; and                  implement continuous learning strategies to                  refine feature extraction and region detection                  algorithms. TI Detecting human papilloma virus, useful for            diagnosis of cervical cancer, comprises detecting            presence of virus-specific nucleic acid from the            conserved E1 genomic region.
AU IFTNER T
AE UNIV TUEBINGEN EBERHARD-KARLS (UTEK-C)
   IFTNER T (IFTN-Individual)
   UNIV TUEBINGEN EBERHARD-KARLS (UTEK-C)
GA 2001536647
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting human papilloma virus (HPV) in                biological samples comprising:
extraction/isolation of nucleic acid from the                sample; and
detecting HPV-specific nucleic acid segments                using any of sequences (S1)-(S3), fully defined in                the specification or sequences that hybridize to                sequences complementary to (S1)-(S3).
   USE - The method is particularly used in a process                for diagnosis and/or early detection of HPV                infections, particularly in the ano-genital region                and especially of cancer of the cervix uteri, but                also skin cancers in cases of epidermodysplasia                verruciformis.
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides early detection, and                typing, of HPV infections. Since the primers are                derived from a highly conserved region of the viral                genome, all types of HPV associated with cancer of                the cervix can be detected, with high specificity                and sensitivity. Since sequence (S1) is not                degenerate at any position, subsequent sequencing                (for typing) is facilitated.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - (S1)-(S3) are:
   AACAATGTGTAGACATTATAAACGAGC;
   ATTAAACTCATTCCAAAATATGA; and
   GAGGYTGCAACCAAAAMTGRCT;
   where:
   Y=T or C;
   M=A or C; and
   R=G or A.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   (S1)-(S3);
   equences that hybridize specifically to                S1-S3;
   equences complementary to (a) or (b);                and
   use of one or more nucleic acid sequences from                the E1 open reading frame of HPV for detection of                HPV.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Process: Detection is by                  amplification of specific DNA in a polymerase                  chain reaction (PCR), particularly comprising the                  stages: heating for 5-15 minutes at 90-100                  &#176; C (especially 10 minutes at 95                  &#176; C); denaturation for 30-90 seconds at                  90-100 &#176; C (30 seconds at 95 &#176;                  C); hybridization for 30-90 seconds at 50-60                  &#176; C (30 seconds at 55 &#176; C);                  polymerization for 30-180 seconds at 67-77                  &#176; C (1 minute at 72 &#176; C) and                  cooling for 2-10 minutes (5 minutes at 72                  &#176; C). The heating rate is 1 &#176;                  C/second and 40 amplification cycles are                  performed. Preferably primer (S1) is used with                  either of (S2) or (S3), forming, respectively                  amplicons of about 220 and 280 base pairs (bp).                  These amplicons are detected conventionally, e.g.                  gel electrophoresis with ethidium bromide                  staining, or the method is made quantitative by                  the LightCycler(TM) instrument with detection                  using CyberGreen I or dye-labeled                  sequence-specific probes. The amplicons may also                  be sequenced for HPV typing.Preferred Nucleic Acid: (S1)-(S3) are                  derived from the highly conserved viral E1 open                  reading frame.
   EXAMPLE - DNA was extracted from biopsies or smear                samples then subjected to targeted amplification by                polymerase chain reaction, using primers (S1) and                (S3) AACAATGTGTAGACATTATAAACGAGC (1) (bases                2082-2108 of the human papilloma virus (HPV) type                16 genome) GAGGYTGCAACCAAAAMTGRCT (3) (bases                2401-2380 of the same genome; Y = T or C; M = A or                C; R = G or A). About 50% of the amplicon was                sequenced conventionally. This method allowed                identification of human papilloma virus (HPV) types                1-8; 10-19; 21-28; 30-38; 40; 42; 44-47; 51-54;                56-60; 65-67; 70; 72; 73; 82; and 83.

   QIU F

   LI B
AE GUANGZHOU BURNING ROCK MED LAB CO LTD (GUAN-Non-standard)

GA 2022B4718Q
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting involves determining comethylation                block, based on correlation coefficient of CpG site                in target nucleic acid, methylation level of CpG                site and position information of CpG site,                determining co-methylation block, based on                correlation coefficient of CpG sites in target                nucleic acid, information amount of candidate                co-methylation block and partition balance degree                of candidate co-methylation block, and determining                presence and content of target nucleic acid in                sample to be tested based on methylation degree of                co-methylation block.
   USE - Detecting used for assessing tumor levels                evaluated in early tumor screening, where tumor is                brain cancer, lung cancer, skin cancer,                nasopharyngeal cancer, throat cancer, liver cancer,                bone cancer, lymphoma, pancreatic cancer, skin                cancer, intestinal cancer, colorectal cancer,                thyroid cancer, bladder cancer, renal cancer, oral                cancer, gastric cancer, solid tumour, ovarian                cancer, esophageal cancer, gallbladder cancer,                biliary tract cancer, breast cancer, cervical                cancer, uterine cancer, prostate cancer, head and                neck cancer, sarcoma, thorax malignant tumor                (except for lung), melanoma, and testicular cancer                (all claimed), and for target nucleic acid                methylation modification.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables to provide advantages in                cancer screening and treatment effect                evaluation.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   1. an analysis device for detecting target                nucleic acid methylation modification, which                comprises block dividing module, based on related                coefficient of CpG site in target nucleic acid,                methylation level of CpG site and position                information of CpG site, determining co-methylation                block, and block division module, based on                corrected correlation coefficient of CpG sites in                target nucleic acid, information amount of                candidate co-methylation block and partition                balance degree of candidate co-methylation block,                determining co-methylation block, and a                determination module determining presence and                content of target nucleic acid in sample to be                tested based on methylation degree of                co-methylation block;
   2. a method for detecting circulating tumor                DNA (ctDNA) by methylation sequencing, which                involves:
   a. selecting differentially methylated CpG                site;
   b. dividing CpG sites into multiple                co-methylation blocks, based on similarity of                methylation state of CpG sites;
   c. sequencing sample to obtain methylation                sequencing reading length; and
   d. detecting average methylation level of each                co-methylation block of sample to perform further                DNA methylation analysis;
   3. a kit for detecting ctDNA by methylation                sequencing, which is used to capture 50, 100, 150,                200, 300, 500, 800, 1000, 1500 or 2000 of                co-methylation block;
   4. a storage medium, which records program                which can run detection method for target nucleic                acid methylation modification; and
   5. a device, which comprises storage medium                and optionally comprising processor coupled to                storage medium, processor is configured to perform                detection method for target nucleic acid                methylation modification based on program stored in                storage medium.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The method detects                  presence and content of methylated modified                  target nucleic acid in sample to be tested. The                  related coefficient of CpG site comprises a                  Pearson correlation coefficient between two or                  more of CpG sites in target nucleic acid. The                  methylation level of CpG sites comprises a                  difference in average methylation allele                  frequency (mAF) between CpG sites in target                  nucleic acid. The position information of CpG                  site comprises a difference in position of genome                  between two or more of CpG sites in target                  nucleic acid. The correlation coefficient of CpG                  sites in target nucleic acid comprises a                  corrected correlation coefficient of CpG sites in                  target nucleic acid. The information amount of                  candidate co-methylation block has number                  information of CpG sites of candidate                  co-methylation block. The partition balance                  degree of candidate co-methylation block has                  difference of number of CpG sites of different                  candidate co-methylation blocks. The average                  methylation level is an average methylation                  allele frequency. The number of co-methylation                  blocks is between 1/30 and 1/5 of number of CpG                  sites. The co-methylation blocks having no                  sufficient depth ( &lt; 100) on most samples                  ( &gt; 80%) are excluded from downstream                  analysis.Preferred Process: The corrected correlation                  coefficient between each two of CpG sites of                  target nucleic acid is determined. The                  co-methylation block is determined so that block                  index of candidate co-methylation block is                  maximized. The block breakpoints of                  co-methylation blocks are determined by iterative                  method of unique breakpoint. The presence and                  content of target nucleic acid is determined,                  based on length of continuous CpG of each                  sequencing reading section (read) of                  co-methylation block, number of CpG on read and                  total number of read of co-methylation block. The                  methylation block score of co-methylation block                  is determined. The sequencing data summary of                  sample to be tested is corrected by unique                  molecular identifier (UMI). The characteristic                  value of MBS of common methylation block of tumor                  sample and healthy sample is extracted by machine                  learning model. The co-methylation blocks are                  further limited by comparing a specific tumor                  sample with a normal tissue sample, such as a                  primary lung tumor and a normal lung tissue                  sample. The co-methylation blocks are separated                  based on improved correlation matrix referred to                  as block index. The depth difference of each of                  methylation blocks is normalized using a                  methylation block score (MBS) for distinguishing                  very small tumor signals, such as 0.1%. The                  sequencing reading length to be analyzed is                  pruned by number of segments of G bases query                  longer than fixed value m, fraction of non-G-base                  is less than fixed number p, and next base is                  high quality A/T/C (Phred score is more than                  30).Preferred Components: The differentially                  methylated CpG sites comprises 4 nucleobases (SEQ                  ID NO: Not defined), that are tcga databases                  generated by Infinium(RTM: Robust methylation                  profiling microarray) HumanMethylation 450K                  array.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.

AB    NOVELTY - The diagnostic system (1000) has a set of                tissue diffractometers (1030,1040,1050,1060)                operatively coupled to a computer database (1010)                over a network e.g. Internet. Each diffractometer                acquires and transfers in situ image data, in situ                diffraction pattern data, and/or subject data to                the computer database over the network. A set of                computer processors (1020) is individually or                collectively configured to receive in situ image                data, in situ diffraction pattern data, subject                data, transmit the data to the database, and                process the data for an individual subject using a                data analytics algorithm that provides a                computer-aided diagnostic indicator for the                individual subject.
   USE - Diffractometer-based global in situ diagnostic                system for early detection and diagnosis of cancer                in patient. Uses include but are not limited to                breast cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian cancer,                liver cancer, kidney cancer, lung cancer, skin                cancer, and liver disease.
   ADVANTAGE - The system provides better in situ diagnostic                tools and analytical methods for early detection                and diagnosis of cancer and other diseases. The                system allows an individual subject or their                healthcare provider to upload the individual                subject's in situ image data, in situ diffraction                pattern data, subject data, or any combination of                the data to the computer database in exchange for                processing of the subject's data to receive the                computer-aided diagnostic indicator for the                subject, thus allowing the healthcare provider or                individual subject to make payments or upload the                patient's signed consent form.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                of using diffractometer-based global in situ                diagnostic system.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows the schematic diagram of                tissue diffractometers operatively coupled to a                computer database over a network.
