AB    NOVELTY - Invention refers to medicine, oncology, surgery, radiology, dermatology, physiotherapy and can be used for treating acute radiation reactions after neutron therapy in patients with locally advanced breast cancer. Irradiation zone and surrounding tissues from the first day of acute radiation detection with infrared laser radiation with constant magnetic field, intensity of magnetic induction within 20 mT, repetition rate of pulsed laser radiation of infrared spectrum within 80 Hz, power 0.51.0 W throughout the irradiation area with defocused beam for 60120 seconds. Further, the VC20 biologically active point is exposed for 35 seconds, after which the treated skin area is treated with cedar nut oil twice a day. Therapeutic course includes 812 daily procedures.
   USE - Medicine.
   ADVANTAGE - Method provides preventing the development of late radiation reactions, reducing the length of recovery of patients in the period of radiation therapy by exposure to infrared laser radiation and treatment of damaged areas of skin with cedar nut oil.

AB    NOVELTY - Composition comprises an agent for measuring                the expression level of methionyl-tRNA synthetase 1                (MARS1) or its fragment, or a gene encoding the                same.
   USE - The composition, kit or device is useful for                diagnosing cancer in the biological sample isolated                from the target individual. The cancer comprises at                least one chosen from thyroid cancer, parathyroid                cancer, pancreatic cancer, stomach cancer, ovarian                cancer, colon cancer, liver cancer, breast cancer,                cervical cancer, lung cancer, non-small cell lung                cancer, prostate cancer, gallbladder cancer,                biliary tract cancer, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma,                Hodgkin's lymphoma, blood cancer, bladder cancer,                kidney cancer, melanoma, colon cancer, bone cancer,                skin cancer, head cancer, uterine cancer, rectal                cancer, brain tumor, anal cancer, fallopian tube                carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma, vaginal cancer,                vulvar carcinoma, esophageal cancer, small                intestine cancer, endocrine cancer, adrenal cancer,                soft tissue sarcoma, urethral cancer, penile                cancer, ureteral cancer, renal cell carcinoma,                renal pelvic carcinoma, central nervous system                (CNS) tumor, primary CNS lymphoma, spinal cord                tumor, brainstem glioma, and pituitary adenoma,                preferably thyroid cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The composition enables accurate diagnosis                even in cases where the thyroid cell morphology is                non-diagnostic or atypical and cannot be                pathologically determined through MARS1 special                staining, and belongs to the indeterminate nodule                category, thus enabling early and precise detection                of thyroid cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a kit comprising the composition;
   a method for providing information for                diagnosing cancer involves measuring the expression                level of MARS1 or its fragment, or a gene encoding                the same in a biological sample isolated from a                target organism; and
   a device comprising (a) a measuring unit for                measuring the expression level of MARS1 or its                fragment, or a gene encoding the same for a                biological sample obtained from a target                individual, and (b) a detection unit for outputting                the presence or absence of cancer from the                expression level of the protein measured by the                measuring unit or the protein encoding it.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecules: The agent for                  measuring the expression level of the protein                  comprises at least one chosen from an antibody,                  an oligopeptide, a ligand, a peptide nucleic acid                  (PNA), and an aptamer that specifically binds to                  the protein. The agent for measuring the                  expression level of the gene comprises at least                  one chosen from a primer, a probe, and an                  antisense nucleotide that specifically bind to                  the gene. Preferred Sample: The biological sample                  comprises at least one chosen from whole blood,                  leukocytes, peripheral blood mononuclear cells,                  buffy coat, plasma, serum, sputum, tears, mucus,                  nasal washes, nasal aspirate, breath, urine,                  semen, saliva, peritoneal washings, ascites,                  cystic fluid, meningeal fluid, amniotic fluid,                  glandular fluid, pancreatic fluid, lymph fluid,                  pleural fluid, nipple aspirate, bronchial                  aspirate, synovial fluid, joint aspirate, organ                  secretions, cells, cell extracts, and                  cerebrospinal fluid. Preferred Kit: The kit is a                  reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) kit, a DNA                  chip kit, an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay                  (ELISA) kit, a protein chip kit, a rapid kit, or                  a multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) kit.                  Preferred Method: The method involves determining                  that the target individual has developed or is                  likely to develop cancer when the expression                  level of MARS1 or its fragment, or a gene                  encoding the same measured in the biological                  sample is higher than that of the control group.                  The method involves determining that the target                  individual has developed cancer or is likely to                  develop cancer when the expression level of MARS1                  or its fragment measured in the biological                  sample, or gene encoding the same corresponds to                  strong positivity (3+) or moderate positivity                  (2+) in the immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis                  result. The method involves determining that the                  target individual has developed cancer or has a                  low probability of developing cancer or does not                  have cancer when the expression level of MARS1 or                  its fragment measured in the biological sample,                  or a gene encoding the same corresponds to a weak                  positive (1+) result in IHC analysis. In the                  method, the expression level of the protein is                  measured by protein chip analysis, immunoassay,                  ligand binding assay, matrix assisted laser                  desorption/ionization time of flight mass                  spectrometry (MALDI-TOF) analysis, surface                  enhanced laser desorption/ionization time of                  flight mass spectrometry (SELDI-TOF) analysis,                  radioimmunoassay, radioimmunodiffusion,                  Ouchterlony immunodiffusion, rocket                  immunoelectrophoresis, tissue immunostaining,                  complement fixation assay, two-dimensional                  electrophoresis analysis, liquid                  chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), Western                  blotting, ELISA, or MRM method. In the method,                  the expression level of the gene is measured by                  RT-PCR, competitive RT-PCR, real-time RT-PCR,                  RNase protection assay (RPA), Northern blotting,                  or DNA chip.

TI Autoantibody detection panel, useful e.g. for            analyzing e.g. plasma to monitor e.g. breast cancer,            comprises autoantibody detection reagent species or            reagent species that are cancer-testis antigen reagent            species, and a substrate.
AU BONNER-FERRABY P
   HEPBURNE-SCOTT H
   MCCORMICK A
   BONNER-FERRABY P W
AE SERAMETRIX (SERA-Non-standard)
   BONNER-FERRABY P W (BONN-Individual)

GA 2010G61146
AB    NOVELTY - Autoantibody detection panel comprises: many                independently selected autoantibody detection                reagent species or the reagent species that are                cancer-testis (CT) antigen reagent species; and at                least one substrate, optionally a solid support,                upon which the autoantibody detection reagent                species are immobilized. At least one of the                autoantibody detection reagent species is a CT                antigen reagent species specifically reactive with                a cancer-associated autoantibody species reactive                with naturally occurring cancer-associated CT                antigen species.
   USE - The autoantibody detection panel is useful for                analyzing a biological sample, where the assay is                useful: as a screen to assess whether the subject                is healthy or diseased, has been administered a                drug, or if the subject has been administered a                drug, whether the subject responds favorably,                detrimentally, or does not respond to the drug; for                monitoring disease progression, disease diagnosis,                disease prognosis, or disease treatment, which is a                cancer e.g. breast cancer, a lung cancer, prostate                cancer, pancreatic cancer, colon cancer, colorectal                cancer, a melanoma, a myeloma, ovarian cancer, a                leukemia or a sarcoma in the biological sample                consisting of a bodily fluid or tissue sample,                where the bodily fluid is whole blood, blood                plasma, blood serum, saliva, urine, synovial fluid,                cerebrospinal fluid, mucous, a nasal secretion,                sputum, amniotic fluid or bronchoalveolar lavage                fluid and the tissue sample comprises cells or                components from of cells, in either case consisting                of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, total white                blood cells, lymph node cells, spleen cells, tonsil                cells, skin cells or cells from a biopsy; and to                assess a change in an autoantibody parameter of                many autoantibody species in biological sample                obtained from a mammalian subject, optionally a                human subject, where the result of the analysis of                autoantibody parameters is used to make an                assessment consisting of (a) whether the subject                has, or is pre-disposed to have, a disease, whether                the subject has a recurrence of a disease and                whether the subject is responsive to a disease                treatment (all claimed). Test details are described                but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The autoantibody detection panel: allows                highly reproducible assays to be performed,                including those run in multiplex or high-throughput                formats; provides high reproducibility, high                throughput and small sample volumes (on the                microliter scale or smaller). The assays have                sufficient sensitivity and dynamic range to measure                physiological levels of multiple serum                autoantibodies in a single assay, hence can be used                as effective tools in the measurement of humoral                immune responses in diseases e.g. cancer as well as                autoimmune disease and diseases caused by                infectious agents (e.g. pathogenic bacteria, fungi,                viruses and prions).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Autoantibody detection panel comprises: many                independently selected autoantibody detection                reagent species or the reagent species that are                cancer-testis (CT) antigen reagent species; and at                least one substrate, optionally a solid support,                upon which the autoantibody detection reagent                species are immobilized. At least one of the                autoantibody detection reagent species is a CT                antigen reagent species specifically reactive with                a cancer-associated autoantibody species reactive                with naturally occurring cancer-associated CT                antigen species. At least first and second CT                antigen reagent species are specifically reactive                with first and second autoantibody species reactive                with naturally occurring cancer-associated CT                antigen species. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also                included for:
   a kit comprising the autoantibody detection                panel and instructions for use of the array or                microarray; and
   analyzing a biological sample, comprising                contacting under binding conditions the                autoantibody detection panel with an aliquot of a                biological sample obtained from a subject and                determining whether the biological sample contains                an autoantibody reactive with at least one CT                antigen reagent species of the autoantibody                detection panel, thus analyzing the sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The panel comprises                  2-500 independently selected CT antigen reagent                  species. Each CT antigen reagent species                  comprises an autoantibody-reactive moiety                  including a polypeptide or a peptide, where the                  polypeptide optionally is a full-length CT                  antigen polypeptide, a fragment of a full-length                  CT antigen polypeptide that comprises a CT                  antigenic domain, a synthetic polypeptide that                  comprises a CT antigenic domain, or a peptide                  that comprises a CT antigenic domain. The panel                  further comprises: at least one                  disease-associated non-CT antigen reagent species                  disposed on the substrate, where the                  disease-associated non-CT antigen reagent species                  comprises a cancer-associated protein, optionally                  p53 or a p53 variant, a matrix metalloproteinase,                  and a mucin; and at least one positive control                  reagent disposed on the substrate, where the                  positive control reagent is reactive with an                  antigen optionally including tetanus toxoid,                  polio virus, rubella, diphtheria, mumps or                  measles. The panel comprises many substrates,                  where each is optionally a solid support upon                  which a different CT antigen reagent species is                  immobilized. The panel is configured as an array                  or microarray, where each of many independently                  selected autoantibody detection reagent species                  is immobilized on the same or different                  substrates, optionally microparticles. Preferred                  Method: The method is performed to determine an                  autoantibody profile of the subject, where the                  autoantibody profile is reflective of                  disease-associated autoantibody species present                  in the biological sample that are reactive with                  autoantibody detection reagent species of the                  autoantibody detection pane. The determining step                  is performed by detecting complexes of                  autoantibody species present in the biological                  sample specifically reactive with a CT antigen                  reagent species of the article, where optionally                  detection of complexes is performed under binding                  conditions using (a) a detection reagent capable                  of binding to at least one autoantibody species                  from the subject and (b) detecting the detection                  reagent, where the detection reagent optionally                  comprises a detectable label and an antibody, an                  antibody fragment, or an antibody derivative. The                  method further comprises assessing a change in an                  autoantibody parameter of at least one                  autoantibody capable of analysis by the method,                  where the autoantibody parameter optionally is of                  presence or absence of the autoantibody and a                  change in an amount of the autoantibody,                  optionally an increase or decrease in the amount                  of the autoantibody.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

GA 2012H43606
AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting cancer cell, involves                contacting peripheral blood sample containing                to-be-tested cell with marker substance under in                vitro condition, where the marker substance is                taken into the to-be-tested cell and the                above-mentioned to-be-tested cell is labeled                marked, and detecting high level of degree of                marker in to-be-tested cell as cancer cell and low                level of degree of marker in to-be-tested cell as                healthy cells.
   USE - The method and kit are useful for detecting                cancer cell (claimed). The cancer includes brain                tumor, pituitary adenoma, acoustic nerve myeloma,                retinoblastoma, lung cancer, breast cancer, stomach                cancer, esophageal cancer, colon cancer, bile duct                cancer, gall bladder cancer, pancreatic cancer,                renal cell carcinoma, prostate cancer, bladder                cancer, uterine cervix cancer, endometrial cancer,                vaginal cancer, ovarian cancer, skin cancer, basal                cell carcinoma, malignant melanoma, malignant bone                tumor, chronic lymphocytic leukemia, small cell                lymphoma and multiple myeloma.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is simple and rapid.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for kit for                cancer cell detection, which comprises the marker                substance, at least one antibody, and washing                liquid.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method involves                  obtaining fluorescence intensity of the                  to-be-tested cell, when using precursor of                  substance labeled with fluorescent material or                  fluorescent material as marker. The method                  involves obtaining at least one type chosen from                  average fluorescence intensity and sum total                  fluorescence intensity of the to-be-tested cell.                  The detection is performed based on the size of                  the to-be-tested cell. The method involves                  subjecting the peripheral blood sample containing                  the to-be-tested cell to hemolysis process. The                  method involves using specific antibody chosen                  from anti- cluster of differentiation (CD)45                  antibody and anti-CD34 antibody. The method                  involves contacting peripheral blood sample                  containing to-be-tested cell with marker                  substance under in vitro condition in presence of                  iron ion and reducing agent at 1-42&#176; C                  for 1-5 hours. The method involves using 0.1                  &#956; M-100 mM of marker substance.                  Preferred Components: The marker substance is at                  least one type chosen from sugar, labeled amino                  acid, cell, and substance metabolized by                  protoporphyrin 9. The sugar is monosaccharide.                  The marker substance is fluorescent labeled                  glucose derivative or labeled amino acid, and the                  amino acid is at least one type chosen from                  natural amino acid and unnatural amino acid. The                  amino acid is at least one type chosen from                  neutral amino acid and acidic amino acid. The                  substance metabolized by the protoporphyrin 9 is                  chosen from aminolevulinic acid and its                  derivative(s). The aminolevulinic acid and its                  derivative(s) are at least one type chosen from                  their salts and esters.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Non-invasive enzyme screen method for facilitating detection of tissue remodeling-associated condition, e.g. cancer, arthritic condition, involves detecting a matrix metalloproteinase in urine sample.
AU MOSES M A
   FREEMAN M R
   WIEDERSCHAIN D
AE CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
GA 2007252431
AB    NOVELTY - A non-invasive method for facilitating detection of a tissue remodeling-associated condition in a subject, comprises detecting a matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) in a urine sample from the subject, where the presence of the matrix metalloproteinase facilitates the detection of the condition in the subject.
   USE - The method is useful for facilitating the detection of a tissue remodeling-associated condition, e.g. cancer, e.g. nervous system, breast, retina, lung, skin, kidney, liver, pancreas, genitourinary tract, and gastrointestinal tract; arthritic condition, e.g. rheumatoid arthritis; an obstructive condition, e.g. ; an ulcerative condition; a degenerative condition; type of renal disorder, e.g. renal tubule obstruction, renal damage, or renal ulcers; and prostate disorder, e.g. hyperplasia, problematic prostatic hyperplasia, or benign prostatic hypertrophy in a subject (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method uses biological fluid samples that may be obtained by personnel without medical training, and do not require visiting clinic or hospital. The method allows early diagnoses of appearance of these conditions and to prognoses of changes in these conditions.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Method: The matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) has a molecular weight of 72-greater than or equal to150, preferably greater than or equal to82-92 kDa. The MMP is detected immunochemically, by radioimmunoassay, or by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The MMP is MMP-9 or MMP-2.

TI Device for tumor site identification, comprises            light irradiation unit for converting protoporphyrin IX            present in tumor site into photo-protoporphyrin,            spectroscopic unit, optical detection unit and tumor            discrimination unit.
AU KOIZUMI N
   TAKAMATSU T
   HARADA Y
   OTSUJI E
AE UNIV KYOTO PREFECTURAL PUBLIC CORP (UKTP-C)
   UNIV KYOTO PREFECTURAL PUBLIC CORP (UKTP-C)
GA 2013A27396
AB    NOVELTY - Device for identification of tumor site,                comprises light irradiation unit for converting                portion of protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) present in                tumor site into photo-protoporphyrin (PPp),                spectroscopic unit/light splitting unit for                separating fluorescence of the PpIX and                fluorescence of PPp into spectra, small optical                detection unit for detecting relative fluorescence                intensity of fluorescence of PpIX and fluorescence                of PPp, and tumor discrimination unit for                discriminating a tumor site and a non-tumor site on                the basis of the relative fluorescence                intensities.
   USE - The device and method are useful for                identifying tumor site preferably tumor                metastasized to the sentinel lymph node (all                claimed), or cancer including skin cancer, lung                cancer, bronchial cancer, esophageal cancer,                stomach cancer, colon cancer, rectal cancer, colon                cancer, liver cancer, renal cancer, breast cancer,                uterine cancer, ovarian cancer, bladder cancer, and                brain tumor.
   ADVANTAGE - The device and method enable rapid diagnosis                of tumor site with high accuracy in an easy and                simple manner, even when the tumor site is covered                with connective tissue preferably fat and collagen,                hence surgical approach of the tumor is also                improved. The device aids intraoperative diagnosis                and leads to a more exact diagnosis and surgery                without limited operation or retention.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Device for identification of tumor site,                comprises (a) light irradiation unit for converting                portion of protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) present in the                tumor site into photo-protoporphyrin (PPp), (b)                spectroscopic unit/light splitting unit for                separating fluorescence of the PpIX and                fluorescence of PPp into spectra, (c) small optical                detection unit for detecting relative fluorescence                intensity of fluorescence of PpIX and fluorescence                of PPp, and (d) tumor discrimination unit for                discriminating a tumor site and a non-tumor site on                the basis of the relative fluorescence intensities                of the PpIX and PPp, where the device                spectroscopically detects fluorescence of the                protoporphyrin chosen from PpIX and PPp present in                the tumor site of test sample. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM                is included for method for identifying tumor site                using the above-mentioned device.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Device: The light irradiation unit                  is provided with optical fiber as light sources                  for guiding light irradiated from the light                  source and excitation light from the light source                  at the test sample. The detection unit is                  provided with a unit for detecting fluorescence                  derived from the PpIX at 635 nm, and unit for                  detecting fluorescence derived from the PPp at                  675 nm. The optical fiber guides fluorescence of                  the PpIX and fluorescence of the PPp to the                  spectroscopic unit. The device further comprises                  display unit for displaying information of result                  determined by the discrimination unit as image                  information corresponding to the position of the                  test sample which generates the fluorescence as                  determined by the determination unit.

GA 2007175669
AB    NOVELTY - Predicting recurrence of cancer in a cancer                patient undergoing surgical resection by obtaining                a tissue sample from the surgical margin of the                resected tumor, and assessing histone levels in the                tissue sample, where elevated histone levels in the                sample are predictive of the recurrence of cancer,                is new.
   USE - For predicting recurrence of cancer, e.g.                cancer of the brain, lung, liver, spleen, kidney,                pancreas, small intestine, blood cells, lymph node,                colon, breast, endometrium, stomach, prostate,                testicle, ovary, skin, head and neck, esophagus, or                bone marrow (claimed), in a cancer patient                undergoing surgical resection.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   prediction of survival of a cancer patient                undergoing surgical resection;
   prediction of cancer progression in a cancer                patient undergoing surgical resection; and
   detection of field cancerization in a cancer                patient, by obtaining a tissue sample from the                surgical margin of the resected tumor, and                assessing histone levels in the tissue sample,                where elevated histone levels in the tissue sample                are predictive of decreased survival time or cancer                progression, or indicative of field                cancerization.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Sample: The tissue sample is an                  intact tissue sample comprising &#8805;6                  (preferably &#8805;96) micro-regions. The                  micro-region is a microwell of 5-200 (preferably                  50) &#956;m.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: Assessing histone levels                  includes subjecting a spatially discrete                  micro-region of intact tissue sample to physical                  or chemical treatment(s), and assessing histone                  levels in a protein sample from the micro-region;                  subjecting a second spatially discrete                  micro-region of intact tissue sample to physical                  or chemical treatment(s), and assessing histone                  levels in a protein sample from the second                  spatially discrete micro-region; and comparing                  the histone levels of the first and second                  spatially discrete micro-regions. The first and                  second spatially discrete micro-regions receive                  the same or distinct physical or chemical                  treatments. The physical or chemical treatment                  includes solvent treatment, detergent treatment,                  lipase treatment, proteolysis, reactive agent                  treatment, or labeling. Labeling includes                  treatment with isotope dilution reagent, labeled                  antibody, or enzyme. Assessing histone levels                  occurs in-situ in the micro-region or after                  removal of protein sample from the micro-region.                  The tissue sample from the micro-region may be                  analyzed for at least two cancer associated                  markers, e.g. protein, nucleic acid, lipid,                  carbohydrate, or metabolite. Assessing histone                  levels may include mass spectrometry, e.g.                  secondary ion mass spectrometry, laser desorption                  mass spectrometry, matrix-assisted laser                  desorption/ionization mass spectrometry,                  surface-enhanced laser desorption/ionization mass                  spectrometry, desorption electrospray mass                  spectrometry, or electrospray mass spectrometry;                  immunological detection; quantitative detection                  of RNA, e.g. RT-PCR or Northern blotting; or                  assessing histone octamer, histone unit (e.g.                  H2A, H2B, H3, H4, or H1), or its fragment. The                  method may include treating the cancer patient                  with an anti-cancer therapy, e.g. chemotherapy,                  radiotherapy, gene therapy, immunotherapy, or                  hormonal therapy.

   ERCIN M

GA 2024A92430
AB    NOVELTY - Method for performing in vitro diagnosis of                insulin-related disease or a neoplastic disease                involves detecting presence and/or changes in level                of at least one microRNA (miRNA) chosen from                miR-30d, miR-124, miR-433-5p, miR-18a, miR-19b,                miR-184, miR-335, miR-146a and miR-503, or DNA,                mRNA or long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) associated                with the miRNAs in a sample.
   USE - The method is useful for performing in vitro                diagnosis of insulin-related disease or neoplastic                disease. The insulin-related disease is metabolic                and neurodegenerative diseases including lactose                intolerance, fructose intolerance, galactosemia,                glycogen storage disease, insulin resistance                syndrome, retinopathy, syndrome X, nephropathy,                foot ulcer, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, metabolic                syndrome, gallbladder disease, osteoarthritis,                cardiovascular disease, stroke, sleep apnea, liver                disease, asthma, respiratory distress, menstrual                irregularities, musculoskeletal system problems,                skin diseases, polycystic ovary syndrome, immune                system disorders, diabetes, obesity, Alzheimer's                disease and other types of dementia, Parkinson's                disease and other diseases associated with                Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease,                amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), Batten                disease, motor neuron disease, spinal muscular                atrophy, Prion disease, spinocerebellar ataxia,                dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple sclerosis (MS),                neuropathy and Friedrich ataxia. The diabetes is                type I diabetes or type II diabetes. The neoplastic                disease is chosen from breast cancer, prostate                cancer, colorectal cancer, skin cancer, small cell                lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer,                mesothelioma, gastrointestinal cancer, pancreatic                cancer, glioblastoma, vulva cancer, cervical                cancer, endometrial carcinoma, ovarian cancer,                liver cancer, hepatoma, bladder cancer, kidney                cancer, salivary gland carcinoma, thyroid cancer,                leukemia, and various head and neck cancers (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables rapid detection of                insulin-related diseases, especially diabetes and                obesity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                biomarker, which comprises at least one miRNA                chosen from miR-30d, miR-124, miR-433-5p, miR-18a,                miR-19b, miR-184, miR-335, miR-146a and miR-503 for                diagnosis of insulin-related disease.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Sample: The sample is chosen from                  blood, plasma, serum, milk, bronchoalveolar fluid                  and cerebrospinal fluid. Preferred Method: The                  detection of presence of the miRNAs or their                  associated DNA, mRNA or lncRNA and/or detection                  of changes in their level is performed by a                  molecular method chosen from Southern blotting,                  Northern blotting, PCR, reverse transcription                  (RT)-PCR, quantitative RT-PCR, microarray and                  sequencing.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Breast skin surface thermal screening device                for early detection of breast cancer comprises: (a)                main controller is a single-board computer (1) used                to run the deep learning (DL) based breast thermal                image recognition program, namely raspberry Pi (1)                with a connected to a wave share LCD monitor (4)                using an high-definition multimedia interface cable                (104), with user interaction with the computer                using an interactive visual component system (105)                to allow the computer software to function; (b)                thermal sensor (2) uses infrared with a 160x 120                image array format specification, image size 12                which functions to capture the reflection of the                body surface temperature in the breast area and                quantize it into an image, which is connected to 8                pins, namely serial data (SDA) to transfer data                serially between the raspberry and the thermal                sensor, serial clock (SCL) to regulate the speed of                serial data transfer between the Raspberry and the                thermal sensor, master input, slave input (MOSI) to                transfer data from Raspberry to the thermal sensor                when communicating serial interface, master input,                slave output (MISO) to transfer data from the                thermal sensor to raspberry when communicating,                clock (CLK) clock pin for which is used to regulate                the data transfer speed between raspberry and the                thermal sensor, voltage input (VIN) is used to                provide input voltage to the thermal sensor,                (ground) to secure the ground connection between                the Raspberry with the thermal sensor, and chip                select (CS) to enable or disable the thermal sensor                when communicating; (c) card with a size of 64GB to                store the DL artificial intelligence based                prediction model which after being equipped with                deploy coding becomes only 4.18 MB in size and the                supporting computation for the detection algorithm                is 10.2 MB with class interpreter to enable access                to the DL model; and (d) LCD monitor (4) to display                the results of the thermal sensor capture and                displayed if the serial interface speed value is                set to 10000000.

AB    NOVELTY - Antifouling microbubble comprises hollow glass                microspheres, antifouling coating, which is                provided on the surface of the hollow glass                microspheres, and a capture layer obtained by                arranging an N-hydroxysuccinimide derivative on the                antifouling coating, where the antifouling coating                is phase-changed bovine serum albumin.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                preparation method of the antifouling microbubble,                involving (a) adding bovine serum albumin solution                and tris(2-carboxyethyl) phosphine solution into a                hollow glass microspheres, adjusting the pH value                to 5 and mixing for 0.5-12 hours, (b) centrifuging                the mixture to remove the lower solution, adding                ultrapure water for washing, repeating                centrifugation for 1-5 times, and vacuum drying to                obtain glass microbubble with antifouling function,                (c) reacting the glass microbubble with antifouling                function obtained in step (b) with                N-hydroxysuccinimide derivatives, centrifuging,                removing the lower layer solution, adding ultrapure                water for washing, repeating centrifugation 1-5                times, and vacuum drying to obtain the                product.

TI Conjugates of perylenequinone compounds with            binding agents used for the photodynamic therapy of            e.g. cancer, skin conditions, viral, retroviral,            bacterial or fungal diseases.
AU MADIYALAKAN R
   LOWN J W
   MILLER G G
   MOORE R B
   DIWU Z
AE ALTAREX CORP (ALTA-Non-standard)
   ALTAREX CORP (ALTA-Non-standard)
   ALTAREX CORP (ALTA-Non-standard)
   UNIV ALBERTA (UYAL-C)
   UNIV ALBERTA (UYAL-C)
GA 1998437128
AB       Conjugates of perylenequinone (PQ) are used in                treatment comprising administering PQ bound to a                binding agent, and activating by exposure to light                of a predetermined wavelength.
   Also claimed are:
   (1) a method of treatment comprising                administering a conjugate comprising a hypocrellin                (HC)-B (HCB) derivative bound to a monoclonal                antibody (MAb) or antibody fragment, and activating                the HCB derivative by exposing the HCB derivative                to light of a predetermined wavelength;
   (2) a composition comprising a PQ conjugated to                a binding agent;
   (3) a composition comprising a HC derivative                conjugated to a binding agent;
   (4) a composition comprising a derivative of                HCB conjugated to a binding agent, the binding                agent selected from an antibody, a MAb, or a                fragment; where the binding agent binds to an                antigen of a cancer cell, and the cancer cell is                selected from ovarian cancer, breast cancer, and                gastrointestinal cancer, and where the derivative                of HCB is a functionalised derivative that can be                activated by exposing the derivative to a                predetermined wavelength of light;
   (5) a method for destroying or inactivating                tumour cells which comprises administering a                suitable amount of 1 HC derivative, and activating                the HC derivative, and
   (6) a method for treating a disease or                condition which comprises administering a                composition comprising a HC derivative and 1 of a                pKa modifier, a buffer, a salt, a base, an acid,                saline, and an adjuvant.
   USE -   The PQ derivatives exhibit high absorption in                the red spectral region and generate singlet oxygen                and a variety of toxic free radicals. The methods                and compositions can be used for treating cancers,                e.g. ovarian, breast or gastrointestinal cancer,                viral diseases, retroviral diseases, bacterial                diseases, fungal diseases or skin conditions such                as lesions of the vulva, keloid, vitiligo,                psoriasis, benign tumours, endometriosis, Barett's                esophagus, Tunea capitis or lichen amyloidosis. The                products can also be used for detection and                diagnosis.

TI BCS-device is a power full tool to detect cancer by using advanced quantitative transmission ultrasound, where ultrasound is powerful and emerging imaging paradigm which has potential to perform image reconstruction of biological tissue.

GA 201951435W
AB    NOVELTY - BCS-device is a power full tool to detect cancer by using advanced quantitative transmission ultrasound (QT), where advanced quantitative transmission ultrasound is a powerful and emerging imaging paradigm which has potential to perform true to fetch 0-360 degrees three-dimensional intelligent image reconstruction of biological tissue. The breast imaging is an important application of QT and allows non-invasive and non-ionizing imaging of complete breast in viva and other advanced technology. The first demonstration of different type of breast tissue is classified in QT imaging. The BCS-device assess of ability of QT images to differentiate between advanced normal breast tissue types. The three QT advanced features are used in support vector machines (SVM) average classifiers, and classifies breast tissue as skin, fat, nose skin, finger skin, gland, duct or connective tissue, which are demonstrated with an overall accuracy of greater than 92%.
   USE - BCS-device.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The classifier is validated on complete breast image volumes to provide various color-coded breast tissue volume, and the study serves as a first and second step towards a computer-aided detection/diagnosis platform for QT.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The BCS-device detects stage of cancer, provides 3-D image of cancer, provides view of object in 0-360 degrees , provides medicine of stage of a cancer, provides time line of stage of cancer, and provides expenses of stage of a cancer.

AB    NOVELTY - The utility model relates to the technical                field of cancer cell detection sampling device,                claims a detection sampling device for detecting                cancer cell gene, comprising two fixing plates, two                fixing columns are fixedly set between the two                fixing plates, two sides of the lower end surface                of the fixing plate at the lower end are fixedly                connected with connecting columns, the lower end                faces of the two connecting columns are movably                provided with adjusting columns, the lower end                faces of the two adjusting columns are fixedly                connected with suction cups, the inner parts of the                two fixing plates are embedded with fixing blocks.                In the utility model, the detection and sampling                device for detecting cancer cell gene has the                following advantages: the sampling structure can be                fixed on the skin surface of the patient, which                ensures the stability of the sampling of the                sampling needle, reduces the pain of the patient,                can accurately adjust the length of the sampling                needle inserted into the body of the patient                according to the need, It is more convenient to                use, the sampling needle can be separated from the                outside in time after the sampling needle is pulled                out of the body of the patient, it avoids the                professional exposure, and it is safer to                use.

TI New antigenic polypeptide, useful for diagnosing and treating cancer, e.g. T cell lymphomas, synovial sarcoma, seminoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Leiomyosarcoma, or breast cancer.
AU BATHEJA A D
   HO G
   DANDREA M
   UHLINGER D J
   D'ANDREA M
AE BATHEJA A D (BATH-Individual)
   HO G (HOGG-Individual)
   DANDREA M (DAND-Individual)
   UHLINGER D J (UHLI-Individual)
   JANSSEN PHARM NV (JANC-C)
   JANSSEN PHARM NV (JANC-C)
GA 2007475581
AB    NOVELTY - An antigenic polypeptide selected from SEQ ID NOS: 6-11 is new.
   USE - The isolated polypeptides, nucleic acids, antibodies and cells are useful in screening methods, drug discovery assays, and in detection assays. The composition is useful for diagnosing and treating cancer, e.g. T cell lymphomas, synovial sarcoma, seminoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Leiomyosarcoma, kidney cancer, fibrosarcoma and Ewings sarcoma, glioma, ovarian yolk sac tumor, melanoma, medulloblastoma, Hodgkin's disease, B cell lymphoma, pancreatic cancer, endometrical cancer, prostate cancer, esophagus cancer, thyroid cancer, skin squamous cell cancer, neuroblastoma, nerve sheath malignant tumor, lung cancer, skin basal cell cancer, urinary bladder, liver cancer, stomach cancer, mesothelioma, gastric cancer, esophageal cancer, cervical cancer, rectal cancer, colon cancer, osteosarcoma, gastro stromal tumor, and breast cancer (preferred).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An antigenic polypeptide is selected from: Tyr-Ser-Gly-Lys-Arg-Lys-Gly-Pro-Asp-Ser-Leu-Ser-Asp-Gly-Pro-Ala;
   Gln-Asp-Phe-His-Gly-Gly-Gln-Val-Phe-Ser-Pro-Pro-Gln-Lys-Cys;
   Pro-Ala-Tyr-Glu-Pro-Asn-Leu-Phe-Asp-Gly-Pro-Glu-Ser-Gln-Phe-Cys;
   Asp-Asp-Ser-Arg-Gly-Gly-Glu-Gly-Leu-Arg-Asp-Ala;
   His-Glu-Leu-Gln-Arg-Asn-Gln-Gln-Pro-His-Ser-Pro-Glu; or
   Lys-Gly-Lys-Ser-Ile-Gln-Gln-Arg-Ala-Pro-Pro-Tyr (SEQ ID NOS: 6-11).
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   (1) an antibody which selectively binds to a polypeptide above;
   (2) a method of detecting cancer;
   (3) a method of detecting a dedifferentiated cell in a tissue sample;
   (4) a kit comprising an antibody of (1);
   (5) a method of decreasing MAIL (Molecule possessing Ankyrin repeats Induced by LPS) expression in a cell;
   (6) an shRNA molecule of 19-30 nucleic acids in length, encoded by a sequence comprising SEQ ID NO: 5, where the shRNA molecule hybridizes under stringent conditions to a MAIL polynucleotide comprising SEQ ID NOS: 2 or 22;
   (7) a method of regulating the expression of an inflammatory cytokine in a cell;
   (8) a method of regulating expression of MCP-1 in a cell; and
   (9) a method of identifying compounds capable of decreasing MAIL expression.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Antibody: The antibody is a polyclonal antibody or a monoclonal antibody. Preferred Method: Detecting cancer comprises contacting a tissue sample with at least one antibody of (1), and detecting binding of the antibody in the sample, where increased levels of antibody binding in the sample relative to a control indicates cancer in the sample. Detection comprises at least one process selected from: ELISA, western blot, immunoprecipitation, IHC, or flow cytometry. Alternatively, the method comprises measuring the level of expression of a MAIL marker in a patient sample, and measuring the normal level of expression of the MAIL marker in a control non-cancer sample, where at least a two-fold elevated expression of the MAIL marker in the patient sample indicates cancer. The method also comprises:(A) measuring the level of expression of a MAIL marker in a patient sample;(B) measuring the level of at least one inflammatory cytokine in the patient sample, selected from: IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p40, MCP-1, and MCP-2;(C) measuring the normal level of expression of the MAIL marker in a control non-cancer sample; and(D) measuring the level of at least one inflammatory cytokine in the control sample, selected from: IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p40, MCP-1, and MCP-2;(E) where at least a two-fold elevated expression of the MAIL marker and an increase in the expression of at least one inflammatory cytokine in the patient sample indicates cancer.Detecting cancer in a patient comprises:(A) measuring the level of expression of a MAIL marker in a patient sample;(B) measuring the level of expression at least one MHC class I marker in the patient sample selected from: HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C;(C) measuring the normal level of expression of the MAIL marker in a control non-cancer sample; and(D) measuring the level of at least one MHC class I marker in the patient sample selected from: HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C;(E) where at least a two-fold elevated expression of the MAIL marker and a decrease in the expression of at least one MHC class I marker in the patient sample indicates cancer.Detecting cancer in a patient comprises:(A) measuring the level of expression of a MAIL marker in a patient sample;(B) measuring the level of at least one MHC class II marker in the patient sample selected from: HLA-DR, HLADQ, HLA-DP;(C) measuring the normal level of expression of the MAIL marker in a control non-cancer sample; and(D) measuring the level of at least one MHC class II marker in the control sample selected from: HLA-DR, HLADQ, HLA-DP;(E) where at least a two-fold elevated expression of the MAIL marker and an increase in the expression of at least one MHC class II marker in the patient sample indicates cancer.Detecting a dedifferentiated cell in a tissue sample comprises contacting a tissue sample with at least one antibody of (1), and detecting binding of the antibody in the sample where increased levels of antibody binding in the sample relative to a control indicates at least one dedifferentiated cell in a tissue sample. Decreasing MAIL expression in a cell comprises introducing an shRNA molecule into a cell where the shRNA molecule binds to a MAIL polynucleotide. The cell is a transformed cell, a primary human monocyte, a macrophage, or a dendritic cell. The shRNA molecule is encoded by a sequence selected from SEQ ID NOS: 5, 23, or 24 (19 bp each). Regulating the expression of an inflammatory cytokine in a cell comprises decreasing a MAIL polypeptide expression by introducing a polynucleotide of SEQ ID NO: 5 into a cell, where the polynucleotide hybridizes to a MAIL polynucleotide and where the cell is a transformed cell, a primary human monocyte, a macrophage, or a dendritic cell. The inflammatory cytokine is IL-6, IL-8 (preferred), IL-10, IL-12p40, MCP-1, or MCP-2. Regulating expression of MCP-1 in a cell comprising decreasing MAIL polypeptide expression by introducing a nucleotide molecule consisting of SEQ ID NO: 5 into a cell where the nucleotide molecule hybridizes to MAIL and where, the cell is selected from: a transformed cell, a primary human monocyte, a macrophage, or a dendritic cell. Identifying compounds capable of decreasing MAIL expression comprises providing a cell membrane comprising MAIL or its fragment, contacting the cell membrane with a compound, treating the cell membrane with an antibody of (1), and determining the effect of the compound on the expression of the MAIL. The cell membrane comprises a cell. Determining step comprises comparing the level of expression of MAIL in the absence of the compound to the level of expression of MAIL in the presence of the compound. Alternatively, the method comprises providing a cell expressing MAIL or its fragment, adding a compound to the cell, and measuring MAIL mRNA or MAIL polypeptide. Measuring step comprises comparing the level of expression of MAIL in the absence of the compound to the level of expression of MAIL in the presence of the compound.

TI Single sensor chip for non-invasive breast cancer            detection made of nanoparticles, has set of radio            frequency arrays comprising combination of planar and            circular arrays, set of biomarkers detect presence of            tumor and biosensor to recognize biomarkers used, and            chip connected to monitor system.
AU PRADHAN K B
   ANDOTRA D S
   ANDOTRA S
AE UNIV CHITKARA (UCTK-C)
   CHITKARA INNOVATION INCUBATOR FOUND (UCTK-C)
GA 202371849A
AB    NOVELTY - Single sensor chip has a set of radio                frequency arrays comprising a combination of planar                and circular arrays to obtain a 3 dimensional (3D)                picture. A set of biomarkers detect the presence of                tumor and a set of biosensor to recognize the                biomarkers used. The chip is connected to a monitor                system to obtain the reconstructed 3D images of the                breast tissue.
   USE - Single sensor chip for non-invasive breast                cancer detection made of nanoparticles.
   ADVANTAGE - The chip has highly sensitive and specific in                detecting presence of cancerous cells, provides                early diagnosis of breast cancer non-invasively,                and is cheap, robust and easy to use, portable and                can be carried out from the comfort of one`s home                to carry out imaging for breast cancer                detection.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for non-invasive diagnosis of breast cancer using                the single sensor chip, which involves:
   (a) applying a radio-opaque gel on the skin                layer to enhance the contrasting and the emitted                rays from the chip;
   (b) placing the chip over the radio-opaque gel                to use a combination of radio frequency arrays and                biosensors; and
   (c) obtaining a real time image of the anatomy                of the breast tissue by connecting the chip to a                monitoring system.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The nanoparticles                  include Quantum Dots (QDs), Iron Oxide                  Nanoparticles, Gold Nanoparticles, Carbon                  Nanotubes, silver based nanoparticles or its                  silicon based nanoparticles. The chip comprises                  of biomarkers selected from human epidermal                  growth factor receptor-2 (HER2), estrogen                  receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR),                  Nucleic acid tumour markers, protein tumour                  markers, cellular tumour markers and/or exosomes.                  The biomarkers include nucleic acid tumour                  markers, selected from BRCA1, BRCA2, microRNA,                  circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating                  cell-free DNA (ccfDNA), circulating RNA (circRNA)                  or long noncoding RNAs(lncRNA). The set of                  biosensors includes electrochemical and optical                  biosensors.

TI Determining efficacy of anthracycline anticancer            agent to patient, comprises detecting/measuring            expression of activated protein kinase B in cancer            cell/tissue and determining efficacy of anthracycline            anticancer agent.
AU HARADA A
   YOSHIDA T
   HARADA S
AE SYSMEX CORP (SYSM-C)
   SYSMEX CORP (SYSM-C)
   SYSMEX CORP (SYSM-C)
GA 2008H21127
AB    NOVELTY - Method for determining an efficacy of an                anthracycline anticancer agent (I) to a patient,                comprises: detecting/measuring an expression of                activated Akt (protein kinase B) in a cancer cell                or a cancer tissue extracted from the patient; and                determining the efficacy of the anthracycline                anticancer agent based on a detection/measurement                result.
   USE - The method is useful for determining an                efficacy of (I) in a cancer cell or a cancer tissue                (lung cancer, stomach cancer, colon cancer, ovarian                cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, prostate                cancer, skin cancer or leukemia) (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides determination of efficacy                of (I) against cancer cell or cancer tissue,                without imposing a heavy burden on a patient. (I)                has reduced side effects.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a device                for determining the efficacy of the anthracycline                anticancer agent, comprising: an input part for                entering the expression level of activated Akt                (protein kinase B) in the cancer cell or the cancer                tissue extracted from a patient; a comparison part                for comparing the entered expression level to a                threshold level; a determination part for                determining the efficacy of the anthracycline                anticancer agent to the patient based on a                comparison result; and an output part for                outputting a determination result.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method further                  comprises detecting/measuring an expression of                  human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER-2),                  and phosphatase and tension homolog (PTEN) in the                  cancer cell or the cancer tissue extracted from a                  patient. The determination step is performed so                  as to determine that the efficacy is high, when                  both the activated Akt and the HER-2 excessively                  expresses. The determination is performed so as                  to determine that the efficacy is extremely high,                  when both the activated Akt and the PTEN                  excessively expresses. Preferred Components: (I)                  is daunorubicin, doxorubicin, pirarubicin,                  aclarubicin, epirubicin, oxaunomycin or                  idarubicin. The determination part determines                  that the efficacy is high, when the expression                  level of the activated Akt is higher than the                  threshold level. The determination part                  determines that the efficacy is extremely high,                  when the expression level of both the activated                  Akt and the HER-2 are higher than the threshold                  level. The input part further enters an                  expression level of HER-2 or PTEN.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Wearable personal digital device i.e. wrist watch,            for performing adoptive cell transfer test, has wire            placed under skin of user beneath sensor to obtain            sample, and sensor for analyzing sample to determine            blood glucose level.
AU XING Z T
   ZHOU A H B
   ZHOU T T G
AE XING Z T (XING-Individual)
   ZHOU A H B (ZHOU-Individual)
   ZHOU T T G (ZHOU-Individual)
GA 201957562M
AB    NOVELTY - The device (750) has a glucose metering unit                attached to a housing. The glucose metering unit is                communicated with a processor (755). The glucose                metering unit accommodates a test strip for                receiving a blood sample of a user. The glucose                metering unit measures a blood glucose level in the                blood sample upon insertion of the test strip                including the blood sample of the user into the                glucose metering unit. The glucose metering unit                communicates the blood glucose level to the                processor. An electrochemical detector is attached                to the housing. A sensor (760) is contacted with a                skin of the user. A wire is placed under the skin                of the user beneath the sensor to obtain a sample,                where the sample includes a blood sample. The                sensor analyzes the sample to determine the blood                glucose level.
   USE - Wearable personal digital device i.e. wrist                watch, for performing adoptive cell transfer test                using saliva, urine and blood of a user to treat                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The device provides quick and accurate                detection, reliable imaging of cancer cells by                biosensors so as to monitor angiogenesis and cancer                metastasis, thus improving effectiveness of                anticancer chemotherapy agents.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of a                wearable personal digital device.

PN WO2023180734-A1; EP4496901-A1; JP2025513709-W; US2025382672-A1
TI Detection or prognosis of clonal hematopoiesis by            extracting nucleic acid from biological sample            comprising thrombocytes, analyzing nucleic acid to            identify presence of clonal hematopoiesis associated            mutations, and indicating presence or prognosis of            clonal hematopoiesis.
AU PSAILA B
   MEAD A
   GREGORY C
AE UNIV OXFORD (UYOX-C)
   UNIV EDINBURGH (UEDG-C)
   UNIV EDINBURGH (UEDG-C)
   UNIV OXFORD (UYOX-C)
   UNIV EDINBURGH (UEDG-C)
   UNIV OXFORD (UYOX-C)
GA 2023A1900A
AB    NOVELTY - Method for detection or prognosis of clonal                hematopoiesis involves providing a biological                sample comprising thrombocytes, extracting nucleic                acid from biological sample, analyzing the nucleic                acid to identify presence of one or more clonal                hematopoiesis associated mutations, and indicating                the presence or prognosis of clonal hematopoiesis                based on presence of one or more clonal                hematopoiesis associated mutations.
   USE - The method is useful for performing detection                or prognosis of clonal hematopoiesis and cancer,                determining treatment for the subject, and treating                subject with clonal hematopoiesis and cancer. The                cancer associated nucleic acid fragment is                associated with gastric cancer, lung cancer,                non-small cell lung cancer, lung adenocarcinoma,                lung squamous cell carcinoma, bone cancer,                pancreatic cancer, colon cancer, colorectal cancer,                skin cancer, cancer of the head or neck, head and                neck squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, uterine                cancer, ovarian cancer, rectal cancer, cancer of                the anal region, stomach cancer, testicular cancer,                breast cancer, brain cancer, hepatocellular cancer,                carcinoma of fallopian tubes, carcinoma of                endometrium, carcinoma of cervix, carcinoma of                vagina, carcinoma of vulva, cancer of esophagus,                cancer of small intestine, cancer of endocrine                system, cancer of thyroid gland, cancer of                parathyroid gland, cancer of adrenal gland, kidney                cancer, sarcoma of soft tissue, cancer of urethra,                cancer of bladder, renal cancer, thymoma,                urothelial carcinoma leukemia, prostate cancer,                prostatic adenocarcinoma mesothelioma,                adrenocortical carcinoma, lymphomas, such as such                as Hodgkin's disease, non-Hodgkin's, and multiple                myelomas (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method exhibits no cytotoxicity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method for detection or prognosis of cancer                involves providing a biological sample comprising                thrombocytes, extracting nucleic acid from                biological sample, analyzing nucleic acid to                identify presence of one or more cancer associated                nucleic acid fragments, and indicating the presence                or prognosis of cancer based on presence of one or                more cancer associated nucleic acid                fragments;
   method for determining a treatment for a                subject involves performing the method of detection                or prognosis, and determining a suitable                treatment;
   kit (K1) comprising reagents for extraction of                nucleic acid from platelets and a panel of reagents                that specifically bind to and/or amplify one or                more clonal hematopoiesis associated mutations, and                optionally instructions for use;
   kit (K2) comprising reagents for extraction of                nucleic acid from platelets and a panel of reagents                that specifically bind to and/or amplify one or                more cancer associated modifications, or cancer                specific mutations;
   method for treatment of a subject with cancer                involves providing a biological sample comprising                thrombocytes, extracting nucleic acid from                biological sample, analyzing nucleic acid to                identify presence of one or more cancer associated                nucleic acid fragments, selecting a treatment, and                administering the treatment;
   method for preparing a nucleic acid fraction                involves providing a biological sample comprising                thrombocytes, extracting nucleic acid from                biological sample to form a nucleic acid sample,                enriching nucleic acid sample for one or more                cancer associated nucleic acid fragments and/or                clonal haematopoesis associated fragments;                and
   method for antenatal screening involves                providing a biological sample comprising                thrombocytes, obtained from a pregnant woman,                extracting nucleic acid from biological sample, and                analyzing nucleic acid for genetic information                related to the fetus.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecule: The clonal                  hematopoiesis associated mutations are chosen                  from JAK2V617F, JAK2 exon12, CALR exon9, MPLS505,                  MPLW515, CBL exon 8, CBL exon 9, KRAS exon 2,                  KRAS exon 3, GNB1 exon 5, DNMT3A all exons, TET2                  all exons, ASXL1 exon 12, IDH2 exon 4, SF3B1 exon                  14, SF3B1 exon 15, SRSF2P95, U2AF1 exon 2, U2AF1                  exon 6, PPM1 D exon 6, and TP53 all exons. The                  cancer associated nucleic acid fragment is DNA                  and/or RNA. The cancer associated nucleic acid                  fragment is a cell free nucleic acid fragment                  that has been released from a cancer and taken up                  by thrombocytes. The cancer associated nucleic                  acid fragment comprises a cancer associated                  modification, or a cancer specific mutation,                  methylation pattern, genetic aberration and/or                  fragmentation pattern. The cancer associated                  nucleic acid fragment is chosen from nucleic                  fragments comprising one or more mutations chosen                  from BRAFV600E, KRASG12D, PIKCAH1047R, and                  TP53R273H. The cancer associated nucleic acid                  fragment comprises 10-1500 nucleotides. The                  cancer associated nucleic acid fragment is                  associated with a solid tumor, sarcoma,                  carcinoma, and/or lymphoma. Preferred Method: The                  method involves extracting DNA and/or RNA from                  the biological sample. The method involves                  converting the RNA into cDNA. The method further                  involves providing a biological sample comprising                  granulocytes, extracting nucleic acid from                  biological sample, and analyzing nucleic acid to                  identify the presence of one or more clonal                  hematopoiesis associated mutations. The method                  involves converting the RNA to cDNA via reverse                  transcription. The method involves selecting a                  subject diagnosed with clonal hematopoiesis for                  further monitoring, or identifying subject                  diagnosed with clonal hematopoiesis as being at                  high risk of cardiovascular disease, heart                  failure, diabetes, autoimmune disease and/or                  myeloid blood cancers. The method involves                  identifying one or more clonal hematopoiesis                  associated mutations via droplet digital PCR,                  next generation sequencing, allele- specific                  polymerase chain reaction (PCR), high resolution                  melting curve analysis, genomic sequencing                  fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH),                  comparative genomic hybridization (CGH),                  restriction fragment length polymorphism (RELP),                  amplification refractory mutation system (ARMS),                  reverse transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR), real-time                  PCR, multiplex ligation-dependent probe                  amplification (MLPA), denaturing gradient gel                  electrophoresis (DGGE), single strand                  conformational polymorphism (SSCP), chemical                  cleavage of mismatch (CCM), protein truncation                  test (PTT), pyro- sequencing, HPLC or                  oligonucleotide ligation assay (OLA). The method                  involves identifying cancer associated nucleic                  acid fragment via droplet digital PCR, next                  generation sequencing, allele- specific PCR, high                  resolution melting curve analysis, genomic                  sequencing FISH, CGH, RELP, ARMS, RT-PCR,                  real-time PCR, MLPA, DGGE, SSCP, COM, PTT, or                  OLA, methylation analysis, and fragmentation                  pattern analysis. The method involves processing                  the biological sample to provide an isolated                  sample of thrombocytes. Preferred Sample: The                  biological sample is a blood sample. Preferred                  Component: The reagents are for parallel analysis                  of cDNA and gDNA comprising one or more clonal                  hematopoiesis or cancer associated mutations. The                  reagents are for detection of clonal                  hematopoiesis associated mutations in one or more                  of JACK2, CALR, MPL, CBL, KRAS, GNB1, DNMT3A,                  TET2, ASXL1, IDH2, SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1, PPM1D,                  and TP53.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details of detection or                prognosis of clonal hematopoiesis and cancer that                do not support the claims.

TI Method for determining compression modulus of            tumor in tissue of patient for detecting e.g. skin            cancer of patient, involves determining modulus at            location from displacement of cantilever and mapping            determined modulus of location of tumor.
AU SHIH W Y
   SHIH W
   MARKIDOU A
   SZWECZYK S T
   YEGINGIL H
AE UNIV DREXEL (UYDL-C)
GA 2014F17440
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves applying regular or                indentation compressive force to a location of a                substrate through a sensor including a cantilever                when the cantilever is in contact with the                substrate. Displacement of the cantilever is                detected due to the force. A compression modulus of                the substrate is determined at the location from                the displacement of the cantilever. The applying,                the detection, and the determination steps are                optionally repeated. The determined modulus of the                location of the substrate is mapped. Depth of a                target located at the location within the substrate                is determined.
   USE - Method for determining a Young's compression                modulus of a substrate or a target i.e. tumor in                tissue, of patients at a set of locations of the                substrate for detecting tissue-stiffness imaging,                cancer e.g. breast cancer, prostate cancer and skin                cancer (all claimed), and disease of the patients                by using a Piezoelectric Finger Sensor (PEFS) by a                physician.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables determining the compression                and shear modules of the tissues of the patients at                the set of locations of the tissues in an effective                and accurate manner with gentle touches to a                surface of the tissues by using the PEFS for                detecting the tissue-stiffness imaging, cancer, and                disease of the patients without the need of number                of unnecessary biopsies.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The target or the substrate is a tumor and                tissue surrounding the tumor. The cantilever is a                lead zirconate titanate/stainless steel cantilever.                An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a method                for determining a shear modulus of a substrate at a                set of locations of a substrate.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic perspective                view of two lead zirconate titanate/stainless steel                cantilevers provided with driving and sensing                electrodes on a top side of the cantilevers and a                bottom sensing lead zirconate titanate                layer.

AB    NOVELTY - The device has a mechanical arm movement                module for training the device to perform                high-precision mammary gland operation and                realizing flexible detection of the device to a                mammary gland such that an electronic skin sensor                attached to a finger of the device is accurately                located and identified to obtain mammary gland                related information. The electronic skin sensor                captures touch feedback of mammary tissue, detects                pressure stress and sliding friction force, and                converts the pressure stress and the sliding                friction force into analyzable touch data. A breast                cancer diagnosis module combines obtained touch                information and the mammary gland molybdenum target                image, extracts and fuses characteristics, and                realizes accurate diagnosis of mammary gland                cancer. A mechanical arm interaction module                understands and processes oral voice input of a                patient, converts the voice input into a                processable text form, and utters the voice input                to generate smooth sound for real-time reply to the                patient.
   USE - Mechanical arm device for facilitating                comprehensive diagnosis of breast cancer of                patient.
   ADVANTAGE - The device is efficient and accurate in breast                cancer diagnosis process, and provides quick                diagnosis service, and communicates with the                patient in a humanized manner, thus ensuring that                the patient feels comfortable and being relieved in                the whole process.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for the                mechanical arm device method.

TI Assessment of diagnosis of medically relevant            conditions from solubilized liquid based cytology (LBC)            samples, comprises detection of marker molecule in            medically relevant condition and comparing measured            value with control sample.
AU RIDDER R
