   MTM LAB AG (MTMM-Non-standard)
GA 2005198145
AB    NOVELTY - Assessment (M1) of diagnosis of medical                condition from solubilized liquid based cytology                (LBC) samples, comprising detection of the presence                or absence of a marker molecule for a medical                condition, and assessing diagnosis of the medically                relevant condition on the comparison between the                levels found in the LBC sample and those known to                be specific for healthy non-diseased body samples,                is new.
   USE - (M1) is useful for assessment of diagnosis of                medically relevant conditions, e.g. cell                proliferative disorder, cancer or a precursor                lesion. The cancer is cancer of the head and the                neck, cancer of the respiratory tract, cancer of                the gastrointestinal tract, cancer of the skin and                its appendages, cancer of the central and                peripheral nervous system, cancer of the urinary                system, cancer of the reproductive system,                anogenital cancer, cancer of the endocrine system,                cancer of the soft tissues and bone, or cancer of                the lymphopoietic and hematopoietic system. The                anogenital cancer is cervical cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - (M1) is cost effective, and enables rapid and                simple assessment of diagnosis of medically                relevant conditions.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Assessment (M1) of diagnosis of medically                relevant conditions from solubilized liquid based                cytology (LBC) samples, comprises detection of the                presence or absence and/or the level of a marker                molecule characteristic for a medically relevant                condition, comparing the presence or absence and/or                level of the marker molecule characteristic for a                medically relevant condition to the presence or                absence and/or the level known to be characteristic                for a healthy non-diseased body sample, and                assessing diagnosis of the medically relevant                condition on the comparison between the levels                found in the LBC sample and those known to be                specific for healthy non-disease body                samples.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                development of immunochemical kits and in-vitro                diagnostic devices for use in assessment of                diagnosis of medically relevant conditions from                solubilized body samples, where the kits and                in-vitro diagnostic devices are designed for the                detection of the presence or absence of marker                molecules characteristic for medically relevant                conditions on a protein or peptide level, and the                development is performed using LBC samples.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure is a graph representing the level                of p16INK4a in solubilized cervical cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: (M1) is performed on the                  basis of the feature chosen from the following:                  the marker molecule characteristic for medically                  relevant conditions is overexpressed in the cells                  contained in the LBC sample compared to a healthy                  non-diseased body sample, expression of the                  marker molecule characteristic for medically                  relevant conditions is lowered or lost in                  comparison to the expression present in a healthy                  non-diseased body sample, and a modified form of                  the marker molecule characteristic for a                  medically relevant condition is expressed in the                  cells present in the LBC sample compared to the                  marker molecule present in healthy non-diseased                  body samples. The marker molecules characteristic                  for medically relevant conditions are chosen from                  cell cycle regulatory proteins,                  metalloproteinases, transmembrane proteins,                  calcium binding proteins, growth factors, marker                  molecule characteristics for viral infections,                  cell proliferation markers, and markers                  associated with DNA replication, tumor marker                  protein, and the nucleic acid coding for the                  respective proteins. The tumor marker proteins                  are chosen from cyclin-dependent kinase                  inhibitors, p53, pRb, p14ARF, cyclin E, cyclin A,                  cyclin B, MN, her2/neu, mdm-2, bcl-2, claudin 1,                  endothelial growth factor (EGF)-receptor, MCM2,                  MCM3, MCM4, MCM5, MCM6, MCM7, complement                  dependent cytotoxicity (CDC)2, CDC6, CD7 protein                  kinase, CDC14 protein phosphatase, Dbf4,                  proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), Ki67,                  KiS1, Id1, osteopontine, CD46, GRP, renal                  dipeptidase, and transforming growth factor                  (TGF)betaII receptor. The cyclin-dependent kinase                  inhibitor is p16INK4a), p13.5, p14, p15INK4b),                  p18INK4c), p19INK4d), p21WAF1/CIP1) or p27KIP1).                  The marker molecules characteristic for viral                  infections is viral proteins. The viral protein                  is a HPV protein derived from a HPV gene chosen                  from HPV L1, HPV L2, HPV E1, HPV E2, HPV E4, HPV                  E5, HPV E6 and HPV E7. The detection of the                  marker molecule is performed using one or more                  probes specific for the molecules to be detected.                  The probe is detectably labeled with                  radioisotope, bioluminescent compound,                  chemiluminescent compound, electroluminescent                  compound, fluorescent compound, metal chelate,                  enzyme, or a biologically relevant binding                  structure. The probe is an antibody, an antibody                  fragment, miniantibody, or a peptidomimetic                  comprising an antigen binding epitope.
   EXAMPLE - To assess the diagnosis of cervical cancer,                cancer samples were mixed with UCM and PreservCyt                solutions and were centrifuged to obtain cell                pellet. The pellets were subjected to RNA                preparation procedure. The isolated RNA was                subjected to reverse transcriptase reaction to                obtain cDNA. cDNA was further subjected to RT-PCR                with forward and reverse primers of p16INK4a) and                p14ARF). As a control, beta-actin and GAPDH were                utilized. The result showed increased expression of                p16INK4a) and p14ARF) in cancer cell in comparison                to the control.

AB    NOVELTY - Human papilloma virus (HPV) DNAs comprising                7000-8000 by and their fragments are new, the DNAs                being derived from HPV 2d, 10b, 14a, 14b, 15, 17a,                17b, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 28, 29, 31, 32, IP2                and IP4.
The indicated HPV strains have been isolated                from lesions in patients with verruciform                epidermodysplasia, except for IP2 (cervical cancer)                and IP4 (precancerous skin lesions). Recombinant                DNAs, e.g. obtained by insertion of the indicated                DNAs into plasmids pBR322, pHV5 (Hind IIIB), pSP64,                pLI55 and pSP65, are also new.
   USE - The DNAs are useful as hybridisation probes                for detection of HPV in biological media. They                broaden the range of probes available (cf. J.                Virol, 43, 436 and 48, 340) and thus provide more                precise diagnostic tests.
   ADVANTAGE - The DNAs are useful as hybridisation probes                for detection of HPV in biological media. They                broaden the range of probes available (cf. J.                Virol, 43, 436 and 48, 340) and thus provide more                precise diagnostic tests.

PN WO2015196303-A1; US2017148618-A1; US10020178-B2
TI System for preparing e.g. prostate tissue sample            from human patient for detecting e.g. fatty acids for            treating prostate cancer of patient, has matrix            dispersion device physically separated from first and            second conductive substrates.
AU BORCHERS C H
   HAN J
   WANG X
AE UVIC IND PARTNERSHIPS INC (UVIC-Non-standard)
   UVIC IND PARTNERSHIPS INC (UVIC-Non-standard)
GA 201601182J
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a first conductive substrate                (100) associated with a biological sample (102). A                second conductive substrate (104) is positioned                parallel and opposite to the first conductive                substrate. The first and second conductive                substrates are separated by distance of 25 mm to 75                mm. A power source is electrically coupled to the                first and second conductive substrates for                establishing electric field between the first and                second conductive substrates. A matrix dispersion                device disperses matrix solution, and is physically                separated from the first and second conductive                substrates.
   USE - System for preparing a matrix-coate biological                sample e.g. prostate tissue sample, breast tissue                sample, lung tissue sample, skin tissue sample,                liver tissue sample and colon tissue sample, from a                human patient for analyzing matrix-assisted laser                desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (MALDI MS)                and detecting lipids e.g. fatty acids,                glycerolipids, glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids,                sterol lipids, prenol lipids, saccharolipids and                polyketides, proteins, nucleic acids,                apolipoprotein C-I, S100 A6, or S100 A8 (all                claimed) for treating cancer e.g. prostate cancer,                breast cancer, lung cancer, skin cancer, liver                cancer, colon cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, brain cancer and oral cancer, of the                patient. Can also be used for preparing blood,                plasma, serum, urine, bile, ascites, saliva,                cerebrospinal fluid, aqueous or vitreous humor or                bodily secretion obtained from an abscess or a site                of infection or inflammation, a joint e.g. normal                joint or joint affected by disease, a single celled                organism e.g. bacteria, yeast, protozoans and                amoebas, a multicellular organism e.g. plant and                animal.
   ADVANTAGE - The system prepares biological samples that                have improved characteristics for facilitating                detection, localization and identification of                biomarkers for disease. The system provides                finer-resolution distribution patterns in porcine                adrenal, so that image quality of lipids can be                significantly improved. The system facilitates                electric field-induced matrix droplet polarization                and subsequent on-tissue micro-extraction of                chargeable compounds of interest into matrix layers                so as to promote improved MALDI-MS detection and                imaging. The system can be cost effective, easily                installed and convenient for users, and does not                require expensive components and set-up.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The matrix dispersion device is a sprayer                (118). An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for preparing a sample for MALDI-MS                analysis.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of a                system for preparing a matrix-coated biological                sample.

TI Vision system for acquiring image of skin surface            of body of patient, has image sensor that is connected            to base over connection so that sensor is aligned with            respect to height of processing unit that is            electronically controlled.

AE FOTOFINDER SYSTEMS GMBH (FOTO-Non-standard)
GA 2013X37230
AB    NOVELTY - The vision system has an image sensor (3)                connected with a processing unit (2). The                processing unit is configured to acquire a group of                images by the image sensor, to analyze the group of                images, to form a record of personal data                associated with the skin of the body of the                patient, and to output the dermatological data                associated with the skin of the body. The image                sensor is connected to the base over a connection,                so that the image sensor is aligned with respect to                the height of processing unit that is                electronically controlled and electro-mechanically                aligned.
   USE - Vision system for acquiring image of skin                surface of body of patient for early detection of                skin diseases e.g. black skin cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The image of the skin surface of the human                body can be easily and quickly created for the                early detection of the skin diseases.

TI Harmful solar radiation detection device uses            colour change of sunlight-exposed fluorescent            composition to indicate exposure to harmful solar            radiation, and sunlight-exposed second fluorescent            composition as control.
AU PETCH D A
   KNJASCHEWITSCH S R
AE KNJASCHEWITSCH S R (KNJA-Individual)
   PETCH D A (PETC-Individual)
GA 1995051345
AB    NOVELTY - A harmful solar radiation detection apparatus                comprises a first fluorescent composition comprised                of a blend of a first and second fluorescent                materials. The first fluorescent material is                capable of absorbing radiation having a wavelength                less than 300 nm and capable of fluorescing at a                fluorescent wavelength above 300 nm upon absorption                of the radiation less than 300 nm.
The second fluorescent material is capable of                absorbing radiation at the first fluorescent                wavelength and capable of fluorescing at a second                fluorescent wavelength which is a visible                wavelength.
The first fluorescent composition and the                second fluorescent composition are capable of being                exposed to sunlight.
   USE - Detecting harmful solar radiation to reduce                risk of developing skin cancer. Durable and                reliable construction. Price is low so that device                can be made available to the buying public.
   ADVANTAGE - Detecting harmful solar radiation to reduce                risk of developing skin cancer. Durable and                reliable construction. Price is low so that device                can be made available to the buying public.

PN WO2010096464-A1; US2012052006-A1; US8968705-B2; US2015258034-A1; US10406111-B2
TI Gold or lanthanide nanoparticle, useful e.g. in            imaging tissue and to treat e.g. skin cancer and            cardiovascular diseases, comprises gold nanoparticle            and lanthanide containing metal organic framework            disposed on gold nanoparticle.
AU BOYES S G
   ROWE M D
AE ROWE M D (ROWE-Individual)
   COLORADO SCHOOL MINES (CRMN-C)
   BOYES S G (BOYE-Individual)
   ROWE M D (ROWE-Individual)
GA 2010K42824
AB    NOVELTY - Gold/lanthanide nanoparticle (A1), comprises a                gold nanoparticle and a lanthanide containing metal                organic framework disposed on the gold                nanoparticle.
   USE - The gold/lanthanide nanoparticles are useful:                in imaging tissue (claimed); as multimodal,                targeting, imaging, and/or therapeutic agents for                the diagnosis and in the treatment of specific                diseases including breast cancer, prostate cancer,                lung cancer, lymphomas, skin cancer, pancreatic                cancer, colon cancer, melanoma, ovarian cancer,                brain cancer, head and neck cancer, liver cancer,                bladder cancer, non-small lung cancer, cervical                carcinoma, leukemia, non-Hodgkins lymphoma,                multiple sclerosis, neuroblastoma and glioblastoma,                T and B cell mediated autoimmune diseases,                inflammatory diseases, infections,                hyperproliferative diseases, AIDS, degenerative                conditions, cardiovascular diseases and transplant                rejection; and in different drug delivery                applications including gene therapy, imaging                applications (vascular imaging), and in external                molecular detection devices including microarrays                and assays. No biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The gold/lanthanide nanoparticle provides a                diagnostic imaging, targetting, and therapy by                administrating a single nanodevice, thus reduces                patient anxiety and discomfort.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   gold/lanthanide nanoparticles conjugate (A2),                comprising: the gold nanoparticle; the lanthanide;                and a polymer, polymer precursor or initiator                grafted onto the lanthanide containing metal                organic framework;
   imaging tissue, comprising: administering the                nanoparticle conjugate to a patient; and exposing                the patient to NMR or computed X-ray tomography, or                exposing samples of the patient's tissue to optical                imaging; and
   making the nanoparticle conjugate, comprising:                either contacting substituted sulfur containing                compounds of formula (R 1 -S-[C(R 4 )(R 3 )] n (R 2                )) (I) or substituted dithiocarbonate compounds of                formula (R 7 -S-C(=S)SR 8 ) (II), with substituted                alkene compounds of formula (R 3 -C(=CH 2 )R 4 )                (III) to form substituted trithiocarbonate                compounds of formula (R 7 -S-C(=S)S-(C(R 3 )(R 4                )-CH 2 ) n R 2 ) (IV), and contacting (IV) with a                gold nanoparticle disposed to a gadolinium                containing metal organic framework to form the                gold/gadolinium nanoparticle conjugate; or                contacting (I) or dithiocarbonate compounds of                formula (R 5 -C(=S)S-R 6 ) (V) with (III) to form                substituted dithiocarbonate compounds of formula (R                5 -C(=S)S-(C(R 3 )(R 4 )CH 2 ) n R 2 ) (VI), and                contacting (VI) with a gold nanoparticle disposed                to a gadolinium containing metal organic framework                to form the gold/gadolinium nanoparticle                conjugate.
   R -R =alkyl, alkoxy, acyl, acylamino,                alkylamino, alkylsulfinyl, alkylsulfonyl,                alkylthio, alkoxycarbonyl, aryl, arylalkyl,                aryloxy, aryloxycarbonyl, carbamoyl, cycloalkyl,                cycloheteroalkyl, dialkylamino, heteroalkyl,                heteroaryl, heteroarylalkyl, heteroalkyloxy or                heteroaryloxy (all optionally substituted), H or                halo; and
   n=integer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - IMAGING AND COMMUNICATION - Preferred Method: The imaging technique is                  nuclear magnetic imaging, positron emission                  tomography, computed X-ray tomography, dark field                  confocal microscopy, light field confocal                  microscopy or optical imaging.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The lanthanide is                  gadolinium (preferred), lanthanum, erbium,                  ytterbium, neodymium, europium, terbium, cerium,                  thulium, praseodymium, promethium, samarium,                  dysprosium, holmium or lutetium. The                  gold/lanthanide nanoparticle is (I).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The additional                  functional group is carboxylic acids or its salt                  derivatives, acid halides, sulfonic acids or its                  salts, anhydride derivatives, hydroxyl                  derivatives, amine or amide derivatives, silane                  derivatives, phosphate derivatives, nitro                  derivatives, succinimide or sulfo-containing                  succinimide derivatives, halide derivatives,                  alkene derivatives, morpholine derivatives, cyano                  derivatives, epoxide derivatives, ester                  derivatives, carbazole derivatives, azide                  derivatives, alkyne derivatives, acid containing                  sugar derivatives, glycerol analogue derivatives,                  maleimide derivatives or protected                  acids/alcohols/acid halide derivatives.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Composition: (B1) further                  comprises: at least one additional functional                  group; an imaging agent covalently bonded to the                  polymer; a therapeutic agent covalently bonded to                  the polymer; and a targeting agent covalently                  bonded to the polymer. Preferred Method: The                  method further comprises the step of contacting a                  reducing agent to (I), before contacting the                  nanoparticle with (I).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Components: In (A2), the polymer,                  polymer precursor or the initiator is grafted                  onto the lanthanide containing metal organic                  framework by a covalent/non-covalent bond from a                  functional group including thiolates, thioethers,                  thioesters, carboxylates, amines, amides,                  halides, phosphonates, phosphonate esters,                  phosphinates, sulfonates, sulfates, porphyrins,                  nitrates, pyridine, pyridyl based compounds,                  nitrogen containing ligands, oxygen containing                  ligands or sulfur containing ligands. The imaging                  agent is a fluorescent monomer, which is                  poly(fluorescein-O-methacrylate).
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Neuroprotective;                Immunosuppressive; Antimicrobial; Anti-HIV;                Cardiovascular-Gen; Antiinflammatory.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of the gold/lanthanide                nanoparticle is intradermal, intramuscular,                intraperitoneal, intravenous, subcutaneous,                intranasal, epidural, oral, sublingual,                intracerebral, intravaginal, transdermal, rectal,                pulmonary, topical or inhalation. No dosage details                given.
   EXAMPLE - Gold nanoparticles were subsequently coated                with a gadolinium-based nanoscale metal organic                framework (NMOF). Coating of the gold nanoparticles                was carried out by a reverse microemulsion system,                which provides gadolinium-based NMOFs (comprised                aqueous solutions of gadolinium(III) chloride (0.5                M) and 1,4- benzenedicarboxylic acid (0.075 M)).                The gadolinium(III) chloride and 1,4-                benzenedicarboxylic acid aqueous solutions were                combined into a                heptane/hexanol/cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (0.0                5M) microemulsion, followed by addition of the gold                nanoparticles. The nanoparticle/gadolinium mixture                was then stirred vigorously for 24 hours. After 24                hours, the microemulsion mixture was centrifuged,                the supernatant was removed, and the nanoparticles                were subjected to three cycles of ethanol                wash/sonication/centrifugation. The supernatant was                collected and discarded. The gold/gadolinium                nanoparticles were then subjected to one last wash                in deionized water followed by centrifugation and                then storage in fresh deionized water.

TI New isolated polynucleotide encoding polypeptide            having lipid kinase activity, useful for e.g.            prognosis, treatment, detection and diagnosis of            cancer, including epithelial cancer e.g. breast cancer,            ovarian cancer and skin cancer.
AU ANDERSON R A
   SCHILL N J
AE WISCONSIN ALUMNI RES FOUND (WISC-C)
   WISCONSIN ALUMNI RES FOUND (WISC-C)
GA 2013L25139
AB    NOVELTY - An isolated polynucleotide encoding a                polypeptide having lipid kinase activity, is new.                The polynucleotide comprises a sequence chosen from                (a) a polynucleotide sequence encoding an amino                acid sequence having at least about 95% sequence                identity to a 707 amino acid sequence (SEQ ID NO:                4) fully defined in the specification, (b) a                polynucleotide sequence comprising a 2124 amino                acid sequence (SEQ ID NO: 2) fully defined in the                specification, and (c) a polynucleotide sequence                which is fully complementary to the polynucleotides                of (a) or (b).
   USE - The isolated polynucleotide or method is                useful for prognosis of cancer, identifying an                agent for cancer treatment (all claimed), and                detecting, diagnosing, monitoring and determining                cancer. The cancer is epithelial cancer including                breast cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer and                skin cancer, preferably breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The polynucleotide improves longevity of                breast cancer patients, and decreases harmful side                effects.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) expression vector comprising the                above-mentioned polynucleotide;
   (2) isolated host cell comprising the                expression vector;
   (3) method (M1) of producing a polypeptide                encoded by the polynucleotide, involves culturing a                cell under conditions suitable for expression of                the polypeptide, where the cell is transformed with                the polynucleotide, and the polynucleotide                comprises a promoter sequence operably linked to                the polynucleotide;
   (4) method (M2) for prognostic evaluation of a                patient, involves (a) detecting a nucleic acid                molecule comprising SEQ ID NO: 2 in a tissue sample                from a patient having, suspected of having, or at                risk of developing breast cancer, (b) comparing the                results of the step (a) with an amount of the same                sequence detected in a control sample, and (c)                evaluating the prognosis of the patient based on                the comparison of the step (b), where a lower                amount of the detected sequence compared to the                amount detected in the control sample indicates a                better prognosis, and an equal or higher amount of                the detected sequence compared to the amount                detected in the control sample indicates a poor                prognosis;
   (5) method (M3) for identifying an agent that                modulates the activity of phosphatidylinositol                phosphate kinase gamma 707, involves (a) contacting                the phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase gamma 707                with the agent in the presence of Lin11, Isl-1 and                Mec-3 (LIM)-domain only 4 (LMO4), and (b)                determining whether the agent modulates the                activity or localization of LMO4 as compared to a                control, where a change in the activity or                localization of LMO4 as compared to the control is                indicative of the agent modulating                phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase gamma 707                activity; and
   (6) kit comprising the nucleic acid.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The patient sample                  comprises a breast tissue sample. The detecting                  step in the method (M2) involves performing                  nucleic acid hybridization, and amplification of                  a nucleic acid molecule comprising SEQ ID NO: 2                  or its fragment by PCR. The PCR comprises use of                  oligonucleotide comprising at least 10 contiguous                  nucleotides of SEQ ID NO: 2 or nucleic acid                  complementary to at least 10 contiguous nucleic                  acids of SEQ ID NO: 2. The PCR comprises use of                  the oligonucleotide of SEQ ID NO: 13 and/or use                  of the oligonucleotide of SEQ ID NO: 14. The                  method (M2) further involves detecting a nucleic                  acid molecule encoding one or more breast cancer                  markers in the patient sample, where the marker                  is chosen from human epidermal growth factor                  receptor (HER)-1, HER-2 and their combinations.                  The method (M2) further involves (d) determining                  the amount of HER-2 nucleic acid present in the                  sample, (e) comparing the results of the step (d)                  with the amount of the HER-2 nucleic acid in a                  control sample, and (f) evaluating the prognosis                  of the patient based on the comparison in the                  steps (b) and (e), where a higher level of HER-2,                  and an equal or higher level of the detected                  sequence in the patient sample compared to the                  amounts detected in the control sample indicates                  a poor prognosis. atggagctggaggtaccgga (SEQ ID                  NO: 13), and ttacccaaagcccttctggaaa (SEQ ID NO:                  14).
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinase gamma                707 activity modulator; Lipid kinase activity                modulator; Sorting nexin-5 binding activity                modulator; beta -Catenin binding activity                modulator. No biological data given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI New isolated nucleic acid molecule that encodes melanocyte-specific protein useful as marker of melanocyte cell lineage, and for treating skin cancer, pigmentation and abnormal function.
AU DUNBAR P R
   HORLACHER O
   FEISST V J
AE AUCKLAND UNISERVICES LTD (UYAU-C)
GA 2010K90514
AB    NOVELTY - An isolated nucleic acid molecule that encodes a melanocyte-specific protein is new.
   USE - As a marker of a melanocyte cell lineage, for identifying melanocyte cell lineage, and in the diagnosis and/or detection of a skin cancer; in the treatment of disorders associated with melanoma and/or disorders of pigmentation (such as hypo-pigmentation and/or hyper-pigmentation), and/or abnormal function, localization or growth of melanocytes (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An isolated nucleic acid molecule that encodes a melanocyte-specific protein, comprising 546 base pair sequence as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its functional fragments, is new. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the following:
   (1) new nucleic acid molecule that is complementary to a nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its fragments;
   (2) new recombinant protein comprising a polypeptide sequence encoded by an isolated nucleic acid molecule comprising 342 base pair sequence as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO: 2) or (SEQ ID NO: 10);
   (3) a cell marker comprising a peptide or polypeptide sequence encoded by the isolated nucleic acid molecule or its part; or a peptide or polypeptide sequence comprising 108 base pair sequence as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO: 11);
   (4) new antibody that binds to the peptide or polypeptide sequence encoded by the nucleic acid molecule or its part, or to a protein comprising (SEQ ID NO: 11) or its part;
   (5) a vector comprising the nucleic acid sequence set or its part, operatively linked to a promoter;
   (6) a prokaryotic or eukaryotic cell comprising the expression vector;
   (7) method (M1) of diagnosing and/or treating a skin cancer;
   (8) method (M2) of screening for the presence of the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, in a sample;
   (9) method (M3) of screening for the presence of a peptide or polypeptide or its part, encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, in a sample;
   (10) method (M4) of screening for the presence of the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, and at least one other nucleic acid molecule which codes for a cell marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage in a sample;
   (11) method (M5) of screening for the presence of a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, and at least one other polypeptide which is a cell marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage in a sample;
   (12) method (M6) of diagnosing and/or detecting skin cancer or skin condition;
   (13) method (M7) of modulating expression of genes associated with skin cancer or skin condition;
   (14) method (M8) of modulating expression of genes associated with changes in skin pigmentation or cosmetic lightening or darkening of skin tone;
   (15) new nucleic acid molecule encoding a protein having (SEQ ID NO: 11), comprising 3' and 5' regulatory regions; and
   (16) new recombinant protein expressed in a prokaryotic or eukaryotic cell and having an amino acid sequence selected from sequence containing 113 amino acids as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO: 3) or (SEQ ID NO: 11).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The skin cell is a melanocyte. The prokaryotic cell is a bacterial cell or a fungal cell. The eukaryotic cell is selected from a mammalian cell, avian cell, amphibian cell, reptilian cell or insect cell. The biological sample is selected from a tissue biopsy, biological fluid or surgical specimen.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No general method for preparation of the isolated nucleic acid molecule that encodes melanocyte-specific protein is given. Preferred Compound: The nucleic acid molecule encodes a protein having 108 base pair sequence as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO: 11) or its functional fragment. The isolated nucleic acid molecule that encodes a melanocyte-specific protein, where the nucleic acid molecule has at least 75 (preferably 80-95)% sequence identity with (SEQ ID NO: 10). The antibody is a monoclonal antibody or its functional fragment. Preferred Components: The short interfering nucleic acid molecule is selected from short interfering RNA, double stranded RNA, micro RNA or short hairpin DNA. The inhibitory or interfering RNA is small interfering RNA (siRNA).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (M1) of diagnosing and/or treating a skin cancer involves administering to a subject an inhibitory or interfering RNA or DNA sense or antisense sequence capable of blocking or inhibiting expression of the nucleic acid molecule or its part, or an antibody that specifically binds to a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule or its part, or a protein comprising the peptide or polypeptide, or a protein having (SEQ ID NO: 11). The method (M2) of screening for the presence of the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, in a sample, involves: contacting a biological sample with a nucleic acid having a sequence that is complementary to nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part; and determining whether the nucleic acid binds to a nucleic acid molecule in the sample. The method (M3) of screening for the presence of a peptide or polypeptide or its part, encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, in a sample, involves: contacting a biological sample with an antibody that specifically binds to the peptide or polypeptide or its part; and determining whether the antibody binds to the peptide or polypeptide, or its part, in the sample. The method (M4) of screening for the presence of the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, and at least one other nucleic acid molecule which codes for a cell marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage in a sample, involves: contacting a biological sample with i) a nucleic acid molecule having a sequence that is complementary to nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part, and ii) a nucleic acid molecule having a sequence that is complementary to the other nucleic acid molecule or its part; and determining whether the nucleic acid molecules bind to the nucleic acid molecules in the sample. The method (M5) of screening for the presence of a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, and at least one other polypeptide which is a cell marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage in a sample, involves: contacting a biological sample with i) an antibody that specifically binds to a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant, and ii) an antibody that specifically binds to the at least one other polypeptide; and determining whether the antibodies bind to their corresponding polypeptides in the sample. The method (M6) of diagnosing and/or detecting skin cancer or skin condition involving: contacting a biological sample with a nucleic acid having a complementary sequence to nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part; or contacting a biological sample with an antibody that specifically binds to a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant; or contacting a biological sample with a nucleic acid having a complementary sequence to nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part, and at least one other nucleic acid complementary to a nucleic acid molecule encoding a marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage or its part; or contacting a biological sample with an antibody that specifically binds to a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, part or variant, and at least one other antibody that binds to a polypeptide that is a marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage or its part; or contacting a biological sample with a panel of nucleic acid molecules or their parts, encoding a marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage, and the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant; or contacting a biological sample with a panel of antibodies that bind specifically to a marker commonly used to identify cells of melanocyte lineage or its part, and a peptide or polypeptide encoded by the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant; and detecting localization of the nucleic acids or antibodies as an indicator of the presence (and/or type) of skin cancer or skin condition. The method (M7) of modulating expression of genes associated with skin cancer or skin condition involves: contacting a cell with a short interfering nucleic acid molecule directed against the nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part; or contacting the cells with an antisense nucleic acid molecule directed against the nucleic acid sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 10) or its part. The method (M8) of modulating expression of genes associated with changes in skin pigmentation or cosmetic lightening or darkening of skin tone involves: contacting a cell with an inhibitory or interfering RNA or DNA, sense or antisense, sequence directed against the nucleic acid molecule, its part or variant. The detection or diagnosis is performed in vivo or ex vivo. Preferred Components: The cell marker is a skin cell marker, or a marker for a skin-related neoplastic condition (preferably melanoma). The cell marker is selected from melanA, gp100, tyrosinase, trp-1 or trp-2.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Dermatological. No dosage details given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene therapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is oral or parenteral (including intravenous, intramuscular, intraperitoneal or subcutaneous), rectal, topical or by inhalation. No dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB       Monoclonal antibodies are produced by a                hybridoma obtd. by fusion between mouse spleen                cells immunised with human mucinous ovarian tumour                and mouse myeloma cells. The antibodies have the                following properties: (1) immunoglobulin class:                IgG1; (2) reaction mucinous ovarian tumour, cervix                uteri adenocarcinoma, gastric cancer, and colon                cancer; (3) no reaction with serious tumours, myoma                uteri, oesophagus cancer,lung cancer, breast                cancer, sarcoma, melanoma, carcinoid, neuroma, and                lymphoma; and (4) no reaction with normal tissues                of ovary, oviduct, endometrium, placenta,                oesophagus, liver, kidney, mammary gland, thyroid                gland, spleen, brain, and skin.
   USE/ADVANTAGE -   Monoclonal antibodies belonging to an IgG1                isotype and reacting specifically and strongly with                mucinous ovarian tumour. Used in detection of human                mucinous ovarian tumour.
   In an example, for immunisation, mucinous                ovarian tumour was inoculated 4 times into BALB/c                mouse, The float cells were obtd. from the mouse                spleen. 10 power 8 float cells and 2 x 10 power 7                mouse myeloma MOPC-21NS/1 cells were fused in 02.ml                PBS containing 42% (W/V) PEG and 15% (V/V) DMSO.                The fusion cells were screened in a HAT medium                (1.36 mg/dl hypoxanthine, 19.1 microg/dl                aminopterin, 387 microg/dl thymidine, 100 microg/dl                streptomycin, 100 units of penicillin, 2mM                glutamine and 10% foetal bovine serum). 3 clones                reacting specifically with ovarian tumour-related                antigens were obtd. from 3 fusion cells. 5 x 10                power 6 hybridoma cells were cultured under 5% CO2                in 15ml PRMI 1640 medium contg. 100 microg/ml                streptomycin, 100 U/ml penicillin, 3.8 g/l                glutamine, and 10% foetal bovine serum, and the                monoclonal antibodies were obtd. from the                culture.

TI Method for detection or analysis of biological            analyte such as nucleic acid molecules of human            suffering from lung cancer for use in gene therapy,            involves imaging substrate using detector comprising            multiple sensors during rotating to detect multiple            signals from multiple analytes.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves rotating a substrate about                a rotational axis, where the substrate comprises                multiple analytes, and the substrate is an open                substrate. The substrate is imaged using a detector                comprising multiple sensors during the rotating to                detect multiple signals from multiple analytes,                where an imaging field of view comprises a first                region and a second region which are placed at                different radial distances with respect to the                rotational axis, the sensors comprises multiple                segments, a first segment and a second segment of                multiple segments image the first region and the                second region, respectively, and are clocked                independently with respect to each other based on                different tangential velocities of the first region                and the second region, respectively, at the                different radial distances.
   USE - Method for detection or analysis of biological                analyte such as nucleic acid molecules (Claimed) of                human suffering from a disease for use in molecular                biology applications. Uses include but are not                limited to protein molecule, carbohydrate molecule,                single cell analyte, single cell, particle,                organism and colony from mammal or non-human mammal                such as a monkey, dog, cat, bird, or rodent, ape,                monkey, chimpanzee, reptilian, amphibian, avian, or                plant sources with a disease such as cancer e.g.                breast cancer, colorectal cancer, brain cancer,                leukemia, lung cancer, skin cancer, liver cancer,                pancreatic cancer, lymphoma, esophageal cancer or                cervical cancer or an infectious disease and a                genetic disorder such as achondroplasia, alpha-1                antitrypsin deficiency, antiphospholipid syndrome,                autism, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney                disease, Charcot-Marie-tooth, cri du chat, Crohn's                disease, cystic fibrosis and Dercum disease for use                in vector designs, gene therapy, vaccine design,                industrial strain design and verification.
   ADVANTAGE - The sample processing and analysis can be                performed with high efficiency. The time-intensive                and wasteful of valuable resources such as reagents                can be reduced.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a system                for analyte detection or analysis.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic bloick diagram                of a computer control system for detection or                analysis of biological analyte.

GA 2008B91622
AB    NOVELTY - Treatment of a disease associated with                gC1q/p32 receptor includes administering a                composition comprising                Cys-Gly-Asn-Lys-Arg-Thr-Arg-Gly-Cys.
   USE - For treating a disease associated with                gC1q/p32 receptor, e.g. cancer such as lymphoma,                mycosis fungoide, Hodgkin's Disease, myeloid                leukemia, bladder cancer, brain cancer, nervous                system cancer, head and neck cancer or carcinoma,                kidney cancer, lung cancer,                neuroblastoma/glioblastoma, ovarian cancer,                pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer, skin cancer,                liver cancer, melanoma, colon cancer, cervical                cancer or cervical carcinoma, breast cancer,                epithelial cancer, renal cancer, genitourinary                cancer, pulmonary cancer, esophagal carcinoma,                large bowel cancer, hematopoietic cancer,                testicular cancer, or rectal cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The composition modulates gC1q/p32 receptor                expression or activity, thus treating or preventing                a disease associated with gClq/p32 receptor.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   detection of the presence of gC1q/p32 receptor                by contacting a cell and a Lyp-1 composition                comprising a moiety linked to a composition                comprising Cys-Gly-Asn-Lys-Arg-Thr-Arg-Gly-Cys (SEQ                ID NO: 1), and detecting interaction between                gC1q/p32 receptor and Lyp-1 composition;
   detection of interaction between gC1q/p32                receptor and Lyp-1 composition;
   delivery of Lyp-1 composition to gC1q/p32                receptor;
   assessment of gC1q/p32 receptor level in a                cell of a subject by contacting a cell and a Lyp-1                composition, and detecting the level of Lyp-1                composition interaction with gC1q/p32                receptor;
   identification of a subject having a disease                associated with gC1q/p32 receptor, by contacting a                cell (e.g. cancerous cell) of subject and a Lyp-1                composition, and detecting interaction between                gC1q/p32 receptor and Lyp-1 composition to detect                the presence or level of gC1q/p32 which identifies                the subject as having a disease associated with                gC1q/p32 receptor; and
   creening a compound that interacts with                gC1q/p32 receptor, by reacting test compound, Lyp-1                composition and gC1q/p32 receptor, and detecting                unbound Lyp-1 composition, in which a given amount                of unbound Lyp-1 composition indicates a compound                that interacts with gC1q/p32 receptor.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The moiety may be                  polypeptide, nucleic acid molecule, or small                  molecule. The Lyp-1 composition may comprise                  virus or phage.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The moiety is                  detectable agent, preferably small molecule,                  fluorophore, fluorescein, rhodamine,                  radionuclide, indium-111, technetium-99,                  carbon-11, and/or carbon-13.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: The composition may                  comprise therapeutic moiety which targets                  DNA-associated process, diagnostic agent, or                  nanoparticle. The therapeutic moiety may be                  cytotoxic agent, alkylating agent, anti-tumor                  antibiotic, sequence-selective agent,                  anti-angiogenic agent, cyclophosphamide,                  melphalan, mitomycin C, bizelesin, cisplatin,                  doxorubicin, etoposide, mitoxantrone, SN-38,                  Et-743, actinomycin D, bleomycin, geldanamycin,                  chlorambucil, methotrexate, or TLK286.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition can be administered topically                (including ophthalmically, vaginally, rectally,                intranasally), orally, by inhalation, or                parenterally (e.g. by intravenous drip,                subcutaneous, intraperitoneal, or intramuscular                injection). No dosage details given.

TI Apparatus for performing endoscopic procedure for            detecting benign, malignant and glandular adipose            ex-vivo human breast tissues of patient, has detection            circuitry for detecting orthogonal function within            emissions from tissues.

GA 201561587K
AB    NOVELTY - The apparatus has a detection probe (912) for                detecting a cancerous tissue and including a first                fiber for emitting an UV light beam with an                orthogonal function and a second fiber for                receiving emissions from tissues responsive to the                UV light beam emitted for the first fiber. An UV                emission source generates the UV light beam. An                orthogonal function processing circuitry (920)                applies the orthogonal function to the UV light                beam. A detection circuitry detects a fluorescence                and orthogonal function within emissions from the                tissues received over the second fiber.
   USE - Apparatus for performing endoscopic procedure                for detecting cancerous tissue e.g. benign,                malignant and glandular adipose ex-vivo human                breast tissues, in patient-care areas of a patient                with breast cancer. Can also be used for skin                cancer, ovarian cancer, gynecological cancer,                choriocarcinoma, oral cavity, esophagus, lung,                gynecological tract and colon based cancers,                digestive cancers e.g. esophageal, stomach,                pancreas, liver, rectal and anal cancers, urinary                cancers e.g. kidney, bladder, testis and prostate                cancers, and tumors e.g. carcinoid, nasophayngeal,                retroperitoneal sarcomas and soft tissue                tumors.
   ADVANTAGE - The apparatus utilizes a fluorescence                spectroscopy with ductoscopy/endoscopy to target                tissue sampling during ductoscopy/endoscopy to                increase yield and reduce sampling errors. The                apparatus compares spectra from healthy mammary                ducts to samples taken with a microendoscope and                utilizes an algorithm to compare the spectra of                healthy ducts with spectra taken during                intervention procedure in real-time to identify                cancerous and pre-cancerous lesions. The apparatus                removes he degeneracy of a first order mode by                special fiber design, thus reducing mode coupling                and enabling OAM modes to propagate within the                fibers.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a method for detecting cancerous tissue using                endoscopic procedure
   a detection probe for performing endoscopic                procedure for detecting cancerous tissue.

AB    NOVELTY - As a serum markers of pathological state,                anti-bcl-2-associated athanogene 3 (anti-BAG3)                antibodies, are used.
   USE - As serum markers of pathological state, such                as heart disease (including angina pectoris,                preinfarction angina, myocardial infarction, heart                failure, ischemia, acute coronary disease, acute                heart failure, chronic heart failure and iatrogenic                heart disease), pancreatic cancer, bladder                carcinoma, inflammation and inflammatory related                diseases of the skin, nerves, bones, blood vessels                and connective tissues (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - Use of anti-BAG3 antibodies as serum markers                of pathological state provides rapid and                non-invasive technique for diagnostic, early                diagnosis and prognostic purposes, risk                stratification; and more efficiently predicts risk                of complications or monitors effects of therapies.                The method detects significant differences between                anti-BAG3 antibodies and/or BAG3/antibodies                complexes between healthy individuals and patients                affected by BAG3-involving pathologies. The                proposed assay method allows statistically                significant separation of the group of cardiac                patients from the group of healthy people.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) detecting (M1) presence of an anti-BAG3                antibody or an anti-BAG3 antibody bound to soluble                BAG3 to form an immune complex in biological sample                involving obtaining biological sample consisting of                serum or plasma and determining presence of                anti-BAG3 or BAG3 associated antibodies in the                biological sample;
   (2) enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)                kit (K1) for detection of anti-BAG3 antibodies or                anti-BAG3 antibodies bound to soluble BAG3 to form                an immune complexes in a biological sample,                comprising BAG3 recombinant protein or BAG3-                specific mouse monoclonal antibodies AC-1, AC-2,                AC-3, AC-4 and AC-5 for capturing soluble BAG3 and                antibodies able to recognize human                immunoglobulins;
   (3) immunohistochemistry kit (K2) for                detection of BAG3 protein in biological sample,                comprising BAG3-specific antibodies and reagents                including probes needed for the staining; and
   (4) kit (K3) for detection of BAG3 gene                expression in biological sample comprising a set of                amplification primers.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Antibodies: The anti-BAG3                  antibodies are bound to soluble BAG3 to form                  immune complexes. Preferred Method: The method                  (M1) additionally involves comparing values                  obtained from the biological sample with                  reference values or with the values obtained from                  healthy donors. The determination step is                  performed by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay                  (ELISA) test. The presence of anti-BAG3 antibody                  or immune complex is associated with pathological                  condition. Preferred Kit: In the kit (K1),                  biological sample is serum or plasma sample. In                  the kit (K3), the amplification primers are                  suitable for detection by quantitative real-time                  RT-PCR, where biological sample is a tissue                  sample.

TI Hand-held device for capturing images of skin            portions for detection of skin lesions, has memory for            storing captured digital image characterized by tank            for storing set of portions of contact gel and            liquid.
AU HELD P
AE DERMOSAFE SA (DERM-Non-standard)
GA 2013Q08887
AB    NOVELTY - The device (20) has an image sensor for                capturing an image. A lens is arranged for                projecting a focused image of the skin on a sensor                when the device is in direct contact with the skin.                A memory stores the captured digital image                characterized by a tank (22) for storing a set of                portions of contact gel and liquid. A contact glass                (2) comprises a canal and a groove for contact gel                or liquid. The tank comprises a lever that actuates                mechanically the tank such that a portion of                contact gel and liquid that is distributed as                required for taking a dermatoscopy image.
   USE - Hand-held device for capturing images of skin                portions for detection of skin lesions and skin                cancer i.e. melanomas for dermatoscopy                analysis.
   ADVANTAGE - The device improves detection of skin lesions                and melanomas. The device provides a distribution                nozzle able to spread on the skin in order to                control the flow and quantity of contact gel and                liquid that is to spread, so that multiple nozzle                of the same type or combination of various types                can be employed to improve the spreading efficiency                and regularity. The device provides a new simple                type of dermatoscopy device that can be used at                home and provide better quality.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                system for capturing and analyzing images of skin                portions.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of a                hand-held device with contact gel and liquid                tank.

TI Human anticancer monoclonal antibodies - obtd. from hybridomas formed from lymph node cells from breast cancer patient and human cell line.
AU KJELDSEN T B
   ZEUTHEN J
AE NOVO IND AS (NOVO-C)
GA 1988229099
AB       Novel human anticancer monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) are synthesised by hybridoma cell lines produced by fusing human lymph node cells from regional axillary lymph nodes from a patient with carcinoma of the breast and a human cell line that is drug or temp. sensitive. Pref. the human cell line is a myeloma-lymphoblastoid hybrid cell line, e.g. KR-12.
   USE/ADVANTAGE -   The MAbs selectively react with non-haematopoietic human cancers, partic. tumours of the breast and testes and to a lesser deg. with tumours of the skin, bladder and colon. The MAbs may inhibit the growth of a wide variety of tumour cell types. They may also be used for detection by e.g. radioimmunoimaging.

PN CN117953207-A
TI Method for segmenting image based on local            isotropic principle for skin lesion segmentation in            skin cancer detection and treatment, involves            distinguishing and classifying each pixel point in            characteristic image by point-by-point convolution and            normalization exponential function.
AU ZENG W
   ZHANG Z
   JIN X
AE NINGBO DIGITAL TWIN EIAS RES INST (NING-Non-standard)
GA 202453805J
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves dividing (S1) the target                image into image blocks with consistent sizes. The                weak correlation association between adjacent image                blocks is performed. The deep semantic features are                extracted (S2) from the associated image blocks                through an isotropic full convolution module. The                deep semantic feature representation is calibrated                (S3). The enhanced feature representation is                upsampled (S4) by a separable transpose convolution                module. The higher-layer semantic features are                extracted (S5) from the supplemented feature images                through isotropic full convolution modules with                different parameters. Judgment (S6) is made to                check whether the respective rates of the feature                images are restored to be consistent with the                target image. The differential classification is                performed (S7) on each pixel point in the feature                map through point-by-point convolution and                normalized index function. The differential                identification is performed.
   USE - Method for segmenting image based on local                isotropic principle for skin lesion segmentation in                skin cancer detection and treatment.
   ADVANTAGE - The method reduces the information loss,                reduces the parameter demand and improves the model                generalization ability through the separable                transposition convolution and the space image                residual error.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for an image                segmentation system based on local isotropy                principle.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow diagram illustrating                an image segmentation method based on local                isotropic principle. (Drawing includes non-English                language text)
   S1Step for dividing the target image into                image blocks with consistent sizes
   S2Step for extracting deep semantic features                from the associated image blocks through an                isotropic full convolution module
   S3Step for calibrating the deep semantic                feature representation through an efficient channel                attention mechanism
   S4Step for upsampling the enhanced feature                representation by a separable transpose convolution                module
   S5Step for extracting higher-layer semantic                features from the supplemented feature images                through isotropic full convolution modules with                different parameters
   S6Step for judging whether the respective                rates of the feature images are restored to be                consistent with the target image
   S7Step for performing differential                classification on each pixel point in the feature                map through point-by-point convolution and                normalized index function

PN WO9741441-A1; AU9726819-A; EP900381-A1; JP2000510949-W; AU200161878-A; EP1418434-A2; AU775537-B2; JP2006311860-A; EP2060917-A2; EP2060917-A3; CA2252648-C; EP2060917-B1; EP2060917-B9; EP1418434-A3
TI Detection of enzymes in biological samples,            particularly urine used for diagnosis and prognosis of            tissue remodelling-associated conditions, e.g. cancer            and prostate disorders.
AU MOSES M A
   FREEMAN M R
   WIEDERSCHAIN D
AE CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
   CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
   CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
   CHILDRENS MEDICAL CENT (CHLD-C)
GA 1998032188
AB       A non-invasive method for facilitating the                diagnosis of a subject for a tissue                remodelling-associated condition (TRAC) comprises:                (a) obtaining a urine sample from a subject; and                (b) detecting an enzyme in the urine sample,                thereby facilitating the diagnosis of the subject                for the TRAC. Also claimed is a kit for                facilitating the diagnosis and prognosis of a TRAC,                comprising: (a) a container having a reagent for                detecting an enzyme in a urine sample, and (b)                instructions for using the reagent for detecting                the enzyme for facilitating the diagnosis and                prognosis of a TRAC.
   The enzyme is involved in a pathway of tissue                remodelling or reshaping or is a matrix-digesting                enzyme, preferably proteases, especially serin                protease, proenzyme or matrix metalloproteinase                (MMP) such as gelatinase A or B. When prognosing                prostate cancer, the protease is a type IV                collagenase having molecular weight 82-92                (preferably 72) kDa. The method for prognosis of                metastatic prostate cancer further comprise removal                of low molecular weight contaminants from the urine                prior to the electrophoretic detection giving a                zymogram. The zymogram substrate is gelatin,                casein, fibronectin, plasmin, plasminogen, type IV                collagen or its derivative. The enzyme is detected                immunochemically by a radio-immune assay or                ELISA.
   USE -   The methods can be used for the diagnosis and                prognosis of TRACs such as arthritic conditions,                obstructive disorders, degenerative disorders,                problematic wound-healing, ulcerative disorders or                cancer, especially organ-confined prostate or                metastatic cancer. It can also be cancer of                epithelial cells, especially cancer of nervous                system, breast, retina, lung, skin, kidney, liver,                pancreas, genito-urinary tract and gastrointestinal                tract.

AU XU K
   CHU Y
   YE X
   CHEN X
AE UNIV HANGZHOU DIANZI (UYHH-C)
GA 201953150V
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves utilizing a normal breast                cell tissue data as background area data to                establish a database, where the breast cell tissue                includes skin and fat tissue. A detected area is                discretized according to a position of an emitting                device and a receiving device. Singular value                decomposition is performed. A possibility                determining part of a source of a lesion part is                determined. An angular frequency of an                electromagnetic wave is calculated. TI Determining suitability of subject to treated with            microtubule targeting agent, comprises receiving sample            from subject, measuring SETDB 1 expression and            determining suitability based on SETDB 1            expression.
AU GERLITZ G
AE ARIEL SCI INNOVATIONS LTD (ARIL-C)
GA 2022981889
AB    NOVELTY - Determining (M1) suitability of a subject to                be treated with a microtubule targeting agent                (MTA), comprises receiving a sample from the                subject, measuring SETDB 1 expression in the sample                and determining suitability based on the SETDB 1                expression, thus determining suitability of a                subject to be treated with an MTA.
   USE - The method is useful: for determining                suitability of subject to be treated with a                microtubule targeting agent, where the subject                suffers from a disease, disorder or condition                treatable by an MTA, where the disease is a                proliferative disease, where the proliferative                disease is cancer, where the cancer is treatable                with MTAs or is known to over express SETDB 1,                where the cancer comprises brain, skin, breast,                lung, renal, liver, pancreatic, head and neck,                hematopoietic, endometrial, bladder, sarcoma,                glioma, colorectal, gastric, prostate, ovarian,                testicular, and cervical cancer; and for treating a                subject suffering from a cancer characterized by                increased SETDB 1 expression (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - None given.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   treating (M2) a subject suffering from a                cancer characterized by increased SETDB 1                expression, comprising reducing microtubule                stability in the cancer, thus treating the                subject;
   treating (M3) a subject suffering from a                cancer characterized by decreased or healthy SETDB1                expression, comprising increasing microtubule                stability in the cancer, thus treating the                subject;
   a kit (K1) comprising a. a microtubule                targeting agent (MTA), and b. an agent for specific                detection of SETDB 1 expression; and
   a kit (K2) comprising an agent for specific                detection of SETDB 1 for use in a method of                determining suitability of a subject to be treated                by a microtubule targeting agent (MTA).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The predetermined                  threshold is an expression level in a healthy                  control. The sample is a tumor sample, comprises                  tumor cells or comprises cell free DNA from a                  tumor cell. The expression is mRNA expression or                  protein expression. The SETDB 1 expression is                  cytoplasmic SETDB 1 expression. The method is an                  in vitro method. The method (M1) further                  comprises administering the MTA to a suitable                  subject. The MTA is a microtubule destabilizing                  agent and further comprising enhancing HDAC6                  expression, function or both in the suitable                  subject. The MTA is a microtubule stabilizing                  agent and further comprising decreasing HDAC6                  expression, function or both in the suitable                  subject. The HDAC6 expression or function is                  within a cancer cell. The method (M2) where the                  reducing comprises administering an MTA that                  destabilizes microtubules. The reducing comprises                  increasing HDAC6 expression, function or both in                  the cancer. The method (M3) further comprising                  measuring SETDB1 expression in the cancer.                  Preferred Components: The MTA is a microtubule                  (MT) stabilizing agent and where expression of                  SETDB 1 above a predetermined threshold indicates                  the subject is unsuitable for treatment with the                  MTA. The MTA is an MT stabilizing agent and where                  expression of SETDB 1 at or below a predetermined                  threshold indicates the subject is suitable for                  treatment with the MTA. The MT stabilizing agent                  is selected from plantbased MT stabilizing agent,                  a bacterial MT stabilizing agent and a small                  molecule stabilizing agent. The MT stabilizing                  agent comprises a e.g. taxane, a taccalonalide,                  an epothilone, ceratamine A, ceratamine B,                  FR182877, dictyostatin. The taxane comprises                  paclitaxel, paclitaxel C, docetaxel, abraxane,                  cabazitaxel, larotaxel tesetaxel, TPI-287,                  10-deacetylbaccatin III, baccatin III, and                  7-epipaclitaxe and its derivatives. The                  taccalonalide comprises taccalonalide A, B, E,                  H2, I, J, N, R, T, Z, AA, AB, AC, AD, AF, AJ, AK,                  AL, AM, AN and AO. The epothilone comprises                  epothilone A, epothilone B, epothilone C,                  epothilone D, epothilone E, ixabepilone,                  sagopilone, patupilone, BMS-310705, KOS-1584 and                  BMS-753493. The MT stabilizing agent is an HDAC6                  inhibitor. The MTA is an MT destabilizing agent                  and where expression of SETDB1 above a                  predetermined threshold indicates the subject is                  suitable for treatment with the MTA. The MTA is                  an MT destabilizing agent and where expression of                  SETDB1 at or below a predetermined threshold                  indicates the subject is unsuitable for treatment                  with the MTA. The MT destabilizing agent                  comprises plant-based MT destabilizing agent, a                  bacterial MT destabilizing agent and a small                  molecule destabilizing agent. The MT                  destabilizing agent comprises a vinca alkaloid,                  maytansine, disorazole Z, a lactone, circumin,                  colchicine, combretastatin, TH588, chaicone,                  podophyllotoxin, indibulin, is                  2-methoxyestradiol, pironetin, noscapinoid,                  noscapine, 9-bromonoscapine, quercetin and its                  derivatives. The lactone comprises plocabulin                  (PM060184), emtansine, rhizoxin, and                  spongistatin. The derivative of combretastatin                  comprises combretastatin A-1, combretastatin A-4,                  fosbretabulin, Oxi4503, combretastatin                  4-O-phosphate (CA-4P), ombrabulin. The MT                  destabilizing agent is HDAC6 or its functional                  fragment.

TI Detection of a mutation associated with squamous            cell carcinoma comprises detecting a point mutation at            nucleotide 148 of the connexin 26 gene.
AU VAN STEENSEL M A M
   VAN GEEL M
AE MULTIGEN HOLDING SA (MULT-Non-standard)
GA 2003633996
AB    NOVELTY - Detection of a mutation associated with                squamous cell carcinoma comprises detecting that                nucleotide 148 of the connexin 26 gene is other                than G.
   USE - For detecting a mutation associated with                squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), this mutation being                correlated with a strongly increased risk for                SCC-type skin cancer (no data given).
   ADVANTAGE - The method is rapid and reliable.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The mutation is detected                  either by:amplifying the connexin 26 gene and                  either:equencing part of the gene including                  nucleotide 148;using an oligonucleotide probe capable of                  hybridizing to a nucleotide sequence including                  nucleotide 148, but not if nucleotide 148 is G;                  ortreating the gene with a restriction                  endonuclease capable of cutting the gene when                  nucleotide 148 is A, especially AspI;expressing the connexin 26 gene and                  analyzing the resulting mRNA; ordetecting the mutation at the protein level,                  especially by:equencing at least part of the connexin 26                  protein including the amino acid encoded by codon                  50; orusing an antibody capable of binding to a                  portion of connexin 26 including the amino acid                  encoded by codon 50 when this amino acid is not                  aspartic acid.

TI Diagnosing oral cancer with digital photograph using system involves capturing video and image of internal portion of mouth from mobile or any other digital camera and uploading these digital photographs on system.
AU KAKADIA P R
AE KAKADIA P R (KAKA-Individual)
GA 2021426592
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing oral cancer with digital photograph using system involves capturing a video and image of the internal portion of mouth from the mobile or any other digital camera; uploading these digital photographs on a system, which are installed with the Machine Learning (ML) algorithms; uploading image processed using installed library and identify different colors from the image photographs and compare the photographs with the database index which cause probability of oral cancer, after color detection these libraries detect an area in the image of the skin surface for the damage by cancer diseases as finding more damaged areas which generate a report with probability.
   USE - Method for diagnosing oral cancer with digital photograph using system.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is carried out in a simple and cost-effective manner at earlier stage in medical field with the help of digital photography.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Conditions: The ML algorithms have multiple features to analyze the photos by NumPay and OpenCV libraries for numerical processing. The probability report is generated on mobile applications and the web application in digital format.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.
