TI Use of an inhibitor of kappa light polypeptide            gene enhancer in B-cells, kinase epsilon (IKK epsilon)            or a nucleic acid encoding IKK epsilon for diagnosing            or treating diseases such as ischemia, diabetic ulcers,            wounds or cancer.
AU KORHERR C
AE XANTOS BIOMEDICINE AG (XANT-Non-standard)
GA 2005296209
AB    NOVELTY - An inhibitor of kappa light polypeptide gene                enhancer in B-cells, kinaseepsilon (IKKepsilon);                its derivative; its encoding nucleic acid; or means                for their detection, is used for preparing a                pharmaceutical composition or a diagnostic agent                for treating or diagnosing diseases or disorders                such as ischemic or dental diseases, smoker's leg,                diabetic ulcers, wound healing disorders, cancer or                inflammation.
   USE - The composition (including the IKKepsilon, its                functional derivative, nucleic acid encoding                IKKepsilon, and/or means for the detection of the                molecules) are useful for preparing a diagnostic                agent for the diagnosis of ischemic or dental                diseases, smoker's leg and diabetic ulcers, wound                healing disorders, cancer, hyperplasia, tumor                progression, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis,                atherosclerosis, retinopathy, osteoarthritis,                endometriosis or chronic inflammation. The nucleic                acid encoding IKKepsilon may also be used for                preparing a pharmaceutical composition for the                treatment of ischemic or dental diseases, smoker's                leg and diabetic ulcers or for the stimulation of                wound healing. The IKKepsilon inhibitor is also                used for preparing a pharmaceutical composition for                the treatment of hyperplasia, rheumatoid arthritis,                psoriasis, atherosclerosis, retinopathy,                osteoarthritis, endometriosis, chronic                inflammation, or preferably cancer, such as brain                cancer, pancreatic carcinoma, stomach cancer, colon                carcinoma, skin cancer, especially melanoma, bone                cancer, kidney carcinoma, liver cancer, lung                carcinoma, ovarian cancer, breast carcinoma,                uterine carcinoma, prostate cancer or testis                carcinoma (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - AN INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for the                method of identifying an anti-cancer drug,                comprising contacting a potential IKKepsilon                interactor with IKKepsilon or its functional                derivative, determining the binding of the                potential interactor to IKKepsilon or its                functional derivative, and determining the                anti-angiogenic capacity of the potential                interactor.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Nucleic Acid: The nucleic acid                  induces the production of pro-angiogenic factors                  and the formation of vascular vessels. Preferred                  Inhibitor: The inhibitor inhibits the production                  of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and                  inhibits the formation of vascular vessels. The                  inhibitor is selected from antisense                  oligonucleotides, antisense RNA, siRNA, aptamers                  and low molecular weight molecules (LMWs). The                  LMWs bind to the ATP-binding site of the kinase                  domain of IKKepsilon.Preferred Method: In identifying an                  anti-cancer drug, the anti-angiogenic capacity is                  determined by measuring the inhibition of VEGF                  production. The potential interactor is provided                  in the form of a chemical compound library. The                  chemical compound library consists of a group of                  molecules or substances that bind to the ATP                  binding site of the kinase domain of IKKepsilon.                  The method is carried out on an array.
   WIDER DISCLOSURE - Also disclosed is a method for treating a                patient in need of such treatment.
   ACTIVITY - Vasotropic; Antiulcer; Dermatological;                Vulnerary; Cytostatic; Antiarthritic;                Antirheumatic; Antipsoriatic; Antiarteriosclerotic;                Ophthalmological; Osteopathic; Gynecological;                Antiinflammatory.
   No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration can be intravenous, dermal,                intradermal, intracutaneous, percutaneous,                subcutaneous, topical or transdermal. No dosage                given.
   EXAMPLE - No relevant example given.

               determining whether a subject has a higher survival                rate after receiving a treatment for a disease (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method uses ctDNA, which is a                non-invasive, tumor-specific biomarker for routine                clinical use, is derived from tumor cells                predominately undergoing cell-death and released                into circulation of various bodily fluids including                blood, provides non-invasive access to the tumor's                molecular landscape and disease burden; detects                ctDNA with increased sensitivity preferably in                subjects with lower abundance of ctDNA; determines                likelihood of a subject having cancer with high                sensitivity and/or high specificity; is inexpensive                and time saving; and enables sensitive ctDNA                detection in early stage of cancers.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   determining (M2) whether a subject has or is                at risk of having a disease;
   processing (M3) a cell-free nucleic acid                sample of a subject to determine whether the                subject has or is at risk of having a                disease;
   determining (M4) whether a subject has or is                at risk of having a condition;
   determining (M5) whether a subject has a                higher survival rate after receiving a treatment                for a disease;
   a system (R1) for determining whether a                subject has or is at risk of having a disease;                and

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method M2 comprises                  (a) subjecting multiple nucleic acid molecules                  derived from a cell-free nucleic acid sample                  obtained from the subject to sequencing to                  generate at least one profile consisting of (i) a                  methylation profile, (ii) a mutation profile, and                  (iii) a fragment length profile, and (b)                  processing at least one profile to determine                  whether the subject has or is at risk of the                  disease at a sensitivity of at least 80% or at a                  specificity of at least about 90%, where the                  cell-free nucleic acid sample comprises less than                  30 ng/ml of the nucleic acid molecules. The                  method M3 comprises (a) providing the cell-free                  nucleic acid sample comprising multiple nucleic                  acid molecules, (b) subjecting the nucleic acid                  molecules or its derivatives to sequencing to                  generate multiple sequencing reads, (c) computer                  processing the sequencing reads to identify the                  nucleic acid molecules, (i) a methylation                  profile, (ii) a mutation profile, and (iii) a                  fragment length profile, and (d) using at least                  the methylation profile, the mutation profile and                  the fragment length profile to determine whether                  the subject has or is at risk of having the                  disease. The method M4 comprises (a) assaying a                  cell-free nucleic acid molecule from at least a                  portion of a sample from the subject, (b)                  detecting a methylation level of at least a                  portion of the cell-free nucleic acid molecule                  comprised in DMR listed in Table 5 of the                  specification, and (c) comparing, using at least                  one computer processor, where the methylation                  level detected in the step (b) to a methylation                  level of corresponding portion(s) of the                  cell-free nucleic acid molecules comprised in the                  DMR listed in Table 5. The method M5 comprises                  (a) assaying a cell-free nucleic acid molecule                  from at least a portion of a sample from the                  subject, (b) detecting a methylation level of at                  least a portion of the cell-free nucleic acid                  molecule comprised in DMR listed in Table 6 of                  the specification, and (c) processing, using at                  least one computer processor, where the                  methylation level is detected in the step (b) to                  a methylation level of corresponding portion(s)                  of the cell-free nucleic acid molecules comprised                  in the DMR listed in Table 6 of the                  specification. The system R1 comprises at least                  one computer processors that are individually or                  collectively programmed to implement a process                  comprising subjecting multiple nucleic acid                  molecules derived from a cell-free nucleic acid                  sample obtained from the subject to sequencing to                  generate at least one profile of (i) a                  methylation profile, (ii) a mutation profile, and                  (iii) a fragment length profile and processing                  the profile to determine whether the subject has                  or is at risk of the disease at a sensitivity of                  at least 80% or at a specificity of at least                  about 90%, where the cell-free nucleic acid                  sample comprises less than 30 ng/ml of the                  nucleic acid molecules. The system R2 comprises                  at least one computer processors that are                  individually or collectively programmed to                  implement a process comprising: (a) providing the                  cell-free nucleic acid sample comprising multiple                  nucleic acid molecules, (b) subjecting the                  nucleic acid molecules or its derivatives to                  sequencing to generate multiple sequencing reads,                  (c) computer processing the sequencing reads to                  identify nucleic acid molecules, (i) a                  methylation profile, (ii) a mutation profile, and                  (iii) a fragment length profile, and (d) using at                  least the methylation profile, the mutation                  profile and the fragment length profile to                  determine whether the subject has or is at risk                  of having the disease. The method M1 further                  comprises: adding a first amount of filler DNA to                  the sample, where at least a portion of the                  filler DNA is methylated, then further optionally                  denaturing the sample. The step (f) in M1                  comprises using a statistical classifier, where                  the classifier is machine learning-derived. The                  step (d) in M1 comprises immunoprecipitating the                  cell-free methylated DNA using an antibody; and                  adding at least 0.05 &#956; g preferably at                  least 0.16 &#956; g antibody to the sample                  for immunoprecipitation. The method M3 further                  comprises: adding a second amount of control DNA                  to the sample after the step (c) for confirming                  the immunoprecipitation reaction; comprising                  adding a second amount of control DNA to the                  sample after the step (c) for confirming the                  capture of cell-free methylated DNA; mixing the                  cell free nucleic acid sample with filler DNA                  molecules to yield a DNA mixture; incubating the                  DNA mixture with a binder that is configured to                  bind methylated nucleotides to generate an                  enriched sample; detecting an origin of cancer                  tissue; generating a report comprising a                  prognosis of the subject's survival rate;                  providing a treatment to the subject; and                  providing a second report indicating whether the                  treatment is effective subsequent to treatment of                  the disease. The process of identifying the                  presence of DNA from cancer cells further                  includes identifying the cancer cell tissue of                  origin by identifying a cancer subtype, where the                  cancer subtype differentiates the cancer based on                  stage, histology, gene expression pattern, copy                  number aberration, rearrangement, or point                  mutational status. In the method M1, the step (f)                  is: carried out genome-wide; is restricted from                  genome-wide to specific regulatory regions, where                  the regulatory regions are functional annotation                  of the mammalian genome 5 (FANTOM5) enhancers,                  CpG Islands, CpG shores and/or CpG Shelves. The                  steps (f) and (g) are carried out by a computer                  processor. The sequencing does not comprise                  bisulfite sequencing. The method M4 comprises:                  performing the sequence analysis, where the                  sequencing analysis comprises a cell-free                  methylated DNA immunoprecipitation (cfMeDIP)                  sequencing; detection by measuring methylation                  level of at least a portion of the nucleic acid                  molecule comprised in: at least 6-100 DMRs listed                  in Table 5 of the specification. The method M5                  comprises detecting by providing a composite                  methylation score (CMS) which is a sum of                  &#946; -values of DMRs listed in Table 6 of                  the specification, where a higher CMS indicates                  an inferior survival for the subject and CMS is                  not dependent on an abundance of ctDNA. Preferred                  Components: The fragment length metric is                  fragment length, preferably the fragment length                  distribution of the subject cell-free methylated                  DNA. The subject cell-free methylated DNA is:                  limited to fragments having a length of less than                  170 base pairs (bp), preferably less than 100 bp;                  limited to fragments having a length of 100-150                  bp, preferably 120-130 bp; limited to fragments                  within the bottom 50th, preferably 10th                  percentile based on length; further limited to                  fragments within differentially methylated region                  (DMR)s; further limited during the capturing; and                  further limited is during the comparing. The                  limiting is during the identifying process. The                  sample is from the subject's blood or plasma. The                  control cell-free methylated DNAs sequences: from                  healthy and cancerous individuals are comprised                  in a database of DMRs between healthy and                  cancerous individuals, and limited to those                  control cell-free methylated DNA sequences which                  are differentially methylated as between healthy                  and cancerous individuals in DNA derived from                  cell-free DNA; and are differentially methylated                  as between healthy and cancerous individuals in                  DNA derived from blood plasma. The sample has                  less than 100 ng, 75 ng, or 50 ng of cell-free                  DNA. The first amount of filler DNA comprises                  5-100% methylated filler DNA with remainder being                  unmethylated filler DNA, preferably 15-30%                  methylated filler DNA. TI Detecting methylation status of nucleic acid            comprises treating nucleic acid with methylation            restriction enzymes, performing PCR reaction on            amplification product, and determining presence or            absence of product and, if present, determining that            target region is methylated.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting the methylation status of                a nucleic acid, comprises (a) obtaining a nucleic                acid from a biological sample, (b) conjugating an                adapter to the obtained nucleic acid, (c) treating                the nucleic acid conjugated with the adapter with                one or more methylation restriction enzymes (MREs),                (d) amplifying the nucleic acid treated with the                restriction enzyme using adapter-specific primers,                (e) performing a PCR reaction on the amplification                product obtained in step (d) using primers capable                of amplifying the target region to amplify the                target region, and (f) determining the presence or                absence of the amplification product obtained in                step (e) and, if present, determining that the                target region is methylated.
   USE - The method is used for detecting the                methylation status of a nucleic acid and providing                information for disease diagnosis. The disease                comprises cancer, neurodegenerative disease,                autoimmune disease, metabolic disease,                cardiovascular disease, rare disease, and other                diseases. The cancer is ovarian cancer, soft tissue                sarcoma, peripheral T-cell cancer, colon cancer,                intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, glioblastoma,                esophageal cancer, cutaneous T-cell lymphoma,                non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, urinary tract cancer, basal                cell carcinoma, epithelioid sarcoma, pancreatic                cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, Hodgkin's                lymphoma, renal cell carcinoma, mesothelioma,                metastatic uveal melanoma, kidney cancer,                hematological cancer, HER2-expressing cancer,                non-melanoma skin cancer, liposarcoma,                hepatocellular carcinoma, small lymphocytic                lymphoma, prostate cancer, breast cancer, anal                cancer, marginal zone lymphoma, cutaneous squamous                cell carcinoma, thyroid cancer, medullary thyroid                cancer, triple-negative breast cancer,                neuroendocrine prostate cancer, bladder cancer,                paraganglioma, medulloblastoma, superficial basal                cell carcinoma, head and neck squamous cell                carcinoma, hematological cancer, melanoma, B-cell                lymphoma, relapsed/refractory acute myeloid                leukemia, hemangiosarcoma, osteosarcoma, refractory                cervical cancer, cholangiocarcinoma,                gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, rhabdomyosarcoma,                carcinoma, non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer,                uveal melanoma, small cell lung cancer, cervical                cancer, primary open-angle glaucoma, follicular                lymphoma, synovial sarcoma, liver cancer,                carcinosarcoma, leptomeningeal brain tumor, T-cell                lymphoma, small cell lung cancer, mantle cell                lymphoma, B-cell malignancies, endometrial cancer,                mucinous/round cell liposarcoma, metastatic Merkel                cell carcinoma, neuroblastoma, chronic lymphocytic                leukemia, tendon sheath giant cell tumor, sarcoma,                acute myeloid leukemia, skin cancer, nasopharyngeal                cancer, relapsed/refractory Ewing sarcoma, bone                cancer, glioma, salivary gland carcinoma, gastric                cancer, benign tumor, low-grade serous ovarian                cancer, metastatic breast cancer, multiple myeloma,                diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, relapsed/refractory                lymphoma, metastatic colorectal cancer, advanced                malignant tumor, and acute lymphoblastic leukemia,                preferably colon cancer, lung cancer, stomach                cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer, and liver                cancer (all claimed). The neurodegenerative disease                comprises Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease,                amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, frontotemporal                dementia, Lewy dementia, corticobasal degeneration,                multiple systemic encephalopathy, progressive                supranuclear palsy, Huntington's disease, and                Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. The autoimmune disease                comprises ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis,                psoriatic arthritis, erythema nodosum, ulcerative                colitis, Graves' disease, Guillain-Barre syndrome,                rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus                erythematosus. The metabolic disease comprises type                2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity,                hypothyroidism, and chronic kidney disease. The                cardiovascular disease comprises hypertension,                ischemic heart disease, heart failure, stroke,                coronary artery disease, arrhythmia, and                arteriosclerosis. The rare disease comprises                developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and                hemispheric hypertrophy.
   ADVANTAGE - The method can secure quantitatively and                qualitatively methylated DNA enrichment pool, and                can detect methylation levels by real-time PCR                using target methylation marker-specific                primers/probes in the methylated DNA enrichment                pool, thus having excellent detection sensitivity,                enabling the detection of methylated DNA with                higher sensitivity and specificity than existing                methods, and enabling analysis regardless of the                type and number of methylation restriction                enzymes.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for providing information for disease diagnosis,                comprising determining the presence of a disease if                a target region is methylated using the                method.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The step (c) comprises                  treating the methylation dependent restriction                  enzyme (MDRE). When two or more restriction                  enzymes are used in step (c), they are treated at                  the same or different ratios. The primer binding                  site is selected by a method comprising (i)                  setting a 100-500 base pair (bp) region in the 5'                  and 3' directions of the target region as a                  target CpG region, (ii) determining the location                  of a region (CMR, consecutive MSRE CpG fragment)                  within the target CpG region, starting from the                  first MSRE recognition site based on the 5' end                  and extending to one or more consecutive MSRE                  recognition sites containing the MSRE recognition                  site, (iii) calculating a detectable fragment                  fraction (DFF) for each CMR and selecting CMRs                  with different DFF values between non-diseased                  and diseased samples as continuous MSRE-resistant                  fragments (CMRFs), and (iv) selecting the region                  with the largest difference in DFF in the                  selected CMRFs as a primer binding site. The DFF                  is calculated by a method comprising (a1)                  counting the total number of reads aligned to                  each CMR in a database capable of identifying                  methylation levels, (b1) counting the number of                  reads (detectable fragments, DF) in which all                  MSRE recognition sites of each CMR are                  methylated, and (c1) calculating the DFF by                  dividing the number of DFs by the total number of                  reads aligned to the CMR. The database capable of                  confirming the methylation level is created using                  any one method comprising pyrosequencing,                  bisulfite sequencing, and methylation                  next-generation base sequence sequencing. The                  step (f) uses a nucleic acid-binding dye or probe                  capable of binding to the amplification product.                  The step (e) is performed by additionally                  including a a primer (digestion control) capable                  of amplifying a region that is completely                  digested by a methylation restriction enzyme                  (complete digestion region), and a primer                  (internal control) capable of amplifying a region                  that is not cut by a methylation restriction                  enzyme. PN WO2019195566-A1; US2021228747-A1; US11607464-B2
TI New benzimidazol-2-yl-carbamate derivatives used            to treat, inhibit and/or prevent cancer e.g. solid            tumor, leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute            myeloid leukemia, multiple myeloma, breast cancer            neuroblastoma and gliomas.
AU BARANOWSKA-KORTYLEWICZ J
   KORTYLEWICZ Z
AE UNIV NEBRASKA (UNEB-C)
   UNIV NEBRASKA (UNEB-C)
GA 201984913W
AB    NOVELTY - Benzimidazol-2-yl-carbamate derivatives (I)                are new.
   USE - (I) are useful for treating, inhibiting and/or                preventing cancer (claimed) e.g. metastases, solid                tumor, leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia,                acute myeloid leukemia, chronic lymphocytic                leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia, lymphoma                Hodgkin lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, multiple                myeloma, breast cancer, prostate cancer, pancreatic                cancer, colon cancer, thyroid cancer, bladder                cancer, liver cancer, neuroendocrine tumor,                neuroblastoma, brain cancers, gliomas, glioblastoma                ,glioblastoma multiforme, meningiomas, pituitary                adenomas, medulloblastoma, lung cancer, esophageal                cancer, ovarian cancer, stomach cancer, skin                cancer, melanoma, cervical cancer, testicular                cancer, kidney cancer, carcinoid tumors or bone                cancer. The ability of (I) to treat cancer was                tested in BE(2)-C neuroblastoma cell line using                clonogenic survival assay. The result showed that                methyl                N-(5-(3'-iodobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate                exhibited an LD50 value of 0.02 mu M.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) has microtubule-disrupting properties as                well as anti-proliferative effects in cancer cell                with decreases toxicity and decreases acquired                resistance.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Benzimidazol-2-yl-carbamate derivatives of                formula (I) are new.
   R = alkyl, aliphatic or aryl (all optionally                substituted), halo or isotope.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   (1) treating, inhibiting and/or preventing                (M1) a cancer comprising administering (I) to                subject;
   (2) imaging and/or detecting (M2) a tumor                comprising (a) administering (I) to the subject and                (b) detecting the presence of the radioactivity                from the radioactive isotope from the subject,                where the presence and/or location of the                radioactivity provides for the detection and/or                image of the tumor in the subject;
   (3) monitoring (M3) progression of a cancer                comprising (i) administering (I) to subject and                (ii) detecting the presence of the radioactivity                from the radioactive isotope in the subject, where                the presence and/or location of the radioactivity                provides for the detection and/or image of the                tumor in the subject and the step (i) or step (ii)                are performed at different time points on the                subject; and
   (4) sensitizing (M4) cancer cells to                chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy comprising                administering (I) to cancer cells.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  comprises administering radiation therapy to the                  subject. The radioactive isotope is: a gamma                  emitting isotope and the step (b) comprises                  performing a single photon emission computed                  tomography or scintigraphy; and a positron                  emitting isotope and the step (b) comprises                  performing positron emitting tomography. The                  method (M4) sensitizes the cancer cells to gamma                  radiation. Preferred Components: (I) is                  non-radioactive. (I) comprises radioactive                  isotope.
   Preferred Definitions:
   R = halo or isotope, stable isotope, isotope                of halogen, radiohalide comprising 18F, 74Br, 75Br,                76Br, 77Br, 81Br, 123I, 124I, 125I, 127I, 131I or                211At or radioisotope is alpha emitter comprising                211At, 212Pb, 212Bi, 213Bi, 223Ra or 225Ac.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   SPECIFIC COMPOUNDS - 4 Compounds (I) are disclosed i.e. methyl                  N-(5-(3'-iodobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate                  of formula (Ia), methyl                  N-(5-benzoyl-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate,                  methyl                  N-(5-(3'-halobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate,                  methyl                  N-(5-(3'-radioiodobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate                  and methyl                  N-(5-(3'-radiohalobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate.
   EXAMPLE - Solution of 1.05 g methyl                N-(6-benzoyl-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate in 3.5                ml of nitromethane and containing 1.50 ml triflic                acid, 800 mg N-iodosuccinimide was added in three                small portions. The reaction temperature was                gradually increased to 75 degrees C and kept at                this temperature for an additional two hours. After                cooling and evaporation of nitromethane under a                high vacuum, the residue was quenched with 20 ml                ice-water and with a solution of 10 ml 10% sodium                bisulfite and then neutralized with 1 M sodium                bicarbonate to pH of 7.5. The precipitated                yellowish solid was filtered, washed with water and                dried under a high vacuum to give (1.12 g) methyl                N-(5-(3'-iodobenzoyl)-1H-benzimidazol-2-yl)carbamate.

AU TLSTY T
   CARUSO J
   KERLIKOWSKE K
   MOLINARO A
   DEFILIPPIS R
AE UNIV CALIFORNIA (REGC-C)
   UNIV CALIFORNIA (REGC-C)
GA 2020690878
AB    NOVELTY - Determining the risk of progression to                invasive cancer in a subject having a precancerous                lesion, involves obtaining a sample from the                subject comprising stromal tissue adjacent to the                precancerous lesion; analyzing the sample to                determine the abundance of CD36-expressing                vasculature in the stromal tissue adjacent to the                precancerous lesion; and by the measured abundance                of CD36-expressing vasculature, determining the                risk of an invasive cancer progression in the                subject. A reduced abundance of CD36-expressing                vasculature in the stromal tissue adjacent to the                precancerous lesion is indicative of increased                cancer progression risk.
   USE - The methods are useful for determining the                risk of progression to invasive cancer in a subject                having a precancerous lesion, and for treating a                subject having one or more precancerous lesions,                where the invasive cancer is selected from breast                cancer, bladder cancer, brain cancer, cervical                cancer, colorectal cancer, esophageal cancer, head                and neck cancer, kidney cancer, lung cancer,                leukemia, lymphoma, myeloma, ovarian cancer,                pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer, sarcoma, and                skin cancer, where the invasive cancer is breast                cancer and the precancerous lesion comprises ductal                carcinoma in situ (DCIS) (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The prognostic biomarker methods can assess                the likelihood of a subsequent invasive event in                subjects having precancerous lesions, so that                subjects may be directed to the most appropriate                treatment, avoiding undertreatment and                overtreatment harms and related expenses.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   (1) treating a subject having one or more                precancerous lesions, which involves determining                the subject's risk of progression to invasive                cancer; and administering an appropriate treatment                based on the assessed risk of an invasive                event;
   (2) a composition for use in a method of                preventing the occurrence of progressive cancer in                a subject, comprising an agent which selectively or                preferentially enhances CD36 expression in the                stromal microvasculature of the subject; and
   (3) a kit for the measurement of the relative                abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature,                comprising a detection agent selective for                CD36-expressing cells; and one or more detection                agents selective for vascular endothelial                cells.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The abundance of                  CD36-expressing vasculature is measured by                  immunohistochemical analysis in samples                  comprising tissue sections, where CD36-expressing                  vasculature abundance is measured as area. It is                  measured as a relative proportion of                  CD36-expressing vasculature in the stromal tissue                  adjacent to the precancerous lesion. The relative                  abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature is                  determined by the ratio: ((CD36+/CD31-) +                  (CD36+/CD31+))/((CD36+/CD31-) + (CD36+/CD31+) +                  (CD36-/CD31+)) where (CD36+/CD31+) denotes the                  abundance of CD36-positive and CD31-negative                  vasculature in the stromal tissue adjacent to the                  precancerous lesion, (CD36+/ CD31+) denotes the                  abundance of CD36-positive and CD31 -positive                  vasculature in the stromal tissue adjacent to the                  precancerous lesion, and (CD36Y CD31+) denotes                  the abundance of CD36-negative and CD31-positive                  vasculature in the stromal tissue adjacent to the                  precancerous lesion. The risk of invasive cancer                  progression is determined by comparing the                  measured abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature                  to a selected threshold value, where a measured                  abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature below                  the selected threshold value is indicative of                  elevated risk of progression to invasive cancer;                  and where the selected threshold value is 50-75%.                  The relative abundance of CD36-expressing                  vasculature is measured as the proportion of area                  of CD36-expressing vasculature in the total area                  of analyzed stromal tissue adjacent to the                  lesion. The cancer is invasive breast cancer; and                  where, if the risk of progression to invasive                  breast cancer is elevated, one or more treatments                  selected from radiation, hormonal treatment, or                  mastectomy are administered; and if the if the                  risk of progression to invasive breast cancer is                  low, no treatment intervention is administered.                  Preferred Components: The stromal tissue adjacent                  to the precancerous lesion comprises tissue                  within 0.5-2.0 mm of the lesion border. Vimentin                  expression is utilized as a marker of mesenchymal                  vasculature. The composition is a CD36 agonist, a                  CD36 mimic, or a gene therapy construct for                  enhancing the expression of CD36. The detection                  agent selective for vascular endothelial cells                  comprises a detection agent selective for                  vimentin-expressing cells. The kit further                  comprises one or more detection agents selective                  for CD31-expressing cells. The detection agents                  comprise labeled antibodies or antigen binding                  fragments. The kit comprises a triplex                  immunohistochemical module for detection of CD36,                  CD31 , and vimentin. It also comprises reagents                  for a flow cytometry or cell counting assay. The                  kit comprises reagents for a quantitative PCR                  assay. Preferred Parameters: The selected                  threshold value is 60-70%. The risk of invasive                  cancer progression is determined by comparing the                  measured abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature                  to a selected threshold value, where a measured                  abundance of CD36-expressing vasculature below                  the selected threshold value is indicative of                  elevated risk of progression to invasive cancer;                  and where the selected threshold value is 2-8 mu                  m2/mm2. The selected threshold value is 4-6 mu                  m2/mm2.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.

   KENET R O
   KENET B J
AE VANGUARD IMAGING LTD (VANG-Non-standard)

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves illuminating predetermined                areas of the skin using standard illumination                source. An image transducer is provided which is                placed with predetermined distance from the                illumination source. A substance that decreases                effects of refractive index is applied on the skin                surface. AB    NOVELTY - Composition comprises a urolithin or its                precursor.
   USE - The composition is used in reducing the risk                of the recurrence of cancer or tumor formation in a                patient in the remission phase of a preceding                cancer therapy in the patient. The patient is a                human or nonhuman mammal, preferably a human,                optionally a human adult, child or infant. The                patient is an immunocompromised patient. The cancer                is a solid tumor or a liquid tumor, preferably a                lymphoma, a carcinoma or a sarcoma, more preferably                a breast cancer, a prostate cancer, an uterine                cancer, a hepatocellular carcinoma, a pancreatic                cancer, a cervical cancer, a colon cancer, a                colorectal cancer, a gastric cancer, a bladder                cancer, a skin cancer, or a lung cancer, or a head                and neck cancer, most preferably a pancreatic                cancer, a colorectal cancer, a skin cancer, a                breast cancer, a hematological cancer, a leukemia,                a lymphoma or a myeloma.    ADVANTAGE - The composition: is highly efficient when                administering to a patient; allows addressing the                remission phase of patients having completed a                previous cancer therapy and beneficially influence                its outcome to increase survival rate and to                support the body's own immune response to fight the                potential recurrence of a tumor; achieves an                intervention as early as in the start of the                remission phase without unduly waiting for the                potential positive detection of biomarkers within                the long period of usually 5 years of remission                after having completed a previous cancer therapy;                significantly increases the beneficial diagnosis                within the long period of remission; and has                specific advantage of the treatment that lies inter                alia in an effective restimulation of T-cell                function in patients recovering from cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for reducing the reducing the risk of                the recurrence of cancer or tumor formation in a                patient in need in the remission phase after a                preceding cancer therapy in the patient, comprising                (a) providing the composition, (b) administering                the composition to the patient, where the patient                is in the remission phase after a preceding cancer                therapy, and (c) optionally monitoring the patient                regularly on the potential recurrence of the cancer                treated in the preceding cancer therapy, preferably                by using cancer specific biomarkers, preferably                concurrent to administering the composition                according to step (b), preferably in predefined                intervals; and
   a kit comprising the composition and an                instruction manual.

PN WO2023064913-A1; US2025003986-A1
TI Determining responsiveness of cancer to            immunotherapy comprises obtaining sample from subject            and detecting expression level of keratin (K)17, in            which low level of K17 expression indicates that cancer            is responsive to immunotherapy.
AU LAMBERT P
   WANG W
AE WISCONSIN ALUMNI RES FOUND (WISC-C)
   WISCONSIN ALUMNI RES FOUND (WISC-C)
GA 2023402801
AB    NOVELTY - Determining (M1) responsiveness of a cancer to                immunotherapy in a subject comprises (a) obtaining                a sample from the subject, and (b) detecting the                expression level of keratin (K)17 in the sample,                where a low level of K17 expression indicates that                the cancer is responsive to the                immunotherapy.
   USE - The method is useful for: determining                responsiveness of a cancer to immunotherapy in a                subject; predicting if a cancer is non-responsive                to an immunotherapy, where the cancer is head and                neck cancer, skin cancer, small cell lung cancer,                cervical cancer, lung squamous cell carcinoma,                breast cancer, pancreatic cancer, or other                epithelial originated cancer (all claimed); and                reducing, slowing or inhibiting the growth of                cancer. Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: provides low level expression of                K17 that corresponds to at least 300-fold,                preferably at least 10000-fold decrease in K17 RNA                expression levels, when compared to the                non-responsive control; and utilizes K17 that                facilitates evasion of tumors from immune                surveillance and potentially identify new druggable                targets, and enhances the efficacy of immune                checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients with                non-responsive tumors.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                predicting (M2) if a cancer is non-responsive to an                immunotherapy comprising the steps (a)-(b) as per                se, where detection of a high level of expression                of K17 indicates that the cancer is non-responsive                to immunotherapy.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  comprises: (c) treating the subject with cancer                  with an immunotherapy when low levels of K17 are                  detected in step (b); (d) detecting the                  expression level of at least one additional                  marker in the sample, where a low level of K17                  expression and detection of the additional marker                  indicates that the cancer is responsive to the                  immunotherapy; (e) treating the subject with                  cancer with an immunotherapy when low levels of                  K17 and increased levels of the additional marker                  expression are detected in step (d); (f)                  detecting the expression level of the additional                  marker in the sample, where a low level of K17                  expression and a low level of the additional                  marker expression indicates that the cancer is                  responsive to the immunotherapy; and (g) treating                  the subject with cancer with an immunotherapy                  when low levels of K17 and of the additional                  marker expression are detected in step (f). AB    NOVELTY - Droplet reactor (100) comprises two aqueous                phase channels (110), one oil phase channel (130),                a junction (140) where nanoparticles fuse to form                droplets, and an output channel (150) extending                from the junction.
   USE - The droplet reactor is used for forming                microdroplets, detecting extracellular vesicles and                diagnosing cancer, and experiments and diagnosis by                reacting a small amount of a sample in the form of                fine droplets, and in drug delivery vehicle                development, extracellular vesicle marker analysis,                profiling, and various experimental applications.                The cancer is squamous cell carcinoma, small cell                lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, lung                cancer, peritoneal cancer, colon cancer, biliary                tract tumor, nasopharyngeal cancer, laryngeal                cancer, bronchial cancer, thyroid cancer, oral                cancer, osteosarcoma, gallbladder cancer, bile duct                cancer, kidney cancer, bladder cancer, renal cell                cancer, melanoma, brain cancer, glioma,                glioblastoma, brain tumor, skin cancer, pancreatic                cancer, breast cancer, liver cancer, bone marrow                cancer, small intestine cancer, esophageal cancer,                colon cancer, stomach cancer, eye cancer, urethral                cancer, cervical cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian                cancer, metastatic cancer, head and neck cancer,                rectal cancer, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, multiple                myeloma, acute myelogenous leukemia, lymphoma,                acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and chronic                myelogenous leukemia.
   ADVANTAGE - The droplet reactor has improved sensitivity                and accuracy of detection, ensures precise control                over stoichiometry of vesicles (extracellular                vesicle and CLIP), prevents unwanted aggregation,                allows precise control, and minimizes potential                aggregation which could occur in bulk scale                reactions.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for detecting extracellular vesicles                using the droplet reactor, involving detecting                genetic mutations inside the extracellular vesicles                by the fluorescence signal of the droplet image                output from the droplet reactor;
   a method for diagnosing cancer using the                droplet reactor, involving fusing extracellular                vesicles and charged liposomes through the droplet                reactor to form droplets, imaging the droplets                using a fluorescence microscope, and quantifying                the number of droplets in which a fluorescent                signal is detected in the image to determine the                presence or absence of cancer cells; and
   a detection kit comprising the droplet                reactor, wherein the kit comprises liposomes for                detecting extracellular vesicles, or charged                liposomes for detecting extracellular                vesicles.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a                droplet reactor.
   100Droplet reactor
   110Aqueous phase channel
   130Oil phase channel
   140Junction
   150Output channel
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Device: The aqueous phase channel                  is the droplet reactor in which liposomes are                  introduced into the first aqueous phase channel                  and extracellular vesicles are introduced into                  the second aqueous phase channel, and the                  junction is where the liposomes and extracellular                  vesicles fuse to form aqueous droplets. The oil                  phase channel is a droplet reactor which is                  orthogonal to the direction in which the droplets                  are output from the junction, and to which an oil                  phase pump is connected. The oil phase channel                  forms a circulating flow path, where the outlet                  of the output channel is formed on the inner                  circumferential side and the upper side of the                  droplet reactor. The junction allows liposomes                  with a charge formed on their surface to fuse in                  a charge-induced manner regardless of the type of                  surface protein of the extracellular vesicles,                  and preventing damage to the membrane                  characteristics of the extracellular vesicles and                  forming fusion droplets. Preferred Components:                  The liposomes comprise cationic lipids and                  neutral lipids, where the droplet reactor                  encapsulates cancer cell-specific molecular                  beacons. The cationic lipid is                  1,2-dioleoyl-3-trimethylammonium propane. The                  neutral lipid is                  1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine.

AB    NOVELTY - Treating or preventing the reoccurence of                cancer in a subject comprises administering a                therapeutic amount of a nanog modulating agent to                the subject.
   USE - The methods and composition are useful for                treating or preventing the reoccurence of cancer,                for diagnosing a disease characterized by                expression or abnormal expression of a                tumor-associated antigen, and for preventing,                treating, or managing cancer resulting in a                reduction in bulk tumor size and/or a reduction in                cancer cells. The cancer is breast cancer,                testicular cancer, lung cancer, melanoma, brain                cancer, myeloma, Hodgkin's disease, hepatoma,                stomach cancer, bladder cancer, uterine cancer,                neuroblastoma, thyroid cancer, sarcoma, cervical                cancer, Wilm's tumor, colorectal cancer, pancreatic                cancer, skin cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian                cancer, kidney cancer, lymphoma, acute myelogenous                leukemia, acute lymphocytic leukemia, multiple                myeloma, ependymoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia,                myelodysplastic syndrome, or chronic myelogenous                leukemia (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method of diagnosing a disease characterized                by expression or abnormal expression of a                tumor-associated antigen by (i) detection of a                nucleic acid which codes for the tumor-associated                antigen or its part, and/or (ii) detection of the                tumor- associated antigen or its part, and/or (iii)                detection of an antibody to the tumor- associated                antigen or its part and/or (iv) detection of                cytotoxic or T helper lymphocytes which are                specific to the tumor-associated antigen or its                part in a biological sample isolated from a                patient, with the tumor-associated antigen the                tumor antigen being nanog or a polypeptide molecule                having at least 80-95&#176; C identity thereto,                encoded by a polynucleotide having a sequence                encoded by a nucleic acid sequence relating to the                human nanog gene;
   a method of screening for therapeutic agents                useful in the treatment of cancer in a mammal by                (i) contacting a test compound with a cancer stem                cell expressing a nanog polypeptide, and (ii)                detecting a deleterious effect on the cancer stem                cell, where a test compound which shows a                deleterious effect is identified as a potential                therapeutic agent for killing, differentiating or                weakening a nanog expressing cancer stem                cell;
   a pharmaceutical composition, for the                treatment of cancer in a mammal comprising a nanog                modulating agent, where the nanog modulating agent                is (i) a small molecule, (ii) an RNA molecule,                (iii) an antisense oligonucleotide, (iv) a                polypeptide, (v) an antibody, or (vi) a                ribozyme;
   a method for preparing a pharmaceutical                composition of (3) by (i) identifying a therapeutic                agent, (ii) determining whether the therapeutic                ameliorates the cancer in a mammal, and (iii)                combining of the therapeutic agent with an                acceptable pharmaceutical carrier; and
   a method for preventing, treating, or managing                cancer resulting in a reduction in bulk tumor size                and/or a reduction in cancer cells by identifying                the presence of cancer stem cells expressing nanog                in a tumor in a human subject, administering to the                human subject a prophylactic or therapeutic                regimen, the regimen comprising the administration                of a therapeutic agent to the human subject, and                monitoring changes in the amount of the cancer stem                cells, where the regimen results in at least an                approximately 10% reduction in cancer stem cells in                the human subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method for treating                  or preventing the reoccurence of cancer in a                  subject, the nanog modulating agent is an                  antibody that binds to nanog. The nanog                  modulating agent is a nanog antibody conjugate.                  The nanog modulating agent is a small interfering                  RNA (siRNA) that binds to a polynucleotide that                  encodes nanog. The method further comprises                  administering an additional therapy to the                  subject prior to, during or subsequent to the                  administering of the nanog modulating agent. In                  the method of screening for therapeutic agents                  useful in the treatment of cancer in a mammal,                  the therapeutic agent causes the nanog expressing                  cancer stem cell to cease expressing nanog.                  Ceasing expression of nanog causes the cancer                  stem cell to become a more rapidly dividing cell.                  Preferred Pharmaceutical Composition: The                  composition further comprises a pharmaceutical                  carrier.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Tests are described, but no                results are given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Nanog Modulator.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration may include, without                limitation, oral, topical, parenteral, sublingual,                rectal, vaginal, ocular, intradermal, intratumoral,                intracerebral, intrathecal, and intranasal.                Parenteral administration includes subcutaneous                injections, intravenous, intramuscular,                intraperitoneal, intrapleural, intrasternal                injection, directly into the lumen of the bladder,                directly into the tumor, or infusion techniques. No                dosage details given.

TI Detecting cancer, preferably breast cancer in            patient, involves obtaining sample from patient,            isolating extracellular vesicles from sample, and            detecting expression of cancer marker in isolated            extracellular vesicles.

GA 201829976Y
AB    NOVELTY - Method (M1) of detecting cancer in a patient,                involves (a) obtaining a sample from the patient,                (b) isolating extracellular vesicles from the                sample, and (c) detecting expression of at least                one cancer marker in the isolated extracellular                vesicles.
   USE - The methods are useful for detecting cancer in                a patient, bioengineering exosomes for targeting                cancer cells, and treating a patient with cancer.                The patient has a solid tumor cancer. The patient                has or is suspected of having breast cancer,                prostate cancer, lung cancer, brain cancer, colon                cancer, gastric cancer, melanoma, pancreatic                cancer, skin cancer, acute myeloid leukemia,                leukemia, lymphoma and their cancer metastasis. The                cancer is breast cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides a rapid and high                throughput profiling of surface molecules at a                single exosome, enables early detection and                characterization of disease progression of cancer,                and enhances the ability to detect exosomes stained                with fluorophore-conjugated antibodies by                conventional flow cytometry.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method (M2) of bioengineering exosomes for                targeting cancer cells, involves (a) expressing a                fusion protein comprising a segment of an exosome                protein fused to a cancer stem cell (CSC) targeting                peptide in a host cell, and (b) isolating secreted                exosomes comprising the fusion protein;
   bioengineered exosome (E1) made by the                above-mentioned method (M2);
   bioengineered exosome (E2) comprising the                fusion protein comprising a segment of an exosome                protein fused to a CSC targeting peptide, where the                segment of the exosome protein comprises a portion                of the transmembrane domain of the exosome protein;                and
   therapeutic bioengineered exosome comprising                the bioengineered exosome, and at least one RNA                oligonucleotide or chemotherapeutic agent.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecule: The extracellular                  vesicles are isolated from the CSCs. The step (b)                  extracellular vesicles are isolated by                  ultra-centrifugation. The extracellular vesicles                  are exosomes. The extracellular vesicles are                  30-150 nm in size. The extracellular vesicles                  express at least one of the exosomal markers                  cluster of differentiation (CD), CD81,                  lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2) B,                  tumor susceptibility 101 (Tsg101), and &#945;                  -1,3/1,6-mannosyltransferase (ALG) 2-interacting                  protein X (Alix). The extracellular vesicles do                  not express glucose regulated protein 94 (Grp94).                  The cancer cell marker is chosen from CD47, CD44,                  CD24, CD29, CD44V6, CD49b, CD49f, CD59, CD66,                  CD109, and human epidermal growth factor receptor                  2 (HER2). The markers on individual extracellular                  vesicles within the isolated extracellular                  vesicles are detected. The CSC targeting peptide                  is a mutant form of signal-regulatory                  protein-&#945; (SIRP-&#945; ). The                  exosome protein is a fragment of LAMP2 comprising                  at least the transmembrane domain. The CSC                  targeting peptide is a mutant form of                  signal-regulatory protein-&#945;                  (mSIRP-&#945; ). The RNA oligonucleotide is a                  small (or short) interfering RNA (siRNA) or                  microRNA (miR) specific for cancer. The miRNA is                  miR-200, miR30c, or miR206. Preferred Method: In                  step (c), the expression of at least one cancer                  marker is detected using a micro flow cytometer.                  The step (c) involves determining a differential                  expression profile for at least one cancer marker                  in the sample as compared to a control. The step                  (a) involves transducing the host cell with a                  viral vector encoding the fusion protein.                  Preferred Sample: The sample is a body fluid                  sample or a tissue sample.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The exosomes are administered by direct                injection into the tumor. No dosage details                given.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves examining an in-vivo                tissue sample using an optical signal detection                system adapted to automatically assign                classification to each region of the tissue sample.                An overlay map indicating the classifications                assigned to each region, is created and displayed                so as to facilitate identification of suspect                regions of the tissue sample.
   USE - For diagnosing cervical tissue of patient for                treatment of cancer using photodynamic therapy,                cryotherapy and direct chemical treatment                techniques. Also for diagnosing animal tissues,                vaginal tissue and other tissues including                colorectal, gastroesophageal, urinary bladder,                lung, skin tissue and tissues comprising epithelial                cells.
   ADVANTAGE - Avoid damage to the non-affected tissue upon                treatment and excision of the diseased tissue and                facilitates minimally-invasive treatment of the                diseased tissue by accurately directing to only the                areas that are identified as diseased.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   ystem for detection of suspect regions of                tissue sample;
   optical signal detection apparatus; and
   method for identifying characteristic of                regions of tissue sample.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows the block diagram of a                tissue characterization system.

TI Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic system            for performing real-time segmentation and            classification of skin lesions from input images, has            SoftAttendNet for integrating deep learning and soft            attention mechanisms to perform real-time segmentation            and classification of skin lesions.
AU PADMAVATHI B
   THILAGAMANI S
   SHREE M N
AE EASWARI ENG COLLEGE (EASW-Non-standard)
GA 202527849D
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a SoftAttendNet for integrating                deep learning and soft attention mechanisms to                perform real-time segmentation and classification                of skin lesions from input images for detecting                skin cancer. A system main unit utilizes RegNetY032                as the backbone convolutional neural network (CNN)                for feature extraction, ensuring robust and                scalable performance across multiple skin lesion                types. The soft attention mechanism comprises                channel and spatial attention layers to dynamically                focus on relevant regions and features within skin                images for enhanced detection accuracy, where data                pre-processing comprise noise removal, GANs                segmentation and data augmentation techniques to                improve model generalization and segmentation                precision.
   USE - Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic                system for performing real-time segmentation and                classification of skin lesions from input                images.
   ADVANTAGE - The system improves classification and                diagnosis of skin lesions, and addresses growing                need for accessible dermatological tools, and                employs a soft attention mechanism to dynamically                monitor attention scores across image paths, and                enhances interpretability of diagnostic decisions,                and revolutionizes dermatological care by offering                an accurate, interpretable and scalable solution                for early skin lesion detection and monitoring, and                provides real-time classification and risk                assessment.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of an                artificial intelligence-based diagnostic system for                performing real-time segmentation and                classification of skin lesions from input                images.

TI New isolated monoclonal antibody that specifically            binds to vimentin polypeptide, where the antibody            competes for binding of polypeptide with monoclonal            antibody, useful for selectively detecting circulating            tumor cells and treating cancer.
AU SATELLI A
   LI S
AE UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
   UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM BOARD (TEXA-C)
   UNIV TEXAS (TEXA-C)
   UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
   UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
   UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
GA 2014R04161
AB    NOVELTY - An isolated monoclonal antibody (A1), where                the antibody specifically binds to a vimentin                polypeptide and the antibody competes for binding                of the polypeptide with a 84-1 monoclonal antibody,                is new.
   USE - In host cell comprising mammalian cell, a                yeast cell, a bacterial cell, a ciliate cell or an                insect cell; for selectively detecting circulating                tumor cells in a patient having an epithelial                tumor, metastatic tumor or mesenchymal tumor; and                for treatment of cancer in a subject, which has                been determined to comprise circulating tumor                cells, where the cancer is breast cancer, lung                cancer, head and neck cancer, prostate cancer,                esophageal cancer, tracheal cancer, skin cancer                brain cancer, liver cancer, bladder cancer, stomach                cancer, pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine                cancer, cervical cancer, testicular cancer, colon                cancer, rectal cancer, or skin cancer                (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The antibody provides early detection of                cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   new isolated polynucleotide molecule                comprising a nucleic acid sequence encoding the                antibody (A1);
   new recombinant polypeptide (P1) comprising an                antibody heavy variable region (VH) domain having                complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) 1-3 of                the VH domain of 84-1 of amino acid sequence                containing                Gly-Phe-Ser-Leu-Thr-Arg-Arg-Tyr-Tyr-Gly-Gly-Val                (SEQ ID NO: 3), amino acid sequence containing 16                amino acids (SEQ ID NO: 4), as given in the                specification, and amino acid sequence containing                Arg-Ser-Tyr-Tyr-Tyr-Ala-Met-Asp-Tyr (SEQ ID NO: 5);                or antibody light variable region (VL) domain                comprising CDRs 1-3 of the VL domain of 84-1 of                amino acid sequence containing 16 amino acids (SEQ                ID NO: 6), as given in the specification, amino                acid sequence containing                Lys-Lys-Val-Val-Ser-Asn-Arg-Phe-Ser-Ser (SEQ ID NO:                7), and amino acid sequence containing                Phe-Gln-Gly-Ser-His-Val-Val-Pro-Leu-Thr (SEQ ID NO:                8);
   new isolated polynucleotide molecule                comprising a nucleic acid sequence encoding the                polypeptide (P1);
   new host cell comprising at least one                polynucleotide molecule encoding the antibody (A1)                or the recombinant polypeptide (P1);
   preparation of the antibody (A1);
   a method (M1) of selectively detecting                circulating tumor cells involving: a) obtaining a                blood sample from a patient; b) incubating the                sample with an antibody that binds to cell surface                vimentin; and c) detecting the antibody-bound                cells, thus selectively detecting circulating tumor                cells;
   a method of treating a patient determined to                have circulating tumor cells by the method (M)                involving administering the antibody (A1);                and
   a composition (C1) comprising the antibody                (A1).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Antibodies (claimed): Preparation of the                  antibody (A1) involves: expressing at least one                  polynucleotide molecule encoding a VL and VH                  chain of the antibody in a cell; and purifying                  the antibody from the cell. Preferred Antibody:                  The antibody (A1) comprises a first heavy                  variable region (VH) complementarity-determining                  region (CDR) at least 80% identical to VH CDR1 of                  84-1 of amino acid sequence containing                  Gly-Phe-Ser-Leu-Thr-Arg-Arg-Tyr-Tyr-Gly-Gly-Val                  (SEQ ID NO: 3); a second VH CDR at least 80%                  identical to VH CDR2 of 84-1 of amino acid                  sequence containing 16 amino acids (SEQ ID NO:                  4), as given in the specification; third VH CDR                  at least 80% identical to VH CDR3 of 84-1 of                  amino acid sequence containing                  Arg-Ser-Tyr-Tyr-Tyr-Ala-Met-Asp-Tyr (SEQ ID NO:                  5); first light variable region (VL) CDR at least                  80% identical to VL CDR1 of 84-1 of amino acid                  sequence containing 16 amino acids (SEQ ID NO:                  6), as given in the specification; second VL CDR                  at least 80% identical to VL CDR2 of 84-1 of                  amino acid sequence containing                  Lys-Lys-Val-Val-Ser-Asn-Arg-Phe-Ser-Ser (SEQ ID                  NO: 7); and third VL CDR at least 80% identical                  to VL CDR3 of 84-1 of amino acid sequence                  containing                  Phe-Gln-Gly-Ser-His-Val-Val-Pro-Leu-Thr (SEQ ID                  NO: 8). The isolated antibody (A1) comprises VH                  domain at least about 80% identical to the VH                  domain of 84-1 of amino acid sequence containing                  116 amino acids (SEQ ID NO: 1), as given in the                  specification and a VL domain at least about 80%                  identical to the VL domain of 84-1 of amino acid                  sequence containing 111 amino acids (SEQ ID NO:                  2), as given in the specification. The antibody                  (A1) comprises a VH domain identical to the VH                  domain of 84-1 (SEQ ID NO: 1) and a VL domain                  identical to the VL domain of 84-1 (SEQ ID NO:                  2). The antibody (A1) is the 84-1 antibody; is                  recombinant; is an IgG, IgM, IgA and/or an                  antigen binding fragment; ia Fab', F(ab')2, a                  F(ab')3, a monovalent scFv, a bivalent scFV, or a                  single domain antibody; is a human, humanized                  antibody or de-immunized antibody; and is                  conjugated to an imaging agent, a                  chemotherapeutic agent, a toxin or a                  radionuclide.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (M1) involves                  isolating viable circulating tumor cells; and                  further involves separating the antibody-bound                  circulating tumor cell of (b) from the sample.                  The step of separating involves immunomagnetic                  capture, adhesion-based cell sorting,                  magnetic-activated cell sorting, or                  fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS). The                  method (M1) further involves depleting the sample                  of CD45-positive cells prior to the incubating                  the sample with an antibody that binds to cell                  surface vimentin; using flow cytometry,                  immunohistochemistry, fluorescence microscopy,                  radioimmunoassay, or enzyme-linked immunosorbent                  assay (ELISA) to detect the antibody-bound cells;                  genotyping the isolated viable circulating tumor                  cells. The method further involves increasing the                  level of cell surface vimentin expression by                  incubating the sample with a protein tyrosine                  phosphatase inhibitor; incubating the sample with                  epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) or                  cytokeratin antibodies; quantifying the number of                  circulating tumor cells in the patient;                  monitoring response to therapy in a cancer                  patient, where if the number of circulating tumor                  cells decreases over time, then the patient is                  the to have had a positive response to therapy.                  The patient has not been previously diagnosed                  with cancer and the method is a method of early                  cancer detection. The patient is in remission and                  the method is a method of detecting relapse. The                  step of detecting at least about three                  circulating tumor cells per milliliter of blood                  is indicative of the patient having a tumor. The                  method (M1) is a method of prognosis and                  detecting at least about five circulating tumor                  cells per milliliter of blood is indicative of                  the patient having a poor prognosis. Preferred                  Composition: The composition (C1) further                  comprises a chemotherapeutic, radiotherapeutic,                  gene therapy, or a second immunotherapeutic                  agent. Preferred Components: The protein tyrosine                  phosphatase inhibitor is sodium orthovanadate,                  dephostatin, mpV(pic), phenylarsine oxide, sodium                  stibogluconate, BAY U6751, a tyrosine phosphatase                  inhibitor cocktail (including sodium vanadate,                  sodium molybdate, sodium tartrate, and                  imidazole), and calcium salt of                  3-hexadecanoyl-5-hydroxymethyl-tetronic acid                  (RK-682).
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Dosage is 1 &#956; g to 1000 mg/kg.                Administration is by parenteral (including                intravenous, intramuscular, sub-cutaneous, or                intraperitoneal) route.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Evaluating the cancer state of a subject comprises            isolating a sample of DNA from the subject, and            determining a first methylation level of the            lecithin:retinol acyl transferase (LRAT) gene promoter            nucleotide sequence.
