GA 2008O00094
AB    NOVELTY - Evaluating the cancer state of a subject                comprises isolating a sample of DNA from the                subject, and determining a first methylation level                of the lecithin:retinol acyl transferase (LRAT)                gene promoter nucleotide sequence, or of the region                upstream of the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                sequence, in the DNA sample where the detection of                a methylated LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                sequence, or region upward, within the sample                permits the evaluation of the cancer state of the                subject.
   USE - The methods are useful for evaluating the                cancer state of a subject; determining the                prognosis of subject having cancer; and treating a                subject for cancer, e.g. colorectal cancer,                prostate cancer, renal cancer, pancreatic cancer,                breast cancer, skin cancer, oral cavity cancer,                lung cancer, gastrointestinal cancer, liver cancer,                head and neck cancer, and brain cancer (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method of determining the prognosis of                subject having cancer comprises assessing the level                of LRAT mRNA expression in a sample obtained from                the subject, and comparing the level of LRAT mRNA                expression in the sample to the level of LRAT mRNA                expression in a reference RNA standard, where a                decrease in LRAT mRNA expression in the sample                compared to the reference standard indicates a                favorable prognosis for the subject; and
   a method of treating a subject for cancer                comprises treating the subject with a                pharmaceutical composition which inhibits LRAT                activity under conditions effective to treat the                cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: Evaluating the cancer                  state of the subject further comprises comparing                  the first methylation level of the LRAT gene                  promoter nucleotide sequence, or region upward,                  to a second methylation level of a LRAT gene                  promoter nucleotide sequence, or region upward,                  in a reference DNA sample, where a difference                  between the first and second methylation levels                  permits evaluation of the cancer state of the                  subject. An increase in the level of methylation                  in the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide sequence, or                  region upward, indicates the detection of cancer                  within the sample. Likewise, an increase in the                  level of methylation in the LRAT gene promoter                  nucleotide sequence, or region upward, is a                  cancer diagnostic. An increase in the level of                  methylation within the LRAT gene promoter                  nucleotide sequence, or region upward, also                  indicates a favorable cancer prognosis. The                  cancer is selected from colorectal cancer,                  prostate cancer, renal cancer, pancreatic cancer,                  breast cancer, skin cancer, oral cavity cancer,                  lung cancer, gastrointestinal cancer, liver                  cancer, head and neck cancer, and brain cancer.                  The evaluation of the cancer state of the subject                  is selected from detecting cancer, diagnosing                  cancer, determining cancer prognosis, and                  monitoring cancer progression, where the                  evaluation of the cancer state of the subject is                  cancer detection, cancer diagnosis, and cancer                  prognosis. Cancer progression in the subject is                  monitored with the cancer evaluation being                  carried out with tissue samples obtained from the                  subject at multiple time points. The methylation                  level of the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                  sequence, or region upward, comprises the level                  of methylation at one or more defined CpG                  nucleotide sites within the promoter nucleotide                  sequence, or region upward. Likewise, the                  methylation level of one or more of target LRAT                  gene promoter nucleotide sequences, or regions                  upward, within a sample is quantified, by                  measuring the number of CpG nucleotides which are                  methylated at a defined site within the promoter,                  or region upward, and measuring the number of CpG                  nucleotides which are unmethylated at the                  corresponding defined site within the promoter,                  or region upward, where a quantitative measure of                  the methylation level at a defined CpG site in                  sample containing LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                  sequences, or regions upward, is determined by                  the ratio of site specific methylated CpG                  nucleotides to the sum of the site specific                  methylated and unmethylated CpG nucleotides.                  Moreover, the methylation level of the LRAT gene                  promoter sequence, or region upward, comprises                  the level of methylation across one or more CpG                  sites in the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                  sequence, or region upward. The methylation level                  of one or more of the LRAT gene promoter                  nucleotide sequences, or regions upward, within                  the sample is further quantified by determining                  the level of methylation at individual CpG sites                  within the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide                  sequence, or region upward, and calculating the                  average level of methylation across the                  individual CpG sites located within the LRAT gene                  promoter nucleotide sequence, or region upward,                  where the average indicates the overall level of                  LRAT promoter nucleotide sequence methylation.                  The detection of methylation within the LRAT gene                  promoter nucleotide sequence, or region upward,                  indicates the detection of cancer within the                  sample, is a cancer diagnostic, and indicates a                  favorable cancer prognosis. Furthermore, the                  methylation level of the LRAT gene promoter                  nucleotide sequence is determined where the                  nucleotide sequence comprises fully defined 950                  bp (SEQ ID NO: 1), given in the specification,                  and also determined by analysis of one or more of                  the CpG nucleotide sites in SEQ ID NO: 1.                  Likewise, the methylation level of the LRAT gene                  promoter nucleotide sequence is determined at                  nucleotides 12, 23, 54, 57, 67, 79, 110, 114,                  124, 156, 160, 169, 172, 204, 219, 222, 242, 252,                  263, 279, 364, 376, 380, 383, 385, 389, 435, 440,                  443, 459, 501, 521, 545, 555, 559, 582, 596, 621,                  623, 644, 650, 680, 710, 721, 723, 779, 788, 814,                  830, or a combination, in SEQ ID NO: 1. The                  methylation level of the region upstream of the                  LRAT gene promoter nucleotide sequence is                  determined, where the nucleotide sequence                  comprises fully defined 4393 bp (SEQ ID NO: 2),                  given in the specification, and also determined                  by analysis of one or more of the CpG nucleotide                  sites in SEQ ID NO: 2. The methylation level of                  the LRAT gene promoter nucleotide sequence is                  determined at nucleotides 263, 445, 516, 629,                  755, 890, 902, 916, 938, 957, 969, 971, 980, 986,                  994, 1000, 1011, 1047, 1060, 1079, 1083, 1140,                  1143, 1158, 1164, 1179, 1187, 1194, 1225, 1230,                  1428, 1553, 1564, 1570, 1586, 1606, 1642, 1649,                  1656, 1718, 1726, 1732, 1739, 1752, 1821, 1887,                  1889, 1954, 1959, 2006, 2027, 2049, 2073, 2085,                  2087, 2276, 2298, 2305, 2317, 2349, 2366, 2375,                  2421, 2436, 2445, 2465, 2474, 2522, 2546, 2557,                  2607, 2645, 2650, 2695, 2701, 2725, 2740, 2751,                  2757, 2785, 2809, 2821, 2844, 2883, 2900, 2904,                  2932, 2935, 2961, 3021, 3035, 3047, 3049, 3063,                  3065, 3072, 3080, 3093, 3116, 3133, 3144, 3148,                  3182, 3195, 3201, 3257, 3269, 3309, 3346, 3350,                  3361, 3364, 3380, 3392, 3401, 3421, 3434, 3448,                  3451, 3453, 3468, 3470, 3477, 3501, 3520, 3522,                  3525, 3574, 3576, 3586, 3601, 3623, 3646, 3692,                  3724, 3764, 3771, 3788, 3811, 3813, 3819, 3877,                  3886, 3912, 3917, 3921, 3958, 4031, 4041, 4043,                  4059, 4070, 4089, 4094, 4152, 4160, 4162, 4165,                  4204, 4209, 4229, 4237, 4239, 4248, 4251, 4257,                  4262, 4264, 4270, 4273, 4293, 4304, 4311, 4317,                  4325, 4328, 4342, 4347, 4362, 4369, 4371, 4373,                  4375, 4387, 4392, or a combination, in SEQ ID NO:                  2. The method                  further comprises establishing a therapeutic                  regimen based on the determining; and                  administering a pharmaceutical composition                  comprising a LRAT inhibitor to the subject based                  on the establishing. In determining the prognosis                  of subject having cancer, the reference RNA                  standard comprises an RNA sample isolated from a                  matched non-cancerous tissue obtained from the                  subject. A favorable prognosis indicates an                  increase probability of survival of the subject.                  The method further comprises monitoring the                  subject's cancer prognosis by obtaining and                  assessing the level of LRAT mRNA in tissue                  samples obtained from the subject at multiple                  time points; monitoring the subject's response to                  cancer therapy by assessing the level of LRAT                  mRNA expression in a tissue sample obtained from                  the subject prior to cancer therapy treatment;                  assessing the level of LRAT mRNA expression in a                  tissue sample obtained from same subject after                  cancer therapy treatment; and comparing the level                  of LRAT mRNA expression in the tissue sample                  obtained prior to cancer therapy treatment to the                  level of LRAT mRNA expression in the tissue                  sample obtained after cancer therapy treatment,                  where a decrease in LRAT mRNA expression in the                  tissue sample obtained after cancer therapy                  treatment compared to that prior to therapy is                  indicative of a favorable response to the cancer                  therapy treatment. Determining the prognosis of                  subject having cancer also comprises assessing                  the level of LRAT protein expression in the                  sample obtained from the subject and comparing                  the level of LRAT protein expression in the                  sample to the level of LRAT protein expression in                  the reference protein standard, where a decrease                  in LRAT protein expression in the sample compared                  to the reference standard indicates a favorable                  prognosis for the subject. Treating the subject                  for cancer further comprises treating the subject                  with the compound that inhibits LRAT activity in                  combination with another standard cancer                  therapeutic treatment under conditions effective                  to treat the cancer, where the pharmaceutical                  composition which inhibits LRAT activity contains                  a compound selected from retinyl bromoacetate,                  N-boc-L-biocytinyl-11-aminoundecane chloromethyl                  ketone, and phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. A series of 133 colorectal cancer                (CRC) patients were identified and their tumor                samples were subjected to bisulfite/PCR-PCR/ligase                detection reaction (LDR)/Universal Array analysis.                As shown in the specification, the analyzed                clinical samples consisted of microsatellite                instable (MSI) (n=40), non-MSI (polyps, n=13; stage                I, n=15; stage II, n=15; stage III, n=21; stage IV,                n=29), metastatic tumors (n=26), and normal colon                mucosa tissues (n=69). LRAT promoter                hypermethylation was associated with the majority                of CRC tumors (92.5%) having a MSI phenotype. MSI                and non-MSI tumors were two distinct subtypes of                CRC. MSI patients typically had better survival and                clinically favorable outcomes. The data also                indicated that high percentage CRC polyps (92.3%)                were associated with hypermethylation of the LRAT                promoter. A bowel polyp (adenoma) was a small                growth that forms on the inside lining of the colon                or rectum. About 1 in 4 people over the age of 50                develop at least one bowel polyp. Polyps were                usually benign and considered the initial step                during CRC development. A benign polyp might turn                cancerous and this change usually took place after                a number of years. Hypermethylation of LRAT gene                promoter was also seen in samples with CRC stages I                (66.7%), II (66.7%), III (33.3%) and IV (41.4%).                However, the normal colon mucosa tissues were                methylated at relatively low percentage (18%) in                these patients.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - LRAT-Inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - Dosage is 1-250 mg. Administration can be                through oral, parenteral, subcutaneous,                intravenous, intramuscular, intraperitoneal,                intranasal, or mucosal route.
   SPECIFIC SEQUENCES - Specifically claimed are the LRAT nucleic                  acid sequences comprising 49-4393 bp (SEQ ID NO:                  1-6), and the probe sequences for ligase                  detection reaction comprising 26-65 bp (SEQ ID                  NO: 8-37). All sequences are fully defined in the                  specification.
   EXAMPLE - To test the possibility of using                lecithin:retinol acyl transferase (LRAT) promoter                methylation as a prognostic and diagnostic marker,                a series of 133 colorectal cancer (CRC) patients                were identified from Memorial-Sloan Kettering                Cancer Center tumor bank and their tumor samples                were subjected to bisulfite/PCR-PCR/ligase                detection reaction (LDR)/Universal Array analysis.                The methylation levels often CpG dinucleotide sites                in the LRAT promoter region were determined for                each CRC sample. The average methylation level of                CpG sites 1-6 was used to score the overall LRAT                promoter methylation status. As shown in the                specification, the analyzed clinical samples                consisted of microsatellite instable (MSI) (n=40),                non-MSI (polyps, n=13; stage I, n=15; stage II,                n=15; stage III, n=21; stage IV, n=29), metastatic                tumors (n=26), and normal colon mucosa tissues                (n=69). LRAT promoter hypermethylation was                associated with the majority of CRC tumors (92.5%)                having a MSI phenotype. MSI and non-MSI tumors were                two distinct subtypes of CRC. MSI patients                typically had better survival and clinically                favorable outcomes. The data also indicated that                high percentage CRC polyps (92.3%) were associated                with hypermethylation of the LRAT promoter. A bowel                polyp (adenoma) was a small growth that forms on                the inside lining of the colon or rectum. About 1                in 4 people over the age of 50 develop at least one                bowel polyp. Polyps were usually benign and                considered the initial step during CRC development.                A benign polyp might turn cancerous and this change                usually took place after a number of years.                Hypermethylation of LRAT gene promoter was also                seen in samples with CRC stages I (66.7%), II                (66.7%), III (33.3%) and IV (41.4%). However, the                normal colon mucosa tissues were methylated at                relatively low percentage (18%) in these                patients.

   ADVANTAGE - The method ensures accurate detection of                diseased cells, disease-associated exosomes,                disease-associated transcriptomes, or                disease-associated polynucleotides in a fluid                sample with high sensitivity, and exhibits desired                therapeutic effect while minimizing unnecessary                side effects.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method for identifying a disease in a subject                involves performing the steps (a)-(c), where the                detection of the presence of one or more diseased                cells, disease-associated exosomes,                disease-associated transcriptomes, or                disease-associated polynucleotides is indicative of                the disease in the subject;
   method for prognosing a subject involves                performing the steps (a)-(c), where the detection                of diseased cells, disease-associated exosomes,                disease-associated transcriptomes, or                disease-associated polynucleotides is indicative of                the subject's prognosis;
   method for predicting disease recurrence in a                subject, involves obtaining a first fluid sample                from the subject and analyzing the quantity of                diseased cells, disease-associated exosomes,                disease-associated transcriptomes, or disease-                associated polynucleotides, administering an                intervening agent, obtaining a second fluid sample                from the subject and analyzing the quantity of                diseased cells, disease-associated exosomes,                disease-associated transcriptomes, or                disease-associated polynucleotide, and determining                change of quantity in the diseased cells,                disease-associated exosomes, disease-associated                transcriptomes, or disease-associated                polynucleotides in the first and the second fluid                samples, and predicting disease recurrence by                evaluating the change;
   method for obtaining actionable information in                a subject involves obtaining a first sample from                the subject, analyzing a biomarker, administering                an intervening agent, obtaining a second sample                from the subject, analyzing the biomarker,                determining change of the biomarker in the first                and the second samples, and obtaining actionable                information;
   method for predicting treatment response of a                subject involves obtaining a first sample from the                subject and analyzing a biomarker, administering                intervening agent, obtaining a second sample from                the subject and analyzing the biomarker, and                determining change of the biomarker in the first                and the second samples, and thus predicting                treatment response by evaluating the change of the                biomarker;
   method for supporting treatment decision of a                subject involves obtaining a first sample from the                subject and analyzing a biomarker, administering                intervening agent, obtaining a second sample from                the subject and analyzing the biomarker, and                determining change of the biomarker in the first                and the second samples, and thus making an optimal                treatment decision by evaluating the change of the                biomarker;
   method for detecting presence or absence of                minimal residual disease in a subject involves                determining presence or absent of one or more tumor                cells, tumor exosomes, tumor transcriptomes, or                tumor DNA, according to the method, where presence                of the one or more tumor cells, tumor exosomes,                tumor transcriptomes, or tumor DNA in the fluid                sample indicates presence of minimal residual                disease in the subject, and the absence of the one                or more tumor cells, tumor exosomes, tumor                transcriptomes, or tumor DNA in the fluid sample                indicates absence of minimal residual disease in                the subject; and
   method for treating cancer in a subject                involves administering CXCR4 antagonist,                growth-related gene product P (GROP) or its                fragment or analog, or coagulation system                modulator, obtaining a fluid sample from the                subject, determining the presence or absence of one                or more tumor cells, tumor exosomes, tumor                transcriptomes, or tumor DNA in the fluid sample,                and administering at least one cancer therapeutic                to the subject if presence of one or more tumor                cells, tumor exosomes, tumor transcriptomes, or                tumor DNA in the fluid sample is detected.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for assaying a biomolecule in a sample                involves (a) incubating a particle in the sample by                adsorbing biomolecules from the sample onto the                particle to form a biomolecule corona, (b)                incubating the particle with a probe comprising (i)                an affinity reagent and (ii) a barcode, where the                affinity reagent binds to a biomolecule of the                biomolecule corona and (c) assaying for the                presence, absence or amount of the probe by                assaying for the presence, absence or amount of the                biomolecule of the biomolecule corona.
   USE - The method is useful for assaying a                biomolecule e.g. proteins, lipids, nucleic acids,                metabolites, saccharides and small molecules in a                sample, which is useful for determining a disease                state, and/or prognosing or diagnosing a disease or                disorder. The disease or disorder includes cancer                (e.g. lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, or skin                cancer), cardiovascular disease, endocrine disease,                inflammatory disease, and neurological                disease.

AB    NOVELTY - A leak detection system, comprising a delivery                device for attachment to individual body, a cannula                or needle (18) to penetrate individual skin (16) at                infusion site (30) and establish fluid between the                delivery device and individual skin, and chemicals                to react with components within leaking fluid near                the infusion site, is new.
   USE - The system is for detecting leakage of                medication fluid, e.g. insulin, human                immunodeficiency virus (HIV) drugs, drugs to treat                pulmonary hypertension, iron chelation drugs, pain                medications, or anti-cancer treatment, under                delivery device near an infusion site. It is for                use with human beings and animals.
   ADVANTAGE - The inventive leak detection system includes                chemical near the infusion site that reacts with                preservatives in the leaking fluid to generate high                visible, brightly-colored chemical complex, thus                leakage can be visibly detected.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a cross-sectional side view                of an infusion set attached to body tissue.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Components: The delivery device                  includes a base (32), where chemical positioned                  near the infusion site is embedded. A guide conducting element                  guides light from a point near the infusion site                  to the optical receiver. The light conducting                  element is a fiber optic cable or a flexible tube                  filled with fluid. The leak detection system                  further includes alarm system, which produces                  audible sound or activates a vibrator when a leak                  is detected. The cannula or needle is surrounded                  by a rosette, which is coupled with electrical                  components to detect a change in electrical                  characteristic in the rosette when leak occurs.                  The electrical component is supplied with power                  by a battery. The rosette is closed circuit, such                  that its impedance across the rosette decreases                  as the fluid leaks near the infusion site.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The chemical near the                  infusion site contains 4-amino-antipyrine,                  potassium ferricyanide, horse radish peroxidase                  (HRP), ninhydrin, and/or Coomassie Brilliant                  Blue. It is encapsulated in micro-spheres. It is                  a component of a gel or adhesive, or associated                  with starch granules.

The underwear can be manufactured in a                cost-effective manner.

TI Method for measuring e.g. cancerous tissue for            non-melanoma skin cancer delineation, involves            detecting polarization components of light from region            of tissue, and processing components to determine            characteristic of tissue.
AU YAROSLAVKSY A N
   GILES R H
   JOSEPH C S
   PATEL R
   YAROSLAVSKY A N
AE UNIV MASSACHUSETTS (UMAC-C)
   YAROSLAVKSY A N (YARO-Individual)
   GILES R H (GILE-Individual)
   JOSEPH C S (JOSE-Individual)
   PATEL R (PATE-Individual)
   UNIV MASSACHUSETTS (UMAC-C)
GA 2014B55821
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves illuminating a region of                cancerous tissue with light from a first light                source i.e. laser (12). A first polarization                component of light is detected from the region of                tissue, and a second polarization component of                light is detected from the region of tissue. The                first detected polarization component and the                second detected polarization component are                processed to determine characteristic of tissue.                The tissue with the light is illuminated from a                second light source within optical wavelength                range. Cross-polarized imaging is performed with                light reflected by the tissue.
   USE - Method for measuring normal and cancerous                tissue for a non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC)                delineation using continuous wave terahertz imaging                (CWT) for medical applications.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables rapidly acquiring                registered optical and terahertz images by                combining two imaging modalities into one imaging                device, so that time required for the detection of                tumor margins can be dramatically reduced in an                effective manner. The method enables using                amplitude and phase information for implementing                post processing noise reduction algorithms such as                DC bias subtraction with a data processor so as to                improve image quality.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                multimodal system for imaging tissue.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a                terahertz reflection system.

TI New fluorescent natural dye compound from a marine            organism useful in e.g. photochemotherapy of skin            cancers.
AU GOSWAMI U
   GANGULY A
   GOSWAMI U N I O O
   GANGULY A N I O O
AE COUNCIL SCI&IND RES INDIA (COUI-C)
   COUNCIL SCI&IND RES INDIA (COUI-C)

GA 2003363024
AB    NOVELTY - A multiple fluorescent natural dye compound                from a marine organism Holothuria Scabra, is                new.
   USE - The fluorescent dye is used as:
as a multiple fluorescent dye;
as a natural in-vivosystem for studying                associated physiological aspects of organosilicon                compound, in cosmetic surgery;
for the preparation of flexible polyvinyl                chloride film that exhibits fluorescent colors for                use in paints, inks, textiles;
for bleaching and brightening a polymer;
for leak detections with a full spectrum of                fluorescent dye;
in automated chemical metering system;
to mark the location of crashed transport                vessel (e.g. aircraft, life crafts and                rockets);
in undersea probes;
in photochemotherapy of skin cancers;
as a chromatophore sunscreen component of                cosmetic creams and lotions;
in moisturizers;
in fluorescent in-situhybridization                application kit component for molecular                diagnostics;
as a component of the non-radioactive labeling                and detection kits used in biochemistry, cell                biology, immunochemistry, and molecular biology for                labeling of DNA, RNA, proteins and enzymes;
in immunofluorescent detection;
in counterstain of DIG-labeled oligonucleotide                probes and Anti-DIG Fab-fragments;
in single and multiple flow cytometry                applications;
in fluorochrome stains for epifluorescence                microscopy;
for a quick check of biocontamination in                health food, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, pesticide,                and chemical industries;
for rapid estimations of biocontaminants in                laboratory cultures;
for a rapid check of biopollutants under field                conditions;
as a competitive inhibitor of                cholinesterases;
in antimicrobial compositions;
as a biosurfactant in toiletry                compositions;
as a natural colorant;
as a bioactive composition of the dye in the                ratio of 1: 20000000 in ultra pure water to obtain                fluorescence of eight colors at eight different                wavelengths and a phase contrast effect under                transmitted light;
for various fluorescent applications to be                performed in areas of sub zero temperatures;
as a base to make derivatives of the dye for                new fluorescent probes;
for molecular reagents;
for making conjugates for molecular                applications;
to obtain a phase contrast and histochemical                counterstain effect for different biochemical                constituents of cells under transmitted light;                and
in all applications of Phycobiliproteins (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A multiple fluorescent dye compound (A) of                formula (I) or (II), having empirical formula C 22H                48O 66N 2S 10Si 7and molecular weight of 1915, is                new.
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for                extraction of (A) from Holothuria                Scabrasea-cucumber.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Compound: (A) comprises a                  1-hydroxy 2,5-di-methylaminobenzene (HDAB)                  (fluorophore of molecular weight 180) of formula                  (III). The organic composition of the pure (A) by                  elemental analysis shows (%) carbon (8.3572),                  hydrogen (1.739), nitrogen (0.9449), and sulfur                  (9.457). The atomic ratio of                  carbon:hydrogen:nitrogen:sulfur is 22:48:2:10 as                  shown by microanalysis. The percentage of silicon                  dioxide is 12.58% as shown by the Atomic                  Absorption Spectrophotometry of its inorganic                  composition. (A) comprises silica as an integral                  part with an atomic ratio of 7 for each 22 carbon                  atom. (A) comprises sugar units. The FT-IR                  signals of sulfates occurring in the range of                  1210 - 1150 and 1060 - 1030 and 650 implies that                  sulfur is present as O-SO 2- type of linkage. The                  strong absorption band for silicate between 1090                  - 1020 (at 1068) implies that silicon is present                  as -Si-O-Si. The CH 3stretching signal is found                  between 2950 - 2850. There is no amide signal and                  (A) is not a protein. The strong and broad                  hydroxy stretch signal implies the phenolic                  group. (A) contains the phenolic group in its                  fluorophore part. (A) also comprises a sterically                  protected quinonoid ring. The fluorophore part is                  connected to Si-O group through the sulfated                  sugar moiety. The phenolic group gives Keto-enol                  tautomerism and thus gives rise to both quinone                  and phenolic types of structures. (A) is phenolic                  sulfated silicated polysaccharide (PSSP). The                  spacers form an integral part of the natural                  compound.The purification of the compound further by                  ion exchange chromatography shows absorbance at                  291 and 451 peaks with a stable peak ratio. The                  high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) of                  the pure ionic form of the compound by reverse                  phase C18 type of analytical column and a                  gradient of 0 - 50% acetonitrile to elute the                  pure dye from the column gives a retention time                  value of 1.909 and a very sharp peak. The                  compound is not decolorized by a reducing agent,                  is not synthetic, and has a crude extract of                  yellowish green color. The purified compound                  liquid dye is brownish with hues of green, yellow                  and red. The purified dried compound is reddish                  brown colored powder when seen with the naked eye                  in daylight, emits some hues of green under tube                  light, gives bluish green under mercury light,                  and fluorescence green color under X-rays. The                  compound is amorphous in nature, soluble in                  water, and insoluble in organic solvents                  including ethanol, methanol and acetone. The                  compound is negatively charged and has a pH of                  2.8. The compound comprises a quinonoid ring, is                  non-proteinaceous in nature, has a reducing                  sugar, and acts as a biosurfactant. The compound                  has antimicrobial qualities and when                  antimicrobial assay is performed, shows zone of                  inhibition. The compound emits fluorescence when                  excited with different wavelengths of X-rays, UV                  and visible spectral ranges on a                  spectrophotometer. The UV, visible spectroscopy                  is 250 - 700 nm and the peaks are marked at 291                  and 451 nm wavelengths. The fluorescent                  spectroscopic emission scanning is done by                  exciting the compound at 270, 340, 361, 400, and                  523 nm to obtain fluorescence peaks at 550, 460,                  490, 470, and 600 nm respectively. The physical                  checking of the dye in concentration of 1:2000000                  times dilution (i.e. at 5 &#215; 10                  -6concentration) under UV bulbs of 260 - 280 nm                  emits bluish green fluorescence. The                  epifluorescence microscopic checking of dye in                  concentration of at least 1:200000000 times                  dilution (i.e. at 5&#215;10 -8concentration)                  under different fluorescent cubes emits                  fluorescence.The compound emits eight different colored                  fluorescence at four different wavelengths of the                  UV and visible ranges of the fluorescent cubes of                  an epifluorescence microscope. The fluorescence                  blue with hues of Indigo color emission occurs in                  380 - 400 nm of UVA when the pure compound is                  excited under ultra violet cube WU - 330 - 385 nm                  excitation range. The fluorescence green color                  emission occurs at the 500 - 570 nm, when the                  pure compound is excited under WB cube of 450 -                  480 nm excitation range. The emission of                  fluorescence red with orange color hues occurs at                  570 - 650 nm, when the pure compound is excited                  under WG cube of 510 - 550 nm excitation range.                  The compound emits hues of bluish grays under the                  ordinary transmitted light bulb of the                  epifluorescence microscope, when seen under 10                  &#215;, 40 &#215;, and 100 &#215;                  objectives. The epifluorescence microscopic                  examination of egg cells of marine animals                  conjugated with the fluorescent compound in                  concentrations of at least 1:200000000 times                  dilution (i.e. at 5 &#215; 10                  -8concentration) under the different fluorescent                  cubes emits fluorescence in colors different from                  the pure compound. The cells labeled with the                  compound emit four different colored fluorescence                  at four different wavelengths of the UV and                  visible ranges of the fluorescent cubes and the                  transmitted light bulb of the epifluorescence                  microscope.The cells labeled with the compound emits                  blue color fluorescence, when excited in the                  range of 330 - 385 nm by the WU - fluorescence                  cube of the epifluorescence microscope. The cells                  labeled with the compound emit bright yellow                  fluorescence, when excited under WB cube of 450 -                  480 nm excitation range. The cells emit red color                  fluorescence, when excited under WG cube of 510 -                  550 nm excitation range. The fluorescence colors                  of the compound persists even after one year at                  room temperature. The fluorescence is highly                  photostable and does not get deteriorated by long                  exposures to direct light. The compound is not                  photobleached and is not quenched while screening                  slide under fluorescence microscope. The                  fluorescence of the compound does not change,                  when frozen at sub zero temperatures even after                  frozen in liquid nitrogen, a temperature at which                  the molecules are unable to attain the energy                  necessary for activation (e.g. in extracts from                  luminescent organisms). The compound is                  non-radioactive. The first natural                  organo-metallic compound has silicon matrix. The                  presence of silica in the compound is identified                  for the first time as an integral part of living                  organism. The compound comprises a longer                  wavelength, narrow bandwidth and small stokes                  shift as given in the specification. The emission                  spectra of the compound are insensitive to                  solvent polarity and pH. The compound has greater                  photostability, longer wavelength and at least                  one emission ranges in the visible spectrum. The                  compound has high water miscibility and                  facilitates easy mixing of additives required for                  cosmetic and drug compositions. The compound                  comprises eight excitation (ex)/eight emission                  (em) nm ranges covering spectra right from                  X-rays, and 270 - 745 nm of UV and visible ranges                  with high and sharp peaks. The compound has                  excitation and emission spectra in the                  fluorescent filter cube at 450 - 480 nm, which                  matches the spectral line of the Argon-ion Laser                  (&#8764; 488 nm) like the fluorescein. The                  cell conjugates emit bright yellow color                  fluorescence making the dye useful in multicolor                  applications. The compound is resistant to                  quenching and the fluorescence intensity                  increases after conjugation to proteins                  irrespective of dilution and concentration of the                  dye. The compound is stable at room temperature                  and at sub zero - 300 &#176;C with a long                  shelf life.The molecular and radioactive kits of the                  compound can be exported at room temperature. The                  microphotography of fluorescent emissions of the                  compound under fluorescence microscopy done by                  using Kodak 400 film with no other special film                  requirement has exposure time of 45 - 60 seconds.                  The compound produces counterstain effect of                  cells and cell components under all fluorescence                  on the cytogenetic slides where no specimen is                  present. The compound emits eight colors of                  fluorescence, when excited at eight wavelength                  ranges of X-rays, UV rays and visible spectral                  ranges even in the dilutions of 1:2000000 times                  in ultra pure water (5&#215;10 -8- 10                  -6concentration). The blue colored fluorescence                  of the dye is comparable to the emission of same                  color by DAPI fluorochrome at the same wavelength                  excitation. The yellow colored fluorescence of                  the dye in the visible range is comparable to the                  same colored emissions of Auramin and FITC. The                  orange colored fluorescent emission is comparable                  to the orange fluorescence color of Propidium                  Iodide fluorochrome, Rhodamine fluorochrome, and                  TRITC fluorochrome. The dye is also comparable to                  the emission of color by Hoechst 33258 and 33342                  fluorochrome. The compound does not undergo loss                  in fluorescence on freezing. The hues of bluish                  grays of the compound under bright field of                  fluorescent microscope when seen under                  10&#215; objective produce a phase contrast                  effect, which is useful in rapid screening of                  cytogentical, cytological, and histochemical                  slides and thus saves expenses on the extra phase                  contrast accessory component of microscope. The                  compound under 100&#215; oil immersion                  objective of an ordinary transmitted light                  microscope show different colors of staining in                  the hues of brownish yellow, yellow, and dark                  blue for the proteins of yolk, nucleoplasm and                  chromatin respectively of actively dividing                  cleavage cells which is useful in rapid bioassays                  of various histochemical components of the                  cells.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Organism: The marine organism is                  obtained from intertidal, submerged, shallow and                  deep waters, usually abundant in shaded areas                  (preferably cloves, crevices, ledges, lagoons,                  overhangings, rocky and sandy habitats); dull to                  bright colored with or without exo- and endo                  skeleton, sessile, sedentary drifters, nektonic                  with varied swimming power usually nocturnal in                  habit, liable to active predation, with and                  without luminescent and fluorescent pigments                  giving emissions in few to all wavelength ranges                  of X-rays, UVB, UVA, visible colored spectrums                  and infra red spectrum.Isolation: Extracting (A) from H. Scabra,                  comprises:collecting the animals from the shores                  during a low tide and maintaining in glass tanks                  containing seawater in the laboratory for                  taxonomic identification and further use;washing the animals thoroughly with Milli-Q                  water and anaesthetizing by chloroform/menthol in                  a closed jar;removing the viscera and the skin portion of                  the animals by peeling off by scraping with a                  scalpel for lyophilizing;taking the lyophilized skin with ultra pure                  water and keeping on a shaker for 4 hours,                  followed by filtration through Whattmann paper I                  and sintered glass filter;evaporating the filtrate and precipitating                  the compound using organic solvents;dissolving the precipitate in minimum volume                  of water and re-precipitating with an organic                  solvent to remove the salts;centrifuging to collect the residue and                  discarding the filtrate;drying the residue to obtain a dry                  powder;dissolving the dry powder in water and                  loading to ion-exchange column;eluting the column with water;lyophilizing the water eluted                  fractions;loading the lyophilized material on DEAE                  cellulose column and eluting with phosphate                  buffer; anddesalting repeatedly the phosphate buffer                  eluted fraction using PD10 column to obtain                  (A).
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Dermatological.
   No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

TI Patch for detecting cancer e.g. melanoma comprises            carrier layer of aqueous solution having probe with            peptide substrate of proteolytic enzyme whose activity            indicate cancer and semipermeable surface permeable to            probe and cleavage product.
AU ROZGA J
   NEUMAN T
AE ARBIOS TECHNOLOGIES INC (ARBI-Non-standard)
   CEMINES INC (CEMI-Non-standard)
   ROZGA J (ROZG-Individual)
   NEUMAN T (NEUM-Individual)
   CEMINES INC (CEMI-Non-standard)
   ARBIOS TECHNOLOGIES INC (ARBI-Non-standard)
   CEMINES INC (CEMI-Non-standard)
   ARBIOS TECHNOLOGY INC (ARBI-Non-standard)
   ARBIOS TECHNOLOGIES INC (ARBI-Non-standard)
   ROZGA J (ROZG-Individual)
   NEUMAN T (NEUM-Individual)
GA 2005306256
AB    NOVELTY - A patch (I) comprises a carrier layer                (a).
   USE - For detecting cancers such as skin cancers                e.g. melanoma in a tissue of mammalian subject                (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The patch provides rapid and non-invasive                detection and diagnosis of cancers.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A patch (I) for detecting cancer comprises a                carrier layer (a). (a) Comprises an aqueous                solution (b) containing a first probe that contains                a peptide substrate of first proteolytic enzyme of                interest; and a semipermeable surface (c) permeable                to first probe and first cleavage product. The                first proteolytic enzyme is an extracellularly                secreted enzyme, the activity of which is                indicative of cancer, where after cleavage of the                peptide substrate by the first proteolytic enzyme a                detectable first cleavage product is formed. The                semipermeable surface is contacted with externally                accessible tissue surface such that the first probe                and the first cleavage product can diffuse through                the semipermeable surface of the carrier                layer.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for detecting                cancer in a tissue of mammalian subject involving:                topically applying (I) to externally accessible                surface of the tissue; allowing the first probe                and/or the second probe to diffuse into the tissue                such that if the first proteolytic enzyme and/or                the second proteolytic enzyme is present in the                tissue, the first probe binds to the first                proteolytic enzyme, the second probe binds to                second proteolytic enzyme resulting in enzymatic                cleavage of the peptide substrate, thereby forming                the first cleavage product and/or second cleavage                product; and then detecting the presence or absence                of the first cleavage product and/or second                cleavage product by applying detection device,                where proteolytic activity is indicative of                cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The peptide substrate                  is oligopeptide substrate analog of the two                  proteolytic enzymes. The cleavage product is                  detectable by interaction with a specific                  antibody, aptamer or nanoparticle. AB    NOVELTY - System for disease detection comprises: one or                more machine learning-based (ML-based)                disease-detection models (218) trained on a dataset                of detection events, where the models are operable                to: receive a first sensor data associated with a                first set of detection animals that have been                exposed to a biological sample of a patient;                calculate a first confidence score corresponding to                a disease category associated with the biological                sample; responsive to the first confidence score                being greater than a first threshold score, receive                a second sensor data associated with a second set                of detection animals that have been exposed to the                biological sample of the patient; and calculate one                or more second confidence scores corresponding to                one or more disease states in the disease category                associated with the biological sample.
   USE - The system is used for detecting disease                including cancer, liver disease, gastrointestinal                disease, neurological disease, metabolic disease,                vascular disease and infectious disease, where the                cancer includes breast cancer, lung cancer,                prostate cancer, brain cancer, bladder cancer,                ovarian cancer, skin cancer, colorectal cancer,                kidney cancer, lower urinary tract cancer, a                carcinoid, pancreatic cancer, cervical cancer,                endometrial cancer, vulvar cancer, stomach cancer,                oropharyngeal cancer, appendicular cancer,                mesothelioma cancer, thymoma cancer and thyroid                cancer, and for determining a progression of a                disease in a patient undergoing a treatment, and                for training a detection animal to provide a                conditioned response to be used with a machine                learning-based (ML-based) disease-detection system                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The system allows for medical diagnostic and                screen tests which have high sensitivity, are                non-invasive, non-expensive, efficient, and capable                of detecting many different diseases.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - System for disease detection comprises: one or                more machine learning-based (ML-based)                disease-detection models trained on a dataset of                detection events, where the models are operable to:                receive a first sensor data associated with a first                set of detection animals that have been exposed to                a biological sample of a patient; calculate, based                on the first sensor data, a first confidence score                corresponding to a disease category associated with                the biological sample, where the disease category                comprises disease states, and the first confidence                score indicates a likelihood of at least one of the                disease states of the disease category being                present in the patient; responsive to the first                confidence score being greater than a first                threshold score, receive a second sensor data                associated with a second set of detection animals                that have been exposed to the biological sample of                the patient; and calculate, based on the second                sensor data, one or more second confidence scores                corresponding to one or more disease states in the                disease category associated with the biological                sample, where each confidence score indicates a                likelihood of a respective disease state in the                disease category being present in the patient.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method (a) of disease detection comprising                (i) receiving a test kit, where the test kit                comprises a biological sample from a patient,                exposing the biological sample to a first set of                detection animals, (ii) accessing a first sensor                data associated with the first set detection                animals, (iii) processing, using a first ML-based                disease-detection model trained on a first dataset                of detection events, the first sensor data to                calculate a first confidence score corresponding to                a disease category associated with the biological                sample, where the disease category comprises                disease states, (iv) responsive to the first                confidence score being greater than a first                threshold score, exposing the biological sample to                a second set of detection animals, (v) accessing a                second sensor data associated with the second set                of detection animals, and (vi) processing, using a                second ML-based disease-detection model trained on                a second dataset of detection events, the second                sensor data to calculate one or more second                confidence scores corresponding to one or more                disease states in the disease category associated                with the biological sample;
   a method (b) for determining a progression of                a disease in a patient undergoing a treatment                comprising (ia) accessing patient data indicating                the patient previously tested positive for a first                disease state in a disease category and has                subsequently received treatment for the disease,                (iia) receiving a new test kit at a time after the                patient has received the treatment for the disease,                where the new test kit comprises a new biological                sample from the patient, (iiia) exposing the new                biological sample to a set of detection animals,                (iva) identifying the new biological sample as                being associated with a second disease state,                comparing the second disease state with the first                disease state, and (va) determining the progression                of the disease in the patient after the treatment                based on the comparing; and
   a method (c) for training a detection animal                to provide a conditioned response to be used with a                machine learning-based (ML-based) disease-detection                system comprising exposing a detection animal to a                first biological sample from a subject having a                target disease state, training the detection animal                to provide the conditioned response by providing                the detection animal with a reward for identifying                the target disease state, inputting, to the                disease-detection system, a first sensor data                corresponding to the detection animal, where the                first sensor data is associated with presence of                the target disease state, storing tangibly, in a                memory of a computer processor, the first sensor                data to obtain a dataset of detection events, and                training the ML-based disease-detection system to                detect the disease state based on the dataset of                detection events.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of the                disease-detection method.

The new                  biological sample comprises breath, saliva,                  urine, stool, skin emanations, tissue and/or                  blood, and the prior biological sample comprises                  breath, saliva, urine, stool, skin emanations,                  tissue and/or blood.    TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The system further                  comprises one or more breath sensors; and the                  models are further operable to detect volatile                  organic compounds (VOCs) in the biological sample                  from the one or more breath sensors, where                  presence of the VOCs validates the biological                  sample as containing biological material from the                  patient. The first sensor data comprises data                  associated with a conditioned response of the                  first set of detection animals and the second                  sensor data comprises data associated with a                  conditioned response of the second set of                  detection animals. The first sensor data and the                  second sensor data comprise data received from                  one or more of: one or more behavioral sensors,                  one or more physiological sensors, or one or more                  environmental sensors. The behavioral sensors of                  the detection animal comprises one or more of: a                  face gesture of the detection animal, tail                  movements of the detection animal, landmarks on a                  skeleton model of the detection animal, a                  duration of a sniff from the detection animal, a                  sniff intensity, a number of repeated sniffs, a                  pose of the detection animal, whether the                  detection animal looks at its handler, a pressure                  of a nose of the detection animal against a                  sampling port, or auditory features of the sniff.                  The physiological sensors comprises one or more                  heart rate sensors, one or more heart rate                  variability sensors, one or more temperature                  sensors, one or more breath rate sensors, one or                  more sweat rate sensors, one or more blood                  pressure sensors, one or more skin temperature                  sensors, one or more pupil size variability                  sensors, one or more salivary cortisol sensors,                  one or more galvanic skin response (GSR) sensors,                  one or more electroencephalogram (EEG) sensors,                  one or more functional near-infrared spectroscopy                  (fNIR) sensors, one or more functional magnetic                  resonance imaging (fMRI) scanners, one or more                  electromyography imaging (EMG) scanners, and/or                  one or more magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)                  scanners. The environmental sensors comprise one                  or more temperature sensors, one or more humidity                  sensors, one or more audio sensors, one or more                  gas sensors, or one or more air particulate                  sensors. The first set of detection animals is                  conditioned to detect the disease category of the                  biological sample, and the second set of                  detection animals is conditioned to detect the                  disease state of the biological sample. The                  breath sensors comprises: Total volatile organic                  compounds (TVOC) sensor, breath VOC sensor,                  relative humidity sensors, temperature sensor,                  photoionization detector (PID), flame ionization                  detector (FID), and metal oxide (MOX) sensor. The                  models are further operable to: receive a third                  sensor data associated with the first set of                  detection animals or the second set of detection                  animals that have been exposed to one or more of                  a service sample, and calculate, based on the                  third sensor data, one or more confidence scores,                  each corresponding to a positive control category                  or a negative control category. The first and                  second sets of detection animals are exposed to                  each of the biological sample and the service                  sample via a sampling port. The sampling port is                  fluidly connected to one or more receptacles of                  receptacles, each receptacle operable to hold the                  biological sample or the service sample. The                  models are further operable to determine which of                  a particular sample to expose to the first set of                  detection animals or the second set of detection                  animals, where the particular sample comprise the                  biological sample from the patient and the                  service sample. The models are further operable                  to: identify the biological sample as associated                  with at least one of the disease states of the                  disease category when the first confidence score                  is equal to or greater than a threshold value; or                  identify the biological sample as not associated                  with at least one of the disease states of the                  disease category when the first confidence score                  is less than the threshold value. The models are                  further operable to: identify the biological                  sample as associated with the respective disease                  state in the disease category when the second                  confidence score is equal to or greater than a                  threshold value; or identify the biological                  sample as not associated with the respective                  disease state in the disease category when the                  second confidence score is less than the                  threshold value. Preferred Method: The method                  further comprises: receiving a third sensor data                  associated with the first set of detection                  animals or the second set of detection animals                  that have been exposed to one or more of a                  service sample; and calculating, based on the                  third sensor data, one or more confidence scores,                  each corresponding to a positive control category                  or a negative control category. The method                  further comprises determining which of a                  particular sample to expose to the first set of                  detection animals or the second set of detection                  animals. The method further comprises:                  identifying the biological sample as associated                  with at least one of the disease states of the                  disease category when the first confidence score                  is equal to or greater than a threshold value; or                  identifying the biological sample as not                  associated with at least one of the disease                  states of the disease category when the first                  confidence score is less than the threshold                  value. The method further comprises: identifying                  the biological sample as associated with the                  respective disease state in the disease category                  when the second confidence score is equal to or                  greater than a threshold value; or identifying                  the biological sample as not associated with the                  respective disease state in the disease category                  when the second confidence score is less than the                  threshold value. The method comprises receiving a                  test kit, accessing a first sensor data                  associated with each detection animal in the                  first set of detection animals, processing, using                  a first ML-based disease-detection model trained                  on a first dataset of detection events, the first                  sensor data associated with each detection animal                  in the first set of detection animals to                  determine whether the detection animal in the                  first set of detection animals indicate a disease                  category to present in the biological sample; in                  response to a determination that less than a                  first threshold percentage of the first set of                  detection animals indicate the disease category                  to be present in the biological sample,                  identifying the biological sample as not                  associated with the disease category; in response                  to a determination that between the first                  threshold percentage and a second threshold                  percentage of the first set of detection animals                  indicate the disease category to be present; in                  the biological sample, exposing the biological                  sample to a subset of detection animals from the                  second set of detection animals; where in                  response to a determination that less than a                  threshold fraction of the subset indicated a                  disease state to be present in the biological                  sample, identifying the biological sample as not                  associated with the disease category, and in                  response to a determination that greater than the                  threshold fraction of the subset indicated the                  disease state to be present in the biological                  sample, identifying the biological sample as                  requiring exposure to the second set of detection                  animals, and in response to a determination that                  greater than the second threshold percentage of                  the first set of detection animals indicate the                  disease category to be present in the biological                  sample, identifying the biological sample as                  requiring exposure to the second set of detection                  animals. The method further comprises: exposing                  the biological sample to a second set of                  detection animals; accessing a second sensor data                  associated with each detection animal in the                  second set of detection animals, processing,                  using a second ML-based disease-detection model                  trained on a second dataset of detection events,                  the second sensor data associated with each                  detection animal in the second set of detection                  animals to determine whether the detection animal                  in the second set of detection animals indicate                  the disease state to present in the biological                  sample; in response to a determination that less                  than a third threshold percentage of the second                  set of detection animals indicate the disease                  state to be present in the biological sample,                  identifying the biological sample as not                  associated with the disease state; and in                  response to a determination that greater than the                  third threshold percentage of the second set of                  detection animals indicate the disease state to                  be present in the biological sample, identifying                  the biological sample as associated with the                  disease state. The method (b) further comprises                  accessing a second sensor data associated with                  the set of detection animals; and processing,                  using a first ML-based disease-detection model                  trained on a first dataset of detection events,                  the second sensor data to calculate a second                  confidence score corresponding to the second                  disease state associated with the new biological                  sample. The method (b) further comprises, prior                  to accessing the patient data: receiving a prior                  test kit, where the prior test kit comprises a                  prior biological sample from the patient;                  exposing the prior biological sample to a set of                  detection animals; accessing a first sensor data                  associated with the set of detection animals;                  processing, using a first ML-based                  disease-detection model trained on a first                  dataset of detection events, the first sensor                  data to calculate a first confidence score                  corresponding to the first disease state                  associated with the prior biological sample; and                  identify the biological sample as associated with                  the first disease state when the first confidence                  score is equal to or greater than a threshold                  value. The prior biological sample and the new                  biological sample are of a same sample type. The                  conditioned response comprises a body pose of the                  detection animal. The method (c) further                  comprises repeating each of the steps until a                  threshold sensitivity is reached by the detection                  animal. The method (c) further comprises                  repeating each of the steps until a threshold                  specificity is reached by the detection animal.                  Preferred Properties: The respective disease                  state is identified with a sensitivity of at                  least approximately 90%. The respective disease                  state is identified with a specificity of at                  least approximately 94%.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION -                 2-{(E)-3-[3,3-Dimethyl-1,3-dihydro-indol-(2E)-ylidene]-propenyl}-3,3-dimethyl-3H-indole                derivatives of formula (I) and their salts are                new.
   R1, R2=-CO-NH-Y1;
   Y1=linear or branched alkyl, cycloalkyl or                heterocyclyl, substituted by at least two OH;
   R3=linear or branched alkyl substituted by -NH                2 , -SO 3 H, -COOH or -CONH 2 ;
   R4=linear or branched bivalent alkyl;
   R5=-COO- or -CONH-;
   S1=spacer;
   T1=a targeting moiety;
   n=1-3; and
   m=0 or 1.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   diagnostic kit comprising (I) together with                additional adjuvants of it for implementing the                optical imaging; and
   an intermediate compound cyanine derivatives                of formula (II).
   R5'=-COOH, -CONH 2 , -COO-Pg or -CONH-Pg;                and
   Pg=protecting group.

   EXAMPLE - 4 mg Compound 4 was suspended in 3 ml dry                dimethylformamide under nitrogen flow. 0.8                &#956; l N-methylmorpholine and 2.3 mg                N,N,N',N'-tetramethyl-O-(N-succinimidyl)uronium                tetrafluoroborate were added and the solution was                stirred for 20 hours. The desired product was                precipitated by addition of cold diethyl ether,                centrifuged and washed twice with diethyl ether.                The solid was dissolved in a solution of 3 mg                cyclic pentapeptide in 2 ml borate buffer at pH 9.                The solution was stirred overnight, then the pH was                adjusted to 6 with 1N hydrochloric acid and the                crude was purified to give                4-(2-((1E,3E,5E,7E)-7-(1-(6-(4-((2S,5S,11S,14R)-14-benzyl-11-(carboxymethyl)-5-(3-guanidinopropyl)-3,6,9,12,15-pentaoxo-1,4,7,10,13-pentaazacyclopentadecan-2-yl)butylamino)-6-oxohexyl)-3,3-dimethyl-5-(2,3,4,5,6-pentahydroxyhexylcarbamoyl)indolin-2-ylidene)hepta-1,3,5-trienyl)-3,3-dimethyl-5-(2,3,4,5,6-pentahydroxyhexylcarbamoyl)-3H-indolium-1-yl)butane-2-sulfonate.
