TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The Plasmodium strain is                  FCR3 strain or 3D7 strain. The expression vector                  is pGEX series of plasmids. The pGEX series                  plasmid is pGEX-4T2. The C-terminal of the                  pGEX-4T2 plasmid is fused to express a protease                  recognition site and a tag protein. The                  expression competent cells are E. coli cells. The                  screening is double-antibody screening. The                  double-antibody comprises ampicillin and/or                  streptomycin. The inducer is                  isopropylthiogalactopyranoside. The purification                  of recombinant protein comprises (a)                  disintegrating the bacterial liquid obtained                  after resuspending the competent cells expressing                  the VAR2CSA recombinant protein; (b) centrifuging                  the crushed bacterial liquid; (c) filtering the                  centrifuged supernatant, adding the supernatant                  to a chromatographic column capable of combining                  the C-terminal tag protein balanced by the                  re-suspension buffer solution for incubation; (d)                  washing by washing buffer solution, eluting the                  VAR2CSA recombinant protein by eluting buffer                  solution; (e) adding the eluted protein product                  to the GST affinity chromatography medium                  balanced by the buffer solution to fully combine;                  (f) washing with buffer solution, replacing into                  protease cutting buffer solution, and digesting                  overnight; and (g) passing the collected and                  digested product through a chromatographic column                  capable of combining the Cend tag protein again,                  collecting the protein eluent, performing buffer                  solution replacement or PBS dialysis by a                  desalting column, and finally performing protein                  concentration. In the step (a), the resuspension                  solution is added to resuspend the                  expression-competent cells. The resuspension                  comprises 10 mM disodium phosphate, 1.8 mM                  potassium dihydrogen phosphate, pH=7.4, 140 mM                  sodium chloride, 2.7 mM potassium chloride, 2.5                  mM &#946;-mercaptoethanol, 1 &#956;M                  DNase I, 1 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride, and                  protease inhibitor I. The resuspension solution                  is added according to the ratio of expression                  competent cells: resuspension solution: 1:5                  (g:ml). The mechanical crushing conditions are                  set at pressure of 800-1200 bar for 2-5 times.                  The centrifugation is carried out at 30000-50000                  g at 3-5&#8451; for 0.5-2 hours. In the step                  (c), the supernatant after centrifugation is                  filtered through a 0.45 &#956;m and/or 0.22                  &#956;m filter membrane. In the step (d), the                  washing buffer is a washing buffer with an                  imidazole concentration of 80-150 mM. In the step                  (d), the elution buffer is an elution buffer with                  an imidazole concentration of 300-700 mM. In the                  step (f), the enzyme is digested at                  3-5&#8451;. The steps (c)-(g) are performed                  at 2-8&#8451;.

AB    NOVELTY - Predicting the responsiveness of a cancer cell                to a mitogen-activated extracellular                signal-regulated kinase (MEK) or extracellular                regulated protein kinase (ERK) inhibitor comprises                detecting the presence of a mutation in the genes                selected from ADAM Metallopeptidase Domain 12                (ADAM12), Collagen, Type XIV, Alpha 1 (COL14A1),                Peroxisomal Biogenesis Factor 5-Like (PEX5L),                Tenascin N (TNN), and Tumor Protein P53 (TP53), in                the cancer cell, by contacting a nucleic acid                sample derived from the cancer cell with an                oligonucleotide which allows specific detection of                the mutation.
   USE - The methods are used for predicting the                responsiveness of a cancer cell to a MEK or ERK                inhibitor; and identifying a likely responder or a                likely non-responder to a MEK or ERK Inhibitor. The                oligonucleotide is used in the manufacture of a kit                for predicting the responsiveness of a cancer cell                or a cancer patient to a MEK inhibitor or a ERK                inhibitor, where the oligonucleotide is useful for                detecting the presence of a mutation in the genes                selected from ADAM12, COL14A1, INN, TP53, and PEX5L                (all claimed). The cancer is selected from, but not                limited to, bone cancer, pancreatic cancer, skin                cancer, cancer of the head or neck, cutaneous or                intraocular melanoma, uterine cancer, ovarian                cancer, rectal cancer, cancer of the anal region,                and stomach cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - An effective method of determining which                patients having mutations in MEK/ERK pathway will                resist to treatment of MEK or ERK inhibitors and                for incorporating such determination into effective                treatment is provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Predicting the responsiveness of a cancer cell                to a mitogen-activated extracellular                signal-regulated kinase (MEK) or extracellular                regulated protein kinase (ERK) inhibitor comprises                detecting the presence of a mutation in the genes                selected from ADAM Metallopeptidase Domain 12                (ADAM12), Collagen, Type XIV, Alpha 1 (COL14A1),                Peroxisomal Biogenesis Factor 5-Like (PEX5L),                Tenascin N (TNN), and Tumor Protein P53 (TP53), in                the cancer cell, by contacting a nucleic acid                sample derived from the cancer cell with an                oligonucleotide which allows specific detection of                the mutation; where presence of mutation in ADAM12,                COL14A1, PEX5L, TNN, TP53 and/or their combination                is indicative of decreased responsiveness of the                cancer cell to the MEK or ERK inhibitor.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   (1) a method of identifying a likely responder                or a likely non-responder to a MEK or ERK Inhibitor                by (a) detecting the presence of a mutation in the                genes selected from ADAM12, COL14A1, PEX5L, TNN,                and TP53, in a sample from the patient, by                contacting the sample with an oligonucleotide which                allows specific detection of the mutation; and (b)                identifying the patient as a likely non-responder                to the ERK inhibitor if a mutation in ADAM12,                COL14A1, PEX5L, TNN, TP53 and/or their combination                is detected in the sample; and
   (2) a kit comprising an oligonucleotide useful                for determining the presence of a mutation in the                genes selected from ADAM12, COL14A1, TNN, TP53,                Integrin, Beta (ITGB), and PEX5L.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - In the method for predicting the                  responsiveness of a cancer cell to a MEK or ERK                  inhibitor, the cancer cell is derived from a                  cancer patient. The                  detecting step comprises contacting the nucleic                  acid sample with the oligonucleotide which                  specifically hybridizes to the mutation of the                  gene to form a complex, and detecting the                  formation of the complex and thus determining the                  presence of the mutation in the gene. The method                  of identifying a likely responder or a likely                  non-responder to a MEK or ERK inhibitor further                  comprises recommending the patient who is                  identified as a likely non-responder not to be                  treated with a monotherapy of the MEK or ERK                  inhibitor, or not to be treated with a MEK or ERK                  inhibitor. The method further comprises                  recommending the patient who is identified as a                  likely non-responder to be treated with a                  different MEK or ERK inhibitor, or to be treated                  with a combined therapy of a different MEK or ERK                  inhibitor and an additional therapeutic agent of                  distinct mechanism. The method further comprises                  recommending the patient who is identified as a                  likely responder to be treated with the MEK or                  ERK inhibitor. The sample is a cancer cell or                  tissue derived from the patient. Preferred Kit:                  The oligonucleotide comprises a first                  oligonucleotide useful for determining the                  presence of a mutation in ADAM12, a second                  oligonucleotide useful for determining the                  presence of a mutation in COL14A1 or PEX5L, a                  third oligonucleotide useful for determining the                  presence of a mutation in TNN, a fourth                  oligonucleotide useful for determining the                  presence of a mutation in TP53, or their                  combination. The oligonucleotide comprises a pair                  of primer useful for amplifying a portion of the                  gene sequence, or comprises a probe useful for                  specifically hybridizing to the mutation of the                  gene to form a complex.

AE VELLORE INST TECHNOLOGY (VELR-C)
GA 2025C1850R
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a web-based user interface for                receiving dermoscopic images, and an image                preprocessing module for resizing input images to                224 by 224 pixels and normalizing pixel values to a                range of 0,1. A dense net-201 convolutional neural                network is trained to classify the images with an                accuracy of 85 percentage and ROC-AUC of 0.85. A                dual explainability module comprises a local                interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME)                component to generate superpixel-based explanations                with feature importance weights ranging from minus                0.02 to plus 0.2. A Gradient-weighted Class                Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) component generates                class activation heatmaps using gradients from                final convolutional layer feature maps, where the                system generates synchronized visualization outputs                comprising malignancy probability scores and                interpretable explanations within 2.0 seconds of                image upload.
   USE - System for performing automated melanoma skin                cancer detection.
   ADVANTAGE - The system provides a comprehensive diagnostic                platform that combines dense net-201 convolutional                neural network architecture with local                interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME)                and Grad-CAM to deliver both high diagnostic                accuracy and transparent, interpretable predictions                for clinical melanoma detection from dermoscopic                images. The system provides a dermoscopic image                classifier with integrated dual explainability that                operates within a browser-based interface. The                system synchronizes gradient-based and                local-perturbation explanations, so that overlays                are pixel-aligned on the same preprocessed image.                The system achieves near-real-time inference with                per-image latency under two seconds while                preserving accuracy. The system normalizes inputs                to a fixed spatial resolution and luminance scale                to stabilize clinical outputs. The system exposes                numeric malignancy probability and a concise                textual rationale alongside the overlays to aid                decisions. The system logs predictions and                explanation metadata for auditability and quality                management. The system supports bias inspection by                flagging saliency outside lesion regions to prompt                review. The system enables secure upload and                display using encryption and role-based access. The                system permits transfer-learning fine-tuning of a                dense convolutional network on curated dermoscopic                datasets. The system provides configurable                thresholds and report templates compatible with                clinical documentation.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for automated melanoma detection.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a functional block diagram                illustrating an end-to-end process flow for                ingestion, preprocessing, inference, and generation                of complementary explanations.

AB    NOVELTY - Treating cancer comprises determining the                ratio of leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptors                (LILRB2) to interferone (IFN)&#947; in a sample                and administering LILRB2 antibody and programmed                cell death protein 1 (PD1) antagonist if elevated                LILRB2 relative to IFN-&#947; is                detected.
   USE - The method is useful for treating cancer                including gastric cancer, melanoma (e.g., skin                cutaneous melanoma), urothelial cancer, lymphoid                neoplasm, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL),                testicular germ cell tumors (TGCT), mesothelioma,                kidney cancer (e.g., kidney renal clear cell                carcinoma, kidney renal papillary cell carcinoma,                or renal cell carcinoma (RCC)), sarcoma, lung                cancer (e.g., lung adenocarcinoma, lung squamous                cell carcinoma, and non-small cell lung cancer                (NSCLC)) stomach adenocarcinoma, pancreatic                adenocarcinoma, head and neck squamous cell                carcinoma, ovarian serious cystadenocarcinoma,                liver hepatocellular carcinoma, skin cutaneous                melanoma, colon adenocarcinoma, breast cancer                (e.g., breast invasive carcinoma or triple negative                breast cancer), rectum adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma                multiforme, uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma,                thymoma, bladder cancer, endometrial cancer,                Hodgkin's lymphoma, ovarian cancer, anal cancer,                biliary cancer, colorectal cancer, and esophageal                cancer, preferably gastric cancer, melanoma, or                urothelial cancer (all claimed). No biological data                given.

AB    NOVELTY - Single domain antibody or antigen-binding                fragment capable of specifically binding to 4-1BB,                comprising: (a) CDR1 having a sequence (SEQ ID NO:                43), as given in the specification, or a sequence                having substitution, deletion or addition of at                least one amino acid to (SEQ ID NO: 43), as given                in the specification; (b) CDR2 having a sequence                (SEQ ID NO: 44), as given in the specification, or                a sequence having substitution, deletion or                addition of at least one amino acid to (SEQ ID NO:                44); and (c) CDR3 having a sequence (SEQ ID NO:                45), as given in the specification is new.    USE - The antibody or antigen-binding fragment,                polypeptide construct or conjugate is useful: in                the preparation of detection reagents for detecting                the presence of 4-1BB in the sample (tumor cells)                or its level from a subject e.g. human or monkey;                and preparing medicine for treating tumor                overexpressing HER2 including breast cancer, colon                cancer, gastric cancer, lung cancer (e.g., lung                squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer,                non-small cell lung cancer and lung                adenocarcinoma), peritoneal cancer, skin cancer,                squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma of the skin or                eyeball, rectal cancer, cancer near the anus,                esophageal cancer, small bowel tumors, endocrine                gland cancer, parathyroid cancer, adrenal gland                cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, urinary tract cancer,                chronic or acute leukemia, lymphocytic lymphoma,                liver cancer , gastrointestinal cancer, pancreatic                cancer, glioblastoma, cervical cancer, ovarian                cancer, liver cancer, bladder cancer,                hepatocellular adenoma, colorectal cancer,                endometrial or uterine cancer, salivary gland                tumors, kidney cancer, cervical cancer, prostate                cancer, vulva cancer, thyroid cancer, head and neck                cancer, brain cancer, bile duct cancer and gall                bladder cancer (all claimed).

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The tumor specific                  targeting polypeptide is AP2H polypeptide, which                  encodes amino acids that are                  Ile-His-Gly-His-His-Ile-Ile-Ser-Val-Gly. The Fmoc                  protecting group of AP2H polypeptide sequence is                  removed, AP2H from resin is cracked by using                  cracking liquid to obtain product. The PLGA is                  dissolved in hexafluoroisopropanol to obtain PLGA                  solution, in electrostatic spinning process,                  silicon sheet is placed in centre of aluminum                  cover receiver, PLGA solution is injected by                  injection pump. The distance and voltage between                  tip end of needle head and receiver is set, after                  spinning for 60 minutes, PLGA nanometre fiber is                  set on surface of silicon sheet, vacuum drying is                  carried out on obtained PLGA nano fiber at room                  temperature to obtain substrate material silicon                  (Si)-PLGA-NF. The PLGA nanometre fiber Si-PLGA-NF                  is placed in six-hole plate. The 0.5 M                  1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide                  (EDC) and 0.05 M N-hdroxysuccinimide (NHS) are                  added for activating reaction to obtain carboxyl                  activated Si-PLGA-NF, in phosphate buffer                  solution, carboxyl-activated Si-PLGA-NF, 1 mg/mL                  cysteamine, 0.45 mg/mL SPDP, 0.5 mg/mL AP2H                  polypeptide are added in coupling reaction to                  obtain polypeptide functionalized micro-nano                  interface material Si-PLGA-NF-AP2H.Preferred Conditions: The fiber diameter is                  100-1500 nm. The disulfide bond of connecting                  polypeptide and nano fiber is represented by                  formula (I). The concentration of PLGA is 3-15                  wt.%. The injection pump flow rate is 0.1-0.5                  mL/hour. The distance between needle tip end and                  receiver is 15 mm, voltage is 10 kV.R1, R2=1-5C alkyl of straight-chain alkane                  or (CH2)2.Preferred Compositions: The cracking liquid                  comprises 95 vol.% trifluoroacetic acid, 2.5                  vol.% water and 2.5 vol.%                  triisopropylsilane.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) a                detection device for detecting material properties                of breast tissue; (2) a portable piezoelectric                detection system.

   FLAGSHIP PIONEERING INNOVATIONS V INC (FLAG-C)
GA 202562951U
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting (M1) a cancer signature in a sample,                comprises (a) obtaining nucleic acids from a single                sample of less than 20 ml obtained from a subject,                (b) determining methylation statuses of many                cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites in the                nucleic acids, where the CpG sites comprise at                least a subset of CpG sites within many low                background regions (LBRs) identified for exhibiting                a maximum methylation frequency of at least one CpG                sites of 0-5% across non-cancer samples and/or a                minimum methylation frequency of the CpG sites of                5-30% across cancer samples, and (c) detecting                presence or absence of the cancer signature in the                sample according to the determined methylation                statuses of the CpG sites, where the detection of                presence or absence of the cancer signature in the                sample achieves at least 40% sensitivity at a given                specificity of at least 85%.
   USE - The method is useful for: detecting a cancer                signature in a sample; identifying a LBR (all                claimed); identifying genomic regions of low                background methylation; predicting presence or                absence of a cancer signature in a sample obtained                from a subject; analyzing methylation statuses of                the CpG sites of LBRs; screening and early                detection of a presence of a cancer signature in a                sample corresponding to an early stage or                preclinical stage cancer, where the cancer is e.g.                a carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, blastoma, leukemia,                seminoma, melanoma, teratoma, lymphoma,                neuroblastoma, glioma, rectal cancer, endometrial                cancer, kidney cancer, adrenal cancer, thyroid                cancer, blood cancer, skin cancer, cancer of the                brain, cervical cancer, intestinal cancer, liver                cancer, colon cancer, stomach cancer, intestine                cancer, head and neck cancer, gastrointestinal                cancer, lymph node cancer, esophagus cancer,                colorectal cancer, pancreas cancer, ear, nose and                throat cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer,                cancer of the uterus, ovarian cancer, lung cancer,                and their metastases; and identifying universal                cancer signatures and determining tumor content. No                biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: achieves at least 40% sensitivity                at a given specificity of at least 85% in detection                of presence or absence of the cancer signature in                the sample; utilizes LBRs that enables improved                detection of presence or absence of cancer                signatures while using smaller samples and fewer                consumable reagents; provides improved                predictability; and achieves at least one                performance metrics (including metrics of                sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive                value, and/or negative predictive value) when                predicting presence or absence of cancer in a                sample.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   detecting (M2) a cancer signature in a sample,                comprising obtaining nucleic acids from a sample                obtained from a subject, the step (b) as per se,                where the CpG sites comprises fewer than 500 CpG                sites comprising at least a subset of CpG sites                within the LBRs identified for exhibiting according                to either a maximum methylation frequency of the                CpG sites across non-cancer samples and/or a                minimum methylation frequency of the CpG sites                across cancer samples, and detecting presence or                absence of the cancer signature in the sample                according to the determined methylation statuses of                the CpG sites comprising fewer than 500 CpG sites,                where the detection of presence or absence of the                cancer signature in the sample according to the                determined methylation statuses of the CpG sites                comprising fewer than 500 CpG sites achieves at                least 40% sensitivity at a given specificity of at                least 85%; and
   identifying (M3) a LBR, comprising obtaining a                first set of methylation statuses of the CpG sites                of nucleic acids from a first many samples,                obtaining a second set of methylation statuses of                the CpG sites of nucleic acids from a second many                samples, determining the LBR comprising the CpG                sites that are differentially methylated between                the first and second sets of methylation statuses,                where the determination of the LBR is according to                one of a maximum methylation frequency of the CpG                sites of the first set of methylation statuses, a                minimum methylation frequency of the CpG sites of                the second set of methylation statuses, or a                threshold differential methylation frequency of the                CpG sites between the first set of methylation                statuses and the second set of methylation                statuses.

the step of determining methylation                  statuses of the CpG sites in the nucleic acids                  comprises performing at least one assays, where                  an assay comprises at least one of sequencing                  nucleic acids via targeted sequencing, whole                  genome sequencing, or whole genome bisulfite                  sequencing, a nucleic acid amplification assay, a                  target enrichment assay, and an assay that                  generates methylation information, the nucleic                  acid amplification assay is a PCR assay, and the                  PCR assay comprises a real-time PCR assay,                  quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) assay, digital                  PCR (dPCR) assay, allele-specific PCR assay, or                  reverse-transcription PCR assay; the                  step of performing the assays comprise obtaining                  bisulfite converted nucleic acids, and                  selectively amplifying target regions of the                  bisulfite converted nucleic acids, where the                  target regions comprise the CpG sites; and the                  step of performing the assays comprises providing                  at least one probes that bind to the subset of                  CpG sites within the LBRs, where the probe binds                  to 1-100 CpG sites within a LBR, at least 10                  probes bind to at least 1 CpG site and less than                  100 CpG sites of the LBRs, the probe binds to                  10-90% of CpG sites within a LBR, the probe binds                  to 20-80%, preferably 40-60% of CpG sites within                  a LBR, and the probe binds to every CpG site                  within a LBR. In the method (M3), the                  LBR and the additional LBRs are ranked according                  to: differential methylation frequencies of the                  CpG sites of the LBR and the CpG sites of each of                  the additional LBRs; their significance in                  distinguishing cancer and non-cancer samples; and                  an importance analysis conducted by performing a                  machine learning model, where the machine                  learning model is a random forest model.    USE - The chimeric protein, chimeric protein                construct, or recombinant cell is useful in                preparing medicine i.e. vaccine for preventing and                treating disease i.e. cancer (non-small cell lung                cancer, papillary thyroid carcinoma, glioblastoma                multiforme, colon cancer, rectal cancer, lung                cancer, head and neck cancer, kidney cancer,                bladder cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer,                liver cancer, bile duct cancer or sarcoma, acute                myeloid leukemia, large cell neuroendocrine                carcinoma, neuroblastoma, prostate cancer,                neuroblastoma, pancreatic cancer, melanoma, head                and neck squamous cell carcinoma, cervical cancer,                skin cancer, glioma, esophageal cancer, oral                squamous cell carcinoma or gastric cancer),                autoimmune disease (lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, or                psoriasis), infectious disease (hepatitis B,                HIV/AIDS, or hand-foot-mouth disease), metabolic                disease (diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia)                or neurological disease (Alzheimer's disease) and                in medicine screening (all claimed).

TI New antibody that recognizes an epitope of human            epidermal growth factor receptor 2 truncated form, used            as an agent for diagnosis and treatment or prevention            of cancers e.g. lung cancer, colon cancer, stomach            cancer or skin cancer.
AU ARRIBAS LOPEZ J
   PEDERSEN K
   ANGELLINI P
   PARRA PALAU J L
   BASELGA TORRES J
AE ICREA FUNDACIO PRIVADA INST CATALANA REC (ICRE-C)
   FUNDACIO PRIVADA INST INVESTIGACIO BIOME (PRIV-Non-standard)
   FUNDACIO PRIVADA INST CATALANA RECERCA (ICRE-C)
   FUNDACIO PRIVADA INST INVESTIGACIO ONCOL (PRIV-Non-standard)
   FUNDACIO PRIVADA INST INVESTIGACIO ONCOL (PRIV-Non-standard)
GA 2011K77070
AB    NOVELTY - An antibody (a1) or its fragment that                recognizes an epitope of human epidermal growth                factor receptor 2 (HER2) receptor truncated form,                is new. The antibody is capable of discriminating                between the truncated variant of HER2 CTF-611 and                CTF-616.
   USE - As an agent for diagnosis and treatment or                prevention of cancers, particularly lung, pancreas,                colon, stomach, prostate, head and neck, skin,                kidney, testicle, thyroids, urinary bladder,                uterus, vulva, endometrium, ovary, oesophagus,                mouth, salivary gland, larynx, peritoneum, nose and                throat region, Fallopian tubes, Wilms tumors, as                well as lymphomas, Swing sarcomas, synovial                sarcoma, medulloblastomas, trophoblastics tumors,                glyomas, glyoblastomas, cholangiocarcinomas,                cholesteatoma, chondrosarcoma, ependymoma,                neurilemmomas, neuromas, rhabdomyosarcomas in                mammals including humans (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The new antibody represents new and efficient                target for diagnosis and therapy of specific type                of cancers and makes it possible to treat it on                time with efficient therapies particularly for                treating tumors having worst prognosis and tumors                which are not treatable with the current therapies.                The presence of one of the truncated forms (CTF) of                HER2, generated by the alternative initiation of                translation, correlates very well with the                prediction of the type of cancer to be treated,                making easier the task of the physician at the                moment of prescribing a course of treatment. This                HER2 truncated form (CTF-611) is used to develop                several tools for detecting its presence in tissue                samples and preferably for distinguishing it from                p95-HER2 and full-length HER2, thus providing a new                and solid diagnosis set that is also applicable in                clinical routine. Anti-HER2 antibodies currently                available recognize CTFs and HER2 or only HER2,                making it very difficult to discriminate patients                expressing only HER2 from patients expressing HER2                and CTFs. In contrast to available anti-HER2                antibodies, the present antibodies preferentially                bind to CTF-611, allowing the identification of                patients expressing this CTF. The present                antibodies specifically detect CTF-611, and are                capable of distinguishing CTF-611 from CTF-616 and                preferably capable of distinguishing CTF-611 from                CTFs-613. The diagnostic method and the kit, allow                the prediction of nodal metastasis, poor prognosis,                and resistance to Herceptin(RTM: transtuzumab,                monoclonal antibody).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An antibody (a1) or its fragment that                recognizes an epitope of a HER2 receptor truncated                form is new. The epitope is defined by a peptide                containing 42 amino acid sequences as given in the                specification (SEQ ID NO: 2). The antibody is                capable of discriminating between the truncated                variant of HER2 CTF-611 represented by a peptide                containing 645 amino acid sequences as given in the                specification (SEQ ID NO: 1), and CTF-616                represented by a peptide containing 640 amino acid                sequences as given in the specification (SEQ ID NO:                7),. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a hybridoma producing the monoclonal antibody                (a1);
   a method for producing the antibody                (a1);
   cancer diagnosis (m2), involving detection of                the presence of the HER2 receptor truncated form                consisting of the amino acid sequence (SEQ ID NO:                1) in a patient sample, using at least one antibody                (a1);
   an agent (Aa) for diagnosis and determination                of prognosis in isolated samples of cancers of the                type that express the HER2 receptor or its                truncated variants, comprising at least one                antibody (a1) or its fragment; and
   a kit for diagnosis and determination of                prognosis in isolated samples of cancers of the                type that express the HER2 receptor or its                truncated variants, where the unit of detection                comprises at least one agent (Aa).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Antibodies (Claimed): The antibody is                  prepared by hybridoma method involving                  immunization with a peptide containing 32 amino                  acid sequences as given in the specification (SEQ                  ID NO: 3) or (SEQ ID NO:4), optionally conjugated                  with an immunogen. For obtaining a monoclonal                  antibody, the hybridoma cell line is grown in a                  suitable culture medium and the monoclonal                  antibody is recovered from this medium. The                  antibody (a1) or its fragment is produced by a                  hybridoma cell line deposited with the Deutsche                  Sammlung von Mikroorganismen und Zellen-DSMZ with                  accession number (DSM ACC3016) or hybridoma cell                  line deposited with accession number (DSM                  ACC3017). Preferred Components: The fragment is                  one selected from the group formed by F(ab),                  F(ab') and Fv. The epitope is a peptide                  corresponding to (SEQ ID NO: 3). The antibody                  (a1) is additionally capable of discriminating                  between the truncated variant of HER2 CTF-611                  represented by (SEQ ID NO:1) and CTF-613                  represented by a peptide containing 644 amino                  acid sequences as given in the specification (SEQ                  ID NO: 6). The antibody (a1) or its fragment is                  suitable to distinguish (SEQ ID NO:1) from (SEQ                  ID NO: 6) or HER2 receptor (preferably HER2                  receptor truncated form 648-CTF/p95). The                  distinction can be visualized by at least one of                  immunofluorescence, flow cytometry,                  immunohistochemistry in cultured cells, and                  immunohistochemistry in samples from patients.                  The antibody (a1) or its fragment is a polyclonal                  antibody or monoclonal antibody or its fragment.                  In the agent (Aa), the antibody (a1) or its                  fragment is arranged on a solid support.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (m2) is a                  prognostic method allowing the prognosis of                  progression of tumor growth and/or metastases.                  For the diagnosis and determination of prognosis                  in isolated samples of cancers the HER2 receptor                  is expressed.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details described no results                given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example is given.

AB    NOVELTY - The device (1) has a flexible structure (10)                that is filled with a viscous fluid. A support and                transfer platform (20) is connected to the flexible                structure to define an interior chamber (11) where                the viscous fluid is contained. A simulating unit                (30) is arranged for simulating a type of                detectable abnormal tissue within the container                flexible structure. A distributor element (40) of                distributing the fluid is provided directly on the                skin of the user coming from the chamber. A                transfer unit (50) is arranged on the platform to                allow the transfer of the fluid from the chamber                towards the distributor element.
   USE - Device for training and direct practice of                breast self-examination techniques for early                detection of breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The device is used for home use as an                accessory to perform a routine activity such as                showering, with simple technology without requiring                a learning process supervised by professionals or                specialized personnel. The device closely resembles                real organs such as female breasts, so that the                user identifies abnormal tissue with the product.                The device allows learning to identify abnormal                tissue during palpation training, so that the user                recognizes the presence of tumor or nodule and                differentiates from other tissues such as breast                cysts when the user performs in a real way.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                training kit to teach and learn breast                self-palpation techniques for early detection of                breast cancer.

TI Diagnosing leptomeningeal metastasis of cancer            comprises obtaining biological sample, and obtaining            blood gas, blood chemistry, or hematological            measurements in biological sample.
AU SMALLEY I
   SMALLEY K S M
   FORSYTH P A
AE MOFFITT CANCER CENT & RES INST INC H LEE (MOFF-C)
   MOFFITT CANCER CENT & RES INST INC H LEE (MOFF-C)
GA 202346951M
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) of a                cancer in a subject comprises: (a) obtaining a                biological sample; and (b) obtaining at least one                blood gas, blood chemistry, or hematological                measurements in the biological sample, where a                significant deviation of at least one measurements                relative to the same measurements from a                non-metastatic control indicates the presence of                LM.
   USE - The method is useful for: diagnosing LM of a                cancer in a subject, where the cancer comprises                melanoma, breast cancer, lung cancer, leukemia, or                lymphoma; treating LM in a subject (all claimed);                treating, inhibiting, reducing, decreasing,                ameliorating, and/or preventing LM of a cancer; and                treating lymphoma, B cell lymphoma, T cell                lymphoma, mycosis fungoides, Hodgkin's disease,                myeloid leukemia, bladder cancer, brain cancer,                nervous system cancer, head and neck cancer,                squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck, lung                cancers e.g. small cell lung cancer and non-small                cell lung cancer, neuroblastoma/glioblastoma,                ovarian cancer, skin cancer, liver cancer,                melanoma, squamous cell carcinomas of the mouth,                throat, larynx, and lung, cervical cancer, cervical                carcinoma, breast cancer, epithelial cancer, renal                cancer, genitourinary cancer, pulmonary cancer,                esophageal carcinoma, head and neck carcinoma,                large bowel cancer, hematopoietic cancers,                testicular cancer, colon cancer, rectal cancer,                prostatic cancer, or pancreatic cancer. Test                details are described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: provides earlier detection of LM,                which allows more time for therapeutic                interventions to work as well as be applied to a                patient in a better state of health; improves                survival and symptom control in patients with                leptomeningeal melanoma metastases from non-small                cell lung cancer, thus leading to median overall                survival of 3 months; and provides improved                identification sensitivity by 91.67%.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                treating LM in a subject comprising the steps                (a)-(b) as per se, and administering anticancer                therapy to the subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method (M1): the                  blood gas, blood chemistry, mass spectrometry, or                  hematological measurements comprise a measurement                  of at least two of chloride, total carbon                  dioxide, anion gap, ionized calcium, lactate,                  glucose, keto acid levels, amino acid levels,                  urea nitrogen (blood urea nitrogen (BUN))/urea,                  creatinine, hematocrit, hemoglobin, pH, partial                  pressure of carbon dioxide, partial pressure of                  oxygen, bicarbonate, base excess, and/or oxygen                  saturation, where the blood gas, blood chemistry,                  or hematological measurements comprise pH,                  partial pressure of oxygen, lactate, glucose,                  sodium, potassium, glutamine, keto acid levels,                  amino acid levels, and/or urea nitrogen; and a                  lower pH, higher partial pressure of oxygen,                  higher lactate, lower glucose, lower potassium,                  lower sodium, lower glutamine, and/or higher urea                  nitrogen indicates LM. In the methods (M1)-(M2),                  the blood gas, blood chemistry, or hematological                  measurements are obtained using a point-of-care                  body fluid analyzer. In the method (M2): the                  blood gas, blood chemistry, or hematological                  measurements comprise a measurement of at least                  one of chloride, total carbon dioxide, anion gap,                  ionized calcium, lactate, sodium, potassium,                  glutamine, glucose, urea nitrogen (BUN)/urea,                  keto acid levels, amino acid levels, creatinine,                  hematocrit, hemoglobin, pH, partial pressure of                  carbon dioxide, partial pressure of oxygen,                  bicarbonate, base excess, and/or oxygen                  saturation, where the blood gas, blood chemistry,                  or hematological measurements comprise pH,                  partial pressure of oxygen, lactate, glucose,                  sodium, potassium, glutamine, and/or urea                  nitrogen; and the anticancer therapy comprises                  radiation therapy, intrathecal chemotherapy, or                  immunotherapy. Preferred Components: In the                  methods (M1)-(M2): the biological sample                  comprises cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), blood, or                  plasma; the keto acid levels measured are                  3-methyl/4-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid and                  3-methyl-2-oxobutanoic acid; the blood gas, blood                  chemistry, or hematological measurements are on a                  cartridge for use with a body fluid analyzer; the                  point of care body fluid analyzer is an                  I-STAT(RTM: Portable handheld blood analyzer);                  and the blood gas, blood chemistry, or                  hematological measurements are on a CHEM8 or CG4                  cartridge.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of the therapy is by                intrathecal route. No dosage details given.

TI Peptide internalized by a tumor cell useful for            targeted delivery of anticancer drugs.
AU CLAYMAN G
   HONG F D
AE UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
   HONG F D (HONG-Individual)
   CLAYMAN G (CLAY-Individual)
   UNIV TEXAS SYSTEM (TEXA-C)
GA 2002195737
AB    NOVELTY - A peptide that targets a tumor cell, where the                peptide is internalized by the tumor cell, is                new.
   USE - For killing a tumor cell, in the cancers such                as human head and neck cancer (e.g. an oral cavity                cell, a pharynx cell, a throat cell, a paranasal                sinus cell, a nasal cavity cell, a larynx cell, a                thyroid cell, a parathyroid cell, a salivary gland                cell, a skin cell of the face, a skin cell of the                neck, or a cervical lymph node cell), squamous cell                carcinoma, and a solid tumor (e.g. breast cancer                cell) (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The peptide provides the necessary dose of a                drug specifically to the tumors, thus does not                produce harmful side effects to other cells. The                potential for the peptide as a shuttle for drug                delivery is further strengthened by the fact that                it is non-toxic, nonimmunogenic, stable in vivo,                protects its cargo during transit, and accumulates                sufficiently in a tumor or tumors within 48                hours.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a DNA segment encoding the peptide;
   a composition comprising a drug and the                peptide;
   method (M1) for detecting cancer or tumor in                vitro involving: i) conjugating a detectable label                to the peptide; ii) administering the conjugated                peptide and label to a patient or to the tumor                containing sample; and iii) detecting binding of                the conjugate to tumor cells by a detection                device;
   a tumor-detection or imaging kit containing in                a container, the pharmaceutical composition, and                optionally bound to the detectable label and/or                containing a detection device;
   a method (M2) for killing a tumor cell                involving administering to a patient a                radiotherapy, chemotherapy, surgery or gene therapy                and the composition containing an anti-tumor                compound conjugated to the peptide;
   a method (M3) for killing a tumor cell                involving administering to a patient a                chemotherapy, and a composition comprising a                liposome comprising an anti-tumor compound linked                to the peptide;
   a composition comprising the peptide, and a                vector comprising a composition for gene                therapy;
   a tumor-treating kit comprising the peptide                and the anti-tumor compound; and
   a method for the isolation of an internalizing                peptide involving individually contacting peptides                from a peptide library with members of a cell                population (preferably cancer cell); and assaying                for endocytosis of the peptides by said members of                the cell population.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Peptide: The peptide comprises the                  sequence Thr Ser Pro Leu Asn Ile His Asn Gly Gln                  Lys Leu.Preferred Components: The DNA segment                  comprises a nucleic acid that encodes (I). The                  DNA segment is further defined as a recombinant                  vector. The vector is a protein, peptide,                  liposome, lipid and/or nucleic acid. The                  composition for gene therapy further comprises a                  nucleic acid (preferably p53 nucleic acid).Preparation: The peptide was isolated from a                  random peptide-display library (preferably a M13                  single-stranded bacteriophage-based random                  peptide-display library).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Drug: The drug is a                  chemotherapeutic agent selected from a cytotoxic                  agent, an apoptopic agent, a DNA-damaging agent,                  or anti-tumor compound (preferably Taxol,                  cisplatin (CDDP), carboplatin, procarbazine,                  mechlorethamine, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide,                  melphalan, chlorambucil, bisulfan, nitrosurea,                  dactinomycin, daunorubicin, doxorubicin,                  bleomycin, plicomycin, mitomycin, etoposide                  (VP16), tamoxifen, transplatinum, 5-fluorouracil,                  vincristin, vinblastin, or methotrexate). The                  drug is conjugated to the peptide.Preferred Method: In (M1), the binding step                  further involves uptake by the tumor cells, and                  the detection is by magnetic resonance imaging,                  x-ray imaging, computerized emission tomography                  or positron emission tomography. The label is a                  radionucleotide, a radioactive isotope, a fluor                  or a spin label, detectable by a non-invasive                  device. In (M1) the radiotherapy is administered                  to the whole body, local or regional. The                  radiotherapy comprises radioisotopic irradiation,                  &#947;-, X-, or ultraviolet-ray irradiation,                  microwave irradiation, or electronic irradiation.                  The patient is administered 40 - 100 (preferably                  55 - 65, especially 62) Gy radiation. The gene                  therapy is directed to a nucleic acid sequence                  selected from ras, myc, raf, erb, src, fms, jun,                  trk, ret, gsp, hst, bcl abl, Rb, CFTR, p16, p21,                  p27, p53, p57, p73, C-CAM, APC, CTS-1, zac1, scFV                  ras, DCC, NF-1, NF-2, WT-1, MEN-I, MEN-II, BRCAI,                  VHL, MMAC1, FCC, MCC, BRCA2, IL-1, IL-2, IL-3,                  IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-9, IL-10, IL-11,                  IL-12, GM-CSF G-CSF and thymidine kinase.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   No supporting data provided.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Targeting of tumor cells.
   Nude mice harboring subcutaneously established                MDA177Tu-derived tumor xenografts were injected                intravenously with FITC-HN-1. Little labeling of                the nuclei was observed. The presence of intact                peptide was confirmed by electrophoretic analysis                of tumor extract and thus confirmed the                internalization of the peptides in the cell lines.                The untreated tumor cells did not                autofluoresce.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition is administered intravenously,                intratumorally, subcutaneously, intraperitoneally,                topically, locally, regionally, or                systemically.
   SPECIFIC PEPTIDES - The peptide of formula Thr Ser Pro Leu Asn                  Ile His Asn Gly Gln Lys Leu (I) is specifically                  claimed as (I).

TI Method used e.g. for assay of synuclein protein in            body fluid or tissue sample involves contacting sample            with lipids under conditions enabling binding of            synuclein to lipids; and detecting lipid-bound            synuclein by synuclein-binding agent.
AU SHARON R
AE YISSUM RES DEV CO HEBREW UNIV JERUSALEM (YISS-C)
   SHARON R (SHAR-Individual)
   YISSUM RES DEV CO HEBREW UNIV JERUSALEM (YISS-C)
GA 2014Q83102
AB    NOVELTY - Method for the assay of synucleins in a sample                involves contacting the sample with lipids under                conditions enabling binding of the synuclein to                lipids; and detecting the lipid-bound synuclein by                a synuclein-binding agent.
   USE - For the assay or detection of synucleins e.g.                alpha , beta and gamma synuclein (preferably alpha                -Synuclein protein ( alpha -Syn)) in a sample e.g.                cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), saliva, erythrocytes,                platelets, whole blood, serum, plasma, urine,                lymph, sputum, brain, skin, intestine, salivary                glands, tumor biopsy, extracts of cultured cells                and human or laboratory animal tissue (preferably                saliva); for the detection of synucleinopathy e.g.                Parkinson's disease (PD), PD with dementia (PDD),                Lewy bodies (LB) dementia, Alzheimer's disease,                multiple system atrophy, NIEMANN-PICK-type 1, and                neuro-degeneration with brain iron accumulation-1,                or cancer e.g. melanoma, other skin cancers and                cancers of the breast, prostate, colon, brain,                kidney and lung; for determining the severity of                specific synucleinopathy or cancer; for monitoring                the effect of anti-synucleinopathy therapy or                anti-cancer therapy (claimed); and for the                diagnosis of a disease.
   ADVANTAGE - The phospholipid-enzyme-linked immunosorbent                assay (ELISA) method is an accurate and sensitive                diagnostic tool for the disease. The highly                sensitive assay detects and measures alpha                -Synuclein protein ( alpha -Syn), even when present                at low levels. The use of membrane proteins in                ELISA to bind the synucleins that are present in                sample being tested, leads to at least two                advantages: i) the form of synuclein being assayed                is the functionally-relevant (and hence                pathogenically-relevant) form of protein; and ii)                epitope recognition by the antibodies used in ELISA                is enhanced following folding of proteins (possibly                by creation of new 3D binding sites), thus leading                to greatly-enhanced sensitivity, and reduced                minimal threshold detection values. The improved                ELISA method is based on the intrinsic property of                synucleins to bind membrane lipids. This property                is exploited in order to provide an assay for the                functional form of proteins, that is, the form in                which they have become folded into their secondary                and tertiary structures, including physiological                and pathogenic (toxic) forms of protein.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for kit for                measuring the concentration of synucleins in a                sample comprising lipids capable of binding the                synucleins and at least one anti-synuclein                antibody.

   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                particle formed by the derivatives (I).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preparation (Disclosed): Preparation of (I)                  comprises performing selective or full                  deprotection of ester compounds of formula                  (R2p-O-P(=O)(-O-R3p)-NH-CH2-C(O)-(CH2)2-C(O)O-R1)                  (III) to give deprotected ester compounds of                  formula                  (R2-O-P(=O)(-O-R3)-NH-CH2-C(O)-(CH2)2-C(O)O-R1)                  (IV) (representative of (I)).R2, R3 = 1-30C alkyl, 2-30C alkenyl, 2-30C                  alkynyl, alkoxy, aryl, heteroaryl, 3-8C                  cycloalkyl, heterocycloalkyl (all optionally                  substituted ), H or lipidic group, where R3 is                  preferably H and R2 is preferably optionally                  substituted phenyl, lipid group or                  squalene;R2p = R2 protected with protective group;                  andR3p = R3 protected with protective group,                  where the protective group is e.g. 1-30C alkyl,                  2-30C alkenyl, 2-30C alkynyl (all optionally                  substituted), H, methyl, ethyl, propyl,                  isopropyl, cyclohexyl, tert-butyl, 1-adamantyl,                  allyl, and 2-trimethylsilylprop-2-enyl.
   Preferred Definitions:
   L1 = -X12-CH(R4)-O-C(=X11)-;

   EXAMPLE - 407 mg Phenyl dichlorophosphate was dissolved                in 20 ml dry tetrahydrofuran and cooled to 0                degrees C on ice. 491 mg Hexyl                5-amino-4-oxopentanoate was added to the cooled                solution followed immediately by dropwise addition                of 600 ml dry triethylamine. The resulting                suspension was stirred at 0 degrees C for 1 hour                and then allowed to warm-up to ambient temperature.                After 2 hours at ambient temperature, the reaction                mixture was quenched with 5 g water and 650 ml                triethylamine. After 30 minutes, the solvents were                evaporated and the crude product extracted with                3330 ml ethyl acetate from 30 ml water. The organic                phase was washed with brine and dried with sodium                sulfate. The crude product was purified to give 542                mg triethylammonium salt of hexyl                5-((hydroxy(phenoxy)phosphoryl)amino)-4-oxopentanoate.

AB    NOVELTY - Method (A) for identifying a therapeutic                composition against cancer comprising at least one                cannabinoid involves (i) determining a therapeutic                efficacy of the composition comprising at least one                cannabinoid with a predetermined chemical profile,                and (ii) performing a computational analysis on the                therapeutic efficacy of the composition comprising                at least one cannabinoid with the predetermined                chemical profile.
   USE - The method (A) is useful for identifying                therapeutic composition against cancer comprising                cannabinoid. The therapeutic composition is useful                for treating condition or disease. The disease is                cancer chosen from lung cancer, colorectal cancer,                thyroid cancer, cervical cancer, breast cancer,                brain cancer, skin cancer, colon cancer and                leukemia. The skin cancer is a melanoma (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method describes dynamic interactions of                cannabinoid compounds with complex system of the                human body, taking into account all available data                at different levels ranging from holistic clinical                data to molecular studies of the interactions of                cannabinoids with their respective targets, and is                capable of quantifying and/or predicting with a                high probability the individual's response to                specific treatment.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   therapeutic composition against cancer                comprising at least one cannabinoid, being obtained                by the above-mentioned method (A);
   use of the therapeutic composition against                cancer comprising at least one cannabinoid, for                treating a condition or disease, where the                treatment targets the endocannabinoid system;
   an in vitro method (B) for performing                personalization of cannabis-based cancer therapy                involves (a) providing a patient sample, (b)                performing a multiomic analysis on patient sample,                where the multiomic analysis comprises detection,                preferably a quantification of the biological                marker, where the multiomic analysis comprises the                cell profiling, the gene expression analysis, the                cytokine expression profiling and/or the protein                phosphorylation analysis, (c) predicting the                patient's response to a therapeutic composition                comprising at least one cannabinoid, by comparing                the generated data to library data, where the                library data is the central database or the                database of potential therapeutic cannabinoid                targets, and (d) selecting a therapeutic                composition comprising at least one cannabinoid for                treatment of the patient based on the prediction of                the patient's response; and
   a method (C) for identifying and/or optimizing                a therapeutic composition against cancer comprising                at least one cannabinoid involves (i) preparing                composition comprising at least one cannabinoid                with a predetermined chemical profile, (ii)                determining a therapeutic efficacy of the                composition comprising at least one cannabinoid,                and (iii) performing a computational analysis on                the data obtained in step (i) or (ii).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The therapeutic efficacy                  is determined by comparing a biological marker of                  a sample that is not exposed to the composition                  comprising at least one cannabinoid to the                  biological marker of a sample that is exposed to                  the composition comprising at least one                  cannabinoid, where the increase and/or decrease                  of the biological marker is indicative of a                  therapeutic effect, and the therapeutic effect is                  cancer cell death, cancer cell viability,                  impairment of tumor angiogenesis and/or                  inhibition of cancer cell proliferation, cancer                  cell adhesion, cancer cell migration, cell                  invasiveness and/or other harmful effects of                  cancer cells. The biological marker is compared                  by conducting a multiomic analysis, by performing                  a cell profiling of the sample, a cell                  composition analysis, a gene expression analysis,                  a neighborhood analysis, a cytokine expression                  profiling and/or a protein phosphorylation                  analysis. The computational analysis is performed                  by correlating the predetermined chemical profile                  with the therapeutic efficacy of the composition                  comprising at least one cannabinoid to create a                  central database. The computational analysis                  comprises use of an in silico model, where the in                  silico model describes docking scores or energy                  calculations of cannabinoids on a potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid target or target                  ensemble, metabolic pathways and/or gene                  expression of a subject (such as of a subject                  suffering from cancer) or preferably of a cell                  (such as of a cancer cell), when exposing the                  subject or preferably the cell to the composition                  comprising at least one cannabinoid. The                  multiomic analysis comprises cell profiling of                  the sample using a multiplexed immunofluorescence                  method, where (i) the multiplexed                  immunofluorescence method comprises a detection,                  preferably a quantification, of a                  cannabinoid-related receptor, (ii) the                  cannabinoid-related receptor is chosen from a                  receptor class of hydrolase, transferase,                  oxidoreductase, signaling protein, cell adhesion                  protein, transport protein, nuclear receptor,                  metalloprotease, ligase, matrix metalloprotease,                  flavoprotein, cell cycle related protein, lyase,                  isomerase, protein involved in immunological                  response, hormone receptor, protein involved in                  blood, transcription and apoptotic protein, and                  (iii) the cannabinoid-related receptor is chosen                  from at least one cannabinoid-related receptor of                  cannabinoid receptor 1 (CBR1) (CNR1 or CB1), CBR2                  (CB2 or CNR2), transient receptor potential                  vanilloid 1 (TRPV1), TRPV2, TRPV3, TRPV4, TRPA1,                  TRPVA1, TRPM8, GPR3, GPR6, GPR12, GPR18, GPR23                  (LPAR4), GPR35, GPR55, GPR84, GPR92 (LPAR5),                  GPR119, peroxisome-proliferator-activated                  receptor (PPAR)-&#945; , PPARP (PPARD) and                  PPAR-&#947; (PPARG). The gene expression                  analysis is a spatial gene expression analysis,                  preferably a transcriptome analysis, a                  transcription factor analysis and/or a pathway                  analysis. The cytokine expression profiling                  comprises conducting a multiplex ELISA. The                  cytokine expression profiling comprises a                  detection, preferably a quantification of at                  least one cytokine chosen from structural                  families of four-&#945; -helix bundle                  (preferably interleukin (IL)-2 subfamily,                  interferon (IFN) subfamily and IL-10 subfamily),                  IL-1, cysteine knot cytokines and IL-17 family.                  The cytokine expression profiling comprises a                  detection, preferably quantification, of at least                  one secretory cytokine chosen from EGF, FGF,                  VEGF, TNF, IFN, TGF, TRAIL, SCF, MSP, CD, OSM,                  BBL, GITRI, LIGHT, OX, TALL, TWEAK, TRANCE and                  interleukins, where the at least one secretory                  cytokine is EGF, FGF, VEGF, TNF and interleukins.                  The protein phosphorylation analysis comprises                  conducting a multiplex ELISA, where the protein                  phosphorylation analysis comprises a detection,                  preferably (i) quantification of the                  phosphorylation of at least one intracellular                  signaling protein chosen from MEK1, ERK1/2, AKT,                  FAK1, CHK2, JUN, CREB1, EGFR, RB, GSK3, HSP27,                  P38, IKB, NF-KB, mTOR, RSK1, SMAD3, AKT1S1, CHK2,                  MARCKS, p70S6K, LCK, PI3K, P53, PTN11, NRF2,                  STAT1, STAT3, STAT6, SRC and/or WNT, or (ii)                  quantification of the phosphorylation of at least                  one intracellular signaling protein chosen from                  MEK1/2, ERK1/2, P38, JUN, CREB, GSK3, STAT3, AKT,                  mTOR, AKT1S1, MARCKS, IKBA, SMAD3, HSP27 and P53.                  The in silico model is composed as mathematically                  modeled logical regulatory network or as a                  deep-learning architecture-type network, both                  representing a biological pathway and its                  responses to applying the composition comprising                  at least one cannabinoid, and/or the in silico                  model is constructed using a network analysis and                  deep learning framework such as FALCON, PyTorch,                  Keras and/or TensorFlow. The computational                  analysis comprises creating and visualizing data                  networks, heat map charts, analyzing nodes,                  and/or performing cluster analyses. The                  computational analysis comprises conducting an                  inverse molecular docking analysis, preferably                  evaluating data from a complete human proteome                  target space, where the molecular docking                  analysis is performed with docking software that                  comprises a molecular docking algorithm,                  preferably ProBis-Dock docking algorithm. The                  computational analysis comprises creation of a                  database of potential therapeutic cannabinoid                  targets, where the database of potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid targets is created by the                  use of in silico target prediction methods. The                  database of potential therapeutic cannabinoid                  targets comprises the complete human proteome as                  experimentally available from RCSB PDB, Uniprot,                  AlfaFold and/or ESM Metagenomic Atlas databases.                  The database of potential therapeutic cannabinoid                  targets comprises AKT, CREB1, GSK3, Hsp27, IKBA,                  MEK1/2, mTOR, p38, MAPK, p53, RSK1, Smad3,                  AKT1S1, CHK2, cJUN, EGFR, p44/42 MAPK (ERK1/2),                  MARCKS, NF-KB, STAT3, PTN11, FAK, JNK, p70S6K                  and/or GAPDH. The in silico target prediction                  methods are chosen from SwissTarget, BioGRID,                  canCAR and/or CaNDis web server. The                  computational analysis comprises steps for                  identifying potential therapeutic cannabinoid                  targets by matching a potential therapeutic                  cannabinoid target with its gene data, preferably                  by using Enrichr toolset, matching a potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid target by its presence in                  key biological pathways, preferably by using the                  KEGG database, and/or matching of a potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid target with its gene and                  expression data by using deep-learning type                  models, using PyTorch, KERAS and/or TensorFlow                  libraries. The potential therapeutic cannabinoid                  targets are linked to common interaction partners                  in the protein-protein interaction String                  database, where additional therapeutic targets                  and/or mechanisms of observed adverse drug                  effects are identified. The potential therapeutic                  cannabinoid targets are in the form of                  experimental crystal complexes such as in the                  RCSB PDB Database, the AlfaFold and/or the ESM                  Metagenomic Atlas database, and the potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid targets are in the form                  of homology models such as in Swiss-Model,                  Modeller and/or Yasara. The method (A) further                  involves studying the interaction of                  cannabinoids, preferably cannabinoids of the                  composition comprising at least one cannabinoid,                  and their metabolites with the potential                  therapeutic cannabinoid targets, preferably at an                  atomistic level. The method (A) involves                  performing inverse molecular docking analysis and                  creation of inverse molecular docking                  fingerprints, which are further subjected to                  machine learning and/or statistical analysis to                  identify key cannabinoid-target interactions. The                  interaction of the cannabinoids and/or their                  metabolites with their potential therapeutic                  cannabinoid targets is evaluated by using direct                  methods, preferably inverse molecular docking,                  and/or by constructing drug-target interaction                  fingerprints, maps and/or structure-activity                  relationships. The direct methods are                  structure-based methods, ligand-based methods                  and/or consensus methods. The computational                  analysis is based on machine learning and/or                  statistical analysis. The method (A) involves                  setting up mechanistic models of action of                  individual cannabinoids and/or combinations of                  cannabinoids, where the mechanistic models of                  action of individual cannabinoids and/or                  combinations of cannabinoids are suitable to                  rationally set effective therapy for selected                  cancer patients. The method (B) further involves                  (i) cell testing as initial evaluation prior to                  performing step (b), by administering a                  composition comprising at least one cannabinoid                  to the patient sample and determining a                  therapeutic effect, and (ii) evaluating the                  efficiency of the therapeutic composition                  comprising at least one cannabinoid, by                  administering a composition comprising at least                  one cannabinoid to the patient sample and                  determining a therapeutic effect, where the                  patient sample comprises cancer cells. The                  library data comprises the predetermined chemical                  profile and the therapeutic efficacy of the                  composition comprising at least one cannabinoid.                  Preferred Component: The therapeutic composition                  against cancer comprises at least one carrier                  and/or excipient. The cannabinoid is a                  phyto-cannabinoid (pCB) and/or the at least one                  cannabinoid is chosen from &#916; 9-THCV-C3,                  &#916; 9-THCVA-C3A, &#916; 9-THCA-C5 A,                  &#916; 9-THC-C5, &#916; 8-THC-C5, CBN-C5,                  CBL-C5, CBLA-C5 A, (E)-CBG-C5, (E)-CBGA- C5 A,                  CBD-C5, CBDV-C3, CBDVA-C3, CBDA-C5, CBC-C5, and                  CBCA-C5 A. The cannabinoid is CBN, CBG, CBD, CBC,                  &#916; 9-THC and/or &#916; 8-THC,                  preferably CBN, CBG, CBD and/or CBC. The                  cannabinoid is THCA, THCVA, CBLA, CBGA, CBDVA,                  and/or CBDA. The cannabinoid is CBGA, THCA and/or                  CBLA, preferably CBLA.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The therapeutic composition in form of                injection, tablet, suppository, pill, capsule,                emulsion, syrup, powder, liquid or suspension is                administered by oral, rectal, transmucosal,                intestinal, or parenteral including intramuscular,                subcutaneous, intramedullary, intrathecal, direct                intraventricular, intracardiac, intravenous,                intraperitoneal, intranasal, or intraocular route.                No dosage details given.

TI Method for detecting image based on quantum hybrid            convolutional neural network model, involves inputting            image data into quantum hybrid convolution neural            network, and performing feature extraction through            input layer.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves inputting image data into                a quantum hybrid convolution neural network.                Feature extraction is performed through an input                layer. Extracted characteristic is processed                through a quantum convolution layer, where the                quantum convolution layer comprises a parameterized                quantum circuit. Efficient convolution operation is                performed on the image characteristic by a quantum                gate. Output of the quantum coil layer is converted                into the characteristic which is processed by a                classical neural network. The image is classified                through a full connecting layer. A cross entropy                loss function optimization classification model is                used. An Adam optimizer is used for training. An                image detection result is output.
   USE - Method for detecting an image based on a                quantum hybrid convolutional neural network model                for breast cancer image classification. Can also be                used in lung cancer, skin cancer image                classification and detection.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables improving calculation                efficiency of the model when processing the                large-scale data set by introducing the quantum                convolution layer. The method enables providing                higher robustness in aspect of high dimensional                feature extraction.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow chart of breast                cancer diagnosis of a model. (Drawing includes                non-English language text).
