AB    NOVELTY - Identifying a glycan-related therapeutic                target comprises: attaching or affixing at least                one target candidate to at least one array carrier;                binding at least one detection candidate to the                target candidate; detecting the binding of the                detection candidate to the target candidate; and at                least one of, identifying the target candidate and                bound by the detection candidate, identifying the                detection candidate bound to the target candidate,                or identifying a glycan-related target candidate or                the detection candidate.
   USE - The methods are useful for: identifying a                glycan-related therapeutic target; identifying a                therapeutic target or a biological marker to a                disease; diagnosing inflammation, cancers or                autoimmune diseases including malignant melanoma,                brain malignant oligodendroglioma, kidney clear                cell carcinoma, skin basal cell carcinoma of head,                throat carcinoma, Hodgkin's lymphoma of                supraclavicular, colon intermediate grade                interstitialoma, thyroid medullary carcinoma and                skin squamous cell carcinoma of left chest wall,                autoimmune hepatitis, autoimmune intestinal                disorders, or biliary atresia; and rapid evaluation                of the safety of vaccines or therapeutic antibodies                caused by an infectious disease, an antibody                induced by a pathogen, a vaccine, a lectin or an                antibody artificially introduced into the subject.                The glycan-binding molecules are useful in a drug                delivery tool. The array carrier is useful for                identification of the glycan-related target. The                composition is useful for treating or preventing a                glycan-related disease including an infectious                disease, a cancer, an autoimmune diseases, an                allergic reaction, inflammation, toxicity or                obesity caused by an influenza virus, a rotavirus,                or Newcastle disease virus, where the influenza                virus is optionally a H5N1 virus, a H1N1 virus, or                a H3N2 virus (all claimed). The method is useful                for the pathogenesis studies, controlling pandemic                diseases; for the development high quality                vaccines, for the development of animal models of                autoimmune diseases, allergies, toxicity, cancers,                obesity and other disorders; and for studies of                epidemiology and biology, preferably evolutionary                biology.    ADVANTAGE - ADVANTAGE u The method is simple and efficient                for the rapid identification of therapeutic                targets. The composition has no side effects.

AB    NOVELTY - Imaging device comprises an optical system is                used for providing a light source with adjustable                power density and excitation area for the magnetic                measuring probe of the diamond containing ensemble                nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color center and collecting                fluorescence of ensemble NV color center. A control                system is used for modulating the microwave signal                generated by a microwave system. The microwave                system is used for microwave modulation and                radiation. A mechanical system is used for                controlling the position of workbench and providing                a bias magnetic field. A signal processing system                is used for converting the voltage signal measured                from the control system into the magnetic field                signal and re-forming the magnetic field signal                into the magnetic particle density image. A display                system for displaying image and/or processed data.                The signal processing system and the display system                are integrated in the computer. A computer controls                control system, micro-wave system and mechanical                system.
   USE - The imaging device is useful for skin cancer                in vivo non-destructive detection.
   ADVANTAGE - The device utilizes high-concentration                ensemble NV color center in the diamond for                measuring the magnetic signal of the                ultra-paramagnetic nanoparticle of the target mark,                realizes the precise and sensitive detection of the                skin cancer, and provides technical means for the                basic research and clinical diagnosis of the skin                tumor disease.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method of using imaging device.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of the                imaging device (Drawing includes non-English                language text).

AB    NOVELTY - In vitrodetection (M1) of methylated DNA,                involves coating a container with a polypeptide                capable of binding methylated DNA, contacting the                polypeptide with a sample comprising methylated                and/or unmethylated DNA, and detecting the binding                of the polypeptide to methylated DNA.
   USE - (M1) or (K1) is useful for in vitro detection                of methylated DNA in a sample, where the sample is                from a subject. The subject is suspected to have                hypo- and/or hypermethylated gene loci. The hypo-                and/or hypermethylated gene loci are indicative of                a cancer, tumor or metastasis (claimed). (M1) is                useful for diagnosis of cancer chosen from e.g.                cancer of skin, breast, brain, cervical carcinomas,                testicular carcinomas, head and neck, lung,                mediastinum, gastrointestinal tract, genitourinary                system, gynecological system and bone, or cancer                metastasis, and for classifying tumors.
   ADVANTAGE - (M1) enables rapid, easy, safe, highly                sensitive and reliable in vitrodetection of                methylated DNA and to analyze target DNA fragments                according to the methylation degree.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                kit (K1) for performing (M1), comprising a                polypeptide capable of binding methylated DNA, a                container which can be coated with the polypeptide,                unit for coating the container, and unit for                detecting methylated DNA.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In (M1), the detection                  step involves restriction enzyme digestion,                  bisulfite sequencing, pyrosequencing, Southern                  Blot or PCR, preferably PCR. (M1) further                  involves analyzing the methylated DNA. The step                  of analyzing the methylated DNA comprises                  sequencing. The polypeptide is chosen from:a polypeptide belonging to the Methyl-DNA                  binding protein (MBD) family,a fragment of (i), where the fragment is                  capable of binding methylated DNA,a variant of (i) or the fragment of (ii),                  where in the variant one or more amino acid                  residues are substituted compared to (i) or the                  fragment of (ii), and where the variant is                  capable of binding methylated DNA,a polypeptide which is an anti-methylated                  DNA antibody or its fragment, anda polypeptide which is at least 70%                  identical to a polypeptide of any one of                  (i)-(iii) and which is capable of binding                  methylated DNA.The polypeptide is fused to a heterologous                  polypeptide chosen from HA-tag, myc6-tag,                  FLAG-tag, STREP-tag, STREP II-tag, TAP-tag,                  HAT-tag, chitin-binding domain (CBD),                  maltose-binding protein, His6-tag,                  glutathione-S-transferase (GST) tag, intein-tag,                  streptavidin-binding protein (SBP) tag and an                  Fc-portion of an antibody. The anti-methylated                  DNA antibody is an anti-5-methylcytosine antibody                  or its Fab, F(ab') 2, Fv or scFv fragment. The                  container is coated directly or indirectly with                  the polypeptide.

TI Method for non-invasive detecting and tracing            cancer, involves measuring oxidation current peak and            detecting cancerous tumor at target location by            comparing measured oxidation current peak with set of            reference values.
AU ABBASVANDI F
   NAMDAR H N

AE ABBASVANDI F (ABBA-Individual)

GA 202187162Q
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves fabricating a probe. The                probe is put on a portion of skin adjacent to a                target location inside a body of patient. The two                reference electrodes inside the target location is                inserted through the portion of skin. The working                electrode and the counter electrode is inserted                into the target location by releasing the working                electrode and the counter electrode through the two                reference electrodes. A cyclic voltammetry (CV)                response of hypoxia-related hydrogen peroxide                release is recorded in the target location by                applying a set of electrical potentials to the                probe. An oxidation current peak of the recorded CV                response is measured. A cancerous tumor is detected                at the target location by comparing the measured                oxidation current peak with a set of reference                values.
   USE - Method for non-invasive detecting and tracing                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is based on measuring the oxidative                currents released during glycolysis from the                tissue. A cancer region is distinguished in-situ                utilizing exemplary CDP in less than about seconds                or even instantaneously before or during surgery                and without any need for resecting and freezing a                sample from a patient. The method is deeply located                tumors within the body of patient is easily                accessible for detection of and tracing of a                cancerous tumor using exemplary probe without any                need to do a surgery or biopsy.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - AN INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for:
   1.A probe for non-invasive detecting and                tracing cancer.

AB    NOVELTY - Method (M1) for detecting a somatic mutation                signature in a sample involves sequencing DNA from                a sample obtained from a subject for obtaining                sequencing reads for the subject, detecting several                mutations in the sequencing reads, and decomposing                the mutations with a reference set of somatic                mutation signatures and a germ-line mutation                signature comprising a frequency of a                classification set unique to a germ-line genome                comprising (i) nucleotide changes, (ii) at least                one unchanged position that is 5' of each                nucleotide change in the set, and (iii) at least                one unchanged position that is 3' of each                nucleotide change in the set for removing germ-line                contamination from the sequencing reads and                detecting at least one somatic mutation signature                for the subject.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting somatic                mutation signature in the sample obtained from the                subject for improved somatic mutation calling,                improved detection of the somatic mutation                signature, and improved detection of TMB. The                subject has cancer, previously had cancer, or is at                risk of developing cancer. The cancer is chosen                from adrenal cancer, anal cancer, bile duct cancer,                bladder cancer, bone cancer, a brain/CNS tumor,                breast cancer, Castleman disease, cervical cancer,                colon or rectum cancer, endometria cancer,                esophagus cancer, a Ewing tumor, eye cancer,                gallbladder cancer, a gastrointestinal carcinoid                tumor, a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST),                gestational trophoblastic disease, Hodgkin disease,                Kaposi sarcoma, kidney cancer, laryngeal and                hypopharyngeal cancer, leukemia, liver cancer, lung                cancer, lymphoma, malignant mesothelioma, multiple                myeloma, myelodysplastic syndrome, nasal cavity or                paranasal sinus cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer,                neuroblastoma, oral cavity or oropharyngeal cancer,                osteosarcoma, ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer,                penile cancer, a pituitary tumor, prostate cancer,                retinoblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, salivary gland                cancer, skin cancer, small intestine cancer,                stomach cancer, testicular cancer, thymus cancer,                thyroid cancer, uterine sarcoma, vaginal cancer,                vulvar cancer, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and                Wilms tumor. The subject has, previously had, or is                at risk of developing leukemia or lymphoma (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides a germ-line mutational                signature that can be used to better filter out                germ-line mutations when it is desirable to analyze                or detect only the somatic mutations in a given                sample.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method (M2) for improved somatic mutation                calling involves obtaining a tumor sample from a                subject, sequencing DNA from the tumor sample for                obtaining sequencing reads, and calling a somatic                mutation signature for the tumor sample by                detecting somatic mutations in the sequencing                reads, and removing germ-line contamination from                the sequencing reads by decomposing the sequencing                reads with a germ-line mutation signature, and                detecting at least one somatic mutation signature,                where the somatic mutation signature has a reduced                negative effect from germ-line contamination                relative a somatic mutation call that does not                account for the germ-line mutational                signature;
   method (M3) for improved detection of a                somatic mutation signature involves retrieving, by                a processor, data associated with a tumor sample,                where the data comprises DNA sequencing reads from                the tumor sample, generating, by a computer device,                a set of mutations in the sequencing reads, and                decomposing, by a computer processor, the set of                mutations with a reference set of somatic mutation                signatures and a germ-line mutation signature for                removing germ-line contamination from the                sequencing reads, and detecting at least one                somatic mutation signature; and
   method (M4) for improved detection of tumor                mutation burden (TMB) involves obtaining a tumor                sample from a subject, sequencing DNA from the                tumor sample for obtaining sequencing reads, and                detecting TMB by quantifying somatic mutations in                the sequencing reads, and removing germ-line                contamination from the sequencing reads by                decomposing the sequencing reads with a germ-line                mutation signature.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method, the                  classification set comprises 96 triplicates,                  where (i) the nucleotide changes comprise six                  types of substitutions, (ii) the at least one                  unchanged position that is 5' of each nucleotide                  change in the set comprises one of four types of                  bases 5' to the substitution, and (iii) the at                  least one unchanged position that is 3' of each                  nucleotide change in the set comprises one of                  four types of bases 3' to the substitution. The                  frequency of the classification set is the                  frequency provided in figure 1 of the                  specification. In the method, (i) the nucleotide                  changes comprise six types of substitutions, (ii)                  the at least one unchanged position that is 5' of                  each nucleotide change in the set comprises at                  least two, at least three, or at least four bases                  5' to the substitution, and (iii) the at least                  one unchanged position that is 3' of each                  nucleotide change in the set comprises at least                  two, at least three, or at least four bases 3' to                  the substitution. The method further involves                  removing germ-line mutations from the mutations                  in the sequence reads by (a) comparing the                  sequences reads for the subject to a set of                  germ-line mutations, where the set of germ-line                  mutations are (i) determined by sequencing a                  germ-line sample from the subject, (ii) compiled                  from a database of germ-line mutations, or (iii)                  a combination of mutations found in sequences                  from a germ-line sample from the subject and                  mutations from a database of germ-line mutations,                  (b) determining the frequency of the sequence                  reads comprising mutations and comparing the                  frequency to a database of germ-line mutations,                  or (c) determining a tumor mutation burden (TMB)                  score based on the number of somatic variants                  having a somatic mutation significance score                  above a threshold. The reference set of somatic                  mutation signatures comprises Signature 1A,                  Signature 1B, Signature 2, Signature 3, Signature                  4, Signature 5, Signature 6, Signature 7,                  Signature 8, Signature 9, Signature 10, Signature                  11, Signature 12, Signature 13, Signature 14,                  Signature 15, Signature 16, Signature 17,                  Signature 18, Signature 19, Signature 20, and                  Signature 21. In the method, sequencing DNA from                  the sample involves whole genome sequencing,                  whole exome sequencing, or targeted gene                  sequencing. The at least one somatic mutation                  signature is selected from Signature 1A,                  Signature 1B, Signature 2, Signature 3, Signature                  4, Signature 5, Signature 6, Signature 7,                  Signature 8, Signature 9, Signature 10, Signature                  11, Signature 12, Signature 13, Signature 14,                  Signature 15, Signature 16, Signature 17,                  Signature 18, Signature 19, Signature 20, and                  Signature 21, or their combination. The method                  involves decomposing the mutations by normalizing                  the at least one somatic mutation signature. The                  germ-line mutation signature comprises a                  frequency of a classification set that is unique                  to a germ-line genome, where the classification                  set comprises (i) nucleotide changes, (ii) at                  least one unchanged position that is 5' of each                  nucleotide change in the set, and (iii) at least                  one unchanged position that is 3' of each                  nucleotide change in the set. In the method,                  removing germ-line contamination further involves                  (a) comparing the sequences reads for the subject                  to a set of germ-line mutations, where the set of                  germ-line mutations are (i) determined by                  sequencing a germ-line sample from the subject,                  (ii) compiled from a database of germ-line                  mutations, or (iii) a combination of mutations                  found in sequences from a germ-line sample from                  the subject and mutations from a database of                  germ-line mutations, (b) determining the                  frequency of the sequence reads comprising                  mutations and comparing the frequency to a                  database of germ-line mutations, or (c)                  determining TMB score based on the number of                  somatic variants having a somatic mutation                  significance score above a threshold. Preferred                  Sample: The sample is a tumor sample or a fluid                  sample. The fluid sample is a blood sample or a                  plasma sample.

Test details are described but no                results given.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Determining the prognosis of a cancer                characterized by a solid tumor in a female patient,                comprises determining the percentage of solid tumor                cells expressing class III beta -tubulin (TUBB3)                protein and class V beta -tubulin isotype (TUBB6)                protein, in a sample from the solid tumor, where                detection of TUBB6 protein expression in a                percentage of the solid tumor cells: that is less                than a median percentage expression for TUBB6                protein and detection of TUBB3 protein expression                in a percentage of the solid tumor cells that is                less than the median percentage expression for                TUBB3 protein indicates that the patient has a good                prognosis; and of the female patient that is equal                to or greater than a median percentage expression                for TUBB6 protein and/or detection of TUBB3 protein                expression in a percentage of the solid tumor cells                of the female patient that is equal to or greater                than the median percentage expression for TUBB3                protein indicates that the patient has a poor                prognosis.    (2) sensitizing a cancer cell of a solid tumor                of a male patient, other than a prostate cancer                cell, to treatment with a chemotherapeutic agent,                comprising administering at least one antiandrogen                and at least one chemotherapeutic agent other than                an antiandrogen, to the patient; and
   (3) a kit for determining the prognosis of                cancer in a female patient with a solid tumor,                comprising a set of reagents that specifically                detects the protein expression levels of TUBB3                protein and TUBB6 protein in cells from the solid                tumor, and instructions for using the kit for                evaluating the prognosis of cancer characterized by                a solid tumor in a female.

The antiandrogen is                  administered to the cancer cell before the                  chemotherapeutic agent. (I) is used to                treat cancer (e.g. solid tumors of liver, lung,                kidney, bladder, head-and-neck, brain, ovary,                prostate, skin, intestine, colon, pancreas and                eye), cardiovascular pathology (atherosclerosis)                and neurodegenerative pathology (Alzheimer's                disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral                sclerosis and multiple sclerosis).

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation (Claimed): Preparation of (I)                  comprises: forming a core comprising one or more                  nanoparticles; optional coating of the core;                  fixing a targeting molecule having an affinity                  for a molecule or an intracellular structure on                  the surface of the particle; and optionally                  fixing a surface targeting element allowing                  specific targeting of biological cells or                  tissues.Preferred Process: The surface element                  specifically allowing the targeting of biological                  cells or tissues is bonded with the optional                  coating or with the core of the particle. (I) is                  primarily present in spherical form.Preferred Components: The core comprises: a                  metallic oxide or a non-oxidized metal, allowing                  a physical reversal of the particle in a magnetic                  field; a photosensitive molecule, allowing the                  production of heat or free radicals by the effect                  of laser light; a semi conducting compound or a                  mixed solution, optionally doped (E) with an                  lanthanide, or an organic molecule, allowing                  production of heat or free radicals by the effect                  of a UV light or laser; and an inorganic compound                  in form of oxide, hydroxide and/or sulfoxide salt                  doped with a lanthanide (optional), or of                  non-oxidized metal, allowing the production of                  heat or free radicals under the effect of X-rays.                  The optional coating is composed of an                  (in)organic amorphous or crystalline structure.                  The targeting molecule: is a biological or                  chemical molecule having an affinity for a                  molecule present in a human or animal cell                  ((poly)peptide, nucleic acid, nucleotide, lipid                  or metabolite); has an affinity for a molecule of                  an intracellular or nuclear membrane, a molecule                  of the cytoskeleton, a cytoplasmic molecule or a                  mitochondrion; has an affinity for an enzyme, a                  nuclear receptor, a factor of transcription or                  translation, a co-factor or a natural or                  synthetic substrate in the cell; is an antibody,                  a receptor ligand, a ligand receptor or a                  fragment or their derivatives; and is bonded with                  the optional coating or with the core                  constitutive of the particle.

AB    NOVELTY - The scanner has an image detector to receive                optical and fluorescence/luminescence images of a                body (4) to be scanned. Pattern projector projects                an optical pattern at a geometrical angle on the                body, where projected pattern is recorded at a                different geometrical angle. Three-dimensional (3D)                position information of surface points of the                scanned body is computed based on the angles.                Images are superposed to form a 3D fluorescence                scan.
   USE - Used for determining molecular composition of                the material such as body of patient, for detection                of cancer e.g. breast cancer, skin cancer,                intestine cancer, rheumatoid arthiritis,                arteriosclerosis of a carotid-arteria, tumor e.g.                brain tumor, pancreas tumor, inflammations.
   ADVANTAGE - The three-dimensional position information of                surface points of the body is computed based on the                projection and recording angles for the optical                pattern, in an inexpensive and less computational                intensive manner. The scanner avoids the need for a                positioning device for rotation and movement of the                body to be scanned, thus reducing the additional                cost of the scanner.

TI Apparatus, useful for detecting circulating tumor            cells e.g. lung cancer in biological subject comprising            blood, urine, saliva, tear, sweat or lymph, comprises            biological subject delivering system, and probing and            detecting device.

GA 2012P61702
AB    NOVELTY - The apparatus (111) comprises a system for                delivering a biological subject, a probing and                detecting device, a device for reading a data from                measuring the property by the probing and detecting                device, a bio-compatible fluid delivering system, a                biological interface, a system controller, a system                for reclaiming or treatment medical waste, a system                for distributing the biological subject, a                distribution channel, a pre-processing unit, a                re-charging unit, a detection device, a global                positioning system, a motion device, a signal                transmitter, a signal receiver, and a sensor.
   USE - The apparatus is useful for detecting                circulating tumor cells in a biological subject                comprising blood, urine, saliva, tear, sweat or                lymph, where the tumor cells are prostate cancer,                lung cancer, colon cancer, breast cancer, brain                cancer, cervical cancer, Hodgkin's lymphoma,                non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, kidney cancer, leukemia,                liver cancer, ovarian cancer, skin cancer,                testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, pancreatic                cancer, endometrial cancer, esophageal cancer or                uterine cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The compact apparatus is capable of reliably,                economically, accurately and rapidly detecting the                circulating tumor cells in the biological subject                at earlier stage with high degree of sensitivity                and specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The apparatus (111) comprises a system for                delivering a biological subject, a probing and                detecting device, a device for reading a data from                measuring the property by the probing and detecting                device, a bio-compatible fluid delivering system, a                biological interface, a system controller, a system                for reclaiming or treatment medical waste, a system                for distributing the biological subject, a                distribution channel, a pre-processing unit, a                re-charging unit, a detection device, a global                positioning system, a motion device, a signal                transmitter, a signal receiver, a sensor, a memory                storage unit, a logic processing unit, an                application specific chip, a unit for recycling and                reclaiming the biological subject, a                micro-electro-mechanical device, a multi-functional                device, a microinstrument to perform surgery, drug                delivery, cleaning or medical function, a filtering                device for removing irrelevant objects from the                biologic subject for detection, a data storage                unit, a data analysis unit, a central control unit,                a biological sample recirculation unit, a waste                disposal unit, a micro-electromechanical device,                and a signal processing unit. The probing and                detecting device is capable of: detecting, counting                and recording the number of tumor cells in a                biological subject; and marking a cancer                progression of the biological subject by the                detected amount of tumor cells. The probing and                detecting device comprises a first micro-device,                and a first substrate supporting the first                micro-device. The fluid to be delivered is liquid                such as a blood sample, a urine sample, a saliva                sample, a tear sample, a sweat sample or a lymph                sample. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   an apparatus for interacting with a biological                subject to detect circulating tumor cells;
   a device comprising a micro-filter, a shutter,                a cell counter, a selector, a micro-surgical kit, a                timer and a data processing circuitry; and
   a micro-device comprising a micro-trench, a                probe embedded along side of the trench's side                walls or bottom floor, a supporting structure to                move the probe and a controlling circuitry.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The diagram shows a schematic perspective                view of a circulating tumor cell detection                apparatus.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Components: The first micro-device                  contacts the biological subject to be detected,                  and is capable of measuring, at a microscopic                  level, an electric, magnetic, electro-magnetic,                  thermal, optical, acoustical, biological,                  chemical, physical-chemical, electro-mechanical,                  electro-chemical, electro-chemical-mechanical,                  biophysical, bio-chemical, bio-mechanical,                  bio-electrical, bio-physical-chemical,                  bio-electrophysical, bio-electro-mechanical,                  bio-electro-chemical, bio-chemical-mechanical,                  bio-electrophysical-chemical,                  bio-electro-physical-mechanical,                  bio-electro-chemical-mechanical, physical or                  mechanical property of the biologic subject or                  cells. A difference in the measured property                  between the detected biological subject and a                  standard biologic sample or between cells                  contained in the detected biological subject and                  normal cells is indicative of the possible                  existence of circulating tumor cells. The                  electrical property is surface charge, surface                  potential, resting potential, electrical current,                  electrical field distribution, surface charge                  distribution, cell electronic properties, cell                  surface electronic properties, dynamic changes in                  electronic properties, dynamic changes in cell                  electronic properties, dynamic changes in cell                  surface electronic properties, dynamic changes in                  surface electronic properties, electronic                  properties of cell membranes, dynamic changes in                  electronic properties of membrane surface,                  dynamic changes in electronic properties of cell                  membranes, electrical dipole, electrical                  quadruple, oscillation in electrical signal,                  electrical current, capacitance,                  three-dimensional electrical or charge cloud                  distribution, electrical properties at telomere                  of DNA and chromosome, capacitance, or impedance.                  The thermal property is temperature or                  vibrational frequency. The optical property is                  optical absorption, optical transmission, optical                  reflection, optical-electrical property,                  brightness, or fluorescent emission. The                  radiation property is radiation emission, signal                  triggered by radioactive material, or information                  probed by radioactive material. The chemical                  property is pH value, chemical reaction,                  bio-chemical reaction, bio-electro-chemical                  reaction, reaction speed, reaction energy, speed                  of reaction, oxygen concentration, oxygen                  consumption rate, ionic strength, catalytic                  behavior, chemical additives to trigger enhanced                  signal response, bio-chemical additives to                  trigger enhanced signal response, biological                  additives to trigger enhanced signal response,                  chemicals to enhance detection sensitivity,                  bio-chemicals to enhance detection sensitivity,                  biological additives to enhance detection                  sensitivity, or bonding strength; the physical                  property is density, shape, volume, or surface                  area; the biological property is surface shape,                  surface area, surface charge, surface biological                  property, surface chemical property, pH,                  electrolyte, ionic strength, resistivity, cell                  concentration, or biological, electrical,                  physical or chemical property of solution; the                  acoustic property is frequency, speed of acoustic                  waves, acoustic frequency and intensity spectrum                  distribution, acoustic intensity, acoustical                  absorption, or acoustical resonance. The                  mechanical property is internal pressure,                  hardness, flow rate, viscosity, fluid mechanical                  properties, shear strength, elongation strength,                  fracture stress, adhesion, mechanical resonance                  frequency, elasticity, plasticity, or                  compressibility. The probing and detecting device                  applies a voltage of 1 mV to 1 V to the                  biological entity. The first micro-device and the                  additional micro-devices comprise a conductive                  material, an electrically insulating material, a                  biological material or a semiconductor material,                  and have a size of 1&#8491; to 5 mm. The                  probing and detecting device further comprises                  additional micro-devices, a second substrate of                  the same or different material as the first                  substrate, a system controller, and a detecting                  micro-device. The additional micro-devices                  comprise a material that is the same as or                  different from the material of the first                  micro-device, and are capable of measuring the                  same or different property of the biologic                  material as the first micro-device. The                  micro-devices are spaced out on the substrate by                  a distance of 10&#8491; . A distance between                  two adjacent micro-devices is 5-100 microns. The                  substrate is present in the shape of a slab, a                  tube or an array of tubes, and is a                  three-dimensional object. The fluid delivering                  system comprises a pressure generator, a pressure                  regulator, a throttle valve, a pressure gauge,                  and distributing kits. The pressure generator                  comprises a motor piston system, and a bin                  containing compressed gas. The pressure regulator                  down-regulates or up-regulates the pressure to a                  desired value. The pressure gauge feeds back the                  measured value to the throttle valve, which                  regulates the pressure to approach the target                  value. The system controller comprises a                  pre-amplifier, a lock-in amplifier, an electrical                  meter, a thermal meter, a switching matrix, a                  system bus, a nonvolatile storage device, a                  random access memory, a data processing unit, a                  logic unit, a processor, or a user interface. The                  interface comprises a sensor. The sensor                  comprises a thermal sensor, a flow meter, an                  optical sensor, a voltage meter, a current meter,                  an electrical sensor, a pH meter, a hardness                  measurement sensor, a thermal sensor, a flow                  meter, or a piezo meter. The pre-processing unit                  comprises a sample filtration unit, a nutrient                  and respiring gas recharging unit, a constant                  pressure delivery unit, or a sample disturbing                  unit. The biological subject delivering system                  comprises a channel inside which the biological                  subject travels in a certain direction. The                  probing micro-device is located before the                  detecting micro-device relative to the direction                  in which the biological subject travels. The                  probing micro-device and the detecting                  micro-device are attached to an interior or                  exterior wall of the channel. The shapes and                  sizes of different sections of the channel are                  the same or different. A width of the channel is                  1 nm to 1 mm. The channel is straight, curved or                  angled channel, and a circular carbon nano-tube.                  The interior wall of the channel defines a                  circular, oval, square or polygon space. The                  carbon nano-tube has a diameter of 0.5 nm to 1                  micron, and a length of 5 nm to 10 mm. The                  interior wall of the channel has a concave                  groove, which defines a cubic space or an angled                  space and has a depth of 10 nm to 1 mm. A                  disturbing fluid is injected into the channel,                  either before or after the biological subject                  passes the probing micro-device, to aid the                  traveling or separation of the biological subject                  inside the channel. The distribution fluid is                  injected into the channel through a distribution                  fluid channel connected to an opening in the                  channel wall. The channel comprises a device for                  separating or dividing the biological subjects                  based on different levels of a same property of                  the biological subjects. The separating or                  dividing device is a slit, and separates or                  divides biological subjects based on their                  surface charges. The apparatus is integrated on a                  single device or a board. The micro-devices are                  fabricated by a method comprising: depositing a                  first material onto a substrate; and depositing a                  second material onto the first material and then                  patterning the second material with a                  microelectronic technology or process. The                  micro-devices: pierce through the membrane of a                  circulating tumor cell; move in different                  directions; and are physically or electrically                  coupled or integrated. The sample filtration unit                  comprises an entrance channel, a disturbing fluid                  channel, an accelerating chamber, a slit, a                  biocompatible micro-filter, and an exit channel.                  The bio-compatible fluid comprises saline, water,                  oxygen rich liquid, an intravenous solution, or                  plasma. An angle between the entrance channel and                  the disturbing fluid channel is 0-180&#176; ,                  30-150&#176; , 60-120&#176; ,                  75-105&#176; , or 90&#176; . The                  biocompatible micro-filter is capable of                  filtering the biological subject based on the                  property consisting of physical size, hardness,                  elasticity, shear strength, weight, surface                  features, dynamic surface features, optical,                  acoustical, thermal, fluid properties, properties                  due to interactions between biological entity and                  micro-filter, dynamic response due to                  interactions between biological entity and                  microfilter, chemical, mechanical, electrical,                  biological, physical-chemical, bio-physical,                  biochemical, electro-chemical, magnetic,                  electro-magnetic, electro-mechanical,                  electrochemical-mechanical,                  bio-chemical-mechanical, bio-physical-chemical,                  bio-electro-chemical, and                  bio-electro-chemical-mechanical property. The                  slit is located in the channel to separate the                  channel into a top channel and a bottom channel.                  The signal is pulsed or constant. The nutrient                  comprises bio-compatible strong or weak                  electrolyte, amino acid, mineral, ions, oxygen,                  oxygen-rich liquid, intravenous solution,                  glucose, or protein. The respiring fluid                  comprises oxygen rich liquids or oxygen. The                  signal processing unit comprises an amplifier, a                  lock-in amplifier, an analog-to-digital                  converter, a micro-computer, a manipulator, a                  display, or network connections. The signal                  processing unit collects signals, which are                  integrated to cancel noise or to enhance the                  signal to noise ratio.

TI Displaying method for showing medical information            about subject involves constructing image based on            selected portion of each spectrum to project image onto            subject after resolving light obtained from each region            of skin.

GA 2009R44702
AB    NOVELTY - The displaying method involves constructing an                image based on a selected portion of each spectrum                to project the image onto a subject after resolving                light obtained from each region of the skin into a                corresponding spectrum. The selected portion                includes medical information about a corresponding                region.
   USE - Displaying method for showing medical                information about subject.
   ADVANTAGE - Assists in detection and characterization of                skin cancers, as well as a wide variety of other                conditions. Enables physician to easily examine a                subject by projecting spectral information onto the                subject and/or by displaying spectral information                on a video display.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a display system; and
   a computer-readable medium.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows the block diagram of a                hyper-spectral medical imaging system.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting tumor-specific T cell                involves incubating activator with peripheral                immune cells, detecting specific molecules of                tumor-specific T cells to realize detection of                tumor-specific T cells, where the activator                comprises tumor cells, tumor tissue whole cells,                tumor cell lysate components, and tumor tissue                whole cell lysate fraction.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting                tumor-specific T cells. The tumor is blood tumors                and solid tumors chosen from endocrine system                tumors, nervous system tumors, reproductive system                tumors, digestive system tumors, respiratory system                tumors, blood cancer, skin cancer, breast cancer,                lung cancer, liver cancer, gastric cancer,                pancreatic cancer, brain cancer, colon cancer,                prostate cancer, rectal cancer, head and neck                cancer, kidney cancer, bone cancer, nose cancer,                bladder cancer, thyroid cancer, esophageal cancer,                cervical cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine cancer,                pelvic cancer, testicular cancer, penile cancer,                lymphoma, tongue cancer, gum cancer, retinoblastoma                and sarcoma (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for detecting content of tumor-specific T cell                involves incubating activator with peripheral                immune cells, and detecting specific molecules of                tumor-specific T cells, and obtaining content of                tumor-specific T cells according to ratio of number                of tumor-specific T cells to number of peripheral                immune cells.
EA    (WO2022061791-A1)   NOVELTY - Detecting tumor-specific T cells comprises                incubating activator with peripheral immune cells,                then detecting specific molecules of tumor-specific                T cells to detect tumor-specific T cells; where the                activator includes tumor cell, tumor tissue whole                cell, tumor cell lysate component, and tumor tissue                whole cell lysate component.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting                tumor-specific T cells, which is useful in                detecting tumor specific T cell in peripheral                immune cells (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method can comprehensively and accurately                detects the cancer specific T cell content patient                the peripheral blood.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Component: The lysate component is                  a water-soluble lysate component and/or a                  non-water-soluble lysate component. The lysate                  component is a free lysate component or a lysate                  component loaded on micro-nano particles. The                  lysate component is carried on inside and/or                  surface of the micro-nano particles. The                  micro-nano particle preparation material is an                  organic material, an inorganic material or a                  biological material and the micro-nano particles                  are micro-particles or nano-particles. The                  specific molecules are proteins, polypeptides,                  nucleic acids, sugars or lipids. Preferred                  Method: The method involves incubating activator                  with peripheral immune cells under conditions                  where the cells can survive.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details of detection of                cancer-specific T cells in peripheral tissues of                melanoma tumor-bearing mice that do not support the                claims.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for delivering a therapeutic agent to a                cancer cell, involves administering a composition                comprising an anti-oncostatin M (OSM)-R beta                antibody that specifically binds to OSM-R beta ,                where the anti-OSM-R beta antibody is associated                with the therapeutic agent.
   USE - The method is useful for delivering                therapeutic agent to cancer cell for inhibiting                growth of cancer cells including adrenal gland                tumors, AIDS-associated cancers, alveolar soft part                sarcoma, astrocytic tumors, bladder cancer                including squamous cell carcinoma and transitional                cell carcinoma, bone cancer including adamantinoma,                aneurismal bone cysts, osteochondroma and                osteosarcoma, brain and spinal cord cancers,                metastatic brain tumors, breast cancer, carotid                body tumors, cervical cancer, chondrosarcoma,                chordoma, chromophobe renal cell carcinoma, clear                cell carcinoma, colon cancer, colorectal cancer,                cutaneous benign fibrous histiocytomas,                desmoplastic small round cell tumors, ependymomas,                Ewing's tumor, extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma,                fibrogenesis imperfecta ossium, fibrous dysplasia                of the bone, gallbladder and bile duct cancers,                gestational trophoblastic disease, germ cell                tumors, head and neck cancers, islet cell tumors,                Kaposi's sarcoma, kidney cancer including                nephroblastoma and papillary renal cell carcinoma,                leukemia, lipomalbenign lipomatous tumors,                liposarcoma/malignant lipomatous tumors, liver                cancer including hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular                carcinoma, lymphomas, lung cancers including small                cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell                carcinoma and large cell carcinoma,                medulloblastoma, melanoma, meningioma, multiple                endocrine neoplasia, multiple myeloma,                myelodysplastic syndrome, neuroblastoma,                glioblastoma, neuroendocrine tumors, ovarian                cancer, pancreatic cancer, papillary thyroid                carcinoma, parathyroid tumor, pediatric cancer,                peripheral nerve sheath tumors, phaeochromocytoma,                pituitary tumors, prostate cancer, hematologic                disorders, renal metastatic cancer, rhabdoid tumor,                rhabdomysarcoma, sarcomas, skin cancer, soft-tissue                sarcomas, including carcinoma of the cervix,                endometrial carcinoma or leiomyoma in subject                including human. The pharmaceuticals include pills,                tablets, syrups or suspensions.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables qualitative and                quantitative detection of cancer. The OSM-R beta                antagonist effectively reduces proliferation and                metastasis of cancer cells, thus increasing quality                of life.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The anti-OSM-R beta                  antibody is a monoclonal antibody or its                  antigen-binding fragment expressed by the                  hybridoma (ATCC No. PTA-6511). The anti-OSM-R                  beta antibody comprises three complementarity                  determining regions from the heavy chain and the                  three complementarity determining regions from                  the light chain of the monoclonal antibody                  produced by the hybridoma. The anti-OSM-R beta                  antibody is a humanized antibody or a chimeric                  antibody comprising the heavy chain and the light                  chain variable regions of the monoclonal antibody                  produced by the hybridoma. The chimeric antibody                  comprises a heavy chain constant region and a                  light chain constant region from a human                  antibody. The anti-OSM-R beta antibody is an                  antigen-binding fragment chosen from antigen                  binding fragment (Fab), Fab', F(ab') 2 and                  variable fragment (Fv), where the antigen-binding                  fragment retains the binding specificity of the                  monoclonal antibody expressed by the                  hybridoma.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - OSM-R beta antagonist.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition is administered at a dose of                0.1-100 mg/kg/body weight (preferably 1-10                mg/kg/body weight) by oral or parenteral                route.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

   BOUSAMRA M
   NANTZ M
   FU X

GA 2021B7013P
AB    NOVELTY - Non-invasive method of detecting a disease                state, or a cancer disease state in a subject                specimen, in which a primary cancer originates in a                tissue outside the lung involves obtaining exhaled                breath from the subject specimen, in the exhaled                breath includes carbonyl-containing volatile                organic compounds (VOCs), forming adducts of                carbonyl-containing VOCs with a reactive chemical                compound, quantifying each of the adducts of each                of the carbonyl-containing VOCs to establish a                subject value for each of the adducts, and                comparing each subject value to a threshold healthy                specimen value for each of the adducts of the                carbonyl-containing VOCs, where the threshold                healthy specimen value corresponding to a value                calculated from healthy specimens, in order to                determine the presence of subject values at                quantities greater than their respective threshold                healthy specimen values for indicating a                substantial likelihood of a cancer disease state in                the subject specimen.
   USE - The method is useful for non-invasive                detection of a cancer disease state in a subject                specimen, in which a primary cancer originates in a                tissue outside the lung, where the cancer disease                state is selected from supraglottic squamous cell                carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, melanoma, colon                cancer, breast cancer, renal cell carcinoma,                prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, esophageal cancer,                chondrosarcoma, cholangiocarcinoma, lymphoma, and                squamous skin cancer (claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                non-invasive method of screening for the cancer                disease state in the subject specimen involving                concentrating carbonyl-containing VOCs contained in                exhaled breath obtained from the subject specimen,                which form adducts with a reactive chemical                compound, forming adducts of the                carbonyl-containing VOCs, quantifying the adducts                of the carbonyl-containing VOCs to establish a                subject value for each member of the adducts of the                carbonyl-containing VOCs, and comparing the subject                value for each member of the adducts of the                carbonyl-containing VOCs to a threshold healthy                specimen value for each member of the adducts of                the carbonyl-containing VOCs to determine the                presence of carbonyl-containing VOCs at quantities                greater than its respective threshold healthy                specimen value thereby indicating a substantial                likelihood of the cancer disease state in the                subject specimen.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method further                  involves concentrating carbonyl-containing VOCs                  contained in exhaled breath obtained from healthy                  specimens, where carbonyl-containing VOCs                  obtained from the healthy specimens form adducts                  with the reactive chemical compound, and                  quantifying the adducts of the                  carbonyl-containing VOCs obtained from the                  specimens to establish the threshold healthy                  specimen values for each of the adducts of the                  carbonyl-containing VOCs. The step of passing the breath sample                  through a chemical preconcentrator involves                  connecting the inflated device to an inlet of the                  chemical preconcentrator, and applying reduced                  pressure to an outlet of the chemical                  preconcentrator to induce flow of the breath                  sample from the inflated device through the                  chemical preconcentrator. The carbonyl-containing                  VOCs react with the reactive chemical compound                  via a dehydration reaction to form adducts of it.                  The step of quantifying each of the adducts                  involves analyzing each of the adducts using a                  mass spectrometer. The mass spectrometer uses                  Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass                  spectrometry. The mass spectrometer is coupled                  with a chromatography apparatus.Preferred Components: The                  carbonyl-containing VOCs comprise at least one                  VOCs comprising 2-butanone,                  2-hydroxyacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxy-2-butanone,                  4-hydroxy-2-hexenal, and a mixture of C5H10O                  compounds comprising 2-pentanone and/or pentanal. AU LALL R
   ANWAR M
AE UNIV CALIFORNIA (REGC-C)
   LALL R (LALL-Individual)
   ANWAR M (ANWA-Individual)
GA 2025303861
AB    NOVELTY - The gamma photon counter has a detector that                produces a voltage pulse in response to detecting                the scintillation light generated from the                y-photon. A digital counter is coupled to the                detector. The digital counter counts y-photon                detection events. Each y-photon detection event                corresponds to the voltage pulse produced by the                detector in response to detecting the scintillation                light generated from each y-photon incident on the                surface of the doped phosphor. An opaque material                is configured for enclosing the optical fiber. The                opaque material shields the optical fiber from                visible light not emitted by the doped                phosphor.
   USE - Gamma photon counter of wearable system                (claimed) for calculating total percent injected                activity per milliliter of tissue for tumors e.g.                gastrointestinal carcinoid tumors and organs at                risk of cancer e.g. pancreatic cancer in subject.                Uses include but are not limited to lung cancer,                gastric cancer, ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer,                colorectal cancer, oral cancer, skin cancer,                cholangiocarcinoma, melanoma and thymic                carcinoma.
   ADVANTAGE - The system can be utilized to personalize RPT,                thus improving the overall safety and efficacy of                the treatment through safe dose management. The                need for bulky scintillating crystals and                collimators is reduced by taking advantage of                longer image acquisition times since this is a                wearable and designing highly sensitive in-pixel                amplification circuitry to maximize detection                sensitivity. The interconnected array is connected                to one another and used with a single common                communication and readout circuit to prevent                excessive wiring, lower power consumption, and                reduce the complexity of data collection during the                course of therapy. The sensors are arranged in                stacks to enable energy resolution and acquire                directional photon information, which enhances                spatial resolution and accuracy of detection of the                radionuclide distribution.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a wearable system;
   a method for calculating total percent                injected activity per milliliter of tissue for                tumors and organs at risk in subject;
   a kit;
   a system for calculating total percent                injected activity per milliliter of tissue for                tumors and organs at risk in subject; and
   a method for using system for calculating                total percent injected activity per milliliter of                tissue for tumors and organs at risk in                subject.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic diagram of a                gamma photon counter.

AB    NOVELTY - A marker comprising APOC2-K70 site                lactoylation modification, is new.
   USE - The marker is used in detecting immune escape                of lung cancer cells. The antibody is used in                preparing a lung cancer immune escape detection kit                (claimed). The lactylated antibody of APOC2-K70                site is used in treating lung cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The marker produces specific APOC2-K70 site                lactylated antibody, which can specifically detect                lactylated modification of APOC2-K70 site in lung                cancer samples treated with immunotherapy, thus                predicting whether lung cancer cells are tolerant                to immunotherapy. The lactylated antibody of                APOC2-K70 site combined with immunotherapy can                effectively kill lung cancer cells.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a lactylated antigen comprising an antigen                against the marker, where the lactylated antigen is                a polypeptide having an amino acid sequence of SEQ                ID NO: 1 (sequence not defined);

   a nucleic acid, where the nucleic acid encodes                the lactylated antigen, and the nucleic acid                comprises a 45 base pair sequence (SEQ ID NO: 2)                fully defined in the specification;
   a detection kit for tumor immune escape,                comprising the antibody;
   an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay detection                kit for tumor immune escape, comprising a blocking                solution, a secondary antibody, a color developing                solution and a buffer, where the blocking solution                is 5% bovine serum albumin, the secondary antibody                is an anti-rabbit secondary antibody, the color                developing solution is tetramethyldisiloxane, and                the buffer is phosphate buffered saline; and
   an inhibitor drug, where the inhibitor drug                targets the lactylated APOC2-K70 site.

TI Non-invasive screening of e.g. human patient for            oral squamous cell carcinoma by administering            composition comprising poly(adenosine            diphosphate-ribose) polymerase inhibitor-fluorophore            onto and/or into tissue in oral cavity of subject.

   REINER T

   MEMORIAL SLOAN KETTERING CANCER CENT (SLOK-C)
GA 201664041U
AB    NOVELTY - Non-invasive screening of subject for oral                squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) comprises                administering composition comprising poly(adenosine                diphosphate-ribose) polymerase                inhibitor-fluorophore (PARPi-fl) onto and/or into                tissue in oral cavity of subject; flushing tissue                in oral cavity of subject to reduce or remove                unbound components of composition while leaving                bound components of composition; and detecting                fluorescence from fluorophore after administering                and flushing steps to identify potential                OSCC.
   USE - Non-invasive screening of e.g. human patient                for oral squamous cell carcinoma.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is also suitable for intraoperative                detection of tumor margin and/or residual tumor                tissue during tumor removal surgery, in which                tissue is from cancers of aerodigestive tract,                gastrointestinal tract, urinary tract, ovarian                cancer, oral cancer, colorectal cancer, stomach                cancer, bladder cancer, cervical cancer, retinal                cancer, skin cancer, lung cancer, bronchus cancer,                esophageal cancer, or cancer that can be observed                close to tissue surface with laparoscopic                microscope (e.g. pancreatic, liver, kidney, spleen)                or cancer that is surgically resected, and where                tissue margins can be observed (e.g. brain). The                administration of composition enables PET imaging.                The topical application of PARPi-fl and subsequent                intraoperative imaging of oral cavities can improve                surgical removal of squamous cell carcinoma cells                compared to healthy cells. The method provides                robust and reliable imaging agent for oral cancer                in oral cavity, thus capable of detecting malignant                growth of mucosa while still local and                treatable.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   assessment of efficacy of cancer therapy in                subject receiving treatment for oral                carcinoma;
   composition comprising PARP inhibitor                conjugated to fluorophore for use as imaging agent                or for use in in-vivo diagnosis; and
   kit comprising PARP inhibitor conjugated to                fluorophore.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Component: The PARPi-fl binds to                  poly(adenosine diphosphate-ribose) polymerase 1                  (PARP1) and preferentially accumulates (or only                  accumulates) in area of elevated PARP1                  expression, thus signifying OSCC at area of                  accumulation.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: The method is performed in                  dentist office or other non-surgical setting. The                  flushing step involves waiting period following                  administering step such that tissue clears                  unbound components of composition via lymphatic                  system or endocytosis; and rinsing or gargling                  with water or saline. The potential OSCC is                  identified at area of accumulation using                  fluorescence scanning imaging device following                  exposure of oral cavity tissue to excitation                  light. The cancer therapy comprises chemotherapy,                  radiation, or surgery. The administering step                  occurs subsequent to cancer therapy. The method                  further comprises administering composition                  comprising 18F-PARPi to subject.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Component: The fluorophore                  comprises boron-dipyrromethene (e.g.                  4,4-difluoro-4-bora-3a,4a-diaza-s-indacene-3-propionic                  acid or salt, moiety, or their equivalent). It is                  conjugated to PARPi or fluorophore and/or at                  least one PARPi moiety is modified to permit                  conjugation. The PARPi-fl has molecular weight of                  &#8815; 1000 Da, preferably &#8815; 800                  Da. It has at least moderate lipophilicity to                  permit penetration into cell nucleus. The                  fluorophore moiety has molecular weight of                  &#8815; 500 Da, preferably &#8815; 300                  Da.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Component: The PARP inhibitor                  comprises AZD2281, AG014699 (rucaparib), ABT888                  (veliparib), BSI2O1 (iniparib), BSI101, DR2313,                  FR 247304, GP115427, GP116539, M4827, NU1025,                  NU1064, NU1085, PD128763, PARP Inhibitor H                  (INIH2BP), PARP Inhibitor m (DPQ), PARP Inhibitor                  VHI (PJ34), PARP Inhibitor IX (EB-47), or                  TIQ-A.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition in form of liquid including                oral rinse, mouthwash, or spray is administered via                intravenous injection or local intramuscular                injection; or in form of gel, paste, or other solid                or spray is administered via topical administration                (claimed). No dosage details gives.

TI Method for calibrating near field synthetic            aperture radar system for detecting breast cancer,            involves scanning reflective and absorbing materials to            create scanning and absorbing profiles based on which            calibrated profile is created.
AU FABRY H
   HENRY T R
   STOLPMAN J L
   STOLPMAN J
   HENRY T
AE INTERSTITIAL LLC (INTE-Non-standard)
   STOLPMAN J L (STOL-Individual)
   FABRY H (FABR-Individual)
   HENRY T R (HENR-Individual)
   INTERSTITIAL LLC (INTE-Non-standard)
   INTERSTITIAL LLC (INTE-Non-standard)
GA 2009L22066
AB    NOVELTY - Several antennas (12) are positioned adjacent                a surface in which the breast tissue is placed. A                reflective material is scanned by the antennas to                create a scanning profile. An absorbing material is                scanned by the antennas to create an absorbing                profile. A calibrated profile is created using the                scanning profile and the absorbing profile. The                breast tissue is scanned to create an uncalibrated                profile. The uncalibrated profile is corrected                using the calibrated profile.
   USE - Method for calibrating near field synthetic                aperture radar system for detecting breast                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The uncalibrated profile of the breast tissue                is corrected using the calibrated profile. The                effects caused by unwanted reflections between the                antennas and skin-air interface can be eliminated.                Hence the desired returns from tumors are not                masked and the capability for early detection of                cancer is not degraded.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for system                for determining localized differences in human                tissue for detecting breast cancer.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows the block diagram of the                near field synthetic aperture radar system.

TI Use of MiR-205-5p in preparing angiogenesis agent,            comprising for quantitative real-time qRT-PCR to detect            the expression of miR-205-5p and CD31 in human gastric            cancer tissues and liver metastases.
AU ZHANG J
   PANG X
   WANG X
   CUI Y
   LIU Y
AE UNIV PEKING FIRST HOSPITAL (UYPK-C)
GA 2020C4843Y
AB    NOVELTY - Use of MiR-205-5p in preparing angiogenesis                agent, comprising (i) for quantitative real-time                qRT-PCR to detect the expression of miR-205-5p and                CD31 in human gastric cancer tissues and liver                metastases, (ii) studying the effect of miR-205-5p                silence and high expression through in-vitro                detection of human umbilical vein endothelial cell                capillary formation and in vivo dorsal skin fold                chamber model, and (iii) for qRT-PCR and western                blot to detect the effect of miR-205-5p on the                expression of VEGFA and FGF1, and MiR-205-5p                down-regulates the expression of VEGFA and FGF1                through the ERK signaling pathway and directly                targeted, is claimed.
   USE - The MiR-205-5p is useful in preparing                angiogenesis agent for inhibiting angiogenesis in                gastric cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The MiR-205-5p inhibits gastric cancer                angiogenesis, plays an important role in                angiogenesis, regulates the expression of VEGFA to                reduce the formation of new blood vessels, and                plays an important role in proliferation and                invasion of different types of tumors.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The MiR-205-5p further                  determines the effect of miR-205-5p expression on                  angiogenesis in-vivo, utilizes different types of                  GC cell clones to establish xenograft models,                  utilizes immuno-histochemical method to detect                  the microvessel density of liver metastases and                  xenografts, and utilizes xenotransplantation                  model for mouse model. In the step (iii), the                  dual luciferase reporter method was used to                  verify the interaction between the 3'-UTR of FGF1                  and VEGFA, and the dual luciferase reporter                  method showed that miR-205-5p directly targets                  the 3'-UTR of VEGFA and FGF1 mRNA, regulates the                  expression of endogenous VEGFA and FGF1, thus                  VEGFA and FGF1 are the direct targets of                  miR-205-5p, and miR-205-5p regulates the                  expression of endogenous VEGFA and FGF1 by                  targeting the ERK signaling pathway and directly                  interacting with miRNA-mRNA. The number of                  different types of cells is 1x 106, and the                  experimental subject is animals.
   ACTIVITY - Angiogenesis-inhibitor.

Including testing of body fluids (other than blood typing or cell counting), pharmaceuticals or veterinary compounds of unknown structure, testing of microorganisms for pathogenicity, testing of chemicals for mutagenicity or human toxicity and fermentative production of DNA or RNA.
