AB    NOVELTY - Accurate detection of cancer comprises:                providing a sample, preferably a sample comprising                a biofluid or tissue, where the biofluid is blood,                serum, or plasma, or the tissue is a tissue lysate,                from a subject; and determining a level of open                reading frame 1 (ORF1p) in the sample with an                ultrasensitive protein assay.
   USE - The method is useful for accurate detection of                cancer, where the cancer is a carcinoma, the                carcinoma is ovarian, breast, liver,                colon/colorectal, lung, esophageal, prostate,                gastric, head and neck, brain (optionally                glioblastoma), soft tissue, kidney, gallbladder,                bile duct (cholangiocarcinoma), bladder, uterine,                or pancreatic cancer, blood or bone marrow                (optionally lymphoma, leukemia, or myeloma), or                skin cancer (optionally melanoma), and the ovarian                cancer is high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC)                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method: is minimally invasive; facilitates                widespread screening; and provides detection and                quantification of blood biomarkers such as ORF1p                for developing a robust assay.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   ingle domain antibody or it's antigen-binding                fragment that binds to human ORF1p, comprising                either a sequence at least 90% identical to a                nanobody sequence or complementarity determining                region (CDR)1, CDR2, and CDR3 form it as given in                table B of the specification, or CDR1, CDR2, and                CDR3 as given in table B of the                specification;
   fusion construct comprising at least 2,                optionally at least 5 of the single domain                antibodies or it's antigen-binding fragments,                optionally with linkers between it, as given in                table C, optionally MT1032, MT1033, MT1034, MT1035,                MT1036, MT1037, MT1038, MT1039, and MT1040;
   antibody or it's antigen binding portion that                specifically binds to human ORF1p, comprising at                least one of a heavy chain variable region (VH)                comprising a VH sequence that is at least 95%                identical to a sequence as given in table D or                figure 20 A-J of the specification, or CDR1, CDR2,                and CDR3 from it, and/or a light chain variable                region (VL) comprising a VL sequence that is at                least 95% identical to a sequence as given in table                D or figure 20 A-J of the specification, or CDR1,                CDR2, and CDR3 from it, preferably where the VH and                VL or CDRs are from the same antibody;
   nucleic acid molecule encoding the                single-domain antibody or it's antigen-binding                fragment, the fusion construct, or the antibody or                it's antigen binding portion;
   vector comprising the nucleic acid molecule,                and optionally a promoter; and
   host cell comprising the nucleic acid                molecule, and optionally expressing the                single-domain antibody or it's antigen-binding                fragment, the fusion construct, or the antibody or                it's antigen binding portion.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method further                  comprises comparing the level of ORF1p to a                  disease reference, where a level of ORF1p above                  the reference indicates that the subject has or                  is at risk of developing cancer. In the method:                  determining a level of ORF1p comprises contacting                  the sample with a capture or detection reagent                  comprising a nanobody comprising Nb2, Nb5, Nb9,                  Nb10, or NB21 or an ORF1p-binding derivative                  comprising CDRs, or it's concatemer, optionally                  MT1032, MT1033, MT1034, MT1035, MT1036, MT1037,                  MT1038, MT1039, or MT1040, and/or a monoclonal                  antibody comprises 62H12, 64C6, 33A8, 61A11,                  36D12, 34H7, 50E9, 34C5, 55A6, 42D10, 4H1, Ab6,                  Ab54 or it's antigen-binding fragment, optionally                  where the capture/detection reagents are                  62H12/MT1036, 62H12/MT1037, 62H12/MT1038,                  62H12/Ab6, 34H7/Nb5-5LL, 34H7/Ab6, 62H12/Nb5-5LL,                  4H1/Nb5-5, or 4H1/Nb5-5LL. The method further                  comprises: recommending or sending the subject                  for additional evaluation, optionally by imaging                  and/or biopsy; and administering a treatment for                  cancer to a subject who has been identified as                  having or at risk of developing cancer. The                  method further comprises determining a level of                  ORF1p in the subject after administration of the                  treatment, and comparing the level of ORF1p prior                  to treatment with the level of ORF1p during                  and/or after treatment, where a decrease in the                  level of ORF1p indicates that the treatment is                  efficient in treating the cancer. The antibody                  comprises a constant region, optionally as given                  in table A of the specification. Preferred                  Components: The ultrasensitive assay is                  single-molecule arrays (SIMOA), molecular on-bead                  signal amplification for individual counting                  (MOSAIC), meso scale discovery (MSD),                  single-molecule counting (SMC), nucleic acid                  linked immune-sandwich assay (NULISA),                  Luminex(RTM: Immunoassay), SOMAscan assay(RTM:                  Aptamer-based proteomics assay), NAB-SURE(RTM:                  Competitive immunoassay version of SPEAR), mass                  spectrometry (optionally matrix-assisted laser                  desorption/ionization (MALDI)-mass spectrometry                  (MS)), and/or mass cytometry (optionally                  Cytometry by Time-Of-Flight(RTM: Mass                  cytometry)). The nanobody comprises a sequence at                  least 80%, preferably at least 95% identical to a                  sequence as given in table B of the                  specification, preferably where the CDRs of the                  nanobody are identical to those from a sequence                  as given in table B of the specification. The                  treatment comprises chemotherapy, hormone                  therapy, immunotherapy, radiation, or surgical                  resection. The antibody comprises a constant                  region, optionally as given in table A of the                  specification. The single domain antibody or it's                  antigen-binding fragment, the fusion construct,                  or the antibody or it's antigen binding portion                  is fused to a tag, where the tag is an                  oligonucleotide, peptide, chemiluminescent,                  fluorescent, radioactive, or colorimetric label.                  The radiolabel is iodine 125.

TI Providing information for diagnosing cancer and            predicting cancer type, by aligning sequence            information (reads) to reference genome database,            deriving terminal sequence motif frequencies,            generating vectorized data, and determining presence or            absence of cancer.
AU CHO E H
   LEE T
   AHN J M
   LEE J
   KI C
   CHO E
   RIM L T
   KI C S
AE GC GENOME CORP (GREC-C)
   GC GENOME CO LTD (GREC-C)
GA 2025800839
AB    NOVELTY - Method (A) for providing information for                diagnosing cancer and predicting cancer type                involves (a) obtaining sequence information of                nucleic acid extracted from a biological sample,                (b) aligning the obtained sequence information                (reads) to a reference genome database, (c)                deriving terminal sequence motif frequencies and                sizes of nucleic acid fragments using the aligned                sequence information (reads), (d) generating                vectorized data using the derived terminal sequence                motif frequencies and sizes of nucleic acid                fragments, (e) correcting batch effects in the                vectorized data using the global reference value of                a negative control (NC), (f) post-processing the                corrected data, (g) inputting the post-processed                data into a trained artificial intelligence (AI)                model and comparing the analyzed output values with                a cut-off value to determine the presence or                absence of cancer, and (h) predicting the cancer                type by comparing the output results.
   USE - The method (A) is useful for providing                information for diagnosing cancer and predicting                cancer type. The cancer includes ovarian cancer,                soft tissue sarcoma, peripheral T-cell cancer,                colorectal cancer, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma,                glioblastoma, esophageal cancer, cutaneous T-cell                lymphoma, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, urinary tract                cancer, basal cell carcinoma, epithelioid sarcoma,                pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer,                Hodgkin's lymphoma, renal cell carcinoma,                mesothelioma, metastatic uveal melanoma, kidney                cancer, hematological cancer, HER2-expressing                cancer, non-melanoma skin cancer, liposarcoma,                hepatocellular carcinoma, small lymphocytic                lymphoma, prostate cancer, breast cancer, anal                cancer, marginal zone lymphoma, cutaneous squamous                cell carcinoma, thyroid cancer, medullary thyroid                cancer, triple-negative breast cancer,                neuroendocrine prostate cancer, bladder cancer,                paraganglioma, medulloblastoma, superficial basal                cell carcinoma, head and neck squamous cell                carcinoma, hematological cancer, melanoma, B-cell                lymphoma, relapsed/refractory acute myeloid                leukemia, hemangiosarcoma, osteosarcoma, refractory                cervical cancer, cholangiocarcinoma,                gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, rhabdomyosarcoma,                carcinoma, non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer,                uveal melanoma, small cell lung cancer, cervical                cancer, primary open-angle glaucoma, follicular                lymphoma, synovial sarcoma, liver cancer,                carcinosarcoma, leptomeningeal brain tumor, T-cell                lymphoma, small cell lung cancer, mantle cell                lymphoma, B-cell malignancies, endometrial cancer,                metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma, neuroblastoma,                chronic lymphocytic leukemia, tendon sheath giant                cell tumor, acute myeloid leukemia, skin cancer,                nasopharyngeal cancer, relapsed/refractory Ewing                sarcoma, bone cancer, glioma, salivary gland                carcinoma, stomach cancer, and benign tumor.
   ADVANTAGE - The method improves detection accuracy of                cancer patients by correcting for experimental                batch effects in cell-free nucleic acid fragment                whole-genome sequencing data, and predicts cancer                type with high sensitivity and accuracy.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method (B) for diagnosing cancer and                predicting cancer type involves performing the                above-mentioned steps (a)-(h);
   a device comprising a decoding unit that                decodes sequence information of nucleic acids                extracted from a biological sample, an alignment                unit that aligns the decoded sequence to a standard                chromosome sequence database, a nucleic acid                fragment analysis unit that derives terminal                sequence motif frequencies and fragment sizes of                nucleic acid fragments based on the aligned                sequences, a data generation unit that generates                vectorized data using the derived terminal sequence                motif frequencies and fragment sizes of the nucleic                acid fragments and then corrects for batch effects                in the vectorized data using reference values of a                NC and then performs post-processing, a cancer                diagnosis unit that inputs the generated                post-processed vectorized data into a trained                artificial intelligence model for analysis and                compares it with a reference value to determine the                presence or absence of cancer, and a cancer type                prediction unit that analyzes the output results to                predict the type of cancer; and
   a computer-readable storage medium comprising                instructions configured to-be-executed by a                processor for diagnosing cancer and predicting                cancer types by performing the above-mentioned                steps (a)-(h).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The step (a) is performed                  by a method involves (a-i) obtaining nucleic                  acids from a biological sample, (a-ii) removing                  proteins, lipids, and other residues from the                  collected nucleic acids using a salting-out                  method, a column chromatography method, or a bead                  method, for obtaining purified nucleic acids,                  (a-iii) constructing a single-end sequencing or                  pair-end sequencing library from the purified                  nucleic acids or from nucleic acids randomly                  fragmented by enzymatic digestion, grinding, or                  Hydroshear(RTM: DNA shearing device), (a-iv)                  reacting the constructed library with a                  next-generation sequencer, and (a-v) obtaining                  nucleic acid sequence information (reads) from a                  next-generation genetic sequencer. The terminal                  sequence motif of step (c) is a pattern of 2-30                  base sequences at both ends of the nucleic acid                  fragment. The terminal sequence motif frequency                  of step (c) is the number of each motif detected                  in the entire nucleic acid fragment. The size of                  the nucleic acid fragment of step (c) is the                  number of bases from the 5' end to the 3' end of                  the nucleic acid fragment. The vectorized data of                  step (d) is characterized in that the X-axis                  represents the type of nucleic acid fragment                  terminal sequence motif and the Y-axis represents                  the size of the nucleic acid fragment. The step                  (e) is performed by a method involves (e-i)                  calculating a global reference value for the                  entire negative control group, (e-ii) calculating                  a normalization factor (NF) by comparing the                  median value of the negative control group within                  the batch with the global reference value, and                  (e-iii) obtaining a normalization value by                  multiplying the vectorized data by the                  normalization factor. The global reference value                  is the median of vectorized data of the entire                  negative control group. The step (e-ii) is                  calculated using a formula: normalization factor                  feature = (global reference feature/batch NCs                  median feature), where the feature is                  characterized by the type of terminal sequence                  motif of each nucleic acid fragment and the                  frequency value of each nucleic acid fragment                  according to its size. The step (f) is performed                  by a method involves (f-i) calculating the mean                  and standard deviation of the frequency values                  for each type of nucleic acid fragment terminal                  sequence motif and each size of nucleic acid                  fragment in the normal group, (f-ii) performing                  Z-normalization by subtracting the mean of the                  frequency values for each type of nucleic acid                  fragment terminal sequence motif and each size of                  nucleic acid fragment in the normal group from                  the frequency values for each type of nucleic                  acid fragment terminal sequence motif and each                  size of nucleic acid fragment in the sample, and                  dividing the result by the standard deviation of                  the frequency values for each type of nucleic                  acid fragment terminal sequence motif and each                  size of nucleic acid fragment to derive a                  Z-normalization value, and (f-iii) correcting the                  Z-normalization value derived in step (f-ii) to a                  reference value if it exceeds the reference                  range. The reference range is -5 to 5, and the                  reference value is -5 or 5. The AI model of step                  (f) learns to distinguish between healthy                  vectorized data and cancer vectorized data. The                  AI model is chosen from a convolutional neural                  network (CNN), a deep neural network (DNN), a                  multi-layer perceptron (MLP), and a recurrent                  neural network (RNN), where if the AI model is an                  MLP, the loss function is expressed by specific                  equation. The output value of the AI model in                  step (g) analyzing the input vectorized data is a                  Deep Probability Index (DPI) value. The reference                  value in step (g) is 0.5, and a value &#8805;                  0.5 determines cancer. The step of predicting the                  cancer type by comparing the output result values                  of step (h) is performed by determining the                  cancer type showing the highest value among the                  output result values as the cancer of the                  sample.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details of method for                extracting DNA from blood and performing                next-generation base sequence analysis that do not                support the claims.

Preferred Method: The method of                  detecting presence and/or amount of CD8 in a                  biological sample, comprises (i) contacting the                  biological sample and the control sample under                  conditions enabling the formation of a complex                  between the CD8-binding polypeptide or the                  conjugated molecule and CD8 CD8-binding                  polypeptides of the invention or conjugated                  molecules, and (ii) detecting complex formation,                  where the differences in complex formation                  between the biological sample and a control                  sample are indicative of the presence and/or                  amount of CD8 in the sample. The method of                  detecting presence and/or amount of CD8 positive                  cells in tissue, comprises (iii) contacting the                  tissue with the conjugated molecule or the                  detection agent, and (iv) determining the                  presence and/or amount of CD8 positive cells in                  the tissue. The method for predicting                  the response of subject with tumor to an                  anti-tumor therapy, comprises administering                  conjugated molecule or the detection agent to the                  subject, and imaging the subject, e.g. ECT                  imaging, to determine whether the subject's tumor                  comprising CD8 positive cells, where the subject                  is identified as being suitable for anti-tumor                  therapy if the presence of CD8 positive cells in                  the tumor is detected, e.g. the subject's tumor                  is infiltrated by CD8 positive cells, the                  individual is likely to respond to anti-tumor                  therapy. The method of treating tumor in subject,                  comprises administering conjugated molecule or                  the detection agent to the subject, and imaging                  the subject, e.g. ECT imaging, to determine                  whether the subject's tumor comprising CD8                  positive cells, where the subject is administered                  an anti-tumor therapy if the presence of CD8                  positive cells in the tumor is detected, e.g. the                  subject's tumor is infiltrated by CD8 positive                  cells. The method for monitoring the efficacy of                  anti-tumor therapy in subject, comprises                  administering conjugated molecule or the                  detection agent to the subject having tumor and                  being treated with an anti-tumor therapy, and                  imaging the subject, e.g. ECT imaging, to                  determine the amount of CD8 positive cells in the                  subject's tumor, where the anti-tumor therapy is                  immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, and the                  anti-tumor therapy is chosen by administering a                  programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor,                  programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) inhibitors,                  cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen                  (CTLA-4)inhibitors, T-cell immunoglobulin and                  mucin domain 3 (TIM3) inhibitors, B and T                  lymphocyte attenuator (BTLA) inhibitors, T-cell                  immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin and ITIM                  domains (TIGIT) inhibitors, CD47 inhibitors,                  glucocorticoid-induced TNFR-related protein                  (GITR) inhibitor, lymphocyte-activation gene 3                  (LAG3) inhibitor, antagonist of another T cell                  co-inhibitor or ligand,                  indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) inhibitors,                  vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)                  antagonists, Ang2 inhibitors, transforming growth                  factor &#946; (TGF&#946; ) inhibitors,                  epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)                  inhibitors, CD20 inhibitors, antibodies against                  tumor-specific antigens, vaccines, adjuvants that                  increase antigen presentation, bispecific                  antibodies, cytotoxins, chemotherapeutics,                  cyclophosphamide, radiotherapy, interleukin-6                  receptor (IL-6R) inhibitors, IL-4R inhibitors,                  IL-10 inhibition agents, cytokines, and                  antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The method for                  isolating and/or purifying CD8 positive cells,                  comprises providing a population of cells                  suspected of containing CD8 positive cells,                  identifying a subpopulation of the cell                  population, where the cells of which bind the                  CD8-binding polypeptide or the conjugated                  molecule; and isolating the subpopulation. The                  method for isolating CD8 positive cells,                  comprises providing a population of cells                  suspected of containing CD8 positive cells;                  contacting the cell population with the                  CD8-binding polypeptide or the conjugated                  molecule, for allowing CD8 positive cells to bind                  to the CD8 binding polypeptide or the conjugated                  molecule; removing cells that are not bound to                  the CD8-binding polypeptide or the conjugated                  molecule; and recovering CD8-positive cells that                  bind to the CD8-binding polypeptide or conjugated                  molecule. The cell population comprising CD8                  positive cells is human peripheral blood                  mononuclear cells (PBMC). The CD8-binding                  polypeptide or the conjugated molecule is                  immobilized on a solid surface, e.g. a gel or a                  magnetic bead surface.

TI Use of compound causing decrease of intracellular            pH for treating cancer, preferably melanoma, or head            and neck cancer with inhibitor of mitochondrial            respiration and proton ionophore.
AU MELNIK S
   MUELLER-DECKER K
   NIEHRS C
   GLINKA A
AE DEUT KREBSFORSCHUNGSZENTRUM (DEKR-C)
GA 2020B6530W
AB    NOVELTY - Use of compound causing decrease of                intracellular pH is claimed, for treating cancer                with an inhibitor of mitochondrial respiration and                a proton ionophore.
   USE - The compound is useful for treating cancer                with an inhibitor of mitochondrial respiration and                a proton ionophore or determining whether a subject                suffering from cancer is susceptible to a combined                treatment. The cancer is pancreas cancer,                colorectal cancer, preferably colon carcinoma, lung                cancer, preferably non-small cell lung cancer,                liver cancer, breast cancer, skin cancer,                preferably melanoma, or head and neck cancer (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   use of proton ionophore for treating cancer                with an inhibitor of mitochondrial respiration and                a compound causing a decrease of intracellular                pH;
   use of inhibitor of mitochondrial respiration                for treating cancer with a proton ionophore and a                compound causing a decrease of intracellular                pH;
   a combined preparation for simultaneous,                separate or sequential use comprising (i) a                compound causing a decrease of intracellular pH,                (ii) an inhibitor of mitochondrial respiration, and                (iii) a proton ionophore; and
   a method for determining whether a subject                suffering from cancer is susceptible to a combined                treatment involves administering a compound causing                a decrease of intracellular pH, an inhibitor of                mitochondrial respiration, and a proton ionophore,                by (a) detecting an inhibitor of mitochondrial                respiration, and a proton ionophore in a sample of                cancer cells of subject whether the cancer cells                (i) are wingless-type MMTV integration site family                (Wnt) signaling-dependent cancer cells, (ii) are                transforming growth factor (TGF)-&#946;                signaling-dependent cancer cells, and/or (iii) show                a decrease in viability upon administration of                compound causing a decrease of intracellular pH,                and (b) determining whether the subject suffering                from cancer is susceptible to a combined treatment                by administering compound causing a decrease of                intracellular pH, an inhibitor of mitochondrial                respiration, and a proton ionophore based on the                result of the detection of step (a).

TI New pharmaceutical composition comprising a compound capable of specifically inhibiting or blocking the binding of HPV protein E7 to Pdcd4 protein, and a carrier, useful for treating or preventing non-melanoma skin cancer.
AU PFISTER H
   AKGUEL B
AE CELL CENT COLOGNE GMBH (CELL-Non-standard)
GA 2006020430
AB    NOVELTY - A pharmaceutical composition for treating or preventing a tumor comprising a compound capable of specifically inhibiting or blocking the binding of human papilloma viruses (HPV) protein E7 to programmed cell death 4 (Pdcd4) protein, and optionally a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier, is new.
   USE - The pharmaceutical composition, compound, agent, kit and methods are useful for treating or preventing tumor, e.g. skin tumor, preferably non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC). The HPV E7 protein is useful for preparing a composition for inhibiting Pdcd4 apoptotic signal transduction pathway (claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for:

TI Anti-metastatic substance screening method for            e.g. breast cancer treatment, involves detecting            presence of E-cadherin at cell surface in cells, and            positively selecting candidate substance or its            combination when E-cadherin is detected.
AU ROUX P
   DE TOLEDO M
AE CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
   CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
   CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
   CNRS CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
   CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
GA 2007175815
AB    NOVELTY - A method for detecting anti-metastatic                substances involves contacting a candidate                substance or a combination of the candidate                substances with a culture of tumorous cell not                expressing E-cadherin on their cell membrane and                having the capacity of forming metastasis, and                detecting presence of E-cadherin expression on cell                surface which is stimulated by the substances. The                E-cadherin is detected using an anti-E-cadherin                antibody. The candidate substance or combination of                candidate substances is positively selected, when                E-cadherin is detected.
   USE - Used for screening an anticancer                anti-metastatic substance (claimed) such as                anti-metastatic active substances, on metastatic                cancerous cells derived from epithelial cells, for                identification of molecules of therapeutic interest                for the treatment of cancer e.g. colorectal cancer,                breast cancer, bladder cancer, ovarian cancer,                uterus cancer, neck cancer, skin cancer, stomach                cancer, epithelial cancer of thymus, prostate                cancer, testicle cancer, lung cancer, throat                cancer, pancreas cancer, liver cancer, gall-bladder                cancer and bladder cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method permits to screen the substances                directly on living cells, thus permitting to                positively select the substances that are not toxic                and having a psychological inhibition effect or                metastasis cells forming capacity, and the                substances that reverse the cancer cells towards                epithelial cells forming intercellular junctions.                The method permits the screening of anti-cancer                substances in conditions in which tested cells are                in a situation close to their in vivo psychological                situation. The detection of the E-cadherin at the                cell surface allows to verify their capacity to                reverse phenotype of treated cells towards a                non-metastatic cell, thus allowing to verify their                anti-metastatic capacity in a simple manner.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                set of kits for screening an anticancer                substance.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows an effect of Y-27632                inhibitor on a correct location of E-cadherin at                the level of inter-cellular junctions in rows of                cancer cells. `(Drawing contains non-English                language text)`
TF ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No relevant example given.

TI Detecting cancer in patient, by administering gene            delivery complex (including chimeric gene construct and            gene delivery vehicle) to patient, and detecting            secreted reporter protein or its variant in biological            sample.
AU GODBEY W T
   FANG Y
AE TULANE EDUCATIONAL FUND (TULA-C)
GA 2014T33275
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting cancer in a patient, comprises (a)                administering a gene delivery complex to a patient                suspected of having cancer, where the complex                comprises (i) a chimeric gene construct that                selectively induces cancer cells to express and                secrete reporter protein or its variant comprising                upstream regulatory element that is activated by an                overexpressed protein in the cancer cells and a                reporter gene or its variant operably linked to the                upstream regulatory element and (ii) a gene                delivery vehicle, and (b) detecting the secreted                reporter protein or its variant in a biological                sample.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting cancer                (including bladder cancer, colon cancer, carcinomas                including intestinal epithelia, esophageal squamous                cells and pancreatic cells, colorectal tumors,                adenocarcinoma, skin, prostate, lung carcinoma,                breast, cervical and ovary) and transitional cell                carcinoma cells following tumorectomy in a patient                such as mammal, preferably human (all claimed) and                for treating cancer. Test details are described but                no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method ensures economical detection of                cancers in rural and underserved areas of the                world.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting cancer cells in a patient, comprises                (a) administering a gene delivery complex to a                patient suspected of having cancer, where the gene                delivery complex comprises (i) a chimeric gene                construct that selectively induces cancer cells to                express and secrete reporter protein or its variant                comprising at least one upstream regulatory element                that is activated by an overexpressed protein in                the cancer cells and a reporter gene or its variant                operably linked to the upstream regulatory element                and (ii) a gene delivery vehicle, and (b) detecting                the secreted reporter protein or its variant in a                biological sample of the patient. The                administration occurs under conditions that permit                transfection of the cancer cells with the gene                delivery complex. The patient is diagnosed as                having cancer if the secreted reporter protein or                its variant is detected in the biological sample.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a kit for detection of cancer comprising the                gene delivery complex, and instructions for                administration;
   a chimeric gene construct to selectively                induce cancer cells to express and secrete reporter                protein comprising at least one upstream regulatory                element consisting of a cytomegalovirus promoter                (PCMV), murine cyclooxygenase-2 (mCox2) and human                osteopontin (hOPN) and at least one reporter gene                or its variant consisting of &#946; -human                chorionic gonadotropin (&#946; hCG), &#946;                2 microglolbulin (&#946; 2m) and                prostate-specific antigen (PSA) that is operably                linked to the upstream regulatory element;
   a gene delivery complex comprising the                chimeric gene construct and a gene delivery                vehicle; and
   a cultured cell comprising the gene delivery                complex.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The gene delivery                  vehicle is a non-viral delivery vehicle. The                  non-viral delivery vehicle is poly(ethylenimine)                  (preferred), Lipofectin(RTM: Synthetic lipid                  polymer), Lipofectamine(RTM: Plasmid transfection                  reagent), polylysine, and alginate. The upstream                  regulatory element is a promoter consisting of                  PCMV, mCox2, hOPN, Pcla3, phmgA2, plasmid                  Glypican 3 (Pgpc3), cytochrome coxidase subunit 2                  (Pcox2), thioredoxin-like 1 (TXNL1), heat shock                  protein 90kDa beta (Grp94), Breast cancer                  metastasis-suppressor 1 (BRMS1), RAs-related                  Nuclear protein (RAN), minichromosome maintenance                  complex component 5 (MCM5), polymerase (DNA                  directed)-&#951; (POLH), and zinc finger                  protein 394 (ZNF394). The reporter gene consists                  of &#946; hCG, &#946; 2m, PSA, matrix                  metalloproteinases, 8 catenin, hepatocyte growth                  factor, thymosin &#946; 15, alkaline                  phosphatase, and luciferase. The biological                  sample is urine. The kit further comprises a                  &#946; hCG urine cassette or dip-stick.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of the gene delivery complex is                topical, transdermal, transurethral, oral, by                inhalation, rectal, or via direct injection,                subcutaneous injection, intravenous injection or                intraperitoneal injection. No dosage details                given.

TI Detecting mutations in telomerase reverse            transcriptase promoter sequence for treating cancer,            involves incubating DNA sample comprising TERT promoter            sequence, and detecting signal from first and second            detectable label.
AU BALAJ L
   MURALIDHARAN K
   YEKULA A
   CARTER B S
AE GEN HOSPITAL CORP (GEHO-C)
   GEN HOSPITAL CORP (GEHO-C)
GA 2021630890
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting mutations in telomerase reverse                transcriptase (TERT) promoter sequence involves                incubating, in reaction mixture, DNA sample                comprising TERT promoter sequence. The DNA sample                comprises cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and exosomal                nucleic acids (exoNA) extracted from biological                fluid of subject. The pair of amplification primers                comprises forward and reverse primer comprising                nucleotides (SEQ ID NOs: 1 and 2), given in the                specification. The pair of detection primers                comprises mutant and wild-type primer comprising                nucleotides (SEQ ID NOs: 3 and 4), given in the                specification. The mutant primer comprises first                detectable label and wild-type primer comprises                second detectable label, under conditions                sufficient for amplifying TERT promoter sequence.                The signal is detected from first and second                detectable label.
   USE - Method for detecting mutations in TERT                promoter sequence used for treating cancer such as                brain cancer such as glioma selected from                astrocytoma, ependymoma and oligodendroglioma, skin                cancer, lung cancer, liver cancer, breast cancer,                thyroid cancer, adrenocortical carcinoma, ovarian                cancer, endometrial carcinoma, renal cell                carcinoma, bladder cancer and gastric cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables to improve detection                sensitivity, specificity and assay sensitivity, and                enhances ability to diagnose, monitor and assess                response to therapy.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting mutations in telomerase reverse                transcriptase (TERT) promoter sequence involves                incubating, in reaction mixture, DNA sample                comprising TERT promoter sequence. The DNA sample                comprises cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and exosomal                nucleic acids (exoNA) extracted from biological                fluid of subject. The pair of amplification primers                comprises forward and reverse primer comprising                nucleotides (SEQ ID NOs: 1 and 2), given in the                specification. The pair of detection primers                comprises mutant and wild-type primer comprising                nucleotides (SEQ ID NOs: 3 and 4), given in the                specification. The mutant primer comprises first                detectable label and wild-type primer comprises                second detectable label, under conditions                sufficient for amplifying TERT promoter sequence.                The signal is detected from first and second                detectable label. The presence of signal from first                detectable label indicates presence of mutant TERT                promoter sequence in sample. The presence of signal                from second detectable label indicates presence of                wild-type TERT promoter sequence in sample. The                mutant TERT promoter sequence comprises C228T or                C250T. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for evaluating reoccurrence of                cancer, which involves detecting TERT promoter                sequence in DNA sample from biological fluid of                subject, determining whether subject has                reoccurrence of cancer, where subject is identified                as having reoccurrence of cancer when level of                mutant TERT promoter sequences in sample is higher                than control level, and administering cancer                therapy to subject identified as having                reoccurrence of cancer; and
   a method for evaluating effectiveness of                cancer therapy, which involves detecting TERT                promoter sequence in DNA sample from biological                fluid of subject, determining whether cancer                therapy has been effective, where cancer therapy is                identified as effective when level of mutant TERT                promoter sequences in sample is higher than control                level, and administering cancer therapy identified                as effective to subject and administering another                cancer therapy to subject; and
   an amplification primer for amplifying                promoter region of telomerase reverse transcriptase                (TERT) gene, which comprises nucleotides (SEQ ID                NO: 2), given in the specification.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Process: The DNA sample is                  extracted from biological fluid using                  ExoLution(RTM: Exosome purification kit for serum                  and plasma) plus kit. The TERT promoter sequence                  is amplified by digital polymerase chain reaction                  (dPCR) or droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). Preferred                  Components: The reaction mixture further                  comprises 7-deaza-2 -deoxy-guanosine-5                  -triphosphate (7-deaza-dGTP). The mutant primer                  comprises locked nucleic acid (LNA) modification                  at positions 4, 5, 6, and 7 in nucleotides (SEQ                  ID NO: 3), given in the specification. The                  wild-type primer comprises LNA modification at                  positions 5, 6, and 7 in nucleotides (SEQ ID NO:                  4), given in the specification. The first                  detectable label comprises first fluorophore and                  first quencher. The second detectable label                  comprises second fluorophore and second quencher.                  The first and second fluorophore are selected                  from FAM, HEX, Cy3, Cy5 and Texas red. The first                  and second quencher are selected from Iowa                  Black(RTM: Dark quencher) FQ, Iowa Black RQ,                  ZEN(RTM: Double-quenched probes) quencher and                  TAMRA(RTM: 3' fluorescent quencher). The                  biological fluid is selected from plasma, urine                  and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The cancer therapy                  is selected from chemotherapy, radiation therapy,                  surgical therapy and immunotherapy. Preferred                  Conditions: The first and second fluorophore are                  different fluorophores. The first and second                  quencher are same quencher. The subject is                  treatment naive or received cancer therapy.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Topoisomerase inhibitor; Mitotic inhibitor;                Immune checkpoint inhibitor; Programmed cell                death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor; Programmed death-ligand 1                (PD-L1) inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - The cancer therapy is administered to subject                (claimed).
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

   USE -   The sequence (I) is part of the 3'-untranslated                region of the human PKC gene and comprises                sequences which are unique to the long mRNA                transcript of PKC. The probes and antisense ONs                based on this sequence are useful for detection of                the human PKC gene and of the long mRNA transcript                of human PKC The antisense ONs are useful for                modulating expression of the PKC gene or the long                mRNA transcript of PKC in a cell and so for                treatment of animals having conditions associated                with PKC . Other oligonucleotides are specific for                different PKC isozymes, i.e. other than PKC-; they                are useful for diagnosing and treating conditions                associated with PKC, esp. such hyperproliferative                disorders as psoriasis, colorectal cancer, lung                cancer, breast cancer or skin cancer.

Val-Tyr-Thr-Val-Asp-Leu-Gly-Arg (SEQ ID NO: 2), and                Val-Tyr-Thr-Val-Asp-Leu-Gly-Arg (SEQ ID NO: 4).                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:

   (2) method (M2) for screening a drug for                preventing or treating cancer involves (a) treating                a sample isolated from a cancer subject or an                animal model of cancer disease with a candidate                agent, and (b) measuring the expression level of                the polypeptide or a gene encoding the polypeptide                in a sample treated with the candidate drug or in                an animal model of cancer disease; and
   (3) apparatus comprising (i) a sample part                containing a sample obtained from a patient, (ii) a                detection unit for detecting the polypeptide or the                gene encoding the polypeptide in the sample, and                (iii) a comparison unit for comparing the                expression level of at least the polypeptide or the                gene encoding the polypeptide of the patient                obtained from the detection unit with the level of                a normal person.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecule: The agent for                  measuring the expression level of the polypeptide                  is an antibody, oligopeptide, ligand, peptide                  nucleic acid (PNA) and aptamer that specifically                  binds to the polypeptide. The                  nanoplatform further comprises a ligand monolayer                  surrounding the siloxane nanolayer. The                  nanoplatform further comprises a gold coating                  layer surrounding the ligand monolayer, where the                  nanoparticle is a core/shell nanoparticle, the                  core is selected from Au, Ag, Cu, Co, Fe, and Pt,                  and the shell is selected from Au, Ag, Cu, Co,                  Fe, Pt or their metal oxides, where the core is a                  strongly paramagnetic Fe core and the shell                  comprises iron. The nanoplatform comprises a                  Fe/Fe xO ycore/shell nanoparticle. The                  nanoplatform is linked via an oligopeptide                  linkage to a particle selected from                  chromophores/luminophores, quantum dots and/or                  viologens, where the oligopeptide linkage                  comprises a protease consensus sequence. The                  nanoplatform is unlinked to any other                  nanoplatform. Preferred Components: The first                  nanoparticle and second nanoparticles are                  respective core/shell nanoparticles. Each core is                  individually selected from Au, Ag, Cu, Co, Fe,                  and Pt. The core is a strongly paramagnetic Fe                  core. Each shell is individually selected from                  Au, Ag, Cu, Co, Fe and/or Pt or their metal                  oxides. The shell comprises iron oxide. The first                  and second nanoparticles have a                  Brunauer-Emmett-Teller multipoint surface area of                  at least about 20 m 2/g. The protective layers                  are individually selected from siloxane                  nanolayers and/or ligand monolayers. At least one                  of the protective layers is a siloxane nanolayer.                  The siloxane nanolayer is an amino functional                  siloxane layer. At least one of the protective                  layers is a ligand monolayer. The ligand                  monolayer comprises at least one member selected                  from thiols, alcohols, nitro compounds,                  phosphines, phosphine oxides, resorcinarenes,                  selenides, phosphinic acids, phosphonic acids,                  sulfonic acids, sulfonates, carboxylic acids,                  disulfides, peroxides, amines, nitriles,                  isonitriles, thionitriles, oxynitriles,                  oxysilanes, alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatic                  compounds, and seleno moieties. The functional                  group is bound directly to the protective layer.                  The particle is chromphore/luminophore selected                  from organic dyes, inorganic dyes, fluorophores                  and/or phosphophores or their metalated                  complexes. The chromophore/luminophore is an                  inorganic dye selected from porphyrins,                  phthalocyanines, chlorins, and metalated                  chromophores. Preferred Assembly: The                  nanoplatform assembly further comprises a ligand                  monolayer surrounding the siloxane nanolayer. In                  the system, the oligopeptide linkage between the                  first and second nanoparticles further comprises                  the functional group, where the functional group                  is a porphyrin selected from tetracarboxylphenyl                  porphyrin and tetrahydroxyphenyl porphyrin.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The ligand monolayer                  comprises ligands selected from T 1-CH 2-CH                  2-NH-C(O)-O-(CH 2CH 2O) n-CH 2-CH 2-O-CH 2-CH 2-R                  2, T 1-CH 2-CH 2-NH-C(O)-CH 2-CH 2-C(O)-O-(CH 2CH                  2O) n-CH 2-CH 2-O-CH 2-CH 2-R 2and/or T 1-CH 2-CH                  2-NH-C(O)-CH 2-CH 2-C(O)-R 2. The functional                  group is bound to the protective layer via a                  protease consensus sequence. The distance between                  the linked nanoplatforms is 5 nm to about 70 nm.                  The chromophore/luminophore is an organic dye                  selected from coumarins, pyrene, cyanines,                  benzenes, N-methylcarbazole, erythrosin-B,                  N-acetyl-L-tryptophanamide, 2,5-diphenyloxazole,                  rubrene, and N-(3-sulfopropyl)acridinium. The                  porphyrins are selected from                  tetracarboxy-phenyl-porphyrin (TCPP) and                  metalated-TCPP. The chromophore luminophore is a                  metalated chromophore selected from ruthenium                  polypyridyl complexes, osmium polypyridyl                  complexes, rhodium polypyridyl complexes,                  3-(1-methylbenzoimidazol-2-yl)-7-(diethylamino)-coumarin                  complexes of iridium(III), and                  3-(benzothiazol-2-yl)-7-(diethylamino)-coumarin                  complexes with iridium(III). The                  chromophore/luminophore is a fluorophore or                  phosphophor selected from phosphorescent dyes,                  fluoresceines, rbodamines, and anthracenes.T =phenyl (di-substituted on 3 and                  4-positions by R 1 );n=2-25;R =optionally protected hydroxyl                  groups;R =-OH, porphyrin of formula (i) or (ii),                  *NH-C(O)-CH 2 -NH 2 , *O-C(O)-CH 2 -NH 2 or                  biotin of formula (iii);R =-OH, -COOH or -NH 2 , -N(R 4 ) 2 , -N(R 4                  ) 3 , -NHR 4 , -NH-CO-AA or -CO-NH-AA;R =1-4C alkyl;AA=any amino acid;M=Zn 2 + , Pd 2 + , Mg 2 + , Al 3 + , Pt 2 +                  , Ni 2 + , Eu 3 + and Gd 3 + .* indicates the atom where R 2bonds to the                  ligand.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: The carrier is                  selected from aqueous buffer, liposomes, and                  tumor-tropic cells. When the carrier is an                  aqueous buffer, the composition comprises                  100-5000 &#956; g of the nanoplatform                  assembly per ml of buffer. The tumor-tropic cells                  are selected from stem cells, monocytes, and                  macrophages. The stem cells are selected from                  neural stem cells, umbilical cord matrix stem                  cells, bone marrow stem cells, and adipose                  derived mesenchymal stem cells. Preferred Method:                  The method (M) for detecting the activity of a                  protease associated with a cancerous or                  precancerous cell in a mammal, involves                  contacting a fluid sample from the mammal with a                  diagnostic assay, where the assay comprises the                  nanoplatform assembly; exposing the assay to an                  energy source; and detecting a change in the                  optical extinction of the assay, where the change                  corresponds to the protease activity. The method                  (M1) for detecting the activity of a protease                  associated with a cancerous or precancerous cell                  in a mammal involves: a) administering to the                  mammal the composition; b) locating the assay in                  a region of interest in the mammal suspected of                  having a cancerous or precancerous cell; c)                  exposing the region to an energy source; and d)                  detecting the back-scattering spectrum of the                  assay. The method (M3) inhibiting the growth of                  cancerous or precancerous cells in a mammal                  involves administering to the mammal the                  composition; locating the assay in a region of                  interest in the mammal suspected of having a                  cancerous or precancerous cell; and heating the                  nanoplatform using magnetic A/C-excitation, so                  that the tissue in the region of interest is                  heated to a temperature of at least about                  40&#176; C. The MRI imaging method (T1) for                  detecting the activity of a protease associated                  with a cancerous or precancerous cell in a mammal                  involves administering to the mammal the                  composition; locating the assay in a region of                  interest in the mammal suspected of having a                  cancerous or precancerous cell; transmitting                  radio frequency pulses to the region of interest;                  and acquiring MR image data of the region of                  interest, the MR image data comprising T1 and T2                  values. The method (M4) of monitoring the                  progress of cancer treatment in a mammal                  diagnosed with cancer involves contacting a first                  fluid sample from the mammal with a first                  diagnostic assay, where the assay comprises the                  nanoplatform; exposing the first assay to an                  energy source; and detecting the changes in the                  absorption or emission spectrum of the first                  assay over time relative to the absorption or                  emission spectrum of the first assay prior to                  contact with the first fluid sample, where the                  changes correspond to a first level of protease                  activity in the first sample. The energy source                  is selected from a polychromatic light source,                  laser, and laser-diode. The change is                  automatically detected by a UV/Vis spectrometer.                  The fluid sample is selected from urine and                  blood. A change in the optical extinction of                  about 0.001 to about 1 indicates the presence of                  a cancerous or precancerous cell in the mammal.                  The concentration of the assay in the sample is                  10 pg to 1000 &#956; of nanoplatform per ml                  of sample. The change in the optical extinction                  of the assay is observed over a time period of 30                  seconds to about 24 hours. The change in the                  optical extinction of the assay indicates the                  activity of a protease selected from uPA, MMP-1,                  MMP-2, MMP-7, and/or MMP-9. The detection method                  further involves correlating the protease                  activity with a prognosis for cancer progression.                  The detection of activity of both uPA and MMP-7,                  and absence of activity of MMP-1, MMP-2, and                  MMP-9 is correlated with a prognosis for                  angiogenesis. The detection of activity of all of                  uPA, MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-7 and MMP-9 is correlated                  with a prognosis for cell invasion. The                  administering step (a) involves injecting the                  composition directly into the region of the                  mammal suspected of having a cancerous or                  precancerous cell; or injecting the composition                  into the bloodstream of the mammal. The signal of                  the backscattering spectrum in method (M1) is                  stronger in the region of interest of the mammal                  suspected of having a cancerous or precancerous                  cell than in surrounding regions. The signal in                  method (M1) is 2-100 times stronger in the region                  of interest of the mammal suspected of having a                  cancerous or precancerous cell than in                  surrounding regions. The method (M1) further                  involves detecting a loss in the backscattering                  spectrum signal over a period of time of from                  about 30 seconds to about 24 hours. The loss of                  the backscattering spectrum is detected as a                  change in the optical extinction of the assay,                  and the change indicates the protease activity. A                  change in the optical extinction of about 0.05 to                  about 1 indicates the presence of a cancerous or                  precancerous cell in the mammal. The method                  further involves correlating the protease                  activity with a prognosis for cancer progression.                  The protease activity detected within 10 minutes                  after locating the assay in the region is                  correlated with a high probability that the                  cancerous or precancerous cell is aggressive. The                  absence of protease activity detection within the                  first 30 minutes after locating the assay is                  correlated with a very low probability that the                  cancerous or precancerous cell is aggressive. The                  loss of the backscattering spectrum signal                  indicates the activity of a protease selected                  from uPA, MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-7 and/or MMP-9. The                  detection of activity of both uPA and MMP-7, and                  the absence of activity of MMP-1, MMP-2, and                  MMP-9, is correlated with a prognosis for                  angiogenesis. The detection of activity of all of                  uPA, MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-7, MMP-9 is con-elated                  with a prognosis for cell invasion. The protease                  activity results in at least two oligopeptide                  sequences selected from Gly-Gly-Val-Pro-Met-Ser                  (SEQ ID No. 43), The MR image data is automatically                  acquired by a computer. The MRI imaging method                  further involves automatically generating an                  image from the acquired MR image data; and                  repeating the transmitting and acquiring steps                  over a time period of at least about two days.                  The radio frequency pulses in MRI imaging method                  comprise a Carr-Purcell Meiboom-Gill spin-echo                  pulse sequence. The MR image data is T2-weighted.                  The MRI imaging method further involves detecting                  a change in the acquired T2 values over time, the                  change corresponding to protease activity. A                  change in the T2 values of a factor of 5 to about                  a factor of 10 is correlated with developing                  cancer. A change in the T2 values of greater than                  about a factor of 10 is correlated to metastatic                  cancer. The T1 values remain unchanged over time.                  The acquiring step begins about 1 minute to about                  24 hours after the administering step. The                  concentration of the nanoplatform assembly in the                  region of interest is 1 &#956; g/g of tissue                  to about 1000 &#956; g/g of tissue. The MRI                  imaging method (M2) for detecting the activity of                  a protease associated with a cancerous or                  precancerous cell in a mammal involves                  administering to the mammal a composition                  comprising a diagnostic assay including the                  nanoplatform assembly, where the protease                  consensus sequence is Ser-Gly-Arg-Ser-Ala (SEQ ID                  No. 2); locating the assay in a region of                  interest in the mammal suspected of having a                  cancerous or precancerous cell; transmitting                  radio frequency pulses to the region of interest;                  and acquiring MR image data of the region of                  interest, where the MR image data comprises T1                  and T2 values. In method (M2) when the MR image                  data indicates protease activity, the method                  further involves administering to the mammal a                  composition comprising a diagnostic assay                  including the nanoplatform assembly, where the                  protease consensus sequence is                  Val-Pro-Leu-Ser-Leu-Thr-Met-Gly (SEQ ID No. 6);                  locating the assay in a region of interest in the                  mammal suspected of having a cancerous or                  precancerous cell; transmitting radio frequency                  pulses to the region of interest; and acquiring                  MR image data of the region of interest, where                  the MR image data comprises T1 and T2 values.                  When the MR image indicates protease activity,                  the activity is correlated to a prognosis for                  angiogenesis or metastasis and the method (M2)                  further involves administering to the mammal a                  composition comprising a diagnostic assay                  including the nanoplatform assembly, where the                  protease consensus sequence is SEQ ID No. 3;                  locating the assay in a region of interest in the                  mammal suspected of having a cancerous or                  precancerous cell; transmitting radio frequency                  pulses to the region of interest; and acquiring                  MR image data of the region of interest, where                  the MR image data comprises T1 and T2 values.                  When protease activity is not indicated by the MR                  image data, the MR image data is correlated to a                  prognosis for angiogenesis. When the MR image                  data indicates protease activity, the protease                  activity is correlated to a prognosis for                  metastasis. The method (M2) further involves                  heating the first and second nanoplatforms using                  magnetic A/C-excitation. The tissue in the region                  of interest it heated to at least about                  40&#176; C. In method (M3), the heating is                  performed for about 10 minutes to about 2 hours.                  The magnetic A/C-excitation in method (M3) is 50                  to about 500 kHz. In method (M3), the tissue is                  heated up to a temperature of 42-60&#176; C.                  In method(M3), the heating results in apoptosis                  of the cancerous or precancerous cells. In method                  (M4), the fluid sample is selected from urine and                  blood and the energy source is selected from a                  tungsten lamp, laser diode, laser and/or                  bioluminescence. In method (M4), a blue-shift in                  absorption or emission spectrum maximum of 5-200                  nm indicates the presence of a cancerous or                  precancerous cell in the mammal. The change                  includes the appearance of a new visible color or                  luminescence band relative to the absorption or                  emission spectrum of the assay prior to contact                  with the fluid sample, where the visible color or                  luminescence band indicates the presence of a                  cancerous or precancerous cell in the mammal. The                  changes in the absorption or emission spectrum of                  the assay are observed over a time period of 1                  second to about 30 minutes. When the mammal is                  undergoing cancer treatment, the method (M4)                  further involves contacting a second fluid sample                  from the mammal with a second diagnostic assay,                  where the assay comprises the nanoplatform;                  exposing the second assay to an energy source;                  detecting the changes in the absorption or                  emission spectrum of the second assay over time                  relative to the absorption or emission spectrum                  of the second assay prior to contact with the                  fluid sample, where the changes correspond to a                  second level of protease activity in the second                  sample; and comparing the second level of                  protease activity to the first level of protease                  activity, where an increase in activity is                  correlated with a prognosis to increase or change                  the cancer treatment, and where a decrease in                  activity is con-elated with a prognosis to                  maintain or decrease the cancer treatment. The                  method (M4) further involves repeating contacting                  to comparing steps on a daily basis during the                  cancer treatment. When the mammal is in                  remission, the method (M4) further involves                  repeating the contacting to comparing steps on a                  monthly basis after the cancer treatment to                  detect reoccurrence of the cancer in the mammal.                  Preferred Composition: The composition comprises                  0.001 to about 0.10 g of the nanoplatform per kg                  of the mammal's weight.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Hyperthermia treatment of BF16F10                melanomas in Charles River mice was carried out.                The effect of nanoplatform on Charles River mice                with BF16F10 melanomas located in their upper hind                legs was tested. Twenty mice with BF16F10 were                inoculated with mouse melanoma cells in both of                their upper hind legs, and then divided into four                groups. Injections of theranostic platforms were                directly into the upper hind leg. The rate of                cancer growth inhibition using the magnetic                hyperthermia was 76% if the untreated melanomas                were used as the control. The injection of the                nanoplatform even without hyperthemia led to 50%                inhibition of cancer growth. The experimental right                leg had inhibition of tumor growth when compared to                the untreated group. The rate of growth inhibition                using magnetic hyperthemia was 78%.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The nanoplatform is administered at a dosage                of 0.001-0.10 (preferably 0.010-0.025) g per kg                intravenously, subcutaneously, by localized                injection, intratumorally or peritumorally.
   EXAMPLE - Gold-coated Nanoplatform was prepared as                follows: nanoplatforms were synthesized with a gold                coating. Fe/Fe 3O 4/ASOX-nanoparticles were                prepared by suspending 20 mg Fe/Fe 3O                4nanoparticles in 10 ml THF. After sonicating for                30 minutes, the undissolved solid (less than 1 mg)                was separated by precipitation through low-speed                centrifugation (1500 RPM, 5 minutes). The clear                solution was transferred to another test tube and                0.30 ml 3-aminopropyltriethoxylsilane was added to                the solution. After sonicating for 10 hours, the                nanoparticles were collected by high speed                centrifugation. After re-dispersion and subsequent                collection in THF, the Fe/Fe 3O                4/ASOX-nanoparticles (7.5 mg) were collected, dried                in high vacuum, and stored under argon.                Aminosiloxane-protected Fe/Fe 3O 4/Au-nanoparticles                were prepared by pre-adsorbing Au(III) (0.50 mg of                H[AuCl 4]) in aqueous medium to the terminal                amino-functions of the Fe/Fe 3O                4/ASOX-nanoparticles. The nanoparticles were then                collected by high speed centrifugation and                re-dispersed in ethanol. Depending on the thickness                of the Au-shell that was desired, 2, 4 or 8 mg of                H[AuCl 4] was then added, followed by sonication                for 1 minute. Au(III) was reduced to Au(0) by                adding 5 mg of NaBH 4at 20&#176; C. The                pre-seeding technique resulted in the formation of                gold-shells. The Fe/Fe 3O 4/ASOX/Au-nanoparticles                (14.0 g) were precipitated by centrifugation and                three times re-dispersed in and collected from                water, dried in high vacuum, and stored under                argon. Due to clustering of the Fe/Fe 3O                4/ASOX/Au-nanoparticles, their hydrodynamic                diameters were rather large. Typical values were                550 nm to 750 nm with polydispersities of 1.3 to                1.5. When adding surfactants (SDS, 0.01 M), the                hydrodynamic diameters dropped to 200&#177; 20                nm.

PN WO2021188188-A1; US2023126411-A1
TI Imaging tissue used e.g. to detect cancer,            involves administering composition of deuterium-labeled            glycolytic substrate or fatty acid substrate, and            imaging with deuterium magnetic resonance imaging to            detect hydrogen-deuterium oxide.
AU DONABEDIAN P
   MAHAR R
   MERRITT M E
AE UNIV FLORIDA RES FOUND (UYFL-C)
   UNIV FLORIDA RES FOUND INC (UYFL-C)
GA 2021B5933G
AB    NOVELTY - Imaging a tissue in a subject, comprises (i)                administering a composition comprising                deuterium-labeled glycolytic substrate and/or                deuterium-labeled fatty acid substrate to the                subject, and (ii) imaging the subject with                deuterium magnetic resonance imaging (DMI) to                detect hydrogen-deuterium oxide (HDO) in tissues of                the subject, where detection of HDO in a location                within the tissue of the subject is an indication                of glucose utilization and/or fatty acid oxidation                in the tissue of the subject.
   USE - The method is useful for: imaging a tissue in                a subject and detecting HDO in the tissue, where                the tissue is brain, heart, muscle, skin, liver,                pancreas, spleen, kidney, stomach, gut or lungs,                where the detection of elevated glucose utilization                in the tissue is an indication of a cancer, the                detection of impaired glucose utilization and/or                fatty acid oxidation is an indication of injury or                pathology, detection of elevated glucose                utilization and/or fatty acid oxidation is an                indication of metabolic activation; and detecting                deuterated glucose uptake in the tissue, deuterated                lactate production in the tissue, deuterated                glutamate/glutamine (glx) production in the tissue,                a ratio of deuterated lactate/glx, an increased HDO                signal as a biomarker of metabolic flux, and any                combination of ratios or HDO to lactate, or HDO to                glx (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method: utilizes deuterated tracers, which                are inexpensive; and provides a sensitive marker of                glucose utilization in tissues and tumor cells in                vivo, with a possibility for a simplified imaging                strategy after administration of deuterium-labeled                glucose; and is reliable, robust and                economical.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The DMI comprises 2H-NMR                  imaging. The DMI further comprises 1H-NMR imaging                  that uses T1 or T2 weighting. In the step (ii),                  the imaging is performed within 8-24 minutes of                  step (i). The method further comprises repeating                  the step (ii) at additional time points to                  determine a rate of HDO enrichment in the tissue                  of the subject. Preferred Components: The                  deuterium-labeled glycolytic substrate comprises                  deuterated glucose or deuterated octanoate. The                  deuterated glucose comprises: (2H7)glucose; and                  at least 3 deuterium atoms. The deuterated fatty                  acid is perdeuterated fatty acid and comprises at                  least 3 deuterium atoms.
