TI Synthesis of 2-6-6 semiconductor nanocrystals of            specific formula, useful in detecting target in sample,            by dissolving group II element, first group VI element,            and second group VI element in solvent comprising            octadecene and fatty acid.
AU QU L
AE QU L (QULL-Individual)
   CRYSTALPLEX CORP (CRYS-Non-standard)
GA 2006135798
AB    NOVELTY - Synthesis of 2-6-6 semiconductor nanocrystals                of specific formula, comprises dissolving a group                II element, a first group VI element, and a second                group VI element in a solvent comprising octadecene                and fatty acid, to provide 2-6-6 semiconductor                nanocrystal precursor solution.
   USE - The method is for synthesis of 2-6-6 SCNs of                specific formula, which is conjugated to a                biological agent useful for a composition                comprising 2-6-6 SCN. 2-6-6 SCN is useful in                detecting a target or the location of the target in                a sample. It is for use in monitoring a biological                process in vitro or in vivo (claimed). The target                can be e.g. protein (including antibodies, or                fragments thereof, peptides, hormones, growth                factors, cytokines, tumor-associated proteins,                cell-surface receptors, coagulation factors, or                proteins associated with a disease or a condition),                a nucleic acid molecule, their fragment, a                small-molecule drug, a cell, a tissue, or a drug                metabolite. The sample can be e.g. blood, lymph,                ductal fluid, tissue, cell cultures, a single cell,                urine, and a biopsy. 2-6-6 SCN is useful in the                detection or prognosis of the disease or the                condition. The disease is cancer including lung                cancer, brain cancer, ovarian cancer, uterine                cancer, testicular cancer, lymphoma, leukemia,                stomach cancer, pancreatic cancer, skin cancer,                breast cancer, adenocarcinoma, glioma, and bone                cancer. It is useful for detecting skin and breast                tumors that are located close to the skin                surface.
   ADVANTAGE - The method eliminates the need to closely time                and stop the synthesis process to achieve a desired                wavelength and/or bandwidth.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Synthesis of 2-6-6 semiconductor nanocrystals                (SCNs) of formula WYxZ(1-x), comprises dissolving a                group II element, a first group VI element, and a                second group VI element in a solvent comprising                octadecene and fatty acid, to provide 2-6-6 SCN                precursor solution; and heating the 2-6-6 SCN                precursor solution at a temperature to produce the                2-6-6 SCNs.
   W = group II element;
   Y, Z = different group VI elements;
   X = greater than 0, less than 1.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   (1) a method of detecting a target in a                sample, comprising contacting a sample with the                composition comprising 2-6-6 SCN, where biological                agent specifically binds to a target in the sample;                allowing the biological agent to specifically bind                to the target; and analyzing the sample via                spectroscopy, obtaining a spectroscopic signature                of the sample, where spectroscopic signature is                indicative of the presence or the absence of the                target in the sample; and
   (2) a method of detecting the location of a                target in vivo, comprising administering the                composition comprising 2-6-6 SCN to a host, where                biological agent specifically binds to a target in                the host; allowing the biological agent to                specifically bind to the target; and imaging the                host, or its section or cell, detecting the                location of the target in vivo.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows the emission spectra of                CdSxSe1-x alloyed semiconductor nanocrystals                synthesized by altering the sulfur (S):selenium                (Se) ratio.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - METALLURGY - Preferred Parameter: The temperature is                  between 270-330degreesC.Preferred Method: The group II element is                  dissolved in the first solvent between                  270-330degreesC.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Component: The fatty acid is oleic                  acid.
   EXAMPLE - Octadecene (4.00 ml) was mixed with oleic acid                (200 muL), and added to cadmium oxide (CdO) (0.1                mmol) in a three neck round bottom flask. The flask                was flushed with 99.999% nitrogen for 20 minutes                and heated to 300degreesC, until the solution was                clear. Stock solutions of selenium and sulfur were                prepared in a glove box under 99.999% nitrogen.                Selenium powder (1.00 g) was mixed with                tributylphosphine (10.00 ml); and sulfur powder                (0.40 g) was mixed with octadecene (20.00 ml).                Selenium precursors (20 muL) were mixed with sulfur                precursors (1.2 ml) in a 20 mL glass vial, diluted                to 2.00 ml with octadecene, and added to the                cadmium precursors and stirred for 60 minutes, or                until no change in emission wavelength was                observed. This produced cores that fluoresce at 525                nm. The entire core solution was added to 50 ml                conical centrifuge tube; and 10 ml of hexanes and                30 ml of butanol were added. The crystals were                centrifuged (2680 G for 10 minutes), and the                supernatant was discarded. The crystals were washed                three times by being suspended in hexanes (10 ml),                precipitated with methanol (30 ml) and centrifuged                (2680 G for 10 minutes). The crystals were                suspended in 5 ml hexanes.

TI Skin condition e.g. skin tone, analyzing method,            involves examining properties of each pixel in            white-light image and ultra violet image for            identifying skin-pixels, and obtaining skin condition            using skin pixels information.
AU CHHIBBER R
   CHHIBBER A
   SHARMA S
AE CHHIBBER R (CHHI-Individual)
   CHHIBBER A (CHHI-Individual)
   SHARMA S (SHAR-Individual)
   BRIGHTEX BIO-PHOTONICS LLC (BRIG-Non-standard)

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves acquiring a set of                white-light images and ultra violet image of skin,                where the white-light and ultra violet images                includes a set of pixels, and each pixel in the                ultra violet image corresponds to a respective                pixel in the white-light image. The properties of                each pixel in the white-light image are examined                for identifying skin-pixels in the white-light                image and ultra violet images. A result associated                with a skin condition is obtained using the                information in the skin pixels in the white-light                image and ultra violet images.
   USE - Used for analyzing a skin condition e.g. skin                tone, ultra violet damage, pores, wrinkle,                hydration level, collagen content, and skin type,                by acquiring and processing digital images. Can                also be used for detecting and diagnosing                afflictions and skin disorders.
   ADVANTAGE - The method allows to more accurately and                easily analyze and diagnose the skin conditions                using digital images, and allows for early                diagnosis of melanoma and other skin cancer                symptoms. The method enables to acquire the ultra                violet image, and to combine autofluorescence of                the skin and image processing technologies, thus                providing automated detection and analysis of                subsurface skin condition.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a computer readable medium storing program                instructions executed by a processor for analyzing                skin conditions
   a computer system including a computer                readable medium for analyzing skin conditions
   a system for analyzing skin conditions.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flowchart illustrating a                method for analyzing skin conditions using digital                images.

TI Determining presence or risk of cancer in human,            by analyzing test sample for presence, amount or both            of genetic biomarker(s) or epigenetic biomarker(s), and            transforming analysis result into parameter(s) for            determination.
AU POULIN M L
   YAN L
AE EPIGENDX INC (EPIG-Non-standard)
   EPIGENDX INC (EPIG-Non-standard)
GA 2011N54629
AB    NOVELTY - Method for determining the presence or risk of                cancer in a human subject, involves obtaining a                test sample from the subject, analyzing the test                sample for the presence, amount, or both the                presence and amount of one or more genetic                biomarkers or analyzing the test sample for the                presence, amount, or both the presence and amount                of one or more epigenetic biomarkers, and                transforming the result of genetic biomarker                analysis and the result of epigenetic biomarker                analysis into one or more parameters for                determining the presence or risk of cancer in the                subject.
   USE - The method is useful for determining the                presence or risk of cancer in human subject. The                cancer is chosen from ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, colon cancer and breast cancer, preferably                ovarian cancer (both claimed) arising from                epithelial cells, stromal cells, germ cells, and                mesenchymal cells. Uses include but are not limited                to biliary tract cancer, bladder cancer, brain                cancer including glioblastomas and                medulloblastomas, choriocarcinoma, endometrial                cancer, esophageal cancer, gastric cancer,                hematological neoplasms including acute lymphocytic                and myelogenous leukemia, thymus (T)-cell acute                lymphoblastic leukemia lymphoma, hairy cell                leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia, multiple                myeloma, AIDS-associated leukemias and adult T-cell                leukemia/lymphoma, intraepithelial neoplasms                including Bowen's disease and Paget's disease,                liver cancer, lung cancer, lymphomas including                Hodgkin's disease and lymphocytic lymphomas,                neuroblastomas, oral cancer including squamous cell                carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer,                rectal cancer, sarcomas including leiomyosarcoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, liposarcoma, fibrosarcoma, and                osteosarcoma, skin cancer including melanoma,                Merkel cell carcinoma, Kaposi's sarcoma, basal cell                carcinoma, and squamous cell cancer, testicular                cancer including germinal tumors such as seminoma,                non-seminoma (teratomas, choriocarcinomas), stromal                tumors, and germ cell tumors, thyroid cancer                including thyroid adenocarcinoma and medullar                carcinoma, and renal cancer including                adenocarcinoma and Wilms tumor, melanoma, and lung                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is accurate and enables early                detection of cancer, preferably ovarian                cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) multi-marker panel; and
   (2) method for determining whether a tumor                sample comprises an ovarian cancer cell.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: At least one of the                  genetic biomarkers provides gene mutation                  information of the subject. At least one of the                  epigenetic biomarkers provides micro RNA                  expression information of the subject. At least                  one of the epigenetic biomarkers provides                  aberrant DNA methylation information of the                  subject. The genetic biomarkers are chosen from                  markers given in table 3A and table 3B of patent                  specification, and the epigenetic biomarkers are                  chosen from markers given in table 4 of patent                  specification. The genetic biomarkers and                  epigenetic biomarkers are chosen from markers                  given in table 5 of patent specification. The                  genetic biomarkers and epigenetic biomarkers are                  indicative of a distinctive sub-type of ovarian                  cancer.

   SCHIRMER A R S
AE RADIOLIFE CO (RADI-Non-standard)
GA 2022D7766A
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves determining size of                to-be-tested virus for in a suspected biological                sample and selecting a test frequency of the virus,                where the test frequency of the virus being                fundamental frequency to resonate a structure of                the virus is maintained for about 1.4 GHz to 1.9                GHz. A first test tube is placed in an analyzer for                exposing a reference biological sample in the first                test tube to radio waves. A second test tube is                placed in the analyzer for exposing the suspected                biological sample in the second test tube to the                radio waves. The test frequency passed through the                suspected biological sample is measured for                calculating suspected biological sample absorption                rate and a suspected sample phase difference. A                first spectral profile of the suspected biological                sample at the test frequency is generated. The                first spectral profile is compared to a second                spectral profile for confirming a positive                detection for the virus when difference exists                between the spectral profiles.
   USE - Method for analyzing a suspected biological                sample to determine frequency to identify, diagnose                and treat virus, bacteria, cellular disease of a                patient. TI Analyzing variant allele frequency (VAF) in            biological sample to provide information necessary for            cancer diagnosis, by mapping nucleic acid sequence            information to reference genome, detecting variants            based on information, and calculating VAF.
AU HOON L S
   MIN N
AE EVERGENOME INC (EVER-Non-standard)
GA 2025C0972M
AB    NOVELTY - Method for analyzing variant allele frequency                (VAF) in a biological sample to provide information                necessary for cancer diagnosis involves (a)                extracting nucleic acids from a biological sample                obtained from an individual and obtaining sequence                information, (b) mapping the obtained sequence                information to a reference genome, (c) detecting                variants based on the mapped sequence information,                (d) calculating the VAF for each variant, (e)                dividing the VAF into two or more ranges based on                the numerical values, and calculating the                proportion of variants included in each range, and                (f) comparing the proportion of variants in each                range with a normal control group.
   USE - The method is useful for analyzing VAF in                biological sample to provide information necessary                for cancer diagnosis. The cancer is chosen from                bladder cancer, bone cancer, blood cancer, breast                cancer, melanoma, thyroid cancer, parathyroid                cancer, bone marrow cancer, rectal cancer, throat                cancer, laryngeal cancer, lung cancer, esophageal                cancer, pancreatic cancer, colon cancer, stomach                cancer, tongue cancer, skin cancer, brain tumor,                uterine cancer, head or neck cancer, gallbladder                cancer, oral cancer, colorectal cancer, anal                cancer, CNS tumor, liver cancer, and large                intestine cancer (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method ensures cancer diagnosis in                non-invasive and accurate manner.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a device for providing information for cancer                diagnosis, comprising (a) a decoding unit that                extracts nucleic acids from a biological sample                obtained from an individual and decodes the                sequence information, (b) a mapping unit that maps                the obtained sequence information to a reference                genome, (c) a variant detection unit that detects                variants based on the mapped sequence information,                (d) a VAF calculation unit that calculates the VAF                for each variant, (e) a ratio calculation unit that                divides the VAF into two or more intervals                according to the numerical value and calculates the                ratio of variants included in each interval, and                (f) an analysis unit that compares the ratio of                variants in each interval with a normal control                group; and
   a computer-readable recording medium used in                the above-mentioned method.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Sample: The biological sample is                  chosen from blood, plasma, serum, tumor tissue,                  urine, saliva, mucosal secretions, sputum, feces,                  and tears. Preferred Biomolecules: The nucleic                  acid is cell-free DNA (cfDNA), circulating tumor                  DNA (ctDNA), or their combination. The enzyme is                  a restriction enzyme. The restriction enzyme is a                  methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme.                  Preferred Method: The nucleic acid is fragmented                  physically, chemically, thermally, optically,                  ultrasonically, or enzymatically. The sequence                  information is obtained by next-generation                  sequencing. In step (f), if the ratio of                  variations in the one or more regions differs                  from that of a normal control group by more than                  a predetermined threshold, the individual is                  determined to have cancer. The threshold is                  predetermined by performing steps (a)-(e) using                  respective biological samples obtained from a                  normal control group and a cancer patient group,                  and analyzing the difference in the proportion of                  mutations in each VAF range between the normal                  control group and the cancer patient group. The                  sequence information is sequence information from                  the entire chromosome, a portion of the                  chromosome, or a specific region within the                  chromosome. Preferred Apparatus: The device                  further comprises a database unit that stores (i)                  information on the variation rate of the normal                  control group in each of the segments and (ii)                  variation rate thresholds in each segment that                  can distinguish between the normal control group                  and the cancer patient group. The device further                  comprises a determination unit that, if the                  analysis unit analyzes that the variation rate in                  each segment analyzed from the individual                  deviates from the threshold when compared to the                  normal control group variation rate stored in the                  database unit, determines that the individual has                  cancer.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details of cancer                diagnosis that do not support the claims.

PN WO2024215677-A2; WO2024215677-A3
TI New polynucleotide construct encoding            phosphatidylserine (PS)-targeted chimeric antigen            receptor polypeptide comprising e.g. signal peptide,            extracellular PS-binding domain, and hinge domain used            e.g. for treating cancer.
AU HOU P
AE UNIV RUTGERS STATE NEW JERSEY (RUTF-C)
GA 2024A9176T
AB    NOVELTY - Polynucleotide construct encoding a                phosphatidylserine (PS)-targeted chimeric antigen                receptor (CAR) polypeptide comprising (a) a signal                peptide, (b) an extracellular PS-binding domain,                (c) a hinge domain, (d) a transmembrane domain, and                (e) at least one intracellular immunostimulatory                activation domains, is new.
   USE - The polynucleotide construct, CAR, vector,                modified macrophage, monocyte, or composition is                useful: for treating cancer in a subject, where the                subject has a solid tumor cancer comprising                pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, lung cancer,                brain cancer, neck cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, prostate cancer, kidney cancer, liver                cancer, colorectal cancer, stomach cancer,                esophageal cancer, and skin cancer (all claimed);                for treating solid tumor cancers; and in a variety                of clinical, research, and commercial applications.                Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The polynucleotide construct: utilizes the                chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) polypeptide for                better activity, stability, expression, production,                storage, administration, detection, delivery                efficiency; and has the potential to penetrate                solid tumors to provokes tumoricidal immune                response.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMs are also included                for:
   a vector comprising the polynucleotide                construct comprising a viral vector, a lentiviral                vector, a plasmid expression vector, an                adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector, a recombinant                AAV (rAAV) vector, a single-stranded AAV vector, a                double stranded AAV vector, and it's                self-complementary AAV (scAAV) vector;
   a phosphatidylserine (PS)-targeted chimeric                antigen receptor (CAR) polypeptide encoded by the                polynucleotide construct or vector;
   a modified macrophage or monocyte comprising                either the polynucleotide construct, vector, or                PS-targeted CAR polypeptide, or surface-expressed                phosphatidylserine (PS)-targeted chimeric antigen                receptor (CAR) polypeptide, the PS-targeted CAR                polypeptide comprising (a)-(d) as per se;
   a composition comprising the modified                macrophage or monocyte; and
   treating cancer in a subject comprising                administering an amount of a composition to the                subject comprising a modified macrophage or                monocyte comprising a surface-expressed                phosphatidylserine (PS)-targeted chimeric antigen                receptor (CAR) polypeptide, and the PS-targeted CAR                polypeptide comprising (a)-(e) as per se.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Components: The signal peptide                  comprises an amino acid sequence having at least                  90-99% identity to the amino acid sequence of SEQ                  ID NO: 1 (comprising a fully defined sequence of                  20 amino acids as given in the specification), or                  SEQ ID NO: 6 (comprising a fully defined sequence                  of 21 amino acids as given in the specification).                  The extracellular PS-binding domain comprises an                  amino acid sequence having at least 90-99%                  identity to at least one portions of the amino                  acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3 (comprising a fully                  defined sequence of 296 amino acids as given in                  the specification) or SEQ ID NO: 7 (comprising a                  fully defined sequence of 277 amino acids as                  given in the specification). The transmembrane                  domain comprises an amino acid sequence having at                  least 90-99% identity to at least one portions of                  the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3                  (comprising a fully defined sequence of 296 amino                  acids as given in the specification), or SEQ ID                  NO: 8 (comprising a fully defined sequence of 45                  amino acids as given in the specification). The                  intracellular immunostimulatory activation                  domains comprise at least one amino acid                  sequences having at least 90-99% identity to SEQ                  ID NO: 4 (comprising a fully defined sequence of                  113 amino acids as given in the specification) or                  SEQ ID NO: 9 (comprising a fully defined sequence                  of 42 amino acids as given in the specification).                  The PS-targeted CAR polypeptide comprises an                  amino acid sequence having at least 90-99%                  identity to the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                  5 (comprising a fully defined sequence of 438                  amino acids as given in the specification), or                  SEQ ID NO: 10 (comprising a fully defined                  sequence of 507 amino acids as given in the                  specification). The polynucleotide construct                  comprises a polynucleotide sequence having at                  least 90-99% identity to the nucleic acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 11 (comprising a fully                  defined sequence of 1317 nucleic acids as given                  in the specification) or SEQ ID NO: 12                  (comprising a fully defined sequence of 330                  nucleic acids as given in the specification). The                  vector is a lentiviral vector comprising pHAGE                  and pLenti. The modified macrophage or monocyte                  is derived from a primary macrophage or monocyte,                  or where the modified macrophage or monocyte is                  derived from an induced pluripotent stem cell.                  The PS-targeted CAR polypeptide comprises an                  amino acid sequence having at least 90-99%                  identity to the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                  5 (comprising a fully defined sequence of 438                  amino acids as given in the specification) or SEQ                  ID NO: 10 (comprising a fully defined sequence of                  507 amino acids as given in the specification).                  The PS-targeted CAR polypeptide is encoded by a                  polynucleotide construct comprising a                  polynucleotide sequence having at least 90-99%                  identity to SEQ ID NO: 11 (comprising a fully                  defined sequence of 1317 nucleic acids as given                  in the specification) or SEQ ID NO: 12                  (comprising a fully defined sequence of 1524                  nucleic acids as given in the specification). The                  additional anti-cancer drugs comprise a KRAS                  inhibitor, and/or a merTK inhibitor. The modified                  macrophage or monocyte comprises the                  surface-expressed PS-targeted CAR polypeptide                  activates an immune response in a tumor                  microenvironment in the subject, thus treating                  the cancer in the subject. Preferred Method: The                  method further comprises administering an amount                  of at least one additional anti-cancer drugs to                  the subject.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

No dosage details given.

GA 2012Q90152
AB    NOVELTY - The assembly has a capsule (1) provided at                distal end for brachytherapy and comprising a                chamber for holding radioactive sources, where the                chamber is defined by a wall (3), and a part of                exterior surface of the wall of the capsule                comprises a coating (4). The coating is selected                from materials such as titanium nitride, titanium                carbonitride, titanium chromium nitride, chromium                nitride, titanium-aluminum chromium nitride,                diamond-like carbon and molybdenum disulphide. The                capsule is attached to a push/pull wire (6) by a                crimp joint, a press joint, a weld and glue                joint.
   USE - Source assembly for use during brachytherapy                for treating cancer tumor of a patient. Uses                include but are not limited to cervical cancer                tumor, prostate cancer tumor, breast cancer tumor,                skin cancer tumor, head cancer tumor and neck                cancer tumor.
   ADVANTAGE - The assembly includes a wall and the coating                material with different colors, so that a user can                able to see the difference in color when the                coating is partly removed. The assembly utilizes a                catheter and a flexible tube/hollow needle to allow                the capsule to be positioned accurately at                treatment site. The assembly provides high                integrity of the capsule wall and a detection                mechanism for detecting wear of the capsule, so                that the assembly can be positioned with high                accuracy.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for preparing a brachytherapy source                assembly.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a cross-sectional view of a                brachytherapy source assembly.

AU ZHAO R

   LI Y
   JIN Y
   HUANG Y
AE CHINESE ACAD SCI CHEM INST (CSCI-C)
   UNIV CHINESE ACAD SCI (UCAS-C)
GA 2019979225
AB    NOVELTY - Bivalent targeting peptide probe has two                tumor-specific targeting polypeptides, two                polyethylene glycol (PEG) linking arms, backbone                core peptide and fluorescent molecule.
   USE - The bivalent targeting peptide probe is useful                in preparation of eukaryotic tumor cell detection                reagents and medicine for treating tumor. The                eukaryotic tumor cells are cancer cells chosen from                liver cancer cells, breast cancer cells, lung                cancer cells, human glioma cells, melanoma cancer                cells, glioblastoma cells, cervical cancer cells,                nasopharyngeal cancer cells, brain cancer cells,                pancreatic cancer cells, ovarian cancer cells,                uterine cancer cells, testicular cancer cells, skin                cancer cells, gastric cancer cells, colon cancer                cells, bladder cancer cells or rectal cancer cells                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The probe improve the targeting polypeptide                probe solubility in an aqueous solution and                targeting polypeptide probe flexibility.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Bivalent targeting peptide probe has two                tumor-specific targeting polypeptides, two                polyethylene glycol (PEG) linking arms, backbone                core peptide and fluorescent molecule, Where each                of the tumor-specific targeting polypeptides is                connected to a PEG linking arm through a group of                formula (I), the backbone core peptide comprises                amino acid sequence of formula Lys-Lys-Gly-Lys-Gly,                the backbone core peptide and the tumor-specific                targeting polypeptide are coupled through a PEG                linking arm and the fluorescent molecule and the                backbone core peptide are connected by a chemical                bond. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for method                for preparing above-mentioned probe, which involves                (a) preparing backbone peptides by using                fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl protecting group (Fmoc)                solid-phase peptide synthesis method to synthesize                peptide Lys-Lys-Gly-Lys-Gly from the C-terminus on                Fmoc-Gly-wang resin, and coupling amino acids to                the resin one by one, coupling N-terminal Fmoc-PEG                9 -CH2-CH2-COOH molecules to the &#945; amino                group and the &#949; -amino group of the amino                acid and connecting azidoacetic acid, fluorescein                isothiocyanate (FITC) to &#949; amino group of                the C-terminal lysine to remove the product from                the resin and cleaving down to obtain                azide-modified backbone core peptide, (b) preparing                tumor-specific targeting polypeptide by a                solid-phase polypeptide synthesis method on the                solid-phase polypeptide synthesis resin, modifying                alkynyl at the amino terminus of the tumor-specific                targeting polypeptide by 5-hexynyl acid in situ                derivatization, cleaving the product from the resin                to obtain alkynyl-modified tumor-specific targeting                polypeptide, and (c) connecting backbone core                peptide and the tumor-specific targeting                polypeptide using liquid phase reaction                mixture.
                                                                                                                     
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecule: The tumor-specific                  targeting polypeptide is suitable for targeting                  the conjugate to a tumor cell, and the marker                  protein lysosomal-associated transmembrane                  protein 4B (LAPTM4B) as a specific target. The                  tumor-specific targeting polypeptide is                  specifically an AP2H polypeptide, and its amino                  acid sequence is of formula                  Ile-His-Gly-His-His-Ile-Ile-Ser-Val-Gly. The                  tumor-specific targeting polypeptide is AP2H, and                  the bivalent targeting polypeptide probe is of                  formula (II). Preferred Component: The                  fluorescent molecule is chosen from one or more                  fluorescein, rhodamine, nile red, naphthalimide                  and cyanine dye, preferably fluorescein.                  Preferred Method: The method involves preparing                  backbone core peptide (a1) using Fmoc-Gly-Wang                  resin, 20% hexahydropyridine as deprotection                  reagent, adding amino acid Fmoc-Lys (Dde)-OH, and                  activating reagent N-methylmorpholine for                  coupling reaction, capping unreacted glycine                  resin, performing coupling reaction, and (c1)                  cleaving backbone core peptide from resin using                  lysing solution. The method involves preparing                  alkynyl-modified tumor-specific targeting                  polypeptide (a2) using FMOC-Gly-Wang resin as the                  starting material, 20% hexahydropyridine,                  N-methylmorpholine and HBTU to synthesize AP2H                  polypeptide sequence, (b2) removing the FMOC                  protecting group at the N-terminus of the AP2H                  polypeptide sequence, adding 4-fold molar amount                  of 5-hexynyl acid and HBTU for coupling reaction                  to obtain an alkynyl-modified tumor-specific                  targeting polypeptide and (c2) lysing the                  alkynyl-modified tumor-specific targeting                  polypeptide from the resin by using lysing                  solution. The step (III) involves performing                  catalysis of copper using solvent in a molar                  ratio of 1:2.4.                                                                                                                              
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves directing excitation light                to a photosensitizer in a target region. The light                emitted by the photosensitizer and/or singlet                oxygen generated in the target region is received.                The returning light is filtered to isolate emission                from the singlet oxygen. The emission from the                singlet oxygen is monitored. A concentration of the                singlet oxygen is determined based on an emission                signal measured by a detection system (362). The                photosensitizer and/or singlet oxygen is monitored                between pulses of the excitation light.
   USE - Method for monitoring singlet oxygen during                photodynamic therapy (PDT) for treatment of acne                and cancer (all claimed) in esophagus, lung, skin,                bladder, and brain. Can also be used in monitoring                singlet oxygen during photodynamic therapy for                treatment of actinic keratosis, and sebaceous                follicle disorders, psoriasis, and eczema.
   ADVANTAGE - The treatment can be optimized without                increasing treatment time per session. Enables the                clinician or physician to identify the treatment                state and lower the energy delivered in real-time                monitoring condition. The light source energy can                be increased.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for apparatus                for photodynamic therapy (PDT).

TI Image quality assessing method for e.g.            computer-aided diagnostic system, involves determining            percentage of blurred blocks if image is blurry, and            detecting obstructions to produce images using            contamination detection.
AU GU J
   LI W
   HARGROVE J
   WOLTERS R H
AE STI MEDICAL SYSTEMS LLC (STIM-Non-standard)
   STI MEDICAL SYSTEMS LLC (STIM-Non-standard)
GA 2008L12026
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves collecting a raw image                free from glare during examination by a digital                imager, and locating a region of interest using an                image classification algorithm. Region assessment                is applied to the region of interest to detect                incorrect camera zooming, incorrect camera                positioning and obstructions. Contrast assessment                is performed on the region of interest, and blur                assessment is performed without a reference image.                The percentage of blurred blocks is determined if                the image is blurry, and the obstructions are                detected to produce standardized images using                contamination detection.
   USE - Method for assessing image quality to produce                standardized images in an archive-quality                electronic medical records and a computer-aided                diagnostic (CAD) system that is utilized during                colposcopy for diagnosing uterine cervical cancer,                colorectal cancer and skin cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method effectively assesses image quality                to produce standardized images in archive-quality                electronic medical records and a computer-aided                diagnostic (CAD) system, maximizes image contrast                and improves image quality.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for blur assessment without a reference                image.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow diagram of a system                framework of automatic image quality assessment                algorithms.

TI Constructing in situ PDX model of lung cancer by            percutaneous puncture inoculation involves collecting            tumor sample and obtaining lung cancer tumor tissues            that grow vigorously without ulcers and necrosis.
AU HE Y
   GAN W
   WANG A
   CHEN F
   CHEN H
   YU B
AE NANCHANG ROYO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD (NANC-Non-standard)
GA 2020B3984B
AB    NOVELTY - Constructing in situ PDX model of lung cancer                by percutaneous puncture inoculation involves                collecting tumor sample, obtaining lung cancer                tumor tissues that grow vigorously without ulcers                and necrosis, tumor sample processing and                detection. The lung cancer tumor tissue is active                and the inactive tissue is removed, and divided                into blocks to make multiple groups of 1x 1x 1mm                tumor masses. The inoculated mice is raised in                SPF-class animal room IVC cages and raising them                regularly. The situation of the mice is observed                regularly, weighed and recorded the weight of the                mice twice a week and ethically executed the mice                with abnormal conditions. The PET-CT examination is                performed. The multiple-year-old nude mice or other                highly immunodeficient mice is chosen as the                inoculation animals. In the SPF animal room, fixed                on the right side of the surgical board.
   USE - Method for constructing in situ PDX model of                lung cancer by percutaneous puncture                inoculation.
   ADVANTAGE - The method makes the mouse vaccination success                rate greatly improve, retains the microenvironment                of the patient's tumor tissue, highly simulates                biological model of human tumors, better reproduces                the pathophysiological characteristics of lung                cancer patients, and has important scientific                research, medical value and economic value.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Constructing in situ PDX model of lung cancer                by percutaneous puncture inoculation involves                collecting tumor sample, obtaining lung cancer                tumor tissues that grow vigorously without ulcers                and necrosis, tumor sample processing and                detection. The lung cancer tumor tissue is active                and the inactive tissue is removed, and divided                into blocks to make multiple groups of 1x 1x 1mm                tumor masses. The inoculated mice is raised in                SPF-class animal room IVC cages and raising them                regularly. The situation of the mice is observed                regularly, weighed and recorded the weight of the                mice twice a week and ethically executed the mice                with abnormal conditions. The PET-CT examination is                performed. The multiple-year-old nude mice or other                highly immunodeficient mice is chosen as the                inoculation animals. In the SPF animal room, fixed                on the right side of the surgical board. The tumor                mass is loaded into the puncture needle, selected                the intersection of the left mid-axillary line and                the eighth intercostal space as the needle puncture                point and marked. The needle puncture site is                disinfected 2-3 times, the skin is cut along the                eighth intercostal space, and the puncture needle                is inserted perpendicular to the intercostal space                and at an angle of 30 degrees to the horizontal                plane. The depth of the needle is 0.8-1.0cm, slowly                pushed out the tumor block, rotated for a week and                pulled out the needle core and needle sheath in                turn. The skin is sutured and disinfected the                puncture site, injected antibiotics after the                operation until the mouse is fully warmed up and                put back into the cage. The mice is sent to PET-CT                for inspection according to the number of weeks and                groups starting from the second week after modeling                for 4 consecutive weeks, and one group a week to                observe the tumor formation and tumor formation of                lung cancer tumors. The mice is killed and the                tumor is collected according to the results of                PET-CT, and the lung cancer tumor tissue is sent                for examination. The pathological test is to                evaluate the tumor formation of mice based on the                results of PET-CT, surgically strip the tumor of                the lung cancer tumor up to 1500 mm3, taken a                portion for pathological test and gene sequencing,                and the remaining tumor tissue is put into the                freezing solution and kept frozen, and the other                portion continues to be passaged.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The tumor tissue with                  vigorous growth at the edge of the tumor without                  ulcer and necrosis is cut out, and quickly put                  into a centrifuge tube containing a tissue                  preservation solution, and the centrifuge tube is                  packed in an ice pack for low-temperature                  transportation. The 0.4% trypan blue stain is                  used to detect tumor tissue activity in a                  laboratory biological safety cabinet, and removed                  inactive tissue. The lung cancer tumor tissue is                  put in 0.2% iodophor solution for 30 seconds to                  disinfect, and rinsed the tissue 2-3 times with                  PBS solution containing 3% bi-antibody. The                  washed tumor tissue is put into a new petri dish,                  added appropriate amount of culture medium, cut                  the tumor tissue block into 1x 1x 1mm tumor mass,                  and washed the tumor mass with culture medium 2-3                  times. The puncture needle is an aspiration                  biopsy needle, which includes a needle core and a                  sheath needle. The sheath surface of the sheath                  needle is provided with a scale and the                  specification is 18Gx 6cm-20Gx 6cm.

TI Detecting copy number variation, by sequencing            extracellular polynucleotides, filtering out reads that            fail to meet set threshold, mapping sequence reads to            reference sequence, quantifying mapped reads and            determining copy number variation.
AU TALASAZ A
   ELTOUKHY H
AE GUARDANT HEALTH INC (GUAT-C)
GA 2017523592
AB    NOVELTY - Method for detecting copy number variation                involves (a) sequencing extracellular                polynucleotides from a bodily sample from a                subject, where each of the extracellular                polynucleotides generates sequencing reads, (b)                filtering out reads that fail to meet a set                threshold, (c) mapping the sequence reads obtained                from step (a) to a reference sequence, (d)                quantifying mapped reads in two or more predefined                regions of the reference sequence, and (e)                determining copy number variation in one or more of                the predefined regions.
   USE - The methods are useful for detecting copy                number variation and rare mutation in a cell-free                or substantially cell-free sample obtained from a                subject (all claimed), detecting copy number                variation profiling or general genetic profiling of                a disease, and also useful in bioinformatics tools.                The method is useful for characterizing the                heterogeneity of an abnormal condition in a                subject, monitoring disease progression, residual                disease, therapy, abnormality or disease within an                individual, such as infection and/or cancer, and                systemic infections caused by a pathogen such as a                bacteria or virus, diagnosing or prognosing a                condition, and diagnosing, monitoring or treating a                disease, preferably cancer. The cancer is chosen                from blood cancers, brain cancers, lung cancers,                skin cancers, nose cancers, throat cancers, liver                cancers, bone cancers, lymphomas, pancreatic                cancers, skin cancers, bowel cancers, rectal                cancers, thyroid cancers, bladder cancers, kidney                cancers, mouth cancers, stomach cancers, solid                state tumors, heterogeneous tumors and homogeneous                tumors. The bodily sample is chosen from blood,                plasma, serum, urine, saliva, mucosal excretions,                sputum, stool and tears. The subject is a pregnant                female.
   ADVANTAGE - The method requires cell-free DNA to detect                and monitor disease, and provides early and                accurate detection of cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method for detecting copy number variation                involves (a) sequencing extracellular                polynucleotides from a bodily sample from a                subject, where each of the extracellular                polynucleotides generates sequencing reads, (b)                filtering out reads that fail to meet a set                threshold, (c) mapping the sequence reads obtained                from step (a) to a reference sequence, (d)                quantifying mapped reads in two or more predefined                regions of the reference sequence, and (e)                determining copy number variation in one or more of                the predefined regions by: (i) normalizing number                of reads in the predefined regions to each other or                the number of unique sequence reads in the                predefined regions to one other, and (ii)                processing the normalized numbers obtained in step                (i) to normalized numbers obtained from a control                sample. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for method                for detecting a rare mutation in a cell-free or                substantially cell-free sample obtained from a                subject, which involves (i) performing the                above-mentioned steps (a)-(b), (ii) mapping                sequence reads derived from the sequencing onto a                reference sequence, (iii) identifying a subset of                mapped sequence reads that align with a variant of                the reference sequence at each mappable base                position, (iv) calculating a ratio of (a) a number                of mapped sequence reads that comprise variant as                compared to the reference sequence for each                mappable base position, to (b) a number of total                sequence reads for each mappable base position, (v)                normalizing the ratios or frequency of variance for                each mappable base position and determining                potential rare variants or mutations, and (vi)                processing a resulting number for each of the                regions with potential rare variants or mutations                to similarly derived numbers from a reference                sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method further                  involves (aa) isolating extracellular                  polynucleotides from the bodily sample, (bb)                  generating copies of the extracellular                  polynucleotides before sequencing, (cc)                  determining a percent of sequences having copy                  number variation or rare mutation or variant in                  the bodily sample by calculating a percent of                  predefined regions with an amount of                  polynucleotides above or below a threshold, (dd)                  attaching one or more barcodes to the                  extracellular polynucleotides or their fragments                  before sequencing or amplification or enrichment                  steps, where each barcode attached to the                  extracellular polynucleotides or their fragments                  before sequencing is not unique, and (ee)                  selectively enriching regions from a genome or                  transcriptome of the subject before sequencing.                  The barcode comprises fixed or semi-random                  oligonucleotide sequence that in combination with                  a diversity of molecules sequenced from a select                  region enables identification of unique                  molecules.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

AB    NOVELTY - Composition comprises (a) an agent, and an                antibody or antibody fragment that binds nidogen 1                (NID1), or (b) an agent that reduces the level                and/or activity of sNID1 i.e. available to interact                with natural killer cell activating receptor                (NK)p44 polypeptide.
   USE - The composition is useful for (a) preventing                or treating a cancer or infectious disease in an                individual, (b) assessing immunosuppression in an                individual having a cancer, (c) reverting or                decreasing immunosuppression, or (d) assessing                state of inhibition of NK cell cytotoxicity in an                individual having a cancer. The individual has a                solid tumor. The individual has a cancer chosen                from bladder cancer, skin cancer, breast cancer,                cervical cancer, head and neck cancer, colorectal                cancer, esophageal cancer, kidney cancer, liver                cancer, lung cancer, prostate cancer, stomach                cancer, uterine cancer, ovarian cancer, endometrial                cancer and testicular cancer (all claimed). The                composition is also used for enhancing immune                responses (e.g. anti-tumor immune response, immune                response against pathogen (e.g. virus) or                pathogen-infected cell) in an individual. The                disease is an infectious disease (e.g. viral                infection).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   an in vitro method (M1) for assessing a state                of inhibition of NK cell cytotoxicity in an                individual having a cancer, involves bringing a                biological sample from an individual into contact                with an agent i.e. capable of specifically binding                a sNID1 polypeptide, and detecting presence and/or                levels of the sNID1 polypeptide, where a detection                of presence of and/or increased levels of sNID1                indicates that the individual has a state of                inhibition of NK cell cytotoxicity and/or that the                individual has sNID1 capable of mediating a state                of inhibition of NK cell cytotoxicity; and
   a method (M2) of treating or preventing cancer                in an individual, involves (a) determining whether                the individual has sNID1, optionally at increased                levels compared to a control, and (b) administering                an agent that enhances the activity or number of NK                cells to the individual, upon a determination that                the individual has sNID1, optionally at increased                levels compared to a control.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Agent: The agent binds sNID1 and                  inhibits binding of NKp44 to sNID1. The agent                  binds mNID1 at the surface of a NID1-releasing                  cell. The agent is an antibody or antibody                  fragment. The agent is an antibody or antibody                  fragment that binds membrane-bound NID1 (mNID1)                  and is capable of mediating the depletion of                  cells expressing mNID1. The agent comprises NKp44                  polypeptide, optionally a NID1-binding fragment                  of NKp44. The agent is an antibody or antibody                  fragment that competes with NKp44 polypeptide for                  binding to a sNID1 polypeptide. The agent                  comprises a sNID1-binding fragment of NKp44.                  Preferred Method: The method (M1) involves                  administering the agent in an amount sufficient                  to decrease sNID1-mediated immunosuppression to                  the individual. The method (M1) involves                  administering the agent in an amount sufficient                  to deplete NID1-releasing cells to the                  individual. The method (M1) involves                  administering the agent in an amount sufficient                  to decrease sNID1 in circulation or in the tumor                  environment to the individual. The individual has                  a disease characterized by immunosuppression,                  optionally a state characterized by a deficiency                  in NK cell activity. The individual has sNID1 in                  circulation and/or tumor tissue, optionally at an                  increased level compared to a healthy individual.                  The individual has tumor or tumor adjacent tissue                  characterized by presence of NID1-releasing                  cells. The method (M1) involves detecting sNID1,                  where the presence of sNID1 or elevated levels of                  sNID1 indicates that the individual has disease                  characterized by a state of inhibition of NK cell                  cytotoxicity. The method (M1) involves detecting                  NID1-expressing cells, where the presence of, or                  elevated numbers of NID1-expressing cells                  indicates that the individual has disease                  characterized by immunosuppression.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Virucide; Immunostimulant. No                biological data given.

AB    NOVELTY - Lipid nanoparticles comprise (a) mRNA, 30-70                mol% phosphatidylcholine lipid, 5-50 mol% ionizable                cationic lipid, sterol chosen from cholesterol and                its derivative, and 0.5-5 mol% hydrophilic                polymer-lipid conjugate, or (b) encapsulated mRNA,                20-70 mol% phosphatidylcholine lipid, ionizable                lipid, and at least one of sterol and hydrophilic                polymer-lipid conjugate, where the lipid                nanoparticles exhibit 10% increase in gene                expression of the mRNA in vivo as measured in a                subset of cells from the bone marrow or spleen                chosen from macrophages, monocytes and/or T-cells                at 24 hours and/or 3 days post-injection as                compared to an Onpattro-type formulation of                MC3/distearoylphosphatidlycholine                (DSPC)/cholesterol/polyethylene glycol (PEG)-lipid                at 50/10/38.5/1.5, and the gene expression is                quantified in an animal model by detection of cells                positive for green fluorescent protein (GFP) using                flow cytometry.
   USE - The lipid nanoparticles are used for preparing                medicament for performing extrahepatic delivery of                mRNA, performing in vivo delivery of mRNA to                mammalian subject, or performing delivery of mRNA                for in vivo production of protein or peptide in                extrahepatic tissue or organ for treating disease                or disorder i.e. autoimmune disorder, infectious                disease, and cancer in vivo (all claimed). The                infectious diseases are bacterial, viral, fungal or                parasitic infections. The cancer includes lung                cancer, colon cancer, rectal cancer, anal cancer,                bile duct cancer, small intestine cancer, stomach                (gastric) cancer, esophageal cancer, gallbladder                cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic cancer, appendix                cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, prostate cancer, renal cancer (e.g. renal                cell carcinoma), cancer of the CNS, glioblastoma,                skin cancer, lymphomas, choriocarcinoma, head and                neck cancers, osteogenic sarcomas, and blood                cancers. Non-limiting examples of specific types of                liver cancer include hepatocellular carcinoma                (HCC), secondary liver cancer (e.g. caused by                metastasis of some other non-liver cancer cell                type), and hepatoblastoma.
   ADVANTAGE - The lipid nanoparticles have improved                stability and biodistribution.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for method                for performing in vivo delivery of mRNA to a                mammalian subject, or performing delivery of mRNA                for in vivo production of protein or peptide in an                extrahepatic tissue or organ, which involves                administering the lipid nanoparticles.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Product: The lipid nanoparticles                  comprise 40-60 mol%, preferably 45-55 mol%                  phosphatidylcholine, less than 40 mol% ionizable                  cationic lipid, and 15-45 mol%, preferably 18-40                  mol% sterol. The lipid nanoparticles exhibit at                  least a 10% increase in gene expression of the                  mRNA in vivo as measured in an extrahepatic                  tissue or organ, where the extrahepatic tissue or                  organ is spleen, bone marrow, lungs, kidney,                  heart, abdominal skin, back skin and/or ear.                  Preferred Components: The phosphatidylcholine                  lipid is DSPC, dioleoylphosphatidylcholine                  (DOPC), 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine                  (POPC) or dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC),                  preferably DSPC or DPPC. The phosphatidylcholine                  is a mixture of two phosphatidylcholine lipids.                  The mixture comprises                  distearoylphosphatidylcholine (DSPC) and                  dioleoylphosphatidylcholine (DOPC). The cationic                  lipid is an amino lipid. The hydrophilic                  polymer-lipid conjugate is a polyethylene                  glycol-lipid conjugate. The green fluorescent                  protein is measured in a macrophage/monocyte cell                  population isolated from the spleen or liver of                  the mouse post-injection, where the increase in                  expression is determined by measuring a                  percentage of cells in the cell population that                  are positive for the enhanced green fluorescent                  protein (eGFP). The green fluorescent protein is                  measured 3 days post-injection and wherein the                  animal model is a mouse. The in vivo expression                  of green fluorescent protein in a                  macrophage/monocyte cell population isolated from                  the bone marrow or spleen of the mouse post                  injection is increased by at least 50% over                  sphingomyelin-containing lipid nanoparticles that                  substitutes sphingomyelin for the DSPC but                  otherwise has an identical lipid composition as                  the lipid nanoparticles. Preferred Method: The                  mRNA accumulates in the spleen or bone marrow of                  the subject at least one day                  post-administration.
   ACTIVITY - Immunosuppressive; Cytostatic; Antibacterial;                Virucide; Fungicide; Antiparasitic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene therapy. Test details are described but                no results given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The lipid nanoparticles are administered by                parenteral i.e. intraarterial, intravenous,                subcutaneous or intramuscular, intratumoral,                intranasal, intravitreal, subretinal or intrathecal                route. No dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details about flow                cytometry in vivo studies, and extrahepatic mRNA                gene expression in immune cell subsets that do not                support the claims.

   BODA R

GA 202600317S
AB    NOVELTY - The system has a preprocessing unit which is                configured for artifact removal using morphological                filtering, BlackHat operations, multi-scale line                detection, and inpainting. A Double U-Net-based                segmentation module extracts precise lesion                boundaries. A DermaNet deep convolutional                classification module performs a multi-class skin                lesion recognition. A dataset processing unit                supports augmentation, normalization, and image                quality verification. A computational controller                manages end-to-end execution of preprocessing,                segmentation, and classification tasks. The                processing unit automatically identifies and                removes artifacts including hair strands,                illumination irregularities, shadows, ruler marks,                and air bubbles.
   USE - Automated dermatological image analysis system                for identifying and classifying skin lesion, skin                cancer and other dermatological disorders. Uses                include but are not limited to cloud-based                diagnostic platforms, embedded medical devices, and                standalone desktop environments.
   ADVANTAGE - The preprocessing, segmentation, and                classification are executed sequentially without                manual intervention. The end-to-end automated                solution improves the precision and dependability                of computer-aided dermatological diagnosis. The                highly accurate and efficient system for segmenting                and categorizing skin lesions is created. The                automated preprocessing method eliminates the hair                and lighting artifacts by combining the                morphological and inpainting techniques.

AB    NOVELTY - Identification of a cancer in an individual                comprising isolating a biological sample from an                individual, and detecting the presence or absence                of amplification of the Met gene, where the                presence of amplification indicates that the cancer                is susceptible to treatment, is new.
   USE - The method is used for the identification of a                cancer and subsequent treatment, e.g.                gastrointestinal cancer, prostate cancer, ovarian                cancer, breast cancer, head and neck cancer, lung                cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, cancer of the                nervous system, kidney cancer, retina cancer, skin                cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic cancer,                genital-urinary cancer, esophageal cancer, bladder                cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method identifies patients who will most                benefit from particular therapies to limit clinical                trial participation to only this subset of                individuals and to provide the most appropriate                therapy to each individual person in need.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   treating cancer comprising identifying a                patient with cancer by amplification of the Met                gene and/or overexpression of the Met receptor, and                administering PHA-665752 (RTM: (3Z)-5-                [(2,6-dichlorobenzyl)sulfonyl] -3- [(3,5                -dimethyl-4- {[(2R)-2-                (pyrrolidin-1-ylmethyl)pyrrolidin-1-yl] carbonyl}-1                H-pyrrol-2-yl)methylene]-1                ,3-dihydro-2H-indol-2-one), or PF-02341066 (RTM:                Not defined);
   a kit for identifying a cancer in an                individual that is susceptible to treatment                comprising an antibody probe that specifically                recognizes Met, a detection probe that specifically                recognizes the antibody probe, products and                reagents required to carry out                immunohistochemistry, and instructions; and
   a method to direct treatment of a subject with                a cancer, where the expression of the Met gene in                an individual is associated with a status utilized                for the direction of treatment, where the status of                an individual as having amplification of the Met                gene directs treatment of the individual with a Met                inhibitor.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows a whole genome profile of an                individual tumor showing the ratio of tumor to                normal DNA from Brcal-11/co Trp53 MMTV-Cre                mice.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Component: The probe is a nucleic                  acid, antibody, antibody fragment, or aptamer.                  The biological sample comprises tumor sample,                  paraffin embedded tumor sample, or a frozen tumor                  sample.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: Amplification of the Met                  gene is analyzed by detecting increased Met gene                  copy number or increased Met protein expression.                  The Met gene copy number and/or increased Met                  protein expression is determined by PCR, qPCR,                  RT-PCR, southern blot, comparative genomic                  hybridization, microarray based comparative                  genomic hybridization, fluorescence in situ                  hybridization (FISH), immunohistochemisty (IHC),                  ligase chain reaction (LCR), transcription                  amplification, LAMP, or self-sustained sequence                  replication. Amplification of the Met gene is                  detected using a probe. The Met treatment is a                  tyrosine kinase inhibitor, or a Met inhibitor                  comprising a small molecule inhibitor, a                  competitive inhibitor, a nucleic acid, an                  antibody, an antibody fragment, or an                  aptamer.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor.

TI Optical system for use in e.g. commercial            microscopes, for examining skin biopsy samples to help            physician identify e.g. psoriasis, has imaging            component located at side surface on opposite side            target lens component to receive optical signal and            generate image.
AU WANG J
AE BEIJING CHAOWEIJING BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD (BEIJ-Non-standard)
GA 2025853526
AB    NOVELTY - The system has an objective lens assembly                located on a side of an object plane for receiving                a first optical signal generated by a sample when                the sample is located on the object plane. The                object lens assembly is provided with an infinite                far conjugate objective lens component and a                tubular lens component. A first imaging component                is located at a side surface of the object lens                assembly far away from the object plane and used                for receiving the first optical signal and                generating a first image. A second imaging                component located at the side surface on the                opposite side of a target lens component is used to                receive a second optical signal and generate a                second image, where the second image is an enlarged                image of a local position in the first image and                the second image comprises an expanded image of the                local position.
   USE - Optical system for use in an optical detection                device i.e. microscopic imaging device such as                commercial microscopes, for examining skin biopsy                samples to help a physician identify characteristic                manifestation of skin cancer, inflammatory skin                diseases such as psoriasis and eczema, and other                skin lesions.
   ADVANTAGE - The optical system overcomes technical                prejudice that the microscopic objective realizes                microcosmic imaging and obtains the image of                macroscopic field of view when using a set of                objective assemblies.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) an                optical detecting device; (2) a method for                detecting an optical detection device.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of an                optical system.
