TI Novel antibody or its fragment with respect to            synoviolin, capable of inhibiting self-ubiquitination            of synoviolin, useful for treating or preventing            rheumatoid arthritis or cancer.
AU NAKAJIMA T
   YAMASAKI S
   ZHANG L
   AMANO T
AE LOCOMOGENE INC (LOCO-Non-standard)
   LOCOMOGENE INC (LOCO-Non-standard)
GA 2006090518
AB    NOVELTY - An antibody (I) or its fragment with respect                to synoviolin, capable of inhibiting                self-ubiquitination of synoviolin, is new.
   USE - (I) or C1 is useful for treating or preventing                rheumatoid arthritis, cancer, fibrosis,                arteriosclerosis, Castleman's disease, myeloma                multiplex, Crohn's disease, idiopathic arthritis,                brain tumor, cancer of the tongue, pharyngeal                cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, esophageal                cancer, stomach cancer, pancreatic cancer, biliary                tract cancer, gall bladder cancer, duodenal cancer,                colon cancer, hepatic carcinoma, uterine cancer,                ovarian cancer, prostatic cancer, renal cancer,                bladder cancer, rhabdomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma,                osteosarcoma, enchondrosarcoma, skin cancer, acute                myelogenous leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia,                chronic lymphocytic leukemia, adult T-cell leukemia                or malignant lymphoma. (I) or its fragment is                useful for inhibiting self-ubiquitination of                synoviolin, which involves reacting (I) or its                fragment and synoviolin; for detecting the cell                that expresses synoviolin, which involves reacting                (I) or its fragment, and biological sample; and for                detecting cell proliferative disease by synoviolin,                which involves reacting (I) or its fragment, and                biological sample collected from a subject. The                cell proliferative disease includes the diseases as                mentioned above, and the cell is chosen from                synovial cell, osteoclast, cornified epithelial                cells, blood cell, cancer cell, myeloid cells,                fibroblast, vascular endothelial cell, dermis cell,                muscle cell, neuron, lymphocyte, vascular smooth                muscle cell, hepatocytes, pigment cell, fat cell,                uterus endothelial cell, alveolar epithelium cell,                undifferentiated mesenchymal cell and apical                ectodermal ridge. R1 is useful for                synoviolin-containing cell detection. R2 is useful                for detecting cell proliferative disease by                synoviolin, where the cell proliferative disease                includes the diseases as mentioned above, and the                cells include the cells as mentioned above                (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - (I) exhibits high affinity and specificity                with respect to synoviolin.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An antibody (I) or its fragment with respect                to synoviolin, capable of inhibiting                self-ubiquitination of synoviolin, is produced by                hybridoma obtained by the cell fusion of an                antibody producing cell of an animal being                immunized using a peptide having any one of 3 fully                defined 15 amino acid sequences (SEQ ID No. 3-5)                given in the specification, as an antigen, and                myeloma cell, where (I) is a monoclonal antibody or                its fragment with respect to synoviolin.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   hybridoma capable of producing (I), obtained                by cell fusion of antibody producing cell of an                animal immunized using a peptide having any one of                SEQ ID No. 3-5, as an antigen, and myeloma                cell;
   producing (I);
   a pharmaceutical composition (C1) comprising                (I) or its fragment;
   elf-ubiquitination inhibitor of synoviolin,                containing (I) or its fragment;
   reagent (R1) for synoviolin-containing cell                detection, comprising (I) or its fragment;                and
   reagent (R2) for detecting cell proliferative                disease by synoviolin, comprising (I) or its                fragment.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: (I) is produced by cultivating                  the fused cell comprising antibody producing cell                  of an animal immunized using a peptide having any                  one of SEQ ID No. 3-5, as an antigen, and myeloma                  cell, and collecting (I) from the obtained                  culture (claimed).Preferred Antibody: (I) does not influence                  ubiquitination of substrate protein of                  synoviolin, and is a monoclonal antibody or its                  fragment.
   ACTIVITY - Antirheumatic; Antiarthritic;                Antiarteriosclerotic; Cytostatic;                Antiinflammatory.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Inhibits self-ubiquitination of synoviolin                (claimed).
   In vitroanalysis of the efficacy of antibody                with respect to synoviolin in inhibiting                self-ubiquitination of synoviolin was carried out                as follows. A His-tagged synoviolin fusion protein                MBP-dTM Syno-His was mixed with SL-1 antibody                (antibody with respect to synoviolin), anti-FLAG                antibody or mouse immunoglobulin G (IgG). The                antigen antibody reaction was performed at                4&#176;C for 1.5 hours. The self-ubiquitination                of synoviolin was detected by mixing ubiquitin                activating enzyme (E1), ubiquitin binding enzyme                (E2), ArP, GST-HA-ubiquitin and MBP-dTM Syno-His                that reacted with the antibody. The mixture was                allowed to react at 37&#176;C for 120 minutes,                and subjected to sodium dodecyl                sulfate-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis                (SDS-PAGE). The ubiquitination of synoviolin was                detected by Western blot analysis. The result                indicated inhibition of self-ubiquitination of                MBP-dTM Syno-His by the SL-1 antibody.
   ADMINISTRATION - C1 is administered by oral or parenteral                including intravenous, intracutaneous,                intramuscular or intraperitoneal route, at a dosage                of 10 &#956;g-100 mg/kg body weight, preferably                100 &#956;g-10 mg/kg body weight.
   EXAMPLE - Three types of peptide comprising partial                amino acid sequence of human synoviolin, and                containing 3 fully defined 15 amino acid sequences                (SEQ ID No. 3-5) given in the specification, were                synthesized. The keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH)                was allowed to couple to each of the peptides                through Cys in the amino acid sequence. Each                synthetic peptide (50 &#956;g) coupled to KLH                was dissolved in physiological saline (0.1 ml).                Freund's complete adjuvant (0.1 ml) was added and                the immunogen was produced. The immunogen (0.2 ml)                was injected into BALB/c (female, 5-week old) mouse                at the subcutaneous portion. Immunization was                performed for a total of 4 times every 2 weeks. A                further immunization was performed once after 1                week. Eight days after the last immunization, blood                was collected from the mouse and serum was                fractionated. Spleen cell was collected from the                mouse and the induction of antibody with respect to                synoviolin was confirmed by enzyme linked                immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The obtained spleen                cells were fused with myeloma cell strain (P3U1),                in the presence of polyethylene glycol (PEG). The                fused cell was cultivated in hypoxanthine,                aminopterin, thymidine (HAT) culture medium for                10-14 days, and the clone capable of producing                antibody with respect to synoviolin was                selected.

TI Detecting or prognosing cancer and/or metastasis            comprises e.g. determining presence of mutation within            sodium leak channel (NALCN) in tumor sample, and            determining whether mutation causes reduction in pore            size of NALCN.
AU GILBERTSON R
   RAHRMANN E
   SHORTHOUSE D
AE CAMBRIDGE ENTERPRISE LTD (UYCA-C)
   CAMBRIDGE ENTERPRISE LTD (UYCA-C)
   CAMBRIDGE ENTERPRISE LTD (UYCA-C)
GA 202358944R
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting (M1) or prognosing cancer and/or                metastasis comprises analyzing a tumor sample                obtained from a subject, determining the presence                of at least one mutation within sodium leak channel                (NALCN) in the tumor sample, compared to a                reference sample, determining whether the mutation                causes a reduction in the pore size of NALCN, where                the mutation causes a reduction in the pore size of                NALCN, and using the reduction in pore size to                determine a risk score of cancer and/or                metastasis.
   USE - The method is useful for: detecting or                prognosing cancer and/or metastasis, where the                cancer comprises gastric cancer, gastric                adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, lung cancer,                non-small cell lung cancer, lung adenocarcinoma,                lung squamous cell carcinoma, bone cancer,                pancreatic cancer, colon cancer, colorectal cancer,                skin cancer, cancer of the head or neck, head and                neck squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma, uterine                cancer, ovarian cancer, rectal cancer, cancer of                the anal region, stomach cancer, testicular cancer,                breast cancer, brain cancer, hepatocellular cancer,                carcinoma of the fallopian tubes, carcinoma of the                endometrium, carcinoma of the cervix, carcinoma of                the vagina, carcinoma of the vulva, cancer of the                esophagus, cancer of the small intestine, cancer of                the endocrine system, cancer of the thyroid gland,                cancer of the parathyroid gland, cancer of the                adrenal gland, kidney cancer, sarcoma of soft                tissue, cancer of the urethra, cancer of the                bladder, renal cancer, thymoma, urothelial                carcinoma leukemia, prostate cancer, prostatic                adenocarcinoma mesothelioma, adrenocortical                carcinoma, lymphomas, e.g. Hodgkin's disease,                non-Hodgkin's, and multiple myelomas; determining                the activity of NALCN; detecting at least one                mutations in NALCN; and determining a risk score of                cancer and/or metastasis (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method utilizes NALCN that: plays a                crucial role in malignant and/or non-malignant cell                metastasis; regulates cell shedding from solid                tissues independent of cancer; does not affect cell                proliferation, apoptosis, immune-infiltration,                vasculature or &#945; -smooth muscle actin                (ASMA) expression in primary tumor; and does not                impact the incidence, tumor-free survival or growth                rates in primary tumors.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   determining (M2) the activity of NALCN                comprising analyzing a biological sample to detect                at least one mutations identified in as given in                table 2 of the specification, where the presence of                the mutation identified in as given in table 2 of                the specification indicates reduced activity of                NALCN;
   a kit comprising reagents for the detection of                the mutations in NALCN, where the mutation                correlates to a reduction in activity of NALCN                and/or a reduction in pore size of NALCN and                optionally instructions for use;
   a composition comprising reagents for the                detection of at least one mutations in NALCN, where                the mutation correlates to a reduction in activity                of NALCN and/or a reduction in pore size of NALCN;                and
   a computer-implemented method (M3) for                determine a risk score of cancer and/or metastasis,                comprising obtaining data indicating presence of                the mutation in a NALCN, in a tumor sample,                inputting the data into a computational model of                NALCN that simulates effects of mutations on NALCN,                determining, using the computational model, whether                the mutation causes a reduction in a pore size of                NALCN, and outputting, when the mutation is                determined to cause a reduction in pore size of                NALCN, a risk score of cancer and/or                metastasis.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method (M1): the                  reference sample is a sample of germline DNA                  obtained from the subject, or a sample of                  germline DNA obtained from a healthy subject;                  computational modelling is used to determine                  whether the mutation causes a reduction in pore                  size of NALCN, where computational modelling is                  performed using HOLE, challenge-handshake                  authentication protocol (CHAP), CAVER, or MOLE;                  the reduction in NALCN pore size is calculated by                  determining the difference in size of the                  ion-selectivity filter radius in the NALCN                  variant comprising a mutation compared to the                  wild-type NALCN filter radius; and the reduction                  in NALCN pore size is calculated by determining                  the difference in size of the gate radius in the                  NALCN variant comprising a mutation compared to                  the wild-type NALCN gate radius. The method (M1)                  comprises analyzing a biological sample obtained                  from a subject, to assess the activity of NALCN,                  and providing a risk score of cancer and/or                  metastasis based on the level of activity of                  NALCN, where the activity of NALCN is assessed by                  whole-cell electrophysiology, a fluorescence                  assay, a membrane potential sensing dye, and/or                  an ion flux assay. The method (M1) further                  comprises comparing the level of activity of                  NALCN in the biological sample with a reference                  value. The method (M1) comprises analyzing a                  biological sample to detect the presence of at                  least one mutations which correspond to a                  reduction of function of NALCN, and providing a                  risk score of cancer and/or metastasis based on                  the presence of the mutations which correspond to                  a reduction of function of NALCN. The method (M1)                  comprises identifying the stage of the cancer                  based on the mutations that are identified. The                  method (M1) comprises a further step of selecting                  a treatment. In the method (M2), the mutations                  are detected via (a1) allele-specific polymerase                  chain reaction (PCR), high resolution melting                  curve analysis, genomic sequencing fluorescence                  in situ hybridization (FISH), comparative genomic                  hybridization (CGH), restriction fragment length                  polymorphism (RELP), amplification refractory                  mutation system (ARMS), reverse transcriptase PCR                  (RT-PCR), real-time PCR, multiplex                  ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA),                  denaturing gradient gel electrophoresis (DGGE),                  single strand conformational polymorphism (SSCP),                  chemical cleavage of mismatch (CCM), protein                  truncation test (PTT), or oligonucleotide                  ligation assay (OLA). The reagents are suitable                  for carrying out the component (a1) as per se.                  Preferred Components: In the method (M1): the                  mutations are located in the pore turret domain                  or voltage sensing domain of NALCN; and the                  mutations comprises the mutations identified in                  as given in table 2 of the specification. In the                  method (M2): the biological sample is analyzed in                  vitro or ex vivo; and the biological sample is a                  tissue sample or a tumor sample.

GA 2024110913
AB    NOVELTY - Constructing humanized patient-derived lung                cancer in-situ xenograft method mouse model                involves selecting fresh tumor tissue, and in-situ                transplanting to corresponding organs of a mouse by                a microsurgery method to construct a model. The                modeling of the patient-derived immune system is                performed by tail vein injection density gradient                centrifugation of patient-derived peripheral blood                mononuclear cells. The mice skin loss, body weight,                activity signs, blood biochemical index detection                and major system histopathological examination                model IRAEs scores are established.
   USE - Method for constructing humanized                patient-derived lung cancer in-situ xenograft                method mouse model.
   ADVANTAGE - The humanized patient-derived lung cancer                in-situ xenograft method mouse model separate                patient-derived peripheral blood mononuclear cells                by tail vein injection density gradient                centrifugation for patient-derived immune system                modelling. The main system histopathological                examination establishing model IRAEs score realize                that the subcutaneous micro-environment is                different from the original micro-environment of                the patient, and observation window is long,                modelling time is less, success ratio is high, and                sample amount of the needed patient is small.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Process: The in-situ transplanting                  of corresponding organs of a mouse by a                  microsurgery method to construct a model involves                  isolating patient sample, then putting patient                  sample into a buffer solution, precooling at                  4&#8451; for 72 hours and storing at                  4&#8451;; dividing the tissue into                  1mm&#215;1mm pieces; inoculating microsurgery                  in situ in the right lung of mice; covering the                  lung of the mouse with a lead sheet after three                  weeks, then performing 0.5Gy irradiation for                  marrow removal, and separating peripheral blood                  mononuclear cells from a patient; and obtaining                  tail vein injection mice, humanized model. The                  step of selecting fresh tumor tissue specifically                  involves carrying out surgical excision for                  patients who have been identified as in need of                  surgical treatment, and obtaining fresh tumor                  tissue simultaneously during the surgical                  procedure. Biopsy is carried out by needle                  aspiration, puncture and like techniques, then                  small amounts of tissue samples are collected                  from the tumor site, and appropriate therapeutic                  guidelines and firm inclusion criteria are                  generally be followed to ensure that information                  collection is truly reliable. An organ                  transplantation is carried out for patients who                  need to carry out organ transplantation such as                  liver transplantation, kidney transplantation and                  the like, a certain amount of fresh tumor tissues                  are left for research and used when the patients                  are removed. The step of selecting a                  transplantation source involves obtaining                  homogeneous or heterogeneous tissues, either                  autonomously or on a professional laboratory                  animal base, and requires attention that these                  tissues of origin must strictly meet the                  requirements of ethical regulations and the                  associated laws and regulations.Preferred Conditions: The desired tissue is                  collected from the donor animal and subjected to                  preliminary treatment and preservation in a                  manner that varies depending on the type of                  tissue, including cutting, handling, storage                  procedures, and care is taken to prevent aging of                  the tissue, and further related physiological                  measurements such as blood oxygen level, pulse                  beat, body temperature are required. A recipient                  surgical procedure is performed by subjecting                  mice to local anesthesia and antibacterial                  treatment by selecting an appropriate surgical                  mode, and then the prepared tissues are rapidly                  injected into the recipient animals by using a                  microscope and a fine surgical tool, and the                  operation process needs careful and highly                  skilled work, so that the living body stress                  reaction and even death are prevented. The                  post-implantation treatment is carried out on                  mice need to be properly monitored and cared for                  to ensure smooth growth and integration of the                  transplanted tissue and, in addition, it is                  subjected to some degree of sterility, for                  example, with preservatives or antibiotics.

TI Method for identifying and administering            customized therapies, comprises obtaining sequencing            data indicating sequence representations derived from            nucleic acid molecules, and analyzing sequencing data            to determine representations.
AU VALOUEV A
AE GUARDANT HEALTH INC (GUAT-C)
GA 202597337E
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves obtaining sequencing data                indicating sequence representations (110-116)                derived from nucleic acid molecules present in                samples obtained from subjects. The sequencing data                is computationally analyzed to determine groups of                sequence representations that correspond to genomic                regions (108), where individual groups of the                sequence representations are aligned with a                discrete genomic region. A set of Convolutional                neural networks(RTM: Deep learning network) is                generated. Tumor indications determined by the                neural networks are computationally analyzed to                determine an overall tumor indication, where the                neural network determines a tumor indication                related to a tumor being present in the subjects                based on images corresponding to the genomic                regions.
   USE - Method for identifying and administering                therapies i.e. customized therapies, to patients or                subjects based on determination of presence or                absence or levels of epigenomic and/or genetic                variation for detecting cancer. Uses include but                are not limited to blood cancers, central nervous                system (CNS), brain cancers, lung cancers, skin                cancers, nose cancers, throat cancers, liver                cancers, bone cancers, lymphomas, pancreatic                cancers, bowel cancers, rectal cancers, thyroid                cancers, bladder cancers, kidney cancers and mouth                cancers.
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides improved cancer detection                using liquid biopsy assays, and has improved                capability to classify a sample as containing                tumor-derived DNA. The method involves partitioning                DNA on basis of a modification, such as                methylation, and removing nonspecifically                partitioned DNA using methylation dependent                restriction enzyme (MDRE) and/or methylation                sensitive restriction enzyme (MSRE) so as to                provide improved efficiency and/or cost over DNA                analysis methods.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                system comprising hardware processors for                identifying and administering therapies.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of a                computational architecture that implements CNNs to                identify samples obtained from subjects in which a                tumor-related biological condition is                present.
   100Computational architecture
   106Reference sequence
   108Genomic region
   110-116Sequence representations
   128Image data

TI Enhancing immunogenicity of cells by increasing            the presentation of major histocompatibility complex            (MHC) Class I surface molecules, by administering a            bio-acceptable substance that promotes transcription of            genes in the cells.

GA 2008K07395
AB    NOVELTY - Enhancing the immunogenicity of cells by                increasing the presentation of major                histocompatibility complex (MHC) Class I surface                molecules for detection by cytotoxic T-lymphocyte                cells comprises administering to the cells an                amount of a bio-acceptable substance that promotes                transcription of genes in the cells to cause                enhanced MHC Class I surface expression of the                cells.
   USE - The methods are useful for enhancing the                immunogenicity of cells and antigen presenting                cells preparing an autologous cancer cell vaccine;                and screening for a cell treatment regimen that                elicits in a cell a histone deacetylase inhibitor                activity and does not elicit an apoptosis promoting                activity. The histone deacetylase inhibitor or                histone acetylase promoter is useful for                formulating a medicament for enhancing the                expression of peptide-loaded MHC Class 1 protein                complexes on a cell surface; for enhancing the                expression of peptide-loaded MHC Class 1 protein                complexes on a cell surface; for stimulating a                T-cell response to a peptide-loaded MHC Class 1                epitope; and for treating an intracellular                microbial infection in a patient, where the                intracellular microbial infection is a viral                infection. It can also be used as a DNA vaccine, a                protein based vaccine, a bacterial based cancer                vaccine, a chemotherapy, an adjuvant, a growth                factor, a primary cancer treatment, or a cancer                vaccine. The TAP-1 expression increasing amount of                the bio-acceptable substance that promotes                transcription of a gene which affects MHC Class I                surface expression in the cells to cause enhanced                MHC Class I surface expression of the cells, or                that is effective to promote transcription of a                gene in the MHC Class II or Class I chromosomal                region to cause enhanced MHC Class I surface                expression of the cells, is useful for preparing or                manufacturing a composition for administration to a                mammal suffering from a disorder involving excess                TAP-1 expression-deficient cells. The disorder is                selected from cervical cancer, colorectal cancer,                non-Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphoma, stomach carcinoma,                liver carcinoma, leukemia , kidney carcinoma,                pancreatic carcinoma, sarcoma, mesothelioma,                uterine carcinoma, bladder carcinoma, head and neck                carcinoma, esophageal cancer, testicular cancer,                ovarian carcinoma, thyroid cancer, oral cancer,                stomach cancer, cancer of the larynx, Hodgkin                lymphoma, breast carcinoma, prostate carcinoma,                melanoma, non-melanoma skin cancer, basal cell skin                cancer, squamous cell skin cancer, lung carcinoma                brain cancer, multiple myeloma, and an infectious                disease (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a pharmaceutical composition for                administration to a mammal to enhance MHC Class I                surface expression of cells, comprising a                bio-acceptable substance that promotes                transcription of transporters associated with                antigen processing (TAP)-1 gene in the cells on                other genes involved in MHC Class I expression, to                cause enhanced MHC Class I surface expression of                the cells and a adjuvant or carrier, where the                amount of bio-acceptable substance is insufficient                to trigger apoptosis;
   use of a histone deacetylase inhibitor or a                histone acetylase promoter to formulate a                medicament for enhancing the expression of                peptide-loaded MHC Class 1 protein complexes on a                cell surface;
   use of a histone deacetylase inhibitor or a                histone acetylase promoter for enhancing the                expression of peptide-loaded MHC Class 1 protein                complexes on a cell surface;
   a method of preparing an autologous cancer                cell vaccine comprising: (a) obtaining cancer cells                from a patient; (b) treating the cancer cells with                a histone deacetylase inhibitor or a histone                acetylase promoter; and (c) vaccinating the patient                with the treated cells; and
   a method of screening for a cell treatment                regimen that elicits in a cell a histone                deacetylase inhibitor activity and does not elicit                an apoptosis promoting activity comprising: (a)                exposing a cell to one or more test compounds at                one or more test concentrations; and (b) assaying                for the level of histone deacetylase activity in                the cell and assaying for the level of apoptotic                activity in the cell.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In enhancing the                  immunogenicity of cells, the cells are                  sub-optimal in TAP-1 expression. The                  bio-acceptable substance is a histone H3                  deacetylase inhibitor, which is a hydroxamic                  acid-based histone H3 deacetylase inhibitor, or a                  transcriptional co-activator having intrinsic                  histone acetyl transferase activity. The histone                  H3 deacetylase inhibitor is trichostatin A.                  Preferably, the bio-acceptable substance is a                  histone acetyl transferase. The histone acetyl                  transferase comprises at least one member of the                  CBP/p300 protein family. Enhancing the                  immunogenicity of pathological cells and antigen                  presenting cells by increasing the presentation                  of MHC Class I surface molecules for detection by                  cytotoxic T-lymphocyte cells, precursors of                  cytotoxic T-lymphocyte cells, and memory                  cytotoxic T-lymphocyte cells comprises                  administering to the cells or animals an amount                  of a bio-acceptable substance to promote                  transcription of genes in the MHC class II or                  class I chromosomal region to cause enhanced MHC                  Class I surface expression of the cells, the                  amount being insufficient to trigger apoptosis                  alone. The genes are selected from TAP-1, TAP-2,                  LMP-2, tapasin, Beta-2 microglobulin, B7-1, B7-2,                  CD28, MHC Class I, Erp57, LMP-7, PA28,                  IRP-1,2,3,4,5,6,7, CBP, CIITA, RFX5, RFXAP,                  TNF-alpha, Complement C2, C4, CD80, CD86, human                  leukocyte antigen (HLA)-DR, HLA-ABC,                  intracellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1),                  Toll-like receptors (1-11), macrophage                  inflammatory protein-3&#946; /chemokine,                  motif CC, ligand 19-induced, nuclear factor-kappa                  B, CBP, PCAF and SRC-1, p21, expression of                  TNF-Related Apoptosis Inducing Ligand (TRAIL)                  (Apo2L, TNFSF10), Stat1, interferon alpha,                  vascular endothelial growth factor,                  hypoxia-inducible factor 1&#945; , or matrix                  metalloproteinase 9. The process further                  comprises adjusting the amount of the                  bio-acceptable substance to a dose that is                  effective to promote transcription of genes in                  the MHC class II or class I chromosomal region to                  cause enhanced MHC Class I surface expression of                  the cells, and insufficient to trigger apoptosis.                  Administration occurs in vivo or ex vivo. In the                  process, the cell is an antigen presenting cell,                  a dendritic cell, a phagocytic cell, a cell of a                  monocyte lineage, a cell of a macrophage lineage,                  a polymorphonuclear cell, a cell of a neutrophil                  lineage, an endothelial cell, an astrocyte, or a                  cell infected by a microorganism. The process                  also comprises confirming prior to the                  administering that the cells are deficient in                  presentation of MHC Class I surface molecules for                  detection by cytotoxic T-lymphocyte cells as                  compared to non- pathological cells. It further                  comprises confirming prior to administering that                  the cells are TAP-1 deficient as compared to                  non-pathological cells. In preparing an                  autologous cancer cell vaccine, the cancer cells                  are rendered replication-defective prior to the                  step of vaccinating the patient. The cancer cells                  are irradiated prior to the step of vaccinating                  the patient to render the cells                  replication-defective. In screening for a cell                  treatment regimen that elicits in a cell a                  histone deacetylase inhibitor activity and does                  not elicit an apoptosis promoting activity, the                  amount is not toxic to the cell. The amount                  evokes immune recognition of the pathological                  cells or evokes an immune response to the                  pathological cells. The use is in vitro.                  Preferred Cell: The cell is a cancer cell. It is                  also selected from a dendritic cell, a phagocytic                  cell, a cell of a monocyte lineage, a cell of a                  macrophage lineage, a polymorphonuclear cell, a                  cell of a neutrophil lineage, an endothelial                  cell, an astrocyte, and a cell infected by a                  microorganism. Preferably, the cell is a cell                  infected by a virus. The cell is a cancer cell                  and the virus is an oncolytic virus. The histone                  deacetylase inhibitor or histone acetylase                  promoter is for use in combination with a                  microorganism that infects the cell. The histone                  deacetylase inhibitor is selected from                  suberonylanilide hydroxamic acid, amide analogues                  of Trichostatin A, Trapoxin, hydroxyamic acid                  analogues of Trapoxin, Scriptaid                  (6-(1,3-Dioxo-1H,3H-benzo[de]isoquinolin-2-yl)-hexanoic                  acid hydroxyamide), or Scriptaid analogs.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Composition: The composition                  further comprises a vaccine formulation.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Antimicrobial; Virucide. Test                details are described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Vaccine; Histone-Deacetylase-Inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - The substance is administered by an exposure                in vitro to the cells at a concentration of not                more than 100 ng/ml for not more than 50 hours. It                is administered at a daily dose of not more than                0.5 mg/kg (all claimed). Administration can be                through intravenous, intramuscular,                intraperitoneal, oral, nasal, parenteral, or                intertumoral route.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI New marker useful for diagnosing cancer e.g.            breast cancer, contains S100A8, S100A9, annexin A2,            keratin 19, thioredoxin, gelsolin, apolipoprotein C1,            fibronectin 1, lipoprotein A, mucin 1 and placenta            enriched 1.

AB    NOVELTY - A marker comprising at least one chosen from                S100A8, S100A9, annexin A2 (ANXA2), keratin 19                (KRT19), thioredoxin (TRX1), gelsolin (GSN),                apolipoprotein C1 (APOC1), carbonic anhydrase 1                (CA1), cell adhesion molecule L1 like (CHL1),                fibronectin 1 (FN1), lipoprotein A (LPA), mucin 1                (MUC1) and placenta enriched 1 (PLAC1), is                new.
   USE - The marker is useful for diagnosing cancer                chosen from breast cancer, ovarian cancer, colon                cancer, stomach cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic                cancer, cervical cancer, thyroid cancer,                parathyroid cancer, lung cancer, non-small cell                lung cancer, prostate cancer, gallbladder cancer,                biliary tract cancer, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma,                Hodgkin's lymphoma, hematologic cancer, bladder                cancer, kidney cancer, melanoma, colon cancer, bone                cancer, skin cancer, head cancer, uterine cancer,                rectal cancer, brain tumor, anal cancer, Fallopian                tube carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma, vaginal                cancer, vulvar carcinoma, esophageal cancer, small                intestine cancer, endocrine adenocarcinoma, adrenal                cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, urethral cancer,                penile cancer, ureteral carcinoma, renal cell                carcinoma, renal pelvic carcinoma, CNS central                nervous system tumor, primary CNS lymphoma, spinal                cord tumor, brainstem glioma or pituitary adenoma.                The method is useful for screening a drug for                preventing or treating the cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The marker enables to diagnose cancer in an                accurate and convenient manner with detection high                specificity and sensitivity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) composition comprising an agent for                measuring expression level of at least one protein                chosen from S100A8, S100A9, ANXA2, KRT19, TRX1,                GSN, APOC1, CA1, CHL1, FN1, LPA, MUC1 and PLAC1, or                gene encoding at least one protein chosen from                S100A8, S100A9, ANXA2, KRT19, TRX1, GSN, APOC1,                CA1, CHL1, FN1, LPA, MUC1 and PLAC1;
   (2) kit comprising the composition;
   (3) method for providing information for                diagnosing cancer involves measuring the expression                level of at least one protein or a gene encoding                the protein chosen from S100A8, S100A9, ANXA2,                KRT19, TRX1, GSN, APOC1, CA1, CHL1, FN1, LPA, MUC1                and PLAC1 in biological samples isolated from the                subject; and
   (4) method for screening a drug for preventing                or treating cancer involves treating a candidate                drug in a sample isolated from a cancer subject or                a cancer disease animal model and measuring the                expression level of at least one chosen from                S100A8, S100A9, ANXA2, KRT19, TRX1, GSN, APOC1,                CA1, CHL1, FN1, LPA, MUC1 and PLAC1 or a gene                encoding the same in a sample treated with the                candidate drug or a cancer disease animal                model.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Composition: The composition                  comprises agent for measuring expression level of                  the protein is at least one chosen from                  antibodies, oligopeptides, ligands, peptide                  nucleic acids (PNA), and aptamers that                  specifically bind to the protein of S100A8,                  S100A9, ANXA2, KRT19, TRX1, GSN, APOC1, CA1,                  CHL1, FN1, LPA, MUC1 and PLAC1. The agent for                  measuring expression level of the gene is at                  least one chosen from primers, probes and                  antisense nucleotides that specifically bind to a                  gene encoding a protein. Preferred Kit: The kit                  is reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) kit, DNA                  chip kit, enzyme linked immunosorbent assay                  (ELISA) kit, protein chip kit, rapid kit or                  multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) kit. Preferred                  Sample: The biological sample is whole blood,                  leukocytes, peripheral blood mononuclear cells,                  white blood cell soft coat, plasma, serum,                  sputum, tears, mucus, nasal washes, nasal                  aspirate, breath, urine, semen, saliva,                  peritoneal washings, ascites, cystic fluid,                  meningeal fluid, amniotic fluid, glandular fluid,                  pancreatic fluid, lymph fluid, pleural fluid,                  nipple aspirate, bronchial aspirate, synovial                  fluid, joint aspirate, organ secretions, cells,                  cell extracts or cerebrospinal fluid. The sample                  is a cell or tissue isolated from a cancer                  individual. Preferred Method: The method involves                  measuring the expression level of protein using                  protein chip analysis, immunoassay, ligand                  binding assay, matrix assisted laser                  desorption/ionization time of flight mass                  Spectrometry (MALDI-TOF) analysis, surface                  enhanced laser desorption/ionization time of                  flight mass spectrometry (SELDI-TOF), radiation                  immunoassay, radiation immunity diffusion method,                  Ouchterlony immunity diffusion, rocket                  immunoelectrophoresis, tissue immunostaining,                  complement fixation analysis, two-dimensional                  electrophoresis analysis, liquid                  chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), liquid                  chromatography-mass spectrometry/mass                  spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), Western blotting or                  enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The                  method involves measuring the expression level of                  protein by a multiple reaction monitoring (MRM)                  method. In the multi-reaction monitoring method,                  the internal standard material uses a synthetic                  peptide or E.coli ( beta ) galactosidase in which                  a specific amino acid constituting the target                  peptide is replaced with an isotope. The method                  involves measuring the expression level of gene                  by reverse transcription polymerase reaction                  (RT-PCR), Competitive RT-PCR, Real-time RT-PCR,                  RNase protection assay (RPA), Northern blotting                  or by DNA chip. The method further involves                  predicting that the possibility of developing the                  cancer is high, when the expression level of at                  least one protein or a gene encoding the protein                  is increased or decreased compared to the normal                  control group. The method further involves                  predicting responsiveness of target individual to                  chemotherapy or immunotherapy and prognosis after                  a surgical operation of the target individual                  and/or diagnosing the stage of cancer of the                  target individual, and/or predicting a recurrence                  probability of the target individual's cancer.                  The screening method further involves determining                  the candidate drug as a drug for preventing or                  treating cancer, if the expression level of the                  gene encoding the same increases or decreases                  compared to before the candidate drug is treated. PT P
PN CN114694750-A; CN114694750-B
TI Next generation sequencing platform based single            sample tumor somatic mutation judging model            constructing method, involves collecting relative gene            region of tumor by hybridization after extracting            single sample deoxyribonucleic acid.
AU REN Y
   LI S
   BU F
   QIN Y
   LEI Y
   DENG W
   YE L
AE JIANGSU SIMCERE MEDICAL EQUIP CO LTD (JIAN-Non-standard)
GA 202290115J
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves collecting a relative gene                region of the tumor by hybridization after                extracting the single sample deoxyribonucleic acid                (DNA). The tumor associated genes are sequenced.                The NGS sequencing data is compared to the human                reference genome. Mutation detection process is                performed based on the Chinese population control                sample sequencing data for seed mutation detection                and each computing mutation of allele frequency and                mutation occurrence frequency. Gene mutation                annotation process is performed by using the public                database. The precursor cell mutation, the first                strain mutation and the mutation allele frequency                (AF) are determined. A copy number fitting model is                constructed. A ploidy and segment copy number and a                secondary allele copy number are obtained. A cell                mutation judgment model is constructed. A body cell                mutation judging result is obtained and filtered to                obtain the reliable somatic mutation result.
   USE - NGS platform based single sample tumor somatic                mutation judging model constructing method. Uses                include but are not limited to skin cancer, bladder                cancer, lung cancer and kidney cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables developing single sample                tumor somatic cell mutation and TMB detection                method based on NGS platform, under the condition                of no pairing sample, can accurately detect somatic                mutation and TMB of the tumor sample. The method                saves the experiment of pairing sample and                sequencing and analysis time and cost, on the other                hand, and accurately detects the clinical decision                provides cancer patient decision without paired                sample detection condition and enlarges the                treating.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) a                tumor mutation load TMB evaluation model                construction method; (2) a computer readable                storage medium stored with a computer                program/instruction to realize a next generation                sequencing (NGS) platform based single sample tumor                somatic mutation judging model constructing method;                (3) a computer program product comprising a                computer program/instruction to realize a NGS                platform based single sample tumor somatic mutation                judging model constructing method.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow chart illustrating a                NGS platform based single sample tumor somatic                mutation judging model constructing method.                (Drawing includes non-English language                text).

PN US2008233125-A1; US7875277-B2
TI Treating squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) comprises            administering antibodies capable of specifically            binding laminin G4 and/or G5 domain or subdomain.
AU MARINKOVICH M P
AE MARINKOVICH M P (MARI-Individual)
   US DEPT VETERANS AFFAIRS (USGO-C)
   UNIV LELAND STANFORD JUNIOR (STRD-C)
GA 2008M61735
AB    NOVELTY - Treating SCC in a patient comprises                administering a therapeutic amount of one or more                antibodies in a pharmaceutical carrier, where one                or more of the antibodies is capable of                specifically binding laminin G4 and/or G5 domain or                subdomain, and inhibiting SCC tumorigenesis.
   USE - The methods and compositions are useful for                treating and diagnosing SCC selected from skin                cancer, lung cancer, head cancer, gastric cancer,                colorectal, throat cancer, cancer of the urinary                tract, cancer of the reproductive tract, esophageal                cancer, or bronchiogenic carcinoma (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The present invention provides new and                alternative methods of detection and treatment of                SCC.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method for diagnosing the presence of SCC by                (i) contacting a sample suspected of comprising                neoplastic epithelial cells with an antibody                capable of specifically binding laminin 5 G4 and/or                G5 domain or sub-domain, (ii) detecting the binding                of the antibody, and (iii) diagnosing the presence                or absence of SCC in the sample; and
   a method of evaluating the effect of a                candidate SCC drug in a patient by (i) detecting                the presence of laminin 5 G4 and/or G5 domain or                subdomain in a tissue sample from a patient                diagnosed with a SCC tumor prior to treatment with                a candidate drug, and (ii) detecting the presence                of a the laminin 5 G4 and/or G5 domain or subdomain                in a tissue sample from the patient following                treatment with the candidate drug, where a decrease                in the laminin 5 G4 and/or G5 domain or subdomain                following treatment with the candidate drug                indicates that the candidate drug is effective in                treating the SCC in the patient.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method of treating                  SCC in a patient, the antibody binds to a                  polypeptide comprising the defined sequence of                  184, 11, 16, 13, or 154 amino acids (ODD SEQ ID                  NOS: 13-19 or 23), given in the specification.                  The antibody binds to a migration facilitating                  protein (MFP) comprising the defined sequence of                  315 amino acids (SEQ ID NO: 21), given in the                  specification. The antibody is a polyclonal                  antibody or a monoclonal antibody. In the method                  for diagnosing the presence of SCC, the antibody                  further comprises a detectable label. The                  epithelial cells are squamous cells,                  keratinocytes, mucosal epithelial cells,                  gastrointestinal epithelial cells, corneal                  epithelia of the eye, or epithelial cells of the                  urinary and reproductive tract. The sample is a                  tissue sample, urine sample, or blood sample. In                  the method of evaluating the effect of a                  candidate SCC drug in a patient, the candidate                  agent is selected from antibodies or their                  fragments, small molecules, polypeptides, or                  aptamers.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Laminin 5 Alpha 3 G4-G5 Domain                Modulator.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is by oral, rectal,                transmucosal, transdermal, nasal, or intestinal                administration and parenteral delivery, including                intramuscular, subcutaneous, intramedullary                injections, as well as intrathecal, direct                intraventricular, intravenous, intraperitoneal,                intranasal, or intraocular injections. No dosage                details given.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The cancer that is treated is melanoma. It is ovarian cancer or estrogen-dependent breast cancer. The hyperproliferative skin disorder is psoriasis.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preparation: (I) is produced by standard chemical synthesis techniques.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: (I) is produced by standard cloning techniques.Preferred Nucleic Acid: (I) is detectably labeled. A polynucleotide which hybridizes under stringent hybridization conditions to (I) is also preferred. (I) comprises a nucleotide sequence 95 % identical to the reference sequence.Preferred Vector: The vector is an expression vector.Preferred Polypeptide: (II) is phosphorylated and is produced or contained in a recombinant host cell.Preferred Antibody: The antibody is detectably labeled.Preferred Method: The cancer that is detected is melanoma.
   WIDER DISCLOSURE - Variants of (I) and (II) are also disclosed.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; antipsoriatic; vulnerary; dermatological; antiproliferative.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene therapy; vaccine. The effect of antisense H11 oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) to inhibit melanoma cell growth was studied. SK-MEL-31 and SK-MEL-2 melanoma cells were exposed (24 hours) to different doses of antisense oligodeoxynucleotides (aODN-1: 3'-GGTACCGACTGCCAGT-5' and aODN-2: 3'-GGTGGTACCGACTGCC-5') complementary to the H11 translation initiation site and analyzed for their ability to proliferate, as determined by (3H)-TdR incorporation. Sense ODNs served as controls. Both antisense ODNs inhibited (3H)-TdR incorporation. Inhibition was seen with as little as 10 micro Molar of the ODNs and was maximal at 30 micrometers. (3H)-TdR incorporation was minimally (10-15 %) reduced by treatment with 30 micro Molar of scrambled ODN. Growth inhibition was 98 and 86 % for aODN-1 and aODN-2 respectively, while cell growth was not decreased in cells treated with the control ODNs.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is by an oral, intravenous, intraperitoneal, intralesional or topical route. The dosage of vaccine is 0.001-100 mg/kg.
   EXAMPLE - H11 cDNA was isolated from a HeLa cDNA library screened by immunoblotting with antibodies to peptides within the herpes simplex virus (HSV-2) ribonucleotide reductase large subunit (RR1) protein kinase (PK) oncoprotein. A total of 1 x 10 to the power of 6 plaques were screened. Eight pure plaque isolates were obtained which contained cDNA sequences. Single-stranded cDNA contained within one phagemid was rescued, isolated and purified. This cDNA, designated H11 was subcloned and sequenced. The gamma-32P-dCTP labeled H11 was then used to screen the melanoma cDNA library. The cDNA in one subcloned plaque was sequenced and found to be identical to H11. H11 cDNA consisted of 1835 base pairs, given in the specification.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves generating a cancer                prediction (240) for patients. A first batch of                images captured from the patients is obtained. A                first set of output values is generated by                providing as input to the first batch of images to                a first convolutional neural network. The                non-interpretable features (225a) are identified by                first convolutional neural network from first batch                of images to generate the first set of output                values. A second set of output values is generated                as input to the interpretable features (235a) and                definable features (237a) of the first batch of                images to a first machine learning model. A third                set of output values informative of the cancer                prediction is generated as input to the first set                of output values and the second set of output                values to a fully connected network (FCN).
   USE - Method for generating cancer prediction for                patients. Uses include but are not limited to                lymphoma, B cell lymphoma, T cell lymphoma, mycosis                fimgoides, Hodgkin's Disease, myeloid leukemia,                bladder cancer, brain cancer, nervous system                cancer, head and neck cancer, squamous cell                carcinoma of head and neck, kidney cancer, lung                cancer, neuroblastoma/glioblastoma, ovarian cancer,                pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer, skin cancer,                etc.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables early treatment                intensification, novel treatment options, and                enrichment for high-risk population for clinical                trial recruitment. The method integrates different                data types to achieve improved detection of cancer                and evaluation of cancer progression. The                integration of radiomics, histopathology, and                electronic health record (EHR) data into a                framework enhances cancer predictions. The                multimodal framework can be useful for developing                or supporting a clinician's treatment decision. For                example, based on the models predictions on the                likelihood of prostate cancer progression under                androgen-deprivation therapy (or therapeutic                resistance), clinicians can decide whether or not                to intensify treatment (e.g., use androgen receptor                directed therapy) early.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for generating cancer prediction for                patients; and
   method for developing set of machine learning                models for generating a cancer prediction for                prospective patients.

TI Isolating microRNA sample from skin, used to            detect, monitor, and diagnosing skin disease and            pathological skin states, comprises non-invasive tape            stripping.
AU BENSON N R
AE DERMTECH INT (DERM-Non-standard)
GA 2007882774
AB    NOVELTY - Isolating an microRNA (miRNA) sample from skin                comprises applying an adhesive tape to a target                area of the skin in a manner to isolate an                epidermal sample, where epidermal sample contains                miRNA, where the tape comprises a rubber adhesive,                and where the tape is pliable, thus isolating an                epidermal sample adhering to the adhesive                tape.
   USE - The method is useful for isolating microRNA                sample from skin, which is further used to identify                miRNA profile indicative of a disease, pathological                or physiological state of a human subject, or to                predict response to treatment for a disease,                pathological or physiological state, e.g.                dermatitis, psoriasis, diabetes, melanoma, or                prostate cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The present invention provides non-invasive                approach for recovering nucleic acids such as DNA,                messenger RNA, or miRNA from the surface of skin                via a simple tape stripping procedure that permits                a direct quantitative and qualitative assessment of                biomarkers; provides valuable genetic information,                not obtainable using a visible detection method;                provides information regarding cells of the                outermost layers of the skin that is not obtained                using biopsy samples; and provides method that is                far less traumatic than a biopsy.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   (1) a method for identifying an miRNA profile                indicative of a disease, pathological or                physiological state of a human subject; and
   (2) a method for predicting response to                treatment for a disease, pathological or                physiological state.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The tape is a rubber-based                  tape. The tape comprises a rubber adhesive on a                  polyurethane film. The tape is applied and                  removed from the skin 1-10 times. Isolating miRNA                  molecules from an epidermal sample from skin                  comprises applying an adhesive tape to a target                  area of the skin in a manner sufficient to                  isolate an epidermal sample adhering to the                  adhesive tape, where the epidermal sample                  comprises miRNA molecules, and isolating miRNA                  molecules from the epidermal sample. Identifying                  miRNA profile indicative of a disease,                  pathological or physiological state of a human                  subject comprises applying an adhesive tape to an                  area of skin in a manner to isolate an epidermal                  sample adhering to the adhesive tape, where the                  epidermal sample comprises miRNA molecules, and                  determining miRNA levels from the sample, or its                  amplification product, and comparing the levels                  with the m1RNA levels of a control sample, where                  a difference in miRNA level is indicative of an                  miRNA profile of a disease, pathological or                  physiological state of a subject. The method                  further comprises comparing the miRNA levels to                  expression levels of mRNA isolated from the same                  sample, thus expression profiling the mRNA                  population in the sample. Predicting response to                  treatment for a disease, pathological or                  physiological state comprises applying an                  adhesive tape to an area of skin in a manner to                  isolate an epidermal sample adhering to the                  adhesive tape, where the epidermal sample                  comprises m1RNA molecules, and determining miRNA                  levels from the sample, or its amplification                  product, and comparing the levels with the miRNA                  levels of an unaffected subject or sample, where                  a difference in miRNA level is indicative of a                  response to treatment of a disease, pathological                  or physiological state. In the above methods, the                  disease, pathological or physiological state is                  dermatitis, psoriasis, diabetes, melanoma, or                  prostate cancer.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves capturing (11304) images                of tooth illuminated with optical electromagnetic                signals. Normalized color channel histogram for                each image is generated (11306). Normalized color                channel histogram is correlated (11308) with                respect to wavelength scale. Spectral plots are                convoluted (11310) by subtracting spectral plot                from non-polarized electromagnetic signals. The                normalized composite blue channel spectral plot is                subtracted from normalized composite red channel                spectral plot to generate spectral signature for                tooth.
   USE - Method for generating spectral signature of                tooth. Uses include but are not limited for                analyzing metal composition, metal identification,                metal purity and strength, water quality, water                composition and purity, skin state, counterfeit                analysis of money, sweat gland activity and                anti-perspirant effectiveness, Mad Cow disease,                food and epidermal diseases, melanoma, skin cancer,                rheumatoid disease and skin disease, post-operative                cosmetic concern, secretion from mammary gland of                lactating women.
   ADVANTAGE - The recurrence and micrometastasis in                surrounding skin can be reduced, while enabling                minimal surgical morbidity and improved cosmetic                appearance. The efficiency of progress monitoring                can be improved easily. Hence monitored data can be                viewed as a recording in real time application. The                qualitative and quantitative parameter for analysis                of tooth can be improved. The process for                generating spectral signature of tooth can be                ensured easily within short period of time. The                accuracy and operability of process for generating                spectral signature of tooth can be ensured                easily.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method for generating spectral signature of                material;

   method for skin epidermal layers;
   method for analyzing water in skin epidermal                layers; and
   method for determination of aging of skin                based on skin epidermal layer.

TI Measuring the activity of UXS1 enzyme used for            screening medicine related to UXS1 enzyme activity,            comprises using UXS1 to hydrolyzes substrate UDPGlcA,            adding XYLT1 to catalyze UDP-xyl, converting UDP into            ATP, and detecting ATP, and inferring UXS1 enzyme            activity by intensity of obtained signal.
AU YANG Q
   ZHANG X
   WANG Q
   XIA Q
   YAN L
   LI Y
AE BEIJING ICE BIOSCI INC (BEIJ-Non-standard)
GA 202525993E
AB    NOVELTY - Measuring the activity of UDP-xylose synthase                1 (UXS1) enzyme comprises (a) using UXS1 to                hydrolyzes the substrate uridine diphosphate                glucuronic acid (UDPGlcA) to generate uridine                diphosphate xylose (UDP-xyl); (b) adding XYLT1 to                catalyze UDP-xyl to generate UDP; (c) converting                UDP into adenosine triphosphate (ATP); d)                quantitatively detecting ATP, and inferring UXS1                enzyme activity by the intensity of the obtained                signal.
   USE - Measuring the activity of UDP-xylose synthase                1 (UXS1) enzyme or the kit used for screening                medicine related to UXS1 enzyme activity, where                medicine is used to treat a disease selected from                Walker-Warburg syndrome and cancer, where the                cancer is bone, bone joint, muscle, lung, trachea,                heart, spleen, artery, vein, blood, capillary,                lymph node, lymphatic vessel, lymph fluid, oral                cavity, pharynx, esophagus, cardia, stomach,                duodenum, small intestine, colon, rectum, anus,                appendix, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, parotid                gland, sublingual gland, urinary kidney, ureter,                bladder, urethra, ovary, fallopian tube, uterus,                vagina, and cancer is caused by lesions in the                uterus, vulva, scrotum, testicles, vas deferens,                penis, eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin, brain, brain                stem, medulla oblongata, spinal cord, cerebrospinal                fluid, nerves, thyroid, parathyroid glands, adrenal                glands, pituitary gland, pineal gland, pancreatic                islets, thymus, gonads, sublingual glands and                parotid glands, and cancer may be lung cancer,                stomach cancer, esophageal cancer, liver cancer,                colon cancer, gallbladder cancer and cardia cancer                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method effectively reduces the cost of                UXS1 enzyme activity detection, helps                pharmaceutical companies quickly and                high-throughput screen the medicine effects of                related targets, and helps to promote the                development of related medicine.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a kit for                determining UXS1 enzyme activity, comprises XYLT1,                a xylosyltransferase substrate peptide, and                components of UDP-GloTM.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The ATP is used to                  oxidize the substrate luciferin and generate a                  light signal under the catalysis of luciferase.                  The UDPGlo(RTM: Glycosyltransferase assay) is                  used for detection. The concentration of UDPGlcA                  is 50-150&#956;M. The concentration of UXS1                  is 70-130nM.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.

PN US2010068151-A1
TI New pharmaceutical compound containing anti-cell            proliferation moiety and cell-specific targeting moiety            directly bound to one another by linker, useful for            treating hyperproliferative disease e.g. brain cancer            and breast cancer.
AU CHEN X
   ROSENBLUM M G
AE ROSENBLUM M G (ROSE-Individual)
   CHEN X (CHEN-Individual)
GA 2010D05526
AB    NOVELTY - A pharmaceutical compound (I) containing an                anti-cell proliferation moiety and cell-specific                targeting moiety, is new. The anti-cell                proliferation moiety and cell-specific targeting                moiety are directly bound to one another or bound                to one another by a linker, and at least one                chelator moiety is bound to the anti-cell                proliferation moiety and/or the cell-specific                targeting moiety.
   USE - For treating hyperproliferative disease                associated with neovascularization. The disease is                cancer comprising brain cancer (glioblastoma                multiforme), breast cancer, lung cancer, prostate                cancer, ovarian cancer, liver cancer, cervical                cancer, colon cancer, renal cancer, skin cancer,                head and neck cancer, bone cancer, esophageal                cancer, bladder cancer, uterine cancer, lymphatic                cancer, stomach cancer, pancreatic cancer,                testicular cancer, lymphoma, and leukemia (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   treating (M1) hyperproliferative disease in a                subject involving administering to the subject the                compound (I);
   diagnosing the presence of a                hyperproliferative disease in a human subject                involving administering to a human subject the                compound (I), where the chelator moiety is chelated                to a valent metal; and performing a noninvasive                imaging technique, where detection of an image                identifies the subject as having hyperproliferative                disease;
   detecting a therapeutic response following                treatment a patient with a hyperproliferative                disease involving: a) administering the compound                (I) to a subject with a hyperproliferative disease,                where the chelator moiety is chelated to a valent                metal ion and is detectable in vivo using a                noninvasive imaging technique; b) imaging the                subject using the noninvasive imaging technique to                obtain a first image; c) repeating the step (a);                and d) imaging the subject using the noninvasive                imaging technique to obtain a second image, where                reduction of the size or intensity of the second                image compared to the first image indicates                presence of a therapeutic response; and
   identifying a subject with a tumor that will                respond to treatment with the compound (I)                involving administering the compound (I) to a                subject with a tumor; and performing a noninvasive                imaging technique on the subject, where presence of                a detectable image identifies the subject as having                a tumor that will respond to treatment with the                compound.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The cell-specific                  targeting moiety is further defined as antibody,                  growth factor, hormone, polypeptide, peptide,                  aptamer, or cytokine. The antibody is full-length                  antibody, chimeric antibody, Fab', Fab, F(ab') 2,                  single domain antibody (DAB), Fv, single chain Fv                  (scFv), minibody, diabody and/or triabody. The                  vascular endothelial-specific targeting moiety is                  a VEGF. The VEGF is an isoform that is VEGF-121,                  VEGF-165, VEGF-189, or VEGF-206 (preferably                  VEGF-121). The VEGF sequence comprises amino acid                  sequence containing 121 [SEQ ID NO: 2], 206 [SEQ                  ID NO: 3], 189 [SEQ ID NO: 4], 183 [SEQ ID NO:                  5], 165 [SEQ ID NO: 6], 148 [SEQ ID NO: 7], or                  145 [SEQ ID NO: 8] amino acids as given in the                  specification.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - IMAGING AND COMMUNICATION - Preferred Components: The imaging comprises                  magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), MR                  spectroscopy, radiography, CT, ultrasound, planar                  gamma camera imaging, single-photon emission                  computed tomography (SPECT), or positron emission                  tomography (PET). The imaging is PET with                  (18)F-FLT.

TI Imaging method for area of interest on surface,            used in imaging, analysis and diagnosis of lesion            involves autofocusing integrated imaging device to            capture image of area of interest so that marker            applied to area of interest is discernible.
