GA 2013L43561
AB    NOVELTY - The imaging method involves applying a marker                to the area of interest to the surface such that                the marker binds to a targeted molecule of                interest. An integrated imaging device is                autofocused on the area of interest to capture an                image of the area of interest so that the marker is                discernible. The marker is a biotag that is applied                topically on the surface or injected into the                surface. A fluorescent fiducial is provided on the                surface within or adjacent to the area of interest.                The area of interest includes a lesion suspected to                be cancerous.
   USE - Imaging method for area of interest on a                surface. Can be used in imaging, analysis and                diagnosis of lesions aligning tissue surfaces, such                as cancers of the skin, mouth, colon, digestive                system cervix, bladder, lung, and in the diagnosis                of skin cancers including melanoma, skin basal cell                carcinoma, and non-cancerous skin diseases.
   ADVANTAGE - Permits early stage disease detection, early                body response to a new antigen and early body                response to a foreign antigen. Enables monitoring                of disease development and progression, and                investigation of macro environment of diseased cell                and tissue as indication of presence of disease.                The imaging method is easy to use, simple, low                cost, it provides a quick test to perform and can                be performed by someone other than the physician,                and it operates independent of skin color or                ethnicity. Provides for immediate test results and                consistency of results, and works for a wide range                of lesion types and body locations or Breslow                thickness and Clark level or the ABCDEF criteria.                The imaging method is minimally dependent on human                interpretation and requires minimal training                necessary. Provides automated or machine-assisted                medical documentation, such as photographs or                quantified test metrics, automated or                machine-assisted electronic medical record keeping,                such as machine readable codes on samples and files                that directly tie to patient, doctor and date.                Enables operation that is independent of visual                cues such as, color, shape and size. Enables                identification of melanoma in amelanotic skin                lesion and melanoma in small lesions, less than 5                millimeters.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a method of imaging a lesion on a                cavity/tissue surface;
   a method of making a camera for medical                diagnostic imaging;
   a camera for medical diagnostic imaging;
   a method of taking a photograph;
   a method of imaging a patient's cavity/tissue                surface for diagnostic purpose of detecting a                cancerous or pre-cancerous lesion;
   a fiducial for medical imaging;
   a method of manufacturing a medical imaging                camera;
   a method of automatic measurement of                cavity/tissue lesion on a patient; and
   a method of imaging a patient's skin for the                diagnostic purpose of detecting skin cancer.

TI New self-assembling polypeptide comprising            beta-strand motif operatively connected to hydrophilic            motif by protease substrate motif to self-assemble with            nominally identical beta-strand motifs and form            anti-parallel beta-sheet structure, used for detecting            protease for detecting e.g. cancer.

AB    NOVELTY - A self-assembling polypeptide comprising a                &#946; -strand motif configured to                self-assemble with nominally identical &#946;                -strand motifs and form an anti-parallel &#946;                -sheet structure, is new. The &#946; -strand                motif is operatively connected to a hydrophilic                motif by a protease substrate motif, the protease                substrate motif comprises a protease cleavage site                configured to specifically hybridize with a                protease, where when in an aqueous milieu and upon                hybridization of the protease to the protease                cleavage site, and the protease cleaves the                self-assembling polypeptide and dissociates the                &#946; -strand motif allowing the dissociated                &#946; -strand motif to self-assemble with the                nominally identical &#946; -strand motifs and                form the anti-parallel b-sheet structure.
   USE - The self-assembling polypeptide is useful for                detecting protease for detecting a cancer chosen                from liver cancer, skin cancer, cervical cancer,                brain cancer, lung cancer, stomach cancer,                bile-duct cancer, gastric cancer, pancreatic                cancer, bladder cancer, breast cancer, lung cancer,                prostate cancer, kidney cancer, brain cancer,                colorectal cancer, ovarian cancer, thyroid cancer,                melanoma cancer, and thyroid cancer, and detecting                a disease, disorder, or syndrome chosen from                pre-cancerous breast hyperplasia, prostate                disorder, Alzheimer's disease, acute coronary                disease, atherosclerosis disease, arthritis                disease, osteoarthritis disease, osteoporosis                disease, and acute coronary syndrome (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The self-assembling polypeptide performs more                sensitive detection of protease activity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method for detecting proteolytic cleavage by                enzyme-instructed &#946; -sheet formation,                involving administering a set of self assembling                polypeptides into an aqueous milieu, administering                &#946; -sheet intercalating dye configured to                emit a fluorescent signal upon forming a complex                with anti-parallel &#946; -sheet structures                formed by the self-assembly of &#946; -strand                motifs dissociated from their respective                self-assembling polypeptides by proteolytic                cleavage into the aqueous milieu to indicate the                presence of the protease in the aqueous milieu, and                detecting the fluorescent signal; and
   kit comprising the set of self-assembling                polypeptide and &#946; -sheet intercalating                dye.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves collecting a fresh medical                sample containing colon adenoma and normal tissue.                A Muller matrix and a polarization decomposition                parameter are obtained. A preset polarized light                characteristic component is extracted according to                polarization information separation and combination                characteristics of the Muller matrix. A                characteristic value distribution of a sample is                obtained. A weight parameter of a linear                combination model is optimized. A final linear                combination model is determined. A colon adenoma                detection result is outputted according to the                final linear combination model.
   USE - Method for detecting colon adenoma based on                Muller matrix analysis using an electronic device                (claimed) for early diagnosis of lesions such as                skin cancer and colon cancer, in a biomedicine                field.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables utilizing the synergy of                M01, M11 and depolarization factor to realize the                high-efficiency distinguishing of the colon adenoma                and the normal tissue prior to the dimensionless                treatment.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a system for detecting colon adenoma based on                Muller matrix analysis;
   an electronic device;
   a non-transient computer readable storage                medium comprising a set of instructions for                detecting colon adenoma based on Muller matrix                analysis;and
   a computer program product comprising a set of                instructions for detecting colon adenoma based on                Muller matrix analysis.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for immobilizing extracellular vesicles                or cells on a superabsorbent polymer surface,                involves (S1) mixing a solution containing                extracellular vesicles or cells with a                superabsorbent polymer, and (S2) incubating for                1-10 hours after step (S1).
   USE - The method is used for immobilizing                extracellular vesicles or cells on superabsorbent                polymer surface. The superabsorbent polymer is used                in a composition for diagnosing a disease. The                disease is cancer. The cancers include breast                cancer, ovarian cancer, colon cancer, stomach                cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic cancer, cervical                cancer, thyroid cancer, parathyroid cancer, lung                cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, prostate                cancer, gallbladder cancer, biliary tract cancer,                non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, blood                cancer, bladder cancer, kidney cancer, melanoma,                colon cancer, bone cancer, skin cancer, head                cancer, uterine cancer, rectal cancer, brain tumor,                perianal cancer, fallopian tube carcinoma,                endometrial carcinoma, vaginal cancer, vulvar                carcinoma, esophageal cancer, small intestine                cancer, endocrine cancer, adrenal cancer, soft                tissue sarcoma, urethral cancer, penile cancer,                ureteral cancer, renal cell carcinoma, renal pelvic                carcinoma, and central nervous system (CNS) tumor,                primary CNS lymphoma, spinal cord tumor, brainstem                glioma, and pituitary adenoma (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method fixes extracellular vesicles or                cells to the surface of a super absorbent polymer,                thus enabling the simple and rapid detection of                various biomarkers present in the extracellular                vesicles or cells while the extracellular vesicles                or cells are fixed to the surface of super                absorbent polymer, and enabling the simple                replacement of a solvent, that dissolves                extracellular vesicles or cells.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   uperabsorbent polymer having extracellular                vesicles or cells immobilized on its surface                prepared by the above-mentioned method;
   a kit for diagnosing a disease, comprising the                superabsorbent polymer on which the extracellular                vesicles or cells are fixed to the surface;
   a method of solvent replacement for a solution                containing extracellular vesicles or cells                comprising (S1) fixing extracellular vesicles or                cells on the surface of the superabsorbent polymer,                and (S2) resuspending the superabsorbent polymer on                which the extracellular vesicles or cells are                immobilized on the surface in a replacement                solvent; and
   a method for preparing a solution containing                extracellular vesicles or cells, comprising (a)                fixing extracellular vesicles or cells on the                surface of the superabsorbent polymer, (b)                resuspending the superabsorbent polymer on which                the extracellular vesicles or cells are fixed to                the surface in a replacement solvent, and (c)                recovering the solution containing extracellular                vesicles or cells resuspended in the replacement                solvent.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The step (S2) is performed                  by resuspending the solvent by pipetting or                  vortexing. Preferred Composition: The solution                  containing the extracellular vesicles or cells                  contains 1 x 106to 1 x 1013extracellular vesicles                  or 1 x 104to x 108cells. Preferred Components:                  The replacement solvent is phosphate buffered                  saline (PBS), distilled water, or a culture                  medium.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Components: The superabsorbent                  polymer is selected from a starch-based polymer                  obtained by copolymerizing starch with monomers                  of acrylonitrile, acrylic acid, acrylamide, or                  methacrylate; cellulose-based polymer obtained by                  copolymerizing the above monomer with                  carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC); and a synthetic                  resin-based polymer including polyvinyl                  alcohol-methacrylic acid block copolymer,                  styrene-maleic anhydride copolymer, polyacryl                  amide, or polyoxyethylene. The superabsorbent                  polymer is poly(acrylamide-co-acrylic acid)                  ((poly(acrylamide-co-acrylic acid)))                  superabsorbent polymer. The superabsorbent                  polymer is a superabsorbent resin bead having a                  diameter of 1-10 mm.

TI Gold nanoparticles useful for e.g. detection and            therapy of various diseases including cancer in animals            and human beings, stabilized with material coating of            soy or lentil plant material.
AU CHANDRA N
   KANNAN R
   KATTI K K
   KATTI K V
   SHUKLA R
   CHANDA N
AE UNIV MISSOURI (UMOR-C)
GA 2009H94880
AB    NOVELTY - Gold nanoparticles (10) stabilized with a                material coating of soy or lentil plant material                (12).
   USE - In sensing method and therapy (claimed); for                detection and therapy of various diseases including                cancer in animals and human beings; for diagnostic                and therapeutic techniques; for hyperthermia                treatment; for diagnostic imaging; as X-ray                enhancers in X-ray therapy of diseases including                cancer; and useful as coatings on skin, hair, for                direct injections into specific tissue, and for                ingestion. Also useful in medical diagnostics and                medical therapies; as therapeutic agents; and in                sensors, electronic materials and coatings on                biological and non-biological surfaces.
   ADVANTAGE - The fabrication process of the gold                nanoparticle is environmentally friendly and                biologically benign. The stabilized, biocompatible                gold nanoparticles generated through                soybeans-mediated experiments did not aggregate,                indicating that the soybean phytochemicals                including proteins serve as an excellent coating.                The gold nanoparticles are generally non toxic                because no external chemicals are used in the                overall process.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   an environmentally friendly method (M1) for                making biocompatible stabilized gold nanoparticles,                involving: mixing soy or lentil plant material or                its reactive extract into an aqueous solution                containing gold salts; permitting reaction of the                gold salts to form stabilized, biocompatible gold                nanoparticles;
   method of sensing involving introducing the                stabilized gold nanoparticles into a human or                animal subject and conducting gold nanoparticle                enhanced imaging; and
   method of therapy involving introducing the                stabilized gold nanoparticles into a human or                animal subject and conducting gold nanoparticle                enhanced therapy.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows a schematic diagram that                illustrates a stabilized, biocompatible gold                nanoparticle.
   10Gold nanoparticle
   12Soy or lentil plant material
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The plant material                  comprises soybeans, a soy extract or a reactive                  extract. The soy extract comprises large                  molecular weight protein fractions of soy, where                  the large molecular weight protein fractions have                  a weight of more than 5 (preferably about 51-80)                  kDa. The plant material comprises cinnamon.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  involves a step of heating the aqueous solution                  during the step of permitting reaction, where the                  step of heating involves microwave heating; a                  step of adjusting the pH of the aqueous solution                  after the step of permitting reaction; a step of                  adding a stabilizing agent to the aqueous                  solution after the step of permitting reaction; a                  preliminary step of separating the reactive                  extract from the soy or lentil plant material.                  The aqueous solution has a physiological                  pH.Preferred Components: The gold salts                  comprise sodium tetrachloroaurate or aurochloric                  acid.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Components: The stabilizing agent                  comprises gum Arabic.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Vasotropic.
   The cytotoxicity of stabilized gold                nanoparticles (Soy-AuNP-2) under in vitro                conditions in human fibroblast cells was examined                in terms of the effect of Soy-AuNPs on cell                proliferation by                3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium                bromide (MTT) assay. Fibroblast cells treated with                0, 25, 50, 125 and 165 &#956;m concentrations                of Soy-AuNPs [Au atoms]for 24 hours were subjected                to MTT assay for cell-viability determination.                After 24 hours of Soy-AuNP-2 treatment, cells                showed more than 78% viability up to 165 ~mm                concentrations of Soy-AuNP-2.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gastrin releasing peptide (GRP) receptor                agonist.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is oral or intravenous. No                dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - Soybean extract (4 mL) was diluted to 8 mL in                deionized water and was heated up to 95?oC for 3                minutes. To this solution, NaAuCl 4(100 ~mL) was                added and further heated to 95?oC with constant                stirring for 5 minutes. After work up, gold                nanoparticles (Soy-AuNP-2) were obtained.

AB    NOVELTY - Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising an                antigen binding domain of a kinase domain region                (KDR)-1121 or DC101 (rat anti-mouse vascular                endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2)                antibody) antibody, an extracellular hinge domain,                a T-cell receptor transmembrane domain, and an                intracellular T-cell receptor signaling domain, is                new.
   USE - The chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) is useful                for: detecting the presence of cancer in a host;                and treating or preventing cancer in a host (all                claimed), where the cancer is e.g. acute myeloid                leukemia, bladder cancer, bone cancer, brain                cancer, breast cancer, colon cancer, esophageal                cancer, cervical cancer, fibrosarcoma, Hodgkin's                lymphoma, kidney cancer, leukemia, liver cancer,                lung cancer, lymphoma, larynx cancer, malignant                mesothelioma, melanoma, multiple myeloma,                non-Hodgkin lymphoma, ovarian cancer, pancreatic                cancer, pharynx cancer, prostate cancer, rectal                cancer, renal cancer, skin cancer, small intestine                cancer, soft tissue cancer, solid tumors, stomach                cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, ureter                cancer, or urinary bladder cancer. Test details are                described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The CAR: redirects T-cell specificity and                reactivity towards a selected target in a non-major                histocompatibility complex (MHC)-restricted manner;                recognizes antigen independent of antigen                processing, thus bypassing a major mechanism of                tumor escape; does not dimerize with endogenous                T-cell receptor alpha and beta chains, when                expressed in T-cells; targets and destroys VEGFR-2                expressing endothelial cells in the tumor                vasculature; facilitates infiltration of immune                cells to the tumor site; and enhances/extends                antitumor responses.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   a nucleic acid comprising a nucleotide                sequence encoding the CAR;
   a recombinant expression vector comprising the                nucleic acid;
   an isolated host cell comprising the                recombinant expression vector;
   a population of cells comprising at least one                host cell;
   an antibody or its antigen binding portion,                which specifically binds to the CAR; and
   detecting the presence of cancer in a host,                comprising: contacting a sample comprising at least                one cell from the host with the CAR, nucleic acid,                recombinant expression vector, host cell,                population of cells, or the antibody or its antigen                binding portion, hence forming a complex; and                detecting the complex, where detection of the                complex is indicative of the presence of cancer in                the host.

TI Skin surface deformation label, has elastic layer            whose surface is divided into square grid by printing            layer, where square grid in printed layer is filled            with color, where adjacent different filling color            includes conterminal grid.
AU LI G
AE BEIJING LINKINGMED MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY CO (BEIJ-Non-standard)
GA 201910509M
AB    NOVELTY - The label has an adhesive layer formed between                an elastic layer and a bottom paper layer. A                surface of the elastic layer is divided into a                uniform square grid by a printing layer. The square                grid in the printed layer is filled with a color,                where adjacent different filling color includes                conterminal grid. The square grid of the printing                layer is filled with different colors and made of                fluorescent material. The square grid is printed                with graphics or digital mark. The square grid is                provided with marking points. The marking point is                made of fluorescent material. The elastic layer is                made of elastic material i.e. gel and rubber or                silica gel.
   USE - Skin surface deformation label.
   ADVANTAGE - The label can perform multi-point monitoring                on a skin to be deformed by detecting skin surface                deformation real-time detection process, so that a                user can adjust a size of the grid as needed to                obtain deformation data with different degrees of                fineness, thus comprehensively obtaining real-time                deformation data of the skin, and hence monitoring                of human involuntary movements in process of breast                cancer radiation therapy through skin deformation                to understand a movement of human organs.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                real time skin surface deformation detecting                method.

AB    NOVELTY - Engineered, non-naturally occurring Clustered                Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeat                (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) system comprises nucleic                acid encoding RNA guide which further comprises                direct repeat sequence of 36 nucleotides (SEQ ID                NO: 65), given in the specification, and spacer                sequence, or RNA guide; and nucleic acid encoding                CRISPR-Cas effector protein, or CRISPR-Cas effector                protein which binds to RNA guide, and spacer                sequence binds to target nucleic acid.
   USE - Engineered, non-naturally occurring CRISPR-Cas                system used for modification and manipulation of                nucleic acids in targeted fashion; used in field of                biotechnology, agriculture, and human therapeutics;                treating cancer or infectious disease, where cancer                is Wilms' tumor, Ewing sarcoma, neuroendocrine                tumor, glioblastoma, neuroblastoma, melanoma, skin                cancer, breast cancer, colon cancer, rectal cancer,                prostate cancer, liver cancer, renal cancer,                pancreatic cancer, lung cancer, biliary cancer,                cervical cancer, endometrial cancer, esophageal                cancer, gastric cancer, head and neck cancer,                medullary thyroid carcinoma, ovarian cancer,                glioma, lymphoma, leukemia, myeloma, acute                lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myelogenous leukemia,                chronic lymphocytic leukemia, chronic myelogenous                leukemia, Hodgkin's lymphoma, non-Hodgkin's                lymphoma, and urinary bladder cancer etc.
   ADVANTAGE - The system enables to provide immunity to                bacteria and archaea against phage infection;                exhibits collateral RNAse activity after binding to                target nucleic acid (e.g., target RNA); more                effectively harnessed for programmable                biotechnologies; have broad spectrum in DNA/RNA                detection (e.g., specific high sensitivity                enzymatic reporter unlocking (SHERLOCK)), tracking                and labeling of nucleic acids, enrichment assays                (extracting desired sequence from background),                controlling interfering RNA or miRNA, detecting                circulating tumor DNA, preparing next generation                library, drug screening, disease diagnosis and                prognosis, and treating various genetic                disorders.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   (1) a cell, which comprises system;
   (2) a method for binding system to target                nucleic acid in cell, which involves: (a) providing                system; and (b) delivering system to cell, where                cell, which comprises target nucleic acid, where                CRISPR-Cas effector protein binds to RNA guide, and                spacer sequence binds to target nucleic acid.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of maximum                tree topology for subset of Cas13d, with genomic                arrangement of genes encoding predicted protein                components of Type VI-D system components shown to                right.

TI Analyzing signals of positive and negative strands            of DNA molecule used for, detecting and screening            cancers by e.g. determining sequence and quantity of            each DNA strand in DNA molecule, determining genomic            region and difference information.

AB    NOVELTY - Analyzing signals of positive and negative                strands of DNA molecule comprises (a) determining                the sequence and quantity of each DNA strand in the                single-stranded DNA molecules and double-stranded                DNA molecules in the biological sample, which is                divided into two sample groups that are different                in biological properties; (b) based on the results                of (a), determining the genomic region                corresponding to the DNA chain, and identifying                whether the DNA chain is the DNA positive strand or                the DNA negative strand of the genomic region; and                (c) determining the difference information between                the positive strand of DNA and the negative strand                of DNA in the genomic region.
   USE - The method or the kit is useful for analyzing                signals of positive and negative strands of DNA                molecule, which is used for characterizing,                detecting, and screening cancers preferably                non-disease screening and non-disease diagnosis                (e.g.lung cancer, gastric cancer, liver cancer,                esophageal cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer,                ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, prostate cancer,                testicular cancer, colorectal cancer, colon cancer,                pancreatic cancer, head and neck cancer, thyroid                cancer, glioma, or skin cancer, preferably                hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer,                esophageal cancer, or gastric cancer).
   ADVANTAGE - The method selects the difference signals                capable of distinguishing cancers from normal                people by means of algorithms, and constructs a                machine learning model based on the difference                signals.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   an analysis model for the positive and                negative strands of DNA molecules;
   obtaining test results from an individual's                biological sample, comprising (a) determining the                sequence and quantity of each DNA strand in the                single-stranded DNA molecules and double-stranded                DNA molecules in the biological sample, (b)                according to a) As a result, determine that the DNA                chain is in the genomic region corresponding to the                individual, and identify whether the DNA chain is                the positive DNA strand or the negative DNA strand                corresponding to the genomic region, (c) according                to at least one of the genomic regions difference                information between the positive strand of DNA and                the negative strand of DNA is obtained to obtain                the detection result of the individual;
   a kit for diagnosing a disease in an                individual, comprising (a) a device for performing                the method of analyzing signals of positive and                negative strands of DNA molecule or (b) for using a                device for analyzing a model, or (c) a device for                implementing; and
   treating a disease in an individual in need,                comprising either by providing medicine,                radiotherapy, and/or surgical treatment to the                individual, where the biological sample of the                individual has received a method and be diagnosed                as suffering from the disease or (1) testing a                biological sample from the individual, and (2) if                the test result is that the patient suffers from                the disease, providing corresponding                treatment;
   a computer system or program comprising a set                of instructions for analyzing signals of positive                and negative strands of DNA molecule; and
   a detection system, comprising the computer                system or program.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flowchart illustrating                the method for detection and analysis of positive                and negative strand imbalance signals of DNA                molecules in a sample (Drawing includes non-English                language text).

   BBPerforming library construction
   CCSequence the library and identify the                sequence
   DDCalculating the difference value
   EEComparing the difference values of positive                and negative strands

AB    NOVELTY - The device (100) has a light source for                generating a light. A light pattern optical system                (150) couples the light from the light source to a                tissue surface (120). An imaging device images the                tissue surface. A tissue modifying element alters                the tissue surface. The light pattern optical                system includes a mask or a digital light                projection device, such that a dot pattern is                formed on the tissue surface. The light source                comprises a laser and an LED, and emits wavelengths                to produce a visible light image of a tissue                lesion. The light source comprises a ring emitter                (110).
   USE - Device for measuring a mobile tissue stiffness                for skin cancer detection, and malignant tumors                such as breast, thyroid, and prostate, via a mobile                wireless device such as tablet display device or                smartphone.
   ADVANTAGE - The device can accurately map out the lesion                for accurately determining excision size and                achieving smaller margins. The device is                non-invasive, and has low manufacturing cost, low                power consumption rate, high accuracy, and high                robustness, and can be arranged to allow standard                clinical images of the lesion for morphology                analysis without additional hardware.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for measuring tissue stiffness.

TI Method for detecting cancer, involves receiving            sequencing data for biological sample, determining            score for genomic region, generating feature vector for            sample, and inputting feature vector into trained model            to generate cancer prediction for sample.
AU NICULA V
   NEWMAN J
   GROSS S S
AE GRAIL INC (ILLU-C)
   GRAIL LLC (ILLU-C)
   GRAIL LLC (ILLU-C)
   GRAIL LLC (ILLU-C)
GA 2021B4842L
AB    NOVELTY - The method (600) involves receiving (610)                sequencing data for a biological sample comprising                many cell free DNA (cfDNA) fragments which overlap                genomic region of many genomic regions. A first                score is determined (620) for the genomic region                for cfDNA fragment of the biological sample. A                feature vector is generated (630) for the                biological sample, where feature of the feature                vector corresponding to a genomic region and                generated according to a count of cfDNA fragments                having a score for genomic region above a threshold                score. The feature vector is inputted (640) into a                trained model to generate a cancer prediction for                biological sample.
   USE - Method for detecting cancer e.g. epithelial                squamous cell cancer. Uses include but are not                limited to skin carcinoma, melanoma, lung cancer                such as small-cell lung cancer and non-small cell                lung cancer (NSCLC), gastric or stomach cancer such                as gastrointestinal cancer, pancreatic cancer e.g.                pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, cervical cancer,                high grade serous ovarian carcinoma, liver cancer                e.g. hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), hepatoma,                hepatic carcinoma, urothelial bladder cancer,                testicular cancer, breast cancer, brain cancer,                colon cancer, rectal cancer, colorectal cancer,                endometrial or uterine carcinoma, salivary gland                carcinoma, kidney or renal cancer, prostate cancer,                vulval cancer, thyroid cancer, anal carcinoma,                penile carcinoma, head and neck cancer, esophageal                carcinoma, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma                (NPC).
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables to analyze methylation                sequencing data from cell-free DNA for the                detection, diagnosis, and/or monitoring of diseases                which allows for earlier treatment and thus a                greater chance for survival. The neural network                architecture improves the efficiency of neural                network training and conserves computational power                due to the reduced number of layers involved in the                training. The sensitivity and accuracy of the                higher-order classifications is improved. The                method improves the efficiency and performance of                training and using a supervised model to determine                a cancer state of a subject.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for obtaining multiple features for determining                cancer state of subject.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flowchart illustrating a                method for detecting cancer.

TI Distinguishing circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from            CTC mimics by determining the presence or absence of            immunofluorescent CTC markers in nucleated cells in a            non-enriched blood sample to detect a CTC            candidate.
AU DITTAMORE R
AE EPIC SCI INC (EPIC-Non-standard)
   EPIC SCI INC (EPIC-Non-standard)
   EPIC SCI INC (EPIC-Non-standard)
GA 201544578C
AB    NOVELTY - Distinguishing circulating tumor cells (CTCs)                from CTC mimics, comprises: (a) determining the                presence or absence of one or more                immunofluorescent CTC markers in nucleated cells in                a non-enriched blood sample to detect a CTC                candidate, (b) determining the presence or absence                of one or more immunofluorescent circulating                endothelial cell (CEC) markers in the CTC                candidate, and (c) assessing the morphology of the                CTC candidate, where CTCs are distinguished from                CTC mimics based on a combination of distinct                immunofluorescent staining and morphological                characteristics.
   USE - The methods are useful for distinguishing CTCs                from CTC mimics; for improving the accuracy and                specificity of CTC quantifications in a blood                sample; for monitoring an anti-cancer treatment                response in a patient; and for determining the                efficacy of an anti-cancer treatment in a patient                (all claimed), where the cancer is selected from                lung cancer (e.g. small-cell lung cancer (SCLC),                non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), including, e.g.                adenocarcinomas or lung carcinoid tumor), skin                cancer, colon cancer, renal cancer, liver cancer,                pancreatic cancer, thyroid cancer, bladder cancer,                gall bladder cancer, brain cancer (e.g. glioma,                glioblastoma, medulloblastoma, neuroblastoma),                breast cancer, ovarian cancer, endometrial cancer,                prostate cancer, testicular cancer and lymphomas                (e.g., Hodgkin's lymphoma, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma,                T-cell lymphoma, B-cell lymphoma).
   ADVANTAGE - The methods provide efficient diagnosis of                cancer, and can be efficiently used in the                identification and quantification of endothelial                cells mimicking circulating tumor cells (CTC                mimics). Also, the methods provide improved methods                for CTC and CEC detection, classification and                quantification. One major advantage of the methods                is the improvement in the accuracy and sensitivity                of CTC detection and quantification.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method of improving the accuracy and                specificity of CTC quantifications in a blood                sample, comprising: (i) quantifying the number of                CTC candidates in the blood sample to obtain an                approximate CTC count, (ii) distinguishing CTCs                from CTC mimics according to the method above,                (iii) quantifying the number of CTC mimics in the                blood sample, and (iv) subtracting the number of                CTC mimics from the number of CTC candidates to                improve the accuracy and specificity of CTC                quantifications in the blood sample;
   a method of monitoring an anti-cancer                treatment response in a patient, comprising: (i)                collecting two or more blood samples from the                patient at different time-points throughout a                treatment period; and (ii) quantifying the number                of CTC mimics in each blood sample according to the                method above, where an increasing number of CTC                mimics in the blood samples collected at different                time-points throughout the treatment period                indicates a positive treatment response in the                patient; and
   a method of determining the efficacy of an                anti-cancer treatment in a patient, comprising: (i)                collecting blood samples from a population of                patients receiving the anti-cancer treatment, (ii)                collecting blood samples form a population of                patients not receiving the anti-cancer treatment,                and (iii) quantifying the number of CTC mimics in                each blood sample, where elevated numbers of CTC                mimics in the blood samples from the population of                patients receiving the anti-cancer treatment                relative to the blood samples from the populations                of patients not receiving the anti-cancer treatment                indicates that the anti-cancer treatment is                efficacious.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In distinguishing CTCs                  from CTC mimics, (a) further comprises                  determining the presence or absence of one or                  more immunofluorescent sample cell markers in the                  nucleated cells. The distinct immunofluorescent                  staining of CTCs includes the presence of an                  immunofluorescent CTC marker, the absence of an                  immunofluorescent CEC marker, and the absence of                  an immunofluorescent sample cell marker. The                  distinct immunofluorescent staining of CTC mimics                  includes the presence of an immunofluorescent CTC                  marker, the presence of an immunofluorescent CEC                  marker, and the absence of an immunofluorescent                  sample cell marker. The immunofluorescent sample                  cell markers are specific for white blood cells                  (WBCs). The immunofluorescent sample cell markers                  comprise cluster of differentiation (CD) 45. The                  method further comprises the initial step of                  obtaining a blood sample from a patient. The                  blood sample was obtained from a non-small cell                  lung cancer (NSCLC) patient. The method is                  performed by fluorescent scanning microscopy. The                  microscopy provides a field of view comprising                  more than 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40 or 50 CTC                  candidates, where each CTC candidate is                  surrounded by more than 10, 50, 100, 150 or 200                  WBCs. Determining the presence or absence of the                  immunofluorescent CTC markers comprises comparing                  the distinct immunofluorescent staining of CTC                  candidates with the distinct immunofluorescent                  staining of WBCs. Determining the presence or                  absence of the immunofluorescent CEC markers                  comprises comparing the distinct                  immunofluorescent staining of CTC candidates with                  the distinct immunofluorescent staining of WBCs.                  The immunofluorescent CTC markers comprise a                  cytokeratin (CK). Determining the presence of CK                  in nucleated cells comprises identifying                  nucleated cells having a relative CK expression                  of &#8805; 3. The immunofluorescent CEC                  markers comprise Von Willebrand factor (vWF),                  cluster of differentiation (CD) 31, CD 34, CD                  105, CD 145 or CD 146. Determining the presence                  of vWF in CTC candidates comprises identifying                  CTC candidates having a relative vWF expression                  of &#8805; 6. Assessing the morphology of the                  CTC candidate comprises comparing the                  morphological characteristics of the CTC                  candidate with the morphological characteristics                  of surrounding WBCs, morphological                  characteristics of a CTC, and/or morphological                  characteristics of a CEC. The morphological                  characteristics comprise nucleus size, nucleus                  shape, cell size, cell shape, nuclear to                  cytoplasmic ratio. Assessing the morphology of                  the CTC candidate comprises assessing the CTC                  candidate by nuclear detail, nuclear contour,                  presence or absence of nucleoli, quality of                  cytoplasm, quantity of cytoplasm, or                  immunofluorescent staining patterns. The method                  also comprises quantifying the number of CTC                  candidates in the blood sample; and quantifying                  the number of CTC mimics in the blood sample. The                  method further comprises quantifying the number                  of CTCs in the blood sample, which comprises (i)                  quantifying the number of CTC candidates in the                  blood sample, (ii) quantifying the number of CTC                  mimics in the blood sample, and (iii) subtracting                  the number of CTC mimics from the number of CTC                  candidates to quantify the number of CTCs in the                  blood sample.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

PN WO200133229-A1; AU200121565-A; EP1226439-A1; HU200203269-B; JP2003513282-W; ZA200203401-A; NZ519065-A
TI Detecting and grading a cell proliferation            disorder in an individual, comprises determining and            comparing the spatial distribution of a component in            the sample cell nucleus with the spatial distribution            in a reference sample.
AU VAN DRIEL R
   VAN DRIEL R U V A
AE UNIV AMSTERDAM (UNAM-C)
   UNIV AMSTERDAM (UNAM-C)
GA 2001328838
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting and grading, or monitoring the                treatment of, a cell proliferation disorder in an                individual, involves determining the spatial                distribution (SD) of at least one specific                component in the cell nucleus of a sample (TS) to                be analyzed, comparing SD with the spatial                distribution of the same component in a reference                sample, and characterizing the component of TS from                the comparison values.
   USE - The method and the data processing system for                carrying out the method are useful for detecting                and grading a cell proliferation disorder such as                colon cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, cervix                cancer, ovary cancer, prostate cancer, skin cancer,                Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin disease (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method is suitable for early detection and                diagnosis of cancer in mammals, particularly in                humans.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                data processing system for analyzing cytological                material for the presence of a cell proliferation                disorder in an individual, comprising:
   a monitoring device (e.g. video camera)                generating data obtained from the spatial                distribution on at least one specific component in                the cell nucleus of a sample from the                individual;
   a first computer processor for processing data                obtained from the monitor;
   a first storage unit for storing data from the                first computer on a first storage medium;
   a second storage unit containing data from                reference cytological material comprising the                spatial distribution of the same specific component                in various types of cancer, the grade of cancer                development, etc.; and
   a second processor for comparing the data from                the first storage unit with the second storage                unit, determining if there are cell proliferation                disorders present in the cytological material, and                assessing the type of proliferation disorder and                the grading of the disorder.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: The sample is derived from                  a tissue, blood, lymphatic fluid, urine or stool.                  The reference sample is derived from a normal                  cell of the same or similar source as the sample                  to be analyzed, and preferably from the same                  individual. The reference sample is a statistic                  mean of spatial distribution patterns from the                  same or similar source as the sample to be                  analyzed, derived from a number of individuals                  and selected by people skilled in the art. The                  spatial distribution patterns are stored in a                  database or on a carrier. The proliferation                  disorder that is investigated is colon, lung,                  breast, cervix, ovary, prostate, or skin cancer,                  Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin disease. At least one                  specific component in the cell nucleus is                  selected from antigens p80-coilin, PML, SC35,                  acetylated histones, CstF64, hnRNP-I, and NuMA                  protein. The spatial distribution of at least one                  specific component in the cell nucleus is                  determined by immunofluorescence microscopy,                  which involves the use of one or more monoclonal                  antibodies raised against nuclear components from                  the type of cells to be analyzed.
   EXAMPLE - Large bowel tissue samples were obtained from                adenocarcinoma patients as well as from healthy                individuals. Tissue samples were fixed in                phosphate-buffered saline for immunofluorescence,                and tumor samples were graded after tissue                processing and histological staining based on their                morphologic features at macroscopic and microscopic                level, and staged. After fixation, tissue sections                were rinsed with phosphate buffered saline (PBS),                cells permeabilized with 0.5 % Triton-X 100(RTM),                and incubated in PBS containing 100 mM glycine for                10 minutes to inactivate remaining free aldehyde                groups, and blocked for 10 minutes in PBG (PBS                containing bovine serum albumin (BSA) and                gelatine). For indirect immunofluorescent labeling,                fixed tissue sections were incubated with primary                antibodies and subsequently with secondary                antibodies. After labeling, tissue sections were                washed, and incubated in PBS containing Hoechst                33258 for 5 minutes. The glass slides were mounted                onto cover slips with mounding medium, as an                antifade agent. A Leica fluorescence microscope                equipped with a CCD-camera was used to collect                microscopic images. The results showing the                correlation of the spatial distribution of various                nuclear components from nuclear proteins of human                colorectal tumors and the untransformed phenotype,                confirmed that factors involved in RNA processing                and acetylated histone distributions were altered                in the nuclei of colorectal cancer tissue.

AB    NOVELTY - Composition (C1) comprises an agent for                measuring the expression level of a pumilio RNA                binding family member 1-TNF receptor associated                factor 3 (PUM1-TRAF3) fusion protein or a fusion                gene encoding the same.
   USE - The composition (C1) is useful in the kit for                determining the suitability of a cancer therapeutic                agent. The diagnostic device is useful for                determining the suitability of a cancer treatment.                The pharmaceutical composition is useful for                preventing or treating cancer in a subject with a                high expression level of the PUM1-TRAF3 fusion                protein or a fusion gene encoding the same. The                cancer comprises at least one chosen from biliary                tract cancer, gastric cancer, breast cancer, colon                cancer, lung cancer, liver cancer, esophageal                cancer, pancreatic cancer, gallbladder cancer,                kidney cancer, bladder cancer, prostate cancer,                testicular cancer, colon cancer, cervical cancer,                endometrial cancer, choriocarcinoma, skin cancer,                ovarian cancer, thyroid cancer, brain cancer, blood                cancer, head and neck cancer, malignant melanoma                and lymphoma (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The composition maximizes the therapeutic                effect and ensures precise treatment by detecting                genetic characteristics of patients and then                applying the NF-kB inhibitor or the NIK inhibitor                to the selected patients with high expression of                the PUM1-TRAF3 fusion gene.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a kit comprising the above-mentioned                composition (C1);
   method for providing information about the                suitability of a cancer therapeutic agent involves                measuring the expression level of PUM1-TRAF3 fusion                protein or a gene encoding same in a biological                sample which is isolated from a target                subject;
   a diagnostic device comprising (a) a                measurement unit for measuring the expression level                of a PUM1-TRAF3 fusion protein or a gene encoding                the same with respect to a biological sample                obtained from a subject of interest, and (b) a                detection unit which outputs the suitability of the                target subject for cancer treatment from the                expression level of the fusion protein or the gene                encoding the fusion protein measured by the                measurement unit; and
   a pharmaceutical composition (C2) comprising a                nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of                activated B cells (NF-kB) inhibitor or an                NF-kB-inducing kinase (NIK) inhibitor, as an active                ingredient.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The PUM1-TRAF3 fusion                  protein comprises at least one amino acid                  sequence chosen from a 996 amino acid sequence                  (SEQ ID NO: 1) fully defined in the specification                  and a 248 amino acid sequence (SEQ ID NO: 2)                  fully defined in the specification. The                  PUM1-TRAF3 fusion gene comprises at least one                  sequence chosen from a 2988 base pair sequence                  (SEQ ID NO: 3) fully defined in the specification                  and a 744 base pair sequence (SEQ ID NO: 4) fully                  defined in the specification. The agent for                  measuring the expression level of the protein                  comprises at least one chosen from an antibody,                  an oligopeptide, a ligand, a peptide nucleic acid                  (PNA) and an aptamer which binds specifically to                  the protein. The agent for measuring the                  expression level of the gene comprises at least                  one chosen from primers, probes, and antisense                  nucleotides which bind specifically to the gene.                  The therapeutic agent has an effect of inhibiting                  non-canonical NF-kB signaling. The therapeutic                  agent comprises NF-kB inhibitor or NIK Inhibitor                  composition. The NF-kB inhibitor comprises at                  least one chosen from                  4-N-[2-(4-phenoxyphenyl)ethyl]-1,2-dihydroquinazoline-4,6-diamine                  (QNZ),                  benzyl[(2S)-4-methyl-1-{[(2S)-4-methyl-1-{[(2S)-4-methyl-1-oxopentan-2-yl]amino}-1-oxopentan-2-yl]amino}-1-oxopentan-2-yl]carbamate                  (MG132), ammonium pyrrolidinedithiocarbamate,                  caffeic acid phenethyl ester, and their salts.                  The NIK inhibitor comprises at least one chosen                  from                  4-[1-(2-amino-5-chloropyrimidin-4-yl)-2,3-dihydroindol-6-yl]-2-(1,3-thiazol-2-yl)but-3-yn-2-ol                  (B022),                  (R)-4-(3-(2-amino-5H-pyrrolo[3,2-d]pyrimidin-7-yl)-4-fluorophenyl)-2-(thiazol-2-yl)but-3-yn-2-ol                  (XT2),                  6-[3-[2-[(3R)-3-hydroxy-1-methyl-2-oxopyrrolidin-3-yl]ethynyl]phenyl]-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide                  (NIK SMI1) and their salts. Preferred Kit: The                  kit is a real-time reverse transcription (RT)-PCR                  kit, a DNA chip kit, an enzyme-linked                  immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit, a protein chip                  kit, a rapid kit, or a multiple reaction                  monitoring (MRM) kit. Preferred Method: In the                  method, when the expression level of the                  PUM1-TRAF3 fusion protein or the gene encoding                  same measured in the biological sample is higher                  than that of the normal control group, the effect                  as a therapeutic agent for treating cancer in the                  target subject is predicted to be high.

TI New antigen associated with normal and cancerous            breast cells useful as a diagnostic marker, and            specific antibodies.
AU HARVEY M A

AE CORNING GLASS WORKS (CORG-C)

GA 1985277969
AB    NOVELTY - A pure antigen (Ag) found on normal and benign                breast epithelial cell membranes (esp. on the                apical surface adjacent to the lumen) and on breast                cancer cells (throughout the entire cell) has the                following characteristics; (1) is a glycoprotein of                mol. wt., in its commonest form, at least 0.3                million; (2) has the same density in CsCl gradients                as normal proteins; (3) is absent from human                foreskin fibroblasts and from coronary artery,                heart, liver, spleen and skin cells; (4) is present                among human milk fat globule proteins and on                sebaceous gland, endocervix, ovary, kidney, bowel,                pancreas and lung cells; (5) is shed by breast                cancer cells; (6) is present in human plasma; and                (7) its mol. wt. is not affected by DNase or                chondroitinase.
Also new are antibodies (Ab) specific for Ag                and continuous cell lines which produce Ab.
   USE - Ag is a marker for diagnosis of breast cancer,                and allows those tumours which would respond to                oestrogen therapy to be identified.
EA    (US4960716-A)   NOVELTY - Detection of breast cancer comprises                incubation of a plasma sample with an immobilised                antibody that binds to the mammary epithelial                antigenic glycoprotein (Mr about 330,000) then                incubation with monoclonal antibody obtd. from                hybridoma cell line 21DD5, and incubation with a                second monoclonal antibody obtd. from the hybridoma                cell line 21D77 and measurement of the amt. of                immune complex formed in each case, comparing the                results with those obtd. from normal plasma                samples.
   USE - The process facilitates the rapid clinical                analysis and diagnosis of breast cancer.                (13pp))

TI Computer-implemented method for classifying            dermoscopic images of skin lesion categories, involves            processing image through modified ResNet50 neural            network architecture, and generating classification            probabilities for multiple skin lesion diagnostic            categories.
AU DHRUV G S
   SINHA S
   SIDDHARTHA A P R
   SARWESH P
AE VELLORE INST TECHNOLOGY (VELR-C)

TI Biological tissue image texture characterizing            method, involves characterizing texture of biological            tissue multi-spectral image by deriving lacunarity            measures from multi-spectral image based on wavelet            analysis.
AU BOGDAN A
AE ELECTRO-OPTICAL SCI INC (ELEC-Non-standard)
   ELECTRO-OPTICAL SCI INC (ELEC-Non-standard)
   MELA SCI INC (MELA-Non-standard)
   MELA SCI INC (MELA-Non-standard)
   MELA SCI INC (MELA-Non-standard)
   MELA SCI INC (MELA-Non-standard)
GA 2009K51511
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves characterizing a texture                of a biological tissue multi-spectral image by                deriving lacunarity measures from the image based                on a wavelet analysis, where the image comprises an                analysis region with a skin lesion. Automatic                segmentation is applied to create a mask of the                lesion, where the lacunarity measures are derived                based on a gliding box process that utilizes a                circular window of fixed characteristic size. The                lacunarity measures are tested for separability of                classes into which the images are grouped.
   USE - Method for characterizing texture of a                biological tissue image in application such as                cancer detection.
   ADVANTAGE - The method utilizes the Wavelet transform that                can selectively enhance and quantify clinically                relevant information in the biological image while                suppressing the noisy background, and provides 100                percent sensitivity of correct classified positive                observations, thus maximizing the number of                correctly classified negative observations in the                cancer detection application.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a pictorial representation                of continuous wavelet transform modulus images for                blue spectral band image of a malignant lesion, and                bright pixels corresponding to points of large                variation.

TI Detecting and replacing a sequence which may cause            an undesired variant in a gene construct comprises            performing an in-silico analysis of the gene construct            to detect a presence of the sequence.
AU ANDRADE J
   BOLOTIN E
   FALK A S
   LIAO E H
   ANDRADE G
   POLK A S
AE KITE PHARMA INC (GILE-C)
   KITE PHARMA INC (GILE-C)
GA 202302901K
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves performing an in-silico                analysis of the gene construct to detect a presence                of the sequence which may cause the undesired                variant. The detected sequence is replaced which                may cause the undesired variant with an alternative                sequence. A frequency percentage of the undesired                variant expressed by the gene construct comprising                performing an in-vivo analysis of several genes                expressed by the gene construct comprising                performing a RNA-sequencing analysis of an RNA                product transcribed from the gene construct is                measured. The in-silico analysis is repeated and                the steps are replaced if the frequency percentage                of the undesired variant in the gene product from                the in-vivo analysis is greater than a                predetermined value of acceptable frequency                percentage of the undesired variant.
   USE - Method for detecting and replacing a sequence                which causes an undesired variant in a gene                construct used in medical technology that have led                to the emerging use of immunotherapies to treat                different types of illnesses and diseases,                including various forms of cancer such as                drenocortical carcinoma, anal cancer, bladder                cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer,                carcinoid cancer, carcinoma, cervical cancer, colon                cancer, endometrial cancer, esophageal cancer,                extrahepatic bile duct cancer, extracranial germ                cell cancer, eye cancer, gallbladder cancer,                gastric cancer, germ cell tumor, gestational                trophoblastic tumor, head and neck cancer,                hypopharyngeal cancer, islet cell carcinoma, kidney                cancer, large intestine cancer, laryngeal cancer,                leukemia, lip and oral cavity cancer, liver cancer,                lung cancer, lymphoma, malignant mesothelioma,                Merkel cell carcinoma, mycosis fungoides,                myelodysplastic syndrome, myeloproliferative                disorders, nasopharyngeal cancer, neuroblastoma,                oral cancer, oropharyngeal cancer, osteosarcoma,                ovarian epithelial cancer, ovarian germ cell                cancer, pancreatic cancer, paranasal sinus and                nasal cavity cancer, parathyroid cancer, penile                cancer, pituitary cancer, plasma cell neoplasm,                prostate cancer, rhabdomyosarcoma, rectal cancer,                renal cell cancer, transitional cell cancer of the                renal pelvis and ureter, salivary gland cancer,                Sezary syndrome, skin cancers, small intestine                cancer, soft tissue sarcoma, stomach cancer,                testicular cancer, thymoma, thyroid cancer,                urethral cancer, uterine cancer, vaginal cancer,                vulvar cancer, and Wilms' tumor.
   ADVANTAGE - The method ensures that gene products used in                cell therapy do not carry a risk of reduced                efficacy or toxicity due to production of                unintended variants. The method reduces the                potential for variant production during the                transgene development stage and during cell therapy                development.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for creating a gene product used in cell                therapy.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of the                variant prediction, detection and elimination                process.
