TI Assessing diagnosis of medically relevant            conditions, comprises comparing a marker molecule level            characteristic for a condition in a solubilized liquid            based cytology sample and a non-diseased sample.
AU RIDDER R
   REICHERT A
   HERKERT M
   DUWE A
   HIPFEL R
   MARTIN P
AE MTM LAB AG (MTMM-Non-standard)
GA 2006167019
AB    NOVELTY - Assessing (M1) diagnosis of medically relevant                conditions from solubilized liquid based cytology                (LBC) samples, by comparing presence or absence                and/or level of a marker molecule characteristic                for a medically relevant condition, to the presence                or absence and/or level known to be characteristic                for a healthy non-diseased biological sample.
   USE - (M1) Is useful for assessing diagnosis of                medically relevant conditions from solubilized LBC                samples, where the medically relevant condition is                a disease. The disease is a cell proliferative                disorder, cancer or a precursor lesion. The cancer                is cancer of the head and the neck, cancer of the                respiratory tract, cancer of the gastrointestinal                tract, cancer of the skin and its appendages,                cancer of the central and peripheral nervous                system, cancer of the urinary system, cancer of the                reproductive system, anogenital cancer, cancer of                the endocrine system, cancer of the soft tissues                and bone, or cancer of the lymphopoietic and                hematopoietic system. The anogenital cancer is                cervical cancer (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - (M1) Enables cost-effective, rapid and                improved diagnosis of the medically relevant                conditions from solubilized LBC samples. (M1)                Enables detection of small amounts of marker                molecules in samples.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Assessing (M1) diagnosis of medically relevant                conditions from solubilized liquid based cytology                (LBC) samples, comprises:
   (a) obtaining an amount of an LBC sample for                application in a biochemical non-cell based                detection method, where the amount of the LBC                sample to be used in the biochemical non-cell based                method is normalized with respect to information                obtained from cytological specimens prepared from                the same LBC sample, detecting the presence or                absence and/or the level of a marker molecule                characteristic for a medically relevant condition,                comparing the presence or absence and/or the level                of the marker molecule characteristic for a                medically relevant condition to the presence or                absence and/or the level known to be characteristic                for a healthy non-diseased biological sample, and                assessing diagnosis on the medically relevant                condition on the comparison between the levels                found in the LBC sample and those known to be                specific for healthy non-diseased biological                samples; or
   (b) detecting the presence or absence and/or                the level of a marker molecule characteristic for a                medically relevant condition on the protein or                peptide level, comparing the presence or absence                and/or the level of the marker molecule                characteristic for a medically relevant condition                to the presence or absence and/or the level known                to be characteristic for a healthy non-diseased                biological sample, and assessing diagnosis on the                medically relevant condition on the comparison                between the levels found in the LBC sample and                those known to be specific for healthy non-diseased                biological samples.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for                developing (M2) kits and in vitro diagnostic                devices, or immunochemical kits and in vitro                diagnostic devices, for use in assessment of                diagnosis of medically relevant conditions from                solubilized biological samples, where:
   (a) the kits and in vitro diagnostic devices                are designed for the detection of the presence or                absence of marker molecules characteristic for                medically relevant conditions and the development                is performed using LBC samples, and normalization                of the amount of LBC sample with respect to                information obtained from the cytological specimen                prepared from the same LBC sample is performed;                or
   (b) the kits and in vitro diagnostic devices                are designed for the detection of the presence or                absence of marker molecules characteristic for                medically relevant conditions on a protein or                peptide level, and the development is performed                using LBC samples.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure is a graph showing the level of                p16(INK4a) in solubilized cervical samples.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In (a) of (M1), the                  assessment of diagnosis is based on one feature                  chosen from the presence or absence of a marker                  molecule characteristic for a medically relevant                  condition, where:(i) the presence or absence of a marker                  molecule is characteristic for diseased                  samples;(ii) the marker molecule characteristic for                  a medically relevant condition is overexpressed                  in the cells contained in the LBC sample compared                  to a healthy non-diseased biological                  sample;(iii) expression of the marker molecule                  characteristic for a medically relevant condition                  is lowered or lost in comparison to the                  expression present in a healthy non-diseased                  biological sample; and(iv) a modified form of the marker molecule                  characteristic for a medically relevant condition                  is expressed in the cells present in the LBC                  sample compared to the marker molecule present in                  healthy non-diseased biological samples.The marker molecules characteristic for                  medically relevant conditions are proteins or                  nucleic acids.The proteins or nucleic acids are chosen                  from:(i) cell cycle regulatory proteins or                  nucleic acids encoding the same;(ii) metalloproteinase proteins or nucleic                  acids encoding the same;(iii) transmembrane proteins or nucleic                  acids encoding the same;(iv) calcium binding proteins or nucleic                  acids encoding the same;(v) growth factor proteins or nucleic acids                  encoding the same;(vi) proteins or nucleic acids encoding the                  same, characteristic for viral infections;(vii) cell proliferation marker proteins or                  nucleic acids encoding the same;(viii) proteins or nucleic acids encoding                  the same associated with DNA replication;                  and(ix) tumor marker proteins or nucleic acids                  encoding the same.The tumor marker proteins or nucleic acids                  encoding the same are chosen from                  cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors, p53, pRb,                  p14ARF, cyclin E, cyclin A, cyclin B, MN,                  her2/neu, mdm-2, bcl-2, claudin 1, epidermal                  growth factor (EGF)-receptor, MCM2, MCM3, MCM4,                  MCM5, MCM6, MCM7, CDC2, CDC6, CDC7 protein                  kinase, CDC14 protein phosphatase, Dbf4,                  proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA), Ki67,                  KiS1, Id1, osteopontine, CD46, GRP, renal                  dipeptidase and transforming growth factor                  (TGF)betaII receptor. The cyclin-dependent kinase                  inhibitor is p16(INK4a). The cyclin-dependent                  kinase inhibitor is chosen from p13.5, p14,                  p15(INK4b), p18(INK4c), p19(INK4d),                  p21(WAF1/CIP1) and p27(KIP1). The proteins or                  nucleic acids encoding the same characteristic                  for viral infections are derived from human                  papillomavirus (HPV) gene chosen from HPV L1, HPV                  L2, HPV E1, HPV E2, HPV E4, HPV E5, HPV E6 and                  HPV E7. The detection of the marker molecules is                  performed using at least one binding agent                  specifically recognizing the molecules to be                  detected. The binding agent is detectably                  labeled. The label is chosen from a radioisotope,                  bioluminescent compound, chemiluminescent                  compound, electroluminescent compound,                  fluorescent compound, metal chelate, enzyme and                  biologically relevant binding structure. The                  binding agent is chosen from nucleic acid                  complementary or reverse complementary to a                  marker molecule nucleic acid, antibody, antibody                  fragment, a miniantibody and peptidomimetic                  comprising an antigen binding epitope.In (b) of (M1), the assessment of diagnosis                  is based on one feature chosen from:(i) the marker molecule characteristic for a                  medically relevant condition is overexpressed in                  the cells contained in the LBC sample compared to                  a healthy non-diseased biological sample;(ii) expression of the marker molecule                  characteristic for a medically relevant condition                  is lowered or lost in comparison to the                  expression present in a healthy non-diseased                  biological sample; and(iii) a modified form of the marker molecule                  characteristic for a medically relevant condition                  is expressed in the cells present in the LBC                  sample compared to the marker molecule present in                  healthy non-diseased biological samples.The detection of the marker molecules is                  performed using at least one binding agent                  specifically recognizing the molecules to be                  detected, where the binding agent is detectably                  labeled, and is chosen from an antibody, antibody                  fragment, a miniantibody and peptidomimetic                  comprising an antigen binding epitope.
   EXAMPLE - Cervical swabs were collected from                individuals. The cervical swab brushes were                transferred into lysis medium containing Triton                X-100 (2%), sodium dodecyl sulfate (0.4%) and                phenylmethanesulfonylfluoride (PMSF) (in mM) (0.6)                in phosphate buffered saline (PBS). The cervical                cells present in the brush were lysed for at least                20 hours. The lysates were centrifuged, and                supernatant was collected. The lysed cell sample                was added to wells of enzyme linked immunosorbent                assay (ELISA) plates, being coated with p16(INK4a)                specific antibody. The samples were incubated for 1                hour at room temperature. A working solution of                biotinylated secondary antibody specific for the                p16(INK4a) protein was added to the well. Then, the                plate was washed, and streptavidin-horseradish                peroxidase (HRP)-polymers were added to the well,                and incubated for 1 hour at room temperature. The                3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB)-substrate was                added to the well and the plate was incubated at                25degreesC for 15 minutes in the dark. After                stopping the reaction, OD(450) nm was determined.                The ELISA test was found to be positive, thus                indicating detection of cervical intraepithelial                neoplasia in the individuals.

TI Identifying patient having virus-associated cancer            comprises e.g. amplifying viral DNA in droplets with            primer/probe sets to produce amplicon signals, if            present, and providing detection signal indicating that            viral DNA fractionated into droplet is tumor-derived            viral DNA.
AU KUMAR S
   CHERA B S
   GUPTA G
AE UNIV NORTH CAROLINA (UNCR-C)
GA 202276172R
AB    NOVELTY - Identifying (M1) a patient as having a                virus-associated cancer, comprises: (a) obtaining a                sample from the patient; (b) obtaining at least two                different primer/probe sets for at least two                different amplicon regions within a viral genome,                where the primer/probe sets each include a first                and second primer/probe set configured to amplify a                first and second region within a viral genome to                produce a first and second amplicon signal; (c)                fractionating viral DNA from the sample into                droplets; (d) amplifying viral DNA in the droplets                with at least first and second primer/probe sets to                produce at least the first and second amplicon                signals, if present; (e) detecting in each droplet                any of the first and second amplicon signals; and                (f) providing a detection signal indicating that a                viral DNA fractionated into the droplet is a                tumor-derived viral DNA only when either the first                amplicon signal or the second amplicon signal, but                not both, is present in the droplet.
   USE - The method is useful for: identifying a                patient as having a virus-associated cancer, where                the virus-associated cancer has not been clinically                detected in the patient, the patient exhibits no                clinical symptoms of a virus-associated cancer, the                virus-associated cancer is a cancer associated with                human papillomavirus (HPV) (preferred), hepatitis B                virus, hepatitis C virus, human T-lymphotropic                virus 1, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human                endogenous retrovirus type K, Merkel cell virus,                HIV, and Kaposi's sarcoma herpes virus, and the                virus-associated cancer is oropharyngeal squamous                cell carcinoma; diagnosing recurrence of a                virus-associated cancer in a patient, where the                patient exhibits no clinical symptoms of recurrence                of a virus-associated cancer (all claimed);                quantifying DNA fragments of a target DNA in a                sample by size; detecting tumor-derived viral DNA                in blood sample and distinguishing from larger                viral DNA from non-tumor sources; detecting,                monitoring or treating an HPV-associated malignancy                in a subject, where the HPV-associated malignancy                is a tumor or cancer of the oral cavity, larynx,                oropharynx, tonsils, esophagus, respiratory tissue,                breast, skin, cervix, vulva, penis and/or anus; and                detecting, monitoring and/or treating malignancies                in a subject or treating patients with a                cancer.
Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: has a 95% sensitivity and 100%                specificity in identifying a patient with a                virus-associated cancer; and is part of clinical                care that may improve the efficacy and reduces the                cost of cancer surveillance for patients with                HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Identifying (M1) a patient as having a                virus-associated cancer, comprises: (a) obtaining a                sample from the patient; (b) obtaining at least two                different primer/probe sets for at least two                different amplicon regions within a viral genome,                where the primer/probe sets each include a first                primer/probe set configured to amplify a first                region within a viral genome to produce a first                amplicon signal, and a second primer/probe set                configured to amplify a second region within the                viral genome to produce a second amplicon signal,                where the first and second amplicon regions are                each less than 170 base pairs in length, and the                first and second regions are non-overlapping; (c)                fractionating viral DNA from the sample into                droplets at a concentration where only 0 or 1 DNA                fragment is present in each droplet; (d) amplifying                viral DNA in the droplets with at least first and                second primer/probe sets to produce at least the                first and second amplicon signals, if present; (e)                detecting in each droplet any of the first and                second amplicon signals; and (f) providing a                detection signal indicating that a viral DNA                fractionated into the droplet is a tumor-derived                viral DNA only when either the first amplicon                signal or the second amplicon signal, but not both,                is present in the droplet, where the presence of a                detection signal in the sample indicates that the                subject has a virus-associated cancer.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for                diagnosing (M2) recurrence of a virus-associated                cancer in a patient, comprising obtaining a sample                from the patient, where the patient has been                previously diagnosed with and treated for a                virus-associated cancer, and the steps (b)-(f) as                per se, where the presence of a detection signal in                the sample indicates that the subject has a                recurrence of the virus-associated cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the method (M1): the                  step of amplifying viral DNA comprises                  amplification using a PCR; the viral DNA from the                  sample is fractionated into microdroplets by                  emulsification; and the viral DNA from the sample                  is fractionated into microdroplets based on size                  prior to performing emulsification into                  microdroplets.Preferred Components: In the method (M1),                  the first and second amplicon regions are less                  than 150 base pairs in length. In the methods                  (M1) and (M2), the sample is a blood (preferred),                  saliva, gargle, or urine sample.
   ACTIVITY - Virucide; Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

TI Diagnosing cancer involves analyzing biological            sample obtained from subject to determine presence of            target molecules representative of expression of four            biomarkers selected from a group consist of MCTP1,            PIBF1, TMTC2 and ANKRD32.
AU POLLARD J W
   FRAGKOGIANNI S
   CASSETTA L
AE UNIV EDINBURGH (UEDG-C)
GA 201865842Y
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing cancer involves analyzing a                biological sample obtained from a subject to                determine the presence of target molecules                representative of expression of four biomarkers                selected from the group consisting of MCTP1, PIBF1,                TMTC2, ANKRD32, CEPT1, ZNF114, CRYBG3, IFI16, PPIF,                SCD, RP11-469M7.1, PTP4A1 and NRIP1, and comparing                expression levels of determined biomarkers with one                or more reference values, where a difference in                expression of biomarkers in the sample from the                subject compared to the one or more reference                values is indicative of cancer presence or                absence.
   USE - Method for diagnosing cancer, and for                identifying that subject requires a treatment for                cancer or not by using kit, where subject has, or                is suspected of having breast cancer, endometrial                cancer, ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, pancreatic                cancer, thyroid cancer, cervical cancer, bladder                cancer, blastoma, brain cancer and gliomas, bowel                cancer, gastric cancer, head and neck cancer,                kidney cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer,                mesothelioma, melanoma, oral cancer, pituitary                cancer, skin cancer, soft tissue cancer, testicular                cancer, uterine cancer, heart cancer, and/or eye                cancer, preferably a solid tumor cancer, such as                carcinoma, or precancerous lesion, for example a                carcinoma in situ, a hormone-related cancer, for                example breast cancer, endometrial cancer, ovarian                cancer, prostate cancer, pancreatic cancer, and                thyroid cancer, and an estrogen-dependent cancer,                for example a cancer selected from breast cancer,                endometrial cancer and ovarian cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables to diagnose cancer, which                allows use of simple and minimally-invasive test to                detect presence of different cancer types, and                makes it an efficient and economical screening                tool.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for identifying that subject requires                a treatment for cancer or not, which involves                analyzing a biological sample obtained from a                subject to determine the presence of target                molecules representative of expression of four                biomarkers; and comparing the expression levels of                the determined biomarkers with one or more                reference values, and in event that there is a                difference in expression of the biomarkers in the                sample from the subject as compared to the one or                more reference values, and identifying the subject                as requiring a treatment for cancer or not;
   a kit, which comprises binding partners                capable of binding to target molecules                representative of expression of four biomarkers;                and
   an assay device, which comprises a loading                area for receipt of a biological sample; a binding                partners specific for target molecules                representative of expression of four biomarkers,                and a detection unit to detect the levels of target                molecules present in the sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The method is a method                  of diagnosing cancer, prognosing cancer,                  predicting efficacy of treatment for cancer,                  assessing outcome of treatment for cancer, and/or                  assessing recurrence of cancer, preferably for                  diagnosing cancer. The method involves                  determining expression levels of four, five, six,                  or seven biomarkers selected from PIBF1, SCD,                  ZNF114, CRYBG3, PPIF, PTP4A1, ANKRD32, and CEPT1.                  The expression levels of PIBF1, SCD, ZNF114,                  CRYBG3, PPIF, PTP4A1 , ANKRD32, and CEPT1 are                  determined. The expression levels of PIBF1, SCD,                  ZNF114, CRYBG3, and PPIF are determined. The                  biological sample is a blood sample or its                  derivative, preferably a peripheral blood sample.                  The expression levels of biomarkers are                  selectively detected in monocytes of the                  biological sample. The biological sample is                  enriched for monocytes or substantially consists                  of monocytes. The subject is human. The target                  molecule for one or more of the biomarkers is                  nucleic acid, preferably an mRNA or ncRNA                  molecule. The levels of target molecules for one                  or more of biomarkers are determined by PCR,                  preferably quantitative PCR, digital PCR or                  multiplex PCR. The target molecule for one or                  more of biomarker is protein, preferably analysis                  of presence of biomarkers is performed by using a                  binding partner selected from a group consist of                  antibodies, antibody fragments and aptamers. The                  reference values correspond to levels of                  biomarkers in samples from subjects not having                  cancer. The method further involves providing a                  subject identified as requiring treatment with                  treatment for cancer. The treatment comprises one                  or more treatments selected from a group consist                  of surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy,                  immunotherapy, hormone therapy, and targeted                  therapy, preferably cancer is breast cancer. The                  cancer is endometrial cancer and treatment is one                  or more selected from a group consist of surgery,                  radiotherapy, chemotherapy and hormone therapy.                  Preferred Components: The biomarker is selected                  from a group consist of PIBF1, SCD, ZNF114,                  CRYBG3, PPIF, PTP4A1, ANKRD32, and CEPT1. The kit                  further comprises an indicators capable of                  indicating when binding occurs. The one of more                  of the binding partners are selected from a group                  consist of complementary nucleic acids and                  aptamers, preferably one or more of binding                  partners are nucleic acid primers adapted to bind                  specifically to mRNA, ncRNA, or cDNA transcripts                  of the biomarkers.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.

Preferred Method: The method comprises a total of                  60-90 photolithographic cycles using                  BOC-chemistry. The method further comprises                  normalizing the binding signature of antibodies                  using control peptides within the array. The                  method further comprises correlating the detected                  binding signature with a stage and/or a type of                  disease. The method further comprises stratifying                  subject diagnosed with a disease for therapy                  based on the binding.

TI Detecting presence of cancer e.g. gastric cancer            involves measuring concentration of specific protein in            fluid sample; and comparing concentration measured with            standard value ranges for concentration of the protein            for healthy individuals.
AU LIM Y P
   LIM Y
AE UNIV SINGAPORE NAT (UNUS-C)
   UNIV SINGAPORE NAT (UNUS-C)
   UNIV SINGAPORE NAT (UNUS-C)
   UNIV SINGAPORE NAT (UNUS-C)
   UNIV SINGAPORE (UNUS-C)
GA 2011B10329
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting the presence of cancer such as                gastric cancer in an individual suspected or at                risk of having cancer involves: (a) measuring the                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein in                fluid sample obtained from the individual; and (b)                comparing the concentration measured in step (a)                with a standard value ranges for the concentration                of Compliment component C9 protein for healthy                individuals.
   USE - As biomarker for detecting and treating the                presence of cancer in an individual suspected or at                risk of having cancer such as gastric cancer                (claimed), lung cancer, bladder cancer, brain                cancer, breast cancer, blood cancer, nasapharynx                cancer, uterus cancer, cervix cancer, colon cancer,                rectum cancer, esophagus cancer, mouth cancer, head                cancer, skin cancer, kidney cancer, ovary cancer,                neck cancer, pancreas cancer, prostate cancer,                testis cancer, liver cancer and stomach                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is fast and effective way of typing                gastric cancer; and using C9 expression levels to                differentiate between the two types of gastric                cancer is useful in determining which treatment                would be useful and monitoring the success during                the course of the treatment without repeated and                excessive invasive tests.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting the presence of a cancer such as                gastric cancer in an individual suspected or at                risk of having cancer involves: (a) measuring the                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein in                a fluid sample obtained from the individual; and                (b) comparing the concentration measured in step                (a) with a standard value ranges for the                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein                for healthy individuals, where when the                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein                obtained from the individual is increased as                compared to the standard value range for the                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein of                healthy individuals it is indicative of the                possible presence of a cancer. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS                are included for the following:
   (1) a kit to detect a potential gastric cancer                in a fluid sample comprising an antibody capable of                binding selectively a Compliment component C9                protein and reagents for detection of a complex                formed between the antibody and a complement                component C9 protein;
   (2) in detecting gastric cancer by measuring a                concentration of Compliment component C9 protein in                a fluid sample, an isolated antibody capable of                binding selectively a Compliment component C9                protein is used;
   (3) as a biomarker for gastric cancer in a                fluid sample, compliment component C9 protein is                used; and
   (4) in detecting or treating gastric cancer,                an aptamer capable of binding selectively a                Compliment component C9 protein is used.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The antibody is                  capable of binding selectively a Compliment                  component C9 protein antigen comprising                  nucleotide sequence (SEQ ID NO: 1) (SEQ ID NO:                  not defined) or (SEQ ID NO: 3) (SEQ ID NO: not                  defined).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The increase of the                  concentration of complement C9 protein is at                  least a threefold increase as compared to the                  standard value range for the concentration of                  Compliment component C9 protein of healthy                  individuals. The method further involves: (c)                  measuring the concentration of carcinoembrioic                  antigen protein in the fluid sample obtained from                  the individual; and (d) comparing the                  concentration measured in step (c) with a                  standard value for the concentration of                  carcinoembrioic antigen of healthy individuals;                  where an increased concentration of                  carcinoembrioic antigen as compared to the                  standard value for the concentration of                  carcinoembrioic antigen of healthy individuals is                  further indication of the possible presence of a                  gastric cancer. The concentration of Compliment                  component C9 protein and/or carcinoembrioic                  antigen is measured using an antibody capable of                  binding selectively a Compliment component C9                  protein and/or carcinoembrioic antigen. The                  concentration of Compliment component C9 protein                  is measured by ELISA. The concentration of                  Compliment component C9 protein and/or                  carcinoembrioic antigen is measured                  spectrophotometricly. The method further                  involves: characterizing gastric cancer                  intestinal type where an increased concentration                  of Compliment component C9 protein of 3-4 fold as                  compared to the standard value for the                  concentration of Compliment component C9 protein                  in fluid sample of healthy individuals is                  indicative of intestinal type gastric cancer; and                  characterizing gastric cancer diffused type where                  an increased concentration of Compliment                  component C9 protein of 4-45 fold as compared to                  the standard value for the concentration of                  Compliment component C9 protein in the blood,                  plasma or serum of healthy individuals is                  indicative of diffused type gastric cancer.                  Preferred Kit: The kit further comprises an                  antibody capable of binding selectively a                  carcinoembrioic antigen.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

PN US2025137984-A1
TI Detection device for performing detection of            target biomarkers related to variety of chronic and            acute diseases, such as diabetes, from subject via            breath, skin, or sweat, comprises first catalyst layer,            which is in thermal communication with first sensor            layer.
AU GREGORY O J
   RICCI P P
AE TRACE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES INC (TRAC-Non-standard)
GA 202547834N
AB    NOVELTY - The detection device comprises a first                catalyst layer in thermal communication with the                first sensor layer, where the first microheater                layer is separated from the first sensor layer by a                first substrate layer. A second microheater layer                is separated from the second sensor layer. A                controller communicates with the first sensor and                the second sensor and is configured to apply a                first amount of power to the first and second                microheater layers to heat the first sensor layer                to a first setpoint temperature and the second                sensor layer to a second setpoint temperature. A                second amount of power is applied to maintain the                first and second setpoint temperatures in response                to an endothermic or exothermic reaction at the                first or second sensor. A measurement of the                difference between the first amount of power and                the second amount of power is determined.
   USE - Detection device for performing detection of                target biomarkers, proteins, deoxyribonucleic acid,                ribonucleic acid, and other small molecules related                to variety of chronic and acute diseases, such as                diabetes, chronic kidney disease, Alzheimer's, and                cancer from a subject via breath, skin, or sweat.                Uses include but are not limited to triacetone                triperoxide, dintrotoluene, fentanyl, cocaine,                cannabidiol, tetrahydrocannabinol, acetone, natural                gas, or propane.
   ADVANTAGE - The detection device ensures high sensitivity                in chemical analysis by utilizing a decoupled                thermodynamic sensor with precisely aligned                microheaters for optimized heating efficiency and                power consumption. The detection device enables                single-molecule detection of vapor phase compounds                while maintaining thermal stability through                controlled catalytic layer temperatures.                Anisotropic heating properties improve efficiency                and selectivity, hence allowing multiple reactions                to be analyzed using a single catalyst. The                detection device supports easy integration of                multiple sensors with minimal thermal interference,                hence enhancing configuration flexibility and                enabling sensor replacements without compromising                detection accuracy.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a top                portion of a sensor.
   100Sensing platform

TI Surface cancerous lesions detecting method for            detection of e.g. melanoma placing probes having array            of temp. sensors in contact with or near skin and            measuring rates of temp. increase at different            sensors.
AU ROGERS G
   SHOPLAND M
AE ROGERS G (ROGE-Individual)
   SHOPLAND M (SHOP-Individual)
GA 1996386910
AB       The lesion detection involves using an array of                thermistors or semiconductor temperature sensors in                a high resolution arrangement for measuring                absolute or relative temperature values. The array                may be hexagonal, circular, triangular, etc.                Sensors may be thermally insulated from each other                and carried by a non-conductive substrate or have                cooling means e.g. by Peltier effect. Probes may be                capable of resolving temperature differences of                0.02 deg. C. or preferably smaller.
   Readings may be taken every 10 seconds, within                and outside the lesion, and during the initial                heating-up phase of the sensors. Data may be                processed by microprocessor before display on a                VDU.
   USE -   Detects cancerous skin lesion by its higher                temp. due to higher metabolic rate and increased                blood supply.
   ADVANTAGE -   High temp. resolution enables determination of                whether skin lesion is cancerous or not, by                non-invasive method, thus reducing number of                hospital referrals for clinical examinations.

   Readings may be taken every 10 seconds, within                and outside the lesion, and during the initial                heating-up phase of the sensors. Data may be                processed by microprocessor before display on a                VDU.

AU ZHAO Y
   HU H

AB    NOVELTY - Gene set for predicting tumor immunotherapy                efficacy comprises ATRX gene or ATRX and ABL1,                ARID1A, ATM, ATR, BRIP1, ERCC4, FANCA, MRE11A, NBN,                PARP1, POLE, RAD50, RAD51B and/or RAD51C, is                new.
   USE - The gene set is used as an immunotherapy                biomarker in preparation of a product for                predicting efficacy of tumor immunotherapy                (claimed), where tumors are e.g. non-small cell                lung cancer, small cell lung cancer, melanoma,                bladder cancer, urothelial cancer, kidney cancer,                head and neck cancer, head and neck squamous cell                carcinoma, esophageal cancer, glioma, colorectal                cancer, lymphoma, liver cancer, gastric cancer,                cervical cancer, Merkel cell carcinoma,                nasopharyngeal carcinoma, tumor of unknown primary                origin, breast cancer and/or non-melanoma skin                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The gene set rapidly provides prediction                result and intuitively display before the medical                staff, provides guidance opinion, and promotes                formulation of effective treatment scheme.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included                for:
   A gene detection panel for predicting efficacy                of tumor immunotherapy to detect whether a mutation                occurs in exon region of gene in gene set;
   Constructing a scoring system for predicting                efficacy of tumor immunotherapy, comprises (a)                obtaining DDR pathway-related gene loci in human                genome, and based on sample data of cancer patients                treated with immunotherapy, multiple loci that are                significantly associated with long-term survival                were screened; (b) obtaining weights of multiple                gene loci in prediction of immunotherapy benefit in                step (i) through multifactor COX regression                analysis, constructing for predicting efficacy of                immunotherapy for obtaining the therapeutic benefit                prediction score; (c) importing cancer patient                sample data into calculation formula for predicting                the efficacy of immunotherapy, and calculating,                obtaining treatment benefit prediction score of all                samples, and sorting corresponding cancer types                from large to small, corresponding samples with                scores before 18-22% in each type of cancer were                used as benefit samples, comparing survival rate of                benefit sample with other samples, selecting                critical point from 18-22%, using corresponding                treatment benefit prediction score of critical                point as the cutoff value of the treatment benefit                prediction score for corresponding cancer type;                and
   Scoring system for predicting the efficacy of                tumor immunotherapy;
   A computer-readable storage medium comprising                a set of instructions for constructing a scoring                system.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The corresponding samples                  with scores before 20% in each type of cancer                  were used as benefit samples, and the                  corresponding treatment benefit prediction score                  value at the 20% cutoff point was used as the                  treatment benefit prediction score cutoff value                  of the corresponding cancer type.

AB    NOVELTY - Natural killer (NK) cell transformed by                chimeric antigen receptor, is new. The chimeric                antigen receptor comprises an extracellular target                molecule binding domain, a transmembrane region                domain and an intracellular signaling domain. The                transmembrane region domain linking the                extracellular target molecule binding domain and                the intracellular signaling domain, and fixes the                two on the cell membrane of the NK cell. The                intracellular signaling domain includes an                intracellular activation signaling domain and/or an                intracellular detection signaling domain.
   USE - The chimeric antigen receptor-engineered NK                cells or medicine composition is useful in                preparing medicine for treating diseases including                tumor (PD-L1 positive or tumor whose PD-L1                expression level is up-regulated in response to                interferon &#947; , specifically solid tumor                (e.g. breast cancer, skin cancer, liver cancer,                ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, brain cancer,                kidney cancer, and lung cancer) and/or                hematological cancer), infection, inflammatory                disease, immune disease, and nervous system disease                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The engineered NK cell can make NK cell target                multiple different antigens and enhance the                proliferation and durability of NK cell in vivo,                finally realize the efficient anti-tumor function,                plays as an important immune cell of organism is                not only associated with anti-tumor antiviral                infection and immune regulation, which involved in                hypersensitivity and autoimmune disease, which can                identify the target cell and kill the cleaning                medium, hence has very important meaning for                improving the NK cell.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   preparing chimeric antigen receptor-engineered                NK cells; and
   a medicinal composition comprising the                chimeric antigen receptor-engineered NK cells or                the chimeric antigen receptor engineered NK                cells.

TI New anti-transmembrane and coiled-coil domain            family 3 (TMCC3) immunoconjugate, useful for detecting            TMCC3 and for treating, preventing and/or diagnosing            cancers.
AU CHUANG S
   HSU C
   CHEN Y
   NIEH Y
   LI T
AE DEV CENT BIOTECHNOLOGY (BIGY-C)
   DCB-USA LLC (DCBU-C)
GA 2018363270
AB    NOVELTY - An immunoconjugate comprising a transmembrane                and coiled-coil domain family 3 (TMCC3) antibody or                its binding fragment, and a therapeutic agent or                label, where the antibody has a dissociation                constant (Kd) of greater than or equal to 100 nM,                and where the immunoconjugate has an                internalization rate of greater than or equal to                50% at an incubation temperature of 37 degrees C                and an incubation time of 60 minutes, is new.
   USE - The immunoconjugate, composition and kit are                useful for detecting TMCC3; and treating,                preventing and/or diagnosing cancers. The                immunoconjugate is used in the manufacture of a                medicament for treating cancer. The cancer is                selected from lung cancer (e.g., non-small cell                lung cancer or NSCLC), ovarian cancer, prostate                cancer, colorectal cancer, liver cancer (i.e.,                hepatocarcinoma), renal cancer (i.e., renal cell                carcinoma), bladder cancer, breast cancer, thyroid                cancer, pleural cancer, pancreatic cancer, uterine                cancer, cervical cancer, testicular cancer, anal                cancer, pancreatic cancer, bile duct cancer,                gastrointestinal carcinoid tumors, esophageal                cancer, gall bladder cancer, appendix cancer, small                intestine cancer, stomach (gastric) cancer, cancer                of the central nervous system, skin cancer,                choriocarcinoma, head and neck cancer, blood                cancer, osteogenic sarcoma, fibrosarcoma,                neuroblastoma, glioma, melanoma, B-cell lymphoma,                non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, Burkitt's lymphoma, small                cell lymphoma, large cell lymphoma, monocytic                leukemia, myelogenous leukemia, acute lymphocytic                leukemia, acute myelocytic leukemia (AML), chronic                myeloid leukemia (CML), and multiple myeloma (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - Safe and effective agents that target TMCC3                for the treatment and diagnosis of TMCC3-associated                conditions, such as cancer, are provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   (1) a composition comprising the                immunoconjugate defined above and a carrier;
   (2) treating cancer in a subject by                administering the immunoconjugate or the                composition defined above, optionally in                combination with a second therapeutic agent, a                radiation therapy, or a surgery;
   (3) detecting TMCC3 in a biological sample by                contacting the biological sample with the                immunoconjugate defined above under conditions                permissive for binding of the immunoconjugate to                the TMCC3, and detecting whether a complex is                formed between the immunoconjugate and the TMCC3 in                the biological sample;
   (4) detecting a TMCC3-positive cancer by (a)                administering the immunoconjugate defined above to                a subject having or suspected of having a                TMCC3-positive cancer, and (b) detecting the                immunoconjugate in the subject, where detection of                the immunoconjugate indicates a TMCC3-positive                cancer in the subject; and
   (5) a kit comprising the immunoconjugate                defined above, and an instruction for the                treatment, prevention and/or diagnosis of                cancers.

The Shiga toxin                  effector polypeptide comprises one of 15(251-262)                  amino acid sequences (SEQ ID NOs: 355-369) all                  fully defined in the specification which further                  comprises a disruption of at least one,                  endogenous, B-cell and/or CD4+ T-cell epitope                  which does not overlap with an embedded or                  inserted, heterologous, CD8+ T-cell epitope. The                  Shiga toxin effector polypeptide comprises one of                  111(251-262) amino acid sequences (SEQ ID NOs:                  6-32, 340-354, and 370-438) all fully defined in                  the specification. The Shiga toxin effector                  polypeptide is capable of exhibiting a ribosome                  inhibition activity with a half-maximal                  inhibitory concentration (IC50) value of 10000                  picomolar or less. The Shiga toxin effector                  polypeptide comprises one or more mutations                  relative to a naturally occurring A subunit of a                  member of the Shiga toxin family which changes an                  enzymatic activity of the Shiga toxin effector                  polypeptide, the mutation chosen from at least                  one amino acid residue deletion, insertion, or                  substitution. The mutation, relative to the                  naturally occurring A Subunit which changes an                  enzymatic activity of the Shiga toxin effector                  polypeptide, reduces or eliminates a cytotoxicity                  of the Shiga toxin effector polypeptide. The                  Shiga toxin effector polypeptide is capable of                  intracellular delivery of the embedded or                  inserted, heterologous, CD8+ T-cell epitope from                  an early endosomal compartment of a cell in which                  the Shiga toxin effector polypeptide is present                  to a major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class                  I molecule of the cell. The Shiga toxin effector                  polypeptide is capable of exhibiting one or more                  Shiga toxin effector functions in addition to                  intracellular delivery of the embedded,                  heterologous, CD8+ T-cell epitope from an early                  endosomal compartment of a cell in which the                  Shiga toxin effector polypeptide is present to a                  MHC class I molecule of the cell. The Shiga toxin                  effector polypeptide comprises a Shiga toxin Al                  fragment region having a carboxy-terminus and a                  disrupted furin-cleavage motif at the                  carboxy-terminus of the A1 fragment region. The                  disrupted furin-cleavage motif comprises one or                  more mutations, relative to a wild-type Shiga                  toxin A Subunit, the mutation altering at least                  one amino acid residue in a region natively                  positioned at 248-251 of the A Subunit of                  Shiga-like toxin 1 (of SEQ ID NO: 1), Shiga toxin                  (of SEQ ID NO: 2), or at 247-250 of the A Subunit                  of Shiga-like toxin 2 (of SEQ ID NO: 3). The                  disrupted furin-cleavage motif comprises an amino                  acid residue substitution in the furin-cleavage                  motif relative to a wild-type Shiga toxin A                  Subunit. The substitution of the amino acid                  residue in the furin-cleavage motif is of an                  arginine residue with a non-positively charged,                  amino acid residue chosen from alanine, glycine,                  proline, serine, threonine, aspartate,                  asparagine, glutamate, glutamine, cysteine,                  isoleucine, leucine, methionine, valine,                  phenylalanine, tryptophan, and tyrosine.

AB    NOVELTY - Method for targeting a payload molecule to an epithelial cell, preferably bladder carcinoma cell, involves contacting the epithelial cell with a protein comprising a polypeptide having one of 3 (376-3075) amino acid sequences (SEQ ID NO: 2, 3 or 4) all fully defined in the specification, where the protein is conjugated to a payload molecule, and the payload molecule slows the growth of the epithelial cell, and the protein stably binds to dystroglycan on the luminal side of the epithelial cell, provided that the epithelial cell lacks apico-basal polarity.
   USE - The method is useful for targeting a payload molecule to an epithelial cell chosen from lung carcinoma, breast carcinoma, colon carcinoma, bladder carcinoma or skin carcinoma (all claimed). The method is used for detecting or treating bladder abnormalities e.g. bladder cancer and interstitial cystitis.
   ADVANTAGE - The method targets payload molecule in an easier, rapid and cost-effective manner with improved detection sensitivity and prevents recurrence rate.

The payload molecule comprises mertansine. The epithelial cell is derived from lung, breast, colon, bladder or skin.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Uropathic; Antiinflammatory. Test details are described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - RNA interference; Dystroglycan binder.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

   CERAMI E G (CERA-Individual)
GA 201605088H
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting presence of feline Gardner-Rasheed                sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (FGR) fusion in a                biological sample comprises: (a) obtaining a                biological sample from a mammal; and (b) contacting                the sample with a reagent that detects FGR fusion                to determine whether FGR fusion is present in the                biological sample. Detection of the FGR fusion                indicates the presence of FGR fusion in the                biological sample.
   USE - The methods are useful for detecting presence                of FGR fusion in biological sample; diagnosing                patient; determining therapeutic regimen for                treating cancer in human subject; identifying                patient likely to respond to treatment with FGR                inhibitor or FGR fusion inhibitor; stratifying                patient population by detecting FGR fusion;                treating patient, where the patient is suffering                from a cancer, where cancer is lung squamous                carcinoma, ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma, skin                cutaneous melanoma, uterine carcinosarcoma, or                esophageal carcinoma; inhibiting proliferation of                cells containing FGR fusion; reducing activity of                FGR fusion; treating condition mediated by aberrant                FGR expression or activity, or treating condition                characterized by overexpression of FGR, or treating                cancer; identifying agent useful for treating lung                squamous carcinoma, ovarian serous                cystadenocarcinoma, skin cutaneous melanoma, and                uterine carcinosarcoma; and for identifying agent                that modulates the activity of FGR fusion (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - Identification of fusions can be an effective                approach to diagnosis of cancers and development of                compounds, compositions, methods, and assays for                evaluating and treating cancer patients.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a method of diagnosing a patient comprising:                (a) obtaining a biological sample from a patient;                and (b) contacting the sample with a reagent that                detects FGR fusion to determine whether FGR fusion                is present in the biological sample, where the                detection of the FGR fusion indicates the presence                of or susceptibility to a disorder associated with                aberrant FGR expression or activity, or                overexpression of FGR;
   a method of determining a therapeutic regimen                for treating a cancer in a human subject,                comprising: (a) obtaining a biological sample from                a tumor in the subject; (b) contacting the sample                with a reagent that detects FGR fusion to determine                whether FGR fusion is present in the biological                sample; and (c) determining the therapeutic regimen                based on the presence or absence of FGR fusion in                the sample;
   a method of identifying a patient likely to                respond to treatment with FGR inhibitor or FGR                fusion inhibitor, comprising: (a) obtaining a                biological sample from the patient; (b) contacting                the sample with a reagent that detects FGR fusion                to determine whether FGR fusion is present in the                biological sample, where the detection of the FGR                fusion indicates the likelihood of the patient                responding to treatment with FGR inhibitor or FGR                fusion inhibitor;
   a method of stratifying a patient population                by detecting FGR fusion, comprising: (a) obtaining                a biological sample from each patient in the                population; (b) contacting each of the samples with                a reagent that detects FGR fusion to determine the                presence or absence of FGR fusion; and (c)                selecting patients having FGR fusion for treatment                with FGR inhibitor or FGR fusion inhibitor;
   a method of treating a patient comprising                acquiring knowledge about the presence of FGR                fusion, and then administering to the patient a                therapeutic amount of FGR inhibitor or FGR fusion                inhibitor;
   a method of inhibiting proliferation of cells                containing FGR fusion comprising contacting the                cells with FGR inhibitor or FGR fusion                inhibitor;
   a method of reducing activity of FGR fusion                comprising contacting the FGR fusion with an agent                that inhibits an activity or expression of                FGR;
   a method of treating a condition mediated by                aberrant FGR expression or activity, or treating a                condition characterized by overexpression of FGR,                or treating cancer; comprising administering to a                subject a therapeutic amount of FGR inhibitor or                FGR fusion inhibitor;
   a method of identifying an agent useful for                treating lung squamous carcinoma, ovarian serous                cystadenocarcinoma, skin cutaneous melanoma, and                uterine carcinosarcoma, comprising contacting a                cell expressing FGR fusion with a candidate agent                and determining whether the expression level of the                fusion is decreased or a biological function                associated with the fusion is altered; and
   a method of identifying an agent that                modulates the activity of FGR fusion, comprising                contacting FGR fusion with a candidate agent; and                detecting a change in a parameter associated with                FGR fusion.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: Detecting FGR fusion in                  the biological sample comprises assays selected                  from: in situ hybridization, comparative genomic                  hybridization, microarray, Southern blot,                  northern blot, PCR, PCR-restriction fragment                  length polymorphism (RFLP) assay, real-time PCR,                  sequence-specific primers, high-performance                  liquid chromatography, or mass-spectrometric                  genotyping, and metaphase cytogenetic analysis by                  karyotype methods. The method comprises: (a)                  performing a PCR amplification reaction with                  polynucleotides from the biological sample, where                  the amplification reaction utilizes a pair of                  primers which will amplify at least a fragment of                  FGR fusion comprising a fusion junction, and                  where the first primer is in sense orientation                  and the second primer is in antisense                  orientation; and (b) detecting an amplification                  product, where the presence of the amplification                  product is indicative of the presence of FGR                  fusion polynucleotide in the sample. Performing a                  PCR amplification reaction comprises: (i)                  providing a reaction mixture comprising                  polynucleotides from the biological sample, the                  pair of primers which will amplify at least a                  fragment of FGR gene fusion comprising a fusion                  junction, where the first primer is complementary                  to a sequence on the first strand of the                  polynucleotides and the second primer is                  complementary to a sequence on the second strand                  of the polynucleotides, a DNA polymerase, and a                  set of free nucleotides comprising adenine,                  thymine, cytosine, and guanine (dNTPs); (ii)                  heating the reaction mixture to a first                  predetermined temperature for a first                  predetermined time to separate the double strands                  of the polynucleotides from each other; (iii)                  cooling the reaction mixture to a second                  predetermined temperature for a second                  predetermined time under conditions to allow the                  first and second primers to hybridize with their                  complementary sequences on the first and second                  strands of the polynucleotides, and to allow the                  DNA polymerase to extend the primers; and (iv)                  repeating steps (ii) and (iii) for a                  predetermined number of cycles. The method                  employs a probe or primer that is detectably                  labeled with a radiolabel, a fluorescent label, a                  bioluminescent label, a chemiluminescent label,                  an enzyme label, a binding pair label, an                  antigen-label, a reporter molecule, an affinity                  tag, an adaptor, a barcode, or a sequence                  identifier. The labeled probe or primer is                  detected using autoradiography, microscopy,                  brightfield microscopy, fluorescence microscopy,                  electron microscopy, enzyme-linked immunosorbent                  assay (ELISA), or immunohistochemistry. The                  biological sample is selected from tissue, whole                  blood, serum, plasma, buccal scrape, sputum,                  saliva, cerebrospinal fluid, urine, stool,                  circulating tumor cells, circulating nucleic                  acids, or bone marrow. It is from a human cancer,                  where the human cancer is lung squamous                  carcinoma, ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma,                  skin cutaneous melanoma, uterine carcinosarcoma,                  or esophageal carcinoma. The FGR gene fusion is a                  Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family, member 2                  (WASF2):FGR gene fusion. The WASF2:FGR gene                  fusion comprises all or part of the nucleotide                  sequence of fully defined 2488 bp (SEQ ID NO: 1)                  given in the specification comprising the fusion                  junction. The reagent is a probe or primer that                  hybridizes to the fusion junction of FGR fusion.                  It hybridizes to nucleotides 178-187, 173-192,                  158-207, 133-232, 108-257, or 83-282 of SEQ ID                  NO: 1. In treating patient, the knowledge about                  the presence of FGR fusion is acquired by the                  method above. In reducing activity of FGR fusion,                  contacting step is effected in vitro, or in cells                  in culture, or in vivo. The agent that inhibits                  activity or expression of FGR is FGR inhibitor or                  FGR fusion inhibitor. In treating cancer, the                  agent that inhibits an activity or expression of                  FGR or the FGR inhibitor is a kinase inhibitor.                  The agent that inhibits an activity or expression                  of FGR or the FGR inhibitor is an anti-FGR                  antibody, or FGR fusion inhibitor.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - FGR Inhibitor; FGR Fusion Inhibitor; Kinase                Inhibitor.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Locating and staging (metastatic) cancer,            comprises using ultrasound scanner and gamma probe to            locate radiolabeled sentinel lymph node, so that a            sample can be taken using a biopsy needle.

AE INTRAMEDICAL IMAGING LLC (INTR-Non-standard)

GA 2006362267
AB    NOVELTY - Locating and determining the stage of                (metastatic) cancer in an individual diagnosed as                having a malignant tumor comprises injecting a                radioactive substance adjacent the tumor, locating                a sentinel lymph nodes using an ultrasound scanner                and gamma camera, and collecting a tissue sample                from the lymph node using a biopsy needle.
   USE - The method and apparatus are useful for                locating and determining the stage of (metastatic)                cancer in an individual through biopsy of a                sentinel lymph node and analysis of the sample. A                therapeutic agent may be delivered to the sentinel                lymph node as part of the biopsy procedure. (All                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Locating and determining the stage of                (metastatic) cancer in an individual diagnosed as                having a malignant tumor comprises:
   injecting a radioactive substance into the                individual in an area adjacent the tumor, and                allowing time for the substance to migrate to                regional lymph nodes or sentinel lymph nodes;
   placing an ultrasound scanner and a gamma                probe or radiation detecting camera on the skin                surface in the region of the sentinel lymph node,                the ultrasound scanner and a gamma probe being                operatively connected so that the relative position                and orientation to each other and to the sentinel                node is mechanically or electronically fixed or                determined, with the lymph node being in the field                of view of the ultrasound scanner and the probe                aimed at the radiation emitting sentinel node, the                direction of orientation of the gamma probe being                adjusted to obtain the maximum possible radiation                count from the sentinel node, indicating that the                radiation source within the labeled sentinel node                had been targeted,
   while holding the ultrasound scanner fixed,                removing the radiation probe and placing a biopsy                needle in the same orientation as established for                the radiation probe in step (b) above and advancing                a distal tip thereof through the skin and into the                sentinel lymph node, and
   collecting a tissue sample from the sentinel                lymph node for subsequent chemical or biological                analysis to determine if the sentinel lymph node                was infiltrated by any cancer cells and if the                disease is stage 1-stage 2 or stage 3 cancer.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included an                assembly for placement on the skin of an individual                to locate radiation tagged tissue within the body,                comprising a gamma probe or radiation detection                camera or a combination of the two. The apparatus                is adapted for percutaneously obtaining biopsy                samples from the tagged tissue, where the apparatus                has an axis of orientation which, when the tagged                tissue is targeted thereby, points to the tagged                tissue and a passageway substantially parallel to                the axis of orientation, where the passageway is                sized to receive along its length a biopsy device                or biopsy needle.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The analysis of the sample                  comprises quantitative reverse transcriptase PCR.                  The analysis is used to determine the presence of                  one or more molecular markers selected from                  IL-13, leptin, lymphotoxin beta receptor (LTbR),                  MIP-1b, interleukin 11 receptor alpha (IL-11Ra),                  indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), interferon                  gamma and IL-10, the quantity of one or more of                  the markers being indicative of infiltration of                  cancer cells into the sentinel lymph node. The                  method further comprises delivering a therapeutic                  agent to the sentinel lymph node. The therapeutic                  agent comprises a compound that provides cytokine                  therapy, gene therapy or RNA or DNA                  interference.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: A blue dye is injected                  into the area adjacent the tumor 1-48 hours after                  the radioactive substance. A biopsy apparatus is                  placed percutaneously in the same orientation as                  the radiation probe along a lumen in the biopsy                  apparatus. The ultrasound scanner and gamma probe                  are operatively connected by a hinge, the                  radiation probe being removably held in a holder                  attached to the hinge, where a biopsy apparatus                  or needle is correctly located for removal of a                  sample by being placed in the holder after                  removal of the radiation probe. The ultrasound                  scanner and gamma probe are operatively connected                  by first and second position sensors mounted on                  the ultrasound scanner and gamma probe. the                  biopsy apparatus or needle has a third position                  sensor. A radiation probe is placed through the                  biopsy apparatus prior to insertion of the biopsy                  needle to verify the location of the sentinel                  node. The orientation of the radiation probe,                  field of view of the ultrasound scanner and the                  location of the sentinel node are simultaneously                  displayed as a visual image on a screen. The                  method further comprises placement of an                  ultrasound detectable marker in or adjacent the                  sentinel lymph node at the same time as the                  removal of the tissue sample.Preferred Apparatus: The apparatus                  comprises:a scintillator-PMT system;a scintillator-PIN diode system;an avalanche photodiode;LSO, YLSO or BGO scintillating crystals                  within a heavy metal collimator;Cd-Te or Zn-Cd semiconductor detectors that                  convert the energy from radiation directly to an                  electronic pulse; ora solid state or silicone                  photomultiplier.The scintillator PMT system uses vacuum tube                  PMTs or scintillation crystals such as NaI(T1).                  The scintillator-PIN diode system uses PIN diodes                  as light detectors, the PIN diodes coupled to the                  scintillator.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene therapy.

AB    NOVELTY - Analyzing relative ratio of microRNA (miRNA)                subtype to family, comprises (a) determining the                content of all miRNA subtypes contained in one                miRNA families in a biological sample, where the                biological sample is divided into two sample groups                having different biological properties; and (b)                calculating the relative ratio of the content of                the miRNA subtype in the total content of all miRNA                subtypes contained in the corresponding miRNA                family.
   USE - The method is useful for analyzing relative                ratio of miRNA subtype to family in a sample i.e.                mammal including human specifically individual with                cancer including lung cancer, gastric cancer, liver                cancer, esophageal cancer, breast cancer, cervical                cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, prostate                cancer, testicular cancer, colorectal cancer, colon                cancer, pancreatic cancer, head and neck cancer,                thyroid cancer, glioma, or skin cancer, preferably                hepatocellular carcinoma, lung cancer, cervical                cancer, colorectal cancer, esophageal cancer, or                gastric cancer, specifically hepatocellular                carcinoma or useful in disease screening and/or                diagnosis specifically in non-disease screening and                non-disease diagnosis (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method can detect and\ analyse the plasma                RNA, more specifically, the calculate the family                ratio of miRNA in a biological sample, and based on                this, distinguishing whether the source individual                of the biological sample has cancer, and the type                and tumor size of the cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   an analysis model for the relative ratio of                miRNA subtypes to families constructed;
   obtaining test results based on biological                samples from individuals, comprising (a)                determining the content of all miRNA subtypes                contained in a miRNA family corresponding to at                least one specific miRNA subtypes in a biological                sample, (b) calculating the relative ratio of the                content of each specific miRNA subtype in the total                content of all miRNA subtypes contained in the                miRNA family to which it corresponds, and (c)                obtaining the test results of the individual based                on the relative ratio information of each specific                miRNA subtype;
   a kit for diagnosing a disease in an                individual, comprising (a) a device for                implementing the analysis method or (b) a device                for using the analytical model or (c) a device for                implementing the analysis method;
   treating a disease in an individual in need,                comprising providing the individual with drugs,                radiotherapy, and/or surgical treatment, where the                biological sample of the individual is tested and                is determined to have the disease or (1) testing a                biological sample from the individual, and (2)                providing corresponding treatment if the test                result is that the individual has the                disease;
   a computer system or program, comprising a set                of instructions for analyzing relative ratio of                microRNA subtype to family; and
   a detection system, comprising computer system                or program.
