AB    NOVELTY - Detecting cell behavior, involves using an                apparatus comprising first working electrode, first                counter electrode, first measurement container in                which culture medium is accommodated in first                measuring container such that the first counter                electrode is immersed, a working electrode on the                bottom face in a second measuring container and a                second counter electrode mutually spaced apart, and                second measurement container for culturing cell in                which culture medium is accommodated in the second                measuring container.
   USE - The method and apparatus are useful for                detecting behavior of cell (claimed) e.g. cells of                vertebrate, invertebrate, plant or insect, and                microbial cells, preferably cancer (e.g. liver                cancer, stomach cancer, colorectal cancer, lung                cancer and skin cancer) cells.
   ADVANTAGE - The method and apparatus can detect the change                of the adhesion state between cells other than the                proliferation of a cell, based on impedance                measurement.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method for detecting cell behavior, involves                using an apparatus comprising first working                electrode placed planarly on the bottom face of a                first measuring container, counter electrode                positioned above the first working electrode and                that spaces apart from the first working electrode,                first measurement container in which the culture                medium is accommodated in the first measuring                container such that the first counter electrode is                immersed, a working electrode on the bottom face in                a second measuring container and a second counter                electrode mutually spaced apart and that is                positioned planarly, and second measurement                container for culturing cell in which the culture                medium is accommodated in the second measuring                container between first working electrode and first                counter electrode and between second working                electrode and second counter electrode, applying a                predetermined voltage, continuously and                respectively measuring information concerning the                impedance between a first working electrode and a                first counter electrode and between a second                working electrode and a second counter electrode,                and determining difference between a time-dependent                change of the information concerning the impedance                between a first working electrode and a first                counter electrode and a time-dependent change of                the information concerning the impedance between a                second working electrode and second counter                electrode. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for                cell behavior detection apparatus.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Method: The difference is                  specified by outputting the curve which shows a                  time dependent change of the information                  concerning the impedance between a first working                  electrode and first counter electrode, and                  impedance between a second working electrode and                  a second counter electrode.

   USE - The method is useful for identifying biomarker                as associated with a disease state to detect,                monitor, and treat disease states e.g. neurological                disease, infection, inflammatory disease or cancer                e.g. pancreatic cancer, ovarian cancer, bladder                cancer, colorectal cancer, lung cancer, brain                cancer, prostate cancer, breast cancer, skin                cancer, lymphoma, tongue cancer, mouth cancer,                pharynx cancer, oral cavity cancer, esophagus                cancer, stomach cancer, small intestine cancer,                colon cancer, rectum cancer, anal cancer, or                leukemia (all claimed). Test details are described                but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: performs in short amount of time                e.g. less than 3 hours, preferably less than 5                minutes; and is unique because while other tests                have potential to improve prognosis for later-stage                cancer, this test can provide higher sensitivity                for detection of early-stage cancer, as exemplified                by our 96% sensitivity for stage I and II                pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cases.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:

AU ZILBERSTEIN J

   YARDEN M

   MEDISIM LTD (MEDI-Non-standard)

GA 2003239462
AB    NOVELTY - Detection of malignant lesions using a thermal                enhancing agent.
   USE - The method is used for the detection of                malignant lesions, especially breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is non-invasive, extremely                inexpensive, does not involve harmful radiationand                does not require trained personnel to administer                the testing and so can be used in an outpatient                clinic. The method has improved sensitivity over                prior art methods.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A method for detecting malignant lesion within                human tissue comprises:
   administering a thermal enhancing agent, the                agent generating heat upon activation from an                external energy source;
   ubmitting the human tissue to a predetermined                amount of energy from an external energy                source;
   monitoring the temperature or other thermal                magnitude on the skin on a plurality of points on                the tissue;
   analyzing the results; and
   detecting specific points on the tissue having                abnormally high temperatures or other thermal                magnitudes in comparison to other points on the                tissue or to predetermined data.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Thermal Enhancing Agent: A                  gas-loaded perlfluorocarbon compound or a                  solution containing a precursor to a gas wherein                  the perfluorocarbon is selected from                  cis-perfluorodecaline, trans-perfluorodecaline,                  perfluorohexane or                  perfluoro-2-butyl-tetrahydrofuran and the gas is                  carbon dioxide or oxygen. The gaseous precursor                  is selected from NaHCO3, aminomalonate, diazonium                  or methylacetate. The agent injected, preferably                  intravenously, may be enclosed within liposomes                  or be in the form of an emulsion with particle                  size 10-100nm.Preferred Energy Source: Ultrasonic energy                  having frequency 0.3-10MHz. The energy is                  activated in a continuous manner or in several                  pulses having predetermined intervals between the                  pulses, the pulses may be of varying                  intensity.Preferred Method: The amount of thermal                  enhancing agent administered and the amount of                  energy submitted are such that will produce a                  maximum internal tissue temperature of 41 degrees                  C. The comparison of results may be with an image                  obtained using an imaging technique other than                  thermal magnitude monitoring. The temperature or                  other thermal magnitudes are monitored using an                  infrared-based camera, an array of sensors or a                  plurality of thermistors. The analysis of the                  results is performed using a prediction                  algorithm.
   EXAMPLE - The example illustrates how perfluorodecalin                amplifies the rise in temperature associated with                the application of ultrasound. 2 test tubes were                chosen, containing saline (0.9M NaCl).                Perfluorodecalin was repeatedly added to one so as                to obtain ten fold increases in perfluorodecalin                concentration. After each new concentration was                reached, the test tube was subjected to ultrasound                energy, frequency 1MHz and intensity 100mW/cm2 for                3 minutes. The temperature was then read using a                temperature probe inserted into the test tube. The                temperature was also measured in the test tube                containing only saline which acted as a control.                The results are shown in Fig 1 below. Each peak on                the graph represents a rise in temperature at a                specific time in the experiment. The first peak on                the left (peak 0) represents a time point when both                test tubes contained only saline and application of                ultrasound raised the temperaturein both to                33degreesC.Subsequent peaks show increasing levels                of perfluorodecalin. Peak 1 shows perfluorodecalin                concentration of 0.01%, peak 2 has perfluorodecalin                concentration of 0.1% , peak 3 has perfluorodecalin                concentration of 10% and peak 4 has                perfluorodecalin concentration 100%.

   USE - The method is useful for detecting cancer                using conjugated quantum dots (claimed), where the                cancer includes breast cancer and skin                cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides enhanced detection                sensitivity and selectivity, and economically                detects cancer in a rapid manner with minimized                risk and pain to the patient.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting cancer comprises: contacting                conjugated quantum dots to tissue, where each of                the conjugated quantum dots comprises a biomarker                specific moiety comprising anti-vascular                endothelial growth factor antibody, anti-Tn antigen                antibody, anti-T antigen antibodies, anti-sial-T                antigen antibodies, anti-sial-Tn antigen                antibodies, anti-human epidermal growth factor                receptor 2 antibodies and anti-insulin like growth                factor receptor antibodies for a time sufficient to                bind quantum dots to the biomarker on the tissue;                removing unbound quantum dots from the tissue;                exciting bound quantum dots with excitation energy;                and analyzing an emission from the bound quantum                dots. TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method is carried out                  during a surgical procedure for the purpose of                  determining whether tissue re-excision is                  required before completion of the surgical                  procedure. The conjugation linker has a binding                  affinity for biotin, where the biomarker specific                  moieties are functionalized with biotin. The                  biomarker specific moieties are conjugated to the                  quantum dot using a biotin-streptavidin                  conjugation scheme.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The ratio of capping                  agent:metal:selenium, tellurium or sulfur, is                  2:1:1-16:8:1 or 4:3:1-8:5:1. The core comprises:                  a metal sulfide, a metal selenide or a metal                  telluride; or 2 different metals. The core is                  cadmium sulfide, zinc sulfide, cadmium selenide,                  cadmium telluride, cadmium lead sulfide, or zinc                  tin sulfide.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The mercaptosilane                  comprises 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane. The                  mercaptocarboxylic acid is mercaptopropionic acid                  (preferred), mercaptoacetic acid,                  mercaptosuccinic acid, mercaptobenzoic acid or                  mercaptoundecanoic acid. The conjugated quantum                  dot comprises at least two thiol-functionalized                  capping agents, where the quantum dot is                  synthesized by capping the core with a first                  thiol-functionalized capping agent and replacing                  at least some of the first thiol-functionalized                  capping agent with a second thiol-functionalized                  capping agent. The thiol-functionalized capping                  agent is 4-aminothiophenol, mercaptosilane or                  mercaptocarboxylic acid. The first capping agent                  is a mercaptocarboxylic acid. The second capping                  agent is 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane. The                  conjugated quantum dot further comprises                  conjugation linkers comprising: sulfosuccinimidyl                  4-[N-maleimidomethyl]cyclohexane-1-carboxylate;                  succinimidyl-([N-maleimidopropionamido]-n-ethyleneglycol)                  ester; SM(PEG) n, where n is 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 or                  24; 1-ethyl-3-[3-dimethylaminopropyl]carbodiimide                  hydrochloride-N-hydroxysulfosuccinimide; or                  streptavidin. The molar ratio of the first thiol                  functionalized capping agent used in the                  replacement step to the moles of quantum dots, is                  0.5-4.

AB    NOVELTY - Analyzing a fluid sample obtained from a                subject involves determining presence or absence of                one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA in the fluid                sample, where the subject was previously                administered a cytokine or growth factor in an                amount effective to mobilize release of the one or                more tumor cells or tumor DNA into                circulation.
   USE - Method for analyzing a fluid sample obtained                from a subject is used to detect one or more tumor                cells or tumor DNA in a fluid sample obtained from                a subject, or to detect presence or absence of                minimal residual disease in a subject, or to treat                cancer in the subject. The cancer is adrenal                cancer, anal cancer, bile duct cancer, bladder                cancer, bone cancer, cancer of the brain or central                nervous system, basal cell skin cancer, breast                cancer, cervical cancer, colorectal cancer,                endometrial cancer, esophageal cancer, eye cancer,                gallbladder cancer, gastrointestinal carcinoid                tumors, gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST),                gastric cancer, glioma, glioblastoma, head and neck                cancer (including head and neck squamous cell                carcinoma), Hodgkin disease, Classical Hodgkin                Lymphoma, diffuse large B cell lymphoma, follicular                lymphoma, Kaposi sarcoma, kidney cancer, laryngeal                and hypopharyngeal cancer, leukemia (including                acute myeloid leukemia), liver cancer (including                hepatocellular carcinoma), lymphoma, melanoma                (including unresectable or metastatic melanoma),                prostate cancer, lung cancer (including non-small                cell lung cancer and metastatic non-small cell lung                cancer) malignant mesothelioma, merkel cell                carcinoma, metastatic urothelial carcinoma,                multiple myeloma, myeloma, myelodysplastic                syndrome, nasal cavity and paranasal sinus cancer,                nasopharyngeal cancer, neuroendocrine cancer,                neuroblastoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, oral cavity                and oropharyngeal cancer, osteosarcoma, ovarian                cancer, pancreatic cancer, penile cancer, pituitary                tumors, renal cancer (including renal cell                carcinoma), retinoblastoma, hematological                malignancy, rhabdomyosarcoma, salivary gland                cancer, sarcoma, squamous cell skin cancer, small                intestine cancer, stomach cancer, testicular                cancer, thymus cancer, thyroid cancer, uterine                cancer, and vaginal cancer (all claimed).
No biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The methods are advantageous for the detection                of minimal residual disease (MRD) or the presence                of undetected micrometastases, because mobilization                of diseased cells (e.g., tumor cells) and/or debris                from diseased cells (e.g., ctDNA) enhances yield of                the diseased cells and/or polynucleotides, thus                enhancing sensitivity of the assay and reducing                false negatives. The detected presence of tumor                cells or ctDNA in the fluid sample is indicative of                MRD in the subject, and the detected absence of                tumor cells or ctDNA in the fluid sample is                indicative of a true MRD absence in the                subject.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) a                method of detecting one or more tumor cells or                tumor DNA in a fluid sample obtained from a                subject, which involves (a) administering to the                subject a cytokine or growth factor in an amount                effective to stimulate release of the one or more                tumor cells or tumor DNA into circulation, (b)                obtaining the fluid sample from the subject after                administering the cytokine or growth factor to the                subject, and (c) determining presence or absence of                the released one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA                in the fluid sample; (2) a method of detecting                presence or absence of minimal residual disease in                a subject in need, which involves analyzing a fluid                sample obtained from the subject or detecting one                or more tumor cells or tumor DNA in a fluid sample                obtained from the subject, where presence of the                one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA in the fluid                sample indicates presence of minimal residual                disease in the subject, and absence of the one or                more tumor cells or tumor DNA in the fluid sample                indicates absence of minimal residual disease in                the subject; (3) a method of treating cancer in a                subject in need, which involves (a) administering                to the subject a cytokine or growth factor in an                amount effective to stimulate release of one or                more tumor cells or tumor DNA into circulation, (b)                obtaining a fluid sample from the subject after                administering the cytokine or growth factor to the                subject, (c) determining presence or absence of the                released one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA in                the fluid sample, and (d) administering at least                one cancer therapeutic to the subject if presence                of the released one or more tumor cells or tumor                DNA in the fluid sample is detected; (4) a method                of prognosing a subject having cancer, which                involves genetically profiling one or more tumor                cells or tumor DNA analytes, where the one or more                tumor cells or tumor DNA analytes were obtained                from a fluid sample obtained from the subject,                where the subject was previously administered a                cytokine or growth factor in an amount effective to                stimulate release of the one or more tumor cells or                tumor DNA into circulation, where the genetic                profile of the one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA                analytes is indicative of the subject's prognosis;                (5) a method of detecting cancer in a subject,                which involves detecting one or more tumor cells or                tumor DNA analytes, where the one or more tumor                cells or tumor DNA analytes were obtained from a                fluid sample obtained from the subject, where the                subject was previously administered a cytokine or                growth factor in an amount effective to stimulate                release of the one or more tumor cells or tumor DNA                into circulation, where the detection of the one or                more tumor cells or tumor DNA analytes is                indicative of cancer in the subject; (6) a kit,                whichcomprises a pharmaceutically acceptable dosage                form of a growth factor or cytokine and                instructions for use; and (7) a system for liquid                biopsy yield enhancement, comprising one or more                pharmaceutically acceptable dosage forms of a                cytokine or growth factor, one or more reagents,                devices, or kits for obtaining a fluid sample from                a subject in need, and one or more reagents,                devices, and/or apparatuses for analyzing tumor                cells and/or tumor DNA in the fluid sample.

TI Treating malignant tumors and            metastases,ncomprises using human and animal medicine,            by specific active substances which activate anaerobic,            adenosine triphosphate- and lactate-forming glycolysis            of cancer cells e.g. glycostimulation.
AU PODZUWEIT T
   PODZUWEIT M E
AE PODZUWEIT T (PODZ-Individual)
GA 201707211T
AB    NOVELTY - Treating malignant tumors and metastases,                comprises using human and animal medicine, by means                of specific active substances which activate the                anaerobic, ATP- and lactate-forming glycolysis of                the cancer cells e.g. glycostimulation, and the                extracellular accumulation of cyclic guanosine-3'                5'-monophosphate (cGMP). The treatment is performed                for epithelial cell tumors e.g. carcinomas and                adenocarcinomas, brain tumors e.g. gliomas,                glioblastomas, and skin cancer e.g.malignant                melanoma).
   USE - The method is useful for treating malignant                tumors and metastases (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method utilizes the carcinogens to treat                cancer, and improves the significance of imaging                methods of nuclear medicine.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Treating malignant tumors and metastases,                comprises using human and animal medicine, by means                of specific active substances which activate the                anaerobic, ATP- and lactate-forming glycolysis of                the cancer cells e.g. glycostimulation, and the                extracellular accumulation of cyclic guanosine-3'                5'-monophosphate (cGMP). The treatment is performed                for epithelial cell tumors e.g. carcinomas and                adenocarcinomas, brain tumors e.g. gliomas,                glioblastomas, and skin cancer e.g.malignant                melanoma), and for cancer precursors e.g.                precancerous diseases, and hyperplasia e.g.                cervical, intraepithelial neoplasia, and benign                prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). The tumors that are                able to use their energy requirements even with                sufficient oxygen supply (normoxia) by glycolytic                substrate chain phosphorylation, and not by                (oxidative) respiratory chain phosporylation, are                treated in the treatment of active substances by                the acupuncture and cleavage of glucose which are                intensively amplified (singular glycostimulation),                and accumulated by ATP-dependent, programmed cell                death (apoptosis). The formation of cGMP in the                tumor cells is inhibited, while the cleavage                (glucose) of glucose to lactate, and the glycolytic                ATP formation are stimulated. The unique feature of                the cancer drugs is such that the tumor cells                secrete less cyclic guanosine-3 ', 5'-monophosphate                (cGMP) and more lactate than untreated cells when                treated with the drugs. The singular,                glycostimulatory cancer therapy is supplemented by                the fact that tumors e.g. melanoma, glioblastoma,                and bladder carcinoma) are treated locally with                highly dosed glucose, preferably greater than or                equal to 15 mmol/l. The local hyperglycaemia,                combined with the glycostimulatory therapy, has the                result that the tumor cells are intentionally                destroyed by hyperacidity (active substance and                glucose-driven lactic acidosis, necrosis). The                imaging of the tumors in vivo is performed by means                of positron emission tomography e.g.                18F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D-gucose-PET and is determined                by the treatment with the glycostimulatory active                substances, including                erythro-9-(2'-hydroxy-3'nonyl)-adenine. The                tumor-specific PET signal is selectively amplified                while the signal generated by the hypoxic tumor                environment remains unchanged. The                hypoxic-cleansed, active substance-induced,                selective stimulation of tumor cell glycolysis in                combination with PET, even the smallest tumors of                hypoxic tissue can be distinguished and clearly                delineated. The glycostimulatory PET is used to                optimize cancer treatment, including early                detection, follow-up, and follow-up care. The                active substances are used as tracers in nuclear                medicine after appropriate labeling with                radionuclides, e.g. 18-fluorine.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The carcinogenic                  agents used are adenine-containing purine                  hydrocarbons, based on the lead structure 9-                  (3'-nonyl) adenine. The structural analog, and                  adenosine deaminase (ADA) inhibitor, erythro-9-                  (2'-hydroxy-3'-nonyl) adenine (EHNA) is attached                  to carbon 2' of the nonyl-(C-9 )aliphatic instead                  of the hydroxyl group. The backbone of the                  carcinogenic agent to be used is the heterozygous                  purine base adenine, or adenine analogs, having a                  primary or secondary N-6 amino group, and a                  lipophilic hydrocarbon ligand. The further                  modifications of the N-9 hydrocarbon chain,                  branches are permitted e.g. substitution of                  2'-hydrogen by methyl or alkyl. The hydrocarbon                  ligand on N-9 can be saturated or unsaturated,                  and can have terminal aromatics. The hydrogen                  atom on carbon 8 of the purine ring (atomic mass                  1) can be replaced by a bulky ligand, eg bromine                  (atomic mass 80), which shields the NC bond                  between nucleobase and hydrocarbon, and protects                  it by steric hindrance from enzymatic lysis                  9-(3'-nonyl) -8-bromo-adenine). The carbon C-2 of                  the puring skeleton may carry, instead of                  hydrogen, a primary or secondary amino group                  (NHR), at guanine for nuclear medical purposes,                  modifications of the active substances are                  possible, for example substitution of the                  2'-hydroxy group, or the 2'-hydrogen of the                  conducting substance 9-(3-nonyl) adenine, by                  radioactive isotopes (tracers) 18-fluoro. The                  carcinogenic agents used have hydrophobic and                  hydrophilic binding sites, and are predominantly                  water- or fat-soluble (amphiphilic), depending on                  the pH value and are bio available. The active                  compounds with hydroxyl-free hydrocarbon ligands                  are 9- (2'-decyl) adenine or 9- (2'-dodecyl)                  adenine) inhibit tumor growth factor. The cancer                  therapy is based on the use of                  glycolysis-stimulating active compounds which                  specifically inhibit tumor growth, and induce                  programmed cell death. The biological-metabolic                  cancer defense is possible to effectively prevent                  the invasive growth of malignant, glycolysophilic                  tumors, and the impending metastasization, and to                  optimize the nuclear medical diagnosis and                  follow-up control.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AU BEZERRA COSTA R

GA 2025A12154
AB    NOVELTY - Method for obtaining a new protein molecule,                classified as Genipa americana lectin (GaBL),                involves using an anticancer agent and/or as a                molecular biomarker, through aqueous extraction                using bark of the plant species Genipa                americana.
   USE - The method is used for obtaining a new protein                molecule, which is used for providing                antiproliferative activity in cancer cells and                anticancer activity against human skin cancer                (A431), melanoma (B16), and tongue squamous cell                carcinoma (SCC9) cell lines, through cell viability                methodologies, cell migration and invasion assays,                identification of cell membrane alterations, and                real-time polymerase chain reaction for caspase-3                and mRNA expression of proteins related to                epithelial-mesenchymal transition (E-cadherin,                Col1A1) (claimed). Test details are described but                no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method obtains protein molecule that is                isolated from the aqueous extract of Genipa                americana bark, using simple and essential                purification processes in the pharmaceutical                industry and biotechnology research, in particular,                as anticancer agents and/or as a biomarker used in                the detection and/or treatment of cancer cells, in                a less invasive manner, when compared with                traditional methods. The method obtains low                toxicity and high selectivity for cancer cells. The                method uses plant extract, originating from a                species that is easy to obtain, and as a home                medicine, for various purposes. The lectin (GaBL)                is isolated using a single chromatographic method                and showed high hemagglutinating activity. The                purified lectin is capable of significantly                reducing migration and cell inviability in the                tumor cells evaluated, with invasiveness being an                important characteristic of cancer cells and a                target for the development of anticancer                agents.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method comprises                  purifying the GaBL protein with anticancer                  activity, obtained from purification using                  Tris-hydrochloride buffer (50 mM, pH 8.0),                  precipitation with ammonium sulfate at 20%                  saturation and molecular exclusion liquid                  chromatography.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - The example section describes the biological                data of cell viability assay and identifying                Acridine orange/ethidium bromide (AO/EB) dual                fluorescent staining that does not support the                claims.

AB    NOVELTY - Nucleic acid aptamer or a fragment is new,                where aptamer comprises a nucleotide sequence with                a sequence identity of 80% to sequence comprising                76 nucleotide sequence of (SEQ ID NOs: 1, 2), given                in the specification, 45 nucleotide sequence of                (SEQ ID NO: 3), given in the specification, 19                nucleotide sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 4), and 40                nucleotide sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 8), given in the                specification.
   USE - Nucleic acid aptamer or a fragment used as                non-therapeutic cosmetic in complex, combination,                composition (such as pharmaceutical or cosmetic                composition), and as medicament for binding                specifically to Olfactory Receptor Family 2                Subfamily AT Member 4 (OR2AT4) receptor and                activating OR2AT4 receptor, in vitro detection and                activation of OR2AT4 receptor in a biological                sample isolated from a subject, treatment and/or                prevention of diseases caused by a decrease in the                expression of the OR2AT4 receptor and/or decrease                in the activation of the OR2AT4 receptor and/or                absence of the natural ligand of the OR2AT4                receptor, and/or low amount of the natural ligand                of the OR2AT4 receptor with respect to the amount                of natural ligand in a subject in normal health                conditions or a healthy subject, cancer, hair loss                in a subject and/or in the promotion of hair                growth, wounds, and skin dysbiosis (all                claimed).
No biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The complex capable of binding specifically to                and activating the OR2AT4 receptor and with the                activity associated with the functional group,                improve of skin appearance, hair appearance, and                proliferation of skin cells, cure, delay, reduce                the severity of, or improve one or more symptoms of                the pathology characterized by a decrease or                inhibition of the expression of the OR2AT4                receptor, and/or decrease or blockage in the                activation of the OR2AT4 receptor, and/or an                absence/low amount of the natural ligand of the                OR2AT4 receptor (low amount with respect to the                amount of natural ligand under normal health                conditions). The pharmaceutical composition help in                treatment of skin dysbiosis in a subject.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Nucleic acid aptamer or a fragment is new,                where aptamer comprises a nucleotide sequence with                a sequence identity of 80% to sequence comprising                76 nucleotide sequence of (SEQ ID NOs: 1, 2), given                in the specification, 45 nucleotide sequence of                (SEQ ID NO: 3), given in the specification, 19                nucleotide sequence tggtgtggagggaactggc (SEQ ID NO:                4), and 40 nucleotide sequence of (SEQ ID NO: 8),                given in the specification.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   Complex, which comprises an aptamer or                fragment and functional group, where the functional                group is selected from a detectable reagent, drug,                and nanoparticle;
   Combination, which comprises: (i) aptamer or a                fragment, or the complex; and (ii)                1,5,5-trimethylcyclopent-1-ene derivative of                formula (I).
   Composition, which comprises the aptamer or a                fragment, complex, and/or combination;
   Method for in vitro detection of OR2AT4                receptor in a biological sample isolated from a                subject, which involves: (a) contacting the                isolated biological sample with the aptamer or a                fragment, or with the complex; (b) separating the                aptamer or complex not bound to the OR2AT4                receptor; and (c) detecting the presence of the                aptamer or complex bound to the OR2AT4 receptor                present in the isolated biological sample;                and
   Method for in vitro activation of OR2AT4                receptor in a biological sample isolated from a                subject, which involves contacting the sample                comprising the OR2AT4 receptor with the aptamer or                a fragment, complex, and/or the combination.
   R=hydrogen or a methyl group.1

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The APCs are dendritic                  cells. The immune effector cells are T cells,                  peripheral blood lymphocytes, natural killer (NK)                  cells, invariant NK cells, NKT cells. The immune                  effector cells have been differentiated from                  mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) or induced                  pluripotent stem (iPS) cells. The T cells are                  cluster of differentiation (CD)8+ T cells, CD4+ T                  cells, or &#947; d T cells, or cytotoxic T                  lymphocytes (CTLs). The population of CD8 or                  CD4-positive and peptide MHC tetramer-positive                  engineered T cells are purified from the                  transduced host cells. The peptide-specific T                  cells are autologous or allogeneic. The                  biological sample comprises: a blood sample or a                  fraction; lymphocytes; or a fractionated sample                  comprising lymphocytes. The T cells is isolated                  from a patient having or suspected of having a                  cancer.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Components: The peptide comprises at                  least 6 contiguous amino acids of a peptide of                  one of SEQ ID NOS: 1-776. The peptide: is 15                  amino acids or fewer in length; consists of 9 or                  15 amino acids; is immunogenic; or is modified;                  has at least 90% sequence identity to a peptide                  of one of SEQ ID NOS: 1-776; has 1, 2 or 3                  substitutions relative to a peptide of one of SEQ                  ID NOs: 1-776; and comprises 100% sequence                  identity to a peptide of one of SEQ ID NOs:                  1-776. The modification comprises conjugation to                  a molecule. The molecule comprises an antibody, a                  lipid, an adjuvant, or a detection moiety. The                  polypeptide comprises: at least 2 peptides (P1)                  or (P2); a cell penetrating peptide (CPP)                  comprising the Z13 variant of ZEBRA CPP Z12; from                  amino-proximal position to carboxy-proximal                  position a cell penetrating peptide, at least one                  peptide (P1) or (P2) and a toll like receptor                  (TLR) agonist; extra domain A (EDA) and Anaxa.                  The polypeptide further comprises: at least one                  toll like receptor (TLR) agonists; and a TLR                  agonist amino-proximal to the cell penetrating                  peptide. The TLR agonist comprises: a TLR2,                  and/or TLR4 agonist. The nucleic acid is DNA or                  RNA. The expression vector comprises an                  adenoviral backbone. The viral backbone comprises                  a simian adenoviral backbone. The host cell                  comprises a viral packaging cell. The dendritic                  cell is a mature dendritic cell. The cell is a                  cell with human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A, HLA-B,                  or HLA-C type. The binding molecule is an                  antibody, TCR mimic antibody, single chain                  variable fragment (scFV), camelid, aptamer, or                  DARPIN. The expression vector comprises a linker                  domain between the TCR &#945; sequence and                  TCR &#946; sequence. The linker domain                  comprises a sequence encoding at least one                  peptide cleavage sites. The cleavage sites are a                  Furin cleavage site and/or a P2A cleavage site.                  The TCR &#945; sequence and TCR &#946;                  sequence are linked by internal ribosomal entry                  site (IRES) sequence. The MHC polypeptide is                  and/or peptide is conjugated to a detection tag.                  The MHC polypeptide and peptide are operatively                  linked: to form a peptide-MHC complex; through a                  peptide bond; through van der Waals forces, where                  at least two, preferably 3 or 4 peptide-MHC                  complexes are operatively linked to each other.                  The average ratio of MHC polypeptides to peptides                  is 1:1-4:1. The peptide is comprised in a                  pharmaceutical preparation, or in a cell culture                  media. Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  comprises isolating the expressed peptide or                  polypeptide. In the method (M2) the step of                  contacting is further defined as co-culturing the                  starting population of immune effector cells with                  antigen presenting cells (APCs), artificial                  antigen presenting cells (aAPCs), or an                  artificial antigen presenting surface (aAPSs),                  where the APCs, aAPCs, or the aAPSs present the                  peptide on their surface. The step of obtaining                  comprises isolating the starting population of                  immune effector cells from peripheral blood                  mononuclear cells (PBMCs), where the starting                  population of immune effector cells is obtained                  from a subject. The method (M2) further                  comprises: introducing the peptide or a nucleic                  acid encoding the peptide into the dendritic                  cells prior to the co-culturing; and cloning of a                  T cell receptor (TCR) from the clonal population                  of peptide- specific immune effector cells. The                  peptide or nucleic acids encoding the peptide are                  introduced by electroporation. The peptide or                  nucleic acids encoding the peptide are introduced                  by adding the peptide or nucleic acid encoding                  the peptide to the dendritic cell culture media.                  The immune effector cells are co-cultured with a                  second population of dendritic cells into which                  the peptide or the nucleic acid encoding the                  peptide has been introduced. The population of                  CD8 or CD4-positive and peptide MHC                  tetramer-positive T cells are purified from the                  immune effector cells following the coculturing.                  The clonal population of peptide- specific immune                  effector cells are generated by limiting or                  serial dilution followed by expansion of                  individual clones by a rapid expansion protocol.                  The cloning of the TCR is cloning of a TCR                  &#945; and &#946; chain. The TCR is                  cloned using a 5'-Rapid amplification of cDNA                  ends (RACE). The cloned TCR is subcloned into an                  expression vector i.e. retroviral or lentiviral                  vector. The host cell is transduced with the                  expression vector to generate an engineered cell                  that expresses the TCR. The starting population                  of immune effector cells is obtained from a                  subject with cancer and the host cell is                  allogeneic or autologous to the subject. The                  clonal population of peptide-specific engineered                  T cells are generated by limiting or serial                  dilution followed by expansion of individual                  clones by a rapid expansion protocol. The method                  (M4) further comprises: introducing the peptide                  or a nucleic acid encoding the peptide into the                  dendritic cells prior to the co-culturing;                  sequencing the TCR &#945; and/or &#946;                  gene(s) and/or performing grouping of lymphocyte                  interactions by paratope hotspots (GLIPH)                  analysis. The step of purifying is defined as                  purifying a population of CD4- or CD8-positive                  and peptide MHC tetramer-positive T cells from                  the immune effector cells following the                  co-culturing. The population of CD4- or                  CD8-positive and peptide MHC tetramer-positive T                  cells are purified by fluorescence activated cell                  sorting (FACS). The step of purifying further                  comprises generation of a clonal population of                  peptide- specific immune effector cells by                  limiting or serial dilution of sorted cells                  followed by expansion of individual clones by a                  rapid expansion protocol. The isolating is                  defined as cloning of a TCR from the clonal                  population of peptide-specific immune effector                  cells. In the method (M5): the peptide is linked                  to a solid support; the peptide is conjugated to                  the solid support or is bound to an antibody that                  is conjugated to the solid support, where the                  solid support comprises a microplate, a bead, a                  glass surface, a slide, or a cell culture dish.                  The step of detecting T cell responses comprises:                  detecting the binding of the peptide to the T                  cell or TCR; or enzyme linked immunosorbent assay                  (ELISA), ELISA SPOT, or a tetramer assay. The                  method (M6) further comprises: counting the                  number of T cells bound with peptide and/or MHC;                  sorting the number of T cells bound with peptide                  and/or MHC; sequencing at least one TCR genes                  from T cells bound with peptide and/or MHC; and                  grouping of lymphocyte interactions by GLIPH                  analysis.

GA 2021C5862Y
AB    NOVELTY - In-vitro method (M1) for detecting a medical                condition in a subject involves (a) obtaining a                sample, (b) enriching very small embryonic like                stem cells from the sample to obtain a mixture                comprising the very small embryonic like stem                cells, (c) obtaining nucleic acid from the mixture                of step (b), (d) performing an assay with the                nucleic acid for analyzing expression level of                octamer-binding transcription factor 4A (Oct4A) in                the very small embryonic like stem cells from the                sample and (e) comparing the expression level of                Oct4A in the very small embryonic like stem cells                from the sample with an expression level of Oct4A                in a control sample, where an increase in the range                of 1.1-3 folds in the expression level of Oct4A in                the very small embryonic like stem cells from the                sample as compared to the expression level of Oct4A                in the control sample detects the presence of a                medical condition in the subject.
   USE - The method is useful for detecting a medical                condition, predicting the onset of cancer,                detecting the presence of cancer, monitoring                response to anti-cancer therapy and treating                cancer, where the medical condition identified is                chosen from multiple sclerosis, kidney disorders,                skin disease, liver disease, lung disease,                cardiovascular diseases, osteoarthritis, viral                disease, cancer and diabetes (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   in-vitro method (M2) for predicting onset of                cancer in a subject involves (a) obtaining a                sample, (b) enriching very small embryonic like                stem cells from the sample to obtain a mixture                comprising the very small embryonic like stem                cells, (c) obtaining nucleic acid from the mixture                of step (b), (d) performing an assay with the                nucleic acid for analyzing expression level of                Oct4A in the very small embryonic like stem cells                and (e) comparing the expression level of Oct4A in                the very small embryonic like stem cells from the                sample with an expression level of Oct4A in a                control sample, where an increase in the range of                3-5 folds in the expression level of Oct4A in the                very small embryonic like stem cells from the                sample as compared to the expression level of Oct4A                in the control sample predicts the onset of cancer                in the subject and the increase of at least 5 folds                in the expression level of Oct4A in the very small                embryonic like stem cells from the sample as                compared to the expression level of Oct4A in the                control sample detects the presence of cancer in                the subject;
   in-vitro method (M3) for monitoring response                to anti-cancer therapy;
   in-vitro method (M4) of detecting a positive                response to anti-cancer therapy;
   in-vitro method (M5) of detecting                cancer;
   method (M6) of treating cancer;
   reagent kit comprising reagents for enriching                very small embryonic-like stem cell from a blood                sample;
   detection kit comprising (a) primer set for                analyzing expression level of at least one                biomarker chosen from Oct4A, Stella and Fragilis in                a mixture comprising very small embryonic-like stem                cell, (b) reagents for performing quantitative PCR                assay, (c) reagents for performing whole genome or                exome or transcriptome sequencing and (d) at least                one tissue-specific array for analyzing a sequence                profile;
   method (M7) for detecting presence of cancer                involves (a) obtaining a blood/tissue sample from a                subject, (b) enumerating the number of very small                embryonic like stem cells in the blood sample and                (c) comparing the number of very small embryonic                like stem cells in the blood sample with the number                of very small embryonic like stem cells in a                control blood sample, where an increase in the                number of very small embryonic like stem cells in                the blood sample as compared to the number of very                small embryonic like stem cells in a control blood                sample detects the presence of cancer, predicts the                onset of cancer or detects the presence of a                medical condition in the subject; and
   method (M8) for predicting the onset of cancer                in a subject involves (a) enumerating in-vivo the                number of very small embryonic like stem cells in                the blood/tissue of a subject and (b) comparing the                number of very small embryonic like stem cells in                the subject with the number of very small embryonic                like stem cells in a control, where an increase in                the number of very small embryonic like stem cells                in the subject as compared to the number of very                small embryonic like stem cells in a control                detects the presence of cancer, predicts the onset                of cancer or detects the presence of a medical                condition in the subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The in-vitro method (M3)                  involves (a) obtaining a sample at one time point                  during an anti-cancer therapy, (b) enriching very                  small embryonic like stem cells from the sample                  to obtain a mixture comprising the very small                  embryonic like stem cells, (c) obtaining nucleic                  acid from the mixture of step (b), (d) performing                  an assay with the nucleic acid for analyzing                  expression level of Oct4A in the very small                  embryonic like stem cells from the sample and (e)                  comparing the expression level of Oct4A in the                  very small embryonic like stem cells from the                  sample with an expression level of Oct4A in very                  small embryonic like stem cells in a reference                  that monitors the response to anti-cancer                  therapy. The method (M4) involves (a) obtaining a                  sample-I before administration of an anti-cancer                  therapy, (b) obtaining a sample-II after                  administration of the anti-cancer therapy, (c)                  enriching very small embryonic like stem cells                  from the sample-I to obtain a mixture-I                  comprising the very small embryonic like stem                  cells, (d) enriching very small embryonic like                  stem cells from the sample-II to obtain a                  mixture-II comprising the very small embryonic                  like stem cells, (e) obtaining nucleic acid-I                  from the mixture-I, (f) obtaining nucleic acid-II                  from the mixture-II, (g) independently performing                  an assay with the nucleic acid-I and the nucleic                  acid-II for analyzing expression level of Oct4A                  and (h) comparing the expression levels of Oct4A                  from the nucleic acid-II with the expression                  level of Oct4A from the nucleic acid-I, where a                  decrease in the expression level of Oct4A from                  the nucleic acid-II as compared to the expression                  level of Oct4A from the nucleic acid-I detects a                  positive response to the cancer treatment. The                  in-vitro method (M5) involves (a) obtaining a                  sample, (b) enriching very small embryonic like                  stem cells from the sample to obtain a mixture                  comprising the very small embryonic like stem                  cells, (c) obtaining nucleic acid from the                  mixture of step (b), (d) performing an assay with                  the nucleic acid for analyzing expression level                  of Oct4A in very small embryonic like stem cells,                  (e) comparing the expression level of Oct4A in                  very small embryonic like stem cells in the                  sample with an expression level of Oct4A in very                  small embryonic like stem cells in a control                  sample, where an increase in the expression level                  of Oct4A in very small embryonic like stem cells                  in the sample as compared to the expression level                  of Oct4A in very small embryonic like stem cells                  in the control sample indicates presence of                  cancer and (f) performing sequence-based assays                  on the nucleic acid and analyzing for mutation in                  at least one cancer-related marker, where the                  presence of mutation in the at least one                  cancer-related marker indicates presence of a                  specific type of cancer based on the                  cancer-related marker analyzed. The method (M6)                  involves (a) obtaining a sample from a subject,                  (b) enriching very small embryonic like stem                  cells from the sample to obtain a mixture                  comprising the very small embryonic like stem                  cells, (c) obtaining nucleic acid from the                  mixture of step (b), (d) performing an assay with                  the nucleic acid for analyzing expression level                  of Oct4A in very small embryonic like stem cells,                  (e) comparing the expression level of Oct4A in                  very small embryonic like stem cells in the                  sample with an expression level of Oct4A in a                  control sample, where an increase in the                  expression level of Oct4A in very small embryonic                  like stem cells in the sample as compared to the                  expression level of Oct4A in the control sample                  detects cancer and (f) administering anti-cancer                  therapy to the subject for treating cancer.                  Preferred Method: The method further involves                  analyzing the nucleic acid by performing                  sequence-based assays, where analyzing the                  nucleic acid by sequence-based assays detects the                  type of cancer. The increase in the expression                  level of Oct4A in the very small embryonic like                  stem cells from the sample is in the range of (a)                  5-10 folds as compared to the expression level of                  Oct4A in the control, (b) 10-15 folds as compared                  to the expression level of Oct4A in the control,                  (c) 15-20 folds as compared to the expression                  level of Oct4A in the control and (d) 20-25 folds                  as compared to the expression level of Oct4A in                  the control. The nucleic acid from the mixture is                  obtained by any one method chosen from (a)                  guanidinium thiocyanate-phenol-chloroform nucleic                  acid extraction, (b) cesium chloride gradient                  centrifugation method, (c) cetyl                  trimethylammonium bromide nucleic acid                  extraction, (d) alkaline extraction, (e)                  resin-based extraction and (f) solid phase                  nucleic acid extraction. The method of performing                  an assay with the nucleic acid for analyzing the                  expression of Oct4A is done by a technique chosen                  from quantitative PCR, flow cytometry and next                  generation sequencing (NGS). The control is the                  expression level of Oct4A in very small embryonic                  like stem cells obtained from a cancer-free                  subject. The method of enriching the very small                  embryonic like stem cells from a blood sample                  involves (a) contacting the blood sample with a                  neutral buffer in a ratio of 1:1-1:20 to obtain a                  first mixture, (b) contacting at least one salt                  solution to the first mixture in a ratio of                  1:2-1:10 to obtain a second mixture and (c)                  processing the second mixture to obtain enriched                  very small embryonic like stem cells, where the                  processing of the second mixture comprises at                  least one method chosen from (a) extraction                  process, (b) washing process, (c) centrifugation                  process and their combinations. The method of                  enriching the very small embryonic-like stem                  cells from the sample is by any method chosen                  from flow cytometry, magnetic bead-based                  separation, filtration, microfluidic-based cell                  sorting, aptamer-based cell isolation and                  buoyancy activated cell sorting. The method                  further comprises analyzing the expression level                  of the cancer-related marker in the nucleic acid                  obtained in step (c). The expression level of the                  marker is analyzed by using quantitative PCR                  techniques. The method is able to detect cancer                  without the intratumor heterogeneity. The method                  of co-relating the sequence profile with a                  reference sequence profile to identify the                  presence or absence of a mutation in the marker                  is done by an algorithm. The method of comparing                  the expression level of the biomarker of very                  small embryonic-like stem cell in the sample with                  an expression level of the at least one biomarker                  in a control sample and co relating the sequence                  profile with a reference sequence profile to                  identify the presence or absence of a mutation in                  at least one marker are done by an algorithm. The                  method encompasses all the organs of a human                  subject in identifying a medical condition. The                  method provides information equivalent to all                  organ biopsy. The method is an in-vitro method.                  Preferred Biomolecules: The reference is at least                  one chosen from (a) a sample obtained prior to                  administration of anti-cancer therapy, (b) a                  sample obtained at a previous time point as                  compared to the time point, (c) a sample obtained                  at a subsequent time point as compared to the                  time point and (d) a sample obtained from a                  cancer-free subject. The decrease in the                  expression level of Oct4A in very small embryonic                  like stem cells in the sample as compared to the                  expression level in the reference indicates a                  positive response to the anti-cancer therapy. The                  cancer-related marker is chosen from well-known                  markers established to be related to cancer. The                  method is independent of invasive techniques. The                  increase in the expression level of Oct4A in the                  very small embryonic like stem cells from the                  sample in the range of (a) 5-10 folds as compared                  to the expression level of Oct4A in the control                  indicates stage I of cancer, (b) 10-15 folds as                  compared to the expression level of Oct4A in the                  control indicates stage II of cancer, (c) 15-20                  folds as compared to the expression level of                  Oct4A in the control indicates stage III of                  cancer and (d) 20 and higher folds as compared to                  the expression level of Oct4A in the control                  indicates stage IV of cancer. TI Preparing a deoxyribonucleic acid fraction            enriched with circulating tumor DNA from a cancer            patient, where cancer is selected from bile duct            cancer, bladder cancer, bone cancer, and breast cancer,            involves obtaining afluid sample from cancer patient            following completion of cancer treatment.
AU WELKER N
   EVANS E A
   HAQUE I S
   CHU C S
   MAGUIRE J R
AE MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)
GA 202487171M
AB    NOVELTY - Preparing a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)                fraction enriched with circulating tumor DNA                (ctDNA) from a cancer patient, involves: (a)                obtaining a fluid sample from the cancer patient                following completion of a cancer treatment, wherein                the fluid sample comprises blood plasma or blood                serum; (b) extracting cell-free DNA fragments                (cfDNA) from the fluid sample; (c) enriching a                fraction of cfDNA corresponding to ctDNA by                contacting the cfDNA fragments with multiple                oligonucleotides, wherein multiple oligonucleotides                comprises at least 10 distinct oligonucleotides and                each of the at least 10 distinct oligonucleotides                comprises a nucleic acid sequence that is capable                of hybridizing to a DNA fragment comprising a                corresponding tumor-specific somatic mutation                sequence selected from a predetermined set of                tumor-specific somatic mutation sequences; and (d)                repeating the previous steps for one or more times                at different times to monitor progression of                disease.
   USE - Method for preparing a deoxyribonucleic acid                (DNA) fraction enriched with circulating tumor DNA                (ctDNA) from a cancer patient, where cancer is                selected from adrenal cancer, anal cancer, bile                duct cancer, bladder cancer, bone cancer, brain/CNS                tumor, breast cancer, Castleman disease, cervical                cancer, colon or rectum cancer, endometrial cancer,                esophagus cancer, a Ewing tumor, eye cancer,                gallbladder cancer, a gastrointestinal carcinoid                tumor, a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST),                gestational trophoblastic disease, Hodgkin disease,                Kaposi sarcoma, kidney cancer, laryngeal and                hypopharyngeal cancer, leukemia, liver cancer, lung                cancer, lymphoma, malignant mesothelioma, multiple                myeloma, myelodysplastic Syndrome, nasal cavity or                paranasal sinus cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer,                neuroblastoma, oral cavity or oropharyngeal cancer,                osteosarcoma, ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer,                penile cancer, pituitary tumor, prostate cancer,                retinoblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, salivary gland                cancer, skin cancer, small intestine cancer,                stomach cancer, testicular cancer, thymus cancer,                thyroid cancer, uterine sarcoma, vaginal cancer,                vulvar cancer, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and                Wilms tumor (claimed), and used in detection of an                individual subject's nucleic acid in a test nucleic                acid sample.
No biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method improve test specificity by                reducing sequence error generated during                amplification, and increases the number of copies                of a polynucleotide template sequence with the use                of a polymerase.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for method                for preparing a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)                fraction enriched with circulating tumor DNA                (ctDNA) from a cancer patient, which involves: (1)                obtaining a fluid sample from the cancer patient                while the cancer patient is in remission, wherein                the fluid sample comprises blood plasma or blood                serum; (2) extracting cell-free DNA fragments                (cfDNA) from the fluid sample; (3) enriching a                fraction of cfDNA corresponding to ctDNA by                contacting the cfDNA fragments with multiple                oligonucleotides, where multiple oligonucleotides                comprises 10 distinct oligonucleotides and each of                the 10 distinct oligonucleotides comprises a                nucleic acid sequence that is capable of                hybridizing to a DNA fragment comprising a                corresponding tumor-specific somatic mutation                sequence selected from a predetermined set of                tumor-specific somatic mutation sequences; and (d)                repeating the previous steos of one or more times                at different times to detect relapse following                remission.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The method preferably                  involves enriching the fraction of cfDNA                  corresponding to ctDNA, which comprises hybrid                  capture-based enrichment; (ii) PCR-target                  enrichment; or on-sequencer enrichment. The                  predetermined set of tumor-specific somatic                  mutation sequences is prepared by obtaining a                  tumor sample and a non-tumor sample from the                  cancer patient; sequencing genomic DNA from the                  tumor sample and sequencing genomic DNA from the                  non-tumor sample, thereby obtaining sequences of                  genomic DNA from the tumor sample and sequences                  of genomic DNA from the non-tumor sample; and                  aligning the sequences of genomic DNA from the                  tumor sample to a reference human genome that is                  not from the patient thereby obtaining a set of                  tumor-specific mutations and further obtaining                  from the set of tumor-specific mutations a set of                  tumor-specific somatic mutation sequences that                  are present in the sequences of genomic DNA from                  the tumor sample but not present in the sequences                  of genomic DNA from the non-tumor sample. The                  sequencing genomic DNA from the tumor sample of                  the patient and sequencing genomic DNA from the                  non-tumor sample of the patient comprises whole                  genome sequencing or targeted sequencing of                  exomes. The oligonucleotide comprises 50 distinct                  oligonucleotides capable of detecting 50                  different tumor-specific somatic mutations. The                  step of enriching the fraction of cfDNA                  corresponding to ctDNA comprises hybrid                  capture-based enrichment; PCR-target enrichment;                  or on-sequencer enrichment. The predetermined set                  of tumor-specific somatic mutation sequences is                  prepared by obtaining a tumor sample and a                  non-tumor sample from the cancer patient;                  sequencing genomic DNA from the tumor sample and                  sequencing genomic DNA from the non-tumor sample,                  and obtaining sequences of genomic DNA from the                  tumor sample and sequences of genomic DNA from                  the non-tumor sample; aligning the sequences of                  genomic DNA from the tumor sample to a reference                  human genome that is not from the patient and                  obtaining a set of tumor-specific mutations and                  further obtaining from the set of tumor-specific                  mutations a set of tumor-specific somatic                  mutation sequences that are present in the                  sequences of genomic DNA from the tumor sample                  but not present in the sequences of genomic DNA                  from the non-tumor sample. The sequencing of                  genomic DNA from the tumor sample of the patient                  and sequencing genomic DNA from the non-tumor                  sample of the patient comprises whole genome                  sequencing or targeted sequencing of exomes. The                  oligonucleotides comprise 50 distinct                  oligonucleotides capable of detecting at least 50                  different tumor-specific somatic mutations.Preferred Process: The method further                  involves sequencing the ctDNA, and obtaining                  multiple sequence reads; and detecting the                  presence or absence of a DNA fragment comprising                  any one of the set of tumor-specific somatic                  mutation sequences.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - None given.

   USE - For attaching to the skin area for absorption                of the ointment or of the active substance included                in the ointment (claimed) useful for detection and                treating cancer and protecting skin against                light.
   ADVANTAGE - The device shows even absorption of the                ointment or the active substance in the skin area                during the time of application of (6). (8)                holds amount of ointment appropriate to the                intended purpose, thus making it easier to dose the                ointment. (6) is made up of dimensionally stable                material that does not get compressed under normal                circumstances thus ensuring that (6) maintains its                shape and thus its function when (I) is used.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A device (I) containing ointment for attaching                to the skin area for absorption of the ointment or                of the active substance included in the ointment                comprises a surface structure (6) containing                depressions (8) between tops (7).    EXAMPLE - A test device comprising surface structure,                depression between tops was filled with                5-amino-levulenic acid (20%). A reference device in                which ointment was arranged in rectangular space in                the plaster was filled with an ointment (2 ml) in                even layer. In the test device the ointment (less                than 1 ml) was applied evenly by spatula so that                the depressions in the structure surface were                filled and the tops were visible. The test and the                reference devices were attached to the back of a                test subject and the ointment was allowed to act                for 3 hours. AB    NOVELTY - Determining (M1) a cell free epigenetic                instability index (cfEII) of a fluid sample                comprises cell-free DNA (cfDNA), comprises                determining a variance of methylation of many                sequencing reads of C-phosphate-G (CPG) sites in                CpG-islands (ReadVarCGI) of the cfDNA, where the                sequencing reads having fewer than 4 CpG sites are                excluded, and the sequencing reads comprises                sequencing reads of at least 15% CpG-islands as                given in table 1 of the specification, and the                variance represents the cfEII of the fluid                sample.
   USE - The method is useful for: determining a cfEII                of a fluid sample comprising cfDNA, where the fluid                sample comprises whole blood sample, a plasma                sample, a serum sample, a urine sample, a                cerebrospinal fluid sample, and a saliva sample,                the sample is obtained from a mammal, and the                mammal is a human; detecting ctDNA in a fluid                sample; assessing a mammal; and treating a mammal                having cancer, where the cancer comprises solid                tumors, breast cancer, a lung cancer, a liver                cancer, a colorectal cancer, a prostate cancer, a                brain cancer, a skin cancer, a head and neck                cancer, a pancreatic cancer, a genitourinary                cancer, a gynecologic cancer, a gastrointestinal                cancer, sarcomas, and a hepatobiliary cancer (all                claimed). The results showed that cancer treatment                exhibited AUC value of 0.87 (units not                defined).
   ADVANTAGE - The method: has the ability to determine                whether a mammal has cancer; and provides a unique                and unrealized opportunity for early cancer                detection in a sensitive, non-invasive assay and                high specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   detecting (M2) circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)                in a fluid sample comprising cfDNA obtained from a                mammal, comprising determining a cfEII of the                cfDNA, and identifying the cfDNA as comprising                ctDNA when the cfEII is greater than a cfEII of a                reference sample;

   treating (M4) a mammal having cancer,                comprising (a1) determining that a cfEII of a fluid                sample obtained from the mammal is greater than a                cfEII of a reference sample, and (b1) administering                a cancer treatment to the mammal; and
