(15) a method of diagnosing                cancer in a patient, comprising preparing tumour                cDNA and amplifying the tumour cDNA using primers                that specifically amplify a human telomerase                nucleic acid sequence, where the detection of                telomerase nucleic acid sequences is indicative of                a diagnosis of cancer; (16) a method of diagnosing                cancer in a patient, comprising determining a                pattern of telomerase RNA expression, comprising                amplifying telomerase from cDNA synthesised from                tumour RNA, and detecting the amplified product by                hybridisation with a ON having all or part of the                sequence of region 1, region &#945;, region                &#946;, region 2, region 3, region X or region                Y, thereby determining the pattern of telomerase                RNA expression from them, where the pattern is                indicative of a diagnosis of cancer; (17) a                non-human transgenic animal whose cells contain a                VT gene that is operably linked to a promoter for                the expression of the gene; (18) a mouse, whose                cells have an endogenous telomerase gene disrupted                by homologous recombination with a nonfunctional                telomerase gene, whereby the mouse is unable to                express endogenous telomerase; (19) an inhibitor of                VT activity, where the inhibitor binds to                telomerase and is not a nucleoside analogue, and                (20) a NAM comprising a sequence selected from                region 1, region &#945;, region &#946;,                region 2 or region 3 as given in the specification                and variants.
   USE - The products can be used for detection,                diagnosis and drug screening. Inhibitors of                telomerase activity can be used to treat cancers                such as melanomas, other skin cancers,                neuroblastomas, breast carcinomas, colon                carcinomas, leukeamias, lymphomas, osteosarcomas or                smooth muscle cell hyperplasias or skin growths.                Enhancers of telomerase may be used to stimulate                stem cell proliferation and differentiation                (expansion of haematopoietic stem cells could be                administered in the bone marrow transplant                context). As well, many tissues have stem cells.                Proliferation of these cells may be useful in wound                healing, hair growth, treatment of disease such as                Wilm's tumour, organ regeneration or                differentiation after injury or diseases, nerve                cell or brain cell growth following injury.

   USE - The method is useful for: detecting a target                nucleic acid sequence; and treating a subject                having a cancer, where the cancer comprises a solid                tumor, renal cell carcinoma, anal cancer, bladder                cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, cervical                cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer,                esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, glioblastoma,                glioma, kidney cancer, liver cancer, lung cancer,                lymphoma, melanoma, myeloma, neuroblastoma, ovarian                cancer, pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer,                sarcoma, skin cancer, thyroid cancer, urothelial                cancer, and/or uterine cancer (all claimed), or                diagnosing and treating a subject e.g. a subject                having a cancer. No biological data given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: improves rapid detection of a                target nucleic acid sequence using a Cas-cRNA                complex and a signal template; and is robust and                efficient strategy that ensures high analytical                sensitivity while maintaining sequence specificity,                a crucial capability for identifying scarce mRNA                targets using Cas activity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMs are also included                for:
   treating (M2) a subject having a cancer,                comprising detecting a level of the target nucleic                acid sequence in the sample according to the                method, comparing the level of the target nucleic                acid sequence in the sample to a reference level,                and administering a treatment if the level of the                target nucleic acid sequence in the sample is equal                to or higher than the reference level; and
   a kit comprising a CRISPR guide RNA (crRNA),                where the crRNA comprises a nucleic acid sequence                that is sufficiently complementary to a target                nucleic acid sequence, a signal template, the                signal template comprises a polymerase promoter                sequence, a RNA sequence comprising a Cas protein                cleavable sequence, and a DNA sequence that is                sufficiently complementary to the target nucleic                acid sequence, and the polymerase promoter sequence                comprises an acceptor moiety and the RNA sequence                comprises a donor moiety, or vice versa, and                instructions for performing the method (M2).

GA 2021C5862Q
AB    NOVELTY - An in vitro method for detecting                immunosuppressive fibroblasts in cancer sample from                subject suffering from cancer comprises detecting                Anthrax toxin receptor 1 (ANTXR1) positive                fibroblasts in the cancer sample from the patient,                where the presence of ANTXR1 positive (ANTXR1+)                fibroblasts is indicative of immunosuppressive                cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs).
   USE - The method is useful for in vitro detection of                immunosuppressive fibroblasts in cancer, preferably                prostate cancer, lung cancer, non-small cell lung                carcinoma (NSCLC), breast cancer, gastric cancer,                kidney cancer, ovarian cancer, hepatocellular                cancer, osteosarcoma, melanoma, hypopharynx cancer,                esophageal cancer, endometrial cancer, cervical                cancer, pancreatic cancer, liver cancer, colon or                colorectal cancer, adenocarcinoma, sarcoma,                non-Squamous cell carcinoma, Squamous cell                carcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors, muscle cancer,                adrenal cancer, thyroid cancer, uterine cancer,                skin cancer, melanoma, metastatic melanoma, bladder                cancer, head and neck cancer, preferably head and                neck cancer, breast cancer, ovary cancer, NSCLC,                melanoma and metastatic melanoma, more preferably                head and neck cancer, NSCLC, melanoma and                metastatic melanoma. The FAP inhibitor is useful in                the treatment of cancer in patient (all claimed).                Test details are described but no results                given.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   in vitro method for predicting a response of a                subject suffering from cancer to an immunotherapy                treatment, comprising detecting ANTXR1+fibroblasts                in a cancer sample from the patient, where the                ANTXR1+fibroblasts in the cancer sample are                predictive of the responsiveness of the patient to                an immunotherapeutic agent;
   use of immunotherapeutic agent in the                treatment of a cancer in a patient, where the                patient presents a cancer sample having (a) low                number or percentage of ANTXR1+fibroblasts, or (b)                no ANTXR1+fibroblasts;
   use of ANTXR1 as biomarker for the                identification of immunosuppressive fibroblasts,                preferably immunosuppressive CAFs;
   use of ANTXR1 in fibroblast populations,                preferably in CAFs populations, as biomarker in a                tumor of a subject suffering from cancer, for                predicting the response of the subject to an                immunotherapeutic agent;
   agent targeting ANTXR1+fibroblasts for use in                the treatment of cancer in patient, where the                patient has ANTXR1+fibroblast activation protein                positive (FAP+) fibroblasts, preferably CAFs, in a                tumor sample from the patient and the agent                suppresses or reduces the immunosuppressive action                of ANTXR1+fibroblasts, preferably the agent being                selected from the group consisting of (i) an                anti-ANTXR1 antibody optionally conjugated to a                cytotoxic drug, a multispecific molecule comprising                an anti-ANTXR1 moiety, an anti-ANTXR1 T cell                receptor (TCR) and an anti-ANTXR1 chimeric antigen                receptor (CAR), and (ii) an immune cell, preferably                a T cell or a natural killer cell, expressing an                anti-ANTXR1 TCR or an anti-ANTXR1 CAR;
   FAP inhibitor in the treatment of cancer in                patient, where the patient has                ANTXR1+FAP+fibroblasts, preferably CAFs, in a tumor                sample from the patient; and
   product or kit comprising (a) an agent                targeting ANTXR1+fibroblasts, and (b) an                immunotherapeutic agent, as a combined preparation                for simultaneous, separate or sequential use in the                treatment of a cancer in a patient, where the                patient has ANTXR1+FAP+fibroblasts, preferably                CAFs, in a tumor sample from the patient.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: The ANTXR1+fibroblasts                  are FAP+ANTXR1+fibroblasts and ANTXR1+CAFs,                  preferably FAP+ANTXR1+CAFs. The                  ANTXR1+fibroblasts are: FAP+ANTXR1+LAM P5                  SDC1+fibroblasts, preferably CAFs;                  FAP+ANTXR1+LAMP5+SDC1+/-fibroblasts, preferably                  CAFs; or ANTXR1+SDC1 LAMP5 CD9+fibroblasts,                  preferably CAFs. The ANTXR1+fibroblasts are                  FAP+ANTXR1+LAM P5 SDC1+fibroblasts, preferably                  CAFs, FAP+ANTXR1+LAMP5+SDC1+/-fibroblasts,                  preferably CAFs, and ANTXR1+SDC1 LAMP5                  CD9+fibroblasts, preferably CAFs. The agent                  targeting ANTXR1+fibroblasts/FAP inhibitor is in                  combination with an immunotherapeutic agent. The                  FAP inhibitor is talabostat, PT-100,                  Tradjenta(RTM: Linagliptin), FAP inhibitors with                  N-(4-quinolinoyl)-Gly-(2-cyanopyrrolidine)                  scaffold, e.g. FAPI-02, FAPI-04 and FAPI-46, a                  peptide-targeted radionuclide e.g. FAP-2286. The                  immunotherapeutic agent is a agent that                  stimulates the patient's immune system to attack                  the malignant tumor cells, immunization of the                  patient with tumoral antigens, molecules                  stimulating the immune system e.g. cytokines,                  therapeutic antibodies, adoptive T cell therapy,                  CAR cell therapy, immune checkpoint inhibitor,                  preferably an immune checkpoint inhibitor. The                  checkpoint inhibitor is an antibody directed                  against cytotoxic T lymphocyte associated protein                  (CTLA-4), programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1),                  programmed cell death ligand (PD-L1), T cell                  immunoreceptor with immunoglobulin (Ig) and ITIM                  domains (TIGIT), Lymphocyte-activation gene 3                  (LAG-3), T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin-domain                  containing-3 (TIM-3), B- and T-lymphocyte                  attenuator (BLTA), indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1                  (IDO1), preferably an antibody directed against                  CTLA-4, PD-1, PD-L1 and TIGIT, more preferably an                  antibody directed against PD-1 or CTLA-4. The                  immunotherapeutic agent is ipilimumab, nivolumab,                  BGB-A317, pembrolizumab, atezolizumab, avelumab,                  or durvalumab, BMS-986016, and epacadostat.                  Preferred Method: The method for predicting the                  response of a subject comprises determining the                  percentage of ANTXR1+fibroblasts and the                  percentage of ANTXR1+fibroblasts is the number of                  ANTXR1+fibroblasts on the total number of                  fibroblasts in the cancer sample or on the total                  number of cells in the cancer sample.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - FAP inhibitor; Immune checkpoint                inhibitor.

AB    NOVELTY - Drug delivery system that is a composition,                comprises microalgae extracellular vesicles (MEVs)                formulated for administration by oral, intravenous,                intratracheal, intramuscular or intranasal                delivery, or inhalation into lungs, the MEVs are                formulated to deliver a bioactive cargo to a target                tissue or immune system, the MEVs comprise the                bioactive cargo. The MEVs comprise one or more                bioactive agents as cargo for delivery.
   USE - The drug delivery system or composition is                useful for treatment or prevention of disease,                disorder, or condition chosen from cancer, a                genetic disorder, a liver disease, a disease                involving the immune system or an immune cell, an                infectious disease, a respiratory disease, a lung                disease, and a neurodegenerative disease, a                gastrointestinal disease, and a brain cancer or                involving internal organs, urogenital organs,                cardiovascular system and associated organs and                tissues, hematopoietic or lymphoid tissues, sensory                organs and tissues, urogenital organs and tissues,                muscle tissues, bones, and/or endocrine tissues and                treating, detecting, diagnosing, or monitoring                treatment of a disease, disorder, or condition of                the brain or involving the brain, CNS or nervous                system. The disease or condition involves an                infectious agent that is a bacterium, virus,                oomycete, or fungus. The internal organs comprise                the pancreas, liver, and/or spleen. The disease,                disorder or condition is a neurodegenerative                disease (such as Parkinson's), or a cognitive                disorder (such as dementia), or a brain disorder                (such as encephalitis), or a nervous system                disorder (such as pain), or a genetic disease (such                as cystic fibrosis), or a multifactorial disease                (such as diabetes), or cancer (such as cancer of                the breast, or ovaries, or bowel, or prostate, or                skin, or other cancer), or high blood pressure, or                high cholesterol, or schizophrenia, or bipolar                disorder, or arthritis, or a metabolic disease                ((such as Gaucher disease), or Niemann-Pick                disease, or phenylketonuria (PKU), or porphyria, or                Tay-Sachs disease, or Wilson's disease, or other                metabolic disease), or a disease of the respiratory                system (such as asthma), or a disease of the                digestive tract (such as irritable bowel syndrome                (IBS)), or a disease of the mucosa (such as                Behcet's disease), or a disease of the muscular or                neuromuscular tissues (such as amyotrophic lateral                sclerosis (ALS)), or a disease of the bones (such                as osteoporosis), or a disease of the endocrine                tissue (such as acromegaly), or primary                hyperparathyroidism, or other disease of the                endocrine tissue, or a disease of hemopoietic or                lymphoid tissues (such as Fanconi anemia), or                lymphoma, or Hodgkin's lymphoma, or non-Hodgkin's                lymphoma, or lymphadenitis, or lymphangitis, or                lymphedema, or lymphocytosis (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The composition readily delivers conveniently                produced EVs to cells and tissues and is                safe.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for delivering a bioactive agent to                the immune system, involves orally administering a                composition comprising MEVs that comprise a                bioactive agent as cargo;
   a method of treatment or prevention of a                disease, disorder, or condition, involves                administering the drug delivery system or                composition;
   a method of cell therapy, involves                administering a composition of cells; and
   a method for delivery of bioactive molecules                into cells in vitro, involves introducing a                composition comprising MEVs containing the                bioactive cargo into a cell in vitro for cell                therapy, diagnostics, and/or detection, where the                bioactive molecule is any molecule that can effect                treatment of a disease, disorder, or condition, or                that can be used to detect a disease, disorder, or                condition, or that can be used to monitor treatment                of a disease, disorder, or condition and the                bioactive molecule is heterologous to the                microalgae and/or the MEVs.

TI DNA specific for Multiple Tumour Suppressor            1E1-beta gene are useful for the diagnosis of cancers            related to MTS1E1-beta mutation(s) and their            treatment.
AU KAMB A
AE MYRIAD GENETICS INC (MYRI-C)
GA 1998250421
AB    NOVELTY - A new DNA molecule (I) comprises a 1131base                pair human cDNA sequence, as given in the                specification, of Multiple Tumour Suppression gene                1E 1&#946; (MTS1E1&#946;).
Also claimed is:
(1) a DNA molecule (II) comprising at least 15                consecutive nucleotides of exon 1, exon 1 being                defined as bases 1 to 334 of (I);
(2) a pair of single-stranded primers for                determining the nucleotide sequence of                MTS1E1&#946; by polymerase chain reaction                (PCR), where the sequence of the primers are                derived from human chromosome 9p21 and results in                the synthesis of DNA defined as exon 1;
(3) a nucleic acid probe complementary to                human wild type MTS1E1&#946; gene exon 1;
(4) a cloning vector comprising (I) or (II)                and a replicon operative in a host cell; and
(5) a recombinant host cell transformed with                (4).
   USE - The MTS1E1&#946; gene locus is also                referred to as the familial melanoma (MLM) gene                locus, located on human chromosome 9p21. Mutations                in this locus have been found to lead to for an                increased risk of skin cancer of up to 50 times.                MTS1E1&#946; gene product is thought to be a                cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (cdk4) inhibitor in the                cell cycle. (I) and the probes are useful for                detection of mutations in MTS1E1&#946; in the                diagnosis of predisposition to cancers, e.g.                melanoma, leukaemia, astrocytoma, gliboblastoma,                lymphoma, glioma, Hodgkin's lymphoma, CLL, and                cancers of the pancreas, breast, thyroid, ovary,                uterus, testis, kidney, stomach and rectum. They                are also useful for the therapy of cancers related                to mutations in MTS1E1&#946; gene.
   ADVANTAGE - The polynucleotides and their derivatives are                specific for MTS1E1&#946;. This is an                alternative form of MTS1 containing an Exon                1&#946; (different to Exon 1 of MTS1) and Exons                2 and 3 of MTS1.

AE SHANGHAI JIAAO INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHAN-Non-standard)
GA 2021B8582H
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves performing pathologic,                digital image processing and related work of                glomerular identification. Hardening and unknown                glomerulus and other glomerules are selected to                prepare a data set. Glomerular is processed by                means of changing loss. The glomerule is classified                according to a type distribution and a visual                characteristic of the glomerul. The glomerular                detection data set is divided into a training set                and a verification set. The verification set is                classified into coarse classification according to                the accuracy, normal, mild and moderate fine                classification, hardening and lunar body                classification.
   USE - Method for recognizing and classifying                pathology image based on glomerular in clinical                medical image analysis. Uses include but are not                limited to thyroid cancer screening, skin cancer                diagnosis, abnormal screening of eyeground image,                prediction of gene mutation.
   ADVANTAGE - The pathological image identification and                classification method solves the problem that the                glomerular of similar category is difficult to be                distinguished. The training and testing of each                stage, respectively is designed with corresponding                data set, so that each stage can more efficiently                exert the corresponding performance. The method                uses two-stage target detection algorithm,                obtaining high detection accuracy and positioning                precision.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   (1) a pathological image recognition and                classification system based on glomerular;                and
   (2) a computer-readable storage medium                comprising a set of instructions for recognizing                and classifying pathology image based on                glomerular.

TI Object information acquiring apparatus i.e.            photoacoustic imaging apparatus, for acquiring image of            human breast for diagnosis of breast cancer, has            holding plate, and discerning unit discerning contact            state between plate and object.
AU OYAMA K
AE CANON KK (CANO-C)
   CANON KK (CANO-C)
GA 2013D34208
AB    NOVELTY - The apparatus has a holding plate (102A) for                holding an object (101). An ultrasonic probe                detects acoustic wave propagated from inside of the                object irradiated with measurement light and                converts the wave into an electric signal. An image                processor (120) generates an image inside the                object from the signal. A photodetector i.e.                optical sensor, detects light reflected by a                peripheral part as a region of the object that does                not come into contact with the plate. A discerning                unit (109) discerns a contact state between the                plate and the object using detection result of the                photodetector.
   USE - Object information acquiring apparatus i.e.                photoacoustic imaging apparatus, for acquiring a                tomographic image of breast of a human or animal                for diagnosis of breast cancer. Can also be used                for acquiring hands and feet or fingers of the                human for diagnosis of skin cancer, malignant tumor                and blood vessel disease.
   ADVANTAGE - The apparatus holds the object by the holding                plate, so that the region of the peripheral part is                discerned, thus ensuring quantitativeness of                photoacoustic measurement of the object. The                apparatus attaches acoustic matching material to a                surface of the probe so as to improve detection                efficiency of the wave. The apparatus enables                placing a light source at a side of the object and                performing the measurement of the object by the                irradiation of the measurement light from the side,                thus improving measurement depth and obtaining the                photoacoustic image with high contrast and high                image quality. The apparatus enables repeatedly                performing object measurement process at same                position of the object and averaging processes so                as to reduce system noise, thus improving                signal-noise ratio of a photoacoustic wave                signal.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The wave is elastic wave, sound wave,                ultrasonic wave or photo-ultrasonic wave. An                INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for an object                information acquiring method.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of a                photoacoustic imaging system.

AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing whether a subject has, or is at                risk for developing, a cancer linked to a                cancer-associated chromosomal feature, comprises                evaluating the status in the subject of at least                one mIR gene located in close proximity to the                cancer-associated chromosomal feature.
   USE - The miR, composition, and method are useful                for diagnosing and treating a cancer-associated                chromosomal feature, where the cancer is bladder                cancer, esophageal cancer, lung cancer, stomach                cancer, kidney cancer, cervical cancer, ovarian                cancer, breast cancer, lymphoma, Ewing sarcoma,                hematopoietic tumors, solid tumors, gastric cancer,                colorectal cancer, brain cancer, epithelial cancer,                nasopharyngeal cancer, uterine cancer, hepatic                cancer, head-and-neck cancer, renal cancer, male                germ cell tumors, malignant mesothelioma,                myelodysplastic syndrome, pancreatic or biliary                cancer, prostate cancer, thyroid cancer, urothelial                cancer, renal cancer, Wilm's tumor, small cell lung                cancer, melanoma, skin cancer, osteosarcoma,                neuroblastoma, leukemia (acute lymphocytic                leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, chronic                lymphocytic leukemia), glioblastoma multiforme,                medulloblastoma, lymphoplasmacytoid lymphoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, B-cell chronic lymphocytic                leukemia, or B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia                associated with an unmutated IgVH gene, ZAP-70                expression, CD38 expression, a deletion at                chromosome 11q23, a loss or mutation of TP53 or                their combination.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Diagnosing whether a subject has, or is at                risk for developing, a cancer linked to a                cancer-associated chromosomal feature, comprising                evaluating the status in the subject of at least                one mIR gene located in close proximity to the                cancer-associated chromosomal feature, provided the                miR gene is not miR-15 or miR-16, by:
   measuring in a test sample from the subject                the level of at least one miR gene product from the                mIR gene in the test sample, where an alteration in                the level of mIR gene product in the test sample                relative to the level of corresponding miR gene                product in a control sample is indicative of the                subject either having, or being at risk for                developing, the cancer;
   analyzing the at least one miR gene in the                test sample for a deletion, mutation or                amplification, where detection of a deletion,                mutation and/or amplification in the miR gene as                compared to the corresponding mIR gene in the                control sample is indicative of the subject either                having, or being at risk for developing, the                cancer; and/or
   measuring the copy number of the at least one                miR gene in the test sample, where a copy number                other than two for an miR gene on a somatic                chromosome or sex chromosome in a female, or other                than one for an miR gene on a sex chromosome in a                male, is indicative of the subject either having,                or being at risk for developing, the cancer.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for a                pharmaceutical composition comprising an isolated                miR gene product or a nucleic acid encoding an                isolated miR gene product from an miR gene located                in close proximity to a cancer-associated                chromosomal feature and is not miR15 or miR16, and                a pharmaceutical carrier; and a method of treating                cancer associated with a cancer-associated                chromosomal feature in a subject.

or (ii)                  when the at least one isolated miR gene product                  is up-regulated in the cancer cells,                  administering to the subject an amount of at                  least one compound for inhibiting expression of                  the at least one miR gene, such that                  proliferation of cancer cells in the subject is                  inhibited.Alternatively, the method comprises                  determining the amount of miR gene product                  expressed from at least one miR gene located in                  close proximity to the cancer-associated                  chromosomal feature in cancer cells from a                  subject, relative to control cells, and altering                  the amount of miR gene product expressed in the                  cancer cells by:(i) administering to the subject an amount                  of at least one isolated miR gene product from                  the miR gene, provided that the miR gene product                  is not miR15 or miR16, if the amount of the miR                  gene product expressed in the cancer cells is                  less than amount of the miR gene product                  expressed in control cells, or(ii) administering to the subject an amount                  of at least one compound for inhibiting                  expression of the at least one miR gene, if the                  amount of the miR gene product expressed in the                  cancer cells is greater than the amount of the                  miR gene product expressed in control cells, such                  that proliferation of cancer cells in the subject                  is inhibited.The isolated miR gene product is                  administered parenterally or enterally. The                  isolated miR gene product is administered by                  transfection of cells of the subject. The                  isolated miR gene product is administered as                  naked RNA, in conjunction with a nucleic acid                  delivery reagent, or as a nucleic acid comprising                  a sequence that expresses the miR gene product,                  where the nucleic acid delivery reagent comprises                  a recombinant plasmid, recombinant viral vector,                  or a liposome.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene Therapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - Dosage is 5-3000 &#956;g/kg by oral,                rectal, intranasal, inhalation, or parenteral                including intravascular, intravenous,                intraarterial, intratumoral, intraretinal, or                subcutaneous means.

AB    NOVELTY - A polypeptide comprising specific amino acid                sequences is new.
   USE - For detecting the presence of cancer in a                mammal; for treating or preventing cancer in a                mammal (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The polypeptides and proteins that                specifically binds to and immunologically recognize                CD276; elicit an antigen-specific response against                CD276; targets and destroys CD276-expressing cancer                cells, reduces or eliminates cancer cells,                facilitates infiltration of immune cells and/or                effector molecules to tumor site(s), and                enhances/extends anti-cancer responses. The cancer                includes pharynx cancer, prostate cancer, rectal                cancer, renal cancer, skin cancer, small intestine                cancer, soft tissue cancer, solid tumors, stomach                cancer, testicular cancer, thyroid cancer, and                ureter cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A polypeptide comprising [SEQ ID NO: 1] to                [SEQ ID NO: 6], [SEQ ID NO: 11] to [SEQ ID NO: 16],                or [SEQ ID NO: 20] to [SEQ ID NO: 25] as available                on WIPO website (Sequences not defined here may be                found at ftp://ftp.wipo.int/pub/published pct                sequences/publication) is new. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS                are included for the following:
   a protein comprising a first polypeptide chain                comprising the [SEQ ID NO: 1] to [SEQ ID NO: 3],                [SEQ ID NO: 11] to [SEQ ID NO: 13], or [SEQ ID NO:                20] to [SEQ ID NO: 22] and second polypeptide chain                comprising the [SEQ ID NO: 4] to [SEQ ID NO: 6],                [SEQ ID NO: 14] to [SEQ ID NO: 16], or [SEQ ID NO:                23] to [SEQ ID NO: 25];
   a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising                an antigen binding domain comprising the                polypeptide or the protein; transmembrane domain,                and intracellular T cell signaling domain;
   an anti-cluster of differentiation 276 (CD276)                binding moiety comprising the polypeptide or the                protein, where the CD276 binding moiety is an                antibody, fragment antigen binding (Fab), F(ab')2                fragment, diabody, triabody, tetrabody,                single-chain variable region fragment (scFv), or                disulfide-stabilized variable region fragment                (dsFv);
   a conjugate comprising the polypeptide, the                protein, the CAR, or the anti-CD276 binding moiety,                conjugated to effector molecule;
   a nucleic acid comprising a nucleotide                sequence encoding the polypeptide, the protein, the                CAR, the anti-CD276 binding moiety or the                conjugate;
   a recombinant expression vector comprising the                nucleic acid;
   an isolated host cell comprising the                recombinant expression vector;
   a population of cells comprising the host                cell; and
   detecting the presence of cancer in a mammal                involving: contacting a sample comprising at least                one cell from the mammal with the polypeptide, the                protein, the CAR, the anti-CD276 binding moiety,                the conjugate, the nucleic acid, the recombinant                expression vector, the isolated host cell, or the                population of cells, thus forming a complex, and                detecting the complex, where detection of the                complex is indicative of the presence of cancer in                the mammal.

AB    NOVELTY - Treatment of cancer in a patient involves                modulating the level of an expression product of                SEMA4D (a 150 kDa surface antigen that belongs to                the semaphoring family) or modulating an                SEMA4D-activity selected from cell proliferation,                cell growth, cell motility, metastasis, cell                migration, cell survival, and tumorigenicity.
   USE - For treating cancer e.g. melanoma, breast                cancer, colon cancer, kidney cancer, liver cancer,                lung cancer, ovary cancer, pancreatic cancer,                prostate cancer, uterine cancer, cervical cancer,                bladder cancer, stomach cancer or skin cancer in a                patient having overexpression of SEMA4D activity                relative to the control (Claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method inhibits tumor growth or the                reduction of tumour volume; and reduces the                invasiveness of a cancer cell.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method (M3) of diagnosing cancer involving                detecting evidence of differential expression in a                patient sample of SEMA4D. The evidence of                differential expression of SEMA4D is diagnostic of                cancer;
   a method (M4) for detecting a cancerous cell                in a patient sample involving detecting evidence of                an expression product of SEMA4D. The evidence of                expression of SEMA4D in the sample indicates that a                cell in the sample is cancerous;
   a method (M5) of assessing the progression of                cancer in a patient involving comparing the level                of an expression product of SEM A4D in a biological                sample at a first time point to a level of the same                expression product at a second time point. A change                in the level of the expression product at the                second time point relative to the first time point                is indicative of the progression of the                cancer;
   a method (M6) of screening for anti-cancer                activity involving:
   contacting a cell that expresses SEMA4D with a                candidate anti-cancer agent; and;
   detecting at least a two fold difference                between the level of SEMA4D expression in the cell                in the presence and in the absence of the candidate                anti-cancer agent. At least a two fold difference                indicates that the candidate anti-cancer agent has                anti-cancer activity;
   a method (M7) of identifying a patient as                susceptible to treatment with an antibody that                binds to an expression product of SEMA4D involving                measuring the level of the expression product of                the gene in a biological sample from that                patient;
   a kit for the diagnosis or detection of cancer                in a mammal comprising an antibody or its fragment                or an immunoconjugate or its fragment. The antibody                or fragment specifically binds an SEMA4D tumor cell                antigen; one or more reagents for detecting a                binding reaction between the antibody and the                SEMA4D tumor cell antigen; and optionally                instructions for using the kit;
   a kit for diagnosing cancer comprising a                nucleic acid probe that hybridizes to an SEMA4D                gene; primers for amplifying the SEMA4D gene; and                optionally instructions for using the kit;
   a composition comprising at least one antibody                or oligonucleotides specific for an expression                product of SEMA4D.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The control in the                  diagnosing cancer is a known normal tissue of the                  same tissue type as in the patient sample.Preferred Cells: The cell is a breast cell,                  colon cell, kidney cell, liver cell, lung cell,                  lymphatic cell, ovary cell, pancreas cell,                  prostate cell, uterine cell, cervical cell,                  bladder cell, stomach cell or skin cell.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method of treatment                  involves administering to the patient, an                  antibody, a nucleic acid, or a polypeptide that                  modulates the level of the SEMA4D expression                  product. The expression level of the expression                  product is upregulated or downregulated by at                  least a 2-fold change. The level of the                  expression product at a first time point is                  compared to the level of the same expression                  product at a second time point and an increase in                  level of the expression product at the second                  time point relative to the first time point is                  indicative of the progression of cancer. In (M3),                  the evidence of differential expression is                  detected by measuring the level of an expression                  product of SEMA4D. The level of expression of                  protein is measured using an antibody which                  specifically binds to an SEMA4D polypeptide. The                  antibody is linked to an imaging agent. The level                  of expression product of the SEMA4D gene in the                  patient sample is compared to a control. The                  level of the expression product in the sample is                  increased relative to the control. In (M4), the                  evidence of the expression product is detected                  using an antibody linked to an imaging agent. In                  (M6), the at least a three fold difference                  between the level of SEMA4D expression in the                  cell in the presence and in the absence of the                  candidate anticancer agent indicates that the                  candidate anti-cancer agent has anti-cancer                  activity. Alternatively the method of diagnosis                  of cancer selected from cervical cancer, kidney                  cancer, ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer and                  skin cancer, involves:measuring a level of mRNA of SEMA4D in a                  first sample comprising a first tissue type of a                  first individual; andcomparing the level of mRNA in (a) to a                  level of the mRNA in a second sample comprising a                  normal tissue type of the first individual, or a                  level of the mRNA in a third sample the third                  sample comprising a normal tissue type from an                  unaffected individual. At least a two (preferably                  at least three) fold difference between the level                  of mRNA in the step (a) and the level of the mRNA                  in the second sample or the third sample                  indicates that the first individual has or is                  predisposed to cancer.Preferred Components: The expression product                  is a protein or mRNA. The antibody is a                  neutralizing antibody; a monoclonal antibody that                  binds to an SEMA4D polypeptide with an affinity                  of at least 1x10 8Ka; a polyclonal antibody; a                  chimeric antibody; a human antibody; a humanized                  antibody; a single-chain antibody; a bi-specific                  antibody; a multi-specific antibody; or a Fab                  fragment. The nucleotide has a sequence                  containing 4157 nucleotides as given in the                  specification (SEQ ID No:7). The monoclonal                  antibody inhibits at least one of cancer cell                  growth, tumor formation, cell survival and cancer                  cell proliferation. The candidate anti-cancer                  agent is an antibody, small organic compound,                  small inorganic compound, or polynucleotide. The                  polynucleotide is an antisense oligonucleotide.                  The at least one oligonucleotide has a sequence                  of SEQ ID NO. 7.Preferred Composition: The composition                  further comprises a conventional cancer                  medicament; and an excipient.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - SEMA4D modulator.
   ADMINISTRATION - The dosage of the pharmaceutical composition                containing the modulator is 0.01 - 50 (preferably                0.01 - 5 or 0.05 - 10) mg/kg. The administration is                by intravenous, intramuscular, intra-arterial,                intramedullary, intrathecal, intraventricular,                transdermal or transcutaneous, subcutaneous,                intraperitoneal, intranasal, enteral, topical,                sublingual, intravaginal, oral or rectal                route.
   EXAMPLE - Rat 1 stable cell lines were grown in two T150                flasks to 70-80% confluency. The cells were                trypsinized, washed twice in phosphate buffered                saline (PBS), and resuspended with PBS to 10 , 10 ,                and 10 cells/ml. The cell suspension was kept on                ice until injection into mice. Female NOD                CB17-Prkdcscid J mice (3 - 5 weeks of age) were                housed 4 per cage in an isolator unit. Using a 25                gauge needle, mice were injected with 0.1 ml cell                suspension subcutaneously in the thoracic region (2                sites per mouse). Once a tumor began to form, tumor                growth was measured twice per week. The tumor was                measured in two directions, rostral-caudal and                medial-lateral. Measurements were recorded as width                length and the tumor volume was calculated. The                results of the tumorgenicity assay for SEMA4D                showed that the code SGRS038 represented cells that                had been transformed with the gene coding for                SEMA4D. In vivo tumour growth was markedly                increased relative to control in cells transformed                with the gene coding for SEMA4D. The tumorigenicity                assays confirm that this gene was an                oncogene.

PT P
PN AU2003235005-A8
TI New probe for distinguishing between functional and non-functional P2X7 receptors, for detecting cancer of breast, skin, or lung, human immunodeficiency virus or Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, or irritable bowel syndrome.
AU GIDLEY-BAIRD A
   BARDEN J
AE INTREAT PTY LTD (INTR-Non-standard)
GA 2004526113
AB    NOVELTY - A probe (I) for detection of a disease or condition, the probe being adapted to distinguish between functional P2X7 receptors and non-functional P2X7 receptors, is new.
   USE - (I) is useful for detecting a disease or condition, which involves providing a receptor expression profile, and comparing the receptor expression profile with that of a normal profile. The receptor expression profile is a proportion of non-functional P2X7 receptors to total P2X7 receptors, and a higher proportion of non-functional receptors to total P2X7 receptors in the receptor expression profile relative to the normal profile indicates the presence of the disease or condition. The receptor expression profile is that of non-functional receptors. The part includes a P2X7 monomer. The receptor expression profile is provided using in situ imaging techniques. The receptor expression profile is provided using microscopy, confocal microscopy or fluorescence activated cell sorting. (II), (III), (IV) and PC is useful for treating or preventing a disease or condition. The disease or condition includes cancer of prostate, breast, skin, lung, cervis, uterus, stomach, oesophagus, bladder, colon and vaginal cancers, other epithelial cell cancers, malignant lymphoma, other blood cancers, irritable bowel syndrome and infection by a virus or other pathological organism. The virus or organism is HIV or Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The condition is irritable bowel syndrome, and the antibody is capable of detecting other regions of the P2X7 receptor unchanged by functional state by detecting an epitope common to both functional and non-functional conformations. (M2) is useful for treating irritable bowel syndrome (all claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the following:
   (1) an isolated cell or tissue sample (II) complexed with (I);
   (2) diagnosing (M1) irritable bowel syndrome, involves detecting P2X7 expression profile of cells and/or tissue, and comparing the profile with a predetermined expression profile of normal cells and/or tissue;
   (3) treating (M2) irritable bowel syndrome, the involves administering a composition adapted to restore P2X7 receptor function;
   (4) an antibody (II) adapted to distinguish between functional P2X7 receptors and non-functional P2X7 receptors and to bind only to non-functional receptors;
   (5) an epitope (III) adapted to cause the generation of (II);
   (6) an isolated polypeptide comprising a segment of a P2X7 receptor of 30 amino acids including Gly200 to Cys216, or Gly200 to Thr215;
   (7) a pharmaceutical composition (PC) for treating or preventing a disease or condition in a patient, comprising (II) or (III), to cause the generation of such an amount, capable of regulating programmed cell death of cells having expressed on their surface aberrant or non-functional P2X7 receptors;
   (8) preparation (IV) for treatment or prevention of a disease or condition in a patient, comprising one or more substances adapted to regulate the expression of ATPases or ATPDases that control the supply of ATP to P2X7 receptors in the patient's cells or tissue;
   (9) a test kit (V) for detecting non-functional P2X7 receptors, comprising (I) and (II) with a normal P2X7 receptor expression profile; and
   (10) a diagnostic kit (VI) comprising a probe that specifically binds to an epitope within and outside the residues Gly200 to Cys216 of a P2X7 receptor without specifically binding to other regions of the P2X7 receptor or epitope Gly200 to Cys216 of a P2X7 receptor.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Probe: In (I), the probe is adapted to distinguish between functional P2X7 receptors and non-functional P2X7 receptors by detecting change in relation to binding of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to the receptors, by detecting change in binding of one or more proteins necessary for pore formation in P2X7 receptors or by detecting one or more parts of the receptor exposed in the absence of bound ATP. The part includes a P2X7 monomer. (I) is natural or artificial. (I) is an antibody such as polyclonal antibody, a monoclonal antibody, a recombinant antibody, a humanized antibody, a human antibody and their fragments. The antibody is directed against an epitope of each receptor located in an extracellular domain adjacent to a site for binding ATP. The receptors are mammalian P2X7 receptors and the probe is adapted to distinguish between functional receptors having a sequence in which proline at amino acid 210 or 199 is in the trans-conformation and non-functional receptors having a sequence in which the proline at amino acid 210 or 199 is in the cis-conformation acting to alter local protein structure. (I) is or includes an antibody raised against an epitope sequence of the P2X7 receptor extending from Gly200 to Cys216 or Thr215. The epitope is Val65-Lys81. (I) is an antibody that specifically binds to an epitope within residues Gly200 to Cys2116 of a P2X7 receptor without specifically binding to other regions of P2X7 receptor. The antibody is used in combination with a second antibody capable of detecting total P2X7 expression. (I) specifically binds to an epitope outside residues Gly200 to Cys216 of a P2X7 receptor without specifically binding to an epitope within Gly200 to Cys216 of the P2X7 receptor.Preferred Method: In (M1), the cells and/or tissues are intestinal cells or tissue. The detection of the P2X7 expression profile includes use of one or more antibodies.Preferred Epitope: (III) is attached to diphtheria toxin through the C-terminal Cys residue by means of the chemical cross-linker maleimidocaproyl-N-hydroxysuccinimide (MCS), so that the conformation adopted by the attached epitope peptide occupies a stable cis-proline configuration.Preferred Antibody: (II) is a chimeric antibody, humanized or human antibody and their fragments. (II) is combined with a radiolabel suitable for detection by use of scanning technology. The scanning technology is positron emission tomography. (II) is combined with a fluorescent label suitable for use in flow cytometry. (II) is combined with a matrix suitable for colorimetric assay.Preferred Kit: (V) is adapted to detect non-functional P2X7 receptors in a blood sample. In (VI), the ATPases and ATPDases are chosen from CD39 and CD73. The one or more substances is one or more ATP analogs.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Anti HIV; Antiinflammatory; Gastrointestinal-Gen.; Antibacterial; Tuberculostatic; Antitubercular. The ability of antibodies raised against the non-functional epitope of the P2X7 receptor to inhibit tumor formation in vivo, was tested as follows. Three groups of 10 Balb-c female mice each received the following treatments. Group 1: 10 mice each injected intraperitoneally (IP) with 1x10 to the power of 6 hybridoma cells in 0.5 ml of cell culture medium on day 1. On days 2 and 3, they received an IP injection of 0.5 ml of cell culture medium. Group 2: 10 mice each injected IP with 1x10 to the power of 6 hybridoma cells in 0.5 ml of cell culture medium containing 1 mg of purified sheep IgG on day 1. On days 2 and 3, they were injected with 0.5 ml of cell culture medium containing 1 mg of purified sheep IgG. Group 3: 10 mice each injected IP with 1x10 to the power of 6 hybridoma cells in 0.5 ml of cell culture medium containing 1 mg of purified sheep anti-P2X7 non-functional epitope IgG on day 1. On days 2 and 3, they received a further injection of 0.5 ml of cell culture medium containing 1 mg of purified sheep anti- P2X7 IgG. Mice from all groups were killed on day 11 and examined for the presence of tumor. The tumors were excised on weighed. Results showed that 9 out of 10 mice had tumors (in control 1, with mean tumor weight per mice (g) of 3.98 / 1.1), 10 out of 10 mice had tumors (in control 2, with mean tumor weight per mice (g) of 2.93 / 0.9), 9 out of 10 mice had tumors (in experimental group, with mean tumor weight per mice (g) of 1.13 / 0.4). An analysis of variance showed a significant different in tumor weight between the groups (probability P less than 0.01). The experimental group treated with the anti- P2X7 non-functional antibodies was significantly different (P less than 0.01) from the two control groups, which showed that treatment with antibodies against the P2X7 non-functional epitope significantly reduced the amount of tumor in the experimental animals.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Immunotherapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - PC is administered through oral, parenteral, intravenous, intramuscular or topical route. No dosage given.
   EXAMPLE - No relevant example is given.

TI Method for detecting non-invasive lesion of spinal            bone in body of patient affected by cancer disease,            involves selecting several identified lesion-like            geometrical regions as lesion candidate.
AU KELM M
   SUEHLING M
   TSYMBAL A
   WELS M
   TESEMBAUL A
   QUELME M
   WELLS M
   HUERIN M
AE SIEMENS AG (SIEI-C)
   SIEMENS AG (SIEI-C)
GA 2014M80769
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves obtaining several medical                images of patient body. The lesion-like geometrical                regions are identified inside medical images of                patient body by applying image processing method.                The identified lesion-like geometrical regions is                controlled by several patient-specific context                features which are not directly extracted from                medical images. Several identified lesion-like                geometrical regions are selected as lesion                candidate.
   USE - Method for detecting non-invasive lesion of                spinal bone (claimed) in body of patient affected                by cancer disease. Can also be used for detecting                non-invasive lesion of skull bone, hip bone, rib                bone, lungs, prostate, thyroid, kidney, pancreas,                liver, breast, uterus, fat tissue, muscle, skin,                nerve and blood vessel.
   ADVANTAGE - The quality of lesion detection and lesion                analysis is improved by intra and inter expert                variations. The accurate analysis enables                successful pain management, such that the                probability of survival for patient can be                significantly improved. The quality of medical                treatments for patients can be improved.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for system                for non-invasive lesion of spinal bone in body of                patient.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a photographic view                illustrating the medical images of spine of                patient's body.
   Images (ML1-ML3)

TI Cancer cell collector for early detection of            cancer patient, has guide box whose bottom is fixedly            connected with pressurizing cylinder whose bottom            passes through box main portion and is connected with            exhaust pipe.
AU YUAN Y
   WANG C
   YANG C
AE JINAN KEJIA MEDICAL INSPECTION CO LTD (JINA-Non-standard)
GA 2022B1435R
AB    NOVELTY - The utility model claims a cancer cell                collector, comprising a box body, the top end                respectively the box body is fixedly connected with                a drain pipe, a pressurizing mechanism and a liquid                inlet pipe, the middle part of the liquid inlet                pipe is provided with a plastic steel pipe, one end                of the liquid inlet pipe far away from the box body                is fixedly connected with a stopping washer, one                side of the outer wall of the liquid inlet pipe                close to the supporting ring is fixedly connected                with a plurality of second sealing rings, the                second sealing ring is connected with a puncture                needle through a first sealing ring, the inner wall                of the puncture needle is fixedly connected with a                rubber ring, the outer wall of the rubber ring is                jointed with the inner wall of the liquid inlet                pipe, the setting of the pressurizing mechanism of                the utility model is convenient for pressurizing                the inner part of the box body, so as to better                extract the blood, the setting of the puncture                needle is convenient for better inserting skin the                setting of the plastic steel pipe is convenient for                better adjusting the angle of the puncture needle,                the sealing plate in the pressurizing mechanism is                convenient for better putting the external air into                the box body.

PN WO2005092038-A2; US2007178445-A1; WO2005092038-A3; US8679788-B2
TI Detecting infectious disease minority variants, by            contacting nucleic acid sample with oligonucleotide            pair to form reaction mixture, subjecting mixture to            ligation reaction, and amplifying ligation product to            form reaction product.
AU ESHLEMAN J R
   SHI C
   ESHLEMAN S H
AE UNIV JOHNS HOPKINS (UYJO-C)
   ESHLEMAN J R (ESHL-Individual)
   SHI C (SHIC-Individual)
   ESHLEMAN S H (ESHL-Individual)
   UNIV JOHNS HOPKINS (UYJO-C)
GA 2005713744
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting (M1) infectious disease minority                variants, by contacting nucleic acid sample from                subject or cell with an oligonucleotide pair to                form a reaction mixture, subjecting the reaction                mixture to a ligation reaction, and amplifying a                ligation product to form a reaction product.
   USE - (M1) is useful for detecting infectious                disease minority variants. The minority variant is                viral or microbial. The viral minority variant is                HIV, HBV, HCV, cytomegalovirus (CMV), influenza,                herpes simplex virus (HSV), RSV or VZV. The viral                minority variant is a viral drug-resistant minority                variant. (M2) is useful for differentiating                pancreatic cancer from chronic pancreatitis. (M3)                is useful for diagnosing a disease in a subject.                The disease is a disease caused by, induced by or                related to a nucleotide difference in at least one                gene. The disease is Parkinson's disease, Duchenne                muscular dystrophy, Niemann-pick disease,                polyposis, neurofibromatosis, polycystic kidney                disease, Tay-Sachs disease, xeroderma pigmentosa,                ataxia-telangiectasia, Huntingdon disease,                Li-Fraumeni syndrome, beta-thalassemia, sickle cell                anemia, hemoglobin C disease, hemophilia, acute                intermittent porphyria, cystic fibrosis, diabetes,                obesity, cardiovascular disease, cancer, chronic                pancreatitis, cerebrovascular disease, respiratory                disease, influenza, pneumonia, Alzheimer's,                infectious disease, septicemia, liver disease or                hypertension. The cancer is leukemia, lymphoma,                melanoma, neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, head and neck                cancer, skin cancer, melanoma, brain cancer,                esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, lung cancer,                breast cancer, colon cancer, ovarian cancer,                testicular cancer, pancreatic cancer, prostate                cancer, rectal cancer, bladder cancer, renal                cancer, uterine cancer, thyroid cancer, liver                cancer, biliary cancer, bronchial cancer, laryngeal                cancer or testicular cancer. The disease is a                residual disease. The diagnosis is for early                detection. The diagnosis is molecular relapse. The                determination is to predict chemosensitivity or                chemoresistance. The subject is a fetus and the                diagnosis is a prenatal diagnosis. (M4) is useful                in forensic identification. The forensic sample is                from a crime scene. The forensic nucleic acid                sample is derived from a biological sample. (M5) is                identifying sample containing an uncommon genetic                change. (M6) is useful for detecting a nucleic acid                sequence difference. The nucleic acid difference is                a base substitution, single nucleotide                polymorphism, microsatellite, transversion,                transition, missense mutation, nonsense mutation,                insertion, deletion, frameshift mutation, internal                tandem repeat, amplification, translocation,                germline mutation, somatic mutation or altered                methylation. The nucleic acid sample is plasmid                DNA, genomic DNA, PCR product, mitochondria DNA,                RNA, DNA virus, RNA virus or a cell. The target                nucleic acid has two strands and where a pair of                oligonucleotides is directed to both nucleic acid                strands. The subject is a mammal. The mammal is a                human. The biological sample is one or more of                pancreatic duct juice, peripheral blood, serum,                plasma, skin, urine, feces, tears, mucus, sputum,                bile, sweat, or fine needle aspirate. (M6) is                operable to detect infectious disease minority                variants, differentiates pancreatic cancer from                chromic pancreatitis, diagnoses a disease, or                forensically identifies samples (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - (M1) is simple, rapid, accurate, and                sensitive.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting (M1) infectious disease minority                variants, involves contacting a nucleic acid sample                from a subject or a cell with at least one                oligonucleotide pair to form a reaction mixture,                where a pair comprises a first (P1) and a second                (P2) oligonucleotide, where P1 comprises a first                gene specific region and a first primer region, P2                comprises a second gene specific region and a                second primer region, either P1 or P2 comprise a                detection region, either P1 or P2 comprise a                nucleotide difference in the gene specific region,                and P1 and P2 are suitable for ligation to one                another, subjecting the reaction mixture to a                ligation reaction, and amplifying a ligation                product to form a reaction product. INDEPENDENT                CLAIMS are also included for the following:
   differentiating (M2) pancreatic cancer from                chronic pancreatitis, involves contacting a nucleic                acid sample from a subject or a cell with at least                one oligonucleotide pair of (M1), subjecting the                reaction mixture to a ligation reaction, and                amplifying a ligation product to form a reaction                product;
   diagnosing (M3) a disease in a subject,                involves obtaining a biological sample from a                subject, contacting the biological sample with at                least one oligonucleotide pair described in (M1),                subjecting the reaction mixture to a ligation                reaction, and amplifying a ligation product to form                a reaction product;
   method (M4) of forensic identification,                involves obtaining a nucleic acid forensic sample,                contacting a nucleic acid forensic sample with at                least one oligonucleotide pair described in (M1) to                form a reaction mixture, subjecting the reaction                mixture to a ligation reaction, and amplifying a                ligation product to form a reaction product;
   identifying (M5) a sample containing an                uncommon genetic change, involves obtaining a                pooled nucleic acid sample, contacting the pooled                sample with at least one oligonucleotide pair                described in (M1) to form a reaction mixture,                subjecting the reaction mixture to a ligation                reaction, and amplifying a ligation product to form                a reaction product;
   detecting (M6) a nucleic acid sequence                difference, involves contacting a nucleic acid                sample with at least one oligonucleotide pair                described in (M1), providing the reaction mixture                with a nucleotide complementary to the nucleotide                difference, subjecting P1, P2, and the nucleotide                to ligation conditions to form a ligation product,                and amplifying the ligation product to form a                reaction product;
   kits (K1) and (K2) for detecting infectious                disease minority variants, differentiating                pancreatic cancer from chromic pancreatitis,                diagnosing a disease, forensic identification, or                detecting a nucleic acid sequence difference.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Methods: In (M1), the nucleotide                  difference detected encodes one or more of the                  amino acid changes K103N, Y181C, K103E, K103R,                  K103T, G190A, P236L, or another substitution in                  the viral genome associated with altered                  susceptibility to one or more antiviral drugs. In                  (M2), the nucleotide difference is in KRAS2. The                  KRAS2 nucleotide difference is one or more of                  G35A, G35T, G35C, G34A, G34T, G38A, or A182T.                  (M1) further involves analyzing the reaction                  product. (M1) further involves determining the                  Lys-Arg-Ala-Ser mutation level. The mutation                  level of less than 0.6% indicates chronic                  pancreatitis. The mutation level of 0.5% to 80%                  indicates pancreatic cancer. (M1) further                  involves monitoring the Lys-Arg-Ala-Ser mutation                  levels. (M4) further involves comparing the                  reaction product to a reference nucleic acid                  sequence. The reference nucleic acid sequence is                  from a family member, a suspect, a person of                  interest, or a standard. In (M5), the pooled                  nucleic acid sample is a pool of samples. The                  mutated gene specific region is at the 3'end of                  P1 and/or the 5' end of P2. The mutated gene                  specific region is the 3' nucleotide of P1 or the                  5' nucleotide of P2. The mutated gene specific                  region is within the 3' five nucleotides of P1 or                  the 5' five nucleotides of P2. The mutated gene                  specific region is 1-5 nucleotides in length. The                  mutated gene specific region is 5-30 nucleotides                  in length. The P1 and P2 ligate only if the                  nucleotide difference is present in the nucleic                  acid sample. (M5) involves contacting the nucleic                  acid sample with a third (P3) and a fourth (P4)                  oligonucleotide, where P3 comprises a third gene                  specific region and a third primer binding region                  and P4 comprises a probe binding region, a fourth                  primer binding region, a fourth gene specific                  region and a second mutated gene specific region.                  (M5) involves contacting the nucleic acid sample                  with a third (P3), where P3 comprises a probe                  binding region unique from P2, a primer binding                  region, a third gene specific region that targets                  the wild-type version of the gene. (M5) involves                  contacting the nucleic acid sample is with a                  fifth (P5) and a sixth (P6) oligonucleotide,                  where P5 comprises a fifth gene specific region                  and a fifth primer binding region and P6                  comprises a probe binding region, a sixth primer                  binding region, a sixth gene specific region, and                  a third mutated gene specific region. (M5)                  involves contacting the nucleic acid sample is                  with 4-1000 oligonucleotide pairs, where one of                  each pair comprises a gene specific region and a                  primer binding region, while the other in the                  pair comprises a probe binding region, a primer                  binding region, a gene specific region, and a                  mutated gene specific region. In (M6), the                  nucleic acid difference is one or more of KRAS2                  nucleotide difference, K103N HIV-1                  drug-resistance nucleotide difference, CFTR                  nucleotide difference, p53 nucleotide difference,                  or Braf nucleotide difference. The nucleotide                  ligates to one or more of P1 or P2 if the                  nucleotide difference is present. In (M6), the P1                  and P2 are 10-140 nucleotides in length. The                  first and second gene specific regions are 10-100                  nucleotides in length. The first or the second                  primer regions comprise one or more of an Ml 3                  forward, Ml 3 reverse, T7, SP6, T3, lambda gtlO                  forward, lambda gtlO reverse, lambda gt11                  forward, lambda gt11 reverse, DNA zipcode,                  address code, DNA barcodes, DNA tags or DNA                  anti-tag sequences. The analyzing step is by bead                  hybridization, rolling circle amplification,                  hyperbranching rolling circle amplification,                  ligase chain reaction, strand displacement                  amplification, transcription mediated                  amplification, or nucleic acid sequence base                  amplification. The analyzing step is by real time                  quantitative PCR, Taqman probing, molecular                  beacons, FRET hybridization probes, scorpion                  probes, Sybr green, or melting curve analysis.                  The detection region is a probe binding region.                  The probe binding region is a known DNA sequence                  that is not complementary to the sequence                  up-stream and down-stream of the gene specific                  regions and the mutated gene specific region. The                  analyzing is with a probe complementary to the                  probe binding region. The detection region is a                  known nucleotide sequence that is not                  complementary to the sequence upstream and                  down-stream of the gene specific regions and the                  mutated gene specific region. The detection                  region is one or more of a lacZ sequence, 16S                  rDNA sequence, M13 forward, M13 reverse, T7, SP6,                  T3, lambda gtlO forward, lambda gtlO reverse,                  lambda gt11 forward, lambda gt11 reverse, DNA                  zipcode, address code, DNA barcodes, DNA tags or                  DNA anti-tag sequences. The detection region                  contains a labeled nucleotide. The labeled                  nucleotide is fluorescent, radioactively,                  chemical moiety or colorimetrically labeled. The                  amplifying step is performed by PCR, quantitative                  PCR, real time PCR, or real time quantitative                  PCR. The amplifying is quantitative. (M6) further                  involves removing unbound P1 and P2 prior to                  amplifying. (M6) further involves providing a                  nucleic acid sample. (M6) further involves                  amplifying genomic DNA to produce a nucleic acid                  sample. The amplifying is by PCR, real-time PCR,                  rt-PCR, real time rt-PCR, Q-PCR, Taqman probing,                  molecular beacons, FRET hybridization probes,                  scorpion probes Sybr green, or melting curve                  analysis. (M6) further involves analyzing the                  reaction product. The analyzing step is performed                  by chromatography, capillary electrophoresis,                  microfluidic analysis, slab gel electrophoresis,                  intercalating agent, Southern blot real-time PCR,                  surface plasmon resonance, flow cytometry,                  fluorescence polarization, hybridization,                  microarray detection, or radiography. The                  intercalating agent is ethidium bromide or an                  unsymmetrical cyanine dye. The amplifying is                  bottom strand synthesis. (M6) further involves                  Q-PCR probe cleavage after the amplification of                  the ligation product. The nucleic acid sample                  contains 1:1 to 1:1000000 ratio of mutated                  nucleic acid to wild-type nucleic acid. (M6)                  further involves providing one or more of a DNA,                  RNA, LNA, and PNA probe complementary and                  overlapping with the wild-type allele to the                  ligation reaction.Preferred Kits: (K1) comprises at least one                  first (P1) and at least one second (P2)                  oligonucleotide to form a reaction mixture, where                  P1 comprises a first gene specific region and a                  first primer region, P2 comprises a second gene                  specific region and a second primer region,                  either P1 or P2 comprise a detection region,                  either P1 or P2 comprise a nucleotide difference                  in the gene specific region, and P1 and P2 are                  suitable for ligation to one another, and                  instructions for use; and (K2) comprises at least                  one first (P1) and at least one second (P2)                  oligonucleotide, where P1 and P2 bind to a                  nucleic acid to form a reaction mixture, and                  where P1 comprises a first gene specific region                  and a first primer binding region and P2                  comprises a probe binding region, a second primer                  binding region and a second gene specific region,                  wherein there a nucleotide gap between the first                  and second gene specific regions contains the                  nucleic acid difference.
