AB    NOVELTY - An isolated polypeptide is new. The isolated                polypeptide is chosen from (a) a polypeptide having                amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1, (b) a                polypeptide having at least 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%,                90%, 95%, and/or 99% sequence identity to SEQ ID                NO: 1, and (c) a polypeptide having one or more                amino acid substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions to SEQ ID NO: 1, and optionally                substitutions, deletions, and/or additions of the                at least one or more amino acids at positions 2                and/or 9 of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                1, in which at position 2 one or more amino acids                are optionally replaced with Met in SEQ ID NO: 1                and/or at position 9 is replaced with Leu, and                optionally polypeptide having amino acid sequences                of SEQ ID NO: 2, 3, or 4.
   USE - The isolated polypeptide is useful in                preparation of a medicament or pharmaceutical                composition for preventing or treating tumor and                disease associated with a mutation in                phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase                catalytic subunit- alpha (PIK3CA) gene in a                subject. The reagent is useful for detecting                polypeptide in a kit for diagnosing a tumor. The                tumor is chosen from breast cancer, lung cancer,                nasopharyngeal carcinoma, liver cancer, gastric                cancer, esophageal cancer, colorectal cancer,                pancreatic cancer, melanoma, skin cancer, prostate                cancer, cervical cancer, leukemia or brain tumors,                preferably, breast cancer (all claimed). The                isolated polypeptide is used for improving                immunity.
   ADVANTAGE - The isolated polypeptide does not cause                adverse side effects. The method detects tumor in                an easier manner with high sensitivity and                specificity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An isolated polypeptide is new. The isolated                polypeptide is chosen from (a) a polypeptide having                amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1, (b) a                polypeptide having at least 70%, 75%, 80%, 85%,                90%, 95%, and/or 99% sequence identity to SEQ ID                NO: 1, and (c) a polypeptide having one or more                amino acid substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions to SEQ ID NO: 1, and optionally                substitutions, deletions, and/or additions of the                at least one or more amino acids at positions 2                and/or 9 of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                1, in which at position 2 one or more amino acids                are optionally replaced with Met in SEQ ID NO: 1                and/or at position 9 is replaced with Leu, and                optionally polypeptide having amino acid sequences                of SEQ ID NO: 2, 3, or 4. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are                included for the following:
   (1) use of a reagent for detecting the                polypeptide in a kit for diagnosing a tumor, where                the tumor simultaneously expresses HLA-A0201 and                polypeptide, and the tumor is chosen from breast                cancer, lung cancer, nasopharyngeal carcinoma,                liver cancer, gastric cancer, esophageal cancer,                colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, melanoma,                skin cancer, prostate cancer, cervical cancer,                leukemia or brain tumors, preferably, breast                cancer;
   (2) isolated nucleic acid encoding the                polypeptide or its complementary sequence;
   (3) nucleic acid construct comprising a                nucleic acid coding sequence, and an optional                control sequence operably linked to the coding                sequence;
   (4) expression vector comprising the nucleic                acid construct;
   (5) host cell carrying the nucleic acid                construct or expression vector, where the host cell                is obtained by transfecting or transforming the                nucleic acid construct or expression vector;
   (6) antigen-presenting cell presenting the                polypeptide;
   (7) immune effector cell capable of                recognizing the polypeptide or antigen-presenting                cells that present the polypeptide on the cell                surface;
   (8) antibody capable of specifically                recognizing the polypeptide;
   (9) method for diagnosing the tumor involves                (i) detecting whether a patient-derived biological                sample carrying the polypeptide, and (ii)                determining whether the patient has a tumor based                on detected result; and
   (10) system comprising a polypeptide detection                device for performing step (i), and diagnostic                result determining device connected to the                polypeptide detecting device for performing step                (ii).
   Gly-Leu-Lys-Asp-Leu-Leu-Asn-Pro-Ile (SEQ ID                NO: 1), Gly-Leu-Lys-Asp-Leu-Leu-Asn-Pro-Leu (SEQ ID                NO: 2), Gly-Met-Lys-Asp-Leu-Leu-Asn-Pro-Leu (SEQ ID                NO: 3), and Gly-Met-Lys-Asp-Leu-Leu-Asn-Pro-Ile                (SEQ ID NO: 4).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Method: The antigen-presenting cells                  are obtained by contacting a cell having                  antigen-presenting ability with the polypeptide,                  and introducing nucleic acid, nucleic acid                  construct or expression vector into the                  antigen-presenting cell, where the cells are                  dendritic cells. The immune effector cells are                  obtained by contacting the antigen-presenting                  cells with cells having an immune effector                  function, where the immunologically competent                  cell is a T cell, preferably cluster of                  differentiation (CD)-8+ T-cell. The antibody is                  obtained by collecting the serum of an animal                  immunized with the polypeptide and purifying the                  antibody of interest from the serum.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Immunostimulant. Test details are                described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Vaccine.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition is administered                intraperitoneal, intravenous, intramuscular,                subcutaneous, topical, oral, nasal or rectal route.                No dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a            patient for treating, reducing or amelioration of the            progression, severity and/or duration of a            proliferative disorder e.g., cancer, involves obtaining            a tumor sample and a non-tumor sample from a subject,            and sequencing DNA from the tumor sample.
AU WELKER N
   EVANS E A
   HAQUE I S
   CHU C S
   MAGUIRE J R
AE MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)
GA 2026156096
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a                patient involves: (a) obtaining a tumor sample and                a non-tumor sample from a subject with a history of                cancer; (b) sequencing DNA from the tumor sample                and sequencing DNA from the non-tumor sample, for                obtaining sequences of DNA from the tumor sample                and sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample, and                determining a set of 10 tumor-specific somatic                mutations that are specific to the subject, and at                one or more timepoints after (a) and (b); (c)                obtaining a fluid sample of whole blood, plasma, or                serum from the subject; (d) extracting cell-free                DNA (cfDNA) from the fluid sample; (e) sequencing                the cfDNA, for obtaining a plurality of sequence                reads; and (f) detecting the presence or absence of                a sequence read comprising any one of the set of 10                tumor-specific somatic mutations that are specific                to the subject.
   USE - Method for detecting circulating tumor DNA                (ctDNA) in a patient for treating, reducing or                amelioration of the progression, severity and/or                duration of a proliferative disorder e.g., cancer,                or amelioration of a proliferative disorder                resulting from the administration of one or more                therapies where cancer is selected from adrenal                cancer, anal cancer, bile duct cancer, bladder                cancer, bone cancer, a central nervous system (CNS)                cancer, breast cancer, Castleman disease, cervical                cancer, colon or rectum cancer, endometrial cancer,                esophagus cancer, Ewing sarcoma, eye cancer,                gallbladder cancer, a gastrointestinal carcinoid                cancer, Hodgkin disease, Kaposi sarcoma, kidney                cancer, laryngeal and hypopharyngeal cancer,                leukemia, liver cancer, lung cancer, lymphoma,                malignant mesothelioma, multiple myeloma,                myelodysplastic syndrome, nasal cavity or paranasal                sinus cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer, neuroblastoma,                oral cavity or oropharyngeal cancer, osteosarcoma,                ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer, penile cancer,                pituitary cancer, prostate cancer, retinoblastoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, salivary gland cancer, skin                cancer, small intestine cancer, stomach cancer,                testicular cancer, thymus cancer, thyroid cancer,                uterine sarcoma, vaginal cancer, vulvar cancer,                Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and Wilms tumor                (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method improve test specificity by                reducing sequence error generated during                amplification, and improve the detection,                monitoring and treatment of a patient suffering                from a disease.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a                patient involves: (a) obtaining a tumor sample and                a non-tumor sample from a subject with a history of                cancer; (b) sequencing DNA from the tumor sample                and sequencing DNA from the non-tumor sample, for                obtaining sequences of DNA from the tumor sample                and sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample, and                determining a set of 10 tumor-specific somatic                mutations that are specific to the subject, and at                one or more timepoints subsequent to (a) and (b);                (c) obtaining a fluid sample of whole blood,                plasma, or serum from the subject; (d) extracting                cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from the fluid sample; (e)                sequencing the cfDNA, for obtaining a plurality of                sequence reads; and (f) detecting the presence or                absence of a sequence read comprising any one of                the set of 10 tumor-specific somatic mutations that                are specific to the subject, where the presence of                a sequence read in multiple sequence reads                corresponding to one or more of the set of 10                tumor-specific somatic mutations that are specific                to the subject indicates the presence of                ctDNA.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The fluid sample is                  plasma. The targeted sequencing comprises                  sequencing exons.Preferred Conditions: The sequencing DNA                  from the tumor sample and sequencing DNA from the                  non-tumor sample comprises whole genome                  sequencing, preferably sequencing DNA from the                  tumor sample and sequencing DNA from the                  non-tumor sample comprises targeted sequencing.                  The set of 10 tumor-specific somatic mutations                  that are specific to the subject comprises 50 or                  500 tumor-specific somatic mutations that are                  specific to the subject.Preferred Process: The method further                  involves repeating (c)-(f) for one or more times                  during a cancer treatment, following completion                  of a cancer treatment, while the subject is in                  remission, or coinciding with or prior to                  surgery.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   EXAMPLE - None given.

AB       The following are claimed: (A) DNA encoding the                antiproliferative protein prohibitin having the                nucleotide sequence shown and allelic and species                variants of the sequence; (B) a construct                comprising DNA as in (A) and a vector for                introducing the DNA into eucaryotic or procaryotic                host cells; (C) a host cell stably transformed or                transfected with a construct as in (B), such that                an antiproliferative protein encoded by the                construct is expressed; (D) a recombinantly                produced protein or synthetic protein having all or                a unique portion of the sequence shown.
   USE -   Man-made alterations in the amt. of prohibitin                in the body can be used to treat human syndromes                that are based on an excess or an insufficienty of                prohibit, e.g. prohibinin and prohibit gene therapy                can be used to treat benign neoplasms and cancer                while agents which inhibit prohibitin or a gene                which makes antisense mRNA can be used to treat                e.g. osteoporosis, fragile skin or poor wound                healing. The prohibitin cDNA can also be used as a                diagnostic probe for genetic diseases linked to                17q21-22, e.g. acute myelogenous leukemia or for                proliferative disorders. Antibodies to prohibitin                can be used to purify prohibitin or for detection,                e.g. in cells.

   PATTERSON P

AB    NOVELTY - Treatment of cancer involves administering a                nucleic acid molecule that results in silencing                endothelin receptor B activity through ribonucleic                acid interference (RNAi) in cancer cells of the                subject.
   USE - For treating the metastasizing or malignant                cancer e.g. cancer of cardiac, lung,                gastrointestinal, genitourinary tract, liver, bone,                nervous system, gynecological, hematologic, skin,                or adrenal glands; for treating cutaneous or lymph                node metastases melanoma (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method inhibits ETRB activity, BCL-2A1 and                PARP-3 activity; exhibits decreased cell viability                to correlated with reduction in ETRB expression and                reduction in ETRB protein levels by siRNA led to an                increase in cell death.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   treating melanoma involving administration of                a selective inhibitor (S1) of BCL-2A1 activity or                selective inhibitor (S2) of                poly(ADP-ribose)polymerase-3 (PARP-3)                activity;
   treating cancer involving administration of a                selective inhibitor of an endothelin receptor B                activity (S3) in combination with a therapeutic                agent;
   identifying (M2) cancer cells amenable to                treatment with a nucleic acid molecule that results                in silencing endothelin receptor B activity through                RNAi involving detecting elevated endothelin                receptor B activity in a sample of cells as                compared to endothelin receptor B activity in                corresponding normal cells;
   identifying (M3) melanoma cells amenable to                treatment with a selective inhibitor of BCL-2A1                activity or PARP-3 activity involving detecting                elevated endothelin receptor B activity in a sample                of cells as compared to endothelin receptor B                activity in corresponding normal cells;
   identifying (M4) cancer cells of subject                amenable to treatment with a selective inhibitor of                an endothelin receptor B activity in combination                with a therapeutic agent involving contacting a                sample of cancer cells with a selective inhibitor                of an endothelin receptor B activity and detecting                an increase in angiogenesis in the cells as                compared to the level of angiogenesis in                corresponding normal cells or untreated cancer                cells;
   identifying (M5) an agent useful for treating                cancer in combination with a selective inhibitor of                an endothelin receptor B activity involving                contacting a sample of cancer cells with at least                one test agent in combination with a selective                inhibitor of an endothelin receptor B activity,                where detection of apoptosis following the contact                identifies the agent as useful for treating                cancer;
   monitoring a therapeutic regimen for treating                a subject having melanoma involving determining a                change in BCL-2A1 activity, PARP-3 activity,                HIF-1&#945;, VEGF, or GRAVIN activity during                therapy.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Components: (S1) Is                  phthalazin-1(2H)-one, isoindolinone,                  nicotinamide, 3-aminobenzamide, benzamide,                  4-amino-1,8-napthalimide, 6(5H)-phenanthridinone,                  5-aminoisoquinolinone hydrochloride,                  4-hydroxyquinazoline, 4-quinazolinol,                  1,5-isoquinolinediol, or                  5-hydroxy-1(2H)-isoquinolinone, and                  3,4-dihydro-5-[4-(1-piperidinyl)butoxy]-1(2H)-isoquinolinone.                  (S2) Is a reticulon proteins, sodium butyrate, or                  antimycin A, ethyl                  2-amino-6-bromo-4-[1-cyano-2-ethoxy-2-oxoethyl]-4H4chromene-3-carboxylate                  (HA14-1). (S3) Is BQ788 or its derivative, an                  antisense molecule to an endothelin receptor-B                  nucleic acid, an endothelin receptor-B agonist                  nucleic acid, or siRNA. The therapeutic agent is                  an antiangiogenic agent or a chemotherapeutic                  agent. The therapeutic agent is thalidomide,                  rofecoxib, celecoxib, bevacizumab, angiostatin,                  or endostatin. The chemotherapeutic agent is an                  antimetabolite, a DNA cross-linking agent, an                  alkylating agent, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, or                  a microtubule inhibitor.Preferred Methods: In (M2), the cells are                  from a biopsy sample or a bodily fluid obtained                  from a subject. (M2) Further involves contacting                  the cells with a nucleic acid molecule that                  results in silencing endothelin receptor B                  activity through RNAi in the cells, and detecting                  a decrease in endothelin B receptor activity                  following the contact, thus confirming that the                  cancer cells are amenable to treatment with a                  nucleic acid molecule that results in silencing                  endothelin receptor B activity through RNAi. (M3)                  Further involves contacting the cells with a                  selective inhibitor of BCL-2A1 activity or PARP-3                  activity and detecting a decrease in endothelin B                  receptor activity following the contact, thus                  confirming that the melanoma cells are amenable                  to treatment with a selective inhibitor of                  BCL-2A1 activity or PARP-3 activity. (M4)                  Involves detecting elevated levels of                  HIF-1&#945; activity and VEGF activity in the                  sample of cells as compared to HIF-1&#945;                  activity and VEGF activity respectively in                  corresponding normal cells or untreated cancer                  cells. (M4) Involves detecting decreased levels                  of GRAVIN activity in the sample of cells from                  the subject as compared to GRAVIN activity in                  corresponding normal cells or untreated cancer                  cells. (M4) Further involves contacting the cells                  with a therapeutic agent and detecting inhibited                  growth, enhanced cell death or apoptosis                  following the contact, thus confirming that the                  cancer cells are amenable to treatment with a                  selective inhibitor of an endothelin receptor B                  activity in combination with a therapeutic agent.                  (M5) Is performed in a high throughput format.                  (M5) Involves contacting samples of cancer cells                  of several samples with at least one test agent                  in combination with a selective inhibitor of an                  endothelin receptor B activity.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Endothelin Receptor-B inhibitor; Antisense                Therapy; RNAi; RNA Interference; Gene Therapy;                BCL-2A1 inhibitor; poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase                (PARP-3) inhibitor; Topoisomerase I                inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is systemic or parenteral and                is directly to a tumor site (claimed).
   EXAMPLE - No relevant example given.

TI Detecting circulating tumor DNA in a sample,            involves obtaining tumor sample and a non-tumor sample            from a cancer patient, sequencing DNA from the tumor            sample and sequencing DNA from non-tumor sample, for            obtaining sequences of DNA from tumor sample and            sequences of DNA from non-tumor sample.
AU BATTEY C J
   GOULD G
   ACEVEDO A
AE MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)
   MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)
GA 202547530X
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a                sample, involves: (a) obtaining a tumor sample and                a non-tumor sample from a cancer patient; (b)                sequencing DNA from the tumor sample and sequencing                DNA from the non-tumor sample, for obtaining                sequences of DNA from the tumor sample and                sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample; (c)                determining somatic variants based on differences                between sequences of DNA from the tumor sample and                sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample; (d) at                a later time, obtaining one further sample of                blood, plasma, or serum from the cancer patient;                (e) extracting cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from the at                least one further sample; and (f) sequencing the                cfDNA, for obtaining a sequencing library.
   USE - Method for detecting circulating tumor DNA                (ctDNA) in a sample, where tumor is selected from                adrenal cancer, anal cancer, bile duct cancer,                bladder cancer, bone cancer, a brain/CNS tumor,                breast cancer, Castleman disease, cervical cancer,                colon or rectum cancer, endometrial cancer,                esophagus cancer, Ewing tumor, eye cancer,                gallbladder cancer, gastrointestinal carcinoid                tumor, a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST),                gestational trophoblastic disease, Hodgkin disease,                Kaposi sarcoma, kidney cancer, laryngeal and                hypopharyngeal cancer, leukemia, liver cancer, lung                cancer, lymphoma, malignant mesothelioma, multiple                myeloma, myelodysplastic Syndrome, nasal cavity or                paranasal sinus cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer,                neuroblastoma, oral cavity or oropharyngeal cancer,                osteosarcoma, ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer,                penile cancer, a pituitary tumor, prostate cancer,                retinoblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, salivary gland                cancer, skin cancer, small intestine cancer,                stomach cancer, testicular cancer, thymus cancer,                thyroid cancer, uterine sarcoma, vaginal cancer,                vulvar cancer, Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia, and                Wilms tumor (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method help in detection and/or monitoring                of blood borne or hematological cancers, and                improving sensitivity and estimation of                tumor-informed MRD assays and reducing error rates                by performing post-sequencing error-correction and                error correction using internal controls that are                proximate to the variant sites.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a                sample, involves: (a) obtaining a tumor sample and                a non-tumor sample from a cancer patient; (b)                sequencing DNA from the tumor sample and sequencing                DNA from the non-tumor sample, for obtaining                sequences of DNA from the tumor sample and                sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample; (c)                determining somatic variants based on differences                between sequences of DNA from the tumor sample and                sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample; (d) at                a later time, obtaining at least one further sample                of blood, plasma, or serum from the cancer patient;                (e) extracting cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from the at                least one further sample; (f) sequencing the cfDNA,                for obtaining a sequencing library; and (g)                detecting the presence or absence of ctDNA                sequences in the sequencing library, where                detecting the presence or absence of ctDNA                sequences in the sequencing library comprises: (i)                calculating, using a computer processor, an allele                balance of the somatic variants based on purity of                the tumor sample obtained from the subject, (ii)                calculating, using a computer processor, a copy                number for each somatic variants, (iii) correcting                for, using a computer processor, an error rate for                each somatic variant, or (iv) any                combination.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Process: The method of detecting                  circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in a sample, which                  preferably involves: (a) obtaining a tumor sample                  and a non-tumor sample from a cancer patient; (b)                  sequencing DNA from the tumor sample and                  sequencing DNA from the non-tumor sample, for                  obtaining sequences of DNA from the tumor sample                  and sequences of DNA from the non-tumor sample;                  (c) determining somatic variants based on                  differences between sequences of DNA from the                  tumor sample and sequences of DNA from the                  non-tumor sample; (d) obtaining further sample of                  blood, plasma, or serum from the cancer patient                  at a later time; (e) extracting cell-free DNA                  (cfDNA) from one further sample; (f) sequencing                  the cfDNA, for obtaining a sequencing library;                  (g) selecting a control site in the sequence                  library for each somatic variant, where the                  control site matches a reference base for the                  corresponding somatic variant; (h) calculating,                  using a computer processor, an error rate for a                  variant allele of the reference base by detecting                  changes at the control site, where the error rate                  is a background probability of detecting the                  variant allele; and (i) detecting the presence or                  absence of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)                  sequences in the sequencing library. The method                  further involves calculating, using a computer                  processor, a dropout rate of sites that do not                  contribute to a ctDNA signal; correcting for,                  using a computer processor, inclusion of latent                  variant classes in the sequencing library by                  comparing the sequence library to a reference                  panel (e.g., known buffy coat sequences). The                  method further involves enriching the extracted                  cfDNA prior to sequencing by contacting the                  extracted cfDNA with multiple oligonucleotides,                  where each oligonucleotide in the plurality of                  oligonucleotides comprises a nucleic acid                  sequence that is capable of hybridizing to a DNA                  fragment comprising one of the somatic variants,                  for obtaining a ctDNA-enriched fraction,                  optionally where the enriching comprises (i)                  hybrid capture-based enrichment, (ii) PCR-target                  enrichment, or (iii) on-sequencer enrichment. The                  method of detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)                  in a sample, further involves determining a tumor                  fraction.Preferred Conditions: The control site is                  located within 160 bases, 120 bases, 20 bases or                  3 bases of the corresponding somatic variant. The                  sequencing comprises whole genome sequencing or                  targeted sequencing, and sequencing of introns,                  exons, intergenic regions, or a combination. The                  somatic variants comprises 10, 50, 100, 150, 200,                  250, or 500 tumor-specific somatic mutations. The                  somatic variants comprises one or more somatic                  mutations selected from SNVs, insertions,                  deletions, and translocations. The tumor fraction                  of zero indicates the absence of the tumor in the                  patient. The patient has completed one cancer                  treatment prior to obtaining the tumor sample and                  the non-tumor sample. The cancer treatment is                  selected from chemotherapy, radiotherapy,                  surgery, immunotherapy, cell therapy, or biologic                  therapy. The method further involves repeating                  (d)-(g) with a second, third, fourth, fifth,                  sixth, seventh, eight, nineth, or tenth further                  sample of blood, plasma, or serum at successive                  time points, or steps (d)-(g) are repeated one or                  more times while the patient is in remission, or                  undergoing treatment for the cancer, or                  coinciding with or prior to surgery; following,                  during, or prior to administration of                  chemotherapy, following, during, or prior to                  radiation therapy, following, during, or prior to                  administration of an immunotherapy, following,                  during, or prior to administration of a cell                  therapy, or following, during, or prior to                  administration of a biologic therapy.Preferred Components: The tumor sample                  comprises a solid tumor biopsy or a fluid sample.                  The fluid sample is selected from blood, blood                  plasma, blood serum, urine, saliva, and cerebral                  spinal fluid (CSF). The non-tumor sample                  comprises a tissue sample matched to a tissue of                  origin of the tumor sampl, more preferably                  non-tumor sample comprises a fluid sample                  selected from a buffy coat sample, blood, blood                  plasma, blood serum, urine, saliva, and cerebral                  spinal fluid (CSF).
   EXAMPLE - The examples provided do not support the                claims.

GA 2014F86601
AB    NOVELTY - A fusion polypeptide comprising fibroblast                growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) polypeptide, and                BAI1-associated protein 2-like-1 (BAIAP2L1)                polypeptide or transforming, acidic coiled-coil                containing protein 3 (TACC3) polypeptide, is                new.
   USE - The fusion polypeptide is useful in                pharmaceutical composition for preventing or                treating cancer including bladder cancer, brain                tumor, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, lung                cancer, lung adenocarcinoma, lung squamous cell                carcinoma, melanoma of skin, esophageal cancer,                stomach cancer, or liver cancer, preferably bladder                cancer, where the stage of bladder cancer is                classified as stage 3 or more in TNM disease                staging (all claimed). The composition is in the                form of tablet, powder, granule, capsule, syrup,                inhalant, injection, ointment, ophthalmic ointment,                eye drops, nasal drop, ear drop, poultice, lotion,                suspension or solution.
   ADVANTAGE - The fusion polypeptide avoids undesirable side                effects. The method rapidly and simply screens the                compound having FGFR inhibitory activity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A fusion polypeptide comprising fibroblast                growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) polypeptide, and                BAI1-associated protein 2-like-1 (BAIAP2L1)                polypeptide or transforming, acidic coiled-coil                containing protein 3 (TACC3) polypeptide, is new.                One portion or all portions of the wild-type FGFR3                polypeptide comprises amino acid sequences of SEQ                ID NOs: 6 or 7, or wild-type FGFR3 polypeptide in                which one or more amino acids are substituted,                deleted or inserted to obtain mutant FGFR3                polypeptide. One portion or all portions of the                wild-type BAIAP2L1 polypeptide comprises amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 8, or wild-type BAIAP2L1                polypeptide in which one or more amino acids are                substituted, deleted or inserted to obtain mutant                BAIAP2L1 polypeptide. One portion or all portions                of the wild-type TACC3 polypeptide comprises amino                acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 9 or wild-type TACC3                polypeptide in which one or more amino acids are                substituted, deleted or inserted to obtain mutant                TACC3 polypeptide. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included                for the following:
   polynucleotide encoding the above-mentioned                fusion polypeptide;
   vector comprising the polynucleotide;
   recombinant cell comprising the vector;
   antibody specifically bonded with the fusion                polypeptide, or its antigen binding fragment;
   pair of oligonucleotide primer for detection                or amplification, comprising the polynucleotide                encoding the fusion polypeptide hybridized with the                polynucleotide of sense primer and antisense                primer, respectively;
   oligonucleotide having activity for inhibiting                translation of mRNA polynucleotide to protein,                where the oligonucleotide binds with the mRNA                polynucleotide encoding the fusion                polypeptide;
   pharmaceutical composition;
   method (M1) for detecting the fusion                polypeptide;
   method (M2) for detecting the polynucleotide                encoding the fusion polypeptide;
   kit for detection of the polynucleotide                encoding the fusion polypeptide;
   method (M3) for testing the presence or                absence of cancer progression;
   method (M4) for selecting the patient to whom                the anticancer agent containing the compound or its                salt having FGFR inhibitory activity is                administered;
   method (M5) for preventing or treating                cancer;
   use of the compound or its salt having FGFR                inhibitory activity in preparation of                pharmaceutical composition for cancer treatment, by                administering the composition to the patient who                has a polynucleotide that expresses or encodes the                fusion polypeptide;
   compound or its salt having FGFR inhibitory                activity; and
   method (M6) for identifying the compound                having FGFR inhibitory activity.
   Sequences not defined here may be found at                ftp://ftp.wipo.int/pub/published_pct_sequences/publication.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Isolation (Claimed): The fusion polypeptide                  is derived from bladder cancer or lung cancer.                  Preferred Composition: The pharmaceutical                  composition comprises (a) the antibody or its                  antigen binding fragment, (b) the                  oligonucleotide, or (c) compound or its salt                  having FGFR inhibitory activity which is                  administered to a patient who has polynucleotide                  that expresses or encodes the fusion polypeptide.                  Preferred Method: The method (M1) involves                  isolating the sample from the test subject, and                  detecting the fusion polypeptide in the sample                  using the antibody or its antigen binding                  fragment that binds with the fusion polypeptide.                  The method (M2) involves hybridizing the                  polynucleotide encoding the fusion polypeptide                  with the polynucleotide of sense primer and                  antisense primer, respectively to obtain pair of                  oligonucleotide primer, and detecting and                  amplifying the polynucleotide encoding the fusion                  polypeptide, in the sample isolated from the test                  subject using the obtained pair of                  oligonucleotide primer. The method (M3) involves                  isolating sample from the test subject,                  determining the presence or absence of fusion                  polypeptide or the polynucleotide encoding the                  fusion polypeptide in the sample, judging the                  subject is suffered from cancer when the fusion                  polypeptide is detected, and identifying the                  presence or absence of cancer progression in the                  subject suffered from cancer when the fusion                  polypeptide is detected. The method (M4) involves                  (a) determining existence or nonexistence of the                  fusion polypeptide or polynucleotide encoding the                  fusion polypeptide, in the isolated sample of the                  test subject, and (b) selecting the patient by                  whom the presence of the fusion polypeptide or                  polynucleotide encoding the fusion polypeptide,                  is confirmed as a patient to administer the                  anticancer agent. The method (M5) involves                  administering the compound or its salt having                  FGFR inhibitory activity to the cancer patient                  who has a polynucleotide that expresses or                  encodes the fusion polypeptide. The method (M6)                  involves (A) (a) culturing cell which expresses                  fused polypeptide, and determining level of cell                  growth in the presence and absence of test                  compound, (b) comparing the level of cell growth                  at the time of culturing the cell in presence and                  absence of test compound, and (c) determining and                  judging the test compound has FGFR inhibitory                  activity when the level of cell growth at the                  time of culturing the cell in presence of the                  test compound is lower than the level of cell                  growth at the time of culturing the cell in the                  absence of the test compound, or (B) (a)                  administering test compound to non-human mammal                  in which the cell that expresses fusion                  polypeptide is transplanted, and determining                  level of proliferation of the cell, (b) comparing                  the level of cell growth of the cell determined                  in non-human mammal with the level of cell growth                  in non-human mammal which is not transplanted and                  has not received administration of the test                  compound, and (c) determining and judging the                  test compound has FGFR inhibitory activity when                  the level of cell growth in the step (a) is lower                  than the level of cell growth in the non-human                  mammal which is not transplanted and has not                  received administration of the test compound.                  Preferred Compound: The compound or its salt                  having FGFR inhibitory activity, is administered                  to cancer patient who has a polynucleotide that                  expresses or encodes the fusion polypeptide.                  Preferred Kit: The kit comprises the pair of                  oligonucleotide primer. The kit comprises the                  antibody or its antigen binding fragment that                  binds with the fusion polypeptide. Preferred                  Polypeptide: The fusion polypeptide comprises (a)                  FGFR3 polypeptide and BAIAP2L1 polypeptide, where                  the fusion polypeptide comprises an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 32 or 38, and/or (b) FGFR3                  polypeptide and TACC3 polypeptide, where the                  fusion polypeptide comprises an amino acid                  sequence (SEQ ID NO: 28, 30, 34 or 36). Preferred                  Polynucleotide: The polynucleotide comprises (a)                  a base pair sequence (SEQ ID NO: 14, 15 or 16),                  and/or (b) a base pair sequence (SEQ ID NO: 27,                  29, 31, 33, 35 or 37). Preferred Oligonucleotide:                  The oligonucleotide is small interfering RNA                  (siRNA) that cleaves mRNA polypeptide. Preferred                  Patient: The patient is a patient selected by the                  above-mentioned method (M4). Preferred Cell: The                  cell is a cancer cell. The cancer cell includes                  bladder cancer cell, brain tumor cell, head and                  neck squamous epithelium cancer cell, lung cancer                  cell, lung adenocarcinoma cell, lung                  squamous-epithelium cancer cell, melanoma skin                  cell, esophageal cancer cell, stomach cancer                  cell, or liver cancer cell. GA 2020C0757U
AB    NOVELTY - Performing digital method involves mixing                sample with a mixture including a buffer, enzymes,                a first oligonucleotide which is an amplification                oligonucleotide, a second oligonucleotide which is                a leak absorption oligonucleotide and a third                oligonucleotide which is a target-specific                conversion oligonucleotide, partitioning the                mixture into compartments so that a fraction of the                compartments does not contain the target                biomolecule, converting the target biomolecule into                a signal, signal being preferably a DNA single                strand, amplifying the signal, and detecting and/or                measuring signal in each compartment.
   USE - Performing digital method for detecting and/or                quantifying one target biomolecule such as from                DNA, RNA and proteins based on isothermal                amplification for diagnosis of a disease selected                from cancer, neuronal diseases, cardiovascular                diseases, inflammatory diseases, autoimmune                diseases, diseases due to a viral or bacterial                infection, skin diseases, skeletal muscle diseases,                dental diseases and prenatal diseases, which is                caused by biotic stress, infectious and/or                parasitic origin, or diseases caused by abiotic                stress, preferably caused by nutritional                deficiencies and/or unfavorable environment (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method allows rapid and selective                detection of biomolecules, and has specificity, the                simplicity and the rapidity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   an in vitro method for diagnosis of a disease                selected from cancer, neuronal diseases,                cardiovascular diseases, inflammatory diseases,                autoimmune diseases, diseases due to a viral or                bacterial infection, skin diseases, skeletal muscle                diseases, dental diseases and prenatal diseases,                which involves using digital method;
   an in vitro method for agro diagnosis of a                disease, which is caused by biotic stress,                preferably by infectious and/or parasitic origin,                or diseases caused by abiotic stress, preferably                caused by nutritional deficiencies and/or                unfavorable environment using digital method;                and
   a kit for detecting and/or quantifying one                target biomolecule, which comprises mixture of                enzymes selected from polymerase, nicking enzyme or                restriction enzyme and exonuclease, mixture of                oligonucleotides comprising a first oligonucleotide                which is an amplification oligonucleotide, a second                oligonucleotide which is a leak absorption                oligonucleotide and a third oligonucleotide which                is a target-specific conversion oligonucleotide and                optionally a fourth oligonucleotide which is a                reporting probe, and partitioning agent, preferably                a water-in-oil emulsion.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Conditions: The target biomolecule                  is a nucleic acid or protein, the protein is                  preferably an enzyme. The target biomolecule is a                  nucleic acid, preferably selected from DNA, cDNA,                  RNA, mRNA and micro RNA, more preferably, the                  nucleic acid is a micro RNA. The enzymes are                  selected from polymerase, nicking enzyme or                  restriction enzyme and exonuclease. The first                  oligonucleotide includes a partial repeat                  structure containing a nicking enzyme recognition                  site, and the second oligonucleotide is able to                  bind, extend, deactivate and slowly release the                  products of polymerization along the first                  oligonucleotide, inducing a threshold effect. A                  fourth oligonucleotide which is a reporting probe                  is added, preferably the reporting probe is a                  fluorescent probe. A fifth oligonucleotide which                  is a cross inhibiting oligonucleotide is added                  for detecting and/or quantifying two or more                  biomolecules. The mixture is partitioned into                  droplets, preferably into water-in-oil emulsion                  droplets. The size of droplet includes between                  0.001 and 100 pL, preferably between 0.01-10 pL.                  The signal is labelled, preferably by                  fluorescence. The detection signal comprises                  detecting and/or counting the compartments                  emitted a fluorescence. The absolute                  concentration of the target biomolecule is                  measured in the tested biological sample, the                  compartments receiving the fluorescent signal and                  the non-fluorescent compartments are counted and                  their ratio is calculated. The target biomolecule                  is used as a biomarker.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - The system (100) has image acquisition device                (110) which includes at least one light source                (120), e.g. UV light source, white light source,                for illuminating a subject (101). The UV and white                light sources comprise at least one LED light                source. The image acquisition device obtains a                first white-light image and a first UV image of a                physical feature of subject. A computer system                identifies the feature pixels in first white-light                and UV images, and obtains results associated with                at least one physical condition using the                information in the feature pixels in the first                white light and UV images.
   USE - Analyzing system for analyzing physical                conditions associated with subject.
   ADVANTAGE - Provides automated detection and analysis of                subsurface skin conditions since the UV light                penetrates deeper into the skin than visible light                to detect subsurface skin conditions and allows                early diagnosis of melanoma and other skin cancer                symptoms. Reduces the glare from the skin to                provide a much clearer image since the acquisition                device includes a broadband circular polarizer.                Enables accurate measurement of pore size, hair                strands, and moles since the acquisition device                includes a zoom lens which provides images with                much higher spatial resolution.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for analyzing at least one condition                associated with physical feature of subject;                and
   a computer readable medium used for analyzing                physical conditions associated with subject.

TI Method for preparing an enriched library of            nucleic acids for detecting circulating tumor DNA in a            patient, where tumor is selected from adrenal cancer,            and anal cancer, involves identifying a            patient-specific panel of somatic variants present in a            tumor sample from a patient.
AU GOULD G
   MUZZEY D
AE MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)
   MYRIAD WOMENS HEALTH INC (MYRI-Non-standard)

AB    NOVELTY - Preparing an enriched library of nucleic                acids, involves: (a) identifying a patient-specific                panel of somatic variants present in a tumor sample                from a patient; (b) generating a subset panel of                somatic variants from the patient-specific panel,                where the subset of somatic variants comprises                multi-nucleotide variants, insertions and                deletions, and genomic rearrangements; (c)                preparing a sample of cell-free DNA (cfDNA)                fragments from the patient for sequencing; and (d)                selectively enriching the cfDNA for the subset of                somatic variants to generate an enriched                library.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves receiving an image data                from an image capture device (102) in which the                image data includes a skin portion. A first set of                information is extracted from the image data                through a machine learning system. A second set of                information is extracted from the image data                through the machine learning system. The first and                second sets of information of the image data are                scored to reflect the image quality metrics. A                threshold score reflecting acceptable image quality                metrics is identified. The image data is submitted                when the score is greater than the threshold score.                The user is prompted to retake the image data when                the score is less than the threshold score.
   USE - Method for assessing image quality metrics for                tracking changes in skin over time for detecting                skin cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - By breaking the method into steps that is                rerun, the system provides flexibility to ensure                that the analysis is on track without affecting the                entirety of the system. The image data is processed                to identify landmarks on body regions to facilitate                matching of keypoints between original and                follow-up images. The method provides accurate                detections, improves the precision in the                properties, removes a larger amount of                false-positives and facilitates comparisons of                images with subsequent sets.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for determining outlier lesions.

The nanoparticle is comprised of a                polymer material, a non-polymeric material, a                magnetic or paramagnetic material. The targeting                entity is comprised of an antibody, peptide,                protein, nucleic acid, small molecule,                carbohydrate, or lipid.
   USE - Shielded nanoparticle conjugate used for                treating, alleviating, ameliorating, relieving,                delaying onset of, inhibiting progression of,                reducing severity of, and/or reducing incidence of                symptoms or features of cancer in tumor or cancer                cells or tissue in mammal, for use in cancer                treatment system using wearable device such as                wrist-mounted device, ankle-mounted device,                waist-mounted device or chest-mounted device (all                claimed). Uses include but are not limited to                treating gastric cancer, skin cancer, e.g.,                melanomas or basal cell carcinomas, lung cancer,                urinary bladder cancer, peripheral nervous system                cancer, esophageal cancer, liver cancer, kidney                cancer, testicular cancer, salivary gland cancer,                thyroid gland cancer, adrenal gland cancer, cancer                of hematological tissues, etc.
   ADVANTAGE - The nanoparticle conjugate has a shielding or                cloaking functionality that can protect the                nanoparticle, including any agents carried by the                nanoparticle, from degradation or deactivation by                body. The pre-labeling of tumor tissue enables the                detection of extravasating cells that leave the                tumor and enter circulation which can be readily                detected by a wearable device. The losses in the                active concentration of the targeted nanoparticle                by off-target binding are minimized. The dosage                amounts are lowered and therapeutic benefit for a                given nanoparticle dosage is increased. The                toxicity due to off-target binding is minimized,                contrast is increased and false-positive rates for                tumor detection are reduced.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The shielding entity is a pH-sensitive                polymer, an idiopathic aptamer directed to a tumor                metabolite, or a protease-sensitive bivalent                peptide that binds to the antigen binding site of                the antibody. The pH-sensitive polymer degrades in                an acidic tumor microenvironment, and bivalent                anti-idiotypic aptamer with tumor                metabolite-binding domain binds to the antigen                binding site of the antibody. The conjugate further                comprises detection label, agent to be delivered to                the tumor cells and moiety that exhibits                fluorescence, luminescence, magnetic or                paramagnetic properties. The agent comprises                anti-tumor agent and contrast imaging agent.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method for in-vivo imaging in mammal of tumor                cells or tissue for killing or inhibiting growth of                tumor cells or tissue in mammal, which involves                administering the composition to the mammal where                the targeting entity is specific for the selected                marker. A time adequate to allow the targeting                entity to bind to the selected markers of the tumor                cells or tissue is waited. The cells or tissue is                imaged with a non-invasive imaging technique that                has a resolution enhanced by the presence of the                conjugate on or within the cells or tissue. The                imaging technique is selected from a group                consisting of MRI, magnetic spectroscopy, X-ray,                positron emission tomography (PET), computer                tomography (CT), ultrasonic imaging, and optical                imaging;
   cancer treatment system which has a                body-mountable device e.g. wrist-mounted device                (1500) that is mountable on external surface of                living body and configured to detect tumor cell                binding response signal transmitted through an                external surface of living body. The tumor cell                binding response signal is related to binding of                the nanoparticle conjugates with one or more tumor                cells. A processor non-invasively detects the tumor                cells based on response signal. The body-mountable                device comprises a detector (1550) for detecting                the tumor cell response signal. A modulation source                modulates tumor cell response signal differently                than a background signal. The processor                differentiates the tumor cell response signal from                background signal based on modulation by the                modulation source. An interrogating signal source                (1560) transmits tumor cell response signal in                response to the interrogating signal; and
   method for treatment of cancer                treatment.

TI Identifying covariate-informative genomic region,            by receiving methylation pattern for training samples            for nucleic acid fragments and reported covariate            values for covariates, determining methylation            features, training machine-learned model with            methylation features, and comparing predictions.
AU SAKARYA O
   VENN O C
AE GRAIL LLC (ILLU-C)
   GRAIL LLC (ILLU-C)
GA 2024D02645
AB    NOVELTY - Method for identifying a covariate-informative                genomic region, involves receiving a methylation                pattern for each of several training samples for                each of several nucleic acid fragments of the                training sample and reported covariate values for                several covariates; determining methylation                features for a genomic region of the training                sample; training a first machine-learned model with                the methylation features overlapping the genomic                region of a first subset to predict the methylation                features overlapping the genomic region; training a                second machine-learned model with the methylation                features to predict the methylation features                overlapping the genomic region; predicting a first                set of predictions of the methylation features;                predicting a second set of predictions of the                methylation features; and comparing the first set                of predictions to the second set of predictions,                and determining whether the genomic region is                informative for predicting the covariate of                interest based on the comparison.
   USE - The method is used for identifying                covariate-informative genomic region for cancer                classification. The method is used for detection                and treatment of cancer e.g. squamous cell cancer,                skin carcinoma, melanoma, lung cancer, including                small-cell lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer,                adenocarcinoma of the lung and squamous carcinoma                of the lung, cancer of the peritoneum, gastric or                stomach cancer including gastrointestinal cancer,                pancreatic cancer, cervical cancer, ovarian cancer,                liver cancer, hepatoma, hepatic carcinoma, bladder                cancer, testicular cancer, breast cancer, brain                cancer, colon cancer, rectal cancer, colorectal                cancer, endometrial or uterine carcinoma, salivary                gland carcinoma, kidney or renal cancer, prostate                cancer, vulval cancer, thyroid cancer, anal                carcinoma, penile carcinoma, head and neck cancer                and esophageal carcinoma. No biological data                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method provides improvements to cancer                detection and treatment, including improvements in                contamination detection to ensure sample quality is                maintained from collection through sequencing and                analysis to computational analysis and prediction.                The improved contamination detection improves the                assaying of samples to ensure accuracy of                analytical predictions and to avoid returning                predictions based on contaminated samples. The                method improves over conventional screening methods                tailored per cancer type by providing a single                comprehensive screening that is capable of                screening and designating an origin of a variety of                cancer types from a single cell-free DNA (CFDNA)                sample.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method for identifying a covariate-informative                genomic region, involves receiving a methylation                pattern for each of several training samples for                each of several nucleic acid fragments of the                training sample and reported covariate values for                several covariates; determining methylation                features for a genomic region of the training                sample based on the methylation patterns                overlapping the genomic region; training a first                machine-learned model with the methylation features                overlapping the genomic region of a first subset of                the several training samples to predict the                methylation features overlapping the genomic region                based on the reported values for a first set of                covariates; training a second machine-learned model                with the methylation features overlapping the                genomic region of the first subset of the several                training samples to predict the methylation                features overlapping the genomic region based on                the reported values for a second set of covariates,                that comprises the first set of covariates and a                covariate of interest; predicting a first set of                predictions of the methylation features based on                the reported covariate values for the first set of                covariates using the first machine-learned model                for each of a second subset of the several training                samples; predicting a second set of predictions of                the methylation features based on the reported                covariate values for the second set of covariates                using the second machine-learned model for each of                the second subset of the several training samples;                and comparing the first set of predictions to the                second set of predictions, and determining whether                the genomic region is informative for predicting                the covariate of interest based on the comparison.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method for training a covariate prediction                model, which involves receiving a methylation                pattern for each of training samples for each of                nucleic acid fragments of the training sample,                determining methylation features for each of the                training samples for each of the several                covariate-informative genomic regions of the                training sample based on the methylation patterns                for the nucleic acid fragments, and training a                machine-learned covariate prediction model with the                methylation features for each of the                covariate-informative genomic regions and reported                covariate values for each of the several training                samples to predict a covariate value for each of                covariates of interest based on methylation                features;
   a method for training a machine-learned cancer                classification model;
   a method for predicting a cancer prediction of                a test sample, which involves receiving a                methylation pattern for each of nucleic acid                fragments of the test sample, calculating                methylation features, predicting a covariate value                with a machine-learned covariate prediction model,                calculating a residual for each of the covariates                based on a difference between the predicted                covariate value and a reported covariate value, and                predicting the cancer prediction;
   a non-transitory computer-readable storage                medium storing instructions that, when executed by                a computer processor, cause the computer processor                to perform the method;
   a system comprising a computer processor, and                a computer-readable storage medium storing                instructions that, when executed by the computer                processor, cause the computer processor to perform                the method; and
   a treatment kit comprising collection vessels                for storing a biological sample comprising genetic                material from an individual, and a                computer-readable storage medium storing                instructions.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The training samples                  are non-cancer samples. The training samples are                  selected based on having sufficiently diverse                  covariate values for the several covariates. The                  methylation patterns are derived from whole                  genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) or targeted                  sequencing. The genomic region is a single CpG                  site. The single CpG site is not subject to                  mutation. The genomic region is CpG-rich. The                  second set of covariates further comprises a                  second covariate of interest that is not in the                  first set of covariates. The first                  machine-learned model and the second                  machine-learned model each comprise a                  machine-learned regression model for continuous                  covariates or a machine-learned classification                  model for discrete covariates. The first                  machine-learned model and the second                  machine-learned model is a deep-learning neural                  network; a support vector machine; a set of                  decision trees; or an autoencoder. The treatment                  kit further comprises several probes targeting                  several covariate-informative genomic regions,                  and reagents for isolating nucleic acid fragments                  in the biological sample. Preferred Method: The                  method involves comparing the first set of                  predictions to the second set of predictions by                  calculating a F-statistic based on the first set                  of predictions and the second set of predictions.                  The method further involves filtering the                  methylation patterns of the nucleic acid                  fragments of the test sample with p-value                  filtering to identify a set of anomalous                  methylation patterns, where the cancer                  prediction, predicted with the machine-learned                  cancer classification model, is further based on                  the anomalous methylation patterns, detecting                  whether there is a sample swap contamination by                  comparing the predicted covariate values for the                  several covariates to reported covariate values                  reported by a user; and predicting the cancer                  prediction responsive to detecting no sample swap                  contamination. The method for training a                  machine-learned cancer classification model                  involves receiving a methylation pattern for each                  of training samples comprising cancer samples and                  non-cancer samples for each of nucleic acid                  fragments of the training sample, determining                  methylation features for each of the training                  samples for each of the covariate-informative                  genomic regions of the training sample based on                  the methylation patterns for the nucleic acid                  fragments, predicting a covariate value for each                  of covariates based on the methylation features                  for each of the covariate-informative genomic                  regions for each of the training samples with a                  machine-learned covariate prediction model,                  calculating a residual for each of the training                  samples for each of the covariates based on a                  difference between the predicted covariate value                  and a reported covariate value, and training a                  machine-learned cancer classification model using                  the residuals for the several covariates and the                  methylation patterns of the training samples to                  predict a cancer prediction based on the                  residuals for the covariates and the methylation                  patterns for each of the covariate-informative                  genomic regions. Preferred Conditions: The                  methylation features for the CpG site are a                  combination of: a methylation density of the CpG                  site; a count or a percentage of highly                  methylated fragments covering the CpG site; and a                  count or a percentage of highly unmethylated                  fragments covering the CpG site. The genomic                  region covers several CpG sites. The methylation                  features for the genomic region are a combination                  of: a methylation density of the genomic region;                  a count or a percentage of highly methylated                  fragments covering the genomic region; and a                  count or a percentage of highly unmethylated                  fragments covering the genomic region. The size                  of the genomic region is selected based on a                  predictive power of the covariate of interest.                  The covariates are chosen from a combination                  comprising an age; a biological sex; a hybrid                  covariate of age and biological sex; a race; and                  a smoking status.

TI Method for isolating, capturing circulating tumor            cell from patient in cancer treatment involves            contacting biological sample with solid phase-capture            binding protein complex; separating the tumor cell            complex from sample by magnetic field.
