GA 2014P44398
AB    NOVELTY - Method (M1) for isolating, capturing, or                enriching circulating tumor cell from patient                involves obtaining biological sample from patient;                obtaining capture binding protein linked to solid                phase to form solid phase-capture binding protein                complex; contacting biological sample with solid                phase-capture binding protein complex to form solid                phase-capture binding protein-circulating tumor                cell complex; and separating solid phase-capture                binding protein-circulating tumor cell complex from                sample and unbound magnetic particle-capture                binding protein complexes by magnetic field on the                sample.
   USE - For isolating, capturing, enriching, detecting                or identifying a circulating tumor cell from a                patient; for isolating or capturing an intact cell                from patient; for detecting and treating cancer in                patient; for monitoring progression of cancer in a                subject undergoing therapeutic treatment; for                determining cancer prognosis in subject; and for                predicting responsiveness of subject having cancer                to course of treatment; where the patient has                breast cancer, colon cancer, lung cancer, prostate                cancer, testicular cancer, brain cancer, skin                cancer, rectal cancer, gastric cancer, esophageal                cancer, sarcomas, tracheal cancer, head and neck                cancer, pancreatic cancer, liver cancer, ovarian                cancer, lymphoid cancer, cervical cancer, vulvar                cancer, melanoma, mesothelioma, renal cancer,                bladder cancer, thyroid cancer, bone cancer,                carcinoma, sarcoma, and soft tissue cancer                (preferably prostate cancer or breast cancer,                especially prostate cancer) (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method does not rely on existing capture                technologies, and provides capturing of circulating                tumor cell (CTC) with mesenchymal phenotype which                is missed by prior art epithelial-based                technologies. The method also provides correlating                CTC detection to diagnosis, monitoring, and                prognosis of disease in cancer patients.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method (M1) for isolating, capturing,                enriching, detecting or identifying a circulating                tumor cell from patient involves obtaining                biological sample from a patient; obtaining at                least one capture binding protein linked to a solid                phase to form a solid phase-capture binding protein                complex; contacting the biological sample with the                solid phase-capture binding protein complex to                allow the solid phase-capture binding protein                complex to bind at least one epithelial-mesenchymal                transition (EMT) biomarker on the circulating tumor                cell to form a solid phase-capture binding                protein-circulating tumor cell complex (C1); and                separating the tumor cell complex (C1) from the                sample and unbound magnetic particle-capture                binding protein complexes by application of                external magnetic field on sample, thereby                isolating, capturing, or enriching the circulating                tumor cell. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a method (M2) for isolating or capturing an                intact cell from patient, where the cell is                &#946; -catenin positive,                4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) positive, and                cluster of differentiation 45 (CD45) negative,                method involving obtaining biological sample from                patient; obtaining capture binding protein, which                is linked to solid phase to form solid                phase-capture binding protein complex (C2);                contacting the biological sample with the protein                complex (C2) to allow the protein complex (C2) to                bind EMT biomarker on the intact cell to form solid                phase-capture binding protein-intact cell complex;                which is then separated from the sample and unbound                magnetic particle-capture binding protein complexes                by application of an external magnetic field on the                sample, thereby isolating or capturing the intact                cell; and
   a kit for isolating or capturing a circulating                tumor cell in biological sample, comprising an                antibody linked to magnetic particle, where the                antibody binds specifically to EMT biomarker and                staining reagent.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Cell: The circulating tumor cell                  and the intact cell have mesenchymal phenotype.                  The capture binding protein is an antibody.                  Preferred Biological Sample: The biological                  sample comprises a tissue sample or fluid sample                  from an organism (preferably blood).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  involves confirming the circulating tumor cell                  which comprises at least one of DAPI staining,                  &#946; -catenin detection, CD45 detection and                  CD31 detection. The circulating tumor cell is                  confirmed if DAPI staining is positive,                  &#946; -catenin expression is positive, CD45                  expression is negative, and CD31 expression is                  negative. The method further involves determining                  the presence or absence of at least one prostate                  cancer-specific genomic event selected from                  androgen receptor amplification, phosphatase and                  tensin homolog (PTEN) loss, gene fusion of                  transmembrane protease, serine 2 (TMPRSS2) gene                  and/or ETS related (ERG) gene. The determining                  step is performed by fluorescence in situ                  hybridization (FISH). The solid phase is a                  magnetic or paramagnetic microparticle. The                  method (M1) further involves determining the                  level of circulating tumor cell in the tumor cell                  complex (C1); comparing the level of circulating                  tumor cell to a reference level of circulating                  tumor cell; detecting cancer in the subject if                  the level of circulating tumor cell is higher                  than the reference level of circulating tumor                  cell; and administrating a therapy against cancer                  to the subject identified as having cancer. The                  method (M1) further involves correlating the                  level of circulating tumor cell with the                  progression of cancer in the subject, where if                  the level of the circulating tumor cell is higher                  as compared to the level of the circulating tumor                  cell in an earlier biological sample from the                  subject, the subject is identified as having                  progression of cancer; and administering a                  therapy against cancer to the subject identified                  as having progression of cancer. The step of                  determining the level of circulating tumor cell                  in the tumor cell complex (C1) comprises                  confirming the circulating tumor cell. Preferred                  Components: The EMT biomarker is OB-cadherin,                  N-cadherin, vimentin, E-cadherin, fibroblast                  growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) splice variant                  isoforms, or CD133 (preferably OB-cadherin or                  N-cadherin, especially OB-cadherin). The staining                  reagent comprises phycoerytherin-labeled                  anti-&#946; -catenin antibody or                  allophycocyanin-labeled anti-CD45 antibody.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Test details are described, but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Sensor apparatus for determining composition            and/or concentration of selected volatile and            non-volatile compounds, comprises chemically sensitive            sensor comprising cubic nanoparticle conductive cores            capped with organic coating.
AU DOVGOLEVSKY E
   HAICK H
AE TECHNION RES&DEV FOUND LTD (TECR-C)

GA 2009J75639
AB    NOVELTY - Sensor apparatus comprises chemically                sensitive sensor(s) for detecting volatile and                non-volatile compounds, where chemically sensitive                sensor comprises cubic nanoparticle conductive                cores capped with an organic coating.
   USE - The sensor apparatus is for a sensor system                used for determining a composition and/or                concentration of selected volatile and non-volatile                compounds (indicative of a disease, spoilage in                food products, or environmental pollution) in a                sample, or for detecting volatile and non-volatile                compounds in a sample comprising bodily fluid(s) or                secretion comprising serum, urine, feces, sweat,                vaginal discharge, saliva, or sperm. The disease is                acute asthma, hepatic encephalopathy, rheumatoid                arthritis, renal failure, schizophrenia, ketosis,                cardiopulmonary disease, uremia, diabetes mellitus,                dysgeusia/dysosmia, cystinuria, cirrhosis,                histidinemia, tyrosinemia, halitosis,                phenylketonuria, or preferably cancer (all                claimed), e.g. carcinomas, sarcomas, myelomas,                leukemias, lymphomas, and mixed type tumors                including lymphoproliferative disorders, breast                cancer, ovarian cancer, prostate cancer, cervical                cancer, endometrial cancer, bone cancer, liver                cancer, stomach cancer, colon cancer, pancreatic                cancer, cancer of the thyroid, head and neck                cancer, cancer of the central nervous system,                cancer of peripheral nervous system, skin cancer,                kidney cancer, their metastases, hepatocellular                carcinoma, hepatoma, hepatoblastoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, esophageal carcinoma, thyroid                carcinoma, ganglioblastoma, fibrosarcoma,                myxosarcoma, liposarcoma, chondrosarcoma,                osteogenic sarcoma, chordoma, angiosarcoma, and                endotheliosarcoma. The sensor apparatus is useful                for differentiating between patients with different                types of cancer; detecting pollutants in water or                air for environmental monitoring, i.e. warning of                pollution incidents, by-products, and wastewater,                detection of nitric oxide and sulfur dioxide in                polluted air and car gas emission, and detection of                spills in the chemical, pharmaceutical, and                biotechnology industries; detecting biomarkers for                diagnostic and prognostic purposes; and detecting                volatile and non-volatile compounds from breath                directly exhaled by the subject on the apparatus,                without a need for preconcentrating or                dehumidifying the sample. It is for installing in                any electronic device including watch or cellular                phone, for use as a warning system for the start of                an infection or other disease in the body of an                individual.
   ADVANTAGE - The apparatus and system have sensitivity of                less than 1 ppm, preferably less than 10 ppb for                volatile and non-volatile compounds to be detected.                Cubic nanoparticles capped with organic molecules                have improved sensitivity as compared to spherical                nanoparticles capped with organic coating. They are                more sensitive, more controlled, and more suitable                to differentiate between subtle differences in                mixtures of volatile and/or non-volatile compounds,                than films/assemblies of spherical nanoparticles                capped with organic coating. The fraction of voids                between adjacent cubic nanoparticles is minimized;                while the fraction of voids between adjacent                spherical nanoparticles in films is larger. The                increased sensitivity of cubic nanoparticles                compared to spherical nanoparticles is even more                pronounced at increased flow rates to produce                values, which are more than 11 times the response                of spherical nanoparticles capped with organic                coating.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a sensor system having a sensor apparatus; and                a learning and pattern recognition analyzer, which                receives sensor output signals and compares them to                stored data; and
   a method of determining a composition and/or                concentration of selected volatile and non-volatile                compounds in a sample.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing is a schematic view illustrating                the swelling- (or aggregation)-based sensing                mechanism for films/assemblies of molecularly                modified cubic nanoparticles capped with an organic                coating, (I) before analyte adsorption, (II) after                analyte adsorption, (III) swelling following                analyte adsorption, or (IV) aggregation following                analyte adsorption.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - METALLURGY - Preferred Component: The cubic nanoparticle                  conductive cores are gold (Au), silver (Ag),                  nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), platinum (Pt),                  palladium (Pd), copper (Cu), aluminum (Al),                  Au/Ag, Au/Cu, Au/Ag/Cu, Au/Pt, Au/Pd,                  Au/Ag/Cu/Pd, Pt-rhodium (Rh), Ni-Co, or                  Pt-Ni-iron (Fe). The cubic nanoparticles capped                  with an organic coating are in a configuration                  from one dimensional (1D) wires, 2D films, or 3D                  assemblies.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Component: The cubic nanoparticle                  conductive cores are capped with an organic                  coating comprising a monolayer or multilayers of                  organic compounds, which are small molecules,                  monomers, oligomers, or polymers. The organic                  coating is alkylthiols with 3-24C chains,                  &#969; -functionalized alkanethiolates,                  arenethiolate, (&#947;                  -mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane, dialkyl                  disulfides, xanthates, oligonucleotides,                  polynucleotides, peptides, proteins, enzymes,                  polysaccharides, and/or phospholipids.

AB    NOVELTY - A polypeptide having an amino acid sequence of                any one of fully defined sequences comprising 6                amino acids (SEQ ID NO. 1-12) given in the                specification, and specifically binds apoptotic                cells, is new.
   USE - The polypeptide is useful as a composition for                preventing and treating stroke, myocardial                infarction, arteriosclerosis, and neoplastic                disease. It is also used as a composition for                imaging stroke, myocardial infarction,                arteriosclerosis, and neoplastic disease. The                polypeptide is useful for detection of apoptotic                cells and for drug delivery. It can also be used                for the preparation of an agent treating neoplastic                disease, stroke, myocardial infarction, or                arteriosclerosis. The neoplastic disease is                selected from colon cancer, lung cancer, stomach                cancer, esophageal cancer, pancreatic cancer,                gallbladder cancer, renal cancer, bladder cancer,                prostate cancer, testicular cancer, cervical                cancer, endometrial cancer, choriocarcinoma,                ovarian cancer, breast cancer, thyroid cancer,                brain cancer, head and neck cancer, malignant                melanoma, skin cancer, liver cancer, leukemia,                lymphoma, multiple myeloma, chronic myelogenous                leukemia, neuroblastoma, or aplastic anemia (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A polypeptide having an amino acid sequence of                any one of fully defined sequences comprising 6                amino acids (SEQ ID NO. 1-12) given in the                specification, and specifically binds apoptotic                cells, is new. Cys-Gln-Arg-Pro-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO.                1), Cys-Ser-Val-Ala-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO. 2),                Cys-Asn-Arg-Pro-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO. 3),                Cys-Gln-Lys-Pro-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO. 4),                Cys-Gln-Arg-Pro-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 5),                Cys-Asn-Lys-Pro-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO. 6),                Cys-Asn-Arg-Pro-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 7),                Cys-Gln-Lys-Pro-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 8),                Cys-Asn-Lys-Pro-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 9),                Cys-Thr-Val-Ala-Pro-Arg (SEQ ID NO. 10),                Cys-Ser-Val-Ala-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 11), and                Cys-Thr-Val-Ala-Pro-Lys (SEQ ID NO. 12).                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   (1) a polynucleotide having nucleotide                sequence encoding the polypeptide;
   (2) a vector comprising the                polynucleotide;
   (3) a transfectant transformed with the                vector;
   (4) a composition for detecting apoptotic                cells comprising the polypeptide as an effective                ingredient;
   (5) a method for detecting apoptotic cells                comprising: (a) mixing the polypeptide with a                sample: (b) removing unbound or unspecifically                bound polypeptide; and (c) detecting the binding                and the location of the polypeptide;
   (6) a composition for drug delivery comprising                the peptide as an effective ingredient;
   (7) a pharmaceutical composition for                preventing and treating neoplastic disease                comprising the peptide and an antitumor agent bound                to it as effective ingredients; and
   (8) a composition for imaging neoplastic                disease site comprising the peptide as an effective                ingredient.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Composition: The polypeptide is                  labeled with coloring enzyme, radioactive                  isotope, chromophore, scintillating material,                  fluorescer, super paramagnetic particles, or                  ultrasuper paramagnetic particles. The                  polypeptide is bound with anyone selected from                  paclitaxel, doxorubicin, vincristine,                  daunorubicin, vinblastine, actinomycin-D,                  docetaxel, etoposide, teniposide, bisantrene,                  homoharringtonine, Gleevec (STI-571), cisplatin,                  5-fluorouracil, Adriamycin, methotrexate,                  busulfan, chlorambucil, cyclophosphamide,                  melphalan, nitrogen mustard, nitrosourea,                  streptokinase, urokinase, alteplase, angiotensin                  II inhibitor, aldosterone receptor inhibitor,                  erythropoietin, N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA)                  receptor inhibitor lovastatin, rapamycin,                  Celebrex, Ticlopin, Marimastat, or Trocade. The                  antitumor agent is selected from paclitaxel,                  doxorubicin, vincristine, daunorubicin,                  vinblastine, actinomycin-D, docetaxel, etoposide,                  teniposide, bisantrene, homoharringtonine,                  Gleevec (STI-571), cisplatin, 5-fluorouracil,                  Adriamycin, methotrexate, busulfan, chlorambucil,                  cyclophosphamide, melphalan, nitrogen mustard and                  nitrosourea. The composition is specific to the                  disease selected from neoplastic disease, stroke,                  myocardial infarction, or arteriosclerosis.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Cerebroprotective; Vasotropic;                Cardiant; Antiarteriosclerotic. Test details are                described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration can be through oral,                transdermal, subcutaneous, intracutaneous,                intranasal, intraperitoneal, intramuscular,                subdural, or intravenous route. No dosage details                given.

AB    NOVELTY - The device has a cone section (6) whose                maximum diameter ranges between 5-10 cm and of                depth between 5-15 mm. A circular field effect                transistor (FET) microphone (5) of diameter between                0.5-2 mm is arranged at the pointed end of the cone                section. A lid (3) with LCD is provided in the                upper portion.
   USE - For ultra-stethoscope used in non-invasive                diagnosis of diseases such as cancers, tumors in                human body/animal body. Also for use in fetus                monitoring, neoplastic tumor detection, insect                infestation testing.
   ADVANTAGE - Facilitates communication with personal                computer thereby provides isometric display of                blood flow velocity. Skin noise is reduced since                direct skin contact is avoided during measurements.                Eliminates need for undressing of clothes of                patients during diagnosis, thereby promotes usage                efficiency.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   Dual acoustic device assembly;
   Electronic stethoscope

GA 2020A33949
AB    NOVELTY - Method (M1) for detecting a biological or                chemical entity in a sample, where the biological                or chemical entity is associated with extracellular                vesicles, involves (a) processing the sample, (b)                detecting the presence of extracellular vesicles                using a detection assay and to isolate the                extracellular vesicles, (c) processing the                extracellular vesicles to expose or release the                biological or chemical entity, and (e) detecting                the biological or chemical entity released from the                extracellular vesicle.
   USE - The method is useful for (a) detecting a                biological or chemical entity in a sample or (b)                detecting fungal antigens in a urine sample. The                biological or chemical entity is biomarker for a                disease or disorder. The disease or disorder                comprises cancer, cardiovascular disease,                respiratory disease, cerebrovascular disease,                Alzheimer's disease, diabetes, influenza,                pneumonia, nephritis, or cirrhosis. The cancer is                chosen from carcinoma of the bladder, breast,                bronchial, colon, kidney, liver, lung, esophagus,                gall bladder, ovary, pancreas, stomach, cervix,                thyroid, prostate, and skin; small cell lung                cancer, squamous cell carcinoma, hematopoietic                tumors of lymphoid lineage, leukemia, acute                lymphocytic leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia,                B-cell lymphoma, T-cell- lymphoma, Hodgkin's                lymphoma, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, hairy cell                lymphoma, Burkett's lymphoma, hematopoietic tumors                of myeloid lineage, acute and chronic myelogenous                leukemias, myelodysplastic syndrome and                promyelocytic leukemia, tumors of mesenchymal                origin, fibrosarcoma and rhabdomyosarcoma, tumors                of the central and peripheral nervous system,                astrocytoma, neuroblastoma, glioma and schwannomas,                melanoma, seminoma, teratocarcinoma, osteosarcoma,                xenoderoma pigmentosum, keratoacanthoma, thyroid                follicular cancer and Kaposi's sarcoma. The fungal                antigens are from above-mentioned drug-sensitive                fungus or drug-resistant fungus (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                (M2) for detecting fungal antigens in a urine                sample, where the fungal antigens are associated                with extracellular vesicles, which involves                processing the sample using a desalting column,                using a detection assay to detect the presence of                extracellular vesicles and to isolate the                extracellular vesicles, processing the                extracellular vesicles to expose or release the                fungal antigens, and detecting the fungal antigens                released from the extracellular vesicle.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The extracellular vesicles                  are made by exogenous infectious agents and                  contain and/or express proteins, glycoproteins,                  peptides, lipids, nucleic acids or other cellular                  components. The step of processing the sample                  involves passing the sample to enrich for                  extracellular vesicles, such as through a                  desalting column that yields fragmentation of                  interfering host proteins, passing the sample                  through a high performance liquid chromatography                  column, ethanol precipitation, centrifugation,                  filtration, separation based on size, separation                  based on charge, filtration based on morphology,                  microfluidic processing to separate based on size                  and flow, performing immunomagnetic isolation,                  precipitation, immunoprecipitation, enzymatic                  degradation, coagulation, sterilization,                  incubation, or lysis. The step of processing the                  extracellular vesicles to expose or release the                  biological or chemical entity comprises lysis by                  detergent. The step of detecting the biological                  or chemical entity comprises the use of an                  immunoassay. The immunoassay involves detecting                  the presence of at least one antibody-antigen                  complex, where the detection of the presence of                  at least one antibody-antigen complex is                  diagnostic of the presence of a microbe in the                  sample. The sample is obtained from a source                  chosen from bacteria, viruses, fungi,                  mycobacteria, protozoa, molds, yeasts, plants,                  humans, non-humans, multi-cellular parasite,                  animals, and Archaebacteria. The sample is                  obtained from a human source. The sample is                  obtained from a source chosen from urine, tissue,                  blood, serum, plasma, sputum, bronchoalveolar                  lavage fluid, saliva, tear, vaginal secretion,                  umbilical cord blood, chorionic villi, amniotic                  fluid, embryonic tissue, lymph fluid,                  cerebrospinal fluid, mucosa secretion, peritoneal                  fluid, ascitic fluid, fecal matter, and body                  exudates. The biological or chemical entity from                  a species different from the species from which                  the sample was taken, where the different species                  is chosen from fungi, bacteria, viruses,                  mycobacteria, protozoa, molds, yeasts, plants,                  humans, non-humans, multi-cellular parasite,                  animals, and Archaebacteria. The method (M1)                  involves (a) processing the sample to                  decrease/minimize/reduce human intelectin (hlntL)                  binding of microbial antigens including                  galactofuranose residues present in the sample,                  (b) using a detection assay to detect the                  presence of extracellular vesicles and to isolate                  the extracellular vesicles, (c) processing the                  extracellular vesicles to expose or release the                  biological or chemical entity, (d) contacting the                  treated sample with at least one antibody                  specific for at least one, antigen,                  polysaccharide or glycoprotein comprising a                  galactofuranose residue in an effective amount to                  produce a detectable amount of antibody-antigen                  complex, and (e) detecting the presence of at                  least one antibody-antigen complex, where the                  detection of the presence of at least one                  antibody-antigen complex is diagnostic of the                  presence of microbial extracellular vesicles in                  the sample. The step of treating the sample                  involves contacting the sample with a substrate                  in step (a), where the substrate comprises an                  intelectin-binding component, where the                  intelectin-binding component comprises glycerol,                  3-keto-2-deoxyoctonic acid;                  D-glycerol-1-phosphate, D-mannoheptose,                  sepharose, or sepharose-containing particles                  (i.e. latex, polystyrene or glass beads,                  microspheres or gels), where the substrate                  comprises a desalting column. The detection of                  the presence of an antibody-antigen complex is                  diagnostic of the presence of Ascomycetes fungi                  in the body. Preferred Microorganisms: The fungus                  is a drug-sensitive fungus or a drug-resistant                  fungus. The fungus is e.g. Aspergillus sp.,                  A.fumigatus, A.flavus, A.niger, A.nidulans,                  A.terreus, A.sydowi, A.glaucus, Candida sp.,                  C.albicans, C.tropicalis, C.parapsilosis,                  C.stellatoidea, C.krusei, C.tropicalis,                  Cryptococcus sp., Histoplasma sp., Coccidioides                  sp., Paracoccidioides sp., Blastomyces sp.,                  Zygomycetes, Rhizopus sp., Rhizomucor sp., Mucor                  sp., Mortierella sp., Cunninghamella sp.,                  Saksenaea sp., Saccharomyces, and Pneumocystis                  sp.. The parasite is a drug-sensitive parasite or                  a drug- resistant parasite. The parasite is                  chosen from Leishmania sp., L.donovani,                  Plasmodium sp., P.vivax, P.ovale, P.falciparum,                  P.malariae, P.knowlesi, Trypanosoma sp., T.cruzi,                  Strongyloides sp., Toxoplasma sp., T.gondii, and                  Helminths. The bacteria is a drug-sensitive                  bacteria or a drug- resistant bacteria. The                  bacteria is e.g. Acidaminococcus, Acinetobacter,                  Aeromonas, Alcaligenes, Bacteroides, Bordetella,                  Branhamella, Brucella, Campylobacter,                  Chromobacterium, Citrobacter, C.freundii,                  Enterobacter, E.aerogenes, E.cloacae,                  Enterococcus, E.faecalis, E.faecium, Escherichia,                  E.coli, Flavobacterium, Francisella,                  Fusobacterium, Haemophilus, Hafnia alvei,                  Klebsiella, K.oxytoca, K.pneumoniae, Legionella,                  Moraxella, Morganella, Morganella morganii,                  Neisseria, Plesiomonas, Proteus, Providencia,                  Proteus mirabilis, Pseudomonas, P.aeruginosa,                  Salmonella, S.typhimurium, Serratia,                  S.marcescens, Shigella, S.flexneri, Veillonella,                  Vibrio, Peptostreptococcus, Bacillus, B.cereus,                  Clostridium, Lactobacillus, Listeria,                  L.monocytogenes, Propionibacterium, and                  Eubacterium. The virus is a DNA virus or an RNA                  virus. The virus is e.g. retrovirus, pathogenic                  virus, non-pathogenic virus, drug-resistant                  virus, drug-sensitive virus, adeno-associated                  virus, bird flu virus, cauliflower mosaic virus,                  cytomegalovirus (CMV), dengue virus, Epstein-Barr                  virus, feline leukemia virus, flavivirus,                  hemorrhagic fever viruses, hepatitis virus                  including hepatitis A, B, C, and B, viruses,                  herpes simplex virus, human herpesvirus type A                  and B, HIV, human papilloma virus, influenza                  virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Respiratory                  syncytial virus, Rubella virus, rotavirus, SARS,                  tomato bushy stunt virus, varicella-zoster virus,                  and vaccinia virus. TI All-normal-dispersion based supercontinuum system,            has pulsed light-source-device for generating train of            light pulses, and hollow core fiber for generating            supercontinuum spectrum based on normal            dispersion.
AU CHRISTENSEN E N
   DEMENIKOV M H
AE NKT PHOTONICS AS (HAMM-C)
GA 202572903G
AB    NOVELTY - The system (1) has a pulsed                light-source-device (2) for generating train of                light pulses (3, 7), where each light pulse is                defined in a frequency domain, and each light-pulse                of the train of light-pulses is defined by a first                center-wavelength. An all-normal dispersion                (ANDi)-fiber i.e. hollow core fiber (4), is                optically coupled to the pulsed light-source-device                and configured to receive the light-pulses of the                train of light-pulses, where the ANDi-fiber                comprises normal dispersion between an absolute                value and ANDi-wavelength range. The hollow core                fiber generates a supercontinuum (SC) spectrum (5)                based on the normal dispersion.
   USE - ANDi based SC system.
   ADVANTAGE - The system enhances contrast, sensitivity,                penetration, and speed, and prevents early-stage                detection of skin cancer and skin diseases.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of an ANDi                SC system.
   1SC system
   2Pulsed light-source-device
   3, 7Light pulses
   4Hollow core fiber
   5SC spectrum

TI Probe for obtaining quantitative optical            properties and chromophore concentrations of tissue            components of skin for e.g. aesthetic application, has            detector fiber detecting backscattered and/or reflected            light returned from tissue.
AU DURKIN A J
   TSENG S
AE UNIV CALIFORNIA (REGC-C)
GA 2010H12236
AB    NOVELTY - The probe (20) has a source fiber (10)                providing light to expose a tissue (16), where                light is directed onto a diffuser layer (14) and                from the diffuser layer to and/or into the tissue.                A detector fiber (12) arranged relative to the                diffuser layer detects backscattered and/or                reflected light returned from the tissue without                transmission through the diffuser layer. A                spectrometer optically coupled to the detector                fiber analyzes the backscattered and/or reflected                light from the tissue to determine quantitative                optical properties and chromophore concentrations                of tissue components.
   USE - Probe for obtaining quantitative optical                properties and chromophore concentrations of tissue                components of skin for aesthetic, therapeutic and                diagnostic applications. Uses include but are not                limited to applications such as monitoring of skin                blood oxygenation and melanin concentration,                detection of breast cancer, laser surgery and                photodynamic therapy.
   ADVANTAGE - The probe ensures decreased separation between                the source fiber and the detector fiber, so as to                reduce the influence from an underlying substrate,                thus increasing the accuracy of the recovered                optical properties.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                method for self-calibrating a tissue probe.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a probe                including a diffuser layer provided with a                reflective boundary.
   Source fiber (10)
   Detector fiber (12)
   Diffuser layer (14)
   Tissue (16)
   Probe (20)

TI Diagnosis of malignant proliferative disorder in            subject involves measuring prothrombinase activity in            sample and comparing the activity with that of control            value, where sample with higher activity is indicative            of malignant disorder.
AU INBAL A
   RABIZADEH E
AE MOR RES APPL LTD (RESA-C)
   UNIV RAMOT AT TEL AVIV LTD (UYTA-C)
   UNIV RAMOT AT TEL AVIV LTD (UYTA-C)
   MOR RES APPL LTD (RESA-C)
GA 2012B07851
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosis (M1) of a malignant proliferative                disorder or malignancy in a subject involves:                measuring prothrombinase activity in a sample from                the subject; and comparing the prothrombinase                activity with that of a control value, where a                sample with prothrombinase activity higher than                control is indicative of the presence of a                malignant disorder or malignancy in the                subject.
   USE - For diagnosis or prognosis of a malignant                proliferative disorder (selected from pancreatic                cancer, breast cancer, squamous cell carcinoma,                multiple myeloma, prostate cancer, Langerhans' cell                sarcoma, thyroid papillary cancer, melanoma,                esophageal cancer, endometrial sarcoma, mammary                gland cancer, mediastinal large cell lymphoma,                Hodgkin lymphoma, lung carcinoma, small cell lung                cancer or non-small-cell lung carcinoma, kidney,                uterus, prostate, bladder, colon, or ovarian                cancer, mixed tumors of salivary gland, tumors in                lip and oral cavity, carcinoma of the eyelid and                carcinoma of the conjunctiva, pharynx, larynx,                paranasal sinuses, colonic adenomas,                adenocarcinomas, sarcomas, liposarcoma, myxoid,                synovial sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma (alveolar),                extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, Ewing's tumor,                other include testicular and ovarian dysgerminoma,                retinoblastoma, Wilm's tumor, neuroblastoma,                malignant melanoma, mesothelioma, breast, skin,                malignant melanoma of the conjunctiva, malignant                melanoma of the uvea, retinoblastoma, carcinoma of                the lacrimal gland, sarcoma of the orbit, brain,                spinal cord, vascular system, hemangiosarcoma,                malignant lymphoma, Kaposi's sarcoma, myeloid                leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia, acute                myelogenous leukemia, acute myelogenous leukemia                with maturation, acute promyelocytic leukemia,                acute non-lymphocytic leukemia, acute                non-lymphocytic leukemia with increased basophiles,                acute monocytic leukemia, acute myelomonocytic                leukemia with eosinophilia, lymphocytic leukemia,                acute lymphoblastic leukemia, chronic lymphocytic                leukemia and myeloproliferative diseases) in a                subject; for diagnosis of malignancy in a sample                (all claimed); for monitoring the efficacy of                cancer treatment; for detection, diagnosis,                assessment of prognosis, screening of cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The detection of FGL-2 prothrombinase activity                higher than control in a sample is indicative of                the presence of a malignant disorder in the                subject. When the activity remains high or                increases over time in the subject, it is an                indication of poor prognosis or resistance to                therapy. Thus, decreasing FGL-2 prothrombinase                activity over time indicates recovery for the                subject. The diagnosis or prognosis of malignant                disorders is effected through measuring the                activity of the prothrombinase enzyme in the                sample.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   prognosis (M2) of a malignant proliferative                disorder in a subject involving: measuring                prothrombinase activity in a sample from the                subject at different time points, where the time                points being before, during and after treatment of                the disorder; and comparing the values of                prothrombinase activity obtained for the different                time points in first step, where increasing                prothrombinase activity over time indicates a poor                prognosis or resistance to therapy whereas a                decreasing prothrombinase activity over time                indicates recovery for the subject; and
   a kit for diagnosis or prognosis of a                malignant proliferative disorder comprising at                least one reagent for measuring prothrombinase                activity; and instructions for measuring                prothrombinase activity in a sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The sample comprises                  FGL-2 expressing cells; peripheral blood                  mononuclear cells (PBMC). The sample is a blood                  sample.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The prothrombinase                  activity comprises fibrinogen-like protein 2                  (FGL-2) prothrombinase activity.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (M1) and (M2)                  involves: measuring prothrombinase activity of                  the prothrombinase enzyme in a sample. Preferred                  Kit: The kit further comprises: at least one                  device for collecting a sample to be tested; and                  optionally at least one control sample. Preferred                  Components: The reagent for measuring                  prothrombinase activity comprises prothrombin.                  The prothrombinase activity measured represents                  FGL-2 prothrombinase activity.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

GA 201716615D
AB    NOVELTY - Array comprises carbohydrates moieties                immobilized on a substrate, where each carbohydrate                moiety is deposited at a discrete location on the                substrate, and the array is fabricated by providing                a substrate, coating the substrate with                nitrocellulose, immobilizing several carbohydrate                moieties at discrete locations on the surface of                the substrate.
   USE - The array is useful for detecting complexes,                diagnosing disease, treatment monitoring or                recurrence monitoring of a subject having cancer,                carcinoma, neoplasm or hyperplasia and determining                therapeutic efficacy of an antineoplastic agent for                cancer treatment in subject, preferably human,                where the cancer is chosen from sarcoma, skin                cancer, leukemia, lymphoma, brain cancer,                glioblastoma, lung cancer, breast cancer, oral                cancer, head-and-neck cancer, nasopharyngeal                cancer, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer, liver                cancer, bile duct cancer, gallbladder cancer,                bladder cancer, pancreatic cancer, intestinal                cancer, colorectal cancer, kidney cancer, cervix                cancer, endometrial cancer, ovarian cancer,                testicular cancer, buccal cancer, oropharyngeal                cancer, laryngeal cancer and prostate cancer (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The array exhibits excellent sensitivity,                specificity and accuracy of glycan-linked surfaces                in the detection of cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Array comprises carbohydrates moieties                immobilized on a substrate. The carbohydrate                moieties has a structure of formula: G-A-Z, where                each G-A-Z moiety is deposited at a discrete                location on the substrate, and the array is                fabricated by providing a substrate, coating the                substrate with nitrocellulose, and immobilizing                G-A-Z moieties at discrete locations on the surface                of the substrate.
   G=tumor associated carbohydrate antigens                (TACAs);
   A=moiety comprising an alkyl, ester or amide                group;and
   Z=lipid chains or spacer group with lipid                chains.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   method (M1) for characterizing the array,                which involves contacting the immobilized G-A-Z                moieties with a labeled antibody to the TACAs,                forming complexes between the antibody and the                glycan and detecting the complexes formed between                the antibody and the glycan;
   carbohydrate compound of formula G-A-Z-X                (I);
   carbohydrate compounds of the formulas                (II)-(IX);
   tumor associated carbohydrate antigen-bound                compounds of formula (X)-(IVX);
   method (M2) for disease diagnosis, treatment                monitoring or recurrence monitoring of a subject                having cancer, carcinoma, neoplasm or hyperplasia,                which involves (a) providing a sample containing                antibodies from a subject suspected of having                cancer, (b) contacting the sample to allow binding                of antibodies in the sample to one or more of G-A-Z                moiety, (c) detecting the amount of one or more                bound antibodies and (d) determining the disease                state of the subject based on the bound antibodies,                where the disease state is indicated based on the                relative antibody binding levels as compared with                disease-free subject;
   method (M3) for detecting a complex, which                involves (a) providing a sample containing                antibodies from a subject suspected of having                cancer, carcinoma, neoplasm or hyperplasia, (b)                contacting the sample to allow binding of                antibodies in the sample to one or more G-A-Z                moieties, (c) detecting the amount of one or more                bound antibodies and (d) ascertaining the relative                antibody binding levels as compared with a                disease-free subject; and
   method (M4) for determining the therapeutic                efficacy of an antineoplastic agent for cancer                treatment in a subject, which involves (a)                providing a sample from a subject, (b) contacting                an array comprising one or more tumor associated                antigens (TACAs) with the sample, (c) detecting the                binding of one or more tumor associated antigens                (TACAs) or antibodies bound to the compound                (I)-(IVX) and (d) determining the therapeutic                effect of an antineoplastic agent in treatment for                neoplasm based on the assayed value of glycan                detection.
   In compound (I),
   G=glycan;
   A=moiety comprising an ester or amide;
   X=substrate, solid surface, coated surface,                polymer surface, nitrocellulose-coated surface or                bead surface, a spacer group attached to the                surface or a spacer group with a group for adhering                the linker to a surface;and
   Z=lipid chains or a spacer group with lipid                chains.
   In compound (X)-(IVX),
   n=5-9;and
   TACA=globohexaosylceramide (Globo-H),                Stage-specific embryonic antigen 3 (SSEA-3),                Stage-specific embryonic antigen 4 (SSEA-4),                &#945; -2,6-N-acetylgalactosaminyl (Tn),                Thomsen-Friendreich (TF), Sialyl-Tn (sTn),                polysialic acid (PSA) globotriaose (Gb3), Gb4,                Lewis (Le)-x, (Le)-y, Le-a, sialyl-Lewis-x (sLe-x),                SLe-a, GD1a, GT1b, ganglioside monoclonal antibody                (A2B5), disialoganglioside (GD2), GD3,                monosialotetrahexosylganglioside (GM1), GM2, GM3,                fucosyl-GM1, N glycolyl GM3 (Neu5Gc-GM3) and/or                their n-pentylamine-functionalized variants.
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Biomolecule: The substrate is                  chosen from a surface, solid surface,                  non-transparent solid, solid transparent to                  chosen wavelengths of visible or non-visible                  light, particle, micro-bubble or bead, preferably                  nitrocellulose. The G-A-Z carbohydrate moieties                  are coated on the substrate. The Z moieties in                  several G-A-Z carbohydrates are adhered to the                  substrate by van der Waals interactions or                  hydrophobic interactions. The carbohydrate                  moieties comprise one or more of polysaccharides,                  oligosaccharides, carbohydrate portions of a                  glycoconjugate and TACA. The labeled antibody                  comprises a label comprising an enzyme,                  fluorescent label, chemiluminescent label and                  nanoparticle label. The enzyme is alkaline                  phosphatase (AP) or horseradish peroxidase (HRP).                  The antibody specifically recognizes the                  immobilized polysaccharides, oligosaccharides,                  carbohydrate portions of a glycoconjugate,                  Globo-H, SSEA-3, SSEA-4, Tn, TF, sTn, polysialic                  acid, Gb3, Gb4, Le-x, Le-y, Le-a, sLe-x, SLe-a,                  GD1a, GT1b, A2B5, GD2, GD3, GM1, GM2, GM3,                  fucosyl-GM1 or Neu5GcGM3 series of antigens. The                  carbohydrate antigen or its immunogenic fragment                  comprises Globo H, SSEA-3, SSEA-4, Tn, TF, sTn,                  Polysialic acid, Gb3, Gb4, Le-x, Le-y, Le-a,                  sLe-x, SLe-a, GD1a, GT1b, A2B5, GD2, GD3, GM1,                  GM2, GM3, fucosyl-GM1 or Neu5GcGM3. The                  antineoplastic agent comprises an antibody or its                  antigen-binding portion capable of binding one or                  more carbohydrate antigens. The carrier protein                  comprises keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH), DT-CRM                  197 (diphtheria toxin cross-reacting material                  197), diphtheria toxoid or tetanus toxoid. The                  antineoplastic agent comprises a vaccine composed                  of a carbohydrate antigen or its immunogenic                  fragment conjugated with a carrier protein.                  Preferred Sample: The sample consists of serum,                  blood, plasma, cells, cell medium, saliva, urine                  or lymph node fluid, tumor biopsy or tissue                  culture. Preferred Composition: The vaccine is                  provided as a pharmaceutical composition, which                  comprises Globo H-KLH and additional adjuvant.                  The additional adjuvant is chosen from saponin,                  Freund's adjuvant or &#945;                  -galactosyl-ceramide (&#945; -GalCer)                  adjuvant. The pharmaceutical composition                  comprises OBI-822/OBI-821.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. Teste details are described but no                results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Vaccine.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Image acquiring and processing method for e.g.            detecting acne, involves elaborating variation profile            of intensity of image according to time of formed image            parameter, and comparing profile with lesion detection            threshold value.
AU PETIT L
AE GALDERMA RES & DEV SNC (CIRD-C)
   GALDERMA RES & DEV (CIRD-C)
   GALDERMA RES&DEV (CIRD-C)
   GALDERMA RES & DEV (CIRD-C)
   PETIT L (PETI-Individual)
GA 2008N92201
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves forming successive images                of a surface to be analyzed using a camera (12). A                variation profile of intensity of the image for                different color components of the image is                elaborated according to time of a formed image                parameter using a central processing unit (15),                where the color components are chosen from a red                component, a blue component and a green component.                The elaborated profile is compared with a lesion                detection threshold value.
   USE - Method for acquiring and processing                dermatologic images for detecting evolutive lesion                e.g. acne, psoriasis, rosacea, pigmentary                disorders, onychomycosis, actinic keratosis and                skin cancer in a skin of a patient, and for                monitoring appearance and evolution of                dermatological pathology, for use by a practitioner                or research laboratory to determine efficiency of                treatment and for implementing clinical test in                estimating efficiency of a new product. Can also be                used in a field of mutatis mutandis.
   ADVANTAGE - The elaborated variation profile is compared                with the lesion detection threshold value, thus                permitting to detect the evolutive lesion in an                easy and efficient manner, without necessitating                comparison of images.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                device for acquiring and processing images for                detecting evolutive lesion.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram                representing functioning of an image acquiring and                processing device.

   19Remote user terminal

Each of the                oligonucleotide is chosen from (a) oligonucleotides                as given in table 5, 7C or 8B provided in the                patent specification, (b) oligonucleotides derived                from a sequence as given in table 5, 7C or 8B                provided in the patent specification, (c)                oligonucleotide with a complementary sequence, and                (d) functionally equivalent oligonucleotide.
   USE - The set of oligonucleotide probes is useful                for determining gene expression pattern of cell,                preparing standard and test gene transcript                patterns and diagnosing, identifying or monitoring                cancer or its stage in organism, preferably                eukaryotic organism, more preferably mammal or                human. The cancer is chosen from stomach cancer,                lung cancer, breast cancer, prostate cancer, bowel                cancer, skin cancer, colon cancer and ovary cancer,                preferably breast cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The set of oligonucleotide probe enables easy                and rapid analysis of sample, is cost-effective,                highly sensitive and highly specific, and enables                accurate detection of breast cancer in its early                stage.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   kit comprising the set of oligonucleotide                probes, where the probes are preferably immobilized                on one or more solid supports;
   method (M1) of using the set of                oligonucleotide probes or kit for determining gene                expression pattern of cell in which the pattern                reflects level of gene expression of genes to which                the oligonucleotide probes bind, involves (e)                isolating mRNA from cell, which may optionally be                reverse transcribed to cDNA, (f) hybridizing the                mRNA or cDNA using set of oligonucleotides or kit,                and (g) assessing the amount of hybridized mRNA or                cDNA with each of the probes to produce the                pattern;
   method (M2) of preparing a standard gene                transcript pattern specific for cancer or its stage                in an organism, involves (h) isolating mRNA from                cells of a sample of one or more organisms having                cancer or its stage, which may optionally be                reverse transcribed to cDNA, and (i) performing the                above-mentioned steps (f) and (g), where the                obtained characteristic pattern reflects level of                gene expression of genes to which the                oligonucleotides bind in the sample with cancer or                its stage;
   method (M3) of preparing a test gene                transcript pattern, involves (j) performing the                above-mentioned steps (h) and (i);
   method (M3) of diagnosing, identifying or                monitoring cancer or its stage in organism,                involves (k) performing the above-mentioned step                (j), and (l) comparing the pattern to a standard                diagnostic pattern prepared using a sample from an                organism corresponding to the organism and sample                under investigation to determine degree of                correlation, where the degree of correlation                indicates presence of the cancer or its stage in                the organism under investigation; and
   method (M4) of monitoring cancer or its stage                in organism, involves performing the monitoring                process after treatment of the cancer in the                organism to determine efficacy of the                treatment.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Nucleic Acid: The oligonucleotide                  (a) and oligonucleotide (b) have at least 60%,                  preferably 100% frequency of occurrence. The                  oligonucleotide (a) has at least 60%, preferably                  at least 100% frequency of occurrence. Preferred                  Set: The set comprises 10-500 oligonucleotide                  probes. The set comprises at least 20                  oligonucleotides and pair of primers, where each                  oligonucleotide in the pair of primers binds to                  same transcript or its complementary sequence,                  and each of the pair of primers bind to a                  different transcript. The set comprises at least                  30 oligonucleotides, pair of primers and a                  labeled probe for each pair of primers in which                  each oligonucleotide in the pair of primers and                  the labeled probe bind to the same transcript or                  its complementary sequence and preferably each of                  the pair of primers and the labeled probe bind to                  different transcripts. Preferred Probe: Each                  probe binds to a different transcript. The probes                  are labeling probes and pair of primers, where                  the labeling probe binds to the target sequence                  which is displaced during amplification to                  generate a signal, and the amount of signal                  generated is assessed to produce the pattern. The                  oligonucleotide probe comprises 15-200 bases in                  length. The probes are immobilized on a single                  solid support and each unique probe is attached                  to different region of the solid support.                  Preferred Component: The solid support is sheet,                  filter, membrane, plate or biochip. Preferred                  Kit: The kit further comprises standardizing                  materials. Preferred Method: The method (M1)-(M3)                  further involves amplifying the mRNA, cDNA or                  their portions using primers, and assessing                  amount of amplified product to produce the                  pattern. The amplification step is performed                  before hybridization step. In the method                  (M1)-(M3), the oligonucleotides and/or mRNA or                  cDNA are labeled, and the pattern is expressed as                  an array of numbers relating to the expression                  level associated with each probe. In the method                  (M1)-(M3), the pattern is mathematically                  projected onto a classification model to produce                  data. Preferred Sample: The sample is tissue,                  body fluid, body waste, or peripheral blood.                  Preferred Cell: The cells contained in the sample                  are not disease cells, and are not derived from                  site of diseased condition.

AB    NOVELTY - The system has a processor for processing a                computer image to produce an enhanced whole-breast                navigator overview image representing a                three-dimensional volume from which influences of                non-breast tissue included in the sonographic                response is segmented out. The processor boosts                representations of the whole-breast navigator                overview image of features related to malignant                abnormalities. A computerized display displays                whole-breast navigator overview image in                association with selected images generated from                sonographic response.
   USE - Commercial automated three-dimensional breast                ultrasound system for automated ultrasound                examination of breast of a patient i.e. women                patient, for early detection of breast cancer                during chestward compression scanning                procedure.
   ADVANTAGE - The system reduces the time for assessing                patients for breast abnormalities with reduced                error, and improves patient flow for ultrasound                breast examination related to acquiring sonographic                responses from patient tissue. The system detects                the breast cancer with ultrasound, thus helping the                patient by early detection and accurate screening                or diagnosis, particularly women with breasts that                are relatively dense to X-rays.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow diagram illustrating                a method for generating and displaying a                whole-breast navigator overview image.
   612Step for detecting skin, chest-wall and                ribs
   614Step for segmenting region containing only                or mostly breast tissue
   616Step for filtering three-dimensional                volume image
   618Step for performing feature weighted                compounding
   624Whole-breast navigator overview                image

GA 2007174692
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves sensing electromagnetic                waves emanating from a skin portion in an extremely                high frequency (EHF) band. An EHF signal is                produced based on the sensed waves. The EHF signal                is heterodyned from a high frequency band to a                lower frequency band to produce an intermediate                frequency electrical signal. The intermediate                signal is demodulated to provide an information                signal. The information signal is converted from                analog form to digital form to produce a                digitalized information signal. The digitalized                signal is analyzed for determining a biometric                signature.
   USE - Used for determining a physiological condition                e.g. environmental condition such as temperature                and humidity, hot weather, illness, puberty,                menopause, menstruation, and metabolism, caused by                exercise, and an emotional state e.g. stress,                anxiety, fear, anger, nervousness, embarrassment,                panic, and general neurological disorder, of a                living organism e.g. human being and mammal, for                correcting a bioelectric activity of a neurally                connected and electromagnetically interacting                structure such as sweat gland, distributed in a                skin of the living organism caused by a hot drink,                spicy food, medication, and illicit drug for                diagnosis of a disease e.g. fever, flu, cold,                pneumonia, malaria, severe pain, hypoglycemic                attack, AIDS, hyperhidrosis, anhidrosis, cancer,                and Frey`s syndrome.
   ADVANTAGE - The method effectively enables radiation                detection i.e. reception of electromagnetic waves                emanating from the skin of the living organism, and                radiation stimulation/excitation of the skin i.e.                transmission of the electromagnetic radiation to                the skin of the living organism.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                system for non-invasive determination of a                condition of a living organism selected from                physiological conditions and emotional states of a                living organism.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a system for non-invasive                detection of an electromagnetic wave produced as a                result of bioelectric activity of eccrine sweat                glands of a living organism.

AB    NOVELTY - A detection unit is moved to positions                associated with views selected by provided                algorithm, for obtaining                radioactive-emission-measurements at the positions.                Another algorithm is provided for reconstructing                volumetric radiation distribution, from the                obtained measurements.
   USE - For functional imaging of liver, kidney,                stomach, colon, small intestine, oral cavity,                throat, gland, lymph node, skin, limb, bone,                prostate, cervix, uterus, ovaries, heart, breast,                brain and whole body by nuclear imaging alone or                together with structural imaging by x-rays,                ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for                diagnosing coronary artery disease, brain cancer                including primary brain tumor such as Astrocytoma,                Brain stem glioma, Ependymoma, Oligodendroglioma,                Medulloblastoma, Meningioma, Schwannoma,                Cranipharyngioma, Germ cell tumor, Pineal region                tumor, tumors associated with multiple endocrine                neoplasia type 1, Neurofibromatosis type 2,                Retinoblastoma, Tuberous sclerosis, Von                Hippel-Lindau disease, blood clots in brain and                other brain pathologies and breast cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - The functional information is optimized from                the views of the corresponding body structure and a                rapid, inexpensive preliminary indication of                coronary occlusive disease is provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   computer system;

   radioactive-emission-measuring probe                system;

   dual imaging system.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figures show the principles of modeling                for obtaining optimal set of views.

TI Device for detecting analyte, e.g. nucleic acid,            RNA, microRNA, DNA, or cancer biomarker, comprises            base, and microneedles having outer surface that is            coated with composition comprising polymer and 1st            peptide nucleic acid (PNA).
