GA 2020C0629A
AB    NOVELTY - Device for detecting an analyte, comprises a                base, and microneedles attached to the base. Each                microneedle has an outer surface. The outer surface                of at least one microneedle is coated with a                composition comprising at least one polymer and at                least one 1st peptide nucleic acid (PNA).
   USE - The device for detecting an analyte in ISF of                a subject , where the analyte is a nucleic acid,                RNA, microRNA, or DNA, or a biomarker for a disease                selected from cancer and infection, where the                infection is bacterial infection, viral infection,                viroid infection, parasite infection, protozoa                infection, or fungal infection (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - PNAs can be used as stable, efficient, and                selective probes for detection and isolation of                nucleic acids, including cfNAs. New generation of                micrfoneedle (MN) patches coated with hybrid                alginate-PNA hydrogels that can sample up to 6.5                &#956; l of fluid in 2 minutes, is developed.                Unlike other sampling technologies reported to                date, attaching PNA oligomers to the hydrogel's                fibers also enables the specific sampling,                purification and release of the only nucleic acid                fragments that are complementary to the PNA                sequence. This versatile platform can be easily                tuned by simply adapting the PNA sequence to that                of any miRNA of interest. Functionalization of the                hydrogel with different PNA sequences complementary                to different miRNAs will also enable the sampling                and sensing of multiple miRNAs simultaneously                (known as multiplexed analysis or profiling).                Optical sensing of the captured biomarkers is also                possible, either directly on-chip or in-solution                after an additional light-triggered release step.                Using a human skin ex-vivo model, the technology                can efficiently capture nucleic acids spiked within                skin interstitial fluids with both high efficiency                and sequence specificity. With the recent                experimental evidence that skin ISF contains the                same RNA species (including circulating miRNAs) as                blood with comparable natural abundance,                minimally-invasive technologies that can not only                sample this body fluid but can also interrogate its                composition have the potential to transform the                field of molecular diagnostics from liquid                biopsies.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for detecting                an analyte in interstitial fluid (ISF) of a                subject, which involves contacting the subject with                the device; exposing the device to the ISF of the                subject; detaching the device from the subject; and                measuring an intensity of the detectable                signal.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The composition                  further comprises at least one 2nd PNA, where the                  2nd PNA is different from the 1st PNA. The 1st                  PNA comprises 5-30 nucleobases. The 1st or 2nd                  PNA comprises 5-8 nucleobases. The analyte is a                  nucleic acid; the 1st PNA is complementary to the                  5' end of the nucleic acid; and the 2nd PNA is                  complementary to the 3' end of the nucleic acid.                  It is microRNA. The 1st PNA comprises but not                  limited to a 1st probe head; the 2nd PNA                  comprises but not limited to a 2nd probe head;                  and the 1st probe head and the 2nd probe head                  selectively bind each other, thus producing a                  detectable signal. The 1st PNA is a hairpin PNA                  comprising a 3rd probe head; and further the 3rd                  probe head produces a detectable signal upon the                  hairpin PNA binding to the analyte. The 1st probe                  head or the 2nd probe head or the 3rd probe head                  comprises a chemical moiety comprising but not                  limited to thiol. The detectable signal is                  fluorescent signal, or electrochemical signal.                  The 1st or 2nd signal is a fluorescence,                  absorbance, or electrical signal. The 1st or 2nd                  detection reagent is selected from a fluorogenic                  reagent or a DNA intercalator. The 1st detection                  reagent is selected from SYBR-Safe, SYBR-green,                  SYBR-red, YOYO-1, YOYO-3, TOTO-1, TOTO-3, TOPO-1,                  TOPO-3, POPO-1, POPO-3, thiazole orange, or                  ethidium bromide. The analyte forms an                  analyte:PNA complex with the 1st PNA. The analyte                  further forms an analyte:PNA complex with the 2nd                  PNA. The 2nd detection reagent is selected from                  SYBR-Safe, SYBR-green, SYBR-red, YOYO-1, YOYO-3,                  TOTO-1, TOTO-3, TOPO-1, TOPO-3, POPO-1, POPO-3,                  Thiazole orange, Ethidium bromide, molecular                  beacon, Taqman probe, or Lexicon probe. The                  detection reagent is selected from a fluorogenic                  reagent, a DNA intercalator, or a 3rd PNA. The                  detection reagent is a 3rd PNA. The 1st PNA is                  complementary to the 5' end of the nucleic acid,                  and the 2nd PNA is complementary to the 3' end of                  the nucleic acid. Preferred Method:                  Alternatively, detecting analyte in ISF of                  subject, involves contacting the subject with the                  device, and exposing the device to the ISF of the                  subject. Detecting an analyte in ISF of a                  subject, involves contacting the subject with the                  device; exposing the device to the ISF of the                  subject; detaching the device from the subject;                  eluting the analyte from the device; and exposing                  the analyte to a detection agent, where the                  detection agent binds to the analyte. The method                  further involves detaching the device from the                  subject; and contacting the device with a 1st                  detection reagent, where the 1st detection                  reagent binds to the analyte and to produce a 1st                  signal. The method also involves determining a                  concentration of the analyte in ISF of the                  subject; and measuring an intensity of the 1st                  signal, thus determining the concentration of the                  analyte. The linker is photocleavable, and the                  method further involves exposing the device to                  electromagnetic radiation, thus releasing a free                  PNA: analyte complex. The method also involves                  contacting the free PNA:analyte complex with a                  2nd detection agent, where the 2nd detection                  agent binds to the free PNA:analyte complex and                  produce a 2nd signal. The method involves                  determining the concentration of the free                  PNA:analyte complex; and measuring an intensity                  of the 2nd signal, thus determining the                  concentration of the free PNA:analyte complex.                  Contacting the subject involves contacting a skin                  surface of the subject. The subject is a human                  subject.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - POLYMERS - Preferred Components: The polymer is                  hydrophilic. It is alginate (preferred), xanthan,                  dextran, hyaluronic acid, poly(vinylalcohol)                  (PVA), polymethacrylic acid (PMAA), polyacrylic                  acid (PAA), poly(N-vinylpyrrolidone) (PVP),                  poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA),                  poly(N-isopropylacrylamide), poly(ethylene                  glycol) (PEG), poly(propylene oxide) (PPO),                  poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate/dimethacrylate                  (PEGDA/PEGDMA), or poly(ethylene glycol)                  acrylate/methacrylate (PEGA/PEGMA), or                  combination. The polymer is covalently attached                  to the 1st PNA or to the 2nd PNA, optionally by a                  linker that is cleavable. The linker comprises                  but not limited to a photocleavable linker.

TI Method of percutaneous preoperative marking of injuried mammary gland duct.
AU SHKOLNIK L D
   SAAKYAN R A
   KURAPOVA YU N
AE UNIV MOSC MED STOMATOLOGY (UYMO-Non-standard)
GA 2009B54326
AB    NOVELTY - Ductograms are applied to frontal and lateral projections. Received ductograms show the pathologic focus marked by solution introduction to mammary gland duct. Using straightedge and ductograms data the skin in pathologic focus projection zone is tagged to point needle direction. Mammogram is carried out with marking site in frontal projection. Considering received mammogram data needle is inserted into pathologic focus. Then mammogram is carried out in lateral projection. Then needle mammogram in frontal and lateral projections is compared to ductograms to evaluate and correct needle position. Duct visual marking solution is injected into needle Solution has composition as follows: 75% verografin in amount 0.5 ml and aqueous solution of methylene blue in amount 0.5 ml.
   USE - Medicine.
   ADVANTAGE - Method allows for more precise detection of injury zones and precision removal of mammary gland tissue and for higher detection fraction of intraduct papillomas and initial forms of mammary gland cancer.8 dwg, 1 ex

AB    NOVELTY - An arylurea derivative is new.
   USE - For preventing or treating disease related to                raf cyclindependent kinase inhibitor selected from                melanoma, liver cancer, kidney cancer, acute                leukemia, non-small-cell pulmonary carcinoma and                prostate cancer, thyroid cancer, skin cancer, and                colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, ovarian                cancer, breast cancer, proliferation syndrome and                esophageal cancer and treatment of gastrointestinal                cancer and mesothelioma (claimed) and treatment of                neoplastic disease and for inhibiting tumor                metastasis.
   ADVANTAGE - The arylurea derivative compound has function                of raf cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor; and is                provided with low toxic side effect.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An arylurea derivative of formula (I), is                new.
   R =optionally substituted pentaheterocycle of                formula (i);
   R -R =C, N, O or S;
   R -R =H, halo, 1-4C alkyl or 1-4C                alkoxy;
   R =halo, nitrile, 1-4C alkoxy or                sulfydryl.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   preparation of                1-(4-chlorine-3(trifluoromethyl)                phenyl)-3-(2-fluorin-4-(2-(1-methyl-4-pyrazolyl)-4-pyridyloxy)                phenyl) urea (IV) or its salt involving: adding                2-fluorine-4-(2-(1-methyl-4-pyrazolyl)-4-pyridyloxy)                aniline (III) (10.2 g) to dissolve in                dichloromethane, adding                3-trifluoromethyl-4-chlorine-phenyl isocyanate                (7.95 g) under the nitrogen protection, stirring                for 12 hours at room temperature to separate out                large amount of solid, concentrating the system,                filtering, washing via ethyl acetate, and drying to                obtain compound (IV);
   preparation of the compound (I) or its salt,                involving: performing nucleophilic substitution                reaction for aminophenol compound and 2,4-dihalogen                pyridine under the action of strong base,                performing Suzuki reaction for the product and the                pentaheterocyclic boronic pinacol cyclic ester                under the catalysis of catalyst; and reacting the                obtained product with                3-trifluoromethyl-4-chlorine-phenyl isocyanate to                obtain the compound (I);
   new intermediate compounds,                2-chlorine-4-(3-fluorin-4-aminophenoxy) pyridine                (II) and (III) and their salts;
   preparation of compound (II) involving: adding                3-fluorin-4-aminophenol (1.34 g) in anhydrous                dimethyl sulfoxide, filling nitrogen for 10                minutes, adding potassium tertiary butoxide (1.24                g), stirring for 30 minutes at room temperature,                adding 2-chlorine-4-fluorin pyridine (1.32 g),                heating the reaction system to 80&#176; C                slowly to insulating for 2 hours, showing the                reaction is complete via TLC detection, cooling to                room temperature, adding water and ethyl acetate,                separating the liquid and using ethyl acetate to                extract for twice, combining the ethyl acetate                layer, washing with water for twice, washing for                once by using saturated salt water, drying by using                anhydrous sodium sulfate, drying, filtering and                concentrating, and purifying the crude via column                chromatography to obtain compound (II); and
   preparation of compound (III) involving:                adding 2-chlorine-4-(3-fluorin-4-aminophenoxy)                pyridine (II) (1.6 g) and 1-methyl-4-pyrazol                boronic pinacol cyclic ester (1.68 g) to dissolve                in tetrahydrofuran (THF) under the nitrogen                protection, stirring and adding potassium carbonate                (2.77 g) and water (4.5 ml), adding platinum                catalyst (0.39 g), insulating and stirring for 24                hours at 70&#176; C, showing the reaction is                complete via TLC detection, cooling to room                temperature, adding water and ethyl acetate,                separating the liquid and using ethyl acetate to                extract for twice, combining the ethyl acetate                layer, washing twice with water, washing once by                using saturated salt water, drying by using                anhydrous sodium sulfate, drying, filtering and                concentrating, and purifying the crude via column                chromatography to obtain compound (III).

   USE - The method is useful for (a) assessing                sensitivity or resistance of a subject having a                cancer to an oncolytic virus, (b) selecting a                treatment, (c) monitoring the response to a cancer                treatment or (d) preventing or treating the cancer                of the subject. The cancer is chosen from a                carcinoma, a sarcoma, a lymphoma, a melanoma, a                pediatric tumour and a leukemia. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:

GA 201907784B
AB    NOVELTY - The imaging system (101) has a scan head (107)                optically coupled to a light source (105) to scan                light from the light source onto a portion of a                specimen (103) and to receive light reflected from                the portion of the specimen. An interferometer                (109) is optically coupled to the light source and                to the scan head to generate an interference output                using light from the light source and light                reflected from the portion of the specimen. A                scanning spectrometer (111) is optically coupled to                the interferometer to receive the interference                output and generate a scanned output having a                sub-spectrum of light which is narrower than the                spectrum of light generated by the light source. A                detector (113) is optically coupled to the scanning                spectrometer to detect the scanned output and                generate a detector signal from the detected                scanned output.
   USE - Imaging system used for different imaging                applications. Uses include but are not limited to                in-vitro biological imaging, ophthalmic imaging,                dental imaging, skin imaging and imaging for                detection of oral cancer and melanoma skin cancer.                Can also be used in clinical and non-clinical                environment.
   ADVANTAGE - Offers compact imaging system that utilizes                optical coherence tomography (OCT) platform to                enable rapid and accurate diagnosis and monitoring                of patients, while reducing cost and time                associated with healthcare services.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows the block diagram of an                imaging system.
   Imaging system (101)
   Specimen (103)
   Light source (105)
   Scan head (107)
   Interferometer (109)
   Scanning spectrometer (111)
   Detector (113)

PN WO9918125-A1; AU9893313-A; US2003228592-A1
TI Nucleic acid encoding a facilitative glucose transporter.
AU ROGERS S D
   BEST J D
AE ST VINCENTS INST MEDICAL RES (SVIN-Non-standard)
   ST VINCENTS INST MEDICAL RES (SVIN-Non-standard)
GA 1999277253
AB    NOVELTY - Nucleic acid (I) encoding a facilitative glucose transporter protein, GLUT8, and its functional fragments, is new.
   USE - Agents that inhibit activity or expression of GLUT8 (particularly non-utilizable glucose analogs, antisense sequences or dominant negative mutants) are used to treat malignancy, particularly cancer of breast, prostate and epithelial cells (e.g. skin or colon). Agents that upregulate expression of GLUT8 (e.g. the GLUT8 gene, administered by tissue-localized gene therapy) are used to treat non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and/or insulin resistance (e.g. central obesity, hypertension, dyslypidaemia or glucose intolerance).
Detecting expression of GLUT8 is used for diagnosis, monitoring and staging of cancers, particularly of the breast. Antibodies raised against GLUT8 are useful as immunoassay reagents and as therapeutic inhibitors.
   ADVANTAGE - GLUT8 is involved in supplying energy to tumor cells at a very early stage of the disease, so its detection should provide early diagnosis. In 5 of 10 patients with breast cancer, GLUT8 expression in cancer cells was significantly higher (by 3 to 20 times) than in normal cells from the same patient.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the following:
   (1) nucleic acid (Ia) that hybridizes to (I) under stringent conditions;
   (2) GLUT8 and its active fragments;
   (3) diagnosis, and monitoring treatment, of malignancy by detecting expression or activity of GLUT8 in a tissue or cell;
   (4) selecting agents for therapy of malignancy from their ability to inhibit activity or expression of GLUT8;
   (5) antibodies, or their functional fragments, against GLUT8;
   (6) treating non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus by upregulating GLUT8 expression;
   (7) detecting a mutation in the GLUT8 gene, or its regulatory region, by gene analysis; and
   (8) screening agents for treatment of:
   (i) cancer or
   (ii) diabetes and/or insulin-resistance conditions
   from their ability to inhibit or upregulate or enhance activity of GLUT8,
   in vivo or in vitro.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred nucleic acid: (I) is genomic DNA, cDNA (preferred) or RNA, especially a 2471 bp cDNA sequence (S1), given in the specification.Preferred protein: GLUT8 is at least 70, particularly over 95,% homologous with a 526 amino acid sequence given in the specification.Preferred assays: GLUT8 is detected by immunocytochemistry, hybridization or (reverse transcription) polymerase chain reaction.To select for a method of treatment, inhibition of GLUT8 expression and/or activity is with either a non-utilizable glucose analog, targeted to malignant tissue, or antisense nucleic acid against sequences encoding GLUT8. This test is performed on adipose tissue or skeletal muscle cells. Mutations in the GLUT8 gene or regulator are detected in patients with non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, particularly by single-strand configuration polymorphism. Screening for potential therapeutic agents is especially by positron emission tomography using a hexose (i.e. glucose analog or hexose specifically transported by GLUT8) that carries a fluorescent marker.Preferred antibodies: These are mono- or poly-clonal and are directed to the C-terminal region of GLUT4. Particularly they recognize at least one epitope in the peptide NKLCGRGQSRQLSPET. They are made by usual methods of immunization and cell fusion, with synthetic peptides used as immunogen.
   ACTIVITY - Antidiabetic; anticancer.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Agents that modulate activity or expression of GLUT8 control the supply of energy to cancer, adipose and muscle cells.
   EXAMPLE - Extracts of the breast cancer cell lines MCF7 and T47-D, and of skeletal muscle, were screened with polyclonal antiserum against GLUT4 to indicate a related protein. Northern analysis of MCF7 cells with a GLUT4 cDNA probe showed a 2.8 kb transcript, contrast 3.5 kb expected for GLUT4. Reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with primers based on GLUT4 sequences gave no product from MCF7 cells, but use of degenerate primers at lower annealing temperature generated a 350 bp amplicon. This encoded a fragment only 60% homologous with GLUT4 and searching of databases identified a clone (IMAGE 43006) of 1.3 kb, isolated from a neonatal human brain library. This clone was used to screen a cDNA library from malignant breast epithelial cells to isolate sequence (S1) of 2471 bp. This sequence was used to screen human genomic DNA; the GLUT8 gene is about 15-18 kb long.

TI Micro-system based on spontaneous Brillouin            scattering for use in biomechanics detection            technology, has detection assembly for performing            heterodyne detection on spontaneous Brillouin            scattering light and second laser to generate detection            result.
AU QI Y
   DU Z
   YANG F
AE CAS SHANGHAI INST OPTICS & FINE MECHANIC (CAOF-C)
GA 202618471P
AB    NOVELTY - The micro-system has a microscopic assembly                for receiving a first laser, where the first laser                is a pulsed laser. The microscopic assembly guides                the first laser to a sample to be tested to                generate spontaneous Brillouin scattered light. A                detection assembly receives the spontaneous                Brillouin scattered light and a second laser. The                detection assembly performs heterodyne detection on                the spontaneous Brillouin scattering light and the                second laser to generate a detection result, where                the detection result is processed to perform                Brillouin microscopic detection on the sample to be                detected.
   USE - Micro-system for spontaneous Brillouin                scattering based on spontaneous Brillouin                scattering. Uses include but are not limited to                cell mechanics research, tissue pathology                diagnosis, cornea biomechanics evaluation, single                cell mechanics, corneal tissue characterization,                plant biology, cancer invasion and skin                mechanics.
   ADVANTAGE - The system reduces the average pump light                power and imaging time of the self-distributed                rillouin microscopic detection without changing the                signal-to-noise ratio.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                microscopic method based on spontaneous brillouin                scattering.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a block diagram of a                spontaneous Brillouin scattering based microscopic                system. (Drawing includes non-English language                text).

PN WO8100260-A; FR2461002-A; EP32145-A; JP56500932-W; EP32145-B; DE3070208-G; US4533635-A; US4670257-A
TI Stimulating growth of epidermal cells with extract            of eye tissue, useful for diagnosing chromosome            abnormalities, growing skin grafts etc..
AU GUEDON I
   BARRITAULT D
   COURTOIS Y
   ARRUTI C
   PRUNIERAS M
   GUEDON BORN SAGLIER I
AE INSERM INST NAT SANTE & RECH MEDICALE (INRM-C)
   GUEDON I (GUED-Individual)
   INSERM INST NAT SANTE & RECH MED (INRM-C)
GA 198113670D
AB    NOVELTY - The growth of epidermal cells, esp. of adults,                is stimulated by treating them with an aq. saline                extract (A) of eye tissue, esp. of the choroid,                iris or vitreous humour. Pref. extracts are of                bovine origin obtd. using a pH 7.2 buffered saline                soln.
The pref. dose is 50-400, esp. 50-100,                microgram (total protein) per ml. of epidermal cell                culture..
The method is useful (a) for studying human                epidermal chromosomes, esp. for detection of                natural or induced abnormalities (e.g. in diagnosis                of psoriasis or skin cancer); (b) to make skin                grafts for treating burns, esp. using tissue from                the patient; (c) for cosmetic use by application to                the skin or hair; or (d) in long-term culture of                epidermal cells without requiring any other cells                as nutrient layers.
(A) activates mitotic activity but has no                mitogenic effect, so allows chromosomal analysis                and sister chromated exchange (SCE) evaluations to                be carried out in vitro. It also induces                synchronisation of the epidermal cells.

AB    NOVELTY - Conjugate comprises (a) a peptide comprising                an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1 and (b) a                moiety.
   USE - The conjugate is used in the composition and                the kit for imaging or therapy of target tissue,                preferably a cancerous tissue or an organ in a                subject. The cancerous tissue is associated with                pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, colorectal                cancer, prostate cancer or oral squamous cell                carcinoma. The conjugate is used in the detection                for the diagnosis or prognosis of a disease or                disorder mediated by an integrin. The disease or                disorder is associated with the expression,                over-expression, or activation of the integrin. The                conjugate is useful for preventing or treating an                integrin-mediated disease or disorder chosen from a                cancer, an inflammatory disease, an autoimmune                disease, chronic fibrosis, chronic obstructive                pulmonary disease (COPD), lung emphysema,                radiation-induced pulmonary fibrosis, and chronic                wounding skin disease (all claimed). The                inflammatory disease are chosen from inflammatory                bowel disease e.g. Crohn's disease or ulcerative                colitis, rheumatoid diseases such as rheumatoid                arthritis, fibrositis, pelvic inflammatory disease,                acne, psoriasis, actinomycosis, dysentery, biliary                cirrhosis, Lyme disease, heat rash, Stevens-Johnson                syndrome, mumps, pemphigus vulgaris, and                blastomycosis. The autoimmune diseases include                organ-specific autoimmune diseases such as Type I                diabetes mellitus, myasthenia gravis, vitiligo,                Graves's disease, Hashimoto's disease, Addison's                disease, autoimmune gastritis and autoimmune                hepatitis.
   ADVANTAGE - The conjugate has high tumor selectivity and                specificity for a6-expressing tumors. The conjugate                binds to &#945; v&#946; 6integrin with high                affinity and selectivity and enables noninvasive                imaging through positron emission tomography (PET).                The conjugate shows significantly better localizing                and/or targeting potential and has increased                metabolic stability and retention at the tumor                site.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Conjugate comprises (a) a peptide comprising                Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys (SEQ ID NO: 1) and                (b) a moiety. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for                the following:
   a kit comprising a conjugate or a composition;                and
   a method for imaging a target tissue in a                subject involves (a) administering a conjugate                comprising an imaging agent or a composition, to                the subject and (b) detecting the conjugate to                determine where the conjugate is concentrated in                the subject.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Biomolecules: The peptide has 8-20                  amino acids in length. The conjugate further                  comprises one or more additional lysine residues,                  attached to the C-terminal end of the peptide                  and/or to one or more moieties. The conjugate                  comprises Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys-Lys                  (SEQ ID NO: 10) and a moiety. The peptide is                  binds to an integrin, preferably &#945;                  v&#946; 6integrin. Preferred Components: The                  moiety is covalently attached to the peptide. The                  moiety is chosen from a polyethylene glycol (PEG)                  moiety, a fluorobenzoyl (FB) group, a methyl                  group, an acetyl group, an imaging agent, a                  therapeutic agent and their combination. The PEG                  moiety has a molecular weight of &#8814; 3000                  daltons (Da) and the PEG moiety is chosen from                  PEG12(PEG 800) and/or PEG28(PEG 1500). The PEG                  moiety is a monodisperse PEG moiety having a                  defined chain length and &#8815; 95% oligomer                  purity. The imaging agent is chosen from an FB                  group, a radionuclide, biotin, a fluorophore, a                  fluorescent protein, an antibody, horseradish                  peroxidase, alkaline phosphatase and their                  combination. The radionuclide is chosen from                  carbon 11 (11C), nitrogen 13 (13N), oxygen 15                  (15O), fluorine-18 (18F), copper 61 (61Cu),                  copper 62 (62Cu), copper 64 (64Cu), copper 67                  (67Cu), gallium 68 (68Ga), indium-111 (111In),                  iodine-124 (124I), iodine-125 (125I), and                  iodine-131 (131I), preferably 18F. The moiety is                  attached to the peptide, to the one or more                  additional lysine residues and/or to another                  moiety. The conjugate comprises an additional                  lysine residue attached to the C-terminal end of                  the peptide and an FB group attached to the side                  chain of the additional lysine residue, then the                  conjugate comprises                  Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys-Lys-FB (SEQ ID                  NO: 2). The conjugate further comprises an FB                  group attached to the N-terminal end of the                  peptide and a PEG28moiety attached to the                  C-terminal lysine residue, then the conjugate                  comprises                  FB-Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys-Lys-FB-PEG28(SEQ                  ID NO: 3). The conjugate comprises                  (Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys-PEG12)2-Lys-Lys-FB                  (SEQ ID NO: 4), and a dimer of the amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO : 1, where the PEG12moiety                  is attached to the C-terminal end of each member                  of the dimer, both PEG12moieties are attached to                  the first of two additional lysine residues and                  the FB group is attached to the side chain of the                  second of the two additional lysine residues. The                  FB groups are attached to the N-terminal ends of                  each peptide of the dimer, then the conjugate                  comprises                  (FB-Val-Gly-Asp-Leu-Thr-Tyr-Leu-Lys-PEG12)2-Lys-Lys-FB                  (SEQ ID NO: 5). The FB group is attached to the                  lysine residue is radiolabeled with 18F. The                  therapeutic agent is chosen from a radionuclide,                  a pro-apoptotic peptide, a nanoparticle, a                  chemotherapeutic agent, a nanodroplet, a                  liposomal drug, a cytokine, and their                  combinations. The imaging agent is covalently                  attached to the peptide, an FB group or a PEG                  moiety. The imaging agent is a radionuclide                  covalently attached to an FB group. The amount of                  the conjugate or the composition is an amount                  sufficient to target delivery of the therapeutic                  agent to a cell expressing the integrin.                  Preferred Kit: The kit further comprises                  instructions for use and one or more reagents.                  Preferred Method: The method involves using the                  radiation from the radionuclide, to determine                  where the conjugate is concentrated in the                  subject.

TI Heater for emitting and radiating far-infrared            rays to cancer patient in e.g. oriental medicine            clinics, has storage space portion for emitting LED            light through formed through-hole, and located on four            sides of case.
AU LEE S J
AE LEE S J (LEES-Individual)
GA 2023B0163T
AB    NOVELTY - The heater (A) has a ceramic heater mounted on                a front of a case (11) accommodated in a space for                emitting far-infrared rays when power is applied. A                control unit is formed inside the case for applying                power to the ceramic heater when a manipulation                signal is input by manipulating on and off                switches. A temperature sensor detects the                temperature of the heater and transmits a detection                signal to the control unit. A separation piece is                protruded from a front part of the case, and                separates the heater from a ceramic tempered glass.                A storage space portion emits LED light through a                through-hole, and is located on four sides of the                case.
   USE - Heater for emitting and radiating far-infrared                rays to a human body i.e. cancer patient, in                hospitals e.g. oriental medicine clinics, physical                therapy rooms or skin care rooms.
   ADVANTAGE - The heater improves blood circulation,                relieves or prevents diseases and pain, promotes                metabolism in the human body, recovers fatigue for                patients with various pains and patients in                recovery stage, obtains thermal effect and                minimizes burden of time and economic costs                associated with visiting expensive oriental                medicine clinics.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of the                heater.

   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Antiarthritic; Antirheumatic;                Antiallergic; Antiinflammatory; Respiratory-Gen.;                Neuroprotective; Immunosuppressive; Nephrotropic;                Dermatological; Virucide; Antiasthmatic;                Antipsoriatic; Gastrointestinal-Gen.; Vasotropic;                Antiarteriosclerotic; Endocrine-Gen.;                Antiparkinsonian; Nootropic; Antidiabetic;                Antibacterial; Muscular-Gen.; Vulnerary; Cardiant;                Osteopathic; Hepatotropic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk) inhibitor. An                efficacy of                6-(benzo[d]thiazol-5-yl)-N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine                (Ia) to inhibit Syk was tested in a biochemical Syk                Kinase assay comprising N-terminally                glutathione-S-transferase (GST)-tagged full length                human wild type Syk (accession number NM-00377).                The compound (Ia) showed IC 50value of less than 1                &#956; M.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is intravenously,                intramuscularly, parenterally or orally (claimed).                Dosage is 0.1-140 mg/kg/day.
   SPECIFIC COMPOUNDS - 602 Compounds are disclosed as (I) e.g.                  N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)-6-(3-methylphenyl)imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine;                  N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)-6-(3-nitrophenyl)imidazo[1                  ,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine;                  5-{8-[(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)amino]imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-6-yl}-1H-indazol-3-amine;                  6-{8-[(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)amino]imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-6-yl}-1H-1,3-benzodiazol-2-amine;                  and                  6-(benzo[d]thiazol-5-yl)-N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine                  (Ia).
                                                                                                                                 
   EXAMPLE - A mixture of                6-bromo-N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)imidazo[1                ,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine (209 mg), and                5-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-1,3,2-dioxaborolan-2-yl)benzo[d]thiazole                (180 mg) in 1M aqueous sodium carbonate (0.76 ml)                and 1,4-dioxane (2.4 ml) was sparged with nitrogen                while stirring for 5 minutes.                Tetrakis(triphenyl-phosphine) palladium(0) (69 mg)                was then added and the resulting mixture reacted                under microwave irradiation at 135&#176; C for                30 minutes to afford                6-(benzo[d]thiazol-5-yl)-N-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazin-8-amine                (169 mg, 70%) as an off-white solid.

AB    NOVELTY - An isolated polypeptide, is new. The isolated                polypeptide is (a) a polypeptide having amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1, (b) a polypeptide having                at least 70%, at least 75%, at least 80%, at least                85%, at least 90%, at least 95%, at least 99%                identity compared to (a), or (c) a polypeptide                having one or more amino acid substitutions,                deletions, and/or additions compared to (a),                optionally, substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions of at least one or more amino acids are                substituted the amino acid residue at positions 2                and/or 9 of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                1, optionally, substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions of at least one or more amino acids are                substituted the amino acid residue at position 2 of                the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1 as Met,                and/or the amino acid at position 9 is substituted                for Val or Leu, optionally, the polypeptide has                amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NOs: 2-6.
   USE - The polypeptide is useful for preparing a                medicament for preventing or treating tumor and                disease associated with a mutation in the GLRA2                gene in a subject. The tumor is chosen from breast                cancer, lung cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer, liver                cancer, gastric cancer, esophageal cancer,                colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer, melanoma,                skin cancer, prostate cancer, cervical cancer,                leukemia, and brain tumor, preferably non-small                cell lung cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The isolated polypeptide causes reduced side                effects, and is easy to synthesize.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An isolated polypeptide, is new. The isolated                polypeptide is (a) a polypeptide having amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1, (b) a polypeptide having                at least 70%, at least 75%, at least 80%, at least                85%, at least 90%, at least 95%, at least 99%                identity compared to (a), or (c) a polypeptide                having one or more amino acid substitutions,                deletions, and/or additions compared to (a),                optionally, substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions of at least one or more amino acids are                substituted the amino acid residue at positions 2                and/or 9 of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                1, optionally, substitutions, deletions, and/or                additions of at least one or more amino acids are                substituted the amino acid residue at position 2 of                the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1 as Met,                and/or the amino acid at position 9 is substituted                for Val or Leu, optionally, the polypeptide has                amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NOs: 2-6.                Thr-Leu-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Ile (SEQ ID NO: 1),                Thr-Met-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Ile (SEQ ID NO: 2),                Thr-Leu-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Val (SEQ ID NO: 3),                Thr-Leu-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Leu (SEQ ID NO: 4),                Thr-Met-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Leu (SEQ ID NO: 5),                and Thr-Met-Ala-Phe-Leu-Ile-Phe-Asn-Val (SEQ ID NO:                6). INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   (1) use of a reagent for detecting a                polypeptide in a preparation kit for diagnosing                tumors, optionally the tumor simultaneously                expresses human leukocyte antigens (HLA)-A0201 and                the polypeptide, optionally, the tumor is chosen                from breast cancer, lung cancer, nasopharyngeal                cancer, liver cancer, gastric cancer, esophageal                cancer, colorectal cancer, pancreatic cancer,                melanoma, skin cancer, prostate cancer, cervical                cancer, leukemia and brain tumor, preferably                non-small cell lung cancer;
   (2) an isolated nucleic acid encoding the                polypeptide or its complementary sequence;
   (3) a nucleic acid construct comprising a                coding sequence, which is the nucleic acid, and an                optional control sequence operably linked to the                coding sequence;
   (4) an expression vector comprising the                nucleic acid construct;
   (5) a host cell carries the nucleic acid                construct or the expression vector, alternately,                the host cell is obtained by transfection or                transformation of the nucleic acid construct or                expression vector;
   (6) a pharmaceutical composition comprising                the polypeptide and adjuvant;
   (7) an antigen-presenting cell capable of                presenting the polypeptide;
   (8) an immune effector cell recognizes the                polypeptide or antigen-presenting cell that                recognizes the polypeptide on the cell                surface;
   (9) an antibody specifically recognizes the                polypeptide;
   (10) a diagnostic method involves detecting                whether a patient-derived biological sample carries                the polypeptide, and determining whether the                patient has tumor based on whether the biological                sample carries the polypeptide; and
   (11) a diagnostic system comprising a                polypeptide detection device for detecting whether                a patient-derived biological sample carries the                polypeptide, and a diagnostic result determining                device connected to the polypeptide detecting                device for determining whether the patient has a                tumor based on whether the biological sample                carries the polypeptide.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Method: The antigen-presenting cells                  are obtained by contacting a cell having                  antigen-presenting ability with polypeptide, or                  introducing the nucleic acid, nucleic acid                  construct, or expression vector into                  antigen-presenting capacity, optionally, the                  cells having antigen-presenting cells are                  dendritic cells. The immune effector cells are                  obtained by contacting antigen-presenting cells                  with cells having an immune effector capacity,                  optionally, the cells having immune effector                  ability are T cells preferably cluster of                  differentiation (CD)8+ T cells. The antibody is                  obtained by collecting serum of an animal                  immunized with the polypeptide and purifying the                  target antibody from the serum.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Vaccine; Glycine receptor alpha -2 (GLRA2)                inhibitor. Test details are described but no                results given.
   ADMINISTRATION - The composition is administered by                intraperitoneal, intravenous, intramuscular,                subcutaneous, oral, topical, nasal, pulmonary or                rectal route. No dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - Detecting or monitoring in a mammal the onset,                predisposition to the onset, or progression of a                condition characterized by modulation of the level                or bioactivity of activin &#946;c, where the                level is modulated relative to normal levels,                comprises screening for the level of activin                &#946;c protein and/or gene expression in a                biological sample derived from the mammal.
   USE - The agent capable of modulating the functional                level of activin &#946;c subunit is useful in                manufacturing a medicament for the treatment of a                condition characterized by an aberrant, unwanted or                inappropriate level of activin &#946;c subunit,                i.e. abnormal cell growth. Down-regulating or                up-regulating activin &#946;c subunit to a                functional ineffective or effective level,                respectively, inhibits the abnormal growth (all                claimed). The method is useful for detecting or                monitoring in a mammal the onset, predisposition to                the onset, or progression of a condition                characterized by modulation of the level or                bioactivity of activin &#946;c. The methods and                compositions are useful in treating and preventing                malignant neoplasia of the pancreas, brain and                neural tissue, adrenal gland, thyroid gland,                stomach, colon, bladder, endometrium, breast, lymph                node, skin, salivary gland, bone, nasal cavity,                duodenum, gallbladder, cervix, thymus, larynx,                tongue, small intestine, rectum or esophagus,                seminal vesicle cancer, brain cancer, splenic                cancer or soft tissue cancer and non-malignant                neoplasia of the fallopian tube, uterus, tonsil,                spleen, appendix, seminal vesicle, myometrium or                soft tissue.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   a composition, used in the method above,                comprising an activin &#946;c detection                means;
   a diagnostic kit, for detecting or monitoring                the onset, predisposition to the onset, or                progression of a condition characterized by                modulation of the level or bioactivity of activin                &#946;c subunit, comprising an activin                &#946;c subunit protein and/or encoding nucleic                acid detection means in a first compartment and                reagents useful for facilitating detection by the                detection means in a second compartment;
   a method of modulating the abnormal growth of                a cell;
   a method of therapeutically and/or                prophylactically treating a condition, or a                predisposition to the development of a condition,                characterized by an aberrant, unwanted or                inappropriate level or bioactivity of activin                &#946;c subunit in a mammal; and
   a pharmaceutical composition comprising an                agent capable of modulating the functionally                effective level of activin &#946;c subunit                together with one or more pharmaceutical carriers                and/or diluents.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The activin &#946;c                  subunit is in monomeric form or in dimeric form.                  The activin &#946;c dimer is activin AC                  (&#946;A-&#946;C), activin BC                  (&#946;B-&#946;C), activin C                  (&#946;C-&#946;C), activin CD                  (&#946;C-&#946;D), or activin CE                  (&#946;C-&#946;E). The modulation is an                  increase or decrease in the level or bioactivity                  of activin &#946;c subunit. The biological                  sample is serum, tissue extracts, body fluids,                  cell culture medium, extracellular medium,                  supernatants, biopsy specimens, or resected                  tissue. The screening assay is directed to                  detecting the activin &#946;c subunit and is                  performed utilizing an antibody directed to                  activin &#946;c subunit. The screening assay                  is directed to detecting activin &#946;c                  dimers and is performed utilizing an antibody                  directed to the activin &#946;c subunit and                  one or more antibodies directed to one or more of                  the activin &#946;A to &#946;E subunits.                  The antibody recognizes an epitope of activin                  &#946;c comprising the amino acid sequence:                  Val-Pro-Thr-Ala-Arg-Arg-Pro-Leu-Ser-Leu-Leu-Tyr-Tyr-Tyr-Asp-Arg-Asp-Ser-Asn-Ile-Val-Lys-The-Asp-Ile-Pro-Asp-Met-Val-Val-Glu-Ala-Cys                  (SEQ ID NO: l) or its equivalent. Alternatively,                  the method comprises contacting a first antibody                  that recognizes an epitope of a first activin                  &#946; subunit with a biological sample                  derived from the mammal, allowing the first                  antibody to bind to the first activin &#946;                  subunit in the sample, washing the sample to                  substantially remove unbound material, contacting                  the sample with a second antibody that recognizes                  an epitope of a second activin &#946;                  subunit, where the second antibody is tagged with                  a labeling agent, and detecting the labelling                  agent to identify an activin &#946;c subunit                  dimer in the sample, where the first or second                  antibody recognizes an epitope of an activin                  &#946;c subunit. The method further comprises                  adding a dissociating agent to the sample to                  remove binding proteins. The dissociating agent                  is SDS, sodium deoxycholate, or Tween 20.                  Modulating the abnormal growth of a cell                  comprises modulating the level or bioactivity of                  activin &#946;c subunit. Up-regulating or                  down-regulating activin &#946;c subunit                  levels or bioactivity to a functionally effective                  or ineffective level, respectively, induces the                  abnormal growth. The method further comprises                  administering to the mammal an amount of an agent                  for a time and under conditions to induce a                  functionally ineffective or effective level of                  activin &#946;c subunit. Therapeutically                  and/or prophylactically treating a condition, or                  a predisposition to the development of a                  condition, characterized by an aberrant, unwanted                  or inappropriate level or bioactivity of activin                  &#946;c subunit in a mammal, comprises                  modulating the level of activin &#946;c                  subunit in the mammal.Preferred Composition: The composition                  comprises an antibody directed to an epitope of                  an activin &#946;c subunit together with a                  suitable diluent, excipient or carrier.Preferred Kit: The detection means is an                  antibody directed to an epitope of an activin                  &#946;c subunit together with a suitable                  diluent, excipient or carrier.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Gene Therapy.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration is by respiratoral,                intratracheal, nasopharyngeal, intravenous,                intraperitoneal, subcutaneous, intracranial,                intradermal, intramuscular, intraocular,                intrathecal, intracerebral, intranasal, infusion,                or rectal, via intravenous dip patch or implant,                and preferably oral means. No dosage given.

TI Skin diagnostics performing method, involves            generating output signature indicative of composition            of material sample, where output signature is based on            output values of pixels of image from imaging            sensor.
AU STRASFELD D B
   HERMAN I M
   LEE W D
   WILLIAMS R D
   MADDEN S P
AE PRECISION HEALING INC (PREC-Non-standard)
   PRECISION HEALING INC (PREC-Non-standard)
GA 2021873811
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves scanning (110) several                optical excitation light wavelength bands on a                material sample. The material sample exhibits                optical spectral characteristics along the light                wavelength spectrum. The excitation response                wavelengths emitted by the material sample is                captured (120) in response to several optical                excitation light wavelength bands. The capturing is                accomplished using an imaging sensor. The output                values of several pixels of an image is measured                (140) from the imaging sensor. The image represents                excitation response wavelengths captured by the                imaging sensor. The measuring detects optical                spectral characteristics of the material sample.                The optical spectral characteristics are in                response to several optical excitation light                wavelength bands. An output signature indicative of                composition of the material sample is generated                (150). The output signature is based on                interpreting the output values that were                measured.
   USE - Method for skin diagnostics using optical                signatures for Wound Care Diagnostics and Treatment                such as healing of a wound such as a tissue wound                or an organ wound, recovery from an infection such                as an infection of the skin or organ, or a                respiratory infection such as COVID-19 or                influenza, detection to facilitate removal of                residual cancer, and so on.
   ADVANTAGE - The method enables handheld, portable, multi                spectral material sample analysis.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a computer program product embodied in a                computer readable medium for skin diagnostics;                and
   a computer system for skin diagnostics.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow diagram for skin                diagnostics using optical signatures.
   110Step for scanning several optical                excitation light wavelength bands on a material                sample
   120Step for capturing excitation response                wavelengths emitted by the material sample
   130Step for including non-florescent                wavelengths
   140Step for measuring output values of                several pixels of an image
   150Step for generating output signature                indicative of composition of the material                sample

TI Identifying a compound or mixture of compounds            with immunomodulatory effect on skin by incubating            dendritic cells and/or Langerhans cells with the            compound, detecting expression product of a gene, and            assigning an immunomodulatory effect.
AU SANCHEZ-MADRID F
   DE LA FUENTE FLORES H
   MITTELBRUNN HERRERO M
   LAMANA DOMINGUEZ A
AE CENT NACIONAL INVESTIGACIONES CIENTIFICA (NAIN-Non-standard)
   UNIV AUTONOMA MADRID UAM (UMAD-C)
   UNIV MADRID AUTONOMA (UMAD-C)
GA 2011A60304
AB    NOVELTY - Identifying a compound or mixture of compounds                with immunomodulatory effect on the skin comprises:                (a) obtaining dendritic cells and/or isolated                Langerhans cells; (b) incubating the cells with the                compound or mixture of compounds; (c) detecting the                quantity of the expression product of at least one                gene in the cell; (d) comparing the amount of                product detected in (c) with a reference control;                and (e) assigning an immunomodulatory effect of the                compound or mixture having a significant difference                observed from the comparison.
   USE - The method and kit are useful for identifying                a compound or mixture of compounds with                immunomodulatory effect on the skin (all claimed).                The compound or mixture of compounds can be used                for treating inflammatory skin diseases and                preventing skin cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Identifying a compound or mixture of compounds                with immunomodulatory effect on the skin comprises:                (a) obtaining dendritic cells and/or isolated                Langerhans cells; (b) incubating the cells with the                compound or mixture of compounds; (c) detecting the                quantity of the expression product of at least one                gene in the cell selected from protein tyrosine                phosphatase receptor type E (PTPRE), inducible                co-stimulatory ligand (ICOSL), galectin-1 (Gal-1),                galectin-3 (Gal-3), Src-like adaptor protein (SLA),                suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (SOCS1),                thrombospondin-1 (THBS1), or growth arrest and DNA                damage 45 (GADD45); (d) comparing the amount of                product detected in (c) with a reference control;                and (e) assigning an immunomodulatory effect of the                compound or mixture having a significant difference                observed from the comparison. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM                is included for a kit for performing the method                above comprising the necessary elements for the                detection of the expression product of at least one                of the genes selected from PTPRE, ICOSL, Gal-1,                Gal-3, SLA, SOCS1, THBS1, or GADD45.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: Identifying a compound or                  a mixture of compounds with immunomodulatory                  effect on the skin further comprises, between (b)                  and (c), irradiating the cells with ultraviolet                  light. Detecting the quantity of the expression                  product comprises detecting the amount of                  expression products of genes selected from PTPRE,                  ICOSL, Gal-1, Gal-3, SLA, SOCS1, THBS1, or                  GADD45. The immunomodulatory effect is an                  immunological tolerance-inducing effect. The                  immunological tolerance inducing effect is                  assigned if: (i) an amount of the detected                  expression product of at least one of PTPRE,                  ICOSL, Gal-1, Gal-3, SLA, or SOCS1 is                  significantly lower than reference control; and                  (ii) an amount of the detected expression product                  of at least one of THBS1 or GADD45 is                  significantly greater than the reference control.                  The immune tolerance inducing effect is assigned                  if: (i) an amount of the detected expression                  product of at least one of PTPRE, ICOSL, Gal-1,                  Gal-3, SLA, or SOCS1 is significantly less than                  the amount of reference control; and (ii) an                  amount of the detected expression product of at                  least one of THBS1 or GADD45 is significantly                  greater than the reference control. The                  immunomodulatory effect is a photoprotective                  effect of UV rays. The photoprotective effect of                  UV is assigned if: (i) an amount of the detected                  expression product of at least one of PTPRE,                  ICOSL, Gal-1, Gal-3, SLA, or SOCS1 is                  significantly greater than the reference control;                  and (ii) an amount of the detected expression                  product of at least one of THBS1 or GADD45 is                  significantly less than the amount of reference                  control. The UV radiation is UVA or UVB. The                  expression product is mRNA, where the mRNA is                  detected by microarray of nucleic acids or by                  reverse transcriptase (RT)-PCR. The expression                  product is also a protein, where the protein is                  detected in a total cell extract and detected by                  Western blot.
   ACTIVITY - Immunomodulator; Antiinflammatory;                Dermatological; Cytostatic. Test details are                described but no results given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - Polypeptide agents (I) (especially antibodies)                comprising claudin cell adhesion recognition (CAR)                sequences and capable of modulating                claudin-mediated cell adhesion, are new.
   USE - (I) may be used to modulate claudin-mediated                cell adhesion, for decreasing undesirable                claudin-mediated cell adhesion, for increasing                vasopermiability in a mammal (by inhibiting                claudin-mediated cell adhesion), for treating                cancer by enhancing the delivery of a drug through                the skin of a mammal, for enhancing the delivery of                a drug to a tumor in a mammal, for inhibiting                angiogenesis, for enhancing drug delivery to the                nervous system, for enhancing wound healing, for                enhancing adhesion of foreign tissue implanted                within a mammal and for inducing apoptosis in cells                that express claudin, for detecting cells that                express claudin (claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a cell adhesion modulating agent (I)                that:
   comprises a claudin CAR (cell adhesion                recognition) sequence; and
   contains 3-16 amino acid residues linked by                peptide bonds;
   a polynucleotide (II) encoding (I);
   an expression vector (III) comprising                (II);
   a host cell (IV) transformed with (III);
   a method (V) for detecting the presence of                claudin expressing cells, comprising contracting a                sample with an antibody that binds to a claudin                comprising a CAR sequence and detecting the level                of antibody-claudin complexes in the sample;
   a kit for use in (V) comprising an antibody                that binds to a claudin comprising a CAR sequence                and a detection agent; and
   a kit (VI) for enhancing drug delivery,                comprising a skin patch and (I) (which inhibits                claudin-mediated cell adhesion).
EA    (EP1127119-A1)   NOVELTY - Polypeptide agents (I) (especially antibodies)                comprising claudin cell adhesion recognition (CAR)                sequences and capable of modulating                claudin-mediated cell adhesion, are new.
   USE - (I) may be used to modulate claudin-mediated                cell adhesion, for decreasing undesirable                claudin-mediated cell adhesion, for increasing                vasopermiability in a mammal (by inhibiting                claudin-mediated cell adhesion), for treating                cancer by enhancing the delivery of a drug through                the skin of a mammal, for enhancing the delivery of                a drug to a tumor in a mammal, for inhibiting                angiogenesis, for enhancing drug delivery to the                nervous system, for enhancing wound healing, for                enhancing adhesion of foreign tissue implanted                within a mammal and for inducing apoptosis in cells                that express claudin, for detecting cells that                express claudin (claimed).

                 and(Z )=optionally present, an amino acid                  residue linked to Z 1 by a peptide bond.(Y1) and (Y2) are preferably cysteine                  residues and may also be linked by a disulphide                  bond, a thioether bond or an amide bond between                  terminal functional groups or amino acid side                  chains.(Y ) and (Y )=are preferably independently                  selected from penicillamine,                  &#946;,&#946;-tetramethylene cysteine,                  &#946;,&#946;-pentamethylene cysteine,                  &#946;-mercaptopropionic acid,                  &#946;,&#946;-pentamethylene-&#946;-mercaptopropionic                  acid, 2-mercaptobenzene, 2-mercaptoaniline and/or                  2-mercaptoproline.Further:(Y )=lysine or ornitine if (Y 2 ) is                  aspartate or glutamate (and vice versa );                  and/oran antibody (or antigen binding fragment)                  that specifically binds to a CAR sequence bound                  by an adhesion molecule other than a                  claudin.The adhesion molecule is either integrins,                  cadherins, occludin, immunoglobulins (e.g. N-CAM,                  JAM and PECAM), fibronectin, laminin and/or other                  extracellular matrix proteins.(I) comprises 1 or more defined claudin-1                  CAR sequences given in the specification, such as                  IYSYand KKIYSYEand in particular the linear                  peptide sequences:N-Ac-WKIYSYAGN-NH2andN-Ac-WKIYSYAG-NH2which are present in a cyclic peptide. In this case (I) binds to                  the claudin-3 CAR sequence WRVSAFIG.(I) may further comprise 1 or more claudin-4                  CAR sequences such as VTAF, VTAFIGand WRVTAFIand                  in particular the linear peptide:N-Ac-WRVTAFIG-NH2present in cyclic peptide comprising a                  defined sequence given in the specification, such                  as CVTAFCand RVTAFI.    ACTIVITY - Cardiovascular; cytostatic; anti-angiogenic;                neuroactive; dermalogical; apoptotic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - Antibody modulation (claimed) of                claudin-mediated cell adhesion.
   The mean electrical resistance across MDCK                (Mandane Derby canine kidney) cell monolayers                cultured for 24 hours in medium alone (control) or                a medium containing Peptide 118 (Ac-WKIYSYAGDN-NH2)                at various concentrations was determined. It was                found that Peptide 118 reduced the electrical                resistance across the monolayer in a dose dependent                manner (e.g. Control = 300 ohms/cm2, 0.062 mg/ml of                peptide = 250 ohms/cm2and 0.5 mg/ml of peptide = 10                ohms/cm2). This demonstrated the ability of Peptide                118 to inhibit the formation of tight junctions in                epithelial cells.
   ADMINISTRATION - (I) may be administered with other drugs in a                sustained release composition (claimed).

AB    NOVELTY - In the treatment of cancer an isolated                antibody or antigen-binding fragment that                specifically binds to specific sequence, is                used.
   USE - For the treatment of cancer selected from                liver cancer, pancreatic cancer, lung cancer,                breast cancer, bladder cancer, kidney cancer, skin                cancer and hematological cancer in a subject                (claimed); and also used in vaccine composition for                treatment of cancer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - In the treatment of cancer an isolated                antibody or antigen-binding fragment that                specifically binds to sequence given in any one of                SEQ ID NOs: 1-24, as available in WIPO website is                used. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   use of an isolated polypeptide comprising a                sequence given in any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24, as                available in WIPO website and/or its fragment or                variant having at least 90% identity to it, in the                treatment of cancer;
   use of an isolated polynucleotide encoding an                amino acid sequence given in any one of SEQ ID NOs:                1-24, or encoding a fragment or variant of a                sequence given in SEQ ID NOs: 1-24 having at least                90% identity to it, in the treatment of                cancer;
   use of an oligonucleotide that is                complementary to a polynucleotide encoding an amino                acid sequence given in any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24,                or encoding a fragment or variant of SEQ ID NOs:                1-24 having at least 90% identity to it, in the                treatment of cancer;
   an endotoxin-free pharmaceutical composition                (C1) comprising a carrier and an isolated antibody                and/or its antigen-binding fragment that                specifically binds the sequence (S1) of SEQ ID NOs:                1-24;
   a pharmaceutical composition (C2) formulated                for intravenous injection for use in a patient                having or at risk for having cancer, comprising a                carrier and an isolated antibody and/or its                antigen-binding fragment that specifically binds                the sequence (S1);
   a pharmaceutical composition (C3) comprising a                carrier and at least one isolated polypeptide of                any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24, or its fragment and/or                variant having at least 90% identity to it, or an                isolated polynucleotide encoding any one of the                polypeptides;
   detecting (M1) the presence of a cancer in a                patient, involving: either obtaining a biological                sample from the patient; contacting the biological                sample with an antibody or antigen-binding fragment                that specifically binds to a polypeptide of any one                of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24; detecting in the sample an                amount of polypeptide that binds to the antibody or                antigen-binding fragment; and comparing the amount                of polypeptide to a predetermined cut-off value and                determining the presence of a cancer in the                patient; or obtaining a biological sample from the                patient; contacting the biological sample with an                oligonucleotide that hybridizes to a                polynucleotide, where the polynucleotide encodes a                polypeptide of any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24, or                encodes a fragment and/or variant having at least                90% identity to it; detecting in the sample an                amount of a polynucleotide that hybridizes to the                oligonucleotide; and comparing the amount of                polynucleotide that hybridizes to the                oligonucleotide to a predetermined cut-off value,                and determining the presence of the cancer in the                patient;
   a diagnostic kit comprising at least one                isolated antibody and/or its antigen-binding                fragment that specifically binds to a sequence of                any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24 and a detection                reagent, where the detection reagent comprises a                reporter group;
   a diagnostic kit comprising at least one                oligonucleotide that hybridizes to a                polynucleotide, where the polynucleotide encodes a                polypeptide of any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24, or                encodes a fragment and/or variant having at least                90% identity to it; and
   treating (M2) a cancer in a patient,                involving: (a) detecting an amount of polypeptide                of any one of SEQ ID NOs: 1-24 in a biological                sample of a patient; (b) comparing the amount of                the polypeptide to a predetermined cutoff value and                determining the presence of a cancer in the                patient; and (c) administering the compositions                (C1) and (C2) to a subject determined to have                cancer in step b).
