TI Identifying variants in tissue sample from subject            comprises e.g. obtaining plasma sample and tissue            sample from subject, extracting nucleic acid molecules            from plasma sample and tissue sample and sequencing            extracted nucleic acid molecules.
AU WEST J
AE PERSONALIS INC (PERS-Non-standard)
GA 202124301H
AB    NOVELTY - Identifying at least one variant in tissue                sample from subject, comprises: (a) obtaining                plasma sample and tissue sample from subject, where                plasma sample comprises cell-free nucleic acid                molecules; (b) extracting nucleic acid molecules                from plasma sample and tissue sample, where                extracted nucleic acid molecules comprise at least                subset of cell-free nucleic acid molecules of                plasma sample; (c) independently sequencing                extracted nucleic acid molecules from plasma sample                and tissue sample to generate set of sequence                reads, where set of sequence reads comprise                sequences derived from at least subset of cell-free                nucleic acid molecules and sequences derived from                tissue sample; and (d) identifying variants in                sequences derived from tissue sample, after step                (c), where sequences derived from cell-free nucleic                acid molecules are normal, and variants are                identified by processing sequences derived from                tissue sample against normal.
   USE - The method is useful for: identifying at least                one variant in tissue sample from subject, where                the variants comprise a copy number variation                (preferred), small insertions and deletions, single                nucleotide polymorphisms and/or multiple nucleotide                polymorphisms, the variants are causal or                predisposing for a disease, the variants are                non-causal for a disease, and the non-causal                variant is a mosaic variant, where the tissue                sample comprises a tumor cell, the tissue sample                comprises malignant tissue and/or benign tissue,                and the tissue sample is a fixed sample, where the                subject is suffering from cancer, and the subject                is a human subject (all claimed); improving                detection and monitoring of human diseases;                generating a mutation map (e.g. developmental                mutation map and/or spatial mutation map) for a                subject to determine the source of a given nucleic                acid sequence or its portion in the subject;                determining the source of a disease in the subject                e.g. cancer; detecting differential mutations in a                blood sample of a subject; monitoring state(s) of                health of at least one tissue of a subject;                identifying a tissue of origin of a tumor                metastasis in a subject; identifying or monitoring                a disease condition (e.g. cancer) in the subject;                monitoring, diagnosing and/or detecting diseases in                a subject e.g. a human subject, by detecting                genetic variations in the subject; detecting                genetic mosaicism; detecting differential mutations                in a blood sample of a subject; detecting,                monitoring, diagnosing, and/or treating neurologic                diseases e.g. amyotrophic lateral sclerosis,                arteriovenous malformation, brain aneurysm, brain                tumors, dural arteriovenous fistulas, epilepsy,                headache, memory disorders, multiple sclerosis,                Parkinson's disease, peripheral neuropathy,                post-herpetic neuralgia, spinal cord tumor and                stroke; predicting, diagnosing, and/or prognosing a                status or outcome of a disease or condition in a                subject based on at least one biomedical output,                where the disease or condition includes e.g.                cancers (e.g. bone cancer, fibrosarcoma,                chondrosarcoma, Ewing's sarcoma, Kaposi's sarcoma,                leiomyosarcoma, liposarcoma, lymphangiosarcoma,                breast cancer, pancreatic cancer, lung cancer,                colon cancer, colorectal cancer, rectal cancer,                kidney cancer, bladder cancer, stomach cancer,                prostate cancer, liver cancer, ovarian cancer,                brain cancer, vaginal cancer, vulvar cancer,                uterine cancer, oral cancer, penile cancer,                testicular cancer, esophageal cancer, skin cancer,                cancer of the fallopian tubes, head and neck                cancer, gastrointestinal stromal cancer,                adenocarcinoma, glioblastoma, Hodgkin's lymphoma,                and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma), and additional                diseases and/or conditions including                atherosclerosis, inflammatory diseases (e.g. acne                vulgaris, Alzheimer's, ankylosing spondylitis,                arthritis, asthma, atherosclerosis, celiac disease,                chronic prostatitis, Crohn's disease, and colitis),                autoimmune diseases (e.g. Addison's disease,                agammaglobulinemia, alopecia areata, autoimmune                cardiomyopathy, Castleman's disease, celiac                disease, Chagas disease, glomerulonephritis,                Goodpasture's syndrome, Hashimoto's thyroiditis,                myasthenia gravis, myositis, vasculitis, vitiligo,                and Wegener's granulomatosis) and rheumatic heart                disease; monitoring the health of a fetus; and                detecting, monitoring, quantitating, or evaluating                at least one pathogen-derived nucleic acid                molecules or at least one disease or condition                caused by at least one pathogen.
Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: provides spatial and/or                developmental localization of the source of each                differential mutation within the body; increases                the sensitivity or specificity when compared to the                sensitivity or specificity of current sequencing                methods; and enables detection of extra or missing                chromosomes, preferably associated with birth                defects or miscarriage.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The method further                  comprises: obtaining an additional blood or                  plasma sample at a later time point, repeating                  the steps (b)-(d), and reporting changes in the                  variants, where the changes are a quantified                  signal of a variant from the variants; providing                  a report and/or a therapeutic intervention based                  on an identification of the variants; enriching                  the extracted nucleic acid molecules of the                  tissue sample or the plasma sample; enriching the                  extracted nucleic acid molecules of the tissue                  sample and the plasma sample, where the extracted                  nucleic acid molecules are enriched based on mean                  size, mean guanine-cytosine content, genomic                  regions, and/or genomic region feature; and prior                  to the step (c), amplifying the extracted nucleic                  acid molecules. The step of enriching comprises                  using a capture probe that hybridizes to at least                  one of the extracted nucleic acid molecules,                  where the capture probe is attached to an array                  or a bead.Preferred Components: The plasma sample is                  derived from a whole blood sample. The cell-free                  nucleic acid molecules comprise DNA.
   ACTIVITY - Neuroprotective; Cerebroprotective;                Vasotropic; Cytostatic; Anticonvulsant; Analgesic;                Nootropic; Antiparkinsonian.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.

TI Miniature medical spectrometer device for e.g.            endoscopic procedure, has housing holding solid state            light source, light projection optical unit, light            collection optical unit, wavelength selector and            detector.
AU COHEN SHWARTZ S
   ORESNTEIN M
   ORENSTEIN M
AE TECHNION RES&DEV FOUND LTD (TECR-C)
   SHWARTZ S C (SHWA-Individual)
   ORENSTEIN M (OREN-Individual)
GA 2010Q60961
AB    NOVELTY - The device (100) has a solid state light                source (11) i.e. two photon emission source,                generating high intensity broad wavelength infrared                light. A light projection optical unit projects the                generated light on a biological subject e.g. human                tissue. A light collection optical unit collects                reflected light from the subject. A wavelength                selector i.e. grating (15), spectrally analyzes the                collected light. A detector e.g. solid state                detector array (16), detects analyzed light.                Housing holds the source, optical unit, wavelength                selector and the detector, where the housing is                sized to be hand held.
   USE - Miniature medical spectrometer device for                therapeutic excision, micro-surgery, endoscopic                procedure, core-needle biopsy, esophagus cancer                surgery, pancreatic cancer surgery in a surgery                room, screening and diagnosis of cervical cancer,                vulnerable plaque, screening and diagnosis of                tumors and polyps in digestive tract, lumpectomy,                nephrectomy, prostatectomy, lung cancer, skin                cancer and other maladies in an                obstetrician/gynecologist and dermatologist office,                and scanning internal organ such as esophagus,                small and large intestines for suspected lesion and                assess glucose level in diabetic patient.
   ADVANTAGE - The device is small in size, thus enabling the                device to insert into the body during medical                procedures, and the light source is made of                available and inexpensive materials. The device                provides a small footprint and low power                consumption inspection device that allows for a                variety of possible configurations such as hand                held spectral inspection tool. The device provides                a health monitoring device such as glucose monitor,                shaped as a wrist watch, thus directing the laser                light to skin of user through a miniature                spectrometer in the monitor, and hence determining                non-invasively glucose level and/or level of other                substances in the tissue in front of tissue's                optical window. The device is capable of real time                acquisition of spectra from tissue adjacent to a                biopsy-obtaining-tip of a biopsy apparatus. The                detector array is positioned at locations in which                relevant wavelengths are focused, and with gaps                where wavelengths irrelevant to the desired                diagnosis are focused, thus reducing number of                detection elements, and hence reducing cost and                power consumption.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a method for acquiring spectra from biological                tissue
   a method for diagnosing tissue.

TI Detecting non-metastatic cancer in subject by            using subset of cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid (cfDNA)            polynucleotides to measure total cfDNA fragment size            distribution, and computer processing total cfDNA            fragment size distribution.
AU WENG L
   FAHAM M
   WITTKOP T
   LU Y
   TANG L F
   DENG L
AE ACCURAGEN HOLDINGS LTD (ACCU-Non-standard)
   WENG L (WENG-Individual)
   ACCURAGEN HOLDINGS LTD (ACCU-Non-standard)
   ACCURAGEN HOLDINGS LTD (ACCU-Non-standard)
GA 202083917E
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting a non-metastatic cancer in a subject                involves: (a) obtaining a sample comprising                cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid (cfDNA)                polynucleotides of the subject; (b) using subset of                the cfDNA polynucleotides or derivatives to measure                a total cfDNA fragment size distribution for the                cfDNA polynucleotides of the subject; (c) computer                processing the total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for the cfDNA polynucleotides of the                subject with the total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for the cfDNA polynucleotides from a                healthy control; and (d) classifying the subject as                having an increased risk of non-metastatic cancer                when, based at least in portion on a result of (c).                The total cfDNA fragment size distribution shows an                increase in fragments having sizes of up to 170                bases in the subject as compared to the healthy                control.
   USE - The methods are useful for detecting a                non-metastatic cancer in a subject, where the                cancer is selected from colon cancer, non-small                cell lung cancer, small cell lung cancer, breast                cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, liver cancer,                skin cancer, malignant melanoma, endometrial                cancer, esophageal cancer, gastric cancer, ovarian                cancer, pancreatic cancer, and brain cancer; for                measuring cfDNA size distribution in a blood sample                from a subject; and for detecting a tumor in a                subject (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The methods can detect cancer early, for                example prior to metastasis of the cancer from the                primary tumor site; and have accurate cancer                detection that is minimally invasive and capable of                being offered to seemingly healthy individuals                during routine health screening.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   measuring cfDNA size distribution in a blood                sample from a subject, which involves: (a)                obtaining a sample comprising cfDNA polynucleotides                from the blood sample of the subject; (b) using                subset of the cfDNA polynucleotides or derivatives                to measure a total cfDNA fragment size distribution                for the cfDNA polynucleotides of the subject; (c)                computer processing the total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for the cfDNA polynucleotides of the                subject with the total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for the cfDNA polynucleotides from a                healthy control; and (d) classifying the subject as                having an increased risk of non-metastatic cancer                when, based at least in portion on a result of (c),                the total cfDNA fragment size distribution shows an                increase in fragments having sizes of 50 bases to                170 bases in the subject as compared to the healthy                control;
   detecting a tumor in a subject, which                involves: (a) obtaining a sample comprising cfDNA                polynucleotides from a blood sample of the subject;                (b) using subset of the cfDNA polynucleotides or                derivatives to measure a total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for the cfDNA polynucleotides of the                subject; (c) computer processing the total cfDNA                fragment size distribution for the cfDNA                polynucleotides of the subject with the total cfDNA                fragment size distribution for the cfDNA                polynucleotides from a healthy control; and (d)                detecting a tumor when, based at least in portion                on a result of (c), the total cfDNA fragment size                distribution shows an increase in fragments having                sizes of 50 bases to 170 bases in the subject as                compared to the healthy control;
   a system for detecting a non-metastatic cancer                in a subject, comprising: (a) a computer configured                to receive a user request to perform a detection of                non-metastatic cancer on a sample comprising cfDNA                polynucleotides; (b) an amplification unit that                performs a nucleic acid amplification reaction on                subset of the cfDNA polynucleotides or derivatives                in response to the user request to yield amplified                cfDNA polynucleotides; (c) a sequencing unit that                (i) sequences the amplified cfDNA polynucleotides                or derivatives to produce sequencing reads; (ii)                determines a length for each individual                polynucleotide of the cfDNA polynucleotides of the                subject; (iii) produces a total cfDNA fragment size                distribution for cfDNA polynucleotides in the                sample; and (iv) computer processing the total                cfDNA fragment size distribution for the cfDNA                polynucleotides of the subject with the total cfDNA                fragment size distribution for the cfDNA                polynucleotides from a healthy control; and (d) a                report generator that sends a report to a                recipient, where the report contains results                indicating a risk of non -metastatic cancer in the                subject; and
   a computer-readable medium comprising code                that, upon execution by one or more computer                processors, implements a method of detecting a                non-metastatic cancer in a subject, the method                involving: (a) receiving a user request to perform                a detection of non-metastatic cancer on a sample                comprising cfDNA polynucleotides from a subject;                (b) performing a nucleic acid amplification                reaction on subset of the cfDNA polynucleotides or                derivatives to yield amplified cfDNA                polynucleotides; (c) performing a sequencing                analysis comprising the steps of (i) sequencing the                amplified cfDNA polynucleotides to produce                sequencing reads; (ii) determining a length for                each individual polynucleotide of the cfDNA                polynucleotides of the subject; (iii) producing a                total cfDNA fragment size distribution for cfDNA                polynucleotides in the sample; and (iv) processing                the total cfDNA fragment size distribution for the                cfDNA polynucleotides of the subject with the total                cfDNA fragment size distribution for the cfDNA                polynucleotides from a healthy control; and (d)                generating a report that contains results                indicating a risk of non -metastatic cancer in the                subject.

TI New multi-specific protein that specifically binds            to interleukin-15 receptor, NKp46 and target antigen            useful in pharmaceutical composition or medicament or            formulation, or pharmaceutical combination for            preventing or treating disorder or disease e.g. cancer            in subject.

AE SHANGHAI EPIMAB BIOTHERAPEUTICS CO LTD (SHAN-Non-standard)
GA 202579659G
AB    NOVELTY - A multi-specific protein that specifically                binds to interleukin (IL)-15 receptor, NKp46 and a                target antigen, is new, where the multi-specific                protein comprises at least three antigen binding                portions (ABPs) comprising one ABP that                specifically binds to NKp46, a second ABP that                specifically binds to IL-15 receptor, and the third                ABP that specifically binds to a target antigen,                the ABP binding IL-15 receptor comprises or                consists of an IL15/IL15R&#945; complex,                optionally an IL15-sushi complex, the three ABPs                are fused to each other with or without a linker,                and optionally the multi-specific protein further                comprises one or two fragment crystallizable (Fc)                region.
   USE - The multi-specific protein, antibody or its                antigen-binding fragment, or immunoconjugate is                useful in the pharmaceutical composition or                medicament or formulation, or pharmaceutical                combination for preventing or treating a disorder                or disease in the subject. The disorder or disease                is a cancer, optionally solid cancer or                hematopoietic cancer e.g. a cancer of a tissue                chosen from colon, rectum, cervix, oropharynx,                nasopharynx, liver, stomach, head and neck, oral                cavity, oesophagus, lip, mouth, tongue, tonsil,                nose, throat, salivary gland, sinus, pharynx,                larynx, prostate, lung, bladder, skin, kidney,                ovary and mesothelium. The disorder or disease is a                cancer chosen from melanoma, metastatic melanoma,                renal cell carcinoma, ovarian cancer, lung cancer,                small cell lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer,                brain cancer, head and neck cancer, breast cancer                (including three-negative breast cancer), colon                cancer, rectal cancer, colorectal cancer, skin                cancer, throat cancer, uterine cancer, cervical                carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate                cancer, pancreatic cancer, gastric cancer, chronic                lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), multiple myeloma,                lymphoma and bladder cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - None given.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   an anti-NKp46 antibody or its antigen-binding                fragment comprising complementarity-determining                region (CDR)-H1, CDR-H2 and CDR-H3 and CDR-L1,                CDR-L2 and CDR-L3, where the CDR-H1 comprises or                consists of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                6, the CDR-H2 comprises or consists of a 17 amino                acid sequence (SEQ ID NO: 7)n fully defined in the                specification or a 17 amino acid sequence (SEQ ID                NO: 16) fully defined in the specification, the                CDR-H3 comprises or consists of the amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 8, the CDR-L1 comprises or                consists of the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO:                10, the CDR-L2 comprises or consists of the amino                acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 11, the CDR-L3                comprises or consists of the amino acid sequence of                SEQ ID NO: 12, optionally, the CDR-Hs and CDR-Ls                are determined according to Kabat scheme;
   a nucleic acid molecule encoding chain of the                antibody or its antigen-binding fragment, or chain                of the multi-specific protein;
   an expression vector comprising the nucleic                acid molecule, preferably the expression vector is                pcDNA, such as pcDNA3.1;
   a host cell comprising the nucleic acid                molecule or expression vector, preferably the host                cell is prokaryotic or eukaryotic, such as HEK293                cells, or CHO cells, such as 293E cells or CHO-K1                cells;
   method for preparing the antibody or its                antigen-binding fragment, or multi-specific                protein;
   an immunoconjugate comprising the antibody or                its antigen-binding fragment, or multi-specific                protein;
   a pharmaceutical composition or medicament or                formulation comprising the antibody or its                antigen-binding fragment, multi-specific protein,                or immunoconjugate, and optionally a supplementary                material;
   a pharmaceutical combination comprising the                antibody or its antigen-binding fragment,                multi-specific protein, or immunoconjugate, and one                or more additional ingredient for treating various                diseases, e.g. a prophylactic and/or therapeutic                agent, such as a detection agent, an anti-tumor                drug, a chemotherapeutic agent, a cytokine, a                cytotoxic agent, an antibody of different                specificity or its functional fragment, a small                molecule drug, an immunosuppressant or a detectable                label or reporter;
   method for preventing or treating a disorder                or disease in a subject involves administering to                the subject, the multi-specific protein,                immunoconjugate, pharmaceutical composition or                formulation, or pharmaceutical combination;                and
   method for detecting the presence of NKp46 in                a biological sample involves (i) contacting a                biological sample with the antibody or its                antigen-binding fragment, or multi-specific protein                under the conditions that allow binding to NKp46,                and (ii) detecting whether a complex is formed                between the antibody or the multi-specific protein                and NKp46, where the formation of a complex                indicates the presence of NKp46.                Asn-Tyr-Tyr-Ile-His (SEQ ID NO: 6),                Ser-His-Phe-Asp-Val (SEQ ID NO: 8),                Ser-Ala-Ser-Ser-Ser-Ile-Asn-Tyr-Met-Asp (SEQ ID NO:                10), Arg-Thr-Ser-Asn-Leu-Ala-Ser (SEQ ID NO: 11)                and Gln-Gln-Arg-Ser-Ser-Tyr-Pro-Tyr-Thr (SEQ ID NO:                12).

The ABP specifically binding to                  IL-15 receptor comprises IL15 and sushi domain,                  forming an IL15-sushi complex, where IL15 is a                  wild type IL15 or a variant comprising one or                  more amino acid substitutions leading to a                  reduced IL-15 potency, optionally the amino acid                  substitutions are chosen from Asp61Ala, Glu64Ala,                  Asn65Ala, Ile68Ala, Leu69Ala, Asn72Ala, Asn65Glu,                  Asn65Ser, Asn65Val and their combination,                  optionally, the substitution are chosen from                  Asn65Ala, Leu69Ala or Asn65Ala+Leu69Ala. TI New dual targeting optical imaging contrast agent            comprising a target binding ligand, an enzyme cleavable            group, a fluorophore and a quencher agent, useful, e.g.            as an optical imaging contrast agent and in diagnosis            to generate images.
AU JOHANNESEN E W M
   JOHANNESEN E
   JOHANNESEN E W
AE GE HEALTHCARE AS (GENE-C)
   GE HEALTHCARE AS (GENE-C)
   JOHANNESEN E W (JOHA-Individual)
GA 2007254276
AB    NOVELTY - Dual targeting optical imaging contrast agent                (A) comprising a target binding ligand; an enzyme                cleavable group; a fluorophore; and a quencher                agent, conjugated with each other in one molecule,                is new.
   USE - (A) is useful: as an optical imaging contrast                agent; in a method of diagnosis to generate images                of a human or animal body by optical imaging; and                for monitoring the effect of treatment of a human                or animal body with a drug to combat a condition                (claimed). (A) is useful: for imaging, diagnosing                (includes screening of selected populations, early                detection, biopsy guidance, characterization,                staging and grading), surgical guidance (includes                tumor margin identification and nerve localization                during resection and sentinel lymph node detection)                for cancer and metastasis, e.g. breast, skin,                colorectal, pancreatic, prostate, lung, stomach,                esophageal, bladder or ovarian cancer; for                detection of diseases where activated macrophages                are present such as vulnerable plaque in                atherosclerosis and in inflammations; for                monitoring the effect of treatment includes therapy                efficacy monitoring and long-term follow-up of                relapse.
   ADVANTAGE - (A) provides an improved target/background                signal ratio and increased specificity and                sensitivity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a composition comprising (A), together with                adjuvants, excipients or diluents;
   generating images of a human or animal body by                optical imaging comprises administering (A) to the                body, and generating an image of a part of the body                to which (A) has distributed; and
   monitoring the effect of treatment of a human                or animal body with a drug to combat a condition,                comprising administering (A) to the body and                detecting the uptake of (A) by cell receptors, the                administration and detection optionally but                preferably being effected repeatedly, e.g. before,                during or after treatment with (A).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preparation (Disclosed): (A) is prepared by                  the procedure described in .Preferred Components: (A) comprises the                  building blocks of the enzyme cleavable group-the                  quencher agent and the target binding ligand-the                  fluorophore. (A) is contrast agent (I) of formula                  (Q-L 1-E-L 2-V 1-L 3-D) or (II) of formula (Q-L                  1-E-L 2-D-L 3-V 1).Q=quencher agent;E=enzyme cleavable group;V =target binding ligand; andD=fluorophore.The target binding ligand has affinity for a                  biological receptor (nucleic acids, proteins,                  lipids, lipoproteins, glycoproteins, receptor                  tyrosine kinases, the family of integrin                  receptors or cancer related antigens) and the                  enzyme cleavable group is activated by an enzyme,                  the receptor and enzyme being co-jointly                  upregulated in the same tissue. The enzyme                  cleavable group is cleaved by an enzyme prior to                  binding of the target binding ligand to a                  receptor. The target binding ligand is peptides,                  peptoids/peptidomimetics oligonucleotides,                  oligosaccharides, lipid-related compounds,                  synthetic small drug-like molecules, inhibitors,                  antibodies and antibody fragments, hormones,                  vitamins, neurotransmitters and derivatives or                  their mimetics. The enzyme cleavable group                  comprises a substrate for an enzyme (a protease,                  a peptidase, an esterase, a phosphatase, a                  phosphodiesterase, a dealkylase or a                  glycosidase/endoglycanase). The enzyme cleavable                  group having affinity for the enzyme (matrix                  metalloproteinases, cathepsins, kallikreins,                  proprotein convertases or membrane bound serine                  proteases).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The quencher agent                  (which is essentially non-fluorescent) is an                  acceptor chromophore and the fluorophore is a                  donor chromophore in a fluorescence energy                  transfer (FRET) relationship. The fluorophore is                  coumarin dyes, benzocoumarin dyes, xanthene dyes,                  phenoxazine dyes, rhodamines dyes, acridone dyes,                  merocyanine dyes, cyanine dyes or derivatives of                  the bis-pyrromethine boron difluoride                  chromophores. The quencher agent is                  2,4-dinitrophenyl, 4-(                  4-dimethylaminophenyl)azobenzoic acid,                  7-methoxycoumarin-4-yl-acetyl or non-fluorescent                  cyanine chromophores.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of (A) is parenteral,                intravenous, transdermal, topical, nasal or                sublingual. No dosage details given.
   EXAMPLE - To Novagel(RTM: Rink amide) resin (0.59                mmol/g), amino acid (1 mmol) in N-methylpyrrolidone                (NMP) was added, and                O-benzotriazol-1-yl-N,N,N',N'-tetramethyluronium                hexafluorophosphate/1-hydroxybenzotriazole in                dimethylformamide (DMF) and diisopropylethylamine                (DIPEA) was added (1 ml) to give the Novagel(RTM:                Rink amide) resin bound peptide (III). (III) was                isolated and then removed the side-chain protecting                groups. Then the resin (65 &#956;mol peptide)                was added with trifluoroacetic acid (3.3 ml)                contained triisopropylsilane and water. To the                reaction mixture diethyl ether (40 ml) was added to                precipitate the peptide. The peptide was washed in                ether to give                Ac-Thr-Met-Gly-Phe-Thr-Ala-Pro-Arg-Phe-Pro-His-Tyr-Lys-Ile-Pro-Gln-Gly-Leu-Leu-Gly-Lys(ivDde)-NH                2peptide (IV). (IV) (40 mg) was dissolved in                N-methylpyrrolidone (10 mg/ml) and DIPEA (160                &#956;l) and Cy5 N-hydroxysuccinimidyl ester                (NHS) (17 mg). The reaction mixture was stirred in                the absence of light for 18 hours, precipitated and                purified to give                Ac-Thr-Met-Gly-Phe-Thr-Ala-Pro-Arg-Phe-Pro-His-Tyr-Lys(Cy5)-Ile-Pro-Gln-Gly-Leu-Leu-Gly-Lys(ivDde)-NH                2peptide (V). (V) was dissolved in DMF contained                hydrazine monohydrate (5 ml). The reaction mixture                was stirred for 1 hour. The DMF solution was then                added to diethyl ether, washed and centrifuged to                give                Ac-Thr-Met-Gly-Phe-Thr-Ala-Pro-Arg-Phe-Pro-His-Tyr-Lys(Cy5)-Ile-Pro-Gln-Gly-Leu-Leu-Gly-Lys-NH                2peptide (VI). (VI) was dissolved in NMP (4 ml) and                DIPEA (160 &#956;l) and Cy7QNHS ester (22.5                mg). The reaction mixture was stirred for 18 hours                and added with diethyl ether (40 ml), precipitated                to give                Ac-Thr-Met-Gly-Phe-Thr-Ala-Pro-Arg-Phe-Pro-His-Tyr-Lys(Cy5)-Ile-Pro-Gln-Gly-Leu-Leu-Gly-Lys(Cy7Q)-NH                2peptide (200 &#956;g, 0.35%).

PN US5796862-A
TI Computer aided identification method of tissue            regions in digital mammographic image involves            producing convex hull image which outlines skin line of            tissue region of body part of digital image by suitable            operation on edge image.
AU SENN R A
   PAWLICKI T F
   GABORSKI R S
AE EASTMAN KODAK CO (EAST-C)
GA 1998467039
AB       The method involves providing a digital image                representing a body part with tissue regions. The                provided digital image is sub-sampled or                interpolated to produce a scaled digital image. The                texture of the scaled digital image is extracted by                a texture extracting unit to produce multiple                texture images with different measure of image                texture of the scaled digital image. A clustered                image is produced by clustering multiple texture                images. The clustered image is labelled based on                both pixel intensity values and geometric adjacency                of pixels, to produce a labelled image.
   A threshold image is obtained by thresholding                the labelled images. The threshold image is                filtered to produce largest component image for                which edge detection is carried out to produce an                edge image containing only edge pixels at high code                value. A convex hull image which outlines the skin                line of the tissue region of the body part of the                digital image is produced by operating an edge                image using a convex hull calculation unit.
   USE -   For breast cancer diagnosis.
   ADVANTAGE -   Distinguishes breast tissue from non-tissue                regions based on image texture energy, reliably.                Attains improved segmentation of breast tissue                region in computationally efficient manner.

TI System for e.g. alerting specialist to suspicious            skin activity between appointments for hair follicle            examinations, has web interface linking computing            device e.g. computer, to web site providing access to            storage of image data.
AU ASAI E M
   DEMAS N P
   SWART E K
AE 3DERM SYSTEMS LLC (THRE-Non-standard)
   SWART E K (SWAR-Individual)
   ASAI E M (ASAI-Individual)

AB    NOVELTY - The system has an imaging device (100) imaging                skin abnormality of a patient and including a                camera. A controller controls linear motion of the                camera over predetermined distance such that the                camera records a set of images from locations                separated by the distance to obtain a stereoscopic                image of the skin abnormality. A data path for                transmission of image data is provided to a                computing device e.g. computer (110). A web                interface (115) links the computing device to a web                site providing access to storage of the image data.                The imaging device includes a track for mounting                the camera.
   USE - System for monitoring skin abnormalities from                a patient's home, and alerting a doctor e.g.                physician and specialist, to suspicious skin                activity between appointments for hair follicle                examinations.
   ADVANTAGE - The system provides a portable, reliable and                user-friendly option to identify, catalogue and                monitor suspicious skin abnormalities to a                patient's primary care physicians and                dermatologists, so that the patients can be                reassured that changes in condition are quickly                noticed and responded to the system, thus improving                patient-doctor interactions by increasing                frequency, and hence reducing cost and time                commitment of the patients and the doctor,                increasing patient awareness of skin health and                improving cancer detection by making easier to                monitor the skin abnormalities. The system images                skin abnormality and sends the images skin                abnormality to the doctor for inspection if the                patients find the abnormality, thus allowing                uploaded scans from a patient portal to be                automatically updated in a doctor portal, and hence                allowing seamless and secure transfers of medical                information and avoiding need for chains of                electronic-mails and attachments between the                patients and the physicians.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The imaging device is a handheld                three-dimensional imaging dermatoscope.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic block diagram                of a system for monitoring skin abnormalities from                a patient's home and alerting a doctor to                suspicious skin activity between appointments for                hair follicle examinations.

GA 2016369490
AB    NOVELTY - Computer-implemented method (M1) to aid in                early detection of the presence of an early stage                cancer in a patient relative to a population,                comprises obtaining a value for each biomarker of a                panel of biomarkers in a biological sample from the                patient, and utilizing a machine learning system                to: e.g. compare each value to a reference value                for that biomarker; and generate, based upon the                comparison, a biomarker composite score, where the                biomarker composite score is a weighted aggregate                of each value and the machine learning system has                determined a weight for each biomarker.
   USE - The method is useful for early detection of                the presence of an early stage cancer in a patient                relative to a population, where the cancer is lung                cancer (preferred), kidney cancer, breast cancer,                bile duct cancer, bone cancer, pancreatic cancer,                cervical cancer, colon cancer, colorectal cancer,                gallbladder cancer, liver or hepatocellular cancer,                ovarian cancer, testicular cancer, lobular                carcinoma, prostate cancer, or skin cancer or                melanoma (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The method reduces the costs, anxiety, and                radiation exposure associated with having lower                risk patients undergo CT (computerized tomography)                scans while helping to ensure that patients at                higher risk of having lung cancer undergo CT                scanning in hopes of detecting the tumor at an                early stage when curative surgery is an                option.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Computer-implemented method (M1) to aid in                early detection of the presence of an early stage                cancer in a patient relative to a population,                comprises obtaining a value for each biomarker of a                panel of biomarkers in a biological sample from the                patient, and utilizing a machine learning system                to: compare each value to a reference value for                that biomarker; generate, based upon the                comparison, a biomarker composite score, where                biomarker composite score is a weighted aggregate                of each value and machine learning system has                determined a weight for each biomarker; generate a                risk score for the patient based on biomarker                composite score and a medical history of the                patient, where risk score is determined by machine                learning system; and classify risk score into one                of many risk categories, where risk categories are                derived from a same cohort population as patient                and each risk category is associated with a                different level of risk, to determine a likelihood                of patient having the cancer. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS                are also included for:
   method (M2) for assessing likelihood that a                patient has lung cancer relative to a population,                comprises obtaining a fluid sample from the                patient, measuring values of multiple biomarkers in                the sample, determining using a machine learning                system, a biomarker composite score from biomarker                measurements, determining a risk score of patient                of having cancer relative to the population, using                machine learning system, where machine learning                system has been trained using a dataset comprising                patients that have been diagnosed with cancer and                patients that have not been diagnosed with cancer,                and determination is made based upon biomarker                composite score and a medical history of                patient;
   method (M3) for determining a risk score for                presence of lung cancer in a patient relative to a                population, comprises measuring a panel of                biomarkers in a patient, determining a normalized                score for each measured biomarker, generating a                biomarker composite score using a machine learning                system, where machine learning system has                determined a weighting for each normalized score                and aggregates normalized score for each biomarker                to form biomarker composite score, quantifying an                increased risk for presence of lung cancer for                patient as risk score, the risk score comprising                biomarker composite score is generated using                machine learning system, and the risk score is                classified into a risk category of many risk                categories derived from a cohort population, with                each risk category comprising a risk score in the                form of a multiplier indicating an increased                likelihood of having the lung cancer relative to                the population, and providing the risk score to                patient along with an indication of whether testing                is recommended to confirm or deny the presence of                cancer;
   grouping of a stratified patient cohort used                to assess a risk for presence of a cancer in a                patient relative to a population, comprising at                least three risk categories, where each risk                category comprises a risk score, a risk identifier                and a range of master composite scores, a patient's                risk score is determined by a machine learning                system based upon a biomarker composite score and a                medical history of the patient, and patient's risk                score is determined by comparison to range of                master composite scores associated with risk                category;
   a kit for use to assess a risk for the                presence of a cancer in a patient relative to a                population, comprising reagents for measuring at                least one cancer biomarker in a sample from the                patient, a risk categorization table, and computer                executable instructions corresponding to a software                application, where upon being executed by a                processor, the instructions generate an interface                with which to access a machine learning system,                determining, by machine learning system, a                biomarker composite score for each sample, and                utilizing biomarker composite score along with a                patient's medical history to generate a master                composite score, where master composite score is                correlated to a category of risk categorization                table;
   a system comprising a machine learning system                comprising at least one processor, the processors                configured to compare each value of a panel of                biomarkers to a reference value for that biomarker,                generate, based upon comparison, a biomarker                composite score, where biomarker composite score is                a weighted aggregate of each value and machine                learning system has determined a weighting for each                biomarker, generate a risk score for patient based                on biomarker composite score and a medical history                of patient, the risk score is determined by the                machine learning system, and classify risk score                into one of many risk categories; and
   a computer program product comprising a                computer readable storage medium storing computer                readable program code comprising instructions                executable by a computerized device, the computer                program code comprising an interface for receiving                biomarker composite scores for a patient, medical                history of patient and information for a data set                having many individuals with cancer and without                cancer, a first neural net module to determine a                cohort population that is the same as the patient,                and a second neural net to determine a likelihood                of the presence of cancer, as compared to cohort                population, based on a risk score, where the risk                score is determined by second neural net based upon                the biomarker composite scores for patient and                medical history, and classify risk score into one                of many risk categories.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Components: The processors are                  configured to: receive data indicating whether or                  not the patient has cancer; determine whether the                  risk score generated by the machine learning                  system is in agreement with the received data;                  and train the machine learning system using the                  received data when the received data is not in                  agreement with the risk score; or determine a                  residence of the patient; analyze geographic data                  to determine whether the residence of the patient                  is a risk factor for having cancer; when the                  residence is determined to be a risk factor,                  determine a weighting for the residence risk                  factor by the machine learning system; and                  utilize the weighted residence risk factor to                  determine the risk score; or determine the                  presence of a genetic mutation in the patient;                  analyze genetic data to determine whether the                  genetic mutation is a risk factor for having                  cancer; when the genetic mutation is determined                  to be a risk factor, determine a weighting for                  the genetic risk factor by the machine learning                  system; and utilize the weighted genetic risk                  factor to determine the risk score; or determine                  whether additional medical information from a                  family member is needed for computation of the                  risk score; obtain the additional medical                  information; and incorporate the additional                  medical information into generation of the risk                  score by the machine learning system. The machine                  learning system is configured to: identify                  problematic information from the medical history                  of the patient; determine parameters for                  constructing a cohort population, based upon                  training data; generate a risk score based on                  imaging data and biomarker velocity data; and                  undergo continuous training, based upon new                  patient data. The program code is executed by the                  processor. In the computer program product,                  another neural net is configured to identify                  problematic information from the medical history                  of the patient. The first neural net is                  configured to determine parameters for                  constructing the cohort population, based upon                  training data. The second neural net is                  configured to: generate a risk score based on                  imaging data and biomarker velocity data; undergo                  continuous training, based upon new patient data.                  The system and the computer program product                  considers information comprising: biomarker                  levels; patient EMRs (electronic medical record);                  medical literature; images; or biomarker                  velocity.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: In the method (M1): each                  value is normalized; and each value is a                  concentration value. The method (M1) comprises                  providing a notification to a physician as to                  whether testing is recommended to determine the                  presence of cancer for the patient. The machine                  learning system further incorporates: imaging                  data from the patient into the generation of the                  risk score; a biomarker velocity of a biomarker                  from the patient into the generation of the risk                  score. The method (M1) comprises: obtaining                  serial values for a biomarker from the patient;                  determining a biomarker velocity for the                  biomarker based upon the serial values; including                  the biomarker velocity into the generation of the                  risk score. The risk score indicates that the                  patient is at a high risk of having cancer                  comprises: obtaining test results which confirm                  or deny the presence of cancer; incorporating the                  test results into a dataset for training the                  machine learning system; and generating an                  improved risk score by the machine learning                  system. The method (M1) comprises at least three                  risk categories, where each risk category                  comprises a risk score correlated to a range of                  master composite scores, and the risk category                  further comprises a risk identifier. The risk                  score is determined, at least in part, from                  retrospective clinical samples. The risk score is                  determined based upon a risk categorization table                  generated by the machine learning system, where                  the risk categorization table includes many risk                  categories, each category correlated to a range                  of master composite scores. The risk score is                  provided to a physician as the patient's                  increased risk of having the presence of cancer                  relative to a rate of having the presence of                  cancer in a population. The method (M3)                  comprises: obtaining a fluid sample from the                  patient, where the sample is blood, blood serum,                  blood plasma, or their some part; and measuring a                  value for each biomarker of the panel of                  biomarker in the sample. In (M3), each risk                  category has associated with master composite                  scores, where the risk categories, each                  multiplier indicating the increased likelihood of                  having the lung cancer within a risk category,                  and each range of master composite scores for a                  risk category are determined by the machine                  learning system, at least in part, from                  retrospective clinical samples of a population;                  the risk categories comprises at least three risk                  categories where the multiplier indicating the                  increased likelihood of having cancer is                  &#8805; 2 or &#8805; 5. The risk                  categorization table, generated by a machine                  learning system and accessible through the                  interface, is utilized for determining a risk                  score of the presence of cancer in the patient                  relative to a population. Preferred Components:                  The medical history of the patient comprises at                  least one clinical parameter comprising age,                  gender, smoking history, symptoms, or family                  history of cancer. The panel of biomarkers                  comprise at least two biomarkers comprising AFP                  (&#945; -fetoprotein), CA125 (cancer antigen                  125), CA 15-3 (cancer antigen 15-3), CA-19-9                  (cancer antigen 19-9), CEA (carcinoembryonic                  antigen), Cyfra 21-1, Pro-GRP                  (pro-gastrin-releasing peptide), NSE                  (neuron-specific enolase), PSA (prostate-specific                  antigen), SCC (squamous cell carcinoma),                  anti-NY-ESO-1, anti-p53, anti-cyclin E2,                  anti-MAPKAPK3 (anti-mitogen-activated protein                  kinase-activated protein kinase 3), HE-4 (human                  epididymis protein 4), calcitonin, PAP                  (plasmin-&#945; 2-antiplasmin complex), BR                  27.29, CA125 II, Her-2 (human epidermal growth                  factor receptor 2), human epididymal protein 4.                  The patient and the population are over age 50                  and have had a history of smoking cigarettes or                  tobacco. The smoking history comprises at least a                  20 pack year smoking history. The risk score of                  the patient is compared to a master composite                  score of patients in at least three categories                  comprising those at high, intermediate, and low                  risk. The risk score of the patient is compared                  to the master composite score of patients in at                  least five categories comprising those at                  highest, intermediate high risk, intermediate                  risk, intermediate low risk, and low risk. The                  risk score is in the form of a multiplier                  indicating an increased likelihood of having                  cancer for each risk category. The biomarker                  composite score is a sum of normalized biomarker                  scores determined from a panel of biomarkers for                  the cancer. The ranges of master composite scores                  are derived from retrospective clinical samples.                  The groupings are in a form of a table form, a                  software application, a computer program, or an                  excel spreadsheet. The reagents are antigens or                  antibodies for measuring biomarkers.

AB    NOVELTY - The method involves acquiring (S201) first                image spectral information, second image spectral                information, third image spectral information, and                object detection labels corresponding to the third                image spectral information. The kernel parameters                of a preset kernel function are optimized based on                the first image spectral information and a preset                convolutional model to obtain target kernel                parameters. The convolutional kernels of the                convolutional layers of the preset object detection                model are initialized (S202) based on the target                kernel parameters to obtain an initialized object                detection model. The initialized object detection                model is pre-trained based on the second image                spectral information to obtain a pre-trained object                detection model. The pre-trained object detection                model is fine-tuned (S203) based on the third image                spectral information and the object detection                labels corresponding to the third image spectral                information to obtain a trained object detection                model.
   USE - Method for training object detection model for                identifying and locating specific target in                hyperspectral image for medical health services                such as old age activity area monitoring such as                nursing home safety monitoring, disease early                screening e.g. skin cancer hyperpectral imaging                diagnosis, automatic compensation such as objective                loss determination, and health monitoring of health                care insurance such as physiological index                detection based on skin tissue spectral                characteristics.

GA 2011G28488
AB    NOVELTY - An antibody or its fragment that recognizes an                epitope of a HER2 (human epidermal growth factor                receptor 2) receptor truncated form, the epitope is                defined by a specific amino acid sequence, is                new.
   USE - For the diagnosis and determination of                prognosis in isolated samples of cancers where the                HER2 receptor is expressed; and in the manufacture                of medicament for treatment or prevention of cancer                in which at least the HER2 receptor truncated form                consisting of [SEQ ID NO: 1] is expressed,                including cancer of breast, lung, pancreas, colon,                stomach, prostate, head and neck, skin, kidney,                testicle, thyroids, urinary bladder, uterus, vulva,                endometrium, ovary, oesophagus, mouth, salivary                gland, larynx, peritoneum, nose and throat region,                Fallopian tubes, Wilms tumors, as well as                lymphomas, Swing sarcomas, synovial sarcoma,                medulloblastomas, trophoblastics tumors, glyomas,                glyoblastomas, cholangiocarcinomas, cholesteatoma,                chondrosarcoma, ependymoma, neurilemmomas,                neuromas, rhabdomyosarcomas, in mammals including                human (claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The antibody is capable of discriminating                between the truncated variant of HER2 CTF-611                represented by a sequence containing 645 amino                acids as given in the specification [SEQ ID NO: 1]                and CTF-616 represented by a sequence containing                641 amino acids as given in the specification [SEQ                ID NO: 7]; capable of discriminating between the                truncated variant of HER2 CTF-611 represented by                [SEQ ID NO: 1] and CTF-613 represented by a                sequence containing 644 amino acids as given in the                specification [SEQ ID NO: 6]; and is suitable for                distinguish the protein of [SEQ ID NO: 1] from the                HER2 receptor, and for distinguish the protein of                [SEQ ID NO: 1]from the HER2 receptor truncated form                648-CTF/p95.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An antibody or its fragment that recognizes an                epitope of a HER2 (human epidermal growth factor                receptor 2) receptor truncated form, the epitope is                defined by a sequence containing 42 amino acids as                given in the specification [SEQ ID NO: 2], where                the antibody is capable of discriminating between                the truncated variant of HER2 Carboxy Terminal                Fragment (CTF)-611 represented by a sequence                containing 645 amino acids as given in the                specification [SEQ ID NO: 1]and CTF-616 represented                by a sequence containing 641 amino acids as given                in the specification [SEQ ID NO: 7], is new.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   preparation of the antibody or its                fragment;
   a hybridoma producing the monoclonal                antibody;
   a method of cancer diagnosis, involving the                detection of the presence of the HER2 receptor                truncated form consisting of the amino acid                sequence [SEQ ID NO: 1] in a patient sample, using                at least one of the antibody;
   an agent for diagnosis and determination of                prognosis in isolated samples of cancers of the                type that express the HER2 receptor or its                truncated variants, comprising the antibody or its                fragment; and
   a kit for diagnosis and determination of                prognosis in isolated samples of cancers of the                type that express the HER2 receptor or its                truncated variants, where the unit of detection                comprises at least one of the agent.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Antibodies (Claimed): The antibody or its                  fragment produced by the hybridoma cell line                  deposited with the Deutsche Sammlung von                  Mikroorganismen und Zellen-DSMZ with access                  number DSM ACC3016 or the hybridoma cell line                  deposited with the Deutsche Sammlung von                  Mikroorganismen und Zellen-DSMZ with access                  number DSM ACC3017. The method of producing an                  antibody involves the immunization with a peptide                  that consists of a sequence containing 32 amino                  acids as given in the specification [SEQ ID NO:                  3] or a sequence containing 32 amino acids as                  given in the specification [SEQ ID NO: 4], which                  is optionally conjugated with an immunogen. The                  antibody is monoclonal antibody and is obtained                  by growing the hybridoma cell line in a culture                  medium and the monoclonal antibody is recovered                  from this medium. Preferred Antibody: The epitope                  is one included in a sequence containing 32 amino                  acids as given in the specification [SEQ ID NO:                  3]. The fragment is one selected from the group                  formed by F(ab), F(ab') and Fv. The antibody or                  its fragment is a polyclonal antibody, monoclonal                  antibody or its fragment. The antibody is                  suitable for distinguish the protein of [SEQ ID                  NO: 1]from the HER2 receptor, and for distinguish                  the protein of [SEQ ID NO: 1] from the HER2                  receptor truncated form 648-CTF/p95, where the                  distinction can be visualized by at least one                  immunofluorescence, flow cytometry,                  immunohistochemistry in cultured cells, and                  immunohistochemistry in samples from                  patients.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method of cancer                  diagnosis is a prognostic method allowing the                  prognosis of progression of tumor growth and/or                  metastases. Preferred Agent: In the agent for                  diagnosis, the antibody or its fragment is                  arranged on a solid support.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic. No biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

TI Selecting cancer treatment for male subject,            comprises e.g. detecting loss of Y chromosome            phenotype, and selecting therapy comprising immune            checkpoint inhibitor, and thymocyte            selection-associated high mobility group box protein            inhibitor.
AU THEODORESCU D
   ABDEL-HAFIZ H
   SCHAFER J M
   LI Z
   KAYE J
AE CEDARS SINAI MEDICAL CENT (CSMC-C)
   OHIO STATE INNOVATION FOUND (OHIS-C)
GA 2024C2372S
AB    NOVELTY - Selecting (M1) a cancer treatment for male                subject, comprises: (a) assaying a biological                sample obtained from the male subject to determine                Y chromosome gene expression signature; and (b)                detecting a loss of Y chromosome (LOY) phenotype,                and selecting a therapy comprising an immune                checkpoint inhibitor, and/or thymocyte                selection-associated high mobility group box                protein (TOX) inhibitor, or detecting a Y                chromosome high phenotype, and selecting a therapy                comprising an immune checkpoint inhibitor and an                inhibitor of at least one genes on the Y                chromosome.
   USE - The methods are useful for: selecting a cancer                treatment for male subject; determining                susceptibility to treatment with an immune                checkpoint inhibitor, and/or TOX inhibitor in a                male subject having cancer; and treating cancer in                a male subject, where the cancer comprises bladder                cancer, colon adenocarcinoma microsatellite                instability, skin cutaneous melanoma, kidney renal                clear cell carcinoma, liver hepatocellular                carcinoma, head and neck squamous cell cancer, lung                squamous cell carcinoma, lung adenocarcinoma,                mesothelioma, esophageal carcinoma, sarcoma,                glioblastoma multiforme, or prostate adenocarcinoma                (all claimed). Test details are described but no                results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The method: provides increased tumor growth                control with higher survival rate; utilizes TOX                inhibitor which achieves beneficial results in a                patient with cancer; and can identify diagnostic                biomarkers for cancer e.g. bladder cancer, thus                enabling early detection and identification of                patients requiring treatment.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   treating (M2) cancer in a male subject,                comprising (a1) administering the therapy                comprising an immune checkpoint inhibitor, and/or                TOX inhibitor to the male subject, where the male                subject has been detected to have a LOY phenotype,                or administering the therapy comprising immune                checkpoint inhibitor, and an inhibitor of at least                one genes on the Y chromosome to the male subject,                where the male subject has been detected to have a                Y chromosome high phenotype, or requesting the                results of an assay of a biological sample obtained                from the male subject to determine Y chromosome                gene expression signature, and the step (a1) as per                se; and
   determining (M3) susceptibility to treatment                with an immune checkpoint inhibitor, and/or TOX                inhibitor in a male subject having cancer,                comprising the step (a) as per se, and detecting a                LOY phenotype, where the LOY indicates a                susceptibility treatment with an immune checkpoint                inhibitor, and/or TOX inhibitor, or detecting a Y                chromosome high phenotype, where the Y chromosome                high phenotype indicates a low likelihood of                susceptibility treatment with an immune checkpoint                inhibitor, and/or TOX inhibitor, or indicates a                benefit from a therapy comprising an immune                checkpoint inhibitor and an inhibitor of the genes                on the Y chromosome.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the methods (M1)-(M3),                  the step of detecting LOY phenotype comprises                  detecting a low level of at least one genes on                  the Y chromosome as compared to each gene's                  reference level. Preferred Components: In the                  methods (M1)-(M3): the genes comprises basic                  charge Y-linked 1 (BPY1), basic charge Y-linked                  1B (BPY1B), basic charge Y-linked 2 (BPY2), basic                  charge Y-linked 2B (BPY2B), basic charge Y-linked                  2C (BPY2C), chromodomain Y-linked 1A (CDY)1A,                  CDY1B, CDY2A, chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan 4                  Y-linked (CSPG4LY), chromosome Y open reading                  frame 15A (CYorf15A), chromosome Y open reading                  frame 15B (CYorf15B), deleted in azoospermia 1                  (DAZ)1, DAZ2, DAZ3, DAZ4, DEAD-box helicase 3                  Y-linked (DDX3Y), eukaryotic translation                  initiation factor 1A Y-linked (EIF1AY), golgi                  apparatus protein (GOLGA)1, golgi apparatus                  protein 2 Y-linked (GOLGA2LY), GOLGA3, GOLGA5,                  GOLGA6B, GOLGA6C, GOLGA6D, golgi apparatus                  protein 6L7 pseudogene (GOLGA6L7P), GOLGA7, heat                  shock transcription factor Y-linked 1 (HSFY1),                  heat shock transcription factor Y-linked 2                  (HSFY2), lysine demethylase 5D (KDM5D),                  neuroligin 4, Y-linked (NLGN4Y), PTPN13-related                  protein on Y chromosome (PRY), PTPN13-related                  protein on Y chromosome 2 (PRY2), RNA-binding                  motif protein Y-linked 1A1 (RBMY1A1), ribosomal                  protein S4 Y-linked 2 (RPS4Y2), thymosin                  &#946; 4 Y-linked (TMSB4Y),                  ubiquitin-specific protease 9 Y-linked (USP9Y),                  ubiquitously transcribed Y chromosome                  tetratricopeptide repeat protein (UTY), or                  X-linked KX blood group-related Y-linked protein                  (XKRY), preferably BPY2, CDY1B, CYorfl5A,                  CYorfl5B, DAZ1, DAZ2, DAZ4, DAZ3, DDX3Y, EIF1AY,                  G0LGA1, G0LGA3, G0LGA5, G0LGA7, G0LGA6B, G0LGA6D,                  G0LGA6C, HSFY2, NLGN4Y, PRY2, RBMY1A1, RPS4Y2,                  KDM5D, TMSB4Y, USP9Y, UTY, XKRY, BPY1, or CDY1A,                  more preferably KDM5D, UTY, TBL1Y, and/or ZFY, or                  UTY and/or KDM5D, or NLGN4Y; and the biological                  sample is a tumor sample.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method (M1) further                  comprises administering the selected therapy.                  Preferred Components: In the methods (M1)-(M3),                  the immune checkpoint inhibitor comprises an                  anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor,                  or an anti-programmed death-1(PD-1) inhibitor, or                  atezolizumab.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - TOX inhibitor; BPY1 inhibitor; BPY1B                inhibitor; BPY2 inhibitor; BPY2B inhibitor; BPY2C                inhibitor; CDY1A inhibitor; CDY1B inhibitor; CDY2A                inhibitor; CSPG4LY inhibitor; CYorfl5A inhibitor;                CYorfl5B inhibitor; DAZ1 inhibitor; DAZ2 inhibitor;                DAZ3 inhibitor; DAZ4 inhibitor; DDX3Y inhibitor;                EIF1AY inhibitor; GOLGA1 inhibitor; GOLGA2LY                inhibitor; GOLGA3 inhibitor; GOLGA5 inhibitor;                GOLGA6B inhibitor; GOLGA6C inhibitor; GOLGA6D                inhibitor; GOLGA6L7P inhibitor; GOLGA7 inhibitor;                HSFY1 inhibitor; HSFY2 inhibitor; KDM5D inhibitor;                NLGN4Y inhibitor; PRY inhibitor; PRY2 inhibitor;                RBMY1A1 inhibitor; RPS4Y2 inhibitor; TMSB4Y                inhibitor; USP9Y inhibitor; UTY inhibitor; XKRY                inhibitor; PD-L1 inhibitor; PD-1 inhibitor.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of the immune checkpoint                inhibitor and/or TOX inhibitor is by intratumoral,                intracranial, intraventricular, intrathecal,                epidural, intradural, intraorbital, intracapsular,                intracardiac, intradermal, intramuscular,                intraperitoneal, intrapulmonary, intraspinal,                intrastemal, intrathecal, intrauterine,                intravascular, intravenous, intraarterial,                subarachnoid, subcapsular, subcutaneous,                transmucosal, or transtracheal routes, or via                infusion, or injection. No dosage details                given.

TI Method for planning minimally invasive surgery            based on image navigation, involves repeating process            until determined puncture point reaches lesion area,            connecting all puncture points, and obtaining final            puncture path.
AU QIU J
   HUANG Z
   WEI W
   XU S
   ZHANG P
AE CHINESE PEOPLES LIBERATION ARMY JOINT (CHPE-Non-standard)
GA 2025A62889
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves continuously scanning (S1)                the patient scanning area through the dynamic CT                technology, obtaining multiple detection images,                and constructing a three-dimensional model                according to the detection images. The structure                analysis is performed on the three-dimensional                model based on medical image segmentation                algorithm, and skin, organ, a blood vessel and rib                area are obtained, and the blood vessel and rib                area is marked as dangerous area. An in vitro                candidate point set is constructed according to the                skin area, using Euclidean distance transformation                algorithm to calculate the shortest distance DF1                from each in vitro candidate point to the dangerous                area. The process is repeated, until the first                puncture point reached the pathological change                area, and all puncture points are connected to                obtain the final puncture path.
   USE - Method for planning minimally invasive surgery                based on image navigation for treatment of liver                cancer to use liver tumor radio frequency ablation                to ablate tumor target area.
   ADVANTAGE - The method automatically obtains the optimal                ablation path through iterative optimization, which                improves the liver tumour ablation                efficiency.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                minimally invasive surgery planning system based on                image navigation.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow chart of a planning                method for minimally invasive surgery based on                image navigation. (Drawing includes non-English                language text)
