GA 2002049157
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting single nucleotide polymorphism by                contacting allele-specific oligonucleotide primer                (P1)-target polynucleotide (TP) complex, where TP                is complementary to P1 at one end but where a                terminal nucleotide (nt) and third nt from terminal                nt at the end of P1 may not be complementary to                corresponding nt in TP.
   USE - Diagnosing a disease characterized by a                genetic mutation involves obtaining a sample of a                mutated gene sequence from an organism afflicted                with the disease, and carrying out (M1), where at                least a portion of the mutated gene sequence is                used as either the target polynucleotide or allele                specific oligonucleotide. The mutated gene sequence                is used as a target polynucleotide. The method is                useful for diagnosing a disease caused by, induced                by or related to a mutation in at least one gene,                such as Parkinson's disease, Duchenne muscular                dystrophy, Niemann-Pick disease, polyposis,                neurofibromatosis, polycystic kidney disease,                Tay-Sachs disease, xeroderma pigmentosa,                ataxia-telangiectasia, Huntington disease,                Li-Fraumeni syndrome, beta-thalassemia, sickle cell                anemia, hemoglobin C disease, hemophilia, acute                intermittent porphyria, cystic fibrosis, diabetes,                obesity or cancers such as leukemia, lymphoma,                melanoma, neuroblastoma, retinoblastoma,                rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, head and neck                cancer, skin cancer, brain cancer, esophageal                cancer, stomach cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer,                colon cancer, ovarian cancer, testicular cancer or                prostate cancer (claimed). The methods facilitate                the detection of mismatched sequences indicative of                different alleles, or mutations in selected target                sequences.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is simple, quantitative and                consistent and provides a more reliable                amplification and detection of a target nucleic                acid sequence containing an allele different from                that of a reference sequence. Additionally,                amplification takes place not in cycles, but in a                continuous, isothermal rolling circle replication,                thereby providing a more reliable, simpler and more                consistent output for subsequent detection and                identification.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting (M1) a single nucleotide                polymorphism (SNP) involves:
   (a) contacting one more allele specific                oligonucleotide primers (P1) with one or more                target polynucleotides (TP), where TP possesses a                first portion that is complementary to a second                portion located on the P1 at or near one end, and                the terminal nucleotide and third nucleotide from                the terminal nucleotide, at the end of the P1 may                not be complementary to the corresponding                nucleotide of TP, to form P1-TP complex, by                hybridization between the first and the second                portions;
   (b) contacting the P1-TP complex with an                exonuclease deficient DNA polymerase enzyme under                conditions that promote extension of the P1 with                the TP as template, thereby forming an extended                segment (ES) of P1; and
   (c) detecting the extended P1.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for a                kit comprising:
   (a) several oligonucleotide probes each of                which is capable of hybridizing to one or more                target polynucleotides that may or may not possess                a mismatch with respect to a terminal residue of                the oligonucleotide probes;
   (b) a sample of an exonuclease deficient DNA                polymerase;
   (c) several amplification primers each of                which being capable of hybridizing to an elongated                segment of the oligonucleotide probe as well as                comprising a primer sequence complementary to a                sequence on an amplification target circle (ATC)                for use in rolling circle amplification;
   (d) a sample of one or more ATC, essentially                single stranded DNA circles, each comprising a                sequence of 10 to 20, even 30, nucleotides in                length, which is complementary to a sequence of the                amplification of part (c) and ATCs act as templates                for rolling circle amplification (RCA);
   (e) a sample of a DNA polymerase capable of                carrying out rounds of RCA;
   (f) an unit for detecting the products of RCA,                including various labeling reagents and address                probes; and
   (g) a set of instructions for carrying out                (M1).
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows the allele discrimination                method, where the genomic wild-type and target DNAs                are distinguished by their relative abilities to                support extension of the primer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: (M1) further involves                  removing TP from the complex formed in step and                  contacting a primer oligonucleotide (P2) with the                  extended P1, where the primer oligonucleotide                  comprises a first segment complementary to at                  least a portion of ES formed in step (b) and a                  second segment that includes the 3'-terminus of                  the primer oligonucleotide (P2) under conditions                  promoting hybridization of P2 and the extended P1                  (EP1) to form an EP1-P2 complex; (f) contacting                  an amplification target circle (ATC) with the                  EP1-P2 complex under conditions that promote                  hybridization between the amplification target                  circle and the P2 portion of the EP1-P2 complex                  to form an EP1-P2-ATC complex, and contacting DNA                  polymerase with the EP1-P2-ATC complex under                  conditions that promote replication of the                  amplification target circle, where the                  replication of the ATC results in the formation                  of tandem sequence DNA (TS-DNA) thereby                  indicating the extension of P1. Preferably the                  target polynucleotide is derived from human or                  non-human genomic DNA or a mixture of human and                  non-human genomic DNA. The DNA polymerase used in                  the method is bacteriophage psi29 DNA polymerase,                  phage M2 DNA polymerase, phage psi-PRD1 DNA                  polymerase, VENT (RTM) DNA polymerase, Klenow                  fragment of DNA polymerase I, T5 DNA polymerase,                  PRD1 DNA polymerase, T4 DNA polymerase,                  Escherichia coli DNA polymerase III holoenzyme,                  Tts polymerase or T7 DNA polymerase. The DNA                  polymerase used in the method is exonuclease                  deficient e.g., Klenow polymerase (exo-), Vent                  polymerase (exo-), Deep Vent polymerase (exo-),                  Pfu (plaque forming units) polymerase (exo-), Taq                  polymerase, the Stoeffel fragment of Taq                  polymerase, Bst polymerase, Tts polymerase, or                  ThermoSequenase. Preferably, the DNA polymerase                  used in (M1) is exonuclease-deficient T7                  Sequenase or Tth polymerase. At least one end of                  P1 is attached to a solid support such as                  acrylamide, cellulose, nitrocellulose, glass,                  polystyrene, polyethylene vinyl acetate,                  polypropylene, polymethacrylate, polyethylene,                  polyethylene oxide, glass, polysilicates,                  polycarbonates, teflon, fluorocarbons, nylon,                  silicon rubber, polyanhydrides, polyglycolic                  acid, polylactic acid, polyorthoethers,                  polypropylfumerate, collagen, glycosaminoglycans,                  or polyamino acids. Preferably, the solid support                  is made of glass or plastic. P1 preferably has a                  sequence of e.g. ctcagtgtgattccaccttctcc,                  ctcagtgtgattccaccttcacc or                  tttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttctattctct,                  P2 has a fully defined sequence of 73 (S27), 73                  (S28), 57 (S34), 56 (S35) nucleotides as given in                  the specification. The ATC comprises a fully                  defined sequence of 78 or 80 nucleotides as given                  in the specification. In (M1) the third                  nucleotide from the end of P1 is complementary or                  not complementary to the corresponding nucleotide                  of the target polynucleotide. Preferably, each of                  the terminal nucleotide and the third nucleotide                  from the end of P1 is not complementary to the                  corresponding nucleotide of the target                  polynucleotide.
   EXAMPLE - The target sequences used were the cystic                fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR)                G542X and M11101K loci characteristic of naturally                occurring mutations in cystic fibrosis. Both                wild-type and mutant allele oligonucleotide targets                were utilized as templates, each template being 80                (G542X) or 68 (M1101K) nucleotides in length.                Target-specific oligonucleotides (allele-specific                oligonucleotides or ASOs) of variable length and                containing a 3'-sequence complementary to the                target sequence of the cystic fibrosis loci were                utilized along with the T7 sequenase as                exonuclease-deficient DNA polymerase. P1 primers                useful in the method were wild-type G4542X: C at                3'-end 5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttacctccactcagtgtgattccaccttctcc-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon 12)-                tttttttttttttttttttttttttagtgtgattccaccttctcc-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttgattccaccttctcc-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttcaccttctcc-3'.                Mutant G542X:A at 3' end: 5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttacctccactcagtgtgattccaccttctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttagtgtgattccaccttctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttgattccaccttctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttcaccttctca-3'.                Wild-type M1101K:A at 3' end: 5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttagaagatgacaaaaatcatttctattctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttaaaaatcatttctattctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttcatttctattctca-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttctattctca-3'.                Mutant M1101K: T at 3' end: 5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttagaagatgacaaaaatcatttctattctct-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttttttttttttaaaaatcatttctattctct-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-ttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttcatttctattctct-3',                5'-NH2-(Carbon                12)-tttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttctattctct-3'.                The P1 primers used for the extension may                optionally have an additional mismatch at the -3                position as a means of increasing discrimination.                Primer extension was followed using a bipolar                primer (the P2) and rolling circle amplification                (RCA). RCA products were detected by fluorescence                using a microarray slide scanner. Successful                allelic discrimination was defined on the basis of                the ability of the primer extension/RCA process to                give at least a 10-fold discrimination of mutant                versus wild-type alleles. Glass slides containing                immobilized microarrays of duplicate serial                dilutions of ASO P1 primers were incubated with                6.25 nM target, 1% glycerol, and 100 microg/ml                single-stranded salmon sperm DNA for 1 hour at 45                degrees C. The slides were than washed once. The                ASO P1 primers were then extended by incubation                with 0.09 Units of T7 sequences. The target was                then removed by washing the slide twice. The RCA                circle was pre-annealed to P2 primer and the                circle/primer mixture was diluted 5-fold and added                to microarrays. Annealing to the extended ASP P1                primer was at 42 degrees C for 1 hour in RCA                buffer. The slides were washed once at room                temperature in RCA buffer for 5 min. RCA was then                initiated. RCA products were detected by incubating                the microarrays with 2x saline sodium citrate                (SSC), 0.05 microM Cy3-labeled oligonucleotide                decorators. The slides were then washed once with                2X SSC for 5 min at 37 degrees C and once with 0.5X                SSC at room temperature for 10 seconds. The slides                were dried by spinning at 1,000 rpm for 5 min on a                table top clinical centrifuge. Fluorescence was                measured using a microarray scanner and spot                intensity quantified.

AB    NOVELTY - A diagnostic method for determining the skin                state and genetic predisposition of a subject to UV                radiation (UVR) damage comprises: (a) collecting                tissue samples from the subject; (b) assaying a                first skin sample for mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)                aberrations; (c) assaying a second skin sample for                one or more melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R)                variants; and (d) determining the skin state and                genetic predisposition of the subject to UVR damage                based on the detection of the mtDNA aberrations and                MC1R variants in the skin samples.
   USE - The methods and kit are useful for determining                the skin state and genetic predisposition of a                subject to UVR damage; for non-invasively                monitoring photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease;                for monitoring the subject's response to a                preventative or therapeutic treatment for                photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease; for                screening for an effective therapeutic or                cosmeceutic agent for the treatment of photo-aging,                UVR damage or skin disease; for determining the                level of photo-damage of the subject; for                determining the skin state and genetic                predisposition of the subject to UVR damage; for                predicting photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease;                and for determining a prophylactic or therapeutic                treatment for preventing or ameliorating                photo-aging, UVR damage or skin cancer (all                claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are:
   a non-invasive method for monitoring                photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease,                comprising: (a) collecting the skin sample from the                subject using a non-invasive skin sampling                technique; (b) assaying the skin sample for mtDNA                aberrations at regular intervals over a prescribed                period of time; and (c) determining any changes in                mtDNA aberration identified over the prescribed                period of time;
   a method for monitoring the subject's response                to a preventative or therapeutic treatment for                photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease,                comprising: (a) collecting the first skin sample                from the subject; (b) assaying the first skin                sample for mtDNA aberrations; (c) assaying the                first skin sample for one or more MC1R variants;                (d) determining the skin state and genetic                predisposition of the subject to UVR damage based                on the detection of the mtDNA aberrations and MC1R                variants in the first skin sample; (e) providing a                preventative or therapeutic treatment for                photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease; (f)                collecting a second skin sample from the subject;                (g) assaying the second skin sample for mtDNA                aberrations; (h) repeating (f) and (g) at regular                intervals over a prescribed period of time; (i)                comparing the level of mtDNA aberrations between                the first skin sample and the skin samples taken at                regular intervals to detect changes in mtDNA                aberrations, thus monitoring the effectiveness of                the treatment; and (j) optionally, adjusting the                treatment based on the genetic predisposition of                the subject and the detected changes in mtDNA                aberrations;
   a method of screening for an effective                therapeutic or cosmeceutic agent for the treatment                of photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease,                comprising: (a) collecting the first skin sample                from the subject; (b) assaying the first skin                sample for mtDNA aberrations; (c) treating the                subject with the therapeutic or cosmeceutic agent;                (d) collecting the second skin sample from the                subject following the prescribed period of time;                (e) assaying the second skin sample for mtDNA                aberrations; and (f) comparing the level of mtDNA                aberrations between the first skin sample and the                second skin sample against a control to determine                the effectiveness of the therapeutic or                comesceutical agent;
   a method for determining the level of                photo-damage of the subject, comprising: (a)                collecting the skin sample from a subject; (b)                assaying the skin sample for mtDNA deletions; (c)                comparing the level of mtDNA deletions of the skin                sample against a population of mtDNA deletions                categorized according to age cohorts, and assigning                a photo-age to the subject; and (d) determining the                level of photo-damage of the subject by comparing                the subject's chronological age to the assigned                photo-age; and
   a diagnostic kit for determining the skin                state and genetic predisposition of the subject to                UVR damage, comprising: (i) material for collecting                tissue samples; and (ii) suitable primers, probes                and reagents for carrying out MC1R genotyping and                the detection of mtDNA aberrations.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In determining the skin                  state and genetic predisposition of the subject                  to UVR damage, the aberration is selected from                  deletions, substitutions, and insertions, where                  the aberration is an mtDNA deletion. The deletion                  is a 3895 bp mtDNA deletion in nucleic acids                  546-4444 of the mtDNA genome. The MC1R variants                  are selected from D84E, R142H, R151C, R160H,                  D294H, V60L, and V92M. The first tissue sample is                  a skin sample obtained using the non-invasive or                  minimally invasive skin collecting technique,                  where the skin sample is collected using a                  Sterile swab, cotton tip swap, a small gauge                  needle to collect micro-cores of skin tissue, or                  .a combination. The skin is collected from the                  dermal or epidermal layer of the subject, where                  the skin sample is derived from the heel, nose,                  inner arm, ear, mouth, scalp, chest, shoulder,                  buttock, back, face, nape of the neck, hand,                  head, or a combination. In monitoring                  photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease, the                  non-invasive skin collecting technique yields                  ultra low levels of DNA, where the ultra low                  levels of DNA is 0.1 ng of nucleic acid. In                  monitoring the subject's response to a                  preventative or therapeutic treatment for                  photo-aging, UVR damage or skin disease, the                  first skin sample, second skin sample and skin                  samples taken at regular intervals are obtained                  using a non-invasive or minimally invasive skin                  collecting technique, where the non-invasive or                  minimally invasive skin collecting technique used                  to collect the second skin sample and samples                  taken at regular intervals yields ultra low                  levels of DNA. The regular intervals are biweekly                  or monthly.
   ACTIVITY - Dermatological; Cytostatic; Nootropic. No                biological data given.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

AB    NOVELTY - The apparatus (100) has a multi-state                polarizing optical circuit for filtering a light                beam producing a series of individual polarization                states consisting of linear, circular and                elliptical polarizations discreetly mapping for                illuminating a target (114). A multi-state analysis                optical circuit produces a discrete series of                filtered images enabling calculation of Stokes                parameters on a pixel basis forming two-dimensional                gray scale images for four Stokes parameters. A                camera (109) takes images of the illuminated                target. A computer (115) and a motor control unit                (116) are used for synchronizing data collection                producing a set of digital gray scale parametric                images forming a data set for each source                wavelength. Data analysis is performed on the                entire parametric data set through a numerical                algorithm based upon biophotonic principles                developed to optimize quantitative target                classification on a pixel basis registered to                physical location or data coordinates of the                target.
   USE - Apparatus for optically probing substrates                using a system containing a light source capable of                producing randomly polarized light beam at various                wavelengths for polarization discrimination of                targets including biological tissues for cancer                detection and demarcation and other materials for                stress or other attribute. Uses include but are not                limited to skin cancers, ovarian cancer, colon                cancer, throat cancer or other expressing tumors in                epithelial tissues.
   ADVANTAGE - The apparatus improves image resolution,                imaging filtering and staining/coloring techniques                for qualitative analyze tissue/substrate                characteristics and development of visual                enhancement methods for cancerous tumor                demarcation. The apparatus allows a computer for                synchronization of data collection, thus producing                a parametric data set consisting of normalized                gray-scale images for each of the four Stokes                parameters for each input polarization states and                input wavelengths.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for making an apparatus providing an optical beam                of a particular polarization state illuminating a                target.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a                system for probing a target surface utilizing an                array of source polarizations at different                wavelengths and detection methodology measuring the                back scattered Stokes parameters on a pixel by                pixel basis.

PN WO2014122467-A1; WO2014122467-A4; EP2953524-A1; US2016007893-A1; EP2953524-B1
TI Implantable/wearable device for detecting presence            of markers of e.g. peptide in blood in human for            treating skin cancer at clinical settings, has            transmitting unit for transmitting information to            receiver-relay unit.
AU ROBERTS C E S
AE LOXBRIDGE RES LLP (LOXB-Non-standard)
   FREENOME HOLDINGS INC (FREE-Non-standard)
GA 2014P57659
AB    NOVELTY - The device has a detection unit (101) being in                fluid communication with a biological fluid for                obtaining information regarding identity and                concentration of a biomolecule. A transmitting unit                transmits the information to a receiver-relay unit.                The detection unit includes a sequencing or                identification module i.e. nanopore detection                device, for identifying the biomolecules, where the                detection unit comprises an array of nanopores for                multiplex evaluation of the biomolecules. A                feedback loop signals patency of a feeding                vessel/system and biological fluid flow to the                device.
   USE - Implantable or wearable device for detecting                presence of markers of biomolecule e.g. nucleic                acid such as DNA and RNA, protein such as antibody,                affibody and aptamer, peptide, polysaccharides such                as lectins and sugars, oligosaccharide, lipid,                glycolipid, enzymes, enzyme substrates, ligands,                receptors, antigens, haptens, prognostic targets                such as enzymatic targets such as galactosyl                transferase II and acid phosphatase, hormone or                hormone receptor targets such as human chorionic                gonadotropin (HOG), adrenocorticotropic hormone and                carcinoembryonic antigen (OEA), lymphoid targets                such as alpha-1-antichymotrypsin, immunoglobulin A,                lambda light chain, plasma cell target, secretory                leukocyte protease inhibitor, terminal                deoxynucleotidyl transferase and unclustered B cell                target, tumor targets, cell cycle associated                targets such as apoptosis protease activating                factor-i, bcl-w, bcl-x, bromodeoxyuridine,                cdk-activating kinase, cellular apoptosis                susceptibility protein (OAS), caspase 2, caspase 8,                caspase-3, cyclin dependent kinases, cyclin A,                cyclin Bi, cyclin Di, cyclin D2, cyclin D3, cyclin                E, cyclin G, minichromosome maintenance proteins,                proliferating cell nuclear antigen, p16 protein,                p27 protein, p34cdc2, topoisomerase I,                topoisomerase II alpha, topoisomerase Ill alpha and                topoisomerase II beta, neural tissue and tumor                targets such as alpha B crystallin, excitatory                amino acid transporter i, GAP43, glial fibrillary                acidic protein, glutamate receptor 2, myelin basic                protein, neuroblastoma target, neurofilament 68 kD,                neurofilament i60 kD, neurofilament 200 kD, neuron                specific enolase, protein gene product 9,                synaptophysin, tau, tryptophan hydroxylase,                tyrosine hydroxylase and ubiquitin, and cluster                differentiation targets such as CD1O5, CD1O6,                CD151, CD158a, CD122, CD123, CD142, CD143, CD144,                CDw145, CD146, CD147, CD152, CD153, CD154, CD155,                CD156, CD157, CD163, CD164, CD165, CD166 and                TCR-zeta, in a biological fluid e.g. blood, serum,                plasma, lymph, perspiration, urine, tears and                saliva, in a subject i.e. human, for treating                disease e.g. neoplastic disease, inflammatory                disease, degenerative disease, metabolic disease                such as obesity disease, cachexia disease, diabetes                and anorexia disease, cardiovascular disease such                as atherosclerosis, cardiomyopathies and arterial                inflammation, immunological disorder such as                chronic inflammatory disease and Crohn's disease,                osteoarthritis such as Lyme disease, organ-specific                autoimmunity such as multiple sclerosis,                Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Grave's disease,                contact dermatitis, psoriasis, graft rejection,                graft versus host disease, sarcoidosis, atopic                conditions such as asthma and allergy e.g. allergic                rhinitis and gastrointestinal allergies, such as                food allergies, eosinophilia, conjunctivitis,                glomerular nephritis, certain pathogen                susceptibilities such as helminthic e.g.                leishmaniasis, and certain viral infections such as                HIV and bacterial infections e.g. tuberculosis and                lepromatous leprosy, myopathies such as                polymyositis, muscular dystrophy, central core                disease, centronuclear/myotubular myopathy, nervous                system disorder e.g. neuropathies, Alzheimer's                disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease,                amyotropic lateral sclerosis, motor neuron disease,                traumatic nerve injury, multiple sclerosis, acute                disseminated encephalomyelitis, mitochondrial                disease, migrainous disorder, bacterial infection,                fungal infection, stroke, aging, dementia,                peripheral nervous system diseases and                physcological disorders such as depression and                schizophrenia, oncological disorder such as                leukemia, throat cancer, breast cancer, skin cancer                and renal cancer, and ophthalmic diseases such                asretinitis pigmentosum and macular degeneration                (all claimed), at clinical settings by a physician                and a healthcare administrator. Can also be used                for a non-human animal e.g. chimpanzee, gorilla and                monkey, domesticated animal such as dog, horse,                cat, pig, goat and cow and rodent such as mouse,                rat, hamster and gerbil.
   ADVANTAGE - The device reduces capacitative noise and                allows exploiting capabilities of low-noise                amplifiers for nanopores, thus enabling large-scale                integration of solid-state nanopores with                microfluidic upstream and downstream processing and                permitting new functions with nanopores i.e.                complex manipulations for multi-dimensional                analysis and parallel sensing in two and                three-dimensional architectures while improving                simplicity, efficiency and scalability of workflows                of the device and reducing power consumption on                transponder.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The receiver-relay unit is selected from a                group consisting of a smartphone, a smartglass, a                watch, a tablet and a personal computer. The                solid-state nanopores are made of synthetic                materials such as silicon nitride or graphene.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   a system for monitoring biomolecules and                determining identity in a biological fluid of a                subject within or leaving the subject
   a method for monitoring a subject to evaluate                efficacy of treatment for a disease by implanting a                detector unit on or in the subject and monitoring                changes in level or presence of biomolecule markers                associated with a disease
   a method for monitoring onset or progression                of a proliferative disease in a subject
   a method for monitoring a state of a condition                in a subject.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a                detector unit implanted as part of a blood vessel                graft for monitoring of biomolecules in                blood.

TI New bispecific antibody comprising antigen-binding            domains (having light and heavy chain variable regions)            specifically binding to c-MET and epidermal growth            factor receptor respectively used to treat cancer e.g.            epithelial cell carcinoma.

AB    NOVELTY - Bispecific antibody comprising a first                antigen-binding domain specifically binding to                c-MET and a second antigen-binding domain                specifically binding to epidermal growth factor                receptor (EGFR), is new. The first antigen-binding                domain comprises a first light chain variable                region (VL) and a first heavy chain variable region                (VH) that collectively form a domain capable of                specifically binding to c-MET. The second                antigen-binding domain comprises a second VL and a                second VH. The second VL and the second VH together                form a domain capable of specifically binding to                EGFR.
   USE - The bispecific antibody, the nucleic acid                molecule or set of nucleic acid molecules, vector,                host cell, and conjugate are useful in a medicine                composition for preventing tumor, preventing and/or                treating and/or acting as an adjuvant in treating                diseases related to c-MET and/or EGFR in a subject,                and/or for inhibiting c-MET and/or EGFR activity in                vitro or in a subject, where the disease related to                c-MET and/or EGFR is cancer (cancer associated with                EGFR activating mutations, EGFR gene amplification,                elevated levels of circulating HGF, c-MET                activating mutations and/or c-MET gene                amplification) e.g. epithelial cell carcinoma,                breast cancer, ovarian cancer, lung adenocarcinoma,                small cell lung cancer, non-small cell lung cancer,                oral cavity cancer, colorectal cancer, anal cancer,                prostate cancer, bladder cancer, pharyngeal cancer,                nasal cancer, pancreas cancer, skin cancer, tongue                cancer, esophagus cancer, vagina cancer, cervix                cancer, spleen cancer, testis cancer, gastric                cancer, thymus cancer, thyroid cancer,                hepatocellular carcinoma, sporadic or hereditary                papillary renal cell carcinoma, colon cancer, liver                cancer, kidney cancer or head and neck cancer and                inhibiting c-MET and EGFR activity of in a cell,                where the cells are cells expressing c-MET and/or                EGFR, e.g. tumor cells (all claimed) and detection                internalizing activity.
   ADVANTAGE - The bispecific antibody: has an enhanced tumor                suppressive effect relative to a monospecific                anti-c-MET antibody and/or a monospecific anti-EGFR                antibody, where the tumor suppression effect                comprises inhibition of EGFR and c-MET signaling                pathways, antibody-dependent cell-mediated                cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity and/or                complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) activity;                inhibits NCI-H292 cell proliferation; can bind both                EGFR and c-MET and/or block the downstream                signaling pathways of EGFR and c-MET by, e.g.,                simultaneously blocking the binding of EGF to EGFR                and of HGF to c-MET; is high-affinity EGFR/c-MET                bispecific antibody, which can specifically                recognize or bind EGFR and c-MET and simultaneously                block the binding of EGF to EGFR and the binding of                HGF to c-MET, thus simultaneously blocking the                downstream signaling pathways of both EGFR and                c-MET, and increasing the inhibition of cell                proliferation. The ability of the antibody to                inhibit NCI-H292 cell proliferation was tested by                determining the IC50 value using adherent human                lung cancer cells NCI-H292 cells (Nanjing Kebai)                and human bronchoalveolar carcinoma cells NCI-H322M                cells. The results showed that the IC50 of the                bispecific antibody was 19.86 nM compared to                onartuzumab control antibody of 3588 nM.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included                for:
   nucleic acid molecule or set of nucleic acid                molecules, comprising a nucleotide sequence                encoding the bispecific antibody;
   vector, comprising the nucleic acid molecule                or set of nucleic acid molecules;
   host cell comprising the nucleic acid molecule                or set of nucleic acid molecules or the                vectors;
   preparing the bispecific antibody; and
   conjugate comprising the bispecific antibody                and a conjugation moiety linked to it, where the                conjugation moiety is a therapeutic agent (e.g. a                cytotoxic agent, cytokine, toxin, or                radionuclide).

GA 2009A43204
AB    NOVELTY - Determining in a biological sample either the                presence of enzyme activities involved in                circularizing a non-circular oligonucleotide probe                or the absence of such enzyme activity in the                biological sample comprises: (a) providing a                biological sample; (b) providing an oligonucleotide                probe; (c) contacting the biological sample with                the oligonucleotide probe; (d) amplifying the                circular oligonucleotide template; or (e)                generating no rolling circle amplification                product.
   USE - The methods are useful for determining in a                biological sample either the presence of enzyme                activities involved in circularizing a non-circular                oligonucleotide probe or the absence of such enzyme                activity in the biological sample, correlating                rolling circle amplification event(s), testing the                efficacy of a drug or drug-lead, diagnosing or                prognosing a disease, treating a disease diagnosed,                and treating prophylactically a disease prognosed,                where the disease is cancer, cancer disease is                selected from bladder carcinoma, blood (and bone                marrow)-hematological malignancies, leukemia,                lymphoma, Hodgkin's disease, non-Hodgkin's                lymphoma, multiple myeloma, brain tumor, breast                cancer, cervical cancer, colorectal cancer - in the                colon, rectum, anus, or appendix, esophageal                cancer, endometrial cancer-in the uterus,                hepatocellular carcinoma - in the liver,                gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), laryngeal                cancer, lung cancer, mesothelioma-in the pleura or                pericardium, oral cancer, osteosarcoma-in bones,                ovarian cancer, pancreatic cancer, prostate cancer,                renal cell carcinoma-in the kidneys,                rhabdomyosarcoma - in muscles, skin cancer                (including benign moles and dysplastic nevi),                stomach cancer, testicular cancer, and thyroid                cancer, the cancer disease is selected from                neuroblastoma, leukemia, a cancer in the central                nervous system, retinoblastoma, Wilms' tumor, germ                cell cancer, soft tissue sarcomas, hepatic cancer,                lymphomas, and epithelial cancer, the disease is                related to cellular aging, and the disease related                to cellular aging is selected from Alzheimer's                Disease, Creutzfeld-Jakob Disease, Dementia,                Multiple Systems Atrophy, Neurodegenerative                Diseases, such as Parkinsonism, Retrogenesis,                Sundown Syndrome and Vascular Dementia.
   ADVANTAGE - The invention rapidly determines not only the                kind of enzyme present in a biological sample, but                also the level of activity exhibited by the                enzyme.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Determining in a biological sample either the                presence of enzyme activities involved in                circularizing a non-circular oligonucleotide probe                or the absence of such enzyme activity in the                biological sample comprises: (a) providing a                biological sample to be analyzed for the presence                or absence of enzyme activity; (b) providing an                oligonucleotide probe comprising an unprocessed                substrate moiety capable of being processed by of                the enzymes, where the oligonucleotide probe                comprises a single strand of contiguous nucleotides                or single strands of contiguous nucleotides capable                of hybridization to each other, where the                oligonucleotide probe comprising an unprocessed                substrate moiety cannot be amplified by rolling                circle replication in the absence of the                processing; (c) contacting the biological sample                with the oligonucleotide probe under conditions                allowing the enzymes, if present in the biological                sample, to act on the substrate moiety, where the                action results in the processing of the substrate                moiety and the formation of a circular,                oligonucleotide template capable of being amplified                by rolling circle replication; (d) amplifying the                circular oligonucleotide template, when such a                template is formed in (c), by using a polymerase                capable of performing multiple rounds of rolling                circle replication of the circular oligonucleotide                template, optionally by initially contacting the                circular oligonucleotide template with a suitable                primer, and generating a rolling circle                amplification product comprising multiple copies of                the circular oligonucleotide template; or (e)                generating no rolling circle amplification product                when no circular oligonucleotide template is formed                in (c) as a result of the enzyme activities not                being present in the biological sample, where (d)                and (e) are mutually exclusive, where the                amplification product is indicative of the presence                in the biological sample of the enzyme activities                involved in circularizing a non-circular                oligonucleotide probe, and where no amplification                product is formed in the absence of such enzyme                activity in the biological sample. INDEPENDENT                CLAIMS are:
   a liquid composition;
   a composition comprising a tissue sample, or a                biopsy sample, obtained from an animal, such as a                human being, and the liquid composition;
   a solid support;
   a microfluidic device comprising reaction                compartments for performing rolling circle                amplification events of a circular oligonucleotide                template and detection compartments for the                detection of the rolling circle amplification                events performed in the reaction                compartments;
   a method for correlating rolling circle                amplification event(s) with the activity of enzymes                in a sample;
   a method for diagnosing or prognosing a                disease in an individual by determining the                activity of enzyme activities involved in                circularizing a non-circular oligonucleotide                probe;
   a method for treating a disease                diagnosed.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In determining in a                  biological sample, the oligonucleotide probe                  further comprises non-hybridized, single stranded                  portion(s) and double stranded portion(s), each                  double stranded portion comprising complementary                  nucleotide strands. The single stranded                  portion(s) of the oligonucleotide probe does not                  hybridize to a complementary nucleotide sequence.                  The oligonucleotide probe comprises nucleotide                  sequence which is complementary to of the single                  stranded portion(s) of the oligonucleotide probe.                  The oligonucleotide probe is in the form of a                  single oligonucleotide comprising a contiguous                  sequence of nucleotides, where at least some of                  the nucleotides are capable of forming a double                  stranded sequence comprising complementary                  nucleotide strands. The oligonucleotide probe                  comprises more than one single oligonucleotide,                  where each oligonucleotide of the probe comprises                  a single contiguous sequence of nucleotides,                  where at least some of the nucleotides of the                  different oligonucleotides of the probe are                  capable of hybridizing to each other. The probe                  is a self-templating probe comprising at least                  two double stranded portions each comprising                  complementary nucleotide strands separated at the                  proximal ends by an unprocessed substrate moiety.                  The at least two double stranded portions                  comprising complementary nucleotide strands are                  each joined at the distal ends by a single                  stranded nucleotide forming a loop structure. The                  unprocessed substrate moiety comprises a nick or                  a single stranded nucleotide region. The single                  stranded nucleotide region is adjoined at both                  ends to a double stranded nucleotide region. The                  single stranded nucleotide region is a 5'                  overhang nucleotide region adjoined at one end to                  a double stranded nucleotide region of the                  oligonucleotide probe. The single stranded                  nucleotide region is a 3' overhang nucleotide                  region adjoined at one end to a double stranded                  nucleotide region of the oligonucleotide probe.                  The single stranded nucleotide region preferably                  contains less than 20 nucleotides. The single                  stranded nucleotide region preferably contains                  less than 15 nucleotides. The single stranded                  nucleotide region preferably contains less than                  10 nucleotides. The single stranded nucleotide                  region preferably contains less than 5                  nucleotides. The single stranded nucleotide                  region preferably contains less than 3                  nucleotides. The substrate moiety conversion is                  mediated specifically by a flap endonuclease                  activity present in the sample in combination                  with a ligase activity present in the sample                  and/or added to the sample. The flap endonuclease                  activity is mediated by Flap endonuclease 1                  (FEN1), DNA2P or exonuclease 1 (EXO1). The                  substrate moiety conversion is mediated                  specifically by a topoisomerase activity present                  in the sample. The topoisomerase activity is                  mediated by a Topoisomerase I. The topoisomerase                  activity is mediated by a Topoisomerase II. The                  unprocessed substrate moiety is selected from:                  (a) unprocessed substrate moieties comprising or                  consisting of nick(s) in single strand(s) of a                  double stranded nucleotide sequence of the                  oligonucleotide probe, the nick(s) forming                  unprocessed substrate moieties of the                  oligonucleotide probe; (b) unprocessed substrate                  moieties comprising or consisting of single                  stranded nucleotide sequence(s) joined at one or                  both ends by a double stranded nucleotide                  sequence, the single stranded sequence(s)                  creating gap structure(s) forming unprocessed                  substrate moieties of the oligonucleotide probe;                  and (c) unprocessed substrate moieties comprising                  or consisting of nick(s) or gap(s), the gap(s)                  being in the form of a single stranded nucleotide                  sequence, the nick(s) or gap(s) being joined at                  one end to a double stranded nucleotide sequence                  and at the other end to single stranded overhang                  joined to a double stranded nucleotide sequence                  of the oligonucleotide probe, where the nick(s)                  or gap(s) in combination with the single stranded                  overhang forms unprocessed substrate moieties of                  the oligonucleotide probe. The unprocessed                  substrate moiety comprises or consists of nick(s)                  in single strand(s) of a double stranded                  nucleotide sequence of the oligonucleotide probe,                  the nick(s) forming unprocessed substrate                  moieties of the oligonucleotide probe. The enzyme                  activities present in the sample comprises a                  ligase activity capable of ligating the nick of                  the oligonucleotide probe. The circular                  oligonucleotide template capable of being                  amplified by rolling circle amplification is                  generated by ligating the nick, the ligation                  being performed by ligase activity present in the                  sample. The circular oligonucleotide template is                  amplified by rolling circle amplification, the                  amplification being indicative of the presence in                  the sample of ligase activity. The rolling circle                  amplification product is detected by detecting a                  label covalently or non-covalently associated                  with the rolling circle amplification product,                  where the label is preferably fluorescently                  detectable, where the label is either a                  fluorescent molecule incorporated into the                  rolling circle amplification product, for example                  by being present in the primer used for probe                  amplification and generation of the rolling                  circle amplification product, or by being linked                  to a nucleotide incorporated into the rolling                  circle amplification product during the probe                  amplification process, or by being linked to a                  fluorescently labeled oligonucleotide hybridizing                  to the rolling circle amplification product, or                  where the label is a molecule or a chemical group                  which can be detected by a fluorescently labeled                  molecule, such as an antibody. The unprocessed                  substrate moiety comprises or consists of single                  stranded nucleotide sequence(s) joined at one or                  both ends by a double stranded nucleotide                  sequence, the single stranded sequence(s)                  creating gap structure(s) forming unprocessed                  substrate moieties of the oligonucleotide probe.                  The circular, oligonucleotide template capable of                  being amplified by rolling circle amplification                  is generated through filling-in the gap by using                  the enzyme activity present in the sample which                  is capable of performing a template directed                  nucleotide extension reaction, and ligating one                  or both of the end-positioned, filled-in                  nucleotides to the remaining, double stranded                  part of the oligonucleotide probe. The circular,                  oligonucleotide template is amplified by rolling                  circle amplification, the amplification being                  indicative of the presence in the sample of                  enzyme activity capable of performing template                  directed nucleotide extension and/or nucleotide                  ligation. The rolling circle amplification                  product is detected by detecting a label                  covalently or non-covalently associated with the                  rolling circle amplification product, where the                  label is preferably fluorescently detectable,                  where the label is either a fluorescent molecule                  incorporated into the rolling circle                  amplification product, for example by being                  present in the primer used for probe                  amplification and generation of the rolling                  circle amplification product, or by being linked                  to a nucleotide incorporated into the rolling                  circle amplification product during the probe                  amplification process, or by being linked to a                  fluorescently labeled oligonucleotide hybridizing                  to the rolling circle amplification product, or                  where the label is a molecule or a chemical group                  which can be detected by a fluorescently labeled                  molecule, such as an antibody. The substrate                  moiety comprises or consists of nick(s) and/or                  gap(s), the gap(s) being in the form of a single                  stranded nucleotide sequence, the nick(s) or                  gap(s) being joined at one end to a double                  stranded nucleotide sequence and at the other end                  to single stranded overhang joined to a double                  stranded nucleotide sequence of the                  oligonucleotide probe, where the nick(s) or                  gap(s) in combination with the single stranded                  overhang forms unprocessed substrate moieties of                  the oligonucleotide probe. The overhang(s) is a                  5' overhang, the oligonucleotide probe further                  comprising 3' end. The 5' overhang is protected                  by a protection group preventing an exonuclease                  from digesting the 5' overhang. The circular,                  oligonucleotide template capable of being                  amplified by rolling circle amplification is                  generated by endonucleolytic digestion of the 5'                  overhang and ligation of the end of the                  nucleotide strand resulting from the                  endonucleolytic digestion to a nucleotide strand                  of the remaining part of the oligonucleotide                  probe. The circular, oligonucleotide template is                  amplified by rolling circle amplification, the                  amplification being indicative of the presence in                  the sample of endonuclease. The rolling circle                  amplification product is detected by detecting a                  label covalently or non-covalently associated                  with the rolling circle amplification product,                  where the label is preferably fluorescently                  detectable, where the label is either a                  fluorescent molecule incorporated into the                  rolling circle amplification product, for example                  by being present in the primer used for probe                  amplification and generation of the rolling                  circle amplification product, or by being linked                  to a nucleotide incorporated into the rolling                  circle amplification product during the probe                  amplification process, or by being linked to a                  fluorescently labeled oligonucleotide hybridizing                  to the rolling circle amplification product, or                  where the label is a molecule or a chemical group                  which can be detected by a fluorescently labeled                  molecule, such as an antibody. The 5' end of the                  5' overhang comprises a protection group in the                  form of a phosphate group or different from a                  phosphate group, where the protection group                  prevents ligation of the 5' overhang to a 3' end                  of a strand of the remaining part of the                  oligonucleotide probe. The protection group                  different from a phosphate group is selected from                  H, biotin, amin, and an optionally substituted                  1-6C-linker. The topoisomerase I activity present                  in the sample cannot process the unprocessed                  substrate moiety of the oligonucleotide probe and                  generate a circular oligonucleotide template. The                  flap endonuclease activity present in the sample                  processes the unprocessed substrate moiety of the                  oligonucleotide probe, the processing resulting                  in the formation of a 5' end having a phosphate                  reactive group capable of being ligated with a 3'                  end of a strand of the remaining part of the                  oligonucleotide probe, generating a circular                  oligonucleotide template capable of being                  amplified by rolling circle amplification. The                  circular oligonucleotide template generated by                  the flap endonuclease activity and a ligase                  activity present in the sample is amplified by                  rolling circle amplification, generating a                  rolling circle amplification product. The rolling                  circle amplification product is indicative of the                  presence in the sample of a flap endonuclease                  activity and a ligase activity. The 3' end of the                  oligonucleotide probe comprises a protection                  group different from a hydroxy group, where the                  protection group prevents ligation of the 5'                  overhang to the 3' end of a strand of the                  remaining part of the oligonucleotide probe. The                  topoisomerase I activity present in the sample                  processes the unprocessed substrate moiety of the                  oligonucleotide probe, the processing resulting                  in the formation of a 3'-phospho-tyrosine                  intermediate, in the form of a covalent                  DNA-protein intermediate, capable of being                  ligated with the HO-group of the 5'-end of the                  5'-overhang of the oligonucleotide probe, where                  the ligation results in the formation of a                  circular oligonucleotide template capable of                  being amplified by rolling circle amplification.                  The circular oligonucleotide template generated                  by the topoisomerase I activity present in the                  sample is amplified by rolling circle                  amplification, generating a rolling circle                  amplification product. The rolling circle                  amplification product is indicative of the                  presence in the sample of a topoisomerase I                  activity. The nucleotides of the 5' overhang each                  comprises a nucleobase and a backbone unit, where                  the backbone unit comprises a sugar moiety and an                  internucleoside linker. The                  backbone units of the nucleotides of the 5'                  overhang are the same or different backbone                  units. PN WO9938500-A2; AU9923516-A; US6296833-B1; WO9938500-A3
TI Use of calcium-sensing receptors, for the development of products for the treatment and detection of cancers and other disorders involving abnormal apoptosis.
AU BROWN E M
   SOYBEL D I
AE BRIGHAM & WOMENS HOSPITAL (BGHM-C)
   BRIGHAM & WOMENS HOSPITAL INC (BGHM-C)
GA 1999479115
AB    NOVELTY - A novel method of treating cancer in a human patient comprises administering to the patient a ligand that binds with specificity to calcium-sensing receptor (CaR), where the ligand is administered at a dosage and for a duration so that one or more symptoms associated with the cancer improve.
   USE - The methods can be used for treating cancers such as breast cancer, prostate cancer, multiple myeloma, a brain tumor, a Leydig cell tumor, colon cancer, renal cell carcinoma, cervical cancer, ovarian cancer, vulvar cancer, skin cancer, esophageal cancer, lung cancer or a cancer of the head or neck (claimed). They can improve one or more symptoms such as tumor size, tumor growth, number of metastases, blood calcium levels, levels of parathyroid hormone related peptide (PTH-RP) or bone resorption (claimed). The CaR agonists and antagonists can also be used in the treatment of diseases characterized by abnormal apoptotic activity, including autoimmune diseases and AIDS.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the following:
   (1) a method of detecting neoplastically transformed cells in a human patient, comprising:
   (a) quantitating the number of CaRs present in biopsy tissue suspected of having the neoplastically transformed cells;
   (b) comparing the results obtained from (a) with the results obtained using tissue derived from normal tissue; and
   (c) determining that the biopsy tissue contains transformed cells if the number of the receptors present differs from the number of the receptors in the normal tissue to a statistically significant extent;
   (2) a method of detecting neoplastically transformed cells in a human patient comprising:
   (a) detectably labeling a ligand that binds with specificity to a CaR;
   (b) incubating the detectably labeled ligand with biopsy tissue to determine the number of CaR receptors present;
   (c) comparing the results obtained in (b) with a similar determination performed using normal tissue;
   (d) determining that the biopsy tissue contains transformed cells if the number of the receptors present differs from the number of the receptors in the normal tissue to a statistically significant extent;
   (3) a method of determining whether an abnormal growth in a human patient is cancerous, comprising:
   (a) administering to the patient a compound that binds with specificity to a CaR and that is labeled with an agent that allows the compound to be detected using in vivo imaging techniques;
   (b) determining the extent to which the detectably labeled compound of (a) becomes localized in the abnormal growth;
   (c) determining that the abnormal growth is cancerous if the amount of the detectably labeled compound is present in the abnormal growth at a statistically different level than the amount found in normal or cystic tissue;
   (4) a method of treating a cancer patient by administering a chemotherapeutic agent that acts by inducing apoptosis in cancer cells, the improvement comprising administering a CaR antagonist at a dosage to sensitize the cancer cells to apoptosis;
   (5) a method of treating a cancer patient by administering a chemotherapeutic agent that acts by some means other than inducing apoptosis in cancer cells, the improvement comprising administering a CaR agonist at a dosage to make normal cells more resistant to apoptosis; and
   (6) a method of altering the sensitivity of the cells of a mammal to apoptosis, comprising administering to the mammal a ligand that binds with specificity to the CaR receptor, where the ligand is administered at a dosage and for a duration to cause a statistically significant change in the apoptosis.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Method: The CaR ligand may be a calcium agonist, e.g. protamine or neomycin, or a calcium antagonist, e.g. suramin.
   EXAMPLE - Cancer patients, particularly patients with multiple myeloma or tumors of the breast, prostate, brain, colon, kidney, ovary, cervix, esophagus, skin or lung may be treated by administering a ligand specific for calcium-sensing receptor (CaR). Depending upon the particular cancer being treated, either antagonists or agonists of calcium may be effective. Treatment should begin by administering a low dose of either an agonist such as protamine or neomycin, or an antagonist, such as suramin. A determination should then be made as to whether there is an improvement in one or more of the symptoms associated with the cancer. If no response is seen at the initial dosage, it may be then raised until a maximum is reached, e.g. treatment may begin by initially administering suramin at 1nmol/kg/day and the dosage increased up to a maximum of 1micromol/kg/day. During this time, the symptoms of the patient would be periodically evaluated. If no improvement was observed for e.g. 3 months, the patient may be switched to a calcium agonist and the procedure repeated. Compositions may also include other active ingredients for the treatment of patients. In particular, compositions may contain cancer chemotherapeutic agents such as cisplatin, tamoxifen, paclitaxel, vincristine and vinblastin.

TI Diagnosing cancer or screening for cancer or a            pre-cancerous condition in a subject comprises            calculating ratio value between copy number at first            genomic locus that exhibits copy number gain in cancer            and determining threshold value.
AU FATEEN W A A
   ARMOUR J A
   AITHAL G P
AE UNIV NOTTINGHAM HOSPITALS NHS TRUST (UYNO-Non-standard)
   UNIV NOTTINGHAM (UNGH-C)
GA 2021C5809D
AB    NOVELTY - Diagnosing cancer or screening for cancer or a                pre-cancerous condition in a subject comprises (a)                calculating the ratio value between the copy number                at a first genomic locus that characteristically                exhibits a copy number gain in cancer and a second                genomic locus that characteristically exhibits a                copy number loss in cancer in a DNA sample obtained                from the subject, and determining whether the ratio                value exceeds a predetermined threshold                value.
   USE - The methods are useful for diagnosing cancer                or screening for cancer or a pre-cancerous                condition i.e. diagnosing or screening                adrenocortical carcinoma, bladder urothelial                carcinoma, breast invasive carcinoma, cervical and                endocervical cancers, cervical squamous cell                carcinoma, endocervical adenocarcinoma,                cholangiocarcinoma, colon adenocarcinoma, lymphoid                neoplasm diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, oesophageal                carcinoma, glioblastomamultiforme,           associated a higher than average risk of developing                one or more types of cancer, such as chronic liver                disease, cirrhosis of the liver, autoimmune disease    ADVANTAGE - The method realizes detection of cancer at                early stage.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMSare also included for:
   (1) PCR primer that targets a first locus and                a second locus;
   (2) kit for performing the method comprising a                PCR primer;
   (3) identifying primer;

   (7) screening for cancer relapse, comprising                applying step (a) to a subject who has previously                suffered from cancer.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The method includes                  distinguishing high-grade dysplastic tissue from                  low-grade dysplastic tissue. The pre-cancerous                  condition is the presence of high-grade                  dysplastic tissue. The predetermined threshold                  corresponds to the ratio value that is exceeded                  by less than 1%, less than 2%, less than 3%, less                  than 4%, less than 5%, less than 6%, less than                  7%, less than 8%, less than 9% or less than 10%                  of subjects that do not have cancer or a                  pre-cancerous condition. The predetermined                  threshold corresponds to the ratio value that is                  exceeded by more than 50%, more than 60%, more                  than 70%, more than 80%, more than 90% or more                  than 95% of subjects that do have cancer or a                  pre-cancerous condition. The predetermined                  threshold is about 1.01, 1.02, 1.03, 1.04 or                  1.05. The predetermined threshold is 1.010, 1.011                  , 1.012, 1.013, 1.014, 1.015, 1.016, 1.017,                  1.018, 1.019, 1.020, 1.021,1.022, 1.023, 1.024,                  1.025, 1.026, 1.027, 1.028, 1.029, 1.030, 1.031 ,                  1.032, 1.033, 1.034, 1.035, 1.036, 1.037, 1.038,                  1.039, 1.040, 1.041, 1.042, 1.043, 1.044, 1.045,                  1.046, 1.047, 1.048, 1.049 or 1.050. The method                  further comprises calculating a second ratio                  value between the copy number at another first                  locus that characteristically exhibits a copy                  number gain in cancer and another second locus                  that characteristically exhibits a copy number                  loss in cancer, and determining whether the                  second ratio value exceeds a second predetermined                  threshold value.The both of the first and second                  loci used to calculate the second ratio value are                  different to the first and second loci used to                  calculate the first ratio value. The second                  predetermined threshold value is different to the                  first predetermined ratio value.The method                  further comprises calculating a third, fourth,                  fifth or further ratio values and determining                  whether they exceed a third, fourth, fifth or                  further predetermined threshold value. The                  presence of cancer or a pre-cancerous condition                  is indicated by any one of the ratio values                  exceeding the corresponding predetermined                  threshold. The presence of cancer or a                  pre-cancerous condition is indicated by all of                  the at least two ratio values exceeding the                  corresponding predetermined thresholds.The method                  further comprises an initial step of obtaining a                  DNA sample from the subject.The method comprises                  taking a solid tissue biopsy from a lesion or                  nodule that is suspected of being cancerous or                  pre-cancerous dysplastic tissue from the subject.                  The method comprises obtaining a sample of blood,                  saliva, urine, stool, lymph or cerebrospinal                  fluid from the subject. The sample of DNA is a                  sample of cfDNA or DNA extracted from a lesion or                  nodule that is suspected of being cancerous or                  pre-cancerous dysplastic tissue. The method                  further comprises DNA having been extracted from                  a tissue or fluid sample obtained from the                  subject.The method further comprises extracting                  the DNA from a tissue or fluid sample obtained                  from the subject. The ratio value is calculated                  by determining the copy number at the first locus                  and the second locus and dividing the copy number                  at the first locus by the copy number at the                  second locus. The ratio value is calculated by                  directly determining the relative copy number                  between the first locus and the second locus. The                  first locus has a statistically significant copy                  number gain in over 50%, over 60%, over 70%, over                  80% or over 90% of cancer in general or in each                  of specific forms of cancer that are to be                  diagnosed or screened.
