AB    NOVELTY - A protein comprising a binding region, a Shiga                toxin effector region, and a carboxy-terminal                endoplasmic reticulum retention/retrieval signal                motif is new.
   USE - The protein, composition and kit are useful                for killing a cell and treating a disease,                disorder, or condition selected from cancer, tumor,                immune disorder, and microbial infection. The                composition is used in the manufacture of a                medicament for the treatment or prevention of a                cancer, tumor, immune disorder, or microbial                infection; and in the diagnosis, prognosis, or                characterization of a disease, disorder, or                condition. The cancer is selected from bone cancer,                breast cancer, central/peripheral nervous system                cancer, gastrointestinal cancer, germ cell cancer,                glandular cancer, head-neck cancer, hematological                cancer, kidney-urinary tract cancer, liver cancer,                lung/pleura cancer, prostate cancer, sarcoma, skin                cancer, and uterine cancer. The immune disorder                associated is selected from amyloidosis, ankylosing                spondylitis, asthma, Crohn's disease, diabetes,                graft rejection, graft-versus-host disease,                Hashimoto's thyroiditis, hemolytic uremic syndrome,                HIV-related diseases, lupus erythematosus, multiple                sclerosis, polyarteritis nodosa, polyarthritis,                psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, rheumatoid                arthritis, scleroderma, septic shock, Sjorgren's                syndrome, ulcerative colitis, and vasculitis (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - Provided are cytotoxic proteins comprising                Shiga toxin regions and cell-targeting binding                regions that exhibit effective                intracellular-routing to provide potent                cytotoxicity.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A protein comprises (i) a binding region                comprising capable of specifically binding an                extracellular target biomolecule, (ii) a Shiga                toxin effector region comprising a polypeptide                derived from the amino acid sequence of the A                Subunit of a member of the Shiga toxin family, and                (iii) a carboxy-terminal endoplasmic reticulum                retention/retrieval signal motif of a member of the                Lys-Asp-Glu-Leu (KDEL) family. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS                are:
   a polynucleotide capable of encoding the                protein defined above, or its complement or                fragment;
   an expression vector comprising the                polynucleotide of (1);
   a host cell comprising any one of the                polynucleotides or expression vectors above;
   a system for conferring improved cytotoxicity                to a protein by adding a carboxy-terminal                endoplasmic reticulum retention/retrieval signal                motif of a member of the KDEL family to a carboxy                terminus of the protein or polypeptide component of                the protein, where the protein comprises (i) a                binding region comprising capable of specifically                binding an extracellular target biomolecule, and                (ii) a Shiga toxin effector region comprising a                polypeptide derived from the amino acid sequence of                the A Subunit of a member of the Shiga toxin                family;
   a method of killing a cell by contacting the                cell with the protein or the pharmaceutical                composition above;
   a method of treating a disease, disorder, or                condition in a patient by administering the protein                defined above or the pharmaceutical composition                comprising the protein;
   a method of collecting information regarding                the presence of a cell physically coupled with an                extracellular target of the binding region of the                protein defined above by contacting a cell with the                diagnostic composition comprising the protein                defined above and a detection promoting agent; and                detecting the presence of the diagnostic agent;                and
   a kit comprising the composition of matter                comprising the protein defined above, and an                additional reagent and/or pharmaceutical delivery                device.

TI Non-invasive, multi-biomarker electrochemical            biosensor device for real-time monitoring of metabolic,            endocrine, and oncological biomarkers, comprises            sampling assembly comprising flexible substrate with            hollow opening for direct skin contact, and removable,            single-use nitrocellulose patch/strip.
AU MANI N
AE DEV SANSKRITI VISHWAVIDYALAYA (SANS-Non-standard)
GA 202547486T
AB    NOVELTY - Non-invasive, multi-biomarker electrochemical                biosensor device comprises a sampling assembly                comprising a flexible substrate with a hollow                opening for direct skin contact configured to                collect sweat, saliva, or urine samples by way of                an inlet, where the flexible substrate is made of                polyethylene terephthalate (PET); a removable,                single-use nitrocellulose patch/strip, pre-coated                with biomarker-specific enzymes or antibodies,                where the patch is color-coded to indicate the                target biomarker (e.g., glucose, cortisol,                electrolytes, or cancer markers); and a                microfluidic channel and reagent reservoir assembly                comprising graphene-based microfluidic channels for                directing collected biofluid samples to a detection                zone, a reagent reservoir stores antibodies and                enzymes, which travel through the microchannel to                the graphene-based microfluidic channel allowing                analyte detection after the lateral flow                assay.
   USE - Non-invasive, multi-biomarker electrochemical                biosensor device for real-time monitoring of                metabolic, endocrine, and oncological biomarkers,                and is used in wearable formats, comprising                wristbands, patches, or smart clothing for                continuous health monitoring, and early detection                of conditions comprising diabetes, stress-related                disorders, electrolyte imbalances, and cancer by                simultaneously monitoring multiple biomarkers in                biological fluids, such as sweat, saliva, and urine                (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The system integrates electrochemical sensing,                microfluidics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to                provide continuous health insights for disease                management, fitness optimization, and early                diagnosis. The non-invasive, multi-biomarker                electrochemical biosensor device further comprises                low-power circuit design to enhance battery                longevity and operational stability during                prolonged use. The system enhances productivity,                minimizes manual intervention, and improves                operational accuracy by leveraging real-time data                analytics, predictive modeling, and intelligent                automation, its modular and scalable design ensures                adaptability for applications in healthcare,                finance, manufacturing, smart cities, and more, and                AI-powered security measures protect sensitive                data, while NLP-based human-computer interaction                improves accessibility and user experience. The                system's Internet of Things (IoT) capabilities                enable real-time monitoring and predictive                maintenance in industrial and urban infrastructure,                ethical AI principles ensure unbiased                decision-making and compliance with data privacy                regulations. The system is designed for                flexibility, security, and efficiency, which                represents a significant advancement in digital                transformation, enabling businesses and                organizations to operate more effectively in an                increasingly automated and data-driven world.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Non-invasive, multi-biomarker electrochemical                biosensor device comprises a sampling assembly                comprising a flexible substrate with a hollow                opening for direct skin contact configured to                collect sweat, saliva, or urine samples by way of                an inlet, where the flexible substrate is made of                polyethylene terephthalate (PET); a removable,                single-use nitrocellulose patch/strip, pre-coated                with biomarker-specific enzymes or antibodies,                where the patch is color-coded to indicate the                target biomarker (e.g., glucose, cortisol,                electrolytes, or cancer markers); a microfluidic                channel and reagent reservoir assembly comprising                graphene-based microfluidic channels for directing                collected biofluid samples to a detection zone, a                reagent reservoir stores antibodies and enzymes,                which travel through the microchannel to the                graphene-based microfluidic channel allowing                analyte detection after the lateral flow assay, and                a paper-based separation layer (1.4) to prevent                salt deposition on electrodes by avoiding direct                contact between the electrodes and the sample                salts; an electrochemical sensing unit comprising                silver nanoparticle-based electrodes comprising a                working electrode (1.5B), counter electrode (1.5A),                and reference electrode (1.5C), for electrochemical                detection of biomarkers, where the working                electrode is responsible for signal generation                based on analyte interactions, and reference                electrode ensures stable potential measurements                during analysis, connector leads creates a link                between the electrodes and transducer for data                processing, and a gel-based encapsulation layer                (1.6) within the microfluidic channels to enhance                reaction efficiency and prevent signal degradation                and buildup of salts; wearable housing unit (1.7)                comprising flexible, and biocompatible casing                (e.g., silicon or PET) integrating all components                into a wristband, patch, or smart clothing format;                sweat induction unit comprising iontophoretic                electrodes coated with pilocarpine to stimulate                localized sweat production for consistent sampling;                and data processing and communication unit                comprising low-power microcontroller for real-time                signal processing and wireless transmitter to relay                data to an external device.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for performing real-time, non-invasive monitoring                of metabolic, endocrine, and oncological biomarkers                using the biosensor, which involves: (a) applying                the color-coded nitrocellulose patch to the skin,                where the patch is selected based on the target                biomarker; (b) collecting biological fluid samples                (sweat, saliva, or urine) through the flexible                sampling area of the biosensor; (c) directing the                samples through graphene-based microfluidic                channels to the reagent reservoir for analyte                binding via lateral flow assay; (d) detecting                biomarker concentrations electrochemically using                silver nanoparticle electrodes; (e) transmitting                the detected data to the data processing and                communication unit for real-time analysis and user                feedback; and (f) replacing the nitrocellulose                patch after each use to prevent salt deposition and                ensure accuracy.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of the                non-invasive, multi-biomarker electrochemical                biosensor device for real-time monitoring of                metabolic, endocrine, and oncological                biomarkers.
   1.4Paper-based separation layer
   1.5ACounter electrode
   1.5BWorking electrode
   1.5CReference electrode
   1.6Gel-based encapsulation layer
   1.7Wearable housing unit
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The device further                  comprises silicon casing for housing the                  biosensor components, where the casing comprises                  an inlet for inserting the removable                  nitrocellulose patch and ensures flexibility for                  comfortable wear. Preferred Conditions: The data                  processing and communication unit provides                  real-time alerts for abnormal biomarker levels,                  historical trend analysis for disease management,                  personalized health recommendations based on                  Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analytics,                  and secure data sharing with healthcare                  providers. Preferred Process: The removable                  single-use nitrocellulose patch is pre-coated                  with glucose oxidase for glucose detection,                  cortisol-specific antibodies for stress                  monitoring, sodium and potassium ion-selective                  membranes for electrolyte imbalance detection, or                  cancer-specific antibodies (e.g., human epidermal                  growth factor receptor 2, HER2) for oncological                  biomarker detection.

AB       The following are claimed: (1) a compsn. comprising purified papillomavirus (PV) proteins E1 and E2, about 68 and 48 KD, resp., and opt. a nucleotide sequence that binds either E1 or E2; (2) a complex of PV proteins comprising pure E1 and E2, about 68 and 48 KD, resp., and opt. a nucleotide sequence that binds either E1 or E2; (3) medicaments for treating PV diseases charactersied by preventing or interfering with E1/E2 complex formation; (4) indentifying medicaments for treating PV disease by: (a) mixing E1 and E2 in soln. to form a complex (b) measuring E1 and E2 complex formation., and (c) repeating (a) and (b) in the presence of the medicaments; (5) identifying medicaments for treating PV disease by: (a) mixing E1, E2 or both with PV DNA under conditions that caus ethe proteins to bind to the DNA and (c) repeating (a) and (b) in the presence of the medicaments; and (6) treating an animal suffering from a PV disease by administering the medicaments of (3), (4) or (5).
   USE -   The medicaments can be used to treat PV diseases, partic. warts and cancers. The identification method involves the detection at early phase of PV proteins E1 and E2, which form an E1/E2 complex involved in the initiation of viral DNA replication. The medicaments are identified by their ability to interfere with the formation of this complex and hence inhibit viral replication. Dosage of the medicaments is 0.1-10 peptide/kg body wt..

GA 2007476966
AB    NOVELTY - Use of a substance (I) modulating the                expression and/or the activity of LOX having a                sequence (SEQ ID No. 1: Not defined) and/or                modulating the expression and/or the activity of                NRAGE having a sequence (SEQ ID No. 2: Not defined)                for making a composition to modulate the                interaction between LOX and NRAGE proteins and to                regulate the equilibrium between the phenomena of                cell proliferation, differentiation and apoptosis,                in particular in the cases where the interaction                between LOX and NRAGE is absent or altered.
   USE - (I) is useful for making a composition to                improve the interaction between proteins LOX and                NRAGE, whenever the interaction between LOX and                NRAGE is absent or altered and to prevent or treat                a state in which cellular equilibrium between the                proliferation, differentiation and the apoptosis is                absent or altered. (I) is useful to treat and/or                prevent a condition caused by an exposure of cells                to a stress, in particular to heat, or radiation,                preferably solar radiation, or exposure of cells to                a toxic agent e.g. chemical or microbiological,                such as skin aging, lichen planus, graft versus                host reaction (GVH - Graft Versus Host), eczema,                psoriasis and cancer, particularly an epithelial                cancer. (I) is useful to reduce cellular                proliferation, hyperproliferation, particularly in                basocellular type or spinocellular type cutaneous                epithelial cancer, psoriasis or eczema. (I) is                useful to stimulate the expression of LOX and                optionally to inhibit the expression of NRAGE at                skin level. The composition is useful as cosmetic,                neutraceutic, dermo-pharmaceutical or                pharmaceutical composition. The anti-NRAGE antibody                is useful for the preparation of a composition for                the detection of an expression modulation of NRAGE                at the cellular level, preferably at                keratinocytes.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) modulates the interaction between the LOX                protein and NRAGE protein, where the interaction                occurs on the level of Interpersed Repeat Domain                (IRD) of NRAGE protein (claimed).
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   an identification of an active ingredient that                modulates the interaction between LOX and NRAGE, to                improve the interaction between LOX and NRAGE when                the interaction is absent or altered and to prevent                or treat a state in which cellular equilibrium                between proliferation, differentiation and                apoptosis, is absent or altered, comprising contact                of the active ingredient with living cells that are                able to express the protein LOX having a sequence                comprising (SEQ ID No. 1: Not defined) and/or                protein NRAGE having a sequence comprising (SEQ ID                No. 2: Not defined) and expression analysis of LOX                and/or NRAGE, to identify an active ingredient                modulating the expression and/or the activity of                LOX and/or NRAGE to improve cellular equilibrium                between proliferation, differentiation and                apoptosis;
   preparation of a composition comprising                identification of the active ingredient using the                identification method and mixing the active                ingredient with an excipient to form a cosmetic,                neutraceutic, dermopharmaceutic or pharmaceutical                composition to prevent or treat a state in which                cellular equilibrium between proliferation,                differentiation and apoptosis is absent or altered;                and
   localization method of NRAGE, comprising use                of anti-NRAGE antibody to detect and locate the                presence of NRAGE, in a rebuilt skin model                comprising the keratinocytes, or a skin section,                preferably a skin section from a person whose                epidermis presents a state in which cellular                equilibrium between the proliferation,                differentiation and apoptosis, is absent or                altered.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: (I) is soya extract,                  ephedra ( Ephedra sinica) extract, hop ( Humulus                  lupulus) extract, cinnamon ( Cinnamomum spp.)                  extract, white saponin ( Gypsophila spp.), red                  sandal ( Pterocarpus santalinus) extract, Bryonia                  dioicaextract, Butcher's-broom ( Ruscus                  aculeatus) extract, lemon ( Citrus limonia)                  extract, tangerine ( Citrus reticulata) extract,                  trans ethyl 3-hexenoate, khella ( Amni Visnaga)                  extract, alginic acid, carrot ( Daucus carota)                  extract, methyl-2-methyl butyrate, staranise tree                  ( Illicium verum), bypress ( Cupressus                  sempervirens) extract, asafetida gum, xylitol,                  sloe ( Prunus spinosa) extract, strawberry (                  Arbutus unedo) extract, wintergreen ( Chimaphila                  umbellata) extract, odorous asperula( Asperula                  odorata) extract, southernwood ( Artemisia                  vulgaris) extract, elder tree ( Sambucus nigra)                  extract, Chinese cabbage ( Brassica                  campestrisvar. Pekinensis) extract , Quassia of                  Surinam ( Quassia amara) extract, cocoa (                  Theobroma cacao) extract, silk ( Serica) extract,                  red sarsaparilla ( Smilax ornata) extract,                  currant ( Ribes rubrum) extract, Pyrethrum (                  Anacyclus pyrethrum) or fennel ( Foeniculum)                  extract.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Components: The expression and/or                  the activity of LOX and NRAGE are modulated in                  epithelial cells, in particular in keratinocytes.                  The living cells are epithelial cells,                  particularly keratinocytes.Preferred Properties: The interaction                  between LOX and NRAGE comprises polymerization,                  particularly dimerization of NRAGE, by enzymatic                  catalysis operated by LOX. The interaction                  between LOX and NRAGE interferes the production                  of hydrogen peroxide, resulting from the                  catalytic activity of LOX, thus activates other                  molecules, in particular neutral sphingomyelinase                  or NF-KB. The interaction between LOX and NRAGE                  utilizes a nonenzymatic activity of LOX, in                  particular an activity carried out by the LOX                  proregion.Preferred Method: The equilibrium between                  the proliferation, differentiation and apoptosis,                  of the living cells able to express protein LOX                  and/or NRAGE, or the interaction between the                  proteins LOX and NRAGE, is absent or altered                  before contacting with the active ingredient. The                  method comprises expression analysis of the                  messenger RNA of LOX and/or NRAGE. The method is                  carried out using a quantitative reverse                  transcription polymerase chain reaction, where                  LOX gene comprises ACGTACGTGCAGAAGATGTCC as sens                  strand and GGCTGGGTAAGAAATCTGATG as antisens                  strand while NRAGE gene comprises                  TGCACAGACATCAGCAGATGG as sense strand and                  TTCACGGATGATATCTCTCAGC as antisense strand.
   ACTIVITY - Tranquilizer; Dermatological;                Antiinflammatory; Antipruritic; Immunosuppressive;                Antipsoriatic; Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - LOX gene expression modulator; NRAGE gene                expression modulator. The ability of (I) to express                messenger RNA of LOX by keratinocytes was tested.                The results showed that (I) significantly expressed                the messenger RNA coding LOX.

PN WO2024232668-A1; KR2024163543-A
TI New anti-prostaglandin f2 receptor negative            regulator monoclonal antibody comprising heavy chain            variable region and light chain variable region, used            for treating or preventing cancer e.g. lung cancer,            thymoma, mesothelioma, liver cancer, lymphoma, acute            leukemia, sarcoma, and glioblastoma.

AE UNIV SEJONG IND ACAD COOP FOUND (UNSE-C)
GA 2024C0742V
AB    NOVELTY - An anti-prostaglandin f2 receptor negative                regulator (anti-PTGFRN) monoclonal antibody, is                new. The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody comprises                a heavy chain variable region comprising a heavy                chain complementarity determining region 1 (HCDR1)                comprising an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 3,                an HCDR2 comprising an amino acid sequence of SEQ                ID NO: 4, and an HCDR3 comprising an amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 5; and a light chain                variable region comprising a light chain                complementarity determining region 1 (LCDR1)                comprising an amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 6,                an LCDR2 comprising an amino acid sequence of SEQ                ID NO: 7, and an LCDR3 comprising an amino acid                sequence of SEQ ID NO: 8, is new, where sequences                not defined here may be found at                ftp://ftp.wipo.int/pub/publishedpctsequences/publication.
   USE - The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody is used in                a composition for treating or preventing cancer,                determining the blood level of cancer cells,                detecting PTGFRN, providing information for                diagnosing cancer, providing information necessary                for determining the level of blood cancer cells,                providing information necessary for predicting the                prognosis of cancer metastasis, and screening the                efficacy of the anticancer drug. The cancer is                selected from brain and spinal tumors, head and                neck cancer, lung cancer, breast cancer, thymoma,                mesothelioma, esophageal cancer, stomach cancer,                colon cancer, liver cancer, thyroid cancer,                pancreatic cancer, biliary tract cancer, kidney                cancer, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, testicular                cancer, germ cell tumor, ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, endometrial cancer, lymphoma, acute                leukemia, chronic leukemia, multiple myeloma,                sarcoma, malignant melanoma, neuroblastoma,                glioblastoma, and skin cancer (all claimed). Test                details are described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody stimulates                PTGFRN to increase the mobility and invasiveness of                cancer cells. The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody                prevents and inhibits the cancer growth of primary                cancer by promoting the migration of primary cancer                cells. The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody can                detect blood cancer cells that are neither                epithelial nor mesenchymal. The anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody can partially detect                circulating cancer cells that have undergone                epithelial-mesenchymal transition. The anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody can detect blood cancer cells                with high efficiency in liver cancer patients. The                blood cancer cells detected by the anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody are measured at a higher level                in patients with secondary metastatic cancer than                in patients with primary cancer, so that the stage                of cancer can be determined through the anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody of the present invention. The                anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody binds to                epithelial-mesenchymal transition circulating                cancer cells and partially epithelial-mesenchymal                circulating cancer cells that express PTGFRN on                their surface, while enabling the detection of                previously undetectable circulating cancer cells.                The anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody can be                internalized into cancer cells, while effectively                delivering the drug into cancer cells.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   an antibody-drug conjugate comprising a drug                conjugated to the anti-PTGFRN monoclonal                antibody;
   a hybridoma producing the anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody;
   a composition for detecting PTGFRN comprising                the anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody;
   a method (A) for providing information for                diagnosing cancer, comprising treating a sample                isolated from a subject with the anti-PTGFRN                monoclonal antibody;
   a method (B) for providing information                necessary for determining the level of blood cancer                cells, comprising treating a sample isolated from a                subject with the anti-PTGFRN monoclonal                antibody;
   a method (C) for providing information                necessary for predicting the prognosis of cancer                metastasis, comprising detecting PTGFRN by treating                a sample isolated from an individual with the                anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody;
   a method (D) for screening the efficacy of an                anticancer drug, comprising detecting PTGFRN by                treating a sample isolated from a patient                administered an anticancer drug with the                anti-PTGFRN monoclonal antibody; and
   a composition for detecting blood cancer                cells, comprising a substance that binds to                PTGFRN.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Sample: The sample is selected                  from blood, plasma, bone marrow, lymph, saliva,                  tear fluid, urine, mucosal fluid, and amniotic                  fluid.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Method: The method (B) further                  comprises treating the sample with a substance                  that specifically binds to EpCAM. The method (D)                  comprises providing information that if the level                  of the detected PTGFRN is higher than that of the                  control group, the cancer metastasis prognosis is                  worse than that of the control group. The method                  (D) comprises predicting that if the level of the                  detected PTGFRN is lower than that of the control                  group, the cancer metastasis inhibition efficacy                  of the anticancer drug is better than that of the                  control group. Preferred Components: The heavy                  chain variable region comprises an amino acid                  sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1. The light chain                  variable region comprises an amino acid sequence                  of SEQ ID NO: 2. The substance that specifically                  binds to epithelial cell adhesion molecule                  (EpCAM) is an anti-EpCAM antibody or its                  antigen-binding fragment. The blood cancer cells                  are blood cancer cells that have undergone                  epithelial-mesenchymal transition or are                  undergoing epithelial-mesenchymal transition. The                  blood cancer cell is not an epithelial cell or a                  mesenchymal cell. The blood cancer cell is a                  blood cancer cell in the blood of a patient with                  liver cancer, lung cancer, colon cancer, thyroid                  cancer, pancreatic cancer, malignant melanoma,                  breast cancer, neuroblastoma, or glioblastoma.                  The blood cancer cell further expresses B7-H3                  (cluster of differentiation 276 (CD276))                  protein.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - The example section describes the biological                data that does not support the claims.

A leakage                object on an ostomy bottom plate is observed                through the transparent detecting sheet. Leakage                condition of the ostomy bottom plate is determined                according to the number of a sector area with mark.                Judgment is made to check whether the stoma chassis                needs to be replaced if the number of the sector                area marked in a radius direction of a detection                piece is greater than half of the number of the                sector area in the radius direction.
   USE - Method for detecting leakage of stoma chassis                for treating intestinal diseases such as rectal                cancer on abdominal wall.

GA 2011K15087
AB    NOVELTY - Stabilizing system comprises a stabilizing agent that completely or substantially prevents degradation or inactivation of a diagnostic marker for insulin resistance or glucose intolerance in a body fluid comprising the diagnostic marker; and a detection agent capable of detecting the diagnostic marker.
   USE - The stabilizing system is useful for stabilizing a diagnostic marker in a body fluid, where the diagnostic marker is a protein, a glycoprotein, a nucleic acid, an enzyme, an enzyme inhibitor or a metabolite; and the body fluid is saliva, a mucous secretion, tears, sweat, semen, urine, a vaginal secretion, exhalate, blood, serum or an anal secretion (all claimed). The stabilizing system is useful for detecting insulin resistance or glucose intolerance biomarkers. The stabilizing system is useful to diagnose a disease state or condition e.g. acidosis, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, acute myocardial infarct, Addison's disease, adrenal insufficiency, alcoholism, allergies, Alzheimer's disease, anemia, angina pectoris, anthrax, arthritis, asthma, autoimmune disorders, autoimmune thyroiditis, bone marrow disorders, breast cancer, cardiovascular disease, celiac disease, diabetes, diarrhea, stroke, swine flu, syphilis, systemic lupus erythematosus, testicular cancer, thalassemia, thyroid diseases, trichomonas, tuberculosis, liver disease, urinary tract infection, venereal diseases, walking pneumonia, Wilson's disease, wound and skin infections.
   ADVANTAGE - The system enhances the sensitivity for detection of specific diagnostic markers for clinical diagnosis. The method improves the signal-to-noise ratio for a better diagnostic yield and reduces or prevents false positive and false negative results. The stabilizing system improves the sampling and testing of a body fluid by conditioning the body fluids for the stabilization of specific biomolecules and/or drug metabolites.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for stabilizing a diagnostic marker, comprising mixing a body fluid comprising a diagnostic marker for insulin resistance or glucose intolerance with the stabilizing agent.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows a diagrammatic view of a detection system.
   Detection platform (100)
   Platform (102)
   Test wells (104)
   Test spot (106)
   Identifier. (108)
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Method: The step of mixing a body fluid with a stabilizing agent comprises introducing the stabilizing agent into a mouth/oral cavity of a patient so that the stabilizing agent mixes with saliva. AU AYYAPPADASAN G

AE AYYAPPADASAN G (AYYA-Individual)

GA 2013R20226
AB    NOVELTY - Too much exposure to the sun light or                artificial sun light (i.e. tanning beds) may lead                to skin cancer and desquamation. UV radiation in                the human body enhances the mutations in the DNA                and terminates the cell division. Search of new                compound which can able to protect the skin from UV                rays is the current scenario in ecological                interference. Natural bioresources are one of the                main sources of UV absorbing compounds which can                able to absorb and resist the UV rays from the                environment. The present invention describes the                preliminary idea to detect and enhance the UV                absorbing compounds from lichen thalli. Microwave                irradiation of lichen powder with corresponding                solvent using magnetron of 2450 MHz with nominal                maximum power of 700 W for 5 minutes. Microwaves                are shorter wavelength and more penetration ability                which intends the direct interaction of active                components present in the thalli. Then the sample                was centrifuged at 5000rpm for lOminutes.                Supernatant was taken and concentrated using a                vacuum desiccator of 100mm in Hg pressure about                3hrs. Then the spot has been developed using Hexane                : Ethanol: Acetic acid : Formic acid (120:50:5:1)                system. Present methodology improves the detection                of a TLC plate by using natural lemon as spraying                reagent. Lemon juice was extracted and filtered                subsequently. It was sprayed with thin layer                chromatography plate. The plate was air dried and                observed under the UV chamber. The results revealed                that UV absorbing components from lichens were                clearly visible on a purple spot in the TLC plate                but the conventional detection methodology was not                much clear in visualizing the spot. Present                invention helps to understand the extraction as                well as detection of UV absorbing compounds in an                effective and easiest way. Moreover, microwave                assisted extraction method also helps to increase                the phenolic content about 10-15% rather than the                conventional methods.

   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a cassette for performing analysis by spectral                reflectance imaging system, which comprises                substrate disposed on binding agent e.g. an                antibody molecule specific for an antigen found on                surface of a cancer cell, e.g. glypican;
   a method for detecting binding of a                circulating extracellular vesicle e.g., exosomes to                a surface of substrate, which involves providing                first specular reflecting interface of substrate                with one or more binding agents specific for                glypican to first specular reflecting interface of                substrate; providing second specular reflecting                interface that is substantially parallel to and                underlies first specular reflecting interface;                illuminating surface with light substantially                centered around one or more wavelengths; imaging                light reflected or transmitted from substrate by                using an imaging device; producing an image of                surface of substrate; and correlating features on                image to discrete circulating extracellular vesicle                biomarkers such as glypican on surface; and
   a method for detecting particle on surface of                layered substrate, which involves providing surface                of layered substrate with a binding agent specific                for glypican; contacting a solution having                circulating extracellular vesicle having an exosome                biomarker such as glypican with surface of                substrate; illuminating surface with wavelength of                light; imaging light reflected or transmitted from                substrate by using an imaging device; and producing                an image of surface of substrate to detect                extracellular circulating vesicle (e.g., exosome)                on surface of the layered substrate.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The one or more                  glypicans comprises member selected from a group                  consist of glypican-1, glypican-2, glypican-3,                  glypican-4 glypican-5, and glypican-6, preferably                  glypican-1, mroe preferably glypican-3. The one                  or more binding agents comprise a member selected                  from a group consist of antibody molecule,                  nucleic acid, polypeptide, and aptamer. The                  antibody molecule comprises member selected from                  a group consist of monoclonal antibody,                  polyclonal antibody, and its antigen binding                  fragment, where one or more binding agents                  comprise rodent, rabbit, mouse, or rat,                  anti-human antibody or its binding fragment. The                  body fluid comprises plasma, serum, whole blood,                  saliva, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), or urine. The                  spectral reflectance imaging system comprises                  substrate having first reflective surface and                  partially transparent layer providing a second                  reflective surface, biolayer bounded to first set                  of one or more binding agent to second reflective                  surface, illumination source, e.g., an                  illuminating source having a light source that                  provides light in narrow frequency band and                  directing frequency band of light at substrate,                  where one of narrow frequency band comprises a                  range of wavelength from 300-800nm, 400-600nm,                  405-455nm, and 420nm, and an imaging device                  directed at second reflective surface of                  substrate and adapted to produce imaging signals                  representative of light from illumination source                  being reflected by first reflective surface,                  second reflective surface, and scattered light by                  particle on second surface. The spectral                  reflectance imaging system comprises image                  acquisition and processing system coupled to                  imaging device and adapted to receive imaging                  signal and under program control and produces an                  image of biolayer/and or particle on second                  reflective surface. The imaging device comprises                  camera having high magnification objective lens                  with a high numerical aperture. The layered                  substrate comprises 30-100nm, preferably silicon                  oxide layered on silicon wafer. The camera                  comprises a spatial filter on camera's optical                  axis. The light is incoherent. The imaging device                  comprises member selected from a group consist of                  monochromatic charge coupled device (CCD) camera,                  complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)                  sensor, and color camera. The particle is                  detected by detecting binding of particle on                  surface of layered substrate. The surface of                  layered surfaces comprises a binding agent for                  binding predefined particle and solution                  comprises a predefined particle. The substrate                  comprises circulating extracellular vesicle e.g.,                  exosome bounded to binding agent. Preferred                  Conditions: The circulating extracellular vesicle                  is isolated by contacting sample obtained from a                  subject with first set of one or more binding                  agent specific for glypican, contacting sample                  with a second set of one or more binding agent                  before binding of circulating extracellular                  vesicle present in sample to surface of substrate                  and post binding of circulating extracellular                  vesicle present in sample to surface of                  substrate, and detecting the extracellular                  vesicle bounded to surface of substrate. The                  method further involves evaluating level e.g.,                  quantity, number, and concentration of                  circulating extracellular vesicle in sample. The                  method involves evaluating a number of                  circulating extracellular vesicle bounded to                  substrate or predetermined portion or area of                  substrate present in sample, or present in                  subject from which sample is obtained. The method                  involves providing a value for parameter e.g. an                  abundance-parameter related to number of                  circulating extracellular vesicle bounded to                  substrate or predetermined portion or area of                  substrate present in the sample or present in                  subject from which sample is obtained. The method                  involves determining size of circulating                  extracellular vesicle bounded to substrate e.g.,                  diameter, volume or a predetermined portion or                  area of substrate present in the sample or                  present in subject from which sample is obtained,                  where diameter is 10-3100nm, e.g., 50-2000nm,                  50-1000nm, 20-300nm, 30-100nm, 50-200nm, and                  200-3000nm. The size is average size of                  extracellular vesicle bounded to substrate or a                  predetermined portion or area of the substrate.                  The method involves providing a value for a                  parameter e.g. size parameter related to diameter                  of an extracellular vesicle bound to substrate or                  a predetermined portion or area of substrate,                  present in sample, or present in subject from                  which sample is obtained. The method involves                  comparing a value for an abundance parameter,                  size parameter (e.g. diameter parameter, volume                  parameter) or a parameter related to both size                  and abundance with a reference value by                  evaluating sample, by characterizing sample and                  by diagnosing the subject, and if value for one                  or more of abundance parameter, size parameter,                  or parameter related to both size and abundance                  meets a predetermined relationship with reference                  value, and sample or subject is classified, and                  if a value for one or more of abundance                  parameter, size parameter, or parameter related                  to both size and abundance is more than a                  reference value then subject is classified as                  sample or subject, e.g., subject is classified as                  at risk for or having cancer. The reference value                  is a value determined for subject not having a                  preselected disorder, e.g., cancer. The reference                  value is function of one or more of abundance                  parameter, diameter parameter, or parameter                  related to both diameter and abundance from a                  subject not having preselected disorder, e.g.,                  cancer. The value for one or more of abundance                  parameter, diameter parameter, or parameter                  related to both diameter and abundance is more                  than a reference value, and subject is classified                  as at risk for or having pancreatic cancer, e.g.,                  pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and if value for one                  or more of an abundance parameter, diameter                  parameter, or parameter related to both diameter                  and abundance is more than a reference value then                  sample or subject is classified as at risk for or                  having cancer. The sample is classified as                  indicative of one of or combination absence of                  preselected cancer such as pancreatic cancer,                  e.g., pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and breast                  cancer, lung cancer, colon cancer, glioblastoma                  and ovarian cancer, or presence of preselected                  cancer, or presences of a non-cancerous disorder                  of a preselected tissue e.g., pancreas, lung,                  colon, breast, brain, ovary, or presence of a                  preselected pre-cancerous lesion of preselected                  tissue. The subject is classified as at an                  elevated chance of one of or combination of not                  having preselected cancer, having non-cancerous                  disorder of preselected tissue, or having                  preselected pre-cancerous lesion of preselected                  tissue. The method involves monitoring or                  evaluating progress or state of the preselected                  cancer. The value for one or more of an abundance                  parameter, size parameter, or parameter related                  to both size and abundance is correlated with                  progress or state of preselected cancer. The                  method involves providing evaluation,                  classification, or diagnosing, selecting and                  treatment option for subject. The antibody                  molecule specifically binds an antigen found on                  surface of cancer cell e.g., a glypican, where                  antibody molecule specifically binds an                  extracellular portion of glypican. The first                  binding agent that is bound to surface of the                  substrate (e.g., a first binding agent that binds                  an extracellular portion of glypican-1, e.g.,                  binding agent that binds an extracellular portion                  of glypican-3 to surface of substrate) is                  different from a second binding agent that to a                  protein on a surface of the circulating                  extracellular vesicles e.g., that binds an                  extracellular portion of glypican-3, e.g., binds                  an extracellular portion of glypican-1, where                  protein comprises a member selected from a group                  consist of CD63, cluster of differentiation (CD)                  CD81, CD9, flotillin-1, mannose binding lectin,                  and lectin, and second binding agent is cancer or                  disease specific, and second binding agent binds                  the circulating extracellular vesicle prior to                  binding to surface of substrate, and second                  binding agent is attached to a label e.g.                  nanoparticle and fluorophore. The circulating                  extracellular vesicle is from a pancreatic cancer                  cell and breast cancer cell. The sample is                  evaluated with reflectance imaging system, e.g.,                  imaging system. The first reflective surface is a                  silicon substrate and transparent layer is                  silicon oxide. The transparent layer has                  thickness of 10-100nm, 40-70nm, preferably 60nm.                  The method involves providing first specular                  reflecting interface of substrate with a binding                  agent for binding circulating extracellular                  vesicle e.g., exosome having glypican to first                  specular reflecting interface of substrate,                  providing second specular reflecting interface                  that is substantially parallel to and underlies                  first specular reflecting interface, illuminating                  surface with light substantially centered around                  one or more wavelengths of light, imaging light                  reflected or transmitted from substrate by using                  an imaging device, producing a spectral                  reflectance image of the surface of the                  substrate, and correlating features (e.g.,                  diameter of circulating extracellular vesicle) on                  image to discrete circulating extracellular                  vesicles on surface by evaluating size of                  discrete circulating extracellular vesicle. The                  transparent layer has thickness of 60nm, and                  narrow frequency band of 420nm, where imaging                  occurs and substrate is immersed in aqueous                  solution, and imaging occurs after drying                  substrate. The wavelength of light is produced by                  separate, narrow band light source, or by a                  broadband light source. The imaging device is a                  monochromatic CCD or CMOS camera. The surface is                  illuminated by a light source from standard                  bright-field microscope optical set up, and                  reflected light is transmitted to an eyepiece.                  The wavelength of light is produced by a separate                  light emitting diode (LED) having a different                  emission peak wavelength. The surface is                  illuminated with white light and imaging device                  includes a color camera. The surface is                  illuminated by red green blue LED and broadband                  light source. The semi-transparent layer is                  silicon oxide. The illumination source produces                  white light and system includes color wheel                  having filter producing a beam of light in three                  narrow frequency bands that is directed at                  substrate. The color camera is a 3-dimensional                  CCD camera. The method involves sequentially                  illuminating substrate with light at increasing                  wavelengths for subsequent illumination, where                  subsequent illuminated wavelength of multiple                  wavelength has longer wavelength than previously                  illuminated wavelength, e.g. where multiple                  wavelength is in range of 500-750nm, 525-700 nm,                  first wavelength of multiple wavelength is 420nm                  and second wavelength of multiple wavelength is                  535nm.

AB    NOVELTY - Composition comprises: (a) a peptide derived                from loop 3 of the C2B domain of synaptotagmin I                comprising SEQ ID NO:1 (a 12 amino acid sequence                fully defined in the specification) or amino acid                sequence                (Gly-Gly-X-Asp-Tyr-Asp-Lys-Ile-Gly-Lys-Asn-Asp-Ala-Asn-X)                SEQ ID NO:13 (I); (b) a peptide derived a                myristoylated alanine-rich C kinase substrate                (MARCKS) effector domain; (c) a trimeric peptide                comprising peptides derived from bradykinin; and/or                (d) a media.
   USE - The composition is useful for detecting,                diagnosing and/or treating the presence of                metastatic cancer cells in a subject having cancer                including liver, pancreas, cervical, kidney, lung,                stomach, colon, breast, prostate, bone, skin or                brain cancer (all claimed). No biological data                given.
   ADVANTAGE - The composition provides robust treatment of                cancer by allowing sensitive and accurate detection                or diagnosis of the metastatic cancer cells in the                subject.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Composition comprises: (a) a peptide derived                from loop 3 of the C2B domain of Synaptotagmin I                comprising SEQ. ID NO:1 (a 12 amino acid sequence                fully defined in the specification) or amino acid                sequence of formula                (Gly-Gly-X-Asp-Tyr-Asp-Lys-Ile-Gly-Lys-Asn-Asp-Ala-Asn-X)                SEQ ID NO:13 (I); (b) a peptide derived a                myristoylated alanine-rich C kinase substrate                (MARCKS) effector domain; (c) a trimeric peptide                comprising peptides derived from bradykinin; and/or                (d) a media.
   X=glycine or leucine residue (both modified                residues in a single peptide capable of creating a                cyclic peptide).
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for:
   a method-I for detecting the presence of                metastatic cancer cells in a subject having cancer,                comprising (a1) obtaining a biological sample from                the subject, (b1) administering the composition to                obtaining the biological sample to the subject, or                administering the composition to the obtained                biological sample without administering the                composition to the subject, (c1) assaying the                subject sample for the presence or amount of lipid                vesicles comprising the administered compound in                the sample versus a control and (d1) detecting the                presence or level of lipid vesicles in the subject,                where the presence or amount of the lipid vesicles                in the subject sample is increased versus control                and diagnosing the presence or level of metastatic                cancer cells in the subject;
   a method-II for determining location of a                cancer cell in a subject, comprising (a2)                administering the composition to the subject, (b2)                detecting the location of the administered                composition in the subject and (c2) identifying the                location of the cancer cell in the subject                according to the location of the composition;                and
   a kit for identifying metastatic cell in the                subject comprising the composition and a suitable                container.

AB    NOVELTY - Method (A) of treating colorectal cancer in a                subject, involves (S1) obtaining a sample from the                subject, (S2) detecting the presence or absence of                gut microbiota, where the gut microbiota comprises                positively correlated bacteria that produce                phenylacetaldehyde (PAA) and negatively correlated                bacteria that do not produce PAA, and (S3)                administering PAA to the subject who is predicted                to have colorectal cancer.
   USE - The method is used for treating colorectal                cancer in a subject, detecting colorectal cancer in                a subject, determining a gut microbiota signature                for cancer detection, and/or predicting a treatment                response to cancer immunotherapy (all claimed). The                cancer includes lymphomas such as B cell lymphoma                and T cell lymphoma; mycosis fungoides; Hodgkin's                Disease; myeloid leukemia (acute myeloid leukemia                (AML) and/or chronic myeloid leukemia (CML));                bladder cancer; brain cancer; nervous system                cancer; head and neck cancer; squamous cell                carcinoma of head and neck; renal cancer; lung                cancers such as small cell lung cancer, non-small                cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), lung squamous cell                carcinoma (LUSC), and lung adenocarcinomas (LUAD);                neuroblastoma/ glioblastoma; ovarian cancer;                pancreatic cancer; prostate cancer; skin cancer;                hepatic cancer; melanoma; squamous cell carcinomas                of the mouth, throat, larynx, and lung; cervical                cancer; cervical carcinoma; breast cancer                including, but not limited to triple negative                breast cancer; genitourinary cancer; pulmonary                cancer; esophageal carcinoma; head and neck                carcinoma; large bowel cancer; hematopoietic                cancers; testicular cancer; and colon and rectal                cancers. Test details are described but no results                given.
   ADVANTAGE - None given.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method (A) of treating colorectal cancer in a                subject, involves either (S1) obtaining a sample                from the subject, (S2) detecting the presence or                absence of gut microbiota, where the gut microbiota                comprises positively correlated bacteria that                produce phenylacetaldehyde (PAA) and negatively                correlated bacteria that do not produce PAA, where                the positively correlated bacteria comprise                Clostridium txid1638787, C.txid1697791, Firmicute                txid1263021, Coprobascillus txid100884,                C.txid127889, C.txid1182556, Streptococcus                txid99822, Acidaminococcus txid1203555, Roseburia                txid1262944, or Butyrivibrio txid1458463, or where                the negatively correlated bacteria comprise                Alistipes txid1262695, Fusobacterium txid1583098,                F.txid712288, F.txid1032505, Leuconostoc                txid1403934, Paenibacillus txid78058, Alcanivorax                txid519051, Arthrobacter txid1690248, Bacillus                txid1127743, and/or B.txid492670, where the subject                is predicted to have colorectal cancer if the                amount of positively correlated bacteria is lower                in the subject than in comparison to a control or                if the amount of negatively correlated bacteria is                higher in the subject than in comparison to a                control, and (S3) administering PAA to the subject                who is predicted to have colorectal cancer; or (I)                detecting the presence or absence of gut                microbiota, where the gut microbiota comprises good                responder bacteria that are positively correlated                to immunotherapeutic response and poor responder                bacteria that are negatively correlated to                immunotherapeutic response, where the good                responder bacteria comprise C.txid1638787,                C.txid1697791, F.txid1263021, C.txid100884,                C.txid127889, C.txid1182556, S.txid99822,                A.txid1203555, R.txid1262944 and/or B.txid1458463,                where the poor responder bacteria comprise                A.txid1262695, F.txid1583098, F.txid712288,                F.txid1032505, L.txid1403934, P.txid78058,                A.txid519051, A.txid1690248, B.txid1127743 or                B.txid492670, where the subject is predicted to                positively respond to the cancer immunotherapy                treatment if the good responder bacteria are higher                in the subject than in comparison to a control, or                the subject is predicted to positively respond to                the cancer immunotherapy treatment if the poor                responder bacteria are lower in the subject than in                comparison to a control, and administering PAA to                the subject that is predicted not to positively                respond to the cancer immunotherapy treatment.                INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the following:                (1) a method (B) for detecting colorectal cancer in                a subject, comprising (B1) obtaining a sample from                the subject, (B2) performing metagenomics                sequencing or qPCR on the sample, and (B3)                determining positively and negatively correlated                bacterial species to PAA production, where the                lower levels of PAA are negatively correlated to at                least one bacterial species, where the negatively                correlated bacterial species comprise Alistipes                txid1262695, F.txid1583098, F.txid712288,                F.txid1032505, L.txid1403934, P.txid78058,                A.txid519051, A.txid1690248, B.txid1127743, or                B.txid492670, the higher levels of PAA are                positively correlated to at least one bacterial                species, the positively correlated bacterial                species comprise C.txid1638787, C.txid1697791,                F.txid1263021, C.txid100884, C.txid127889,                C.txid1182556, S.txid99822, A.txid1203555,                R.txid1262944, or B.txid1458463; (2) a method (C)                of determining a gut microbiota signature for                cancer detection, comprising (i) obtaining a serum                sample from a subject and a control, (ii)                determining PAA levels in the serum sample, (iii)                obtaining a fecal sample from the subject and the                control, (iv) performing metagenomic sequencing or                qPCR on the fecal sample, and (v) determining                bacterial species which are positively and                negatively correlated to the PAA levels in the                serum sample, where the positively correlated                bacterial species produce PAA and negatively                correlated bacterial species do not produce PAA,                and the subject has cancer if the negatively                correlated bacterial species are higher than                positively correlated bacterial species in the                subject as compared to the control; and (3) a kit                for detecting colorectal cancer in a sample from a                subject, comprising (A) a panel of 10 bacterial                species positively correlated with increased PAA                levels in the subject.

TI Wide field co-location optical detection device            for amplifying and observing microstructures to assist            in diagnosis and analysis, has second imaging component            located at side of object lens component far away from            object plane for receiving second optical signal.
AU ZHANG G
   WANG J
AE BEIJING CHAOWEIJING BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD (BEIJ-Non-standard)
GA 202607073A
AB    NOVELTY - The device has an objective lens assembly                located on a side of an object plane for receiving                a first optical signal generated by a sample when                the sample is located on a non-object plane. The                objective lens assembly comprises an infinite far                conjugate objective lens assembly and a tubular                lens assembly. An adjusting mechanism adjusts a                distance between the objective lens assembly and                the sample. A first imaging component is located at                a side of the object lens component far away from                the object plane for receiving the first optical                signal when the sample is located at the non-focal                plane of the object lens component and generating a                first image.
   USE - Wide field co-location optical detection                device for use in dermatology. Uses include but are                not limited to skin cancer, inflammatory skin                diseases, psoriasis and eczema.
   ADVANTAGE - The device improves detection efficiency and                detection accuracy. The device allows the adjusting                mechanism to be controlled to move the sample from                the non-focal plane to the focal plane, so that the                sample is imaged in the microscopic field of view,                thus performing microscopic imaging of the position                to be detected. The device allows the macroscopic                imaging mode and the microscopic imaging mode to                share the same objective lens assembly, so that                different imaging modes are strictly concentric,                thus realizing the co-locating of macro imaging and                micro imaging, and avoiding blind area of sight                line, which is good for quickly locating the                position to be detected in the detecting                process.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a using                method.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view of a wide                field co-location optical detection device.

   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of the composition is by                parenteral, cardiovascular, intravenous,                intraarterial (claimed), spinal, epidermal,                intramuscular, intra-arterial, intrathecal,                intracapsular, intraorbital, intracardiac,                intradermal, intraperitoneal, transtracheal,                subcutaneous, subcuticular, intraarticular,                subcapsular, subarachnoid, intraspinal, epidural or                intrasternal routes or infusion. TI Diagnosing neoplastic lesion in expanded            biological tissue sample of patient, involves analyzing            sample with computer, detecting and segmenting nuclei,            calculating molecular characteristics, and determining            pathology of sample.

AE MASSACHUSETTS INST TECHNOLOGY (MASI-C)
   BETH ISRAEL DEACONESS MEDICAL CENT (BEIS-C)
   MASSACHUSETTS INST TECHNOLOGY (MASI-C)

GA 201868382W
AB    NOVELTY - Method (M1) for diagnosing a neoplastic lesion                in an expanded biological tissue sample of a                patient, involves providing at least one sample                image of the expanded biological tissue sample,                providing a computer configured to analyze the                sample, analyzing the sample with the computer,                detecting and segmenting nuclei, calculating                molecular characteristics of those nuclei with the                computer, and determining a diagnosis of the                pathology of the sample with the computer by                comparing the sample with a normal tissue                reference.
   USE - The methods are useful for (a) diagnosing a                neoplastic lesion in an expanded biological tissue                sample of a patient, and (b) diagnosing breast                neoplastic lesions, and breast cancer in a patient.                The neoplastic lesion is cancer. The cancer is a                solid tumor. The solid tumor is chosen from breast                cancer, ovarian cancer, preferably ovarian                adenocarcinoma and ovarian teratocarcinoma, lung                cancer, including small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and                non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), preferably                squamous cell lung carcinoma and adenocarcinoma,                gastric cancer, hepatic cancer, pancreatic cancer,                skin cancer, preferably basal cell carcinoma and                squamous cell carcinoma, malignant melanoma, head                and neck cancer, preferably malignant pleomorphic                adenoma, sarcoma, preferably synovial sarcoma and                carcinosarcoma, bile duct cancer, cancer of the                urinary bladder, preferably transitional cell                carcinoma and papillary carcinoma, kidney cancer,                preferably renal cell carcinoma including clear                cell renal cell carcinoma and papillary renal cell                carcinoma, colon cancer, small bowel cancer,                including cancer of the ileum, in particular small                bowel adenocarcinoma and adenocarcinoma of the                ileum, testicular embryonal carcinoma, placental                choriocarcinoma, cervical cancer, testicular                cancer, preferably testicular seminoma, testicular                teratoma and embryonic testicular cancer, and                uterine cancer. The neoplastic lesion is a benign                neoplasm. The sample is an expandable sample (all                claimed). The method is also used for diagnosing,                prognosing, and/or treating cancer, immune system                disorders, neuropsychiatric disease,                endocrine/reproductive disease,                cardiovascular/pulmonary disease, musculoskeletal                disease, and gastrointestinal disease.
   ADVANTAGE - The method is simple and convenient to                use.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   a computer-implemented method (M2) for                diagnosing breast neoplastic lesions, involves (a)                providing a system comprising a computer                information pertaining to at least one image of an                expanded tissue sample, (b) evaluating at least one                image and detecting and segmenting nuclei by                applying at least a segmentation analysis to the                sample image using the computer, (c) evaluating the                information of step (b) with an algorithm                configured as code executing in the computer using                the processor, where the algorithm configures the                processor to output a value corresponding to (i) a                risk score for cancer occurrence or (ii) a                diagnosis of the sample; and
   a method (M3) for diagnosing breast cancer in                a patient, involves (1) capturing at least one                sample image of an expanded tissue sample with an                imaging device, (2) accessing a patient dataset                containing clinical feature data values for the                patient corresponding to breast cancer from a                database, using a processor, (3) evaluating at                least one sample image recorded by the imaging                device and deriving hundreds of molecular feature                values indicative of phenotypic information of                nuclei/molecular regions of tissue by applying                first detection and segmentation of these regions                and then computing phenotypic characteristics in                the sample image, and several morphometric                measurements using the processor, (4) updating the                patient dataset using the processor, by associating                with each patient dataset the derived molecular                feature values and morphometric measurements, and                (5) evaluating the updated patient dataset of step                (4) with an algorithm configured as code executing                in the processor using the processor, where the                algorithm configures the processor to output values                corresponding to a diagnosis of the sample.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Device: The image of an expanded                  tissue sample is captured using an imaging                  device, where the imaging device is a microscope.                  The imaging device is a microscope or a pathology                  slide scanner. Preferred Method: The method (M2)                  further involves generating a report based on the                  risk of cancer occurrence assigned to the                  patient/diagnosis of cancer in the patient using                  the computer. The method (M3) further involves                  generating a report based on the diagnosis of                  cancer in the patient using the processor. The                  morphometric measurements relate to the shape,                  size, intensity distribution and/or texture of                  the molecular regions. The method (M3) further                  involves expanding the sample by contacting the                  swellable polymer with a solvent or liquid to                  cause the swellable polymer to swell. Preferred                  Sample: The expandable sample is prepared by (a)                  contacting the sample with a bi-functional                  linker, (b) permeating the sample with precursors                  of a swellable material, (c) polymerizing the                  precursors to form a swellable polymer within the                  sample, where the bi-functional linker attaches                  (or crosslinks) to the swellable material, and                  (d) incubating the sample with a non-specific                  protease in a buffer comprising a metal ion                  chelator, a nonionic surfactant, and a monovalent                  salt. The sample is a previously preserved                  clinical sample. The sample is a formalin fixed                  paraffin embedded (FFPE) or a hematoxylin and                  eosin (H and E) stained tissue sample, or a fresh                  frozen sample. The sample is subjected to (i)                  de-coverslipping the sample if it is mounted,                  (ii) treating the sample to mounting medium                  removal, (iii) treating the sample to                  re-hydration if step (ii) is performed, and (iv)                  subjecting the sample to antigen-retrieval,                  before examining. The sample is incubated with                  1-100 U/ml non-specific protease in a buffer                  having a pH of 4-12, where the buffer comprises                  5-100 mM metal ion chelator, 0.1-1% nonionic                  surfactant, and 0.05-1 M monovalent salt.                  Preferred Biomolecule: The bi-functional linker                  attaches to the swellable material during or                  after polymerization. The bi-functional linker                  comprises a protein-reactive chemical moiety and                  a gel-reactive chemical moiety. The                  protein-reactive chemical moiety is a                  succinimidyl ester of 6-((acyloyl)amino)hexanoic                  acid (AcX).
