TI New fluorescent natural dye compound from a marine organism useful in e.g. photochemotherapy of skin cancers.
AU GOSWAMI U
   GANGULY A
AE GOSWAMI U (GOSW-Individual)
   GANGULY A (GANG-Individual)
   COUNCIL SCI&IND RES INDIA (COUI-C)
GA 2003801197
AB    NOVELTY - A multiple fluorescent natural dye compound from a marine organism Holothuria scabra is new.
   USE - As a multiple fluorescent dye; as a natural dye in-vivo system for studying associated physiological aspects of organosilicon compound, in cosmetic surgery; for the preparation of flexible polyvinyl chloride film that exhibits fluorescent colors for use in paints, inks, textiles; for bleaching and brightening a polymer; for leak detections with a full spectrum of fluorescent dye; in automated chemical metering system; to mark the location of crashed transport vessel (e.g. aircraft, life crafts and rockets); in undersea probes; in photochemotherapy of skin cancers; as a chromatophore sunscreen component of cosmetic creams and lotions; in moisturizers; in fluorescent in situ hybridization application kit component for molecular diagnostics; as a component of the non-radioactive labeling and detection kits used in biochemistry, cell biology, immunochemistry, and molecular biology for labeling of DNA, RNA, proteins and enzymes; in immunofluorescent detection; in counterstain of DIG-labeled oligonucleotide probes and Anti-DIG Fab-fragments; in single and multiple flow cytometry applications; in fluorochrome stains for epifluorescence microscopy; for a quick check of biocontamination in health food, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, pesticide, and chemical industries; for rapid estimations of biocontaminants in laboratory cultures; for a rapid check of biopollutants under field conditions; as a competitive inhibitor of cholinesterases; in antimicrobial compositions; as a biosurfactant in toiletry compositions; as a natural colorant; as a bioactive composition of the dye in the ratio of 1: 20000000 in ultra pure water to obtain fluorescence of eight colors at eight different wavelengths and a phase contrast effect under transmitted light; for various fluorescent applications to be performed in areas of sub zero temperatures; as a base to make derivatives of the dye for new fluorescent probes; for molecular reagents; for making conjugates for molecular applications; to obtain a phase contrast and histochemical counterstain effect for different biochemical constituents of cells under transmitted light; and in all applications of Phycobiliproteins (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The dye is stable at the room temperature and at 0 - 300 degrees C, and has a long shelf life. The molecular and radioactive kits of the dye can be exported at the room temperature. The single dye has characteristics of at least 100 different fluorochromes e.g. DAPI, Hoechst 33258, Hoechst 33342, FITC, acridine orange, auramine, Rhodamine, TRITC, and propidium iodide. The dye can be used in all applications where presently Phycobiliproteins are used. The dye is a natural, non-toxic and eco-friendly. Unlike most synthetic fluorescent dyes, there is no need of intervening steps of strong acids and alkalis in their productions; the dye is easily separable from the conjugant biomolecule, which is negatively charged protein. Unlike most of the synthetic dyes, the natural dye does not need to be mixed with another dye from getting different fluorescent hues at different wavelengths. The dye has agglutinating qualities.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A multiple fluorescent dye compound (A) of formula (I) or (II), having empirical formula C22H48O66N2S10Si7 and molecular weight of 1915, is new.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is also included for extraction of (A) from Holothuria scabra sea-cucumber involving:
   (a) collecting the animals from the shores during a low tide and maintaining in glass tanks containing seawater in the laboratory for taxonomic identification and further use;
   (b) washing animals thoroughly with Milli-Q water and anaesthetizing by chloroform/menthol in a closed jar;
   (c) removing the viscera and the skin portion of the animals by peeling off by scraping with a scalpel for lyophilizing;
   (d) taking the lyophilized skin with ultra pure water and keeping on a shaker for 4 hours, followed by filtration through Whatman paper-1 and sintered glass filter;
   (e) evaporating the filtrate and precipitating the compound using organic solvents;
   (f) dissolving the precipitate in minimum volume of water and re-precipitating with an organic solvent to remove the salts;
   (g) centrifuging to collect the residue and discarding the filtrate;
   (h) drying the residue to obtain a dry powder;
   (i) dissolving the dry powder in water and loading to ion-exchange column;
   (j) eluting the column with water;
   (k) lyophilizing the water eluted fractions;
   (l) loading the lyophilized material on DEAE cellulose column and eluting with phosphate buffer; and
   (m) desalting repeatedly the phosphate buffer eluted fraction using PD10 column to obtain (A).
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Compound: (A) comprises a 1-hydroxy 2,5-di-methylaminobenzene (HDAB) (fluorophore of molecular weight 180) of formula (III).Preferred Dye: (A) has the following characteristics:(1) is not-decolorizes by a reducing agent;(2) is not a synthetic compound;(3) crude extract of the dye is yellowish green in color;(4) purified compound liquid dye is brownish with hues of green, yellow and red; and reddish brown colored powder, when seen with the naked eye in daylight;(5) emits hues of green color under tube light;(6) under mercury light it gives bluish green color;(7) under X-rays it fluoresces green in color;(8) is amorphous in nature;(9) is soluble in water, insoluble in organic solvent (e.g. ethanol, methanol and acetone);(10) is negatively charged;(11) has a pH of 2.8;(12) comprises a quinonoid ring;(13) is non-proteinaceous in nature;(14) has a reducing sugar;(15) act as a biosurfactant;(16) has antimicrobial qualities and when antimicrobial assay is performed, shows zone of inhibition;(17) emits fluorescence when excited with different wavelengths of X-rays, ultraviolet and visible spectral ranges on a spectrophotometers;(18) UV, visible spectroscopy is from 250 nm - 700 nm and the peaks are marked at 291 nm and 451 nm wavelengths for the compound;(19) fluorescent spectroscopic emission scanning is done by exciting the compound at 270 nm the peak of fluorescence came at 550 nm;(20) when the compound is excited at 340 nm the fluorescence peak is at 460 nm;(21) when the excitation wave length is fixed at 361 nm, fluorescence emission is at 490 nm in maximum quantity;(22) when the excitation wave length is fixed at 400 nm, the fluorescence emission is at 470 nm in maximum quantity;(23) when the compound is excited at 523 nm the emission is maximum at 600 nm;(24) physical checking of dye in concentration of 1 :2000000 times dilution i.e. at 5x10-6 concentration of compound, under UV bulbs of 260 - 280 nm range emits bluish green color of fluorescence;(25) epifluorescence microscopic checking of dye in concentration at least 1:200000000 times dilution i.e. at 5x10-8 concentration of compound, under different fluorescent cubes emits fluorescence;(26) the compound emits eight different colored fluorescence at four different wavelengths of the UV and visible ranges of the fluorescent cubes of an epifluorescence microscope;(27) fluorescence blue with hues of Indigo color emission occurs in the 380 - 400 nm of OVA when the pure compound is excited under ultra violet cube WU-330 nm - 385 nm excitation range;(28) fluorescence green color emission occurs in the 500 - 570 nm when the pure compound is excited under WE cube of 450 nm -480 nm excitation range;(29) emission of fluorescence red with orange color hues occurs in the 570 - 650 nm when the pure compound is excited under WG cube of 510 - 550 nm excitation range;(30) the compound emits hues of bluish grays under the ordinary transmitted light bulb of the epifluorescence microscope when seen under 10x, 40x, 100x objectives;(31) the compound emits hues of bluish grays under the ordinary transmitted light bulb of the epifluorescence microscope when seen under 10x, 40x, 100x objectives;(32) the cells labeled with the compound emits four different colored fluorescence at four different wave lengths of the UV and visible ranges of the fluorescent cubes and the transmitted light bulb of the epifluorescence microscope;(33) the cells labelled with the compound, emits blue color fluorescence when excited at 330 - 385 nm by the WU-fluorescence cube of the epifluorescence microscope;(34) the cells labeled with the compound emits bright yellow fluorescence when excited under WB cube of 450 - 480 nm excitation range;(35) the cells emit red color fluorescence when excited under WG cube of 510 - 550 nm excitation range;(36) the fluorescence colors of the compound persists even after one year at room temperature;(37) the fluorescence of the compound is highly photostable and does not get deteriorated by long exposures to direct light;(38) the compound is not photobleached;(39) the compound is not quenched while screening slide under fluorescence microscope;(40) fluorescence of the compound does not change when frozen at sub zero temperatures even after frozen in liquid nitrogen, a temperature at which the molecules are unable to attain the energy necessary for activation like in extracts from luminescent organisms;(41) organic composition of the pure compound by elemental analysis shows carbon 8.3572, hydrogen 1.739%, nitrogen 0.9449% and sulfur 9.457%;(42) atomic ratio for the elements in the compound was in the ratio of C:H:N:S of 22:48:2:10 shown by the microanalysis;(43) inorganic composition of the compound by subjecting it to atomic absorption spectrophotometry to estimate Silica and the percentage of the silicon dioxide 12.58%;(44) silica is an integral part of the compound;(45) atomic ratio of silicon is 7 for each 22 carbon atom;(46) purification of compound further by ion exchange chromatography and the absorbance at 291 and 451 peak to peak ratio found stable;(47) compound comprises sugar units;(48) HPLC of the pure ionic form of the compound by reverse phase C 18 type of analytical column and a gradient of 0 - 50% acetonitrile to elute the pure dye from the column gave the value of retention time 1.909 and a very sharp peak;(49) FT-IR the signals of sulfates occurring at 1210 - 1150 and 1060 - 1030 and 650 implied that sulfur is present in the compound in O-SO2- type of linkage;(50) strong absorption band for silicate found between 1090 - 1020 (at 1068) implied that silicon is present in the compound as -Si-D-Si-O-Si;CH3 stretching signal is found at 2950 - 2850;(51) there is no amide signals and the compound is not a protein;(52) hydroxy stretch signal is strong but broad which implies to the phenolic group;(53) compound contains phenolic group in the fluorophore part of the compound;(54) compound also comprises the quinonoid ring which is sterically protected;(55) fluorophore part is connected to Si-O group through; and(56) phenolic group of the compound only gives Keto-enol tautomerism and thus giving rise to both quinone types of structure and phenolic structure.The compound is non-radioactive. The first natural organo-metallic compound has silicon matrix. The presence of silica in the compound is identified for the first time as an integral part of living organism. The compound comprises a longer wavelength, narrow bandwidth and small stokes shift as given in the specification. The emission spectra of the compound are insensitive to solvent polarity and pH. The compound has greater photostability, longer wavelength and at least one emission ranges in the visible spectrum. The compound has high water miscibility and facilitates easy mixing of additives required for cosmetic and drug compositions. The compound comprises eight excitation (ex)/eight emission (em) nm ranges covering spectra right from X-rays, and 270 - 745 nm of UV and visible ranges with high and sharp peaks. The cell conjugates emit bright yellow color fluorescence making the dye useful in multicolor applications. The compound is resistant to quenching and the fluorescence intensity increases after conjugation to proteins irrespective of dilution and concentration of the dye. The compound is stable at room temperature and at 0 - 300 degrees C with a long shelf life. The molecular and radioactive kits of the compound can be exported at room temperature. The microphotography of fluorescent emissions of the compound under fluorescence microscopy done by using Kodak 400 film with no other special film requirement has exposure time of 45 - 60 seconds. The compound produces counterstain effect of cells and cell components under all fluorescence on the cytogenetic slides where no specimen is present. The compound emits eight colors of fluorescence, when excited at eight wavelength ranges of X-rays, UV rays and visible spectral ranges even in the dilutions of 1:2000000 times in ultra pure water (5x10-8 - 10-6 concentration). The blue colored fluorescence of the dye is comparable to the emission of same color by DAPI fluorochrome at the same wavelength excitation. The yellow colored fluorescence of the dye in the visible range is comparable to the same colored emissions of Auramin and FITC. The orange colored fluorescent emission is comparable to the orange fluorescence color of propidium iodide fluorochrome, rhodamine fluorochrome, and TRITC fluorochrome. The dye is also comparable to the emission of color by Hoechst 33258 and 33342 fluorochrome. The compound does not undergo loss in fluorescence on freezing. The hues of bluish grays of the compound under bright field of fluorescent microscope when seen under 10x objective produce a phase contrast effect, which is useful in rapid screening of cytogenetical, cytological, and histochemical slides and thus saves expenses on the extra phase contrast accessory component of microscope. The compound under 100x oil immersion objective of an ordinary transmitted light microscope show different colors of staining in the hues of brownish yellow, yellow, and dark blue for the proteins of yolk, nucleoplasm and chromatin respectively of actively dividing cleavage cells which is useful in rapid bioassays of various histochemical components of the cells.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Preferred Components: The marine organism is obtained from intertidal, submerged, shallow and deep waters, usually abundant in shaded areas (preferably cloves, crevices, ledges, lagoons, overhangings, rocky and sandy habitats); dull to bright colored with or without exo- and endo skeleton, sessile, sedentary drifters, nektonic with varied swimming power usually nocturnal in habit, liable to active predation, with and without luminescent and fluorescent pigments giving emissions in few to all wavelength ranges of X-rays, UVB, UVA, visible colored spectrums and infra red spectrum.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Dermatological; Antimicrobial.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   EXAMPLE - Animals from Holothuria scabra were thoroughly washed with Milli-Q water and anaesthetized by chloroform/menthol. The animals were then dissected, skin portion was pealed out by rubbing with a scalpel and the skin was lyophilized in the lyophilizer by cooling at -110 degrees C. The lyophilized skin sample (20 g) was then weighed and milli-Q water (200 ml) was added to it and shaken to extract the pigment completely from the animal for 4 hours. The extracted dye was then collected from the skin by decantation and filtered, collected and heated at 60 degrees C followed by addition of alcohol (approximately 100 - 150 ml) and the mixture was worked up to give precipitated dye.

   USE - (I) is useful for: stabilizing a diagnostic marker in a body fluid, where the diagnostic marker is a protein, a glycoprotein, a nucleic acid, an enzyme, an enzyme inhibitor or a metabolite, luteinizing hormone and progesterone, and the body fluid is saliva, a mucous secretion, tears, sweat, semen, urine, a vaginal secretion, exhalate, blood, serum or an anal secretion (all claimed); determining fertility; and collecting and analyzing body fluids. The diagnostic marker or biomarker is useful for analyzing and diagnosing disease state, which is e.g. cancer, metabolic disease (such as diabetes I or II), cardiovascular disease, infection of the patient by a bacteria (e.g. Clostridium tetani and Borrelia burgdorferi), virus (e.g. Hepatitis B virus), yeast, fungus (e.g. Candida albicans and Filobasidiella neoformans ), or parasite (e.g. Leishmania braziliensis and Strongyloides stercoralis), acid-base disorders, acidosis and alkalosis, Addison's disease, and acute coronary syndrome, heart disease, hemochromatosis, hepatitis, herpes, herpes zoster, high blood pressure, hospital-acquired pneumonia, human papilloma virus, hypercoagulable disorders, hypersensitivity, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, infectious arthritis, infectious polyneuritis, infertility, inflammatory bowel Disease, influenza, influenza A, influenza B, insulin resistance, jaundice, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid diseases, Travelers' diseases, tuberculosis, types of liver disease, urinary tract infection, venereal diseases, vitamin B12 and folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, vitamin K Deficiency, walking pneumonia, Wilson's Disease, wound and skin infections.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) improves the sampling and testing of the body fluid by conditioning the body fluids for the stabilization of specific biomolecules and/or drug metabolites.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: a method of stabilizing a diagnostic marker, comprising: mixing the body fluid comprising the diagnostic marker for fertility with the stabilizing agent, where the stabilizing agent completely or substantially prevents the cleavage, degradation, or inactivation of the diagnostic marker.

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INSTRUMENTATION AND TESTING - Preferred Components: The stabilizing agent is a protease inhibitor, a deoxyribonuclease inhibitor or a ribonuclease inhibitor. The stabilizing agent is Fixanal (RTM: Buffer having a pH of 6), acetic acid, aluminum hydroxide bentonite, aluminum sulfate hydrate, aluminum potassium sulfate dodecahydrate, benzoic acid, caffeine, and/or 3-tert-butyl-hydroxyanisole. AB    NOVELTY - Method for dermatological treatment involves                ablating epidermal and dermal tissue in a                dermatological treatment to form discrete holes in                a selected region of skin, evaluating, with a                sensing element, at least a portion of tissue from                the selected region in connection with the ablating                step for a selected tissue target, detecting, in                response to the evaluation, gathering, in response                to the detection, and applying at least one pulse                of the nonablative electromagnetic energy into                inside of the hole at which the selected tissue                target was detected.
   USE - The method is useful for dermatological                treatment of selected targets of skin (claimed),                e.g. lipid-rich targets, foreign bodies (tattoo                ink, cancers and PDT drugs), hair follicles, hair                bulge cells and vascular tissue.
   ADVANTAGE - The method actively controls delivery of                treatment energy to the selected targets. The                detection wavelengths improve the sensitivity and                selectivity of optical measurements.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method for dermatological treatment involves                ablating epidermal and dermal tissue in a                dermatological treatment to form discrete holes in                a selected region of skin, which resulting in both                ablated tissue and remaining tissue that was not                ablated within the selected region, evaluating,                with a sensing element, at least a portion of                tissue from the selected region in connection with                the ablating step for a selected tissue target,                detecting, in response to the evaluation, the                selected tissue target in tissue surrounding a base                of at least one of the discrete holes, gathering,                in response to the detection, at least one                energy-delivery parameter of an electromagnetic                source to begin emission of nonablative                electromagnetic energy, and applying at least one                pulse of the nonablative electromagnetic energy                into inside of the hole at which the selected                tissue target was detected for treating the                selected tissue target with the nonablative                electromagnetic energy. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is                included for apparatus for dermatological                treatment, which comprises an electromagnetic                source configured to emit ablative and nonablative                electromagnetic energy, delivery system configured                to deliver the ablative electromagnetic energy to                multiple discrete locations at a selected region of                skin to form a pattern of discrete holes in the                selected region including both ablated tissue and                remaining tissue that was not ablated within the                selected region, a sensing element configured to                evaluate at least a portion of the tissue from the                selected region for a selected tissue target and                detect the selected tissue target in tissue                surrounding a base of at least one of the discrete                holes, a controller configured to, in response to                detection data received from the sensing element,                alter at least one energy-delivery parameter of the                electromagnetic source to begin emission of                nonablative electromagnetic energy, and the                delivery system further configured to apply at                least one pulse of the nonablative electromagnetic                energy into inside of the hole, at which the                selected tissue target was detected for treating                the selected tissue target with the nonablative                electromagnetic energy.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: The detecting step                  involves detecting a presence of at least one of                  hair follicles, hair bulge cells, and vascular                  tissue. The detecting step involves detecting a                  presence of lipid-rich tissue. The evaluating                  step involves measuring a characteristic of a                  portion of tissue that contains at least part of                  the ablated tissue and where the measured                  characteristic comprises at least one of an                  ablation rate, a fluorescent emission of the                  portion of tissue, a scattering property or an                  absorption property of the portion of tissue for                  at least one optical wavelength, and an optical                  absorption or scattering of the portion of tissue                  at least two wavelengths. The evaluating step                  involves measuring a characteristic of a portion                  of tissue that contains at least part of the                  remaining tissue underlying at least one of the                  holes, the measured characteristic comprising a                  characteristic chosen from acoustical or                  radio-frequency absorption spectrum of the                  portion of tissue, fluorescent emission of the                  portion of tissue, depth of at least one of the                  holes, scattering property and an absorption                  property of the portion of tissue for at least                  one optical wavelength, and an optical absorption                  of the portion of tissue at least two                  wavelengths. The applying step involves creating                  a nonablative thermal treatment zone at the base                  of the hole where the lipid-rich tissue was                  detected. The pulse of nonablative                  electromagnetic energy is emitted from an optical                  source and the optical source emits energy at an                  infrared fat selective wavelength or an infrared                  water absorbed wavelength. The ablating step                  involves directing a laser beam to the selected                  region to heat water in the selected region, and                  where at least two of the discrete holes are                  created in a pattern corresponding to the optical                  intensity profile of the laser beam. The pulse of                  nonablative electromagnetic energy is emitted                  from a second laser, and where the altering step                  further involves delivering a beam from an                  optical source comprising at least one of the                  laser and the second laser to at least two of the                  holes to cause treatment of at least one lipid                  rich target. The laser comprises carbon dioxide                  laser and at least one pulse of nonablative                  electromagnetic energy is emitted from                  Raman-shifted fiber laser or at least one of                  erbium-doped fiber laser and erbium-doped fiber                  amplifier. The method further involves applying                  an absorbing agent applied to the surface of the                  selected region and where the ablating step                  involves directing a laser beam to the absorbing                  agent. The density of the holes is 100-10000/cm                  2, preferably 1000-2000/cm 2in the selected                  region. The altering step involves activating the                  delivery of the pulse of nonablative                  electromagnetic energy in response to the result                  of the evaluating step. The altering step                  involves selecting at least one location at the                  selected region for delivery of the pulse of                  nonablative electromagnetic energy in response to                  the result of the evaluating step. The method                  further involves focusing at least one pulse of                  nonablative electromagnetic energy using an                  optical lens array. The hole has a depth of 0.5-6                  mm and diameter of 0.2-2.0 mm. Preferred                  Apparatus: The electromagnetic source comprises                  exactly one laser or at least two lasers. The                  electromagnetic source comprises at least two                  optical sources with different optical emission                  spectra. The electromagnetic source comprises at                  least one of carbon dioxide laser, thulium-doped                  fiber laser that is configured to be tunable,                  Er:YAG laser, a Raman-shifted fiber laser, an                  erbium-doped fiber laser with an erbium-doped                  fiber amplifier, fiber laser, carbon dioxide                  laser with at least one of flash lamp or                  radio-frequency source, and holmium laser. The                  electromagnetic source emits energy at an                  infrared fat-selective wavelength or infrared                  water-selective wavelength. The sensing element                  is configured to measure a characteristic of the                  portion of tissue only after the portion of                  tissue has been ablated, the measured                  characteristic chosen from ablation rate,                  scattering property or absorption property of the                  portion of tissue for at least one optical                  wavelength a fluorescent emission of the portion                  of tissue and an optical absorption of the                  portion of tissue for least two wavelengths. The                  sensing element comprises an element chosen from                  ultrasonic transducer, optical source with                  optical detector, and a spectral filter. The                  electromagnetic source comprises an optical                  source that emits light with a wavelength of                  350-450 nm. The electromagnetic source is further                  configured to create nonablative thermal                  treatment zone at the base of the hole, where the                  selected tissue target was detected. The                  apparatus further comprises a controller that                  independently controls parameters of the ablative                  and nonablative electromagnetic energy that                  affect the dermatological treatment. The                  apparatus further comprises a positional sensor                  that measures at least one of the relative                  position, relative velocity, relative speed, and                  relative acceleration between the hand piece and                  the selected region. The controller is further                  configured to receive data from the positional                  sensor and control at least one parameter of the                  electromagnetic source that affects                  dermatological treatment in response to data                  received from the positional sensor. The delivery                  system comprises a system chosen from optical                  scanner, optical lens array, and patterned                  mask.

AB    NOVELTY - Slidably mounted within a cartridge (24)                having upper and lower light-tight seals (26,28),                is a case (12) having an upwardly extending rod                (18) on to which the shroud (88) is elastically                fitted (90). Extending downwards from the case is a                tubular needle (4) terminating in a sharp end (16)                for penetrating the patients skin (22). A foam                collar supports the cartridge from the skin surface                whilst a resistor (44) and thermistor (46) in the                tip of the needle form the temp. sensing                element.
Light from a source (52) is transmitted,                through optical fibre (60), and projected outwardly                at the needle tip, to be reflected by tissue and                returned via the point (64) and fibre (62), and                eventually focussed (70) on to the film plane (58)                to record the tissue colour.
   USE - Applicable to 'in-vivo' determination of                ovulation in females and in diagnosis and treatment                of cancer.
   ADVANTAGE - Applicable to 'in-vivo' determination of                ovulation in females and in diagnosis and treatment                of cancer.
EA    (US4502487-A)   NOVELTY - The appts. has a housing
including a case and a needle-like extension                projecting.
The extension has a sharp end for piercing the                skin of a patient.
A temperature element is disposed within the                housing and has an indicator responsiVe to a                predetermined change in temp.
An optical element is disposed within the                housing for recording colouration of tissue.
The recording of colouration of tissue takes                place as the extension is withdrawn from a depth                within the skin of a patient. The recordation on                film of the colouration of the tissue corresponds                to the recordation of the temp.
(11pp)
   (US4633885-A)   NOVELTY - The probe has an enclosure with an extension                and has a device for manually setting a fixed                reference temperature. A device is disposed within                the extension for detecting a predetermined change                in temperature from the reference temp.
The detection of the predetermined change in                temp. is indicated.
An electronic circuit operatively connects the                indicator in response to the predetermined change                in temp.
The indicator includes a light which is                illuminated upon the energisation of the indicator,                a device for flashing the light on and off when the                temp. measured is greater than the reference temp.                and less than the predetermined change in temp.                above the reference temp.
The light is illuminated in a steady state                when the measured temp. is greater than the                predetermined change in temp. above the reference                temp.

AB    NOVELTY - A new isolated peptide (I) comprising:
(a) a fully defined sequence of 398 amino acids, given in the specification;
(b) an allelic variant or an ortholog of (i) that is encoded by a nucleic acid molecule that hybridizes under stringent conditions to the opposite strand of a fully defined sequence of 1206 or 18554 bp, given in the specification; or
(c) a fragment of (i) comprising at least 10 contiguous amino acids, is new.
   USE - The methods and compositions of the present invention are useful for diagnosing and treating disorders mediated by the human lipase protein, such as cancer of the colon, kidneys, skin, brain and testis, and Burkitt's lymphoma.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for:
   (1) an isolated antibody (II) that selectively binds to (I);
   (2) an isolated nucleic acid molecule (III) comprising of a nucleotide sequence that encodes (I) or its complement;
   (3) a gene chip (IV) comprising the nucleic acid molecule (III);
   (4) a transgenic non-human animal (V) comprising the nucleic acid molecule (III);
   (5) a nucleic acid vector comprising (VI) the nucleic acid molecule (III);
   (6) a host cell (VII) containing the vector of (VI);
   (7) a method (VIII) for producing (I) comprising introducing a nucleotide sequence encoding (I) into a host cell, and culturing the host cell under conditions in which the peptides are expresses from the nucleotide sequence;
   (8) a method (IX) for detecting the presence of (I) in a sample, comprising contacting the sample with a detection agent that specifically allows detection of the presence of the peptide in the sample and then detecting the presence of the peptide;
   (9) a method (X) for detecting the presence of the nucleic acid molecule (III) in a sample, comprising contacting the sample with an oligonucleotide that hybridizes to the nucleic acid molecule under stringent conditions and determining whether the oligonucleotide binds to the nucleic acid molecule in the sample;
   (10) a method (XI) for identifying a modulator of (I), comprising contacting the peptide with an agent and determining if the agent has modulated the function or activity of the peptide;
   (11) a method (XII) for identifying an agent that binds to (I), comprising contacting the peptide with an agent and assaying the contacted mixture to determine whether a complex is formed with the agent bound to the peptide;
   (12) a pharmaceutical composition (XIII) comprising an agent identified by the method of (XII), and a carrier;
   (13) a method (XIV) for treating a disease or condition mediated by a human lipase protein, comprising administering an agent identified by the method of (XII);
   (14) a method (XV) for identifying a modulator of the expression of (I), comprising contacting a cell expressing the peptide with an agent, and determining if the agent has modulated the expression of the peptide;
   (15) an isolated human lipase peptide (XVI) with a sequence at least 70% identical to a fully defined sequence of 398 amino acids, given in the specification; and
   (16) an isolated nucleic acid molecule (XVII) encoding a human lipase peptide, the nucleic acid molecule sharing at least 80% homology with a fully defined sequence of 1206 or 18554 bp, given in the specification.

AB    NOVELTY - Anti-human ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73)                antibody or its antigen-binding fragment,                comprising: a heavy chain variable region; and a                light chain variable region, where the heavy chain                variable region includes three heavy chain                complementarity determining region (HCDRs), HCDR1                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.10, HCDR2                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.11, HCDR3                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.12, or HCDR1                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.16, HCDR2                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.17, HCDR3                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.18, and the                light chain variable region includes three light                chain complementarity determining region (LCDRs)                LCDR1 comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.13, LCDR2                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.14, LCDR3                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.15, or LCDR1                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.19, LCDR2                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.20, LCDR3                comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.21, is                new.
   USE - The antibody is useful: in a kind of                recombinant protein, and polynucleotide which is                used in a vector, and genetically engineered host                cell; in antibody conjugate, and CAR construct                which is used recombinant immune cell; in a                composition; for in vitro detection of CD73 protein                in a sample; and for preventing and/or treating                CD73-related diseases comprising blood cancer,                lymphoma, malignant glioma, melanoma, skin cancer,                gastric cancer, gastrointestinal stromal tumor,                liver cancer , cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder                cancer, peritoneal cancer, colorectal cancer, small                bowel cancer, anal cancer, multiple myeloma,                pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer,                uterine cancer, cervical cancer, vaginal cancer,                bladder cancer, kidney cancer, non-small cell lung                cancer, small cell lung cancer, prostate cancer,                testicular cancer, penile cancer, thyroid cancer,                head and neck cancer, esophageal cancer, bone                cancer, or sarcoma (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The antibody: can bind to a CD73 antigen with                high specificity, has high affinity, has remarkable                anti-tumor activity and has excellent clinical                application prospects; and has excellent biological                activity, and can block the production of adenosine                by inhibiting the enzymatic activity of CD73 and                directly destroy the immunosuppression mediated by                adenosine, preferably combination of the                CD73-targeting humanized antibody and the                programmed cell death protein 1-targeting antibody                has a synergistic effect and can significantly                enhance the curative effect of each single                drug.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Anti-human ecto-5'-nucleotidase (CD73)                antibody or its antigen-binding fragment,                comprises: a heavy chain variable region; and a                light chain variable region, where the heavy chain                variable region includes three heavy chain                complementarity determining region (HCDRs), HCDR1                comprising amino acid of Ser-Tyr-Trp-Met-His (SEQ                ID NO.10), HCDR2 comprising amino acid of SEQ ID                NO.11 (comprising a fully defined sequence of 17                amino acids as given in specification), HCDR3                comprising amino acid of                Arg-Val-Tyr-Gly-Thr-Met-Asp-Thr (SEQ ID NO.12), or                HCDR1 comprising amino acid of Arg-Tyr-Tyr-Ile-Tyr                (SEQ ID NO.16), HCDR2 comprising amino acid of SEQ                ID NO.17 (comprising a fully defined sequence of 17                amino acids as given in specification), HCDR3                comprising amino acid of                Asp-Val-Tyr-Asp-Tyr-Ala-Gly-Phen-Ala-Tyr (SEQ ID                NO.18), and the light chain variable region                includes three light chain complementarity                determining region (LCDRs) LCDR1 comprising amino                acid of SEQ ID NO.13 (comprising a fully defined                sequence of 11 amino acids as given in                specification), LCDR2 comprising amino acid of                Arg-Ala-Asn-Ile-Trp-Val-Asp (SEQ ID NO.14), LCDR3                comprising amino acid of                Leu-Gln-Tyr-Asp-Glu-Leu-Tyr-Thr (SEQ ID NO.15), or                LCDR1 comprising amino acid of SEQ ID NO.19                (comprising a fully defined sequence of 11 amino TI System for reconstructing e.g. diffusion            properties, of e.g. digestive tract, of human/animal to            detect digestive tract cancer, has computing unit            computing base parameter and reconstructing optical            properties from base parameter.
AU DINTEN J
   BOUTET J
AE COMMISSARIAT ENERGIE ATOMIQUE (COMS-C)
   COMMISSARIAT ENERGIE ATOMIQUE (COMS-C)
   COMMISSARIAT ENERGIE ATOMIQUE (COMS-C)
GA 2013L37868
AB    NOVELTY - The system (10) has a detector (16) receiving                a signal emitted by a diffusing medium (12) upon                illumination by a pulsed radiation source (14). A                processing unit processes time distribution of a                signal for a source-detector pair. Another detector                (22) measures signal intensity corresponding to                equivalent moment of order 0 for a source-latter                detector pair. A computing unit (62) computes a                base parameter by combining characteristic                magnitude of the distribution with intensity                measured for the source-latter detector pair and                reconstructs optical properties from the                parameter.
   USE - System for use in fluorescence imaging and                optical molecular imaging field to reconstruct                optical properties e.g. light absorption                properties, diffusion properties and fluorescence                properties, of a diffusing medium e.g. area of                organ such as brain, breast, prostate and digestive                tract of human or animal to detect breast cancer,                prostate cancer or digestive tract cancer and                pathologies on a surface of digestive tract. Can                also be used in dermatology to characterize skin                inflammation reaction.
   ADVANTAGE - The system calculates the moments of order 0                using two types of measurements e.g. intensity                measurements, at a large number of points directly                provided by the detector of the image sensor and                measurements of the time distribution of the                photons picked up by detection sensors of another                detector so as to reduce parasitic fluctuations in                terms of base parameters for improving                reconstruction of the optical properties.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The detector is formed of set of pixels from                an image sensor (18) e.g. charge-coupled device                (CCD) sensor or a complementary metal oxide                semiconductor (CMOS) sensor. The detectors are                respectively time resolved detector and                non-time-resolved detector. An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is                also included for a method for reconstructing                optical properties of a diffusing medium.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a schematic view                illustrating reconstruction system comprising an                imaging probe including pulsed radiation sources                and detectors.
   Reconstruction system (10)
   Diffusing medium (12)
   Pulsed radiation source (14)
   Detectors (16, 22)
   Image sensor (18)
   Computing unit (62)

The cells                were co-transfected with two additional plasmids,                one for a fusion &#946;                (1,4)-N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase III (GnTIII)                polypeptide expression (a GnT-III expression                vector), and one for mannosidase II expression (a                Golgi mannosidase II expression vector) at a ratio                of 4:4:1:1, respectively. Cells were grown as                adherent monolayer cultures in T flasks using                Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's medium (DMEM)                supplemented with 10% of fetal calf serum (FCS) and                were transfected into flask. Cells (15 million)                were seeded for 24 hours before transfection in                DMEM culture medium (25 ml) supplemented with FCS                (at 10 vol.%), and cells were placed at                37&#176; C in an incubator with a 5% of carbon                dioxide atmosphere overnight. For each flask to be                transfected, a solution of DNA, calcium chloride                and water was prepared by mixing 94 &#956; g of                total plasmid vector DNA divided equally between                the light and heavy chain expression vectors, water                to a final volume of 469 &#956; l and 469                &#956; l of a 1M calcium dichloride solution.                To the solution, 938 &#956; l of a 50 mM                4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid,                280 mM sodium chloride, 1.5 mM sodium hydrogen                phosphate solution at pH 7.05 were added, mixed                immediately for 10 seconds and left to stand at                room temperature for 20 seconds. The suspension was                diluted with 10 ml of DMEM supplemented with 2%                FCS, and added to flask in place of the existing                medium. Then additional 13 ml of transfection                medium are added. The cells were incubated at                37&#176; C, 5% of carbon dioxide for 17-20                hours, then medium was replaced with 25 ml of DMEM,                10% of FCS. The conditioned culture medium was                harvested for 7 days post-media exchange by                centrifugation for 15 minutes at 210x g, the                solution was sterile filtered (0.22 &#956; m)                and sodium azide in a final concentration of 0.01                wt/vol.% was added, and kept at 4&#176; C. The                secreted wild type or glycoengineered afucosylated                antibodies were purified from cell culture and                worked up to give glycoengineered antibodies.

PN WO2007113473-A1; EP2005235-A1; US2009218527-A1; JP2009532732-W
TI Confocal microscope for imaging an object, useful            in e.g. optical biopsy to examine lesions for detecting            skin cancer, comprises a two-dimensional array of light            emitting diodes as light source.
AU FRENCH P M W
   DUNSBY C W
   NEIL M A A
   FRENCH P
   DUNSBY C
   NEIL M
AE IMPERIAL INNOVATIONS LTD (UNLO-C)
   IMPERIAL INNOVATIONS LTD (UNLO-C)
GA 2007845618
AB    NOVELTY - A confocal microscope (2) for imaging an                object (12), comprises light source, light detector                and optical system. The light source includes a                two-dimensional array (4) of light emitting diodes                (LED); and a source array driver (6) for driving                the two-dimensional array of LED, to generate a                sequence of illumination patterns of illuminating                light. The optical system directs illuminating                light to the object, to illuminate object with the                sequence of illumination patterns; and directs                light from the object to the detector. The detector                includes a two-dimensional array (18) of detector                cells.
   USE - For performing confocal microscopy to image an                object; to be located at a tip of an endoscope;                useful for performing fluorescence imaging and                surface imaging such as finger print scanning;                useful for performing cell-based assays (claimed);                useful as a read-out device or monitor for                technologies including biochips and microfluidic                devices; useful in optical sectioning; useful for                optical biopsy to e.g. examine lesions to detect                diseases such as skin cancer; useful in profiling                surfaces for e.g. geology and forensic                applications; useful in biometrics; and useful as a                basis for a slit-scanning ophthalmoscope.
   ADVANTAGE - The two-dimensional array of light emitting                diodes is small and robust; operates without                generating excess heat; has low cost; is devoid of                moving mechanical parts; and produces desired                illumination patterns simply by use of appropriate                electrical signals. The light emitting diodes are                bright, and the imaging time for the confocal                microscope can be reduced accordingly. The                two-dimensional array provides individually                addressable light emitting diodes. The                two-dimensional array of detector cells is                advantageously complementary to the two-dimensional                array of light emitting diodes. The degree of                miniaturization permitted by the use of arrays of                light emitting diodes to generate the illumination                patterns, enables many different types of new                confocal microscope arrangements, and hence the                confocal microscope can be particularly used on the                tip of the endoscope. As the light emitting diodes                are bright, they do not generate an excessive                amount of heat or consume a large amount of power,                thus extending the range of possible applications                of confocal microscopes. The compact, robust and                low-cost nature of the confocal microscope achieved                using the array of light emitting diodes, enables                the use of confocal microscope in various                applications.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A confocal microscope (2) for imaging an                object (12), comprises a light source, a light                detector, and an optical system. The light source                includes a two-dimensional array (4) of light                emitting diodes (LED); and a source array driver                (6) for driving the two-dimensional array of LED,                to generate a sequence of illumination patterns of                illuminating light. The optical system directs the                illuminating light to the object, to illuminate the                object with the sequence of illumination patterns;                and directs light from the object to the light                detector. The light detector detects light. The                light detector includes a two-dimensional array                (18) of detector cells; and a detector array reader                (20) to read detected light levels from a sequence                of detection patterns of detector cells, where the                sequence of detection patterns is synchronized with                and corresponds to the sequence of illumination                patterns. The sequence of illumination patterns                preferably includes patterns formed of line(s) of                illumination, and is used for line scanning the                object. The illuminating light is an ultraviolet                light, a visible light or a near infrared                light.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The figure shows a confocal microscope with                separate illumination and detection optical                paths.
   2confocal microscope
   4two-dimensional array of light emitting                diodes

TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ELECTRONICS - The light detector comprises a                  charge-coupled device (CCD) camera array, or a                  complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS)                  camera array. The two-dimensional array of light                  emitting diodes includes aluminum-gallium-indium                  nitride (AlGaInN) light emitting diodes.

TI New copper organocomplexes obtained by reacting            copper(II)acylate with organic compound e.g.            4-(bis(2-chloroethyl)-amino)-D,L-phenylalanine or amino            carbonyl aziridine, in chloroform/methanol mixture,            useful e.g. to treat tumor diseases.

GA 2009N01985
AB    NOVELTY - Copper organocomplexes (I) obtained by                reacting a copper(II)acylate having an acidic to                neutral pH-value with an organic compound, which is                4-(bis(2-chloroethyl)-amino)-D,L-phenylalanine                (sarcolysin) or its hydrochloride,                N-(2-furanidil)-5-fluorouracil (tegafur) or amino                carbonyl aziridine (leacadin), in a                chloroform/methanol mixture, are new.
   USE - (I) are useful: for the treatment of tumor                diseases and/or protection of healthy tissue                against ionizing radiation; in radiotherapy; and                for the in vivo detection of malignant cells (all                claimed), where the tumor is e.g. colon tumor,                brain tumor, eye tumor, pancreatic tumor, bladder                tumor, lung tumor, breast cancer, ovarian tumor,                cervical tumor, skin tumor, testicular tumor,                kidney tumor, germ cell tumor, liver cancer,                leukemia, malignant lymphoma, nerve tumor,                neuroblastoma, prostate cancer, soft tissue tumor                and esophageal cancer. (I) are useful: to treat                disease caused by hyperproliferative cells; and as                antioxidants for the treatment of inflammatory                diseases associated with tumors. The ability of (I)                to treat tumor disease was tested in lymphoma-cell                line. The results showed that copper complex of                4-(bis(2-chloroethyl)-amino)-D,L-phenylalanine-hydrochloride                (0.1 mmole) exhibited an apoptosis induction of                43.5%.
   ADVANTAGE - (I) treat diseases with less side effects. (I)                are: non-toxic; and highly selective against                excessive proliferating cells. (I) in combination                with cytotoxic drugs e.g. ethyleneimine, exhibit                synergistic effect to treat tumor. (I) exhibit very                strong antioxidant activity against inflammatory                diseases.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a                combination preparation comprising (I), at least a                cytostatic and optionally an auxiliary material                and/or carrier materials.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The copper(II)acylate                  is copper(II) acetate or copper(II) propionate.                  Preferred Process: The                  copper-sarcolysin-hydrochloride-complex is                  obtained by reacting sarcolysin-hydrochloride and                  copper(II) acetate at a pH of 2-3, where: the                  complex exhibits a melting point of 147 degrees C                  and comprises 15% of copper, 37.3% of carbon,                  4.43% of hydrogen, 24.4% of chlorine, 6.74% of                  nitrogen and oxygen; the deviation of the                  indicated analysis values for carbon, nitrogen                  and chlorine is less than 3%; and the deviation                  of the indicated analysis values for hydrogen and                  copper is up to 4.5%. The                  copper-sarcolysin-complex is obtained by reacting                  sarcolysin and copper(II) acetate at a pH of 6-7,                  where: the complex exhibits a melting point of                  177 degrees C and comprises 9.2% of copper, 45.3%                  of carbon, 5.4% of hydrogen, 20.6% of chlorine,                  8.1% of nitrogen and oxygen; the deviation of the                  indicated analysis values for carbon, nitrogen                  and chlorine is less than 3%; and the deviation                  of the indicated analysis values for hydrogen and                  copper is up to 4.5%. The copper-tegafur-complex                  is obtained by reacting tegafur and copper(II)                  acetate at a pH of 1, where the complex exhibits                  a melting point of 127 degrees C and comprises                  26.8% of copper, 18.16% of carbon, 3.08% of                  hydrogen, 25.3% of chlorine, 3.39% of nitrogen,                  oxygen and fluorine; the deviation of the                  indicated analysis values for carbon, nitrogen                  and chlorine is less than 3%; and the deviation                  of the indicated analysis values for hydrogen and                  copper is up to 4.5%. The process comprises:                  dissolving the copper(II)acylate and the organic                  compound in the chloroform/methanol mixture;                  optionally acidifying and heating at 50 degrees                  C; and subsequently washing and drying the                  obtained precipitate after cooling.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The ratio of                  chloroform/methanol mixture is 1:1-3:1.
   ACTIVITY - Cytostatic; Antiinflammatory.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of (I) is 0.01-10, preferably                0.5-1.5 mg/kg/day, orally, perorally,                intravenously, intraperitoneally, intratracheally,                intra-abdominally, transdermally, intramuscularly                or pulmonarily.
   EXAMPLE - Sarcolysin hydrochloride (0.0125 mole) was                dissolved in a mixture (50 ml) comprising 1 part of                methanol and 3 parts of chloroform to obtain a                solution A. Copper(II) acetate (0.01 mole) was                dissolved in a mixture (50 ml) comprising 1 part of                methanol and 3 parts of chloroform to obtain a                solution B. The obtained solution A and B were                stirred permanently and heated. The mixture was                held for further 30 minutes under stirring and                cooled at room temperature. The pH of the mixture                was 2-3. Within some hours the obtained fine                crystalline, green precipitate was washed,                separated and dried at 65-70 degrees C in air to                give a copper complex of                4-(bis(2-chloroethyl)-amino)-D,L-phenylalanine-hydrochloride                as a microcrystalline powder with a melting point                of 147 degrees C, copper content of 15%, carbon                content of 37.3%, hydrogen content of 4.43%,                chlorine content of 24.4%, nitrogen content of                6.74% and oxygen content of 10.3%.

PN WO9904238-A2; AU9884030-A
TI Methods for diagnosis and prognosis of hyperproliferative disorders - by determining the level of cyclin kinase inhibitor protein(s), particularly p27.
AU PAGANO M
   DRAETTA G
   ROLFE M
   LODA M
AE MITOTIX INC (MITO-Non-standard)
   DEACONESS HOSPITAL (DEAC-Non-standard)
GA 1999132426
AB       Methods are claimed for: (a) diagnosing a hyperproliferative disorder, associated with the destabilisation of a cyclin kinase inhibitor (CKI) protein in cells of a patient, comprises: (i) ascertaining the CKI protein level in a sample of patient cells; and (ii) diagnosing the presence or absence of a hyperproliferative disorder by utilising the ascertained CKI protein level, where a reduced CKI protein level, relative to a normal control cell sample, correlates with the presence of a hyperproliferative disorder; (b) evaluating the aggressiveness and/or rate of recurrence of a disorder marked by aberrant hyperproliferation, aberrant dedifferentiation and/or aberrant apoptosis of cells, comprises: (i) ascertaining the CKI protein level in a sample of patient cells; and (ii) ascertaining the aggressiveness and/or risk for recurrence of the disorder, from the ascertained CKI protein level, where a reduced CKI protein level, relative to a normal control cell sample, correlates with a more aggressive form of the disorder and an increased risk of reccurence of the disorder; and (c) evaluating a cancer patient's risk of death due to cancer and/or recurrence of a cancer, comprises: (i) ascertaining the CKI protein level in a sample of patient cancer cells; and (ii) predicting the patient's risk of death and/or reccurence of cancer by utilising the ascertained CKI protein level, where a reduced CKI protein level, relative to a normal control cell sample, correlates with an increased risk of death and/or recurrence of a cancer.
   USE -   The methods are useful for diagnosing (A) disorders associated with hyperproliferation, evaluating their aggressiveness and/or rate of recurrence (B) and as prognosis for evaluating a cancer patient's risk of death (C). In method (C) the cancer includes cancer of the epithelial tissue; , melanomas, sarcomas and carcinomas of breast, ovaries, lung, intestinal, pancreas, prostate, testis, liver, skin, stomach, renal, cervical and colorectal. In breast carcinoma conditions include ductal carcinoma, mucinous carcinoma or a lobular carcinoma, or a node-negative breast carcinoma (claimed). From the observations, treatment can be applied on the basis of the patient's risk of death and/or recurrence of the cancer. The diagnostic methods may also be employed as follow-up to treatment, e.g. quantitation of the level of p27 protein may be indicative of the effectiveness of current or previously employed cancer therapies as well as the effect of these therapies upon patient prognosis . Also, the methods and reagents allow the detection of loss of p27 protein from a cell in order to diagnose and phenotype proliferative disorders arising from tumourigenic transformation of cells, or other hyperplastic or neoplastic transformation processes as well as differentiative disorders such as degeneration of tissue e.g. neurodegeneration.

TI Hand held dermoscopy illumination device for            non-contact illumination of e.g. mammalian tissue,            during medical treatment, has light source array            comprising light source for emitting orange light with            specific wavelength.
AU MULLANI N
AE 3GEN INC (THRE-Non-standard)
   3GEN INC (THRE-Non-standard)
GA 201511594C
AB    NOVELTY - The device has a hand held medical device                including a housing (14). A light source array is                incorporated into the housing, and comprises a                light source i.e. LED, for emitting orange light                having a wavelength of between 581 nm and 600 nm.                The light source is cross-polarized relative to                other light source of the array. An array of LEDs                includes five LEDs emitting light in the range of                581 nm and 600 nm for every fourteen LEDs emitting                white light, and a diode for emitting the white                light and illuminated by a switch.
   USE - Hand held dermoscopy illumination device for                non-contact illumination of organic tissue e.g.                mammalian tissue and human tissue (all claimed) of                skin during medical examination and                treatment.
   ADVANTAGE - The device illuminates the skin with white                light and/or light in a color range that provides                more advantageous viewing of the skin and                sub-surface skin structures to enable a more                enhanced viewing of pigments and lesions found in                the skin to aid in a visual early detection of                various types of skin cancer. The device includes a                high quality multi-element lens that provides color                correction and reduced image distortion to produces                an image rich surface detail. The device includes                an ability to toggle between multiple modes of                operation, so that the viewer can toggle between                images to provide an enhanced perspective of the                skin to a doctor, researcher or healthcare                professional. The device provides that the cross                polarized orange light can be used with                non-polarized light to enhance the imaging of                deeper pigmentation when using a glass-liquid                interface and white light.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIMS is also included for in                a hand held dermoscopy illumination device and a                hand held illumination device for non-contact                illumination of organic tissue.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a perspective view of a                hand held dermoscopy illumination device showing                removable and retractable features.

TI Detecting chromosomal rearrangement comprises            isolating genomic DNAs from cells of test and reference            samples, and hybridizing the test and reference DNA            products to a tiling density DNA microarray comprising            genomic DNA sequences.
AU SHETTY S
   MAO R
AE UNIV UTAH RES FOUND (UTAH-C)
   UNIV UTAH RES FOUND (UTAH-C)
GA 2012Q20268
AB    NOVELTY - Detecting the presence of a chromosomal                rearrangement in a test sample comprises isolating                a first genomic DNA from cells of a test sample and                a second genomic DNA from cells of a reference                sample; and hybridizing the test and reference DNA                products to a tiling density DNA microarray                comprising genomic DNA sequences, where the there                is a 3-12 base pair overlap of DNA oligomeric                probes.
   USE - The methods, kit and array are used for                detecting the presence of a chromosomal                rearrangement; diagnosing of a disease or condition                associated with chromosomal rearrangement; and                detecting a balanced chromosomal                translocation/rearrangement. The disease is                lymphoma or leukemia. The disease or condition is                selected from lymphoma, B cell lymphoma, T cell                lymphoma, mycosis fungoides, Hodgkin's Disease,                myeloid leukemia, bladder cancer, brain cancer,                nervous system cancer, head and neck cancer,                squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck, lung                cancers such as small cell lung cancer and                non-small cell lung cancer,                neuroblastoma/glioblastoma, ovarian cancer,                prostate cancer, skin cancer, liver cancer,                melanoma, squamous cell carcinomas of the mouth,                throat, larynx, and lung, colon cancer, cervical                cancer, cervical carcinoma, breast cancer, and                epithelial cancer, renal cancer, genitourinary                cancer, pulmonary cancer, esophageal carcinoma,                large bowel cancer, hematopoietic cancers;                testicular cancer; colon and rectal cancers,                prostatic cancer, cervical and anal dysplasias,                other dysplasias, severe dysplasias, hyperplasias,                atypical hyperplasias, neoplasias, and pancreatic                cancer (all claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - A sensitive and cost-effective assay to detect                balanced reciprocal translocations/rearrangements                is provided.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Detecting the presence of a chromosomal                rearrangement in a test sample comprises (a)                isolating a first genomic DNA from cells of a test                sample and a second genomic DNA from cells of a                reference sample; (b) hybridizing the test and                reference DNA products to a tiling density DNA                microarray comprising genomic DNA sequences, where                the there is a 3-12 base pair overlap of DNA                oligomeric probes; and (c) comparing the pattern                and extent of hybridization of the test DNA product                with the reference DNA product to the DNA                microarray; where a patterned loss and recovery of                hybridization of the test sample DNA product over                the reference sample DNA product to a DNA                microarray element indicates the presence of                chromosomal rearrangement. INDEPENDENT CLAIMS                are:
   a method of diagnosing of a disease or                condition associated with chromosomal rearrangement                in a test sample by (a) isolating a first genomic                DNA from cells of a test sample and a second                genomic DNA from cells of a reference sample; (b)                hybridizing the test and reference DNA products to                a tiling density DNA microarray comprising genomic                DNA sequences, where the there is a 3-12 base pair                overlap of DNA oligomeric probes; and (c) comparing                the pattern and extent of hybridization of the test                DNA product with the reference DNA product to the                DNA microarray; where a patterned loss and recovery                of hybridization of the test sample DNA product                over the reference sample DNA product to a DNA                microarray element indicates the presence of                chromosomal rearrangement; and where the presence                of a chromosomal rearrangement at a location                associated with a disease or condition indicates                the presence of the disease or condition;
   a kit for detecting a balanced chromosomal                translocation/rearrangement, comprising (i) an                array for the detection of product, and (ii) the                reagents needed for dye labeling and comparative                genome hybridization (CGH) microarray                hybridization; and
   an array for CGH analysis of a chromosomal                rearrangement associated with a disease.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preferred Method: In the methods above, the                  patterned loss and recovery of hybridization                  occurs at the translocation breakpoint. The                  rearrangement is a balanced reciprocal                  translocation. The first and second genomic DNA                  are labeled with a first and second detectable                  label, respectively, where the detectable labels                  are incorporated using random priming, nick                  translation or end labeling, and where the first                  and second detectable label are fluorescent                  labels. The cell of the test sample is a tumor                  cell and the reference cell is a normal cell,                  where the tumor cell is a lymphoma or leukemia or                  solid tumors. The oligomeric probes are 50-80                  base pairs in length. The oligomeric probes on                  the microarray cover the sequence of the target                  gene comprising at least 100 base pairs upstream                  and downstream of the open reading frame. The                  spacing between contiguous probes on an array is                  3-12 base pairs. The method further comprises the                  detection of a second chromosomal rearrangement;                  where the first and second rearrangement identify                  fusion partners associated with a balanced                  reciprocal translocation/rearrangement. The                  detection is by PCR, sequencing, mass                  spectrometry, hybridization, or CGH analysis.                  Preferred Kit: The kit further comprises one or                  more primers for amplifying the reference and                  test samples prior to hybridization. The kit                  comprises primers for the amplification of loci                  implicated in translocations. Preferred Array:                  The array comprises probes specific for at least                  two loci, where the loci are implicated in a                  chromosomal rearrangement associated with a                  disease. At least one rearrangement associated                  with a disease is a balanced                  translocation/rearrangement.
   EXAMPLE - No suitable example given.

   (1) pharmaceutical composition comprising                complex (I) and carrier or diluent;
   (2) cold sterilizing (P2) a surgical or other                device, involving providing complex (I) on the                device and subjecting the device to irradiation or                sound; and
   (3) chlorin e4-zinc complex, linked or                attached to a magnetic element, is new.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - INORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Method: The process (P1) involves                  adding a solution of the zinc compound to a                  solution of chlorin e4 and the tetraalkylammonium                  salt. In the process (P1) metalation reaction is                  carried out at 25-80 degrees C for 1-12 hours.                  The complex (I) is purified by filtering or                  chromatography. In the process (P1) device is                  subjected to irradiation or sound simultaneously                  with or after provision of the complex (I) on the                  device (preferably irradiation after provision of                  the complex (I) on the device). Preferred                  Components: The chlorin e4, the                  tetraalkylammonium salt and the zinc compound are                  used in a ratio of 0.15-1:15-20:1-12. The zinc                  compound is a carboxylic acid zinc salt, a zinc                  halide, zinc hydride, or zinc acetylacetonate.                  The carboxylic acid zinc salt is zinc stearate or                  zinc acetate (preferably zinc stearate). The                  tetraalkylammonium salt is tetrabutylammonium                  hydroxide. The irradiation is electromagnetic                  radiation with a wavelength of 500-1000 nm. The                  magnetic element is gadolinium, iron or                  manganese.
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - ORGANIC CHEMISTRY - Preferred Components: The solvent is                  N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF), methanol,                  chloroform, dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) or toluene                  (preferably N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) or                  methanol).
   TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - PHARMACEUTICALS - Preferred Method: The pharmaceutical                  composition is adapted for administration                  simultaneous with or prior to administration of                  irradiation or sound (preferably prior to                  administration of irradiation, especially 10-100                  or 3-60 hours before the irradiation). The                  pharmaceutical composition is an aqueous solution                  or suspension having a pH of 6-8.5.
   ACTIVITY - Antiarteriosclerotic; Neuroprotective;                Antidiabetic; Ophthalmological; Antiarthritic;                Antirheumatic; Fungicide; Virucide; Antibacterial;                Antiparasitic; Anti-HIV; Respiratory-Gen;                Antiinflammatory; Hepatotropic;                Cardiovascular-Gen.; Cardiant; Vasotropic;                Dermatological; Antiseborrheic; Antipsoriatic;                Cytostatic. No biological data is given.

The mode of                administration is parental (including intravenous,                subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal,                intratracheal, intraperitoneal, intraarticular,                intraabdominal, intracranial and epidural),                transdermal, airway (aerosol), rectal, vaginal,                topical, buccal, mucosal, sublingual, or oral in                the form of a tablet, capsule, hard or soft                gelatine capsule, caplet, troche or lozenge, as a                powder or granules, or as an aqueous solution,                suspension or dispersion (claimed).
   EXAMPLE - Chlorin e4 (276 mg) were dissolved in                N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) (60 ml), and the                solution was stirred slowly for 10 minutes at 40                degrees C. Tetrabutylammonium hydroxide (15 ml) was                added, and stirring was continued for a further 20                minutes. Zinc stearate (378 mg) were dissolved in                DMF (50 ml), and the solution was stirred at 40                degrees C. The zinc stearate solution was added to                the chlorin e4 solution, and the reaction mixture                was stirred slowly for 3 hours at 40 degrees C.                Then the reaction mixture was filtered. The product                was purified. Then the solution was distilled and                chlorin e4-zinc was isolated.
