AE UNIV ZHEJIANG NORMAL (UYZN-C)
GA 2025A5165J
AB    NOVELTY - The method involves performing (S1) size                normalization and noise suppression on a skin                mirror image. A deep division network fused with                Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a deep                division network fused with CNN and a deep division                network fused with CNN and a deep division network                fused with CNN is constructed (S2). A focusing                characteristic interaction fusion module is used                for realizing the complementary interaction and                fusion between the convolution neural network                characteristic and the thin characteristic. An                image of the data set is inputted (S3) into a deep                division network. The image of the data set is                inputted into the deep division network. The                network weight is optimized by the joint loss                function of Dice loss and binary cross entropy                loss. An over-fitting is prevented by combining the                early-stop strategy. The to-be divided skin mirror                image is inputted (S4) into the trained deep                division network. The division mask image of the                skin lesion area is outputted.
   USE - Method for segmenting skin lesion image based                on feature interaction fusion for early detection                and treatment of disease such as skin cancer using                CNN.
   ADVANTAGE - The method solves the problems of complex                shape, variable size and low contrast in the lesion                area of the skin lesion image, and to improve the                segmentation precision and robustness of the image.                The multi-scale context attention module is                constructed to realize multi- scale precise feature                extraction by extracting space information from                local to global scale, at the same time,                maintaining calculation efficiency.
   DESCRIPTION OF DRAWING(S) - The drawing shows a flow chart of a method                for segmenting skin lesion image based on                characteristic interaction fusion. (Drawing                includes non-English language text)
   S1Step for performing size normalization and                noise suppression on a skin mirror image
   S2Step for constructing a deep division                network fused with CNN and a deep division network                fused with CNN and a deep division network fused                with CNN and a deep division network fused with                CNN
   S3Step for inputting the image of the data                set into a deep segmentation network
   S4Step for inputting the to-bedivided skin                mirror image into the trained deep division                network

TI New 5' adapter useful e.g. for diagnosing            neurodegenerative disease and cancer in patient,            comprises 5'-terminal nucleotide sequence and            nucleotide sequence capable of forming stem-loop            structure containing loop and double stranded            stem.
AU HOROS R
   STEINKRAUS B
   BIEG-SALAZAR C
AE HUMMINGBIRD DIAGNOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
   HUMMINGBIRD DIAGNOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
   HUMMINGBIRD DIAGNOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
   HUMMINGBIRD DIAGNOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
   HUMMINGBIRD DIGANOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
   HUMMINGBIRD DIAGNOSTICS GMBH (HUMM-Non-standard)
GA 202320375R
AB    NOVELTY - A 5' adapter comprising in the following order                from 5'-3', (i) a 5'-terminal nucleotide sequence                comprising 6-15 deoxynucleotides, where the 6-15                deoxynucleotides are reverse complementary to a                5'-terminal sequence of a target RNA and (ii) a                nucleotide sequence capable of forming a stem-loop                structure containing a loop and a double stranded                stem, where at least 2 nucleotides at its 3' end                are ribonucleotides or modified ribonucleotides and                the nucleotide sequence is locked nucleotide-(LNA-)                enhanced, is new.
   USE - The 5' adapter and 3' adapter are useful in                kit and combination for determining and/or                quantifying a target RNA in a sample and diagnosing                a disease or condition in a patient. The disease is                chosen from neurodegenerative disease, an                autoimmune disease, an infectious disease, and                cancer. The neurodegenerative disease is chosen                from Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other dementias,                Parkinson's disease (PD) and PD-related diseases,                Prion disease, Motor neurone diseases (MND),                Huntington's disease (HD), Spinocerebellar ataxia                (SCA), Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), AIDS dementia                complex and atherosclerosis. The autoimmune disease                is chosen from diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis (RA),                multiple sclerosis (MS), systemic lupus                erythematosus (lupus), Graves' disease, Sjogren's                syndrome, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, myasthenia                gravis, vasculitis, pernicious anemia and celiac                disease. The infectious disease is viral infection,                preferably chronic or persistent viral infection,                bacterial infection or parasitic infection. The                cancer is skin cancer, nasopharyngeal cancer,                neuroendrocrine cancer, lung cancer, colon cancer,                urothelial cancer, bladder cancer, liver cancer,                ovarian cancer, gastric cancer, esophageal cancer,                pancreatic cancer, kidney cancer, stomach cancer,                esophageal cancer, breast cancer, renal cancer,                head and neck cancer, brain cancer, lymphatic                cancer, blood cancer, squamous cell cancer,                laryngeal cancer, retina cancer, prostate cancer,                cervical cancer, uterine cancer, testicular cancer,                bone cancer, lymphoma or leukemia (all                claimed).
   ADVANTAGE - The 5' adapter and 3' adapter detect small                non-coding RNAs in a sample. The method allows                detection and quantification of miRNAs and isomiRs                in a simple, fast, cost-effective, reliable and                precise manner with high specificity and                sensitivity and improves diagnosis and/or prognosis                of diseases.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for the                following:
   3' adapter comprising in the following order                from 5'-3', (i) a nucleotide sequence capable of                forming a stem-loop structure containing a loop and                a double stranded stem, where the 5'-terminal                nucleotide is phosphorylated and the nucleotide                sequence is locked nucleotide- (LNA-) enhanced, and                (ii) a 3' terminal nucleotide sequence comprising                6-15 deoxynucleotides, where the 6-15                deoxynucleotides are reverse complementary to a                3'-terminal sequence of a target RNA and the 3'                terminal deoxynucleotide is an inverted                deoxynucleotide;
   combination comprising 5' adapter and 3'                adapter;
   method for ligating two adapters to a target                RNA in a sample involves (i) providing a                composition comprising a denatured target RNA in a                sample, the renatured 5' adapter and the renatured                3' adapter, where the 5' adapter and the 3' adapter                are annealed to the target RNA and (ii) ligating                the 5' adapter and the 3' adapter to the target RNA                using/with a double stranded RNA ligase, for                producing a ligation product;
   method for determining and/or quantifying a                target RNA in a sample involves (a) performing the                above-mentioned method, (b) reverse transcribing                the ligation product, for obtaining a cDNA product                from the target RNA and (c) amplifying the cDNA,                for determining and/or quantifying the target                RNA;
   method for diagnosing a disease or condition                in a patient involves performing the                above-mentioned method for determining the presence                of the target RNA and diagnosing whether the                patient is afflicted by the disease or condition                based on the presence of the target RNA, or                performing the above-mentioned method for                quantifying the target RNA, comparing the                quantified target RNA with a reference and                diagnosing whether the patient is afflicted by the                disease or condition based on the comparison;                and
   kit comprising the 5' adapter, 3' adapter or                their combination.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation: No preparation method is given.                  Preferred Biomolecules: The nucleotide sequence                  capable of forming a stem-loop structure                  comprises a 5' positioned first stem sequence and                  a 3' positioned second stem sequence that are                  reverse complementary to each other. Each one of                  the 5' positioned first stem sequence and the 3'                  positioned second stem sequence has a length of                  5-10 nucleotides. The 5' positioned first stem                  sequence and the 3' positioned second stem                  sequence have the same length. The 5'-positioned                  first stem sequence and/or the 3'-positioned                  second stem sequence is (are) LNA enhanced. The                  LNA enhanced sequence comprises 2-5, preferably 3                  locked nucleotides. The nucleotide sequence                  capable of forming a stem-loop structure                  comprises a loop sequence which is located                  between the 5'-positioned first stem sequence and                  the 3'-positioned second stem sequence. The loop                  sequence comprises 12-20 nucleotides. The                  nucleotides are deoxynucleotides. The 5'-terminal                  sequence is configured such that it forms a                  single stranded 5'-protrusion after formation of                  the stem-loop structure. The 6-15                  deoxynucleotides which are reverse complementary                  to the 5'-terminal sequence of a target RNA                  encompass g and c but &#8814; 4 in a row. The                  5'adapter has the following sequence from 5'-3':                  (6-15x)ncgtggcgtggagtgtgtgctttgccarcrg (SEQ ID                  NO: 1), where r is ribonucleotide, (6-15x)n                  designates the sequence reverse complementary to                  a 5' terminal sequence of a target RNA and one or                  more nucleotides in the underlined portion and/or                  one or more nucleotides in the double underlined                  portion are LNA enhanced. The target RNA is RNA                  having a length of less than 200 ribonucleotides,                  preferably a miRNA or a miRNA isoform (an                  isomiR). The reference is a reference target RNA.                  The inverted deoxynucleotide is inverted dt, da,                  dc, or dg. The 3'-adapter comprises a base pair                  sequence:                  /5Phos/ctcagtgcagggtccgaggtattcgcactgag(6-15x)n/3InvdT/                  (SEQ ID NO: 2), where /5Phos/ indicates that the                  5'-terminal nucleotide is phosphorylated, one or                  more nucleotides in the underlined portion and/or                  one or more nucleotides in the double underlined                  portion are LNA enhanced, (6-15x)N designates the                  sequence reverse complementary to a 3'-terminal                  sequence of a target RNA and /3InvdT/ stands for                  3'-inverted deoxynucleotide. The total length of                  the 5' terminal nucleotide sequence comprising                  6-15 deoxynucleotides and the 3' terminal                  nucleotide sequence comprising 6-15                  deoxynucleotides is shorter by at least 2                  nucleotides than the length of the target RNA.                  The double stranded RNA ligase is a T4 RNA ligase                  2 (Rnl2) or a Kodl ligase. The reverse                  transcriptase (RT) is Maxima H-RT or Tth                  polymerase. The RT-primer is reverse                  complementary to the nucleotide sequence capable                  of forming a stem-loop structure containing a                  loop and a double stranded stem of the 3'                  adapter. The RT-primer comprises a base pair                  sequence: ctcagtgcgaatacctcggaccct (SEQ ID NO:                  3). Preferred Method: The denatured target RNA is                  produced by heating the target RNA at                  65-75&#176; C, preferably at 70&#176; C                  for 1-3 minutes, preferably 2 minutes. The                  renatured 5' adapter is produced by denaturing                  the 5' adapter at 75-85&#176; C, preferably                  at 82&#176; C, for 1-3 minutes, preferably 2                  minutes, and renaturing the 5' adapter by cooling                  down to 4&#176; C, preferably at a rate of                  0.1&#176; C/second. The renatured 3'adapter                  is produced by denaturing the 3'adapter at                  75-85&#176; C, preferably 82&#176; C, for                  1-3 minutes, preferably 2 minutes, and renaturing                  the 3'adapter by cooling down to 4&#176; C,                  preferably at a rate of 0.1&#176; C/second.                  The renatured 5' and 3'-adapters are produced                  separately and in the absence of target RNA. The                  method involves denaturing and renaturing in an                  aqueous buffer comprising 10 mM                  tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane hydrochloride                  (tris HCl) pH 7.5, 50 mM sodium chloride and 0.1                  mM EDTA. The composition is produced by mixing                  the denatured target RNA, the renatured 5'                  adapter and the renatured 3' adapter with each                  other, for annealing the 5'adapter and the                  3'adapter to the target RNA. The ligation is                  carried out in a ligation buffer comprising                  polyethylene glycol (PEG). The ligation is                  performed at 36-38&#176; C, preferably                  37&#176; C for 30 minutes-1.5 hours,                  preferably 1 hour, or 15-20&#176; C,                  preferably 16&#176; C for 30 minutes-2 hours,                  preferably 1-2 hours and then overnight at                  12&#176; C. The reverse transcription of the                  ligation product is carried out by annealing a                  primer for reverse transcription (RT-primer) with                  the ligation product and reverse transcribing the                  ligation product by using a reverse transcriptase                  (RT). The annealing step is performed at                  60-80&#176; C, preferably 65&#176; C or                  75&#176; C for 2-7 minutes, preferably 3 or 5                  minutes. The reverse transcribing step is                  performed at 40-65&#176; C, preferably at                  50&#176; C, 55&#176; C, 58&#176; C or                  62&#176; C, for 10-40 minutes, preferably 15                  or 30 minutes, and subsequently at                  75-90&#176; C, preferably at 85&#176; C,                  for 2-4 minutes, preferably 3 minutes or at                  60-75&#176; C, preferably 68&#176; C for                  10-30 minutes, preferably 15 minutes. The method                  further involves between steps (b) and (c),                  performing cDNA preamplification with a forward                  primer comprising a base pair sequence:                  tggagtgtgtgctttgccacg (SEQ ID NO: 4) and a                  reverse primer comprising a base pair sequence:                  gtgcgaatacctcggacc (SEQ ID NO: 5). The                  amplification is performed using PCR chosen from                  real-time PCR (quantitative PCR or qPCR),                  preferably TaqMan(RTM: Universal PCR master mix)                  qPCR, multiplex PCR, nested PCR, high fidelity                  PR, fast PCR, hot start PCR and gc-rich PCR. The                  TaqMan(RTM: Universal PCR master mix) qPCR is                  performed with the forward primer of SEQ ID NO: 4                  and reverse primer of SEQ ID NO: 5. The                  TaqMan(RTM: Universal PCR master mix) qPCR is                  carried out in the presence of a TaqMan(RTM:                  Dual-labeled hydrolysis probe) probe. Preferred                  Sample: The sample is a biological sample. The                  biological sample is a blood sample. The blood                  sample is a whole blood or a blood fraction,                  preferably blood cells, serum, or plasma. The                  sample contains total RNA. The sample contains                  cellular total RNA. Preferred Kit: The kit                  further comprises a double stranded RNA ligase,                  preferably a T4 RNA ligase 2 (Rnl2) or a Kodl                  ligase. The kit further comprises instructions on                  how to carry out the method. The kit further                  comprises a reverse transcriptase. The kit                  further comprises a DNA polymerase and a forward                  primer and/or a reverse primer allowing the                  amplification of the cDNA. The kit further                  comprises a reference.
   EXAMPLE - The examples provide details of sequences of                the specific adapters and TaqMan(RTM: Dual-labeled                hydrolysis probe) probes used for detection and                combinations of the adapters and probes used for                the discrimination assays that do not support the                claims.

TI New nanovectors containing polymer chains, useful            for treating neurological diseases e.g. Alzheimer's            disease, inflammatory processes e.g. arthritis or            colitis, cancer e.g. brain cancer or liver cancer, and            blood diseases.
AU BERTRAND P
   DELATOUCHE R
   HEROGUEZ V
   COLLETTE F
   GREGOIRE M
   BLANQUART C
   GUEUGNON F
AE CENT NAT RECH SCI (CNRS-C)
   UNIV POITIERS (UPOI-C)

   INSERM INST NAT SANTE & RECH MEDICALE (INRM-C)
GA 2013A22618
AB    NOVELTY - Nanovectors containing polymer chains (I), are                new.
   USE - The nanovector is useful for treating diseases                comprising neurological diseases, inflammatory                processes, cancer or blood diseases (claimed),                where the neurological disease is Alzheimer's                disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis,                neuropathy, polyneuropathy, epilepsy or meningitis;                the inflammatory process is arthritis, arteritis,                colitis, conjunctivitis, cystitis, dermatitis,                encephalitis, endocarditis, endometritis,                gastritis, meningitis, myocarditis, myelitis,                pancreatitis, peritonitis, sinusitis or tendonitis;                the cancer is hematopoietic cancers, leukemias,                lymphomas, carcinomas, adenocarcinomas, sarcomas,                melanoma, carcinoma of head and neck cancer, oral                and pharyngeal cancer, laryngeal cancer, bladder                cancer, colorectal cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical                cancer, penile cancer, vulva and vaginal cancer,                cervical cancer, prostate cancer, renal cancer,                skin cancer, bone cancer, joints cancer, articular                cartilages cancer, testicular cancer, stomach                cancer, gastrointestinal cancer, genitourinary                cancer, lung cancer, thymoma, mesothelioma,                teratoma, brain cancer, liver cancer, pancreatic                cancer, glioma, glioblastoma, oligoastrocytoma,                meningioma, pituitary adenoma, glioblastoma                multiforme, medulloblastoma, ependymoma, anaplastic                astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, thyroid cancer,                anaplastic cancer, hemangiosarcoma of the thyroid                gland, Kaposi's sarcoma, lymphangiosarcoma,                Hodgkin's lymphoma, indolent non-Hodgkin's lymphoma                or retinoblastoma; and the blood diseases are from                red blood cells, leukocytes or platelets. Tests                details are described but no results given.
   ADVANTAGE - The nanovectors have improved solubility and                permeability, treat diseases with reduced toxicity                and circulate longer in blood vessels of a mammal,                preferably human, for 24 hours, thus avoiding their                elimination by macrophages.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Nanovectors containing polymer chains of                formula (I), are new.
   P1=polymer chain containing 30-10000 monomer                units, derived from polymerization of 4-12C                monocyclic alkenes or 6-20C polycyclic                alkenes;
   t, n, v=0 or 1;
   q=1-10;
   u=0-10;
   X=O, NH or S;
   R1, Ra1=when t is 1, triazole group of formula                (a), or when t is 0, triazole group of formula (b)                or (c) connected to a monocyclic alkene or                polycyclic alkene;
   Z=monocyclic or polycyclic alkene;
   m, p=1-1000, preferably 70-200;
   r=0-10, preferably 0 or 1;
   R3=epigenetic modulator, detection probe                including fluorescent or radio transmitter, or                cell-penetrating peptide, where if n is 0 and v is                1, and then R3 is directly bonded to the carbon                bearing R2 and Ra2;
   R4=vinyl, ethyne, OR1a or SR2a;
   R1a, R2a=H, 1-20C alkyl or 3-20C cycloalkyl;                either
   R2, Ra2=phenyl (optionally substituted by                1-20C alkyl, 3-20C cycloalkyl, 1-20C alkoxy,                NRaxRbx, NO 2 , CO 2 Rcx or 1-20C acyl) or H, where                preferably R2 and Ra2 are 2- or 4-methoxyphenyl, 2-                or 4-methylphenyl, phenyl or 2,4-dimethoxyphenyl;                or
   R2Ra2=if n is 0 and v is 0, monovalent group                of formula (d) or (e); or
   R2Ra2=if n is 1 and v is 1, divalent group of                formula (f) or if n is 1, divalent group of formula                (g);
   Yx=O or NRdxRex, where the nitrogen atom has a                positive charge associated with a monovalent                anion;
   Rdx, Rex=H, 1-20C alkyl or 3-20C cycloalkyl,                where the 1-20C alkyl which may form a ring with                the 1'-3'C;
   Ya=OR1a, 1-20C alkyl, 3-20C cycloalkyl, 1-20C                alkoxy, NRfxRgx, NO 2 , CO 2 Rcx or 1-20C                acyl;
   A =monovalent anion;
   Rfx, Rgx=H, 1-20C alkyl or 3-20C cycloalkyl,                where the 1-20C alkyl which may form a ring with                the 1-3C;
   Rcx=benzyl (optionally substituted), H, 1-20C                alkyl or 3-20C cycloalkyl;
   Rax, Rbx=H or 1-20C alkyl, which may form a                ring with ortho position to carbon bearing the N or                3-20C cycloalkyl;
   Y1, Y2=OR1a, 1-20C alkyl, 3-20C cycloalkyl,                1-20C alkoxy, NRhxRix, NO 2 , CO 2 Rcx or 1-20C                acyl; and
   Rhx, Rix=H, 1-20C alkyl or 3-20C cycloalkyl,                where the 1-20C alkyl which may form a ring with                the 1-3C in Y1 and 1'-3'C in Y2.
   An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for the                preparation of nanovectors.
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                     
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOTECHNOLOGY - Preparation (Claimed): Preparation of                  nanovector comprises polymerizing by ring opening                  metathesis and then bioconjugating. Preferred                  Process: The process comprises: (a) preparing a                  triazole compound of formula (II) containing                  monocyclic or polycyclic alkene and azide                  function, (b) polymerizing by ring-opening                  metathesis in the presence of a catalyst to form                  a triazole compound of formula (III) containing                  azide function on the polymer surface, (c)                  preparing a triazole compound of formula (IV)                  containing alkyne function, and (d) contacting                  (II) with (III) in the presence of copper to                  obtain nanovectors.=0-10, preferably 0 or 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
   Preferred Definitions:
   P1=monocyclic alkenes containing                cyclooctapolyene (preferred), cyclobutene,                cyclopentene, cyclopentadiene, cyclohexene,                cyclohexadiene, cycloheptene, cyclooctene,                cyclononene, cyclononadiene, cyclodecene,                cyclodeca-1,5-diene, cyclododecene or acetate of                2,3,4,5-tetrahydrooxepin-2-yl, cyclopentadecene,                paracyclophane or ferrocenophane, or polycyclic                alkenes containing monomer containing cyclobutene                ring or cyclopentene ring, norbornene,                norbornadiene dimer, dicyclopentadiene,                tetracyclododecadiene (all preferred),                norbornadiene, 7-oxanorbornene, 7-oxanorbornadiene,                bicyclo[5,1,0]oct-2-ene or bicyclo[6,1,0]non-4-ene;                and
   R3=epigenetic modulator (containing                nucleoside, preferably cytidine, uridine,                adenosine, guanosine, thymidine or inosine, histone                deacetylase inhibitors (HDAC) including Zolinza                (RTM: Suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid),                trichostatin A, valproic acid,                [4-(2-amino-phenylcarbamoyl)-benzyl]-carbamic acid                pyridin-3-yl-methyl ester or                4-acetylamino-N-(2-amino-phenyl)-benzamide, or DNA                methyltransferase inhibitors, preferably                5-azacytidine, 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine or                zebularine), detection probe (containing                fluorophore substance including                [6-diethylamino-9-(2-prop-2-ynyloxycarbonyl-phenyl)-6,9a-dihydro-xanthen-3-ylidene]-diethyl-ammonium,                fluorescein, coumarins, preferably                7-hydroxy-4-methylcoumarin, boron-dipyrromethene,                cyanines, preferably                1-methyl-2-{(E)-3-[1-methyl-1,3-dihydro-indol-(2E)-ylidene]-propenyl}-2,3-dihydro-1H-indolium                iodide or                1-ethyl-2-{(E)-3-[1-ethyl-1,3-dihydro-indol-(2E)-ylidene]-propenyl}-2,3-dihydro-1H-indolium                iodide,                1-ethyl-2-{(1E,3E)-5-[1-ethyl-1,3-dihydro-indol-(2E)-ylidene]-penta-1,3-dienyl}-2,3-dihydro-1H-indolium                iodide or                1-methyl-2-{(1E,3E)-5-[1-methyl-1,3-dihydro-indol-(2E)-ylidene]-penta-1,3-dienyl}-2,3-dihydro-1H-indolium                iodide, or a radio transmitter substance including                99-Technetium as ligand or contrast agents for                medical imaging such as lanthanides (gadolinium)),                or penetrating peptide (including polylysine,                polyarginine, polylysine imidazole or mimetics of                polyglycine with chain bearing a nitrogen                containing terminal group).
   ACTIVITY - Neuroprotective; Antiinflammatory;                Gastrointestinal-Gen.; Cytostatic; Antianemic;                Nootropic; Antiparkinsonian; Anticonvulsant;                Antiarthritic; Vasotropic; Ophthalmological;                Dermatological; Cardiant; Gynecological;                Immunomodulator; Anticoagulant; Thrombolytic.
   MECHANISM OF ACTION - None given.
   ADMINISTRATION - Administration of (I) is 5-500 mg,                intravenously (claimed).
   EXAMPLE -                 2-[2-(2-Azidoethoxy)ethoxymethyl]bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene                compound of formula (V) (333.4 mg), 1-5 equivalents                of                [6-diethylamino-9-(2-prop-2-ynyloxycarbonyl-phenyl)-6,9a-dihydro-xanthen-3-ylidene]-diethyl-ammonium                (85 mg) and 2 equivalents of                N,N,N',N'',N''-pentamethyldiethylenetriamine (0.06                ml) were dissolved in degassed                dichloromethane/ethanol (10 ml) and placed under an                inert atmosphere. Copper bromide (2 equivalents)                was added to the solution. The solution was stirred                at room temperature for 6 days. After 6 days, the                solvent was evaporated and the polymer was                dissolved in dichloromethane (20 ml). The organic                phase was washed (10 times) with water and then                dried with sodium sulfate. The dichloromethane was                evaporated and the residue was dissolved in                tetrahydrofuran (15 ml), precipitated in diethyl                ether (100 ml) and dried under vacuum to give                4-methyl-7-(1-methyl-1H-[1,2,3]triazol-4-ylmethoxy)-chromen-2-one                compound of formula (VI).

AB    NOVELTY - Isolated human polynucleotides obtained by                screening for differential expression in colon                cancer, breast cancer and lung cancer cell lines                are new.
   USE - The PNs encode polypeptides with similarity to                known protein families and are predicted to have                similar properties. The novel PNs can be used to                develop products for use as therapeutic agents and                in forensics, genetic analysis, mapping and                diagnostic applications. In particular, the product                can be used for the detection and management of                cancers. They can be used for treating e.g.                cervical cancers, melanomas, colorectal                adenocarcinomas, Wilm's tumor, retinoblastoma,                sarcomas, myosarcomas, lung carcinomas, leukemias,                such as chronic myelogenous leukemia, promyelocytic                leukemia, monocytic leukemia, and myeloid leukemia,                and lymphomas such as histiocytic lymphoma,                anhydric hereditary ectodermal dysplaisa,                congenital alveolar dysplasia, epithelial dysplasia                of the cervix, fibrous dysplasia of bone, and                mammary dysplasia, hyperplasias, e.g. endometrial,                adrenal, breast, prostate or thyroid hyperplasias                or pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia of the                skin.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - A novel library of polynucleotides (PNs)                comprises the sequence information of at least one                of sequences 1-844.
   INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following:
   an isolated PN comprising a nucleotide                sequence (NS) having at least 90% sequence identity                to an identifying sequence of 844 sequences (given                in the specification) or a degenerate                variant;
   an isolated PN as in (1) which comprises a                sequence encoding a polypeptide of a protein family                selected from 4 transmembrane segments integral                membrane proteins, 7 transmembrane receptors,                ATPases associated with various cellular activities                (AAA), eukaryotic aspartyl proteases, GATA family                of transcription factors, G-protein alpha subunit,                phorbol esters/diacylglycerol binding proteins,                protein kinase, protein phosphatase 2C, protein                tyrosine phosphatase, trypsin, wnt family of                developmental signaling proteins and WW/rsp5/WWP                domain containing proteins;
   a PN as in (1) which comprises a sequence                encoding a polypeptide having a functional domain                selected from Ank repeat, basic region plus leucine                zipper transcription factors, bromodomain, EF-hand,                SH3 domain, WD domain/G-beta repeats, zinc finger                (C2H2 type), zinc finger (CCHC class), and                zinc-binding metalloprotease domain;
   a recombinant host cell containing a PN as in                (1);
   an isolated polypeptide encoded by a PN as in                (1);
   an antibody that specifically binds a                polypeptide as in (5);
   a vector comprising a PN as in (1);
   detecting differentially expressed genes                correlated with a cancerous state of a mammalian                cells comprising detecting at least one                differentially expressed gene product in a test                sample derived from a cell suspected of being                cancerous, where the gene product is encoded by a                gene corresponding to a sequence of at least one of                the 66 sequences (given in the specification),                where detection of the differentially expressed                gene product is correlated with a cancerous state                of the cell from which the test sample was                derived.
TF TECHNOLOGY FOCUS - BIOLOGY - Isolation: The PNs were isolated by studying                  differential expression in cDNA libraries                  prepared from human colon cancer cells, human                  breast carcinoma cells and human lung cancer                  cells.
   EXAMPLE - Human colon cancer cell line Km12L4-A was used                to construct a cDNA library from mRNA isolated from                the cells. A total of 4693 sequences expressed by                the Km12L4-A cell line were isolated and analyzed,                most sequences were 275-300 nucleotides in length.                The KM12L4-A cell line is derived from the KM12C                cell line. The KM12C cell line, which is poorly                metastatic was established in culture from a Dukes'                stage B2surgical specimen. The KML4-A is a highly                metastatic subline derived from KM12C. The                sequences were first masked to eliminate low                complexity sequences using the XBLAST masking                program. Masking resulted in the elimination of 43                sequences. The remaining sequences were then used                in a BLASTN vs. GenBank search with search                parameters of greater than 70% overlap, 99%                identity and a p value of less than 1 x 10-40,                which search resulted in the discarding of 1432                sequences. Sequences from this search also were                discarded if the inclusive parameters were met, but                the sequence was ribosomal or vector-derived. The                resulting sequences were classified into 3 groups                and searched in a BLASTX vs. NRP (non-redundant                proteins) database search:
   unknown (no hits in the GenBank search);
   weak similarity (&#8805;45% identity and p                value of &#8804;1 x 10-5), and
   high similarity (&#8805;60% overlap,                &#8805;80% identity, and p value &#8804;1 x                10-5). This search resulted in discard of 98                sequences as having &#8805;70% overlap,                &#8805;99% identity, and p value of &#8804;                1 x 10-40.
   The remaining sequences were classified as                unknown (no hits), weak similarity, and high                similarity. 2 searches were performed on these                sequences. First a BLAST vs. EST database search                resulted in discard of 1771 sequences (sequences                with &#8805;99% overlap, &#8805;99%                similarity and a p value of &#8804;1 x 10-40,                sequences with a p value of &#8804;1 x                10-65when compared to a database sequence of human                origin were also excluded). Second, a BLASTN vs.                Patent GeneSeq database resulted in discard of 15                sequences (&#8805;99% identity, p value                &#8804;1 x 10-40, &#8805;99% overlap). The                remaining sequences were subjected to screening                using other rules and redundancies in the dataset.                Sequences with a p value of &#8804;1 x 10-111in                relation to a database sequence of human origin                were specifically excluded. The final result                provided the 404 sequences (given in the                specification).

TI Medication infusion device for delivering doses of            fluid medication from e.g. pre-filled cartridge, to            e.g. Type-I Diabetes Mellitus patients, through            transcutaneous portion, has controller coupled to            sensor and making pump to act based on information on            whether detection of wearer skin exists.
AU BARRAUD A

AE TANDEM DIABETES CARE SWITZERLAND SARL (TDEM-C)
GA 2023A8726D
AB    NOVELTY - The medication infusion device has a patch                pump (300) removably adhered to a wearer skin for                delivering doses of medication from a cartridge                through a transcutaneous portion. The patch pump                comprises a pump housing (302). A pump motor is                arranged in the pump housing, and pumps the                medication in the cartridge toward the                transcutaneous portion. A sensor detects the wearer                skin and generates information on whether detection                of the wearer skin exists. A controller is                operatively coupled to the pump motor and the                sensor, and makes the patch pump to act based on                the information on whether the detection of the                wearer skin exists.
   USE - Medication infusion device for delivering                doses of fluid medication i.e. insulin, from a                cartridge e.g. pre-filled cartridge, to a patient                with diabetes i.e. Type-I Diabetes Mellitus                patients, through a transcutaneous portion. Uses                include but are not limited to antibiotics,                nutritional fluids, total parenteral nutrition                (TPN), analgesics, morphine, hormones or hormonal                drugs, gene therapy drugs, anticoagulants,                analgesics, cardiovascular medications,                Azidothymidine (AZT) or chemotherapeutics for                treating cardiovascular disease, pain, chronic                pain, cancer, Alzheimer's Disease disorders (ADDS),                neurological diseases, Alzheimer's Disease,                amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), Hepatitis,                Parkinson's Disease or spasticity.
   ADVANTAGE - The medication infusion device effectively                delivers precise and repeatable doses of medication                in a user-friendly, environmentally-friendly                manner, low cost, discreet and less prone to errors                and accessories. The medication infusion device                ensures that the patch pump does not deliver the                medication when the wearer holds the patch pump by                ensuring that the sensor detects the wearer skin.                The medication infusion device reduces noise from                inserting a cannula, so that a lower stopping                portion can clamp a joint between two surfaces to                slow rotation of a link and an applicator needle.                The medication infusion device adopts a sleep mode                to allow fine-tuning of a wearer glucose level to                provide better sleep well and improve time in a                targeted glucose range. The medication infusion                device ensures that a portion of a plunger of the                cartridge contacting the medication does not move                than distance needed to expel desired volume of                medication of microdose, thus ensuring enhanced                accuracy of microdose volumes of medication. The                medication infusion device makes welded portions to                increase watertightness efficiency, so that levers                can provide less pressure on a dosing tube while                preventing the medication from flowing toward the                wearer.
   DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for utilizing a medication infusion device for                delivering doses of medication from a cartridge                through a transcutaneous portion.
